reviews.comment: First class I've ever had where assignments don't have any rubric. "Delight me" makes no sense when I don't know you.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never take this man's class if you want to know how to make your professor happy. Before writing our essays, we asked him if there were instructions. His instructions were "delight me". When asked for clarification on what delights him he said "being delighted". The next day he came into class and told us that none of us knew how to write.

Professor Badshah did a good job teaching this class and the lectures were engaging. The challenge with this course is that 'Global Business' is an incredibly broad topic, which can make it feel a bit unfocused at times. The selected readings were interesting and be prepared to discuss them and current events.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ghosts emails and forces you to go through a 'manager' for personal questions. Heavy group work with no class time to collaborate — slackers will drag you down. Little empathy for individual situations. Avoid if you hate chasing teammates.
Ghosts emails. Heavy group work with no class time to collaborate — slackers will drag you down. Avoid if you hate chasing teammates.
He is a very nice guy. Taking Retik is not a mistake, you can genuinly learn a lot from him if you listen and ask questions.

Dr. Retik is one of the most caring professors I've ever met at UWB. He has supported me in many ways; during my internship, when I was considering applying for a master's program, and beyond. He is always willing to help his students, and I was impressed by his professionalism. I highly recommend taking his class, even if it's not CSS 350.

350 is a pointless class and a waste of space in the CSSE curriculum, however professor Retik is a very kind and well meaning professor, but this is offset by him being a very obvious capitalist. Most of the class breaks down to talking about are great companies are and how employees just need to work harder, I came to learn not to be preached too.

Professor Retik is a chill guy. Lectures are clear and engaging. The class is team-based - make sure you create or join a good team. There are quite a few short presentations (mostly group-based) in the quarter and there's an emphasis on improving your presentation skills. Some quizzes are tricky but are curved and allow cheat sheets and critique.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Most dull lectures I've experienced in a long time; they made me hate the class and subject matter. He's a good guy though, so I feel bad. Assignments weren't very difficult and quizzes were pretty lenient. "You have to actively try to fail the class" -- Retik
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: From the first day of class you will learn to appreciate his humor. He's a down to earth guy and wants the best for his students.

There isn't any hard-coding that you need to do for this class, as the project just focuses on the development (1 deliverable weekly) of a plan for a theoretical project that you don't have to do. Besides the project, the homework and tests are pretty easy. Just read the parts of the textbooks specified by the lectures, and this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Group projects, choose a good team. Grading standards on quizzes and exams were terrible. Too harsh on students and unexpected grading criteria. I did not enjoy the class and did not learn much from it. Professor is nice though his lectures could be faster-paced and more planned out. CSS360 does not feel like a core class.
Class is project heavy, requires constant collaboration so pick good group members. Quizzes are not that clear, and the TA was horrible.

Yes, it's 2 hours of him talking but he puts effort and actually knows what he is taking about. I really enjoyed his lectures, he made the material interesting! He also was very caring and accommodating, I've had technical issues during an exam, and helped me a lot to get my points back. The only con was the TA's grading, Prof's grading was better!

5 minutes of useful information buried in the most boring 2.5 hour lecture of all time. Spends way too much time explaining extremely obvious things but doesn't spend enough time on the important stuff. His graders are also very harsh. You can understand the concept perfectly, but if you don't use the exact phrase he wants, you lose full points
Lectures are very boring. Tests are open internet, open book, open everything. He takes student feedback. Nice professor over all.
Very, very, very boring lectures. Also, he spends time talking about politics instead of lecturing. He's so unorganized. DON'T take his classes.

Dr. Retik is a nice professor, I think one of the previous comments is rude. I learned new ways of thinking from this course. there are many of writing homework in this course, just make sure you understand the requirements then you will be fine.

Professor Retik is one of the easiest professors I have taken. Yes, his lectures can be boring but what he discusses for 360 in his lectures were topics that were on quizzes and exams. At least when taking his class you know what to expect and he has open-note exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Retik's lectures aren't the greatest, but he is very accommodating with deadlines or if you have personal issues that might interfere with the class. He is open to talking and easy to approach if you need help with something. This class can be rough, but if you do all the assignments, you will do well on exams! Also, Lots of Extra Credit!

His lectures are extremely boring; you will learn very little from him, therefore be prepared to study everything on your own from the textbook. There are four projects, three quizzes, two exams, and some group activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Retik is very unorganized. The class was initially moving very slowly, and since he pushed back on many assignments, the last two weeks of the quarter became very brutal. Group work and exams take up the majority of your grade.  Most of the assignments and directions were just unclear.

Professor Retik is a gentle and nice professor who you can choose. As I see there is a review complaint on his TA. My exp is worse than that. If he is always unfair like this, even has a bias or you know that r-word, that is a big problem. It's the student's right to study at school without fear. TA's complex personal RSN shouldn't affect students

Dr. Retik is a decent choice for 360 as it heavily depends on group projects. However, our TA was very picky and docked points literally whenever possible. Lectures are long and boring but he gives breaks. He goes off-topic very often during class. We couldn't finish all the concepts. This isn't the most interesting class, but you can get above 3.5
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Retik is an overrated professor overall. His lectures are some of the most boring I have ever experienced, but when it comes to group work his class is enjoyable. Quizzes however were absolutely terrible. 20 mins for 5 paragraph free response questions, just insane. Final project is heavily weighted, and class is VERY group oriented, choose wisely.

The class was extremely disorganized. Most assignments were pushed back as he forgot to discuss them or ran out of time. Slides and assignments were full of incorrect dates from previous quarters.

Reading was done with PDFs of chapters from optional textbook, but a lot of the time he forgot to link them so assignments were pushed back.
Best available for CSS 350. Good teacher, very organized, and always willing to help. I don't understand his obsession with Elon Musk.

Textbook is tedious and helpful, but his long lectures are good enough. He repeats what he says, which can be helpful or annoying. Group projects are easy if everyone's cooperative and know what they're doing. Exams and final aren't difficult, if you studied the materials. He allows a sheet of notes for each exam. Extra credit questions on them.
Lots of group assignments, but they're generally pretty easy. Professor Retik is also very caring as a professor.

Favorite class I've taken since declaring MIS, and Prof. Retik was definitely why. He is very committed to making sure all students understand the material and are engaged in class, and is very compassionate and easy to talk to. Lectures are easy to pay attention to, and all the work feels meaningful. Fair grader, but not a super easy one.

Professor Retik does a really nice job of engaging the class, despite it being online. He uses different forms of teaching with videos, lectures, and quizzes during class to test our learning. Practice coding, it is especially important getting into programming. Make sure to good on the 2 midterms and final! Bad exam grades will sink your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class has a lot of assignments that get annoying after a while. These assignments aren't hard but consume a lot of time. His instructions for assignments are not clear and leave you wondering what you're supposed to do. 4 out of 5 quizzes are considered and they are very time constricting. The final group project is pretty straightforward.

I am glad to have taken Retik. CSS 350 is not very interesting but you can tell Retik cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. That's way more important than the content of the class. If you have problems with how he does things, just talk to him. He is willing to listen to feedback in office hours.

He's a solid professor, I just got really frustrated that his quizes did not pertain to the topics that we discussed in class or they were worded in a way that was not relevant to how we discussed topics. I got a fine grade in the class but probably because it was online. These quizes seemed to be copy and pasted from other classes and not proofed.

I'm a physics major pursuing a (potential, I'm declaring soon?) CSSE minor, and Dr. Retik's engineering class has to be one of my favorite classes I've taken so I may want to declare it now. He's the best intersection of great prof and great person - very knowledgeable but also very supportive and understanding. Love him!

One of the worst professors I've had. Very vague grading criteria so you need to be good at reading his mind. Expects you to take a quiz that is meant to be 45 minutes in like 20 minutes. Cannot explain a concept in a proper manner. Jumps from topic to topic. You just hear him talking on and on but don't understand the point he's trying to make.

Great class and professor! Super caring, always helpful if you ask, and really optimistic and understanding. Had him during quarantine and he gave me life - there was never a day I didn't look forward to his class. I also have had Hebrew conversations with him (we both Jewish) in class.
worst grader, and lecturer
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A professor who comes to class with a solid plan. What he will lecture on depends on the reading responses from the students. A few homework assignments are difficult and require material that may have not been taught during lecture. Two midterms (40% total) and a final (20%). May give extra information that is not needed (labeled FYI in lectures).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall amazing teacher. He teaches the course in a way that would make you most successful. If you do everything the class requires and put in your best effort, then you would be really successful in this class. His class is the best possible class you can take for css 142.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This is where you learn what goes on around the coding in industry. He is very knowledgeable and lectures well. Reading, exercises and group activities help you keep up with the material. His exams reflect the level of difficulty of the assignments, no surprises here. His experience in industry comes through in the lectures, great stuff.

Interesting lectures with relevant assignments. Tests reflect work done in the assignments. If you do all the reading, review the lectures you will do well. He provides a lot of real world examples and offers lots of industry knowledge. Alway answers email and makes time to speak with students.

He's a really nice guy, and seems to really care about his students, but his lectures are a complete waste of time, I honestly did not learn anything from his class . He is hard to understand and he doesn't understand half the stuff his students are saying. A lot of busy work and group projects are involved, and he's not very organized.

Im expecting to major in CS , so i needed to do well in this class. However, the midterm 2 hit us hard (i got a 70). Arkady saw this and gave us five points, told us if we did corrections, we would get five more points. On top of this he introduced a project a week before finals, for a hw grade of XC. Good teacher, hw instructions were confusing.
He seems like a caring guy, but is really hard to understand and has bad grammar. For a teacher teaching us presentation and holding discussions, its a real challenge trying to communicate.

Isn't super clear on the criteria he wants for the homework, but he grades so liberally that it doesn't really matter if you understand what you're doing or not. He basically rubber stamps all work except the tests, which are pretty easy if you read the book and his slides. Good grade is attainable with minimal effort.

Arkady Retik lectures a lot. However, his slides get straight to the point on important facts you need to know for exams and quizzes. He also loves to use a lot of visuals in addition to his lecture material as well. Even better, if you disagree with your grade, he lets you appeal and will change your grade if you prove you deserve a better grade.

Not the best lecturer, but overall he's really nice and easy to work with. The group project/assignment guidelines can be hard to understand, but don't hesitate to talk to him and ask for clarification. If you're having any issues with the class, just talk to him - he's very responsive and will work with you. Pretty funny too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Just a really nice guy in general. Lectures can feel really long sometimes but his power points are well organized so if you miss something you can always look at his slides later. Sometimes the directions to the assignments can be a little bit confusing but if you ask him to clarify he will and is open to moving/changing due dates.
He is a good teacher. He explains the topics properly which are important for you to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great professor. He has an accent but it's easy to understand. Lectures are great and  fun. Defiantly would recommend.

All of the assignments in this class were with group projects, so if you get a good group it's fine. Assignment guidelines are unclear and confusing a lot of the time, but are graded leniently. Prof. Retik is very nice and cares about his students. He tells lots of stories about his time working at Microsoft and what it's like in the CS industry.

He is probably the best CS teacher at UWB. He discusses almost everything in class and also has group work towards the end which is graded on effort. He cares about everyone's grades and gives out extra credit!! He curves the tests sometimes. If you are taking CS161 or CS162 to get into the Comp sci major, you should definitely take Mr. Retik.

Arkady is a very nice guy who wants you to learn without you having to stress about your grades 24/7. He lets you use a cheat sheet on all quizzes and exams, so you won't have to memorize a bunch of text. 45% of the grade is based on a group work, so choose people carefully. His TA does most of the grading and it's mostly based on effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Arieh (Arkady) Retik is a GREAT professor. He is by far the best CSS professor at UW Bothell. He cares about your grades and knowledge. Be ready to read a lot. Most of the assignments are group assignments so make sure to be ready to be in a group of 3 other hard workers. This is really important. He grades very fairly and is nice to students.

This professor uses OneNote which lets you study ahead and makes notes the professor writes during teaching a lot more accessible for studying. The professor sometimes makes mistakes with scheduling due dates online but often changes them and you don't get marked down for missing them. There's group cold calling as well. Exams based on group work.

The structure of the class is.. unconventional, to say the least. You're expected to watch lecture videos at home, complete a quiz on the lesson before class, and then class is just worksheets. Then you also have homework based on the lesson, so overall, it's just a lot of work. Attendance is not mandatory; you'd probably learn more alone, anyway.

Y'all are hating, yes he is disorganized but you never have to deal with the consequences of it. He will make mistakes but it will never effect your grade just point them out and he will fix it. He is passionate about his teaching and he is very helpful if you have question. I could not recommend him enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was frustrating. The professor is easily raged, gets irritated over small things like students helping each other or talking after finishing early. He rarely teaches, relying mostly on another professor's videos, and speaks to us like we're in high school. The environment felt tense and unproductive.

Class is highly disorganized with assignments and homework dates getting changed (even changed an exam date). Good person outside of class but a poor teacher and can be a bit passive-aggressive with students.

-Attendance isn't required. 
-Required to watch a video and take notes on worksheets before class.
-Classes include group work. 
-Homework assignments are on MyMathLab.
-Can be disorganized and doesn't always let us know when due dates and lock dates are adjusted.
-Class is easy to pass if you do all of the work.
-Drops the lowest test score.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Worst prof I've had. He doesn't run his own course so he's disorganized. He'll get mad at the students for his disorganization. Ran by lecture videos that you do on your own and he doesn't do anything but complain and make horrible jokes. You practically just show up do group work and that's it, really self taught. Don't recommend at all.

Terribly disorganized professor he'll post assignments the same day that they're due 'cause he forgot to post them earlier He doesn't really understand the content he's teaching. All of the content is taught through lecture videos which are too long for what they are. If you want to do well in this class just teach it yourself from the textbook.

This professor does not teach whatsoever. He gives us Lecture Notes videos, not even created by him btw, and expects us to know the material by the time we are next in class. If you wanna be happy with yourself throughout the entire quarter along with wanting a professor that teaches in class, then do NOT take Andrew Abian.
DOES NOT TEACH, Assigns youtube videos that attempt to teach the coursework.

Great guy and really nice. Enjoys what he does and can ask any dumb question. This goes for any math prof, show your work clearly and precisely or you'll get docked. Follow how he solves them and show it on quiz, exams. Follow practice exams, and your good.
Good professor overall.
Just do the homework. Assignments, lecture vid, and grading system are a little unorganized but if you are competent with OneNote it'll be fine. Very friendly, helpful professor!

He enjoys feeling superior over his students, and will single you out while offering no assistance as a teacher. In my experience he was pretentious, unhelpful, and just plain rude. I wish he had done better, and left his attitude behind.

I took the professor a second time with no other choice. First time I took STMATH 124 he was not good. However, this time, he assign assignments on time and is lenient, makes the test more aligned with the study guides, and responds to students emails better. He is also more lenient when grading. He is better now and not as bad.

Expectation is that you do the lecture notes outside of class using the online lecture videos and then in class you work on problems with people in your group. Class is very group work oriented. He is very nice and will help with questions but will constantly ask if everyone in your group is there before answering the question.

is unorganized sometimes and a little less than tech savvy lol altho genuinely tries his best and course layout is easy to understand. Lectures are before class using online videos which can be a hassle to watch but worth doing, classtime is for group assignments which are super helpful. Midterms allow notecard and are more like unit tests!

Unorganized for sure, and isn't flexible on the class progress if he messes up assignments. Though the class had a very flexible late work policy, and he is a forgiving grader. He also offered extra credit at the end of the quarter. Overall he wants every student to pass.

Although his online lectures aren't so great, the in-class group work does help a lot in solidfying your understanding. Make sure to supplement your learning with youtube courses if the online lectures doesn't make sense for you. Otherwise, homework is frequent but short to get through and typos/errors on the test/quiz earn you extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Group problems in class and teach yourself at home. You watch another professor's videos to learn, which add up to 30 mins. How can students learn everything in only 30 mins?! I spend class doing one singular problem with my group, and he never properly teaches how to do problems. There's barely a study guide, and it's not like the tests at all.

STMATH124
"Forget" to post HW until a couple of hours before the due date. Confuse himself when lecturing. Used lecture videos from another professor that had to be watched outside of class. In class was just working on examples without his help. Took weeks and multiple verbal and email reminders to grade. Study guides not in alignment with exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: THE GOAT. Love Abian. Study his practice quizzes for sure. Overall exams were not bad, though plenty of homework. His class is pretty unorganized but it never impacts you negatively.

Very disorganized, homeworks are often posted hours before they are due. Study guide is not at all like the exam. Great guy, not great at teaching. Relied on another's professors videos after a while. Syllabus was not followed. Take the course if you're fine teaching yourself and on the flow, as it'll be easy for you. Otherwise, seek another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but super disorganized. Almost never posted the homeworks and quizzes on time, and miswrote my grade twice. He does give a lot of partial credit, and the tests are exactly like the study guide.

I took STMATH 124. The professor is a nice person. However, the professor never checks his emails or canvas messages. The professor also sometimes assigns assignments late at night and makes it due early the next day. The professor does not really teach well and is disorganized. I would only recommend this professor if you have no options left.

He forgets to post any homework until just hours before its due. Gives you an anxious fear of missing work. Doesn't actually teach, assumes you've watched hours of another professor's lecture before coming to class. If you haven't, you're screwed. Class consists of doing groupwork after he stumbles through unexplained examples. Disorganized joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take his class. He does not know what he is doing. While the material learned may be easy, his lack of organization and unpreparedness makes the class very difficult. He would tell us the night of our homework being due that we had homework. For your sanity, don't take his class.

Learned primarily through assigned video lectures, very few concepts were covered by the prof. himself. Practice exams were super helpful and similar to real exams. Waited till the last minute multiple times because he forgot to assign homework and prequizzes that were then due the next day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a very nice person (but a little disorganized). Come to office hours! He's willing to help, and available literally right after class. Quizzes were take-home and very easy. Exams were very similar to practice tests. Be prepare to read, sometimes his lecture is hard to understand. As long as you do the work in this class, you'll be fine.

Disorganized. Always starts class late, prints worksheets in class (slowly), gives too much time for group problems, then crams actual instruction into the last minutes of class. Didn't finish teaching the content for the quarter, instead made the last day a pop quiz, telling us to read about what we didn't finish because it's still on the final.
Very Good
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Abian was late for class a lot and seemed unprepared, you need to be prepared to learn on your own. But he is a very easy grader, and he did not require the final be taken for this course!

In a Dif math class now but I miss him so much. Though doesn't really teach and you need to rely on yourself, he was a super easy grader. Homework was more heavy than the tests, it's practically impossible to fail as long as you do the homework. Enjoy it while it lasts

Had him remote for summer B at eight in the morning, and I was expecting the class to suck bc of the timeslot + 4 week rush + these reviews. But it was actually great. He was personable, his lectures and exams were clear and understandable, and he was very understanding about deadlines. No dis but surprised Arian has a higher score than him on here

Abian is really nice as a person but he wasn't the best professor. He doesn't seem to know what he is doing and the class structure is a mess. He uses other professors videos to do the lecture on the homework and then piggy backs off of that in class. It's a lot of group work, he will have you ask your group members first. He is understanding tho

Seems like a nice guy, but he was a terrible teacher. He insists on not giving the answer keys to practice exams. He will change notation from homework to test. He does not go through the types of problems that will be on the test in class. Instead, he opts to waste class time doing things that should be done in announcements or over email. Sloppy.

Going through his class was watching a slow motion train wreck. He had no idea what he was doing so everyday was a learning moment for him as well. His tests were so difficult that they were literally brewed in Satan's pot. I only did well because I relied on the textbook. At some point, playing video games was a more learning experience than class

Good teacher. Spends time going over homework. Sometimes unorganized and if you don't know an answer in class, he might get a bit testy. Lots of time working in groups. I'm not great at math and the lowest score I got on a test was 85. He also drops your lowest test score if you do good on the final. If you do the test reviews you should be good

Overall a great professor. Lectures are written digitally on a computer, lots of group work (allows you to meet new people and familiarize yourself with the class), and homework is all done online. Exams are straight forward. However, he does tend to go over time 5-7 mins! He is very caring and makes himself available outside of class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing man and teacher. Taught me all about Physics and calc and also just life in general. Ive grown so much after meeting this beautiful man with his amazing largish, pointy, long nose.

Word of advice: Don't have a class scheduled immediately after his classes. He lectures up to the end of class and we usually leave 5 minutes late. Other than that he is great at handing out partial credit, will work with you on homework due dates, and overall is very helpful.

Andrew is really tech-savvy and uses all the technology provided to us efficiently. He pushes back due-dates as needed and lessens stress on students as much as he can. He is also knowledgeable and cares about helping you get the grades you want. Highly recommend taking him for 307 and 308

Abian is one of my fav math profs He genuinely cares and makes things as understandable and accessible as possible. He is intelligent, witty, and knows how to teach to people with varying backgrounds. At times he can be disorganized, but he never lets the class fall behind. He encourages group work, and gives quizzes to offset exams. SOLID!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors thus far. He knows his stuff, doesn't make things too confusing and is a genuine person. Make a connection with him and you'll do great. He is a personable person with humor and intelligence. His tests are beyond fair, and he is fair about helping a student if they miss class however he can. Learned a lot!

He's very disorganized. In fact every lecture always ends in him rushing and realizing he's out of time. Some of the hw questions contain material that he didn't teach in class. He does group work but he will humiliate your entire group if someone in your group doesn't know the answer. I could go on but def go to his office hours
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very pretentious teacher, if you dont already know whats going on he will not fill you in. Goes way too fast and doesn't explain. If you dont understand he kinda just brushed you off and hopes your group can help you. But if nobody knows in your group, youre not in a good spot. has crazy attitude and makes you feel dumb for getting wrong answers.

If you take a class with him and have a good knowledge of math, you'll do fine. If you don't, you're out of luck as he is extremely bad at helping students understand material. In my class with him, we have sat there in silence for minutes when he calls on a student who doesn't know how to do an example,and he doesn't prompt or help in any way.
Awesome sometimes goes of topic but that's fine. cute kid. Clear during lectures and is good with computers also grate a lecturing while using  something on a progector. Fun and Funny.

He knows math very well, but he makes the class harder with his lack of organization.  Does examples on the whiteboard, but when he makes a mistake, he'll re-do the entire problem.  When he runs over the end of class, he rushes to finish the problem, and then fails to explain how he got to the answer.

Decent professor, boring but fair. He uses powerpoints which are pretty difficult to learn Diff Eq from but his tests are completely fair and similar to the practice exams he gives. If you understand the HW and study the practice exams, you should be fine
Knowledgeable and approachable for help Straightforward fair grader. Online hw.
is no help when you visit in his office hours

This professor basically has story time where the story is the textbook. His lectures are incredibly boring and don't help you at all with the homework. Assigns online homework that he refuses to help with, or even sympathize about syntax issues. Upon request for more example problems instead of aforementioned story time he blatantly refuses.

He is very unorganized. He would pass out worksheets, but didn't know the answers to them so we couldn't double check.   He writes his lectures on the boards, but may miss something, so will go back to redo it all.  He is very confusing.  He's the type of teacher who won't tell you the answer and will stare at you until you figure it out.
Andrew is a very solid teacher that really knows math... I liked his course set up and found him to be a willing helper regardless of office hours. I recommend him to anyone that is in EE.
Tests were pretty rough, but pretty close to in class examples, homework, and lectures. Flexible enough with homework, will postpone dates if enough people ask. Only real complaints is that

Horrible professor. I've has some bad professors in the past but he is the worst. I generally do well in math but Andrew does an awful job setting up a class. His notes  unorganized and not helpful. Get ready to spend hours reading the textbook and trying to figure things out on your own.

Good class, easy material. Abian made the course as a whole extremely easy. We were behind on learning most of the time but Abian did manage to get all of the important concepts across. The course seem like it could and should be a lot more challenging but none the less the course as a whole is very decent. Do recommend.

Very good course as a whole. Abian went through the material at a reasonable pace, made sure we all understood the concepts and always encourage students to express their opinions. Abian is often behind on grading though other then that the course is good.
I don't know why Professor Abian has so many negative reviews, but I really enjoyed his class. He took the time to explain things by using examples. Overall, he is a really cool professor.

Maybe in the past Professor Abian wasn't the best, but I don't know why anyone would review him that way now. The in-class session has worksheets with written problems that you have to go up to the board to solve. He doesn't give answers to any of the worksheet problems which is very frustrating since exam questions are similar to them compared to the Pearson HW.

Professor Barchechat is great, everyone says attendance is mandatory but its not, he checks your notes every other lecture but you can show anytime. If you email a question he will always answer extremely quickly. His video lectures are meh but if you ask any questions in class or email hell make sure to explain until you understand completely

Avoid this prof if you can. Exams weighted 50-60% of your grade. Attendance is mandatory - he rolls a lottery to check your notebooks every class. Class time is essentially glorified study hall, so be prepared to do much of the learning on your own. He is very stubborn and does not offer any leniency beyond the few dropped quizzes and HWs.

We met once a week, where we would go over a few problems from the homework and do a set of problems. He prerecords lectures which you are expected to watch, does not lecture much in person. Homework is easy as it is all online with multiple attempts, easy to use chegg or something else, answers are all on there. Beware of midterms, they are tough.

If I could rate this professor a 0 I would. A lot of the notes were inconsistent to what was stated in the textbook, there's way too many quizzes that felt fairly irrelevant to what was on tests, the tests were extremely difficult (which is why our class test average was around a 60%, while the other classes were around 85%), among other things.

Doesn't lecture in person. Instead, he uses pre-recorded online videos which you have to watch on your own time. Tons of short quizzes and he checks your notes on these videos at the start of every class. Very generous with partial credit and he knows what he's doing as far as math goes. He believes in letting the student discover things themself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Barchechat goes above and beyond for his students. The people complaining below are only doing so because they don't want to put the effort in to succeed.Whenever I had a question about hw or thought I deserved a higher score on an exam or a quiz he would take my argument seriously. He is receptive to emails and is a caring professor.

Awful Professor! Very strict grading on already very conceptual exams. Attendance is necessary as he has notebook checks, meaning he requires written/typed notes when you arrive. Class can be considered office hours since all of his lessons are on pre-recorded and spends most in-class time having students work on problems. Never gives clear answers

I'm confused as to why they have a 4.0 rating. Attendance mandatory cause he checks if you took notes. No lecture in class- prerecorded videos. Doesn't finish examples in videos. Doesn't believe in giving students answers so you never know if you're right. Never directly answers your question. Class just means working on problems without answers.

Terrible professor. He literally does not teach, and will provide no guidance and act arrogant on top of it. He doesn't provide any solutions and will expect students to be able to answer his questions without any margin of error. His tests are terrible and unnecessarily difficult. Do yourself a favor and avoid this guy at all costs. He is terrible

Attendance is mandatory, you can only miss 2 days before getting a 0 for the whole quarter. You also lose an attendance mark if your notes aren't perfect. His lectures are pre-recorded videos you have to watch at home. Actual in person classes is glorified study hall. Which could be useful if he actually answered questions without being cryptic.

no review sheet and any sort of review we did have he refused to give an answer sheet for us to compare answers. made class proof heavy when its a class also for engineering students who have no need for these proofs. gave us new material the week of the test rather than review material/ let us ask questions on those topics which would be covered.

Responsive in and out of class, very willing to help students out.
Accepts and responds to feedback.

Make sure to take notes on the video lectures.

You'll need a lot of scratch paper...
and to practice solving problems often on your own time.

His lectures are incomplete.  He doesn't fully explain concepts because he wants you to discover it on your own.  Extremely harsh grader.  You get zero points for having the right answer with an explanation that isn't detailed enough.  Almost every quiz needed revision because it is filled with errors and covers things not covered in lecture

Ok yeah the meditation stuff it’s a little weird but I ended up liking it. Super nice prof, explains concepts really well. If you can do the practice you will ace the midterms. Talk to him if you have concerns, always willing to help at end of quarter, and always wants to understand where students are coming from.

Really cool prof, super easy to understand and explains concepts well. Gives really helpful practice exams which help prepare fully for all exams. Gives a bit of extra credit but not to much, but always willing to talk about how to improve in the class. Probably my favorite calc prof so far.

No required participation. But plz, plz, make it to the class, at least once a week. He'll give you a 1-1 help on problem (if and only if you have tried it out, or explain what you're stuck on). Friendly. His tests are heavy. Lots of questions. BUT show your work, he's generous on giving extra credits. Beware of meditation stuff.

Tests are very hard, and they are very conceptual. The class average for the tests are around a 73% after an almost 10% curve. The lectures are kinda boring and could be pretty confusing. I studied a lot by myself watching the lectures in mymath lab, which could be a great resource for people.

When I first saw his ratings, I was honestly intimidated but I am very glad that I took him for math 124. He makes sure you understand. He promotes a very cooperative environment in class. This class is not easy but if you meet him for office hours, ask him questions, listen in class, and give your best efforts, you will do fine.
This is really an easy and a relaxed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This instructor is really amazing. I took his multivariable calculus class during this summer. He gives you two chances to take both Midterm and Final (First chance is a practice exam).
Lowest Quizzes and Lowest Online Homework dropped! He is the best instructor Ive ever had!

Professor Barchechat is perfectly well at online teaching style. His quizzes, tests, and HW are both in MyMathLab. Especially on tests, he gives you two times (Highest grade submitted). If you work hard on his class, practice outside of his class, and review his PowerPoint notes (not from textbooks), you'll be definitely fine.
Wont give clear info on work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you have the option, pick the other teacher that teaches Math 144. I took him during the pandemic and it was awful. He prerecorded all his lectures and tried to fly through them so he could be done working as soon as possible. The homework assignments are super easy compared to his tests/quizzes. DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY ON HIM BEING YOUR TEACHER!

I had him for spring quarter 2020, during the Covid pandemic. He is much less helpful and understanding than the other professors. He is VERY stubborn, and doesn't seem to really even read the emails you send expressing concerns, let alone care about them. He has been accommodating at times, however, but the bad far outweighs the good imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't know if its because this is the first time he has ever done an online class due to the pandemic, his teaching style sucks!!! He makes everything super complicated then it needs to be and his lectures has nothing to do with his exams. I did not go to any of his lectures through Zoom and definitely waste of my $4k tuition.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very poor examples and explanations; poor use of class time in a course where good time management makes a major difference. Additionally, DO NOT READ THE MANDATORY TEXTBOOK: YOU WILL FAIL. I REPEAT, YOU WILL FAIL IF YOU STUDY FROM THE TEXTBOOK. None of his tests cover many (if any) concepts discussed in the book or homework. Take notes!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dont take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I did not like his teaching style at all! I love math but he made this class extremely difficult for me. He only shows one example and expects you to do the rest on your own, his homework does not reflect on the tests. does not give you enough to help prepare you for the tests. I had to do a lot of self study and even went to class everyday :(

Professor Barchechat might seem intimidating at first, but he's actually really helpful. His tests are kind of difficult, but during his lectures, he explains concepts really well, so if you pay attention then, read the chapter before class or even after the lecture, and use the homeworks as practice, the class is fairly easy.

Barchechat is a pretty good calc professor, but sometimes his lectures are a bit confusing or incomplete. That being said he is extremely helpful while doing in class work and doesn't make you feel like an idiot for not understanding something. Currently taking him for STMATH125 and would take him again for 126 if he taught it this winter.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Had him for UW in the High School calculus last year. Tests could be easier and assignments/worksheets more thorough, but class overall is fine. He's really nice too.

Although this teacher is caring, his teaching style sucks, is a VERY tough grader, and hw does not reflect the tests at all. He hastily gives 1 or 2 examples of a concept on the board and gives a a bunch of exercises. He expects us to just understand. No one feels like calling him over for help at every single step. I learned more from self study.
Very hard teacher and for no reason, plus makes you memorize all the formulas unlike the other calculus teachers.

Matrix Algebra is a very abstract concept and it is fairly difficult to understand some topics. He teaches the topic pretty well and is very accessible during office hours. his feedback on tests is informative and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awful teacher, and I do not say that about teachers almost ever. He gives packets every day with a few examples and rushed through them on the white board. he actually laughs when something is hard for us and is VERY condescending, making sarcastic and rude comments. He doesn't input any grades because "we are math students and we should do it". NO
Great teacher, very clear, understands the subject (matrix algebra) is confusing, and tries to make it so everyone understands.

I'm taking calculus 3 in uwb with this professor and it's actually my first quarter ever in uwb.  He cares a lot about every students and the way he explains things is inspiring me to pull off better approach to problems that he goes over in the class.  I feel like I can deal with any problems I see from the homework without facing any difficulty.

His way teaching does not really fit my study style. He just writes everything on the board and let you take notes. I do not think he gives students enough time to think about the examples. Also, he makes hard quizzes and tests. And those quizzes can decide whether you fall or not. However, it is almost impossible to get really high grade unless you are the top 3 students. The average grade is about 65 percent for my class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a very great professor. He wouldn't hesitate to answer mathematical questions. He really cares about the understanding of the concepts and will guide you through step by step without missing any details. He provides an example each chapter/section during Lecture which helps when doing homework. I recommend barchechat for any math course
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Mad whiteboard skillz

The style of the class is very different. He lectures for about 10-15 minutes then gives you problems to work on by yourself the rest of class and he is there to answer questions and check that you did them correctly. Though different, this was a very effective way to get students to do the learning in the classroom rather than outside of it.
Great teacher, knows his stuff.
A fine lecturer who gives tough exams.

Overall, a solid professor. He's tough, but fair. A core part of his class are worksheets which he provides, but he refuses to give any solutions to them. However, you are absolutely free to ask questions and send emails to him to check your work. In other words, while a little inconvenient, definitely fair. I personally enjoyed his dry humor too.
best math teacher I've ever had. So patient with people who don't understand what's going on in class!  tests aren't that bad if you study your notes

Barchechat rocks! Funny, awesome teaching style, incredibly helpful. Always will answer questions to make sure everyone understands the material. Ask him for helpclarity if you need it. Master solving the problems he gives in class, and you will ace the quizzes and exams. He grades harshly, but curves, so it's more than fair. Chili Pepper.

He moves at a good pace through the material, so class is neither boring nor overwhelming.  He gives you in-class problems to work on to enhance learning. Ask him for help if you need it! You will get out of this class what you put into it. Don't expect to pass just by doing hw and sitting in class observing. Do the in class problems, ask for help.

His lecture is really clear and he knows what he is talking about. Tests are not easy though he curves. Not easy to get 4.0, but still will get a fair enough grade. Homework are not too much, but not little for sure. Would take him again for sure!

Homeworks were sometimes longer than necessary. He does try to challenge you, however the exams are much easier than the homework. Plus, he lets you have a half sheet(midterms) full sheet(final) of notes to use if the class requests. This saved my exam grades. He often ends class early, but sticks around for questions. He also curves the exams.
NEVER TAKE HIM!!!!!!!!!!
Awful. Avoid at all cost. No homework feedback, answers. Simply marks off grades if didn't get the answer correct, even though the process is correct.
Awful period(.). Do NOT take him.
The worst professor in the world. Doesn't care if you learn or if you understood. Cares way too much about yoga and less about students! DO NOT TAKE HIM!
His grading is fair and he is clear about what we need to learn. Great professor overall.

Alex Barchechat is there to make sure you understand the material. He does so by going through wild examples and giving rigorous tests. But he always grades on a good curve. Do not, I repeat, DO NOT whine about not understanding material in any class he teaches if you won't raise your hand when you first feel lost. Ask him. He'll help. He's great!
Great professor! The class is relatively easy and with a good amount of practice anyone should get a decent grade.

The class was challenging and requires lots of visualization, but Barchechat goes through the material at a steady pace and allows a generous amount of class time to practice problems. The class is pretty much half lecture and half practice time and during the practice Barchechat is extremely helpful.  Definitely recommend.

Took Calc II with him last winter. Barchechat is not only an expert at integration, he was also extremely effective at teaching the subject. His tests are challenging but if you pay attention in lectures and practice the problems you should have no problem getting a good grade. Fantastic and definitely would take him again!

Brilliant Mathematician.. who is passionate about the field. Happy to have been a part of his class, and would highly recommend him to anyone who is serious about becoming better in math, but would discourage anyone who is looking to do minimums and skate to just cut a grade.... bad format for that mentality.

Math 324 is a pretty brutal class in general.  Concepts are hard, but most people should be able to grind through it.  He will answer questions you have to try to make things more clear to you.  The tests are not like homework problems so to prepare for them really try to understand and conceptualize them.

I really liked the set up of the class. For about 30mins, he would lecture, then give us a worksheet to work on. Then pause the worksheet and move on, lecture for another 30 minutes, and let us keep working on the worksheet. The back and forth helped not fall asleep during the 2 hour class, and the practice really helped solidify what you learned.
Online homework is aweful, completely useless.  In class worksheets are quite helpful.
He got through all of the required material (and more) in a timely manner, and was still able to convey the ideas to students. Very big on theory, which is expected for a matrix algebra class.

He has a generous amount of office hours where you can come ask questions about anything and he gives a lot of effort to make sure you actually understand your question before leaving his office. His quizzes and tests are definitely a challenge. He sets the standard high for UWB students, which I like! As long you put in the effort you will do OK.
Difficult material but he explained it well and had an effective teaching style, lots of hands-on work instead of just lecturing
he's so smart that each text would not be easy. but he gave really good lecture and extra help. i like him, he's great !!

Honestly, Multivariable Calculus is a hardcore, no matter whom you take. Alex is always there to help you. In his class, you are expected to spend half of the class taking lecture, half of the time doing practice, if you have questions, then hands up.  Please be aware that if you are shy to rise your hands, this is not your class. Test aren't easy

What an awesome teacher! His lectures are well worth your time. Doing the homework is required to get a good grade in the class. His lectures only cover the basics and the homework is required to have in depth knowledge. His test are very fair. They test you on basic knowledge but also have hard questions that can be worked through during the test.

Barchechat expects you to know what you are doing and his tests are hard, but he will never test you on something you haven't been taught in class. You get your money's worth with him.  His homework assignments can be ridiculously long sometimes, but you only get one per week, so it evens out if you don't wait until the last minute to start them.

Professor Barchechat demonstrates his thorough command of mathematics topics in each calculus lecture he gave when I had him for calc IV. I enjoyed his classes very much and I found his assessments to be fun and challenging.
Dr. Barchechat is thoroughly knowledgeable in Calculus IV and gave great  notes. Reading the text was imperative.
Easiest professor ever!!!!!!! No way you can fail. Dont even try!!!! :) Good Luck!!!!!
Best math professor I've ever had. I was initially intimidated by the subject but he taught it sooo well. I learned so much in his class. Do the work, listen to the lectures, ask questions.

Barchechat, is a awesome professor. Hes extremely clear with his expectations for class and for exam questions. While he can be picky at times he does so, that you truly understand the concept. He teaches mostly through in class worksheets that are extremely helpful. He always willing to give help. He just wants you to have given effort beforehand

Alex is a pretty cool professor. His exams and exam grading were brutal, but fair. The homework is online and expect to spend more than 4 hours per assignment. It's really difficult to earn an A, but Multivariable Calculus is supposed to be hard.

The first math class I have taken after 3 years of not being exposed to the subject.  After taking his class, I knew I was in college.  I was able to pass my past math courses with flying colors, but he dove into the subject deeply and covered as much as possible.  I loved the class and it has changed my perspective on math.  Respect to this man.

I had three classes with Dr. Barchechat.  He's old school, the way it should be.  You really gotta earn that 'A'.  That's how college should be.  Not this watered down, new-age "everyone's a winner" philosophy where teachers give out A's like candy.  That type of grading is what's undermining the whole system.  I give Barchechat mad respect.

Tests were exceptionally hard, professor requires wileyplus homework to be done in comp notebook which is turned in. uses hallett book, which is sometimes off course with lectures, very bad book. intimidating personality,  I do not recommend this professor.
This teacher has the toughest tests ever, his class is hard. It totaly don't recomend anyone taking him.

He is the hardest teacher I have ever had, his test is hard. The average is 50% in his class that means most like half of the class will fail. Usualy I am a A person in my math class but in his class I hardly get the average. I always feel like he enjoy when his exams is hard and the average is low. I will never ever take his class again.
super helpful!! His explanation is clear and vivid. Class attendance is not mandatory and could postpone or bring forward the exam date. Just like him!

I have nothing but bad things to say about this guy, if you have the option, really consider taking your course with someone else. I ended up failing the quarter & ruining my transcript because of him. Didn't sympathize with me at all. He made me feel extremely uncomfortable. He half teaches. Major disappointment over the summer
Really Helpful... but really wants clarity and intrepetations... a lot of group work

I have had Alex for 4 quarters. In my opinion he is a really good teacher. His lectures are clear and well thought through. However, he does make sure you understand the subject well before you leave his class. So yes he is a tougher math teacher.... he likes clarity.

Hey is a very tough teacher but always very fair.  If you don't understand something the best thing to do is go to his office hours.  The one on one is very helpful.  Had him for three quarters and have learned a lot from him.

He was okay. Very picky about how things were done and isn't very lenient. I spent three quarters with this teacher and felt like my math skills were no good, even though I have done well in everything else. If you ask a a lot of questions, you may get a good answer out of him, but he is very hard to adapt to.

Great professor to have, if you lock in and talk you'll get a great grade. Showing up matters. because a ton of your grade is being there and talking. She tries to really get her points across, class only meets once a week, the other "class" is just online readings and videos.

Professor Follmer is quirky and straightforward. You will succeed in her classes if you participate and follow instructions. Lots of opportunity for extra credit through participation that can bump your grade up to 0.2 GPA points. Quizzes open note and online.

this class was fun and interesting, and I liked professor follmer. class was just short lectures and then class discussions. participation & attendance required for points but its worth coming bc some of the convos get interesting. overall shes nice, workload is straight forward, and all quizzes online ;)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: First of all, attendance being mandatory for this class in insane, and she is not willing to make it work with you. During storm, when even UWB got closed, a big tree fell on my driveway blocking my way out, so I had to miss class. she said I purposely skipped class and denied helping me earn those attendance points.

The biggest waste of time I've had in a class following high school. It feels like the entire class is made up fluff, where no one learned anything. We took a Kahoot and you could see her visibly stressing due to no one knowing any of the answers from her made up lectures. Spent the entire class doing some boring simulation that lasted 10 weeks.

If you want to completely waste your money and time, take this class! Follmer teaches you absolutely nothing on this subject or how to work in teams at all. Forced us to buy the weirdest, most useless and pointless simulation that we were doing throughout the quarter, but then when asking for your opinion on it would straight up disagree with you.

This is actually the worst class I ever took in my life. Her instructions are never clear, ever. She always changes what she wants you to do. She does not teach the class at all, all you do is activities like "marshmallow tower". She has a completely wrong idea of this course's purpose, and does not explain her grading at all.

Dr. Follmer is an easy but fair grader. I took her for BUS 462 Negotiations. Here is what you need to know.?
Show up to class, you can get half credit for not showing up and emailing but she values participation a lot.
Make sure to follow her rubrics on writing assignments, its not hard and you'll get 90% or better.
She's really chill.

The best professor I've taken. Very organized, no midterm, one hw, and quiz a week. If you show up to class and participate, you'll have no problem getting an A. Take her!! Cares more about your opinion than if you're right or wrong.

Overall an easy class, Focused mainly on opinion. Consists of a quiz and a couple homework questions every week and a final exam. Engagement points are earned in class or through discussion post. A lot of students said that she likes to cut people of when they are talking, be ready for that. Otherwise, class should not be hard.
Mandatory to talk in class to get full engagement points.

Professor Follmer's TA did a lot of the grading and it was obvious she wasn't really looking at what you wrote, she would just read the first few sentences. If you get a grade that doesn't make sense you should ask her about it because she will probably change it. Participation matters - you need to talk a lot in class to get a decent grade.
I hope the professor takes it easy, it's not that serious, it's a prerequisite class.
Good prof, super super nice, would take again

I really enjoyed this class! I felt like the material was very engaging and the workload was super easy to manage. If you do the work the quizzes/ tests are easy. My only complaint was ambiguity around expectations for the final. She graded it harshly without setting clear expectations.
Unclear and vague final presentation/paper and harshly grades such paper. Considering the final is worth a large majority of points its very frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's very knowledgeable in her field and does a good job at teaching the dynamic between the humanities and the environment and what it means to begin with. She deserves valor for sure, and just come to class prepared by skimming the material before hand and you'll be fine. Also pay attention to the rubrics for the assignments and all's good.
She was great!! I took her and Cynthia Chang's combined bcore class fall 2024 and it was a good decision. If you're looking for a fun bcore with reasonable workload, then it's perfect :)

Jennifer is great. Very sweet and easy to talk to. Class can be demanding at times but if you ask for help she'll explain everything you need to do well on assignments. Doesn't assign that much reading which is nice. Attendance is basically required for your participation grade but she's understanding if you can't attend and gives make-up work.

Not just a great teacher but a genuinely open hearted person. Jennifer is *SO* in tune with students' needs and very easy to talk to. She cares about the future, and it shows in her class! An incredible class.
Very interesting lecture. Highly recommend taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is interesting and Jennifer is a great teacher and person. She may seem tough at first but she knows the material well and wants you to get a lot out of it! Lectures and activities are fun. Go to class, or else you'll get docked participation points!
Awesome class! Jennifer cares so much about students and is ready and willing to support them when anything comes up. I loved the assignments, and each week I came looking forward to class.
Seems like a great teacher but the material for the portfolio class in IAS was pointless. She did her best though.

Jennifer seemed intimidating at first like others said and can be hard on you, but it's because she wants you to do well. It's her way of caring about you and it's a blessing to have. I'm a much better writer because of her and found her to be easy to talk to in 1:1 settings. If you go to class and try your best you will do great!

Good teacher but you seriously need to go to class. Both to get a good participation grade and understand what she's looking for in assignments. She can be intimidating at first, but is actually very friendly and approachable, and gives very thorough feedback on work. The feedback can come off as harsh but she's just telling the truth.

I took 3 classes with her and she's great. If you're the type of person who shows up to class and turns your assignments in on time, you'll get a high grade. Well organized, generous grader but never gives 100%. Expect 2 readings per week, 5 reading response papers (650 words min) per quarter, plus a final project. Always gives thoughtful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class seems hard at first but Jennifer (prefers her first name) is so kind and gives lots of really helpful feedback on work. You kinda need to attend to do well, but this shouldn't be as much of a problem as it is - YOU ARE IN COLLEGE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She gave me a really high grade, but I always attended and participated. She seemed "fake-nice." The subject matter was interesting and I got a lot out of it, but I just never trusted her. I wouldn't take a class with her again. She just rubbed me the wrong way. RMP should bring back "skip class? you won't pass" as a tag bc it's true for her.

This class is interesting but Jennifer really doesn't teach it effectively. Seems charismatic/likable at first but is actually rather passive-aggressive and nagging. Talks way too much about herself in lectures. Only wants things done her way. Likes students who participate and attend. I will say, though, that the final project is fun.

If you get on her good side - AKA go to class, participate, and do the work - this class is fairly easy. If you're on her bad side, she'll be harsher. I've seen both sides depending on the students. If it's in your major, take her and hope that she likes you. You'll learn important stuff even if she's demanding and kind of a windbag.

I don't like how her class is set up. It's an elective class so it should be fun but it's filled with an insane amount of reading. The bi-weekly reading responses aren't easy to write down either because she is a tough grader on those assignments and they matter a lot. Lastly, if you miss class your grade goes down because of participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a hard grader, but I really enjoyed her class. The assignment prompts helped me produce writing I normally wouldn't have written. I loved the readings. If you don't skip class, you'll miss out on important info, especially how to do well on assignments/projects. She really cares about what she's doing and what we get out of the class.

I was in the Climate Anxiety class last year as a major requirement. I wouldn't say Professor Atkinson was terrible, but she wasn't great either. Readings are interesting and assignments are reasonable. Activities can be a waste of class time. If you don't attend class (without a reason to not be there) she will dock your participation grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I thought environmental ethics was going to be fun. It was just boring. There were 6 different books for the class that she expected you to read in a few class periods. Not a fan of her lecture style or activities. She likes students that suck up to her and/or participate a lot, and picks on students that skip class.

Definitely one of the most caring, educated, and helpful professors in IAS. She assigns readings and then creates weekly assignments based on those readings in class, which helps with understanding them and getting to hear your classmates. Great feedback, and also great discussions in class. ATTEND because you will lose points if you don't!
I think she grades particularly hard for essays, but is a wonderful teacher nonetheless. Concepts are easy but grading and assignments could be hard at times.

WOW. I am in her class this quarter and I am impressed by her dedication to changing the way we think about climate change and the related emotions. The activities and assignments are interesting and relevant. I'd say these ratings are accurate and I hope I can take her again!

Not the easiest class, but this teacher is ALWAYS here to support you. She's very kind and always willing to talk. Assignments can be stressful coupled with the readings, but her lectures basically give you hints. PLEASE ATTEND CLASS - she exclusively teaches in-person and does not post lectures, so it's gonna be rough if you're behind.

Jennifer is a great teacher, but definitely caters to a certain type of student. If you don't like working with peers, don't take the readings/workload seriously, or don't attend class, her classes will be hard. Overall interesting class with a teacher who really cares about your learning.
She is very sweet and cares a lot about students. Her lectures are fun and engaging. I felt educated and engaged which I can't say about all my professors. Thank you Jennifer for a good class.

Her assignments are rather challenging but the class is still a wonderful classroom experience. She is so sweet. Go to class because it affects your participation grade (unless you have illness, etc.).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: I had quite a difficult time deciphering between assignments due to the difference between what was said on Canvas and what she told us in class, but otherwise Enviro Ethics was a great class. Very nice teacher, awesome readings and lectures, quick grading and excellent feedback, responsive to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Jenny cares about the work she's doing and will inspire you to think critically about your daily life and its relation to the environment. I was a psychology major and found a lot of relevant information that informed my intended career. Make sure you attend: not only is participation graded but also the homework will be addressed every week.

The class was pretty straightforward and enjoyable. Lots of readings but they're all interesting, and as long as you do the assignments, attend, and participate, you will pass with an A. She really cares a lot about your learning.

To put it simply: she is incredible! Not only are her lectures engaging but she is truly one the kindest, most compassionate, and understanding teachers I have had. She will make herself available to support you in any capacity both in & out of class. Easy to get an A if you attend (THIS IS IMPORTANT for your participation grade!) and do the work.

AMAZING professor! She really cares about each and every one of her students. She has a big heart and a passion for education. Thank you so much for the being the best teacher EVER for BCORE Dr. Atkinson!

WOW! Environmental ethics was the best class I've taken at UWB! This professor may teach a hard subject to talk about, but she just has so much enthusiasm and passion that she makes the class worth it. Not the hardest grader but there is a lot of work, so it's important to stay on top of things. Very approachable and encouraging.

Among the best teachers I've ever had! Very friendly with students; interacts with them outside class too. She tries to make classes interesting by promoting student involvement and discussion. She's clear, organized and knowledgeable about her subject. Readings were amazing. You kinda have to attend because of how she grades participation.

Dr. Atkinson was awesome and very kind. Gives very helpful feedback on writing. Concepts and reading material are super interesting. You will work often with classmates, but there are some great lectures too. Not an easy A but the class is straightforward enough that it's achievable. I would take her again in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Atkinson is an excellent lecturer. You can tell she is passionate about the topics that she teaches and really wants students to learn. If you're in her class, you HAVE to attend or your participation grade will drop significantly. I really enjoyed having her as a professor!

Jennifer is very nice and is a great teacher too. She talks really fast, because she's enthusiastic about the material. Not super hard to follow along. She assigns interesting readings and films and is just really passionate about having us learn. Writing assignments can be confusing at times, but she can answer any and all questions you may have.
She is one of the best professors I ever had. Will go above and beyond to help you succeed in and outside of the classroom.

Jennifer is awesome! Not only does she have life experience that supports what she's teaching about, but she is really flexible when events come up in your schedule and is always open to discuss assignments and give you the most meaningful outcome.

I love Prof. Atkinson! She gives you lots of freedom on assignments and gives incredibly useful feedback. She is nice, a great lecturer who encourages collaboration between students, and always assigns writing that is very interesting and fun to do. Reading material is extremely interesting, even if dull at times. Would definitely take her again!

Jennifer was very helpful and always - and I mean ALWAYS - willing to work with students. She is probably the best lecturer in IAS. She does expect a lot of engagement in-class and on Canvas, but if you keep up with the readings you'll be fine with that. Very flexible and creative assignments.

I've taken three classes with this professor. Kept coming back because she was AMAZING. She encourages thoughtful discussions and is very kind and easy to talk to as well. For this specific course, she allowed a lot of creative liberty on assignments/projects. As long as you show up and put a fair amount of effort in, you'll get an A.

Took this class just for credits in my final quarter and I was stunned by how much I loved it. She gives clear and interactive lectures with lots of space for student input and discussion. Lots of readings, some of them dense, but she discusses them before the papers are due. Final project has a lot of freedom. Great class and teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's a really caring and considerate professor and I'd definitely recommend taking her for any class. Her lectures can drag a bit, but she always finds ways to make them interesting. She genuinely wants to see students do well and is easy to please for an A.

Jennifer is an amazing, caring teacher! Even in online environments, she worked hard to create a sense of community where every student felt like they had a voice. Her grading is fully based on your effort, so engage with the course materials and contribute to class. Attendance is important because of how she grades participation.

Great source of knowledge, very well-respected in her field, and always willing to make time to discuss ideas presented in the readings and in class. Cares so much about students and their learning. There may be some heavier weeks, especially right in the middle of the quarter, but if you put an honest effort into all the work, you will get an A.

Professor Atkinson is a kind and engaging teacher who cares about your learning. She's got some major achievements in environmental studies under her belt, and co-INVENTED the concept of "eco-anxiety." She assigns great reading material and facilitates some great discussions with her questions. Honestly life-changing.

Jennifer is a wonderful teacher and scholar. Her willingness to be honest while still providing a comprehensive course is astonishing. Environmental Studies and Environmental Humanities are naturally depressing fields yet she finds many ways to encourage and support students to keep moving forward. I am truly happy to have been in this class.

Immediately caught my attention as someone who's really passionate about what she does. She did a great job generating active discussions about the readings, which were extremely interesting, and provided useful real-world examples to clarify concepts.

I can only say that other reviewers are right. Jennifer is amazing in every way. A great human being and a fantastic teacher and scholar. I've taken classes with all the other 5/5-rated IAS profs: Gardner, Dana, Krabill, Cram. I loved them all. Then I took Atkinson. My life changed. I am not kidding! She is a truly unique, exceptional professor.

Wonderful teacher! Really blew my mind! You can't imagine that she's as good as the reviews say, until you end up taking a class with her. She has great lectures and activities, and is a kind, caring person once you get to know her. Take a class with her if you're in IAS. She can - and probably will - change the way you view environmental crises.

This was my favorite class at UWB. You do need to attend because of the participation requirement including in-class activities. Jennifer is a really nice lady and lectures with passion. Weekly activities and assignments based on the readings, with occasional film viewings, and a final with lots of freedom. Also, she brought food to class twice.

Jennifer is a really sweet and caring lady, very considerate of students and their needs. She gives REALLY good feedback and advice. The course material was daunting but she made it very accessible. She created a really friendly environment for the class. Take any class with her that you possibly can.

A fantastic class. Everyone I know enjoyed it. I learned a LOT about philosophy and how it's applied to environmental issues, and feel like I'm a much better writer because of the way Atkinson taught. She cares so much about students! It felt refreshing to be in her class.

She was the first prof at this school to really let me speak my mind and express myself. She gives great feedback, is an amazing lecturer and great at building class community, and cares about giving students the learning experiences they want. Like the other reviews say, attendance is mandatory because of how she grades your participation.

Jennifer always has something to teach you and you can tell she cares about your learning. She's easy to pay attention to, very kind, doesn't pile a bunch of unnecessary BS work, and she's...pretty? Idk if I can say that. Attendance is important because of how she grades participation. Strongly recommend taking a class from her.
