Jennifer is a wonderful teacher! Extremely upbeat, kind, and inspirational, and she works hard to make all students feel welcome. She opens your eyes to a lot of important issues, and her class makes you think and reflect on your own life and experiences.

It's easy to do well if you attend, do the work on time, and participate. She is dedicated to honest and supportive feedback, and is a very kind person who is extremely passionate about what she does. Lots of interesting readings and creative prompts for assignments. Lots of "participation" points are based on attendance.

Jennifer is a great teacher in that she is kind, enthusiastic, always communicates clearly and effectively, and truly cares about our learning. In all her classes (I also took 356) there is heavy emphasis on working with peers. She gives excellent feedback on writing. I got a lot out of her classes, so glad I got to work with her twice!

I will definitely take her again if I can. She is sweet, kind, energetic, and understanding, all of which are great. She values your engagement with the material any way that you can and is willing to work around prompts to give you a meaningful outcome, like another review here says. Highly recommend.

Jenny is F'ing awesome. She's got a lot of energy and joy which really makes the class engaging, and cares a lot about students. I got a 3.7 and I'm happy with that because while my assignments weren't perfect they reflected real-world issues I'm passionate about and she showed me how I can still learn meaningfully without perfection as a goal.

Absolutely one of the most amazing professors at UWB. She is one of the few people who I felt has truly cared, and in her class and beyond I felt supported in what I want to pursue. Her lectures were amazing, readings were super interesting. One of the few must-takes at UWB!

She is the best teacher I've had in a long time. Great lectures, great readings, great feedback on work, and really cares about your learning. This class (environmental ethics) gave me practical ways to improve the world, my life, and the lives of others. Wonderful experience and I can't think of a classmate who DIDN'T like it.

Jennifer is an excellent instructor. She has an unconventional way of teaching, but she really cares. Her support throughout the quarter was unparalleled to any other professor I've had here, she gave me confidence to advocate for my learning and give myself the most creative and meaningful outcomes on assignments. Highly recommend.

Dr. Atkinson is hands down the best professor in IAS. Lectures are extremely engaging and there's never a dull moment with her, readings are fascinating and not that hard, and she's a fair enough grader if you show effort. She is also super caring about your learning and success, even outside of class, and is very approachable and easy to talk to.

Dr. Atkinson is so nice! She cares so much and really wanted us to all pass! There's a lot of group work and a few reading responses but it's all manageable. You get docked participation points if you skip class, so attendance is important here!

Jennifer is passionate about what she does, and as a result she's an amazing teacher. She is organized, really invested in your learning, and assigns some amazing readings and it's helpful that she always goes over them in class BEFORE the reading responses are due. There's lots of group work. Also, her podcast and her website are really good.

Brilliant teacher with a ton of real-world experience in environmental activism so you can tell she isn't a poser. Extremely kind and cares so much about students. It's nice that she is willing to work around and reformat assignments for you to give you the most creative and meaningful outcome. She allows you to express any opinions you have.

Jennifer is passionate and enthusiastic about environmental studies. She's always ready to help whenever you need it. There is a lot of reading, but it's all super interesting. The papers are really fun to write as well! I would definitely recommend this class if anybody has any interest in environmental studies.

I took two online classes with Atkinson and loved everything about them. She is a very good lecturer and you can tell that she is passionate about what she is doing. She gives really helpful feedback on writing assignments. Do your work and contribute and you'll be fine. She is genuinely one of the best teachers here.

Dr. Atkinson is amazing. Truly one of the best professors in IAS and at UWB in general. Every assignment has a purpose, no busy work. Lectures with passion. Always willing to answer questions. Extremely invested in her students and their success, and easy to talk to. A lot of material but no tests or quizzes, only essays and a final group project.

Dr. Jen is a sweetheart, a great lecturer, and is willing to let you work around and reformat assignments to give you the most meaningful outcomes. The readings are phenomenal. I'm so glad I took this class.

Incredibly interesting class and the professor is an amazing lecturer. Readings are very interesting. Her expectations were very clearly stated on each assignment and thus it was very straightforward. She's a quick grader and gives really detailed feedback. One of those courses that REALLY makes you think. She was very approachable and encouraging.

Jennifer was always super enthusiastic about lectures and made learning enjoyable. She explained concepts very clearly and was easily accessible. Gives really helpful feedback on writing. The one bad thing I can say is that she sometimes took a few days to upload recordings of lectures, but this is not a big deal if you're attending in person.

Professor Atkinson really cares about students and their learning. She is very passionate about her area of study and incredibly knowledgeable. Material is interesting, lots to learn in a short time but she goes over it well in class. Reading responses are due after everything on them is discussed so take good notes if you were confused by any.

If you have the chance, please take a class with Prof. Atkinson! I took her BIS 345 Environmental Literature class and it was one of the best classes I have ever taken. She is very kind, open, and communicative, and her lectures and readings are super engaging. She honestly makes you WANT to participate and get to know her better!

Jennifer is a really knowledgeable, kind, and outgoing woman who loves what she teaches and loves her students. She encourages students to be very self-expressive and take creative risks while at the same time helping them develop an identity through their writing. She is very supportive and always inspires students to put in their best effort.
Good teacher, very talkative. Just go to class, skim the readings a little bit and you'll be fine. It seems like a lot of work up front but it really isn't a huge work load. Compelling too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Atkins is a great teacher totally recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Atkinson is a really knowledgeable, kind teacher who loves what she teaches and teaches what she loves. This class does require a couple of hours of work outside of class, but as long as you focus on what the assignment asks for and nothing else, you'll minimize the effort you put in and maximize your grade. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Atkinson is a great and out-going professor. I had her for the BIS 499 course, in which she was clear on grading criteria, gave helpful feedback, and just generally very friendly and helpful. I was not expecting to learn new material and such because this is a standard course meant for the IAS exhibition/graduation, but I definitely recommend her.

The amount of information that Jennifer throws at you is a bit overwhelming. You are expected to read so much it's ridiculous. I stopped doing the readings about 1/3 of the way in because it was impossible to keep up.

Very nice! I loved when she would lecture! The stuff she taught was very interesting. She is definitely my favorite so far. I felt like she got to know me well. And i thought she was funny. She is a little strict sometimes and may seem intimidating but shes very kind.
I loved her. I wish all teachers could be like her. The reading was interesting, she's really smart and funny, and their tests are straight-forward. I would love to take her class again.

LOVE LOVE LOVE this professor!!! Do yourself a favor and take her class! As long as you do the required work and show up to class you will get a high grade. She keeps the class very interesting and informative. I will definitely take another one of her classes!
Just a great, enthusiastic and smart professor who really knows how to communicate with students.  The reading is not overwhelming but you absolutely must keep up.  No surprises.

Extremely clear of what she wants. There are no surprises on exams. She tells you beforehand, you just may need to study and come to class to get all of your info. Grades attendance. Pop quizzes every week, maybe.  Approachable. Cares about what she teaches. Not too difficult if you show up, take notes, READ, & study.
She is so sweet, but she be asking things and we were like what? I definitely did not like the book she assigned us -.- ! But other than that she is pretty awesome!
She is just a fun person to learn from which really is helpful.

Jennifer is one of the best professor ever.  She knows how to teach and always try to avoid the boring lecture.  She always use interesting youtube to demonstrate the knowledge.  Test  is kind of challenge but her class is worth to take it.  Go FOR IT!!!!

Jennifer is one the best professors and teachers I've ever come across. She could make a brick interesting. She's passionate, enthusiastic, young and extremely approachable. She cares about what she's doing and how well you do. I've taken 3 of her classes and wish I could take more. Amazing professor.
She speaks really well, and is easy to follow in her lectures. She is also very approachable, and helpful.

Atkinson is a fabulous teacher. Very approachable, very helpful, very nice. She's passionate about her field, and her enthusiasm makes class enjoyable. The workload is heavy on reading/writing, but it us a literature class...I would definitely take another one of her classes.

Jennifer Atkinson is an awesome professor. Read the books (she's pretty good about not assigning things that are boring), involving yourself in the "close readings" counts as participation and be really detailed or long winded in your journal (it isn't due till the end of the quarter!) and you'll be JUST fine.

Jennifer is extremely helpful, willing to take as much or as little time as the class needs to truly appreciate the material. Her classes are discussion based, guiding the class along the material without constricting the students. Grading is flexible and very fair. If you are even mildly interested in talking a lit class, this is the one to take!

I had a flipped format class but, honestly content wasn't too bad. Dr. Stiber answered any and all questions all the time and in office hours as well. The quizzes and homework weren't too bad but the tests always felt like 2x hard then what we did in class. But, I think now I shoulda done the review packets.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ridiculous grading standards. If you miss three lectures, say goodbye to your gpa. Never again.

She's caring and genuinely wants you to do good, but I don't like the fact that you have to teach yourself, and you HAVE to listen to a bunch of lectures. She doesn't teach in class at all. No late passes, 2 midterms and a final (45% of grade), LOTS of quizzes (20% of your grade), she'll let you bring an index card with notes for the test though.

Math isn't my strong suit, but with practice I improved on every test. There's a short online quiz at the start of class, and she gives the answers, so you get full points if you're on time. Definitely come on review days the worksheets are very similar to exams, even the final. She's super nice and helpful one-on-one.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor is caring and was merciful towards students who mess up, but there isn't much to learn in class. If you're okay with teaching yourself, this is fine.

Horrible class structure, 65% of the class is made up of 2 exams and the final so if you do bad on one exam your grade is completely shot. Speeds through lectures and doesn't do a good job explaining key points and concepts, yet urges the class to master the material so we do good on exams. You're basically teaching yourself calc thewholetime lol
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She obviously cares and is passionate but she is genuinely so hard to get taught from her. From heavy accent, to skipping steps in ex., to just going way to fast, she is not a good teacher from someone who is average. Ur cooked if you don't understand even only one concept, the test will lobotomize you. Be ready to hear formulerr and zoom zoom 100x
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful with a syllabus that doesnt leave any room whatsoever for one single missed assignment nor does the final replace one of the two midterms as other classes usually do. Truly a lesser desirable instructor.

She's sweet and obviously cares about students, but also one of the worst teachers I've had. Most of the lecture is her speeding through the material, while providing little explanation for many concepts. 65% of the grade is on 3 exams (2 midterms + final), so just doing the HW and other graded stuff will NOT cut it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely think that if you miss 3+ classes with her you should just drop the class.
didnt seem interested in helping students succeed SUPER test heavy -- teaching style is very lecture based which is hard because professor skips steps and has a heavy accent. take other professors
VERY test heavy. 2 tests before the final. If you do bad, drop out and retake it because you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are very hard and there's a good amount of homework

Going to class and doing hw can't be enough for class. You gotta deeply master the material since the test are hard and practice exams are no where near the actual exam. Reviewing material before class will be best since she makes problems seem very complicated at times. Ended up dropping the class. Heavy accent as well takes a sometime to get use.

Ms. Stiber is a super sweet lady, but my God she has to be the worst math teacher on earth. Her accent is impossible to understand, she goes through problems faster than God himself could understand, and the textbook is just extra problems! No instructions!!!  this is honestly the worst math class I've ever taken. Bellevue college was better.

Don't take this professor, she moves through problems at a comically fast speed and the lectures are so bad you are basically teaching yourself calculus. its at a point where it she is actively hindering our success as opposed to help us be successful. Car accidents are not emergencies btw so dont crash or u get a 0 on the final. goodluck

this is the worst teacher you can possibly pick. There are no lectures/clear introductions to topics, so you will eseentially just enter the class, be shown a formula and are expected to instantly understand it whilst she finishes problems at a comedic speed...
The cherry on top is that the exams are the hardest piece of material in the class. 😭
Pretty light class, just attend and do the homework.
So sweet and honest, which is weirdly very helpful for math, at least for me.
lot of homework and cannot miss a lecture even when sick

This teacher's class was a total disappointment. Their teaching lacked enthusiasm and clarity. Communication was poor, assignments were confusing, and they seemed disinterested in helping students succeed. I wouldn't recommend them.
I would not recommend this teacher at all. A terrible grader. The mid-term comes out of pocket. You cannot miss an assignment even when you let her know.

Professor Stiber is supportive, kind, and approachable. Please don't hesitate to ask if you need help. She is considerate of students, especially because this course is hard. The course is homework-heavy, but this is Calculus. Please expect it to be hard. Try to do well on the midterms.
Allot lots of time for homework, and teaching yourself the materials from class. It is necessary to do well because she teaches quickly and not very thoroughly.

Worst professor ever! Teaches too fast, strong accent makes her hard to comprehend. Mandatory attendance counts for 5-10% of grade. CP/CW problems are much easier than test questions (don't help in ANY way). If you take any of her classes (done 2) get ready to learn outside of class. Avoid if you can, college is strictly based on your professor.

Professor Stiber was a really caring professor and it's easy to understand why certain people may think negatively about her. She does have a thick accent which get's a while to get used to but she really does try her best for you to understand. Calc 2 is hard so lectures take the whole class time but is always willing to help in between or after.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Stiber was a great professor and was always open to answering questions. Lectures are fast-paced but it is calc 2. She has an accent but it was easy to get used to and she'll only give corrections or make up work for exams if the class average is low which did not happen this quarter. She cares about concepts over memorization. Great overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AVOID IF POSSIBLE. She's a dictator - no clear explanations of grading, doesn't like to be asked for other solutions to a problem. She said if you had covid during finals, no make-ups given. Basically, you should shut up and spread the virus. She lies about the curves, nothing happen. Shows no care when needed. Take other profs or adjust your plans

Good professor, capable of giving clear explanations and also makes sure that students understand material, and if you don't then there are many opportunities to get extra help. Though, the best thing you can do for yourself in this class is to review the lesson the day ahead and even do the homework if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Its going to take half the term just to get used to her accent. 
There are pop quizzes every morning, they are all 1 point each. 
Here is a quick tip: if she continues doing what she did to our class, you can count on her dropping 2 lowest hw grads and 1 lowest quiz grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This was by far the hardest class I've taken she gives absolutely no review for her exams. The homework and tests look nothing alike. The class average for her exams was around 30% again you will have no idea what the problems look like. You better know the concepts and be able to relate them back perfectly or good luck

Stiber's only down side is her accent. 2 midterms 1 final. If you plan on learning in class it will be hard. I learned through youtube and only went to class for the exams and did fine. She's a lieneant grader. She gave test corrections for midterm 2 and curved the final. Final is easier then midterms. Hardest topic of the class was chapter 6.

I had to change this course into an S/NS grade because I am teaching myself Calc 2. She is caring enough but she isn't very good at teaching her subject. She teaches like a textbook was put in text-to-speech. Scheduled a test on Halloween. She expects memorization of math, not actual learning of the concepts. Works through problems at light speed.

One of the worst profs I've had. Three exams in this course so if you mess one up your grade is done. She gave us the study guide and a student asked her if the exam will be similar to the study guide, she said "it might be". Took the exam and it was nothing like the study guide and killed my grade. Don't take her class

In my previous post, I accidentally typed STMATH142 when it's actually STMATH124. Sorry about that. To add to my previous post, I highly suggest that you go to her office hours and go to the QSC if you're stuck on something. Online because of the pandemic. Her online exams are open-notes. In a normal quarter, in-person exams are probs closed-notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't suggest her class if you're not really confident in algebra and trigonometry. She's nice, fast-paced, and has an accent. Worksheets show the basics. HW can be time-consuming and hard. Little-to-no partial credit given on exams because she wants answers, not steps. Offers extra credit after a tough exam. The final's easier than the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Stiber has been sweet, caring, and understanding during a terrible time for both students and professors. Tests are on MyLab due to the class going online so its a bit harder to get credit. But she has given extra credit after every exam that is easier than the actual exam. She knows the material very well and will spend time explaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Your algebra and trigonometry should be really strong. Pop quizzes are a given 100%. The worksheet only shows the basics. HW can be hard and long. Exams are 70% of your grade. She only wants your answer, not your steps. So a few silly mistakes on an exam can cost your grade a lot. Always read the problems carefully and double check your answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Did not understand anything from her lectures when it was in person, bc of accent but she is caring outside of class but she is heavily grading depends on tests which all you need to study for it,

Most of the reviews here are a little too harsh. Yes, calculus with her is challenging, but I think the difficulty is just inherent in calculus. She explains problems very well especially when you tell her you're confused. She's overall a really nice person and she even gave an extra credit opportunity to students after one tough exam.

Online because of the pandemic, everything is online which was not an issue with my other courses. But exams are on canvas and number/letter entry only, so no partial credit given AT ALL. she makes it very clear she does not want to see your steps, answers only. so a tiny mistake can cost you 10% of your grade, awful professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I've ever had. Took during coronavirus. Completely not understanding, doesn't care about students. Thinks online is the same as in person. Offers NO partial credit so if you forget a minus sign enjoy losing 20% of the grade for that exam. Just overall not a nice person. I'd rather take this class 19 times over with a better professor.

She gives out a worksheet every class with all the theorems and definitions, then explains the material (including proofs and example problems! Very useful!) on the whiteboard. Calc 3 is a very difficult class, but as long as you pay attention in class, ask questions when you don't get it, and do the HW, you will be ok. Teaching style is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a solid professor with great lectures, but 1 on 1 conversations with her can be rough. She clearly knows what she's talking about, but she sometimes does not understand where her students are struggling. Only take her is you are confident in your math abilities, as her tests throw everything they've got at you.

The worst math teacher I've ever had and as a Math major, I've had plenty. Her lectures are incredibly hard to follow because she goes extremely fast and makes you feel like an idiot if you can't keep up, then ends 10min early. Tests are RIDICULOUS compared to anything done in class, feels like she is trying to trick you with the questions on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's very good at explaining, as well as helpful outside of class. Plus, she's friendly. She assigns a lot of work (especially for STMATH 124), but with dropping a few of your low grades coupled with opportunities for extra credit (BMATH 121 has more), she's trying to help you pass. I got an A in 121 and a B+ in 124.

Isn't very good at teaching, she really briefly talks about the topic and expects everyone to understand. On an exam most of the class didn't do so well and she just up and said that the deadline to drop the class was soon and if you aren't gonna try, basically just drop the class and don't waste your time. Overall I won't ever take her class again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Skips way too many steps, assumes you know it, not helpful and makes students feel dumb by pointing out individual mistakes out loud to rest of class. Teaches to fast and does not give out much individual help. 10/10 would not recommend. How is she a teacher!?!?

Dr. Stiber is a great professor. She goes through lectures pretty fast, mostly practicing solving problems. Her accent is a bit heavy, so sit in the front would be helpful. Pop quiz almost everyday, but most of the time if you show up for class, you'll get full points. Not recommended if you don't have strong algebra skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: DOES NOT TEACH! She skims topics and expects students to understand all the content right after going over one example problem. Taking Stiber's class is not good for students who are taking Calculus for the first time. It's obvious she cares about her students, but she needs to change the way she teaches because it's not effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her style doesn't encourage an intuitive understanding, and instead says "here's the formula, now use it". Lecture slides are copy/paste, given at start of class. Glosses over proofs that are purely mathematical, and not derived organically. Breezes through class, and ends 10-15 minutes early. She does care, but needs to work on her style.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Almost all of the positive ratings on here are from A students. In her class, an A student didn't need a teacher there to begin with. A students in Stiber's class already grasp the subject. Stiber does -not teach-. She skips over steps then tests you on those steps. She treats the whole subject like we should already know it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I wouldnt take Stiber again. Save yourself the trouble of purchasing the textbook, we havent looked at it. She has a habit of skipping steps when learning new content. When you ask questions, she is passive aggressive and shifts the blame on poor algebra skills. She assigns tons of homework- which takes 3-5 hours if youre teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goes way too fast in class. Skips steps. "Any question? *1.5 sec pause* Ok we move on." Questions asked get condescension. Homework help sections don't match problems. Defers HW questions to QLC or other students. Tests significantly harder than assignments. Lectures are useless. Teaching myself. I only show up for quiz points Genius, but useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She goes very fast in class and when asking questions her answers always seemed condescending like we should already know all the skills. She made questions into arguments with the student. I had calc 2 with her and I regret my choice. Go for a teacher that uses class time to explain the reason behind concepts not just how to plug and chug.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great teacher when it comes to explaining topics. Throughout the course, she emphasizes what problems will show up in the Chapter Exam along with the Final at the end of the quarter. I really recommend going in during her office hours to clarify any issues if you have any. Do the homework and show up to class and you will be just fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Stiber is a very good instructor her accent is a little heavy so sitting towards the front where its easier to hear will help. She covers each subject well and provides many examples, she goes fast but has good office hours and answers questions well. I wish I could have taken her for the whole math sequence. Good instructor challenging class.

She is a really good prof, but her accent is quite heavy (it take time to get used it). U defenitely need to go to her office hour, she is always care about her student and really willing to solve ur question.

If you are taking her, you will have to attend the class every day because there will be a quiz at the beginning of the class. She is pretty nice, and always willing to see students ask her questions at her office hour. But you do have to work really hard in order to get a 4.0

She goes over material very fast and skip steps while showing practice problems. I feel like she thinks we know a lot more than what we actually do, this made it hard to keep up. I felt behind a lot during class.  Also there is a lot of homework involved with this class that is time consuming and can be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She doesn't want her students to fail and therefore makes sure that there is plenty of opportunity for hw help. I loved being in her class for calc 1 and am taking her class again for calc 2. My only real complaint about her is that she has a thick accent which is sometimes an obstacle but if you activley pay attention the class is relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She speeds through the lessons really fast and her having a pretty thick accent doesn't help with keeping up with her. If you are new to calculus, you will probably struggle unless you actually spend several hours of studying outside of class. However, she does put in a lot of effort to help save your grade and she curves final grades.

Stiber is a caring professor and if you put in the advised amount of time into the typical 5 credit technical classes, you should expect a good grade in return. Her pop quizzes are prior to the beginning of each lecture, so you must study the previous chapter section before each class. Still, you are able to talk to others during the quiz. Curves!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgable but seems to not understand that most of the students are learning this for the first time. She rushes through the material and skips steps when showing examples. Unless you have taken Calculus 2 before, I would not recommend her. She also has a thick accent which did not help because she would also talks extremely fast.
Has an accent, but otherwise a great teacher!
Has an accent, but a great teacher regardless.
Her exams were really tough. They took the concepts you learned in class farther than expected. On the up side, the final exam seemed easy in comparison to her midterms.
There's no denying that she's good teacher with tremendous knowledge, but her strong accent makes it pretty hard to understand what's going on, especially in this calculus class.

Bilin Stiber is a cool math professor that challenges you to think critically. While I wasn't the best in her class, her support was outstanding. She is very strict, but a good strict. She expects you to work for the grade! SO work for it. Make it. Bless up. When you get a bad grade, don't panic. It's a roadblock, overcome it.

She is a great math teacher. Her accent is least of your worries if you're basics aren't strong enough. I would recommend taking her class if you're algebra skills are Fairly good to amazing. She gives pop quizzes everyday but you get to work with other people. Don't be late to her class. Don't buy a hard copy of the book everything is  online.

As long as you put forth the effort, even if you struggle, as long as you talk to her, whether it be outside class or through emails, she will do her best to get you through the class with a positive attitude. Great professor for me.

Wish I could take off my previous rating :(.  I thought I would get a D but instead she gave me a 2.1... this class is hard and you also might get confused what an equation does.  Attendance is required and you can't be over 10 minutes late since she gives a pop quiz everyday.  70% of grade goes into the 3 exams.  10-20 questions on Pearsonlab.

get 30-60 questions per week with Pearson.  Very tedious homework.  Pop quiz every morning. Tests worth 70% of grade and homework+quiz+attendance is 30%. She likes to use easier examples in lectures and hard ones in the classwork.  I prefer the opposite.  She also will always try to help after class and emails.  lectures are fast but take up 2 hour

She is a great professor. I had her two quarters in a row. She is very helpful and as long as you put effort in she will do what she can to get you a good grade. So far one of my best math professors.

This class is challenging but managable. If you show up to class and do the homework you should be fine for the midterm and final. And she's always there to help you if your having trouble. She does have a very thick accent so you must pay close attention! I'd recommend her class

Overall, a great math teacher. She made the class fun and entertaining, and is always willing to help her students. She cares about your grade, and it is easy to ask for help via office hours or email. Does have a thick accent which can be hard to understand at times.

She is very helpful and always tries to answer questions when asked. It's hard to understand sometimes when she lectures due to her accent but she hands out copies of the lectures anyways. All the homework is online so there's no need for a textbook. Attendance is somewhat mandatory because she randomly assigns pop quizzes which can't be made up.
Hard to understand and speaks way to fast. Would not put pp online. Her learning style is not good for those who need clarity in math.

She is a nice lady, but has a strong accent and speaks really fast. It is difficult to understand her. Attendance is compulsory and fetches participation points. If you take her class, be ready to work and learn Math on your own.

Speaks very fast with a very heavy accent.  Powerpoint slides are also incredibly text heavy and she will not post them online.  HW is fairly easy, but exams are incredibly difficult, often taking concepts and placing them in a word problem type scenario.  Her HW and review does NOT cover this.  3/4 of our class couldn't finish exam 2 in 2 hrs.

May have some issues with English but is genuinely interested in the success of her students. The online homework provides enough opportunity to get every problem correct and homework is a large part of final grade, so it really helps. Overall, awesome teacher!
Bilin Stiber is a wonderful Math instructor. Organized and very helpful. Will take again.

VERY nice teacher. If you missed homework for any reason, talk to her and she will compromise with you. She genuienly cares about you and going to class is always stress-free. Attendance is vital to grade. Allows 1 page of notes (front+back) for tests, which is WAY more than enough. A++ Would take again

Stiber is a nice lady, but the way that she handles her class is unorganized. She gives you copies of lectures but she doesn't include some things that you actually need to write down. If you decide to take her, write your own notes instead, do all your homework, and study for your exams.

Very nice lady, but could not understand half the things taught in class.  Used slideshows and handouts to teach the class, which was the only useful material to learn from. Didn't have to use the book once.  She probably gets her teaching style from her husband. Would recommend Alexandre Barchechat over her and Abian.

Stiber has been my favorite professor at UWB. The way she taught math encouraged me to pursue a math major. That is after having barchechat for calc 2 lol... She DOES NOT CURVE but instead gives students much more participation points and much more partial credit on exams. She is really funny however some students got beef with her english. 3.9-4.0

SUPER nice. She's also really funny. Strong accent, but you do get used to it. I would strongly recommend her for Calc 3 if she teaches it again, because the alternatives aren't pretty. She learns your name by the second day, gives out group "pop quizzes" that she gives you 100% on even if you're wrong, and encourages going to her office hours.

Hardly speaks English, difficult to understand but you will get use to her. Her class was easy, little homework 15 questions a night online. Plus you have as many chances to get the answer correct online so always a 100% on homework. She is helpful and kind, always willing to stay after to answer questions! DONT buy the book never opened it once.

Very hard to understand but is such a sweetheart. You can tell she cares and can meet with her whenever youd like. It is just frustrating during class when its difficult to write down notes with a language barrier. Text book is marked as required but literally is NEVER used. All online for homework. Overall a fun class if you pay CLOSE attention
Exams are weighted 70%. So much has to be self-taught. Lectures only go over basic concepts and there just isn't enough information for exams.
Lectures are good but stingy grader, wont hesitate to knock points off on the smallest things especially in lab.

he CANT teach, so you have to self-teach yourself CHEM!! 70% of your grade is exams. i swear he doesn't want us to learn chemistry.
i already knew a lot of chemistry, and every lecture he manages to teach in twisted ways that kind of are false. GOOD LUCK, plz be carful not to trust everything he states. 
He is also rude so don't be sensitive ig.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very entertaining lecturer and made this class easier to tolerate. However, this is a challenging class you will have to dedicate lots of time to. Strict criteria to pass the class. If you're easily offended don't take his class; he's very blunt. However, he does care about his students and clearly loves his job. He wants to help you pass.

Professor Finley's lectures are very enjoyable and aren't boring but I think the only way to really pass his class is by self teaching yourself the materials. Your overall grade is basically determined by your exam score, other than that there's the aleks completion grade but it doesn't make that much of a impact if your exams don't go well.

Clear expectations, lectures are not boring, he gives very clear explanations step by step. He also ends lecture early sometimes ! If I took him again, Id review the chapter before class (10 mins), do aleks, and watch his canvas videos before the exam, and do his practice problems. Some of the exam is literally the same as the practice problems.
I rode to school with my seatbelt off.

Really funny guy, really enjoy his class. Lots of mid class graded questions which count to your grade. However, he will happily explain whatever you ask. He is very good at telling you what you need to know for the course and the test.

Amazing professor. Yes, his grading is strict and the class is difficult, but Chemistry is just HARD!! It's going to be difficult no matter who you take. His lectures are the most thorough, engaging lectures I've ever had in college so far. I am eternally grateful that I had Finley as my prof for all three gen-chem courses. Do practices on canvas!!

Dr Finley is the GOAT, one of the best professor in UWB, I took all general chemistry series, quantitative analysis lab/lecture and investigative chemistry! He is always ready to help students, be ready to put an effort for the classes!

Summer '25: He really cares about his students' success and wants us to actually learn the material to better us in the long run. He always answered all my questions after class and helped me brainstorm ways to improve on exams. He grades tests HEAVY (70%), which can make you fail easily, so make sure you put in the time/effort to actually study!!!

Absolutely amazing professor. His class is very difficult, but he is ready to teach you everything as long as you put in effort. No hand holding, but as long as you come to every lecture and pay full attention, and use his practice problems, you will be fine.

This is by far the hardest class between the chem series. But he is a great professor and answers questions clearly but has a mean tone or passive aggressive tone. Don't let that get to you because he is super kind and means well. Super test heavy and recommend studying a lot (15-20 hours). He gives resources on canvas so use those.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like that the lectures are interactive and engaging and being engaged rewards your grade. Exam concepts can be kind of trippy, but the calculations represent the practice hw well. Take pictures, he doesn't post recent slides. Write down all PollEV questions to review. If you struggle in chem look for explanations outside of his. Goodluck lol.

He can come off as harsh in lectures with certain remarks, can be discouraging. Mentioned large portions of class had been failing/struggling but didn't seem like things were being modified. Lectures are good but exams seemed to be unreasonably fast paced and are weighted 70%. Homework was average for a class like this.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid anything taught by him. The 495 class supposed to prepare career or research after graduation. But he shames people badly if he isn't  satisfied with work turned in, regardless effort invested in. Comment sounds dismissive and discouraging, doesn't help for revising resume/CV. Go elsewhere for career advising. Utterly frustrating experience.

Dr.Finley is very open to helping his students and I really wish I had gone to his office hours more for feedback on lab reports. He's very helpful during lab and answers any questions. But, his grading on lab report is sooooo harsh.

Dr. Finley's chemistry lectures are the best, he is so straightforward and gives us everything we need to know. I would take him again for lecture. He also gives good study guides/practice. His exams are hard though and heavily weighted. But, given his lectures, I knew exactly what to study for, but alot of effort is definitely needed.

Had Finley for lecture AND lab and generally speaking, he's a very passionate instructor. However, he sometimes comes across as aggressive and harsh; not really for the faint hearted. Tough grader because he's quite particular.

Extremely harsh grader, so go to his office hours (or corner him after lecture). Finley is open to helping, and his detailed feedback improved my lab reports. Although he's tough, you actually learn and develop skills needed to pass. During lab itself, Finley is there to help but he doesn't hover. If you're used to a chill prof: prepare yourself.

Harsh grader but if you ask him questions in office hours he will explain in detail what he expects in a lab report. ALWAYS go his office hours for every lab report. He is a very harsh grader super strict and takes off points for simple mistakes. But he is a nice person overall looks mean but is nice. I would definitely NOT take him. work load loco
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hes a chill guy, he looks scary but very nice sounds aggressive but thats just who he is. Definitely take him helps u understand the material. Tests are pretty hard but if you study and do the practice questions on canvas its pretty easy. Overall take him but know that you will have to put in effort for an A. I spent like 10 to 15 hours each test.

lowkey if u don't pay attention in lectures u not gon pass I didn't pay attention much during lectures and am lucky I still passed. Maybe I'm just a retard but the test were hard as hell. I am taking 153 right now and I don't know if i'm going to pass.

very very very exam heavy, if you do not well one one of the exams there is no way to recover. his lectures are very fast paced and you wont even have time to comprehend what he says let alone write notes.

Horrible awful professor! I don't think there's one time I asked him a question in office hours and he helped clearly explain that question. He thinks we know everything already and should have everything memorized from the beginning when that's impossible. Doesn't do much to help with exams either and grades super harshly on everything like labs.

Loved Prof Finley, he structures his classes as mostly lecture based with review questions throughout the class time. Typically you get out of class early. Attendance isn't "mandatory" but you are graded for in class participation on the review questions. He's super friendly and answers all questions very well. NO FINAL.

Great teacher, good lectures, just very heavy and hard class if you don't put 100% of effort in, especially if math and science aren't your strongest subjects comparing to others like english or history. Easy to fail and fall behind but he is kind and easy to reach out to if you ask for help. He cares about his students and is passionate about chem

Before the lecture, watch and take notes from the module videos to know what to focus on. After the lecture, review and complete his practice exams, his practice exams are designed in a way that separates the topics instead of mixing them, making it easier for you to organize and focus on the specific topics you want to practice. 
Good luck!

Brandon cares a lot about his students and ultimately wants them to succeed, which is why he hammers home core concepts and provides plentiful free resources for learning and review. There are a lot of exams in the class, but I see that as a benefit, because your grade doesn't rest on just a midterm and final.

Very straightforward class. ALEKS and PollEV have a light course load with lenient grading, so you can prioritize studying for the 4 exams and 1 (30 min) quiz. No finals! Highly recommend reviewing online videos before class, attending lectures for PollEV questions (slides aren't posted), and asking for feedback (EXTREMELY helpful for CHEM 144).

Great prof! Very knowledgeable, super helpful in office hours/after class. HW is just Aleks, but exams once every 2 weeks. No final, but he does grade participation via polleverywhere, so show up when you can! Exams are a bit tricky, do his practice problems and study math word problems and you'll be golden. Don't rely on the curve, it's minimal.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. I would definitely recommend taking him but some people might not like him. Coming to class is important he does PollEV which is basically him asking questions online and answer online. He is very approachable. I put in a lot of effort to get a good grade in his class. Watch his online videos they helped alot more then lec.

Attend all lectures and take full advantage of the resources provided to study outside of class. He provides outstanding feedback for improvement, which I deeply appreciate, in addition to his enthusiastic and friendly attitude during class. However, BCHEM143 is a fast paced course, so you will do well as long as you put in the effort.

amazing person. course content HARD & material volume heavy, but he teaches it very well. completely hilarious person. great sense of humor helped long lectures & tough topics. good as both lab/lecture prof which is rare. office hours taught me double what class did. incredibly helpful 1-on-1 and cares ab students who show they want to pass.

Took him for Bchem 153 and Bchem 163. Amazing lecturer, though can go overtime often. Finley is a really funny professor that knows his audience, but attendance is very important for the class as he does not record them and PollEV is graded (fairly leniently). Gives a lot of practice problems for exams, which are emphasized heavily in his class.

He is a great person and all but his class isn't. If you value your sleep and your sanity do not take him. Your GPA is ONLY based on 4 exams, 4 Aleks objectives, 1 quiz. you have to be Albert Einstein to pass his exams. no study guides, no retakes, no extra credit, lots and lots of studying. His in class presentations aren't on canvas
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic lecturer, tells you and teaches you what he puts on exams, friendly and helpful attitude. Finley is a great professor. Beware, lectures are not accessible out of class so attendance is recommended.

He truly cares about his students, and tries his best. I have taken chem with other professors and non of them are as helpful as finley. You have to do questions and train urself on ur own because it's CHEMISTRY, but not because he's a bad prof.
Professor assumes you already know a lot of chemistry information, PE are graded and he will ask PE questions for topics you haven't gone over causing you to lose points. Very lazy teacher.

If you talk to him early and often then you should be in good standing. He lectures quickly so you can also watch his videos on Canvas that was helpful. tests are pretty tough though so get early practice and ask for help because it seems he just wants the best for you, but you gotta put in effort as well y'know?

He is a funny professor, but I would have to disagree with the majority of the previous raters. From personal experience, I found the lectures to be very complicated if you don't do homework (Aleks). I would highly recommend watching Roxi Hulet if you would like to get a better comprehension of specific Aleks questions. Good luck taking this guy.
exam heavy, not a good lecturer treats you as if you are dumb

Prof.Finley genuinely wants his students to do well. There is a PollEverywhere that counts for grades for each class. To excel in class, make pre-class notes(ppt), take notes and ask questions in class, and solve the practice problems (Canvas). I highly recommend taking Prof.Finley for Chemistry and I will be taking 153/154 with him too.

I love this guy. He inspires me to become a chemist, and he still does classes to classes. He taught me how to be a good scientist, and show me why I should do well in classes and be responsible with my knowledge bc I need it for future career in healthcare. I'm grateful to meet him in my life. Would give the school $$$ in his name if I have $$$ fr

Finley is hilarious and outgoing, making chemistry content bearable and lecture entertaining. Class is heavily weighted on exams and ALEKS homework assignments each unit. Be prepared to self-study content using his pre-recorded lectures as well as the problem sets and self-quizzes all readily available on Canvas to preview and review content.

Very fun and caring. There aren't that many assignments, just the ALEKS homework and the few tests. Get ALEKS done as early as possible.Getting it out of the way helps so much, then you can just study for the upcoming chapter tests. Go to his office hours, print out and do the practice problems, email him about any questions and easy pass.

This is his first time teaching Org Chem, but it is very fun and meaningful. He focuses on the big picture and inspires me to pursue more org chem. Class handouts are clear and organized, he sometimes make small mistakes but correct it right away. Very approachable and humble. Exams are a little long but not tricky. No chapters are left behind.

Overall a decent Professor with some hiccups. He is strict with his grading. Be careful units on tests as he does not give partial credits, at least when I had him. Participation was with PollEv and counted towards grades. Accessible out of class and he did make an effort to give out 1-2 points per test for curves.
Finley is a very funny person but he is a tough grader on tests. But the knowledge needed to pass all of the tests is in the homework, lectures, and practice questions.

Nice guy, has a great sense of humor. Passionate about teaching for sure. But his class is extremely difficult and most of the grading are through taking tests; you get one shot at it. No grade curves, no extra credit whatsoever and no partial credit (problems are either right or wrong). ALEKS and participation are also very prevalent as well.
He is a nice teacher, but it was really hard to follow his lectures. Exams are most of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sign up for this class only if you enjoy dropping your GPA. Finley is a very nice person, but one of the most difficult professors I've ever had. The ALEKS and lectures don't help much and the exams are a big chunk of your grade. BEWARE!!!

Finley makes chem class better just because of his humor. He is always down to help. There is in-class participation so make sure you go to class The lectures help tremendously. It is pretty test-heavy but no final. There's also no extra credit which is one thing I wish there was. He usually curves a small bit as well which helps! Recommend!

In my 4 years, I've never had a professor bump me up an entire letter grade due to my participation in lab. It was a pleasant surprise to be recognized and rewarded for helping other peers with laboratory techniques when Dr Finley was busy.
Is super funny, makes material engaging, is flexible, and cares about his students. Not intimidating at all especially in lab class. If you can, take a class with him!

Brandon truly cares and encourages anyone willing to work hard. If you want an easy pass for chem class, this will not work for you. If you show a good work ethic, he always goes above and beyond for you. I took four classes with him, and the grades are directly related to the time I spent studying. He is a funny and smart chem prof!

I always ask dumb questions and he is SUPER CHILL. He really helps me navigating from mess. I'm usually afraid of lab profs if they are not approachable and abandon me when I was lost. He is a responsible, genuine guy. He grades harshly for 1st report, but feedback is helpful and you will learn real things that I swear you will need in the future.

Brandon is sweet and very knowledgeable. He understands and is able to expand Chemistry-related topics beyond just class materials. I'm so proud to have a professor who is truly a professor and never afraid of any kind of questions. Lecture is funny and he is very clear on what you should do. If you're lazy and loves complaining, you're doom.

Probably one of the best professors I've had so far. Finley is super straight-forward, and upfront. Everything is super clear, and he uses his humor to make the lectures bearable. He is also great as a lab prof. You do need to attend every class because there is a participation grade but I feel like that really helped me focus on the lecture.

I love that he was very clear about his grading criteria as well as the breakdown of topics on each chapter. It made it really easy to be sure about what youre studying and the material you need to know. Hes always helpful when you ask questions which was a huge bonus as well. I would definitely choose him as a professor again.

Oh man, just absolutely terrible. Worst professor in my entire 4-year degree. He acts like god and gatekeeper to medical school and constantly tells people to give up on being physicians if they can't ace his class? Like wtf. He treats class like a comedy skit, he has no interest in actually teaching--I'm 100% no joking. Lecture is a waste.

If you rely on office hours don't take him. He's the worst person behind closed doors, will constantly suggest you drop his class so you don't drag down his class grade average, will constantly berate you for not understanding something because he's bad at explaining things, will OVER simplify lecture, then test at a WAY higher complexity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Allows the expansion for critical thinking! He's really funny. Only downside is having to do ALEKS.

If you love learning and thinking about how things work, you will really enjoy his class. His lecture slides and in class questions are always giving you interesting concepts to think about. The class does take some work, and you will probably get frustrated with ALEKS, but that will happen in any intro chem class no matter the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good professor, I really liked him. I didn't earn the best grade because I didn't work hard enough. He struggles to give feedback though. All chem professors struggle with this especially the ones that teach a lab class.

His class can be difficult at times and will force you to think, but he is still available to answer questions. He is straightforward and follows the syllabus to a tee. He is very enthusiastic about chemistry and is concerned about his students' progress. I'll stay in his chemistry series for as long as I can. Finley comes highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Finley does a good job of explaining lessons. If you are confused, he is able to answer them right away. Do the aleks and practice problems and you are good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Finely is a terrible professor who doesn't teach you. Online class with him is terrible, and you will regret it. He makes you study information that isn't included the same way on the test. He expects you to know information that he didn't teach you.

Though his class can be challenging at times and will push you to think, he is always there to answer questions. He is straightforward and doesn't deviate from the syllabus. He is very passionate about chemistry and cares about his students and their success. I will continue in his chem sequence as long as possible. I highly recommend Finley.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR. His lectures are concise and informative. Chemistry is a very complex topic and he somehow makes it easy to understand. Anytime you have a question, he makes sure to answer it in an email or through office hours. Even though I had to work hard to get a 4.0, I didn't feel any pressure or confusion regarding the topic.

Going into college as a Freshman during a pandemic was kind of a let-down, but Finley really made my first quarter the best. He really does the most for all of his students and wants them all to pass. Also, he's a super funny dude and knows how to make lectures fun and easy to follow.

I've taken Finley for all three of the chem series, and trust me, he's a solid professor. Please don't be intimidated by him, he might seem like a mean or dismissive person but he's NOT. If you go to his office hours, he'll take the time to help you understand. His exams tend to be challenging so STUDY THE REVIEW!! I promise It prepares you a lot!

reviews.comment: LITERALLY THE WORST PROFESSOR ON THE PLANET. Swears it is his God-given-destiny to "thin the heard," so don't be upset when he fails you for no reason. reviews.comment: Great guy. Really fun to have for an instructor. Hope to have him for all my chemistry courses. He jokes around a lot, which I find helps makes the whole learning process easier. Very intriguing professor.  He's easy to follow, and adds humor into his lectures.  I definitely recommend him if you aren't that "Chem-savvy".

A definite no-bs kind of guy, but he is one of the best professors I have had to date. He is intimidating when lecturing but is kind and patient when you approach him privately. His lectures are valuable and intellectually stimulating, if not interesting.

The most straightforward, forgiving, helpful professor you'll have. He doesn't give up on you if you're willing to try. reviews.comment: Brandon is the best professor at UWB. A professor that gives you extra credit for writing jokes on exams? What get's better than that? His class is very difficult, but study your material and follow what he tells you to do before the exam and you would most likely get 80% or higher.

Brandon is the nicest and most helpful professor at UWB. He makes chemistry bearable. He is energetic and makes a lot of jokes and he's a nerd which makes him relatable. He also teaches you how to formulate good sentences. He will stay after class until you understand the material. His quizzes are HARD, don't rush through them. 4.0 is 94%.
He's a wonderful professor, really cares about his students. He makes class interesting and he's really funny!

Finley is by far the best professor I have ever had. The way he teachers is very easy to understand, and his jokes make the lecture bearable. This tests are hard, but if you study, read the textbook and finish the ALEKS homework you will be fine. Taking the rest of my chem series with Finley and I wouldn't choose anyone else.

Chemistry doesn't come easy to me, but somehow, Brandon manages to shove information into my brain! I had his for Chem 1 and I'm gonna be taking him for Chem 2 & 3. Hilarious and easy going, with really good lectures. I also have him for labs and he's simply amazing! I would recommend him to anyone in the Chem series! Fabulous professor all around!

Finley is by far the best professor I had in my freshmen year at uwb. I took chem with him and I've never seen a prof be so organized and knows what they are doing. His exams are a bit tough but if you ask for help  on anything and show him that you care about the course you will succeed. I would take any class with him again!

Finley is the best professor I have ever had in my 4 years of college. I have had him for Chem 1 and 2 and next quarter I have him for 3. He has this magical way of shoving the information into your brain making it much easier to learn. He may even be a wizard... He puts in a lot of extra time helping students on the side. Oh, and he's hilarious.
Very good at explaining things in a clearer concept. You must read the textbooks before attending lectures though. He's a tough grader and hw is given and is due daily.

Prof. Finley is generous with grading, but he deeply cares about your understanding of the material. He's more than glad to answer questions, clear confusion, discuss a problem and guide you to the correct path. He even finds joy in it.  He's very smart and is definitely interesting. I would definitely take all his classes if I could!

This has been by far one of the best professors I've had. Helpful, funny, down to earth, and incredibly smart. He pushes his students to the limit with the amount of study required to pass the class, but if you have a genuine interest in learning, and doing your best, he will see that and help you that much more. Definitely take his class!
Best prof ever he's so caring

I can't believe anyone would have something negative to say about him. He is very helpful and wants everyone to succeed in their classes. Great class.

VERY HARD CLASS!!! EVEN THOUGH YOU ARE STUDYING A LOT, YOUR EFFORTS ARE HARDLY PAID OFF. IT IS MORE CONCEPTUAL CLASS, THAN DOING MATH. PROFESSOR IS HELPFUL, BUT EXPECTS TOO MUCH. THE FIRST TIME I SAW STUDENTS NOT PASSING THE CLASS EVEN THOUGH THEY WERE STUDYING HARD!!

had labs with him for CHEM 142. a lot of prelab work required but nothing too extreme. very helpful during the labs and answers questions very clearly so you understand. fairly good grader, just do the assignment correctly.

Very hard teacher, but he is always there for office hours and he is so helpful and will boost your grade if u go to his office hours. Really nice and cares about his students that show they care too.

love him

Awesome - wish every teacher was like him. Very laid back, very easy to talk to, and grades fairly. Have a question? He'll explain it great detail. I'll miss him!
he is awesome ! smart, funny, helpful, he is a cool dude ever!!

Loved him! Taught a very relaxed and flexible class. His lectures were fascinating and even entertaining which is a rare find. And not that it matters, but he is super hot!! I'd take him again if given the chance.

Be prepared for working on multiple assignments at the same time. I found him as a very tough grader and defiantly assigning too many homework assignments. If you are interested in computer vision or like 'cat' images, then I would defiantly recommend him.

reviews.comment: He's the best! Lecture notes are amazingly clear & complete, & posted online so you don't have to stress about note taking.  He grades tests leniently. Programming hws are interesting, challenging and FUN(image processing!). He also quickly responds to student questions primarily via a discussion board that everyone can see. Does his own grading.

Prof. Olson does research on computer vision so be prepared for all the programming assignments to be about image manipulation. His lectures are very clear and notes are always posted for you to review. 343 is a mix of programming in C++ and discrete math, so lots of challenging concepts but if you work hard the material isn't that difficult.

He teaches as though he doesn't care at all about whether or not the student learns and only offers his way of looking at problems, leading to narrow, confusing explanations. Office hours are no better. If you have to take his class for the Grad Certificate, just live with it I guess. But if you have a chance to avoid him, do it.

I really like this teacher. Every time I have questions he will give very clear explanations. And the usage of the online message board is very helpful. Cuz I can use it any time and post my questions there, of course, get answers from there. Besides, his feedback for our assignments is clear.

Appreciate the fact that the feedback is very detailed.   He has an interest in students learning he material which is great.  Really like his availability for questions with office hours and message board responses.  The most responsive instructor I have had.  His lectures can get scattered a bit, but claims his lecture notes will be right.

reviews.comment: He was new to this course, but I was not able see any extra effort from his side to make ppl understand the concepts. It was obvious that he knows stuff, but seemed to me that he was not interested in teaching this course.
Awesome enthusiastic professor that always provides great feedback.  Exams are straightforward, if you know the material you'll do fine.  Dont, and expect trouble.

Professor Olson is simply one of the best professors I have ever seen: Well organized to the point where you can use his notes as a book, he grades the assignments himself and his notes on your assignments can be used to better your programming practices with a realistic reason why they were graded as such, and fun to learn from - Take his class!
HE IS THE BEST CSS PROFESSOR AT UWB HANDS DOWN! I wish I could take all of my CSS classes with him.

Prof. Olson is definitely one of the best at UWB. His lectures and assignments are clear as well as his expectations. He also grades very fairly on both assignments and exams with good feedback for improvement. You learn a lot with him and he makes all of the material very approachable.

Professor Olson was very helpful and clear with his expectations. Coming from Professor Dimpsey for 342 it was like a breath of fresh air. He is really fast about getting tests back to the students and always gives feedback on your last assignment before your next assignment is due. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on assignments out of class.

Great class! Gave lots of specific feedback on assignments, which was very helpful. He's also very active on the discussion board, so it's super easy to get your questions answered. I highly recommend taking classes with Professor Olsen!

One of the best teachers ever. Always clear on expectations, gives amazing feedback on assignments, and is incredibly responsive to students' emails and message board posts.   If you have the chance, take a class from Dr. Olson, you won't regret it and will learn tons.
Excellent teacher!
He's just Awesome.  Good grader and he even goes through your assignment and tells you how you can improve.

a very good professor, very clear and informative lectures. exams can be quite tedious (you have to write multiple programs by hand) instead of concept knowledge. book is very helpful, homework and labs are fair. overall a very good course and professor to take.

Dr. Olsen is quite a good professor. He is good at explaining concepts and stays in touch with students via email. However, I found his ambiguity regarding testing material and his assignments, which you CANNOT get 100% correct, to be rather frustrating. Especially along with random harsh grading.
It is great that Prof. Olson gives out class notes, so that students can pay more attention on white boards. FYI, Prof. Zander also teaches great 343.

Clark Olson is one of the easiest people to relate to in the computer science world -- he's not intimidating at all and is actually pretty funny.  He's very careful with his words, so you don't get confused.  He talks fast and to the point. You probably won't be able to keep up, but he provides excellent lecture notes online!

Clark Olson is favorite instructor in the CSS program, and I'm in my last quarter. His comment guidelines for code are hard to get used to at first, but you'll thank him later. He's very enthusiastic and he's a cool guy. I've found his exams to be more enjoyable than most other CSS exams I've taken.

Mr. Olson is absolutely fantastic. He genuinely cares about students learning the material. For example, he'll lecture on a topic, then handout an in-class worksheet to practice it, then assign homework for more practice, give a quiz on it, and finally, you'll see it on the exam. Sounds like a lot of work... but it really isn't bad at all. If you DO the homework (on your own), the quizzes/tests will be very straightforward. Bonus: he's funny, helpful, and is fast at grading/returning materials.
Good teacher, knows his subject matter and can teach it too. Sometimes too much powerpoint, but his classes are heaven compared to some of the other CSS classes.

Without a doubt the best teacher in the CSS program. Incredibly helpful...you can practically count on message board replies within a couple hours, 8am-10pm every day. Very fair (not easy, not unreasonable -- just right) tests and assignments. Provides terrific lecture notes so you can focus on understanding material in class.
Very fair both as instructor & grader, could be better (use transparencies) but is still quite organized.   Does move thru topics quickly on occassion.
Great teacher!  Humorous and helpful.  Very organized and has detailed lesson plans.
The mock software development team was a good idea, I really appreciated the experience of practicing pulling recent changes, making changes, and submitting them for review.

The presentations used in class were very well designed and explained the content (also useful for review content). The textbooks used for this class stretch my thinking and introduce me to important team management and communication skills that are crucial in future careers. The team project in this class gives me a chance to apply this knowledge.

This class is one of the most useful ones I have taken. It introduced new ideas about how artificial intelligence models learn and make decisions, which was interesting to explore through the projects and assignments. I feel like I got a lot of value out of what the professor taught in this class.

This class is intellectually stimulating because of how much the contents of the class were really valuable, as well as applying the knowledge into the project, which I was planning on making it as a project for my resume and GitHub

The use of Zybooks helped a lot. It was a more modern approach to learning coding, compared to the other classes which taught the same syllabus. I also loved how open the professor was to the student's opinions and concerns. Also, the lectures going over zybooks examples in detail helped me the most to understand Java.

Camelia is a really smart and educated individual. She went above and beyond to meet the students needs even meeting on Saturdays before the midterm and final as well as having multiple reviews in class. She knows her material really well and has a passion for it. She does want you to succeed!

Don't take her class... And with all that money you wont be wasting, you should be buying me a beer for my great advice to you.

DON'T TAKE HER. I REPEAT DON'T TAKE HER. Worst teacher I have ever had in my life. So rude to students, rolls her eyes and gets enjoyment out of people failing. Literally she is horrible.
