Sure, she had review sessions but one was on a SUNDAY and the final review wasn't during class time. Not everyone can attend those! So unfair. She blames the class for low grades saying we can't study correctly.

This class is awesome as well as a Professor. You really have to study hard but it is very rewarding. Two exams and 7 Homeworks. Lots of extra points to increase your grade  If you have questions, Camelia will answer even before or after class. Great class!

TERRIBLE TEACHER! She needs to teach a subject like math because that is all you will do in this class. She will not take any responsibility for the collective grade of the class, no matter how bad it is, and doesn't give any supplemental material to study with until a week before her impossible tests. Do NOT take this teacher!

This is a tough class, naturally, given the subject. However, if you put 100% into this class you will learn a lot and pass the class. This class is not an easy class by any means but the instructor is knowledgeable and clear. You will need to attend all reviews and go to office hours regularly if you want to do good in the class. Good teacher.

Extremely tough class, she expects us to be able to master economics after just a few weeks. Tests are unreasonably hard, the final especially was terrible. It takes a lot for teachers to get a bad review from me, but this is one of those classes. Will destroy your GPA.

Camelia is a very nice and knowledgeable professor with a great personality. See her if you need help during office hours. Also, you can ask you questions when class starts. The material in this class is not easy and she is very open to make it more understandable. Do not forget to read textbook and do all online assignments which are really helpfu

Refresh your calculus before taking the class. It will be very helpful. However, Professor will go through the basic formulas to prepare class for math. You must read textbook and do not miss her lectures. Class is very interesting and catches very important econ concepts. Would take another class with Bejan.

Extremely unreasonable expectations: you will be blown out of the water with the difficulty of her exams in comparison to the homework and lectures and her lack of empathy doesn't help the matter. Both classes for the midterm averaged a 60%  after being curved and were told it was completely our fault. I highly do NOT recommend this teacher.

Bejan Strengths: challenging, high expectations, pushes you to fully understand economics - no cutting corners in her class. Office hours very helpful. Will curve grade  Bejan Weakness: takes no responsibility even when entire class is failing, not compassionate, tests about 10x more difficult than class material, homework, and sample questions.

I've taken many hard classes. The calculus series, differential equations, Engineering physics series, statics, and dynamics. I have never taken a harder class and trust me, calculating a complex set of forces and moments is much harder than anything I did in this class, which should not be the case. Point is, she made this class nearly impossible.

This is the hardest class I've taken and personally I liked the challenge. She made you work really hard. Her lectures are boring, but she's a really nice and helpful person. She scheduled one review session before the midterm and another before the final. It really helps to go!! The only problem I have is the way she grades. Super tough!!
She is awesome! Has additional office hours. Always asks applications from review sessions. Would take another class with her!

I am surprised with these negative comments. This Professor is very nice. Managerial Econ is really complicated subject but if you work on it consistently, you will be OK.  There are two exams and several HWs on myEconLab. The textbook is very similar to the MicroEcon textbook. She gives extra points just for participating  in the games.

Avoid this teacher at ALL costs. Hold off on a class if she is the only option that quarter. DO NOT TAKE HER, YOU WILL FAIL. Everyone will fail the class, and you will be forced to get a petition to finally have a chance to get your grades up. She is never wrong, and it's always the students faults. Seriously, don't take her, and thank me later...

She can be ok in one on ones in office hours, but hardly anybody could come since they were set up at a bad time. Otherwise, in class she doesn't explain things well and gets defensive and flat out rude if you ask a question she doesn't like. You can't approach her or talk with her, she basically tells students to shut up and stop being stupid.

I understand that managerial economics is a hard course. But she just takes it to the next level. An example of this. The class will get a problem wrong not because we don't understand economics and how to apply it, but because she gives us the longest and most complicated derivative possible. This is NOT a calc class!

This class is very hard. The average for the first test after the curve was a 60. The homework is a waste of time and does not help you on the test. Textbook is expensive and does not help. Her lectures fry your brain. Do not take this class with her unless you are an expert in calculus or want to get a low grade.

Classes are a mix between boring lectures, badly explained and executed class activities, and time where we can ask questions (her telling us how dumb we are for not getting it) She's unapproachable and makes simple concepts hard to understand, so try to learn the content from some online website or something. And tests are very hard, don't take.

Create professor, very knowledgeable. Do not miss lectures, do homework assignments and read textbook. Midterm has the same assignment from the lecture. She is always ready to help. Managerial Econ is not easy. You have to study.  Definitely, would take another class with such a great Professor.

Extremely hard class. Tests do not match up with homework or class discussions. Tests are huge percent of grade too. To pass you must study her weekly practice questions and learn how to do those! She has an accent, but not too hard to understand. She is there for you if you need extra help after class, which I took advantage of!
Do not take this class. You will regret it and most likely have to retake it.

Do not take!!! Worst teacher I have ever encountered. The tests are absolutely impossible, she literally expects you to be an economist after 5 weeks of her course. Class material and homework and NOT reflected in tests which are worth practically your entire grade. Blames class for poor performance when it's really her test writing ability.

Oh so awful... Boring lecturer whose tests are much harder and nothing like the homework or practice problems. Constantly blaming class for not keeping up with Material when she doesn't teach it well at all. Also very rude, not approachable, and she gets upset if you disagree with her in the slightest. DO NOT TAKE.
Dr. Matthews was great- really cared about the course and students. She does ramble sometimes but I didn't mind. I liked her style.

constantly unprepared for class, assignments that had nothing to with the curriculum, baffling grading system, and continually made offensive and uncomfortable comments. the class was easy enough but i would not recommend if you hope to actually learn anything

While she seems to have good intentions, I wouldn't advise taking her class. She would often come to class with no lesson plan, then seem to make it up on the spot. She made several uncomfortable comments during class, would rant about random stuff. Class felt like a waste of time. It was an easy A, but I don't think I have gained any knowledge.
worst prof ever, very snarky and offensive comments
Would not recommend. Not structured well, confusing tangents, group projects that were painful, unclear grading criteria and contract.
very understanding, easy class, just do the work, light work load, didn't study at all in this class

The worst professor I have ever had. Was not understanding and will never let you make up work. Never has clear instruction and does not have rubrics or a clear way to understand what you are supposed to be doing, i recommend you do not take this class.

I did engl299 with carrie. She is a friendly person. As a non-native speaker(mother tongue: Chinese). Writing in Chinese and English are totally different. I hadnt been taught how to write an essay in English well before entering her class. She helped me a lot at this point. 2 essays per quarter, thats pretty easy! Take her class!

Prof. Carrie is really a friendly and nice lady. She is always willting to help and very patient. Though there is a lot to read and write, I really refelct and learn a lot from the readings. The peer-review conference is great. You will have the chance to know how other peer students think of your work. Take this class! You will not regret.

Carrie is really nice! She is very specific and clear about what she expects from her students. She is also very willing to help when you need it. She is also very encouraging and she acknowledges your improvement throughout the quarter. However, I felt like she didn't give as good of a feedback on papers as I had expected. Still great!

Carrie is a great ENGL teacher. Her feedback + peer conferences really help your writing get better. We went over a bunch of example papers in class and practiced giving them grades, which was really helpful for expectations for our own papers. Nice person and willing to help; all she expects is that you do your work and learn how to improve.

Carrie was exceptionally helpful whenever I stopped by her office hours. She is incredibly easy to talk to, explains assignments clearly, and is willing to give you a hand or point you in the right direction if you need it. The quality of my work improved dramatically throughout the quarter. I would absolutely take a class with her again.

Dr. Matthews rocks. She assigns a lot of homework, but all the assignments actually help you with the papers you have to write. She's very clear, and always available if you have questions. She's there to help.

I attended Eng 108 (EFS). She is super nice, clear, and helpful. I actually learned a lot during that month. I improved my writing and reading skills. Not a intense class, but still one formal essay per week and reading assignment. I do hope that I will be in her class someday.

Professor Matthews is awesome. As an instructor, she's clear, exciting, and patient. As a grader, she's critical, observant, and understanding. Her poetry course over summer quarter was just four weeks, but I learned a lot of great stuff! Take her poetry class if you want something different than your typical English course. Take the risk.
Carrie's conferences are very helpful. Make sure to attend class and finish the assignments on time. Leinient overall grader. Great professor!

extremely chill, extremely sweet prof. He's so adorable the way he talks about his daughters. clearly passionate about the world of finance. makes hard finance topics simpler by teaching us financial calculator keys. exams not too bad allows note card and pretty similar to the practice guides. LENIENT GRADER
A caring professor, though lectures are somewhat long. Homework and project are easy, but the exams are hard. A lot of extra credit opportunities in the class as well, which is very nice.

Absolutely amazing professor, he genuinely cares about his students going over everything very carefully making sure everyone understands. He does do some cold calling but still guides you through to the answer. Has well structured exams with practice exams that help a lot. And if you're not a good test taker theres plenty of extra credit options:)

Great professor! Just show up to class and do the assignments. He is caring especially to students who show effort. His lectures are engaging and he really loves his students. Also gives plenty of opportunity for extra credit.

Very kind professor, cares about your success. But thick accent on top of a challenging course made lectures hard. Content heavy project, good group is necessary. Mid term & final are multiple choice and hw is a lot easier than exams which can be good or bad based on preference.

Professor Choi is one of the best instructors I've had. His lectures are clear and crucial to succeeding in the class. Missing them makes quizzes and exams much harder. I was overwhelmed at first, but his guidance helped me stay on track. Even with a weak project group, I still did well. I'd take his class again without hesitation.

he's really kind but it's a bit hard to follow with the accent. the homework is extremely easy but the midterm and final are much harder. so homework doesn't do much to help you prepare. the study guides were also only somewhat helpful. big extra credit opportunity offered though which was great
He is an easy-going professor, we do not encounter much homework with his classes. He offers quite a lot of extra credit opportunities which ultimately helped my grade quite a bit.

Professor Choi is so kind and caring. His accent is thick and his explanations can be confusing, but he truly cares about whether his students learn and succeed. Homeworks, quizzes, and exams are easy as long as you show up to class and take notes.

Absolutely an incredible professor! One of the most sweetest and understanding professor I have ever had so far. The study guide is exactly like the exam, which is really helpful. He does everything he can to make sure you understand the material. Highly recommend.

I'm not sure why Professor Choi has a terrible rating. The assignments are straightforward and based on what you learn in class, and the quizzes are fairly easy—especially since he often hints at what will be on the exam. The exams are all multiple-choice, with partial credit awarded for quantitative questions.

this was for BBUS 350. he is underrated. very nice guy. partly due to his accent his lecture is a bit dry and hard to follow sometimes. but the class is quite easy. very easy grader when it comes to participation and there's a huge extra credit opportunity. mid term and final problems are basically taken directly from the study guide.

Actually took BBUS350. Homework helped me prepare for the exams, but the lectures can be a bit dry. Speaking of those, if he asks the class if they want online, don't do it. He will just post a prerecorded lecture so, in my experience, I would rather attend in-person for the convenience of online for this reason.

Coming from a 4.0 student, I have no idea what's going on in his class. He gave us a literal 30 page study guide just to pull 20 questions from it for the exam, which was pretty difficult. He's a bum, doesn't teach and makes us watch pre recorded lectures where he just rambles and stutters for 2 hours straight. What is he getting paid for?
doesnt listen to feedback even tho asks for it, terrible exam and quiz design, overall potentially the worst class I've taken
Don't take this piece of bad work, he shows you pre recorded videos and makes you come in to watch them. Plus his tests are super hard.

Not a good professor. The class was unreasonably challenging. I didn't learn a thing from his class. He also has a thick accent, so it's hard to understand him most of the time. I don't understand how having to teach yourself the content by "reading the book" and then having a heavy midterm/final is justified. What is he getting paid for?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 words: DONT TAKE HIM.

took in autumn. one of if not best lecture givers at this school. cares about your knowledge depth, lots of resources/prep, some exams may be unexpectedly difficult if you fall behind. gives great feedback on exams, exam score release feels exciting and personal. so far so good, cinematic.

My favorite EE prof at UWB. Amazing at breaking down concepts and able to answer questions clearly. Really cares for his students, so go to office hours! The course will be easy for those who show up to class and not procrastinate on the self-studies and HW. Wholesome prof who just wants to see his students succeed.

A very passionate professor who clearly enjoys teaching. His exams can usually have 1 or 2 tough problems but he is very good at teaching the material especially with the online homework and the homework you do on canvas. However be prepared to do the homework EARLY DO NOT last minute the homework or anything he assigns.
I took this professor in spring 2024. I love the way he teaches. He explains things very well. I also like his long yellow stick that he uses - it became a meme throughout the whole EE department lol
Choi is the EE goat. His classes aren't easy but if you can't make it through his class I don't think the major is for you. Shimple ohms law

Best professor at UWB. Actually cares about his students. Stayed late for office hours and worked with students up until 11 PM. Went to study sessions with his students and made sure they did well in his class. Responds to emails quickly and is easily accessible during office hours, and makes extra time if necessary. If you can take him, DO!

I struggled the first half of the quarter and got better in the second half. His lectures are good but sometimes they don't make sense(only bc he runs out of time and has to rush his lecture) so you have to put in the work outside of class. He's great one on one and during online office hours. I suggest completing all worksheets before the exams

Anyone who says they do not like Choi is putting the blame on the wrong person. They don't like how tough the class is. Choi is very, very clear on the exact steps you must take in order to perform decently in his class. He makes his grading criteria very clear. If you follow his advice to a T, like I did, you should be able to pass the class.

Very clear on explanations and willing to help any student that request help. If you don't understand go to office hours or email him. Makes himself available at many hours to help students out. He is very enthusiastic and fun lecturer. He offers many opportunities to practice and get better. Do the work and ask for help to get clear.
Look here

Don't mess up ohm's law in this class! Circuitry made so much sense after taking Choi. Works examples on the board. I wish I'd taken him for 215. Good lecturer. He'll keep you awake. Don't let the red ink on your test scare you. Tests are from lectures and HW. Be prepared to use load lines and graphical analysis for circuit problems.
He is very knowledgeable about his subject. Easy to approach and good with providing answers to student questions. This class is good to take prior to capstone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Good class to take prior to starting your Capstone
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Choi was very nice. He has so much knowledge. His lectures are amazing and he posts all the lectures on the class website so you don't have to bother taking notes in class and listen instead. He grades super easy  which is nice because his exams are also super hard. Overall a great teacher. I would take his class again

It could be that our class was below the average standards of the EE program, but according to him our class was "the worst class he has ever had and the only class he has ever had to curve".  He is by all means the best of the best in teaching and explaining things, but grading is very tough.  Take him if you are looking for a challenge.
This class was extremely difficult.

The online lecture videos are actually really helpful; I usually hate when teachers do this kind of format in which all the actual learning happens at home and class is just glorified office hours. But he does it a little better than my past teachers, and I actually don't mind it as much.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I think the flipped schedule kind of forced me to do my work, which was really helpful. If there was ever a time where I struggled with something, he was always ready to help me until my question was answered, or he always gave pointers to guide me in the right direction so I could solve the problem myself.
Doesn't allow notes for exams at least when I took him. Watch out if that's an issue for you.

In-class worksheets and lecture notes have 24 hr leniency, absences for illness + emergency excused: email prof, if in class, must stay full class, calc not provided for exams, exams have 4-5 questions per hour (total of 65% of your grade, 4 exams), MLM HW has late penalty of 15% + accepted until 2 days before exam
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Okay professor. Seems like he doesn't care about teaching. They have lectures that you're expected to watch on your own time and do worksheets in class. Four exams in total (including final exam), however, there were only 3-4 questions on each midterm and 45 mins long. If you miss one question, you're basically cooked as exams are weighed heavily.

He is a great lecturer and answers questions well. His videos are used in other math courses and they are all great. Yes you have to do work outside of class boohoo its not that bad. Ask him questions and he will help, the worksheets in class are also helpful if you pay attention and stay engaged as he goes along.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Believe the reviews here. 0 concern for student success. He doesn't even like teaching. Will be curt and borderline helpful during office hours.

He's a very approachable person and will help you if you need it, but the flipped class thing essentially makes it office hours with required attendance and it's hard to give someone who doesn't teach a high rating. You will need to be on task and do worksheets for the entire class to receive those points. He grades easily, though.

This professor has a very bad temper; all coursework is in the lecture videos. While attendance is mandatory, class time is wasted on a worksheet which he never helps us with. I am confused how he even got the job to begin with... though the coursework is relatively easy, you might get a good grade, but you won't learn in the process.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Most useless professor I have ever had in college. Class attendance is mandatory, but we do not do anything during the class time. He simply hands us a worksheet and expects us to fill it out on our own. During class, he usually eats lunch or reads a book. Whenever I ask a question, he is always annoyed with me as if I offended him.

Taking this class drained me. I'd walk in every day questioning why I was even there. He doesn't teach, the flipped setup feels like an excuse to avoid helping, and the class feels pointless. His ego makes it worse. If you can, take Piero instead—he actually teaches and supports students.

Grades fairly according to what your actually being tested on. Most of his lecture videos cover a lot of theory about the equations your working with, and can be a little difficult to understand the actual topic on hand. Would recommend for math majors/minors, and people who work effectively outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His class is completly self taught. Has you watch videos then just gives u a packet to work on. Doesn't teach and has a temper. the only difference between his class and a online one is attendance is graded. waist of a quarter

It's true that CM is considered a "tough grader". But honestly, Clark is a nice guy who will help you out if you just reach out. Don't fall for the "soulless professor" propaganda. His grading criteria - while strict about things like notation - is very clear and you understand exactly what needs to be done to pass his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't be fooled by the positive reviews of musselman on rmp. He's terrible. Unfriendly, egotistical, uncaring--all the typical traits of a prof who doesn't care about you or your grade. Not sure why people like this get into education, there must be so many people that would love to and be enthusiastic about his job. Deserves to be canned

Don't be fooled by his low RMP score, Professor Clark is good at what he does. We have 4 midterms + a final. The grading is fair, Online HW 20%, Worksheets 15%, Midterm Exams 45%, Final Exam 20%. He's organized and he replies to canvas messages fast. The questions on the exams are the exact same as the ones he tells you to study in the review.

One of the worst Professor I have ever seen in my life. Attendance is mandatory in his class and he never teaches in his lectures. Basically it is like study session, when you ask a question he is giving careless answer for ex: “Watch this lecture video”. There are 5 exams including 4 midterms 1 final exam. The grading process sucks.

Very careless, prideful instructor. God help you if he makes a mistake because his ego will prevent him from admitting that he can be wrong. One of those people you would never be friends with because he is an actual a-hole, acts like he is so cool. Becoming more learned should make one more humble, I guess Clark has never fathomed this. Avoid.

He uses a reverse classroom style, meaning watch lectures at home and do homework in class.  I liked this style a lot and his lectures were very clear on the material.  It is a tough class and he does not curve at all but if you put in the work you can succeed here.

The entire course is taught through videos and the examples barely even help you! He puts you in groups to work with throughout the quarter so he doesn't have to ever actually teach. The online homework is ridiculous and he is so stingy about form, I do NOT reccomend

The exams are very harshly graded and doesn't give any margin for error. Makes us learn a bunch of topics, but then announces what we should know an hour before the exams. The lectures are videos online and are somewhat helpful, while the in-person classes are offered as office hours. NO CURVES!!! Exams are worth 45% of grade and there are 4 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible professor. his lectures make no sense, his quiz grading scale only serves to take points away from students, and gives almost no help to students. I found myself on youtube because his lectures were that bad. Additionally, the quizzes make up half your grade, and as a result if you fail the quizzes you fail the class. STAY AWAY!

I really don't recommend this teacher. He was MIA for roughly 40% of the classes in total. He also doesn't try his best to help students who reach him for help. His classes just consist of problems in class and self-learn through the online math lab.

Worst teacher I havent take. The first time I failed and didnt get a good score on math class. He didnt give a lecture only recorded online which not the latest record. He asked us using cocalc and didnt give us enough information to do the assignment. Tough grader, dont wanna take his class again.
Class is super hard but he's a nice guy. Had him a LONG time ago back in 2013 at Seattle. Heard he's at a different UW campus now, everyone's lucky to have him.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best math teacher I've had at UW Bothell. He conveys all the concepts very well (his slides and notes are all very good and available online). Clark has a passion for math and loves teaching. He requires attendance for a participation grade, and don't be late or he will implement a "draconian attendance policy". He seems a bit tough but he's fair.
EASY A....
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: No extra credit, No curve, No note card on tests. His tests are only 30 minutes long. Attendance is a part of the grade, but he only takes it some of the classes, and when he does it is after most of the class has left.

Great professor. Very clear on everything he is grading you on. Specifically states that he is "not trying to trick you", meaning that he will slightly change the problems from the homework and put them on the quizzes/exams. TAKES ATTENDANCE. Also, make sure to do all your hw (STRESSED)
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Clark is a great professor. He makes you work in a group setting, and doesn't really lecture. But he's still nice, and you can reach him out of class easily. Remember to do the assignments on time, because one late homework can drop your grade quite a bit.

Awful professor. Skips steps saying "teacher privilege" and makes you feel stupid for  not answering a question. Doesn't give example problems and expects you to know everything he is talking about. Gets frustrated when you don't answer a question & will yell at you. Doesn't grade 90% of homework problems so you don't know if you're doing it right.
He's pretty god at explaining thing. Go to class, do the homework and you're good to go.

He explains everything so well. I cannot put into words how amazing he is at explaining math. Hands down the best math teacher i have ever had so far. All you need to do is attend classes and do all of the homework to lock in the principles taught, and you will do amazing in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Worse professors ever

Clark is an absolutely amazing teacher. I would take every math class with him if i could! he explains everything extremely well and will explain anything to you in multiple ways until you understand. Clark also does a really good job at relating what we are learning in class to real world scenarios.  Just pay attention, come to class, & do the hw!

Clark is a fantastic teacher. His tests are easy enough (no super tricky stuff) and very meaningful, and his lectures are great. As the other commenter says, coming to class is worth it; Clark provides insight into things that the book does not cover as well.

I took Clark for both Calculus 2 & 3, and he is honestly the best math teacher out there. He is super thoughtful about his lectures + the feedback he gives, all while maintaining an inviting and laid back environment. Stay focused (he provides meaningful explanations), do the homework (basis for tests), and ask for help if you need ANY! MUST TAKE!
Least lenient/ understanding prof at uw, told us that she doesn't like giving out 4.0's on exams whatever that means
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Previous chem knowledge definitely helps and it's best to do a little review every day because there's a lot of material to keep fresh (This includes ALEKS). You don't have to show up all the time, but look over posted class notes after lectures in Canvas if you decide lectures aren't worth it. Having a study group helps!

Lovitt's lectures could have been a bit more substantial, but she made up for this by the sheer amount of resources she posts to Canvas. Exam questions are nearly identical to quizzes and ALEKS homework. Quizzes are online and retakeable, and she employed exam replacements if you didn't do well on the first midterm. Overall very caring professor.

Dr. Lovitt usually comes prepared and ready to each lecture. Her slides helped me personally. She had more office hours open than all of my other classes combined. The ALEKS online homework might seem overwhelming but it helped me the most. And if it is take advantage of the vast amount of office hours. Ask questions don't fall behind in silence.
doesn't lecture at all and assigns a large amount of aleks due weekly, be prepared to self teach, avoid at all cost

doesn;t lecture at all spends more time talking about off topic stuff than lecturing. attending is no help whatsoever, class is filled with peer facilitators that do more teaching than her so be prepared to do lots of self teaching
Overall was fine. Overall not very understanding of her students and rushed us severely at the last week of lecture. If you can take Finley

She is a good lecturer but doesn't do that a lot. Group work is okay but doesn't elaborate on concepts. I wish she would help with some review sessions but it's just peer facilitators that lead it. We were still learning 2 chapters less than a week before the final and study guides were ok. Overall an okay prof.

Yeah no don't she just made us learn 2 new chapters two lectures before the final also we had snow and every other professor canceled or move class to zoom but not her and it was the last lecture before the final which she knew students probably won't attend bc of weather but still made it in person
Walks around with peer facilitators instead of actually lecturing and complains about giving out A's on tests for some reason

Okay lecturer but doesn't lecture spends more time talking about other stuff rather than chemistry. Class is 80% group work and doesn't lead the exam review sessions. Only take her if you life self teaching

She's actually really good at teaching chemistry, but for some reason barely does that. Most of the class time is spent doing group worksheets on stuff she didn't cover in lecture. Overall the key to doing well in this class is the ALEKs homework. It's tedious but DONT DO IT LAST MINUTE. Practice daily from the beginning, it'll pay off for exams.

spends too much time discussing things that are irrelevant. Kind person but lacks in some professor skills. needs to understand that her teaching skills could improve & that students are not always at fault.
Classes really don't teach anything; you are forced more to use online resources and learn from there

FOR THE LOVE OF GOD, get the textbook, if you do the reading she posted for before class, i SWEAR it all makes sense. AS a chem HATER, i had fun in this class because i understood it. lots of group work during class, but it's not bad tbh. She knows how to teach and wants you to succeed. Unlike some teachers (b FINLEY).

cant stand her
entire 2 hour class is spent on groupwork where no one has a clue what theyre doing 
she doesnt lecture at all and is a complete waste of 2 hours
gives 10 different types of homework you have to spend all week on plus teaching yourself all the material she doesnt teach 

would learn better if a monkey taught me

she's a nice person, but if you hate doing group works and learning from other people rather than a person who has a PHD in chemistry I would avoid taking her. If you do enjoy group work and learn better that way then take her. She also is kinda harsh on grading and your grade depends on if she is in a good mood or not
I hate dis woman
Very detail oriented graded, its really bad. Picks on unnecessary things to take points off. Doesnt give good criticism. Very random feedback that makes no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very detail oriented in grading, does not give good criticism. Picks on random stuff to take points off for.

Had her for BCHEM 143 last quarter, but this time the class wasn't as easy. She's a very nice and caring person and offers a lot of help and extra credit/student grade benefits, but even then, the majority of the class had a hard time passing. Had her for BCHEM 154 too, and she was more laid back in lab than in lecture. Sweet soul, but hard to pass

Dr.Lovitt is really kind as a person, but I really did not find her teaching style helpful this quarter. We mostly did gilt problems as a group in class. I really cant stand the group work, and would have preferred more lecturing because it feels like im not learning much in class. I started skipping so much class. Lecture is very brief.

Very nice person, not a good professor. Offers a lot of office hours and is available outside of class, but most everything is online. Class time is spent in groups working on problems, but I hope you don't have any other classes. Online homework takes hours of your time; I emailed her, confused about the material, she p much replied "skill issue."
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I hope you don't have a social life! She's a very nice person, but not a good professor. I saw her hand a friend of mine an exam back and congratulate her. I asked her what she got and she said a 47/100. Asked her for help on the material, pretty much said I need to get better at studying. We have online work outside of class and meet 3 days a week

She doesn't actually teach much. Class time is spent working in groups on google docs and much of the content is learned online in ALEKS (homework program). She posts lecture slides after class, so theres no way to learn at your own pace / take notes during class time. She is very passionate about her subject which makes her nice to work with.

Very chill class. Attendance is not mandatory, lectures are kind of boring, but most of the class is group work which helps you grasp the concepts better. The exams are very well weighed, there is basically no way to fail this class.

This was my third time taking chem and I finally passed bc of Dr. Lovitt! She's really caring, encouraging, and easy to talk to. The class itself is really hard and very easy to fall behind and fail, but the online quizzes and aleks hw are weighted the most which makes it easier to pass. She also had amazing PFs in class which helped out a lot!

One of the best profs ive ever had. I failed chem previously but she made me love chem. Her lectures make so much sense and she's very accessible outside of class. Offers lots of office hours and help if you ask. All quizzes online and only 2 in person exams. Opportunity for makeup points and late work submissions.

Her chemistry class relies heavily on group work. You're working with your neighbors every class period, so be prepared to socialize or else take the class with friends. The tests are not super difficult, but participation is counted, and again it is group work-heavy.

This professor is a wonderful person. The class structure was very good, and I found it helpful. There is a lot of group work during class, I found it very useful to ask a lot of questions and be prepared.

Dr.Lovitt fails to teach her students and if you take this class you need to teach yourself all the material. Her class is teamwork oriented and if that doesn't work for you she doesn't care. You have to learn the class material with a group rather than her actually teaching chemistry. I DO NOT recommend anyone take her class.
She's one of the kindest professors I've had. She's extremely understanding of her students wellbeing and I constantly felt supported in her class!

She is a kind professor and is also very understanding, however, she assigns so much homework and group projects that weren't very useful but rather just time consuming stuff. Didn't learn that much from the group assignments or the little projects.

Assignments are relatively easy, there were no in-person exams for her 143 class but there were "mastery quizzes" due for every ALEKS chapter, which are asynchronous online. There are many graded activities based on teamwork. Nice and understanding professor, lectures are decent but the majority of your learning is through ALEKS. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Awesome.

I was put off by the lower ratings she previously got but the course was great. In-person class, quizzes are all online (3 tries each and the highest score is recorded) and gives out 3 late passes as well. Do your ALEKS and work with your groupmates for team projects and you'll easily pass. Take this professor for Chem 143 if you can!

Professor Lovitt was very organized with things and loved that she gave chances to catch up on late work (3 token rule). Her class is pretty easy as long as you do your ALEKS & you're actually on top of things. Lots of group work in class. Overall, would take her again. Pretty straight forward and I like that!
Easy class, solid prof, no complaints, no midterms, just 9-10 timed quizzes. Do the work and the class is a vacation. Sometimes she gets a bit flustered but honestly who wouldn't these days.
Good professor really goes above and beyond to help students.Also is accessible outside of class time. And is really clear when it comes to her grading. You can definitely succeed in her class.

Gives you all materials necessary to succeed. Lectures are pointless, so you gotta teach yourself most stuff; because of this, I wouldn't say that she's a great chem teacher, but she's a great person. Lots of unnecessary excess work but it's all manageable. Easy to succeed if you take charge of your learning and you aren't lazy.

Bruh. What even was this class. Literally had no other option but her for the intro to gen chem course (bchem139) and the first two classes in the gen chem series (bchem143 and 153). So I've had her for for three quarters in a row. We use this website called ALEKs and it's just practice questions. That's the ONLY way you're going to learn.

This is the hardest thing I've ever done. Class is only once a week for some reason and even then she discusses things not related at all to chemistry. Quizzes are worth the most of the grading scale and the only place where we have to learn from is ALEKS. There are so many things wrong with this class, I could litreally type out a few paragraphs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's a very nice professor, you just have to put in a little bit of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Genuinely caring. Her lectures are not all too helpful. Be prepared for lots of group work. Also be prepared for large amounts of homework. BCHEM143 was kind of a self lead class when taught by her. However, she gives you every chance to succeed. Just do the work and you'll be fine. Accessible outside of class most of the time.
Not accessible outside of class at all. Lectures are useless and non informative. I regret taking her as the whole quarter i had to rely on tutors, friends, and ALEKS hw to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very useless class. Made us read a book that was not useful in our learning at all. The lectures did not teach anything and the professor went on tangents on random topics. The zoom meetings did not relate to anything in the class. We had to make a comic book as a group project, and she was very nitpicky on how we were supposed to make it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: ONLY LECTURES ONCE A WEEK. This course is very much self teach, so if you're not into that don't take. Somewhat impossible to tell what she wants from you (grading wise). However, she is a genuinely great person and is very sweet. Willing to answer questions during office hours and accessible outside of class. Take her as a last resort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: It's impossible to tell what she wants from you. She takes off points for things that aren't on the rubric. Very frustrating. Her lectures are not informative - the class is spent on surface-level busy work from a workbook instead of actually teaching. I learned more from ALEKS, the online hw platform. Also, she had a lot of mistakes in her quizes.
She's a very kind professor! Very good lectures and really answer your questions in detail. However, try not to miss class. Participation counts!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lovitt is a great outside of the class teacher. Her lectures are very hard to follow and about half the time Im not sure if she knows whats next in the lecture. I took her chemistry and bcore class but never attended her office hours until the end of the quarter. If you go to office hours youll be fine if not be ready to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class itself isn't very difficult so as long as you study, you should be fine. With that being said, when you are confused, she isn't the best at clarifying things and she often gets thing mixed up which may confuse you even more. Asking the peer facilitators are a better option to ask questions. ALEKS is a huge pain in the ass. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Not a great professor. Often gets herself confused when student asks questions and doesn't give good or clear answers. Seems like a good person, but as a teacher she is not the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Funny. Very nice overall but strict and grades hard. Not that thats a bad thing. Overall pleasant prof.

Dr. Lovitt is very passionate both about chemistry and her students. While she's a tough grader, her grading is consistent and the criteria she grades for is clear. She's got a good sense of humor. Work hard and you'll learn a lot in this lab!
Great teacher! Really prepares you for CHEM 143.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good class.  She was easy to follow.  No complaints.
Awful, useless class. As a teacher bad, as a person good.

She gave long, confusing and pointless lectures that were not even related to our exams. Gave study guides only a few days before the exams and assigned group projects a few days before the deadline. Mostly a fair grader except for the bigger things. Never manages to get through the lesson plan, a lot of unnecessary discussion and activity.

Heavily graded on participation to the point where you can fail if you show up, but just don't speak. 90% of your work is dependent on your peers and not individual. 'Strange' style of teaching and yet is somehow teaching half of marketing courses and electives.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Undisputed GOAT professor. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it is essential for success in the class, as there are a lot of group discussions and your participation can impact your grade. There's a course pack you need to purchase and a simulation, but it isn't very expensive, and you can share it with classmates.

Super cool professor. There is a lot of reading but as long as your do the readings and assignments on time the class is pretty easy. Engage in the discussions and argue your points and you'll be good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This is my second class with Professor Ceri, going on third. Her classes aren't structured very well and she grades harshly, but she has a lot of industry knowledge and you will learn a lot from her. Assignments apply course topics thoughtfully and quizzes are take-home and short answer.
horrible grader, marks you down on everything including participation if you don't talk enough

Participation was a huge part of the grade and even though I came every lecture and talked, it was still not enough to get higher points than people never coming to class. Her grading is all over the place, I would pour my heart writing 12 pages worth for the mini project and got a lower score than somebody who wrote two sentences for each section.
Harsh grader. Didn't like her teaching style she was not very helpful. We had a simulation and she didn't help us with it at all.

Professor makes you tackle many different marketing concepts that are interesting and fun to examine. Course relies heavily on group projects and you work together to complete papers, presentations and lead the class in cases and articles. Chill grader as long as you follow the rubric. No exams but pretty workload heavy. Participation is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took 3 classes with her and she's great. Weekly article and case write-ups along with a group simulation. Also, each group is tasked with presenting a chosen case and article for presentations. I didn't like how students had to lead the class to talk about articles/cases so participation matters. Pretty workload heavy and dependent on group effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've taken 3 classes with her and I would take more if I could! She's an amazing teacher, my favorite one in all UWB. It's not an easy class, but it's so worth it if you put in the work. She doesn't treat her students as dumb people, she treats you with respect and pushes you to be better; she's really open to communication. Love her!

This is my 2nd time taking this professor and I have enjoyed her informative and fun lectures. Weekly case write-ups where a lot of them are interesting reads. I feel she is a fairly chill grader as long as you actually put in the effort in the assignments. Group project at end of the quarter but I felt there was not a clear grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The best professor in the marketing department. If you want to be successful in marketing you must take classes with ceri. Her classes are very thoughtful, and it will stretch your the way you will think about marketing. The classes NOT HARD, participation Is very important. Not a lot of HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ceri is one of the most solid professors at UWB. She really cares about people, is very interesting, and does well with lectures. I respect her so much and wish I could take more of her classes. There is a lot to read, but it is not dry content. Get ready to LEARN a bunch of useful things. Thank you, professor! You really made my marketing journey!
Class time is NOT used effectively. She asks "US" TO LEAD THE CLASS. Um... then what are you being paid for as our professor? The class is not helpful and its value is not clear.

I don't understand any negative reviews of Ceri. I've had her for 3 different classes now and I enjoy her so much! She is one of the only professors that has great lectures. She makes it so much fun and interactive, always has great stories to tell. I have found her classes pretty easy as long as you show you are engaged and try.

She has a great personality but her class has no structure. Very unclear grading criteria and deadlines for assignments that are not set in stone. Hard to access outside of class. Exams are worth 40% of your grade, fill out the review sheet and you'll do fine. HUGE group project worth 30% with little guidance. Take it with someone else if you can.

Ceri is an amazing professor. She really respects and cares for her students just as long as you return the same. The first couple weeks are lecture heavy, and after that it is nothing but article and case write ups and presentations. There is a simulation throughout the quarter and that will take up a lot of time but it was so much fun!
She has high expectations. And she never give clear instructions on her assignments.
Ceri is a fantastic professor! Reasonable grader and hilarious
Unclear instructions on assignments. Super strict grader. Workload is stressful because you don't know what her expectations are. She also doesn't give examples on how to write the papers.

I'm not here to complain about the professor because I do not put in the work or not try my hardest. I really try my best within my abilities. However, her class is extremely challenging. Workload is heavy since you read one case (about 20 pages) and two articles (also about 20 pages) and complete write-ups PER week. There's also a simulation.
She's funny, but that's not important. She grades extremely hard and tons of workload. Her assignments are back to back and time consuming. Her expectations are very high.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She seems like a nice lady who is very knowledgeable, but the layout of the course is horrible. Gives very little explanation of expectations for projects and long response test answers, then grades extremely tough. Lectures are mostly off topic and can get very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm surprised on the negative reviews. I love her lectures and if you put effort in, you'll get a good grade. Take detailed notes. Quiz's are long, but if you do well on first two, you do not have to take the last, so it evens out. Keep lecturing, Ceri! Yuo are great.

Too tough of a grader. She seems like a nice person but I dont love the class. Lectures are way too long- please Ceri, break them up with breakout room activities or something. Its just too much. And relax on your grading pleaseeee.

Her lectures are funny and engaging, but that's not important. She grades tough and her exams are crazy long. You will never reach her standard even if you try your hardest, her expectations are very high.

The professor is so harsh because she grades so tough and gives long exams. What's funny is that she named "Quiz 1, Quiz 2, Quiz 3" when each "quiz" takes you 5 hours to do because it is essay-typed, no multiple choices. Also, she suggests you to write 1-3 pages for some questions. The more you write, the better grade you get... hopefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Ceri for BBUS 436 and im taking her right now during summer quarter for BBUS 438. Ceri is really great at keeping her students engaged and she is funny! in 436 there is one article write up per week and a group project at the end. There is a ton of work to do in 438 especially in summer term since its condensed into 4 weeks. overall, 100/100
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ceri is hands down the best professor I ever had. She really cares about her students and is one of the best lecturers i've seen. There is a good of homework and she is tough grader, but she also lets you argue back points on tests which is awesome! The group project was lengthy but easy if you split it up and get good group members. Take her!!
Lots of case to read
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ceri has a heart of gold. I loved every minute of her class and if you are struggling she help you out. Her consistent teaching styles and her humor will make you want to major in marketing. Do not expect an easy A because she will make you work for it :)
A true gem and an inspirational professor. I was blessed to have Dr. Ceri as my marketing professor. Tough grader but it was all worth it.

Dr. Ceri is a wonderful professor! She truly cares for her students and gives great feedback on cases and projects. I love participating in that class because she makes me feel valuable. Her class is pretty difficult and her tests can be challenging. But she's truly amazing!
Really nice easy going Professor. However her tests can be very tricky and she grades tough! I read the book and studied hard and didnt get a good grade.
I thought this class was Marketing Not a muscle memory class.
She's a pretty good teacher. The lectures are funny. The 25-page group project and presentation is tough. I don't know anyone who got higher than a B on their presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Both her 426 & 438: lots of reading and writing. 426: 1 case study/week. 438: 1 case study + 1 article writeup/week. THE ONLY THING I learned from 426 was ENGLISH WRITING SKILLS instead of marketing. The amount of hw and time spent in 438 is more than both of my 470 & 480 combined and IT'S JUST A MARKETING CLASS! Didn't learn much not recommended.

reviews.comment: participation matters. it worth 10% and I lose my 4.0 because of it. read the slides to prepare exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgeable and you'll learn a lot from her lectures. Tests are a bit on the harder side but just go over her slides and read the textbook and you'll do fine. I wish more professors are as passionate about their subject as professor Nishihara is. She has good sense of humor so her classes are never boring.
She is a pretty good teacher, not a tough class. She is super funny and I was laughing in every class. HOWEVER, get a good group for your group project or you will be sorry.

I really liked Ceri's personality. Made her lectures really easy to listen to. However, she was quite vague with what she expected for any assignment she ever gave. Tests are impossible if you don't read the textbook, and even then, they force you to memorize A LOT of info. I genuinely enjoyed her, but the class is definitely not an easy A.

There is a solid amount of studying in this class and a group project that is left pretty open ended. Overall Ceri is a great, reasonable professor who gives interesting lectures and real life examples to go along with the concepts taught. I didn't always appreciate the inevitable tangent conversations she brought but it kept class lighthearted.

She's a tough grader for sure, and the tests are pure memorization. I found that by reading the textbook as well as her power point slides helped me perform a lot better in the tests. Don't skip classes, I did a few times and she took off 0.2 of my final gpa. This was by far the hardest class I've taken so far though.

she takes off points without explaining why even if it answers the question completely.  your answer must be the same as her answer key for full credit (they answer things not asked in the question).  Grades extremely harsh. expect 75 as normal.  I believe 85 was generally the top score.  no curve.  find alternative if possible.  lecture is textboo

She's very nice and has engaging lectures which is great. She does have a pretty time consuming group project that you work on all quarter. Her tests are pretty tough. To pass the tests, you DEFINITELY have to read the book. All the multiple choice questions come straight from the book and short answer is based on class discussions.
I got a 3.9 in her class. As long as you buy the book and read it before the exam, you'll do fine.

I've really enjoyed Nishihara for Marketing. She has a great personality, and the coursework is reasonable. You will be assigned readings that correspond to exams. People have complained that the exams are hard and require a lot of memorization, but if you fill out the study guide provided and read, it will be no problem. Overall, a great teacher.
Ceri is awesome. Took her twice, for BUS438 and International Marketing. Both were great, she's nice, smart, and the classes were fun. Highly recommended.

Her lectures are long and somewhat boring but she is pretty funny. Barely anyone participated in my class but I did and she rewarded me well for that. The cases are harder than they look so start early same with the group project, definitely give it your all and start as early as you can. Powerpoints help for the exams you have to memorize a lot.

Ceri is one of the funniest, most intelligent professors I've ever had. However, the class is structured where students are 95% of the time the ones lecturing, and not Ceri. I appreciate her empowerment of her students, but wish she would have chimed in a little more given her wealth of experience. Other than that, it was a great class!

Of all the profs I've had at UWB, Ceri is decent. Basically average. Overall the material is decent but she is unclear about what she expects on assignments, then grades them strictly. Then after she grades strictly, she doesn't provide reason for the grade she gives. If you want to do well, you must (I REPEAT, MUST) ask what she's expecting

One of my favorite professors I've ever had. I had her twice. The two classes were structured totally different, but both really good. She truly cares about her students. She is open and very helpful. She has a great sense of humor. Is a wonderful wealth of knowledge and has great stories of her experiences.

350 characters is just not enough, but I'll do my best. Great teacher. One that actually cares about the students. Really. Very knowledgeable, so don't even try to bs. Go to class, speak up, and ask questions. You will do well. Join a group that you enjoy working with, it adds to the experience. This is one of the best professors I have had yet.

This class is only "easy" if you study! Professor Nishihara's class has been a fascinating learning experience. You will not regret taking her classes. Most of the Asian professors can't even speak clear English but do not fret, her English is perfectly fine. Now only if she could teach MORE classes! She is UWB's best kept secret!!!
Great teacher. Its a lot of student lead discussions which is an interesting teaching method. She knows her stuff. Just do the readings and participate and class and you'll do great.

I took her marketing class a while ago. You will not have note for exams,which means you will have to remember everything. I though it was hard but not impossible. For the marketing project, try to go over her before you turn it in. I know a lot of groups who got a pretty low score on it. Just read the book and don't cram at the last minute like me

Dr. Nishihara is an intelligent, witty professor and a wonderful human being. She conducts her classroom in such a way that students not only learn from her but from each other as well. Pay attention, do your readings and participate, and she will reward you with a good grade.
Very unclear with how he wants his lab reports and very much a harsh grader. Do everything he says in the rubric for your next lab report? He'll still find something to grade you off from.

He seems to take offense to being asked questions during labs, ignores his own safety PPE while inspecting and handling student's lab material, and is otherwise a somewhat petty grader. The curriculum he's left with isn't helping with any of this but it's easy to see he'd rather be doing something else with different people.
Generally nice guy but would not take him again. His grading is kind of weird and some comments he makes when grading are petty lol. Not the worst but not the best.
Tests are hard but there are plenty of resources he provides to ensure your success. You need to put the work in. He is very helpful after class and during office hours. TAKE HIM
Easy to follow his pre-lab videos and instructions! Very knowledgable

Sommerfeld was a very caring, soft spoken, and down-to-earth professor. Though this class doesn't use PE, Sommerfeld had physical practice sheets and would go through them on the board. He is very understanding and easy to approach after class, and is very generous with his curves. He doesn't deserve the low ratings. I'd 100% take him again!!
Great professor and super easy to talk to if you have any questions. Take with him over any other chem profs if you can!

I took Sommerfeld last year (winter 2024) and was curious to look at his RMP now and so surprised to see it so low. Sommerfeld was a great lecturer and went through all the practice problems on the board and gives lots of resources outside of class to do good on exams. I took 143 with him and Finley and prefer Sommerfeld BY FAR.

He knows what he's talking about and passionate about what he does but his grading system is the worst. We have to calculate our grade percentages from a formula he will give to us after each exam and assigns way too many ALEKS topics and only gives us 2.5-3 weeks max to finish which doesn't give us time to study for the exams. 10/10 hard grader.

he is a nice person but his grading and teaching style does not make any sense. Read his feedback and did it exactly how he wanted but still took points off because it wasn't good enough. Spoke to him multiple times to see what I could do but wasn't helpful at all.

This professor cares about his students but the work outside class proves a challenge for many students. Although below 50% test grade averages, no improvements have been made to the homework load and course so far. He is a passionate kind professor, just wish the fault in the short exam time was addressed. Great professor, poor course
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Summerfeld is a very harsh grader, I'm sure if I took PChem with him I'd rate him a bit differently. He does assign a lot of work. I liked sommerfeld as a person though. He was very social and would check up on all of his students to make sure they were doing well. You don't usually get teachers like that, so it was nice.

Sommerfield is by far the WORST professor I've had the displeasure of having. His grading is designed in a way to intentionally screw your GPA, and his lab instructions are not consistent with what is needed in your lab reports. STAY AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible. I have never seen such a bad teacher. Some teachers earn bad ratings but they still have an organized way of teaching. He was the vaguest teacher I have ever taken. His expectations are NOT clear, after completing an assignment he will grade something that wasn't part of his expectations. No good feedback and he's also rude.

In class practice problems were always much easier than his exams. Exams were hard as sometimes questions would have us make an assumption or use an equation we had never used before. Also only grading on exams with a small curve was tuff.

Nice guy, but class is just dry and boring. The flipped class format just does not work for zoom. It's hard to get motivated with him and how the content is taught, but that's pretty normal for pchem.

Seems nice, grades like a beast. Took a month to grade assignments, which led to not knowing when I was making mistakes until halfway through the class. Impossible to get a 4.0. Vague in explanation, because he wants you to figure it out.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AVOID him if you can. Final does NOT reflect anything learned in the quarter. Very vague in explanation and in lecture, you would think you're doing okay and learning but on the exam, it's a whole different level. Does not prepare you at all for exams. Unsure of expectations for students' learning.

This professor is the human version of a never ending podcast, bring headache relief cause this is a marathon not a lecture. kind, but he WILL talk until the very last second, just when you think he's done another 90s story begins. You'll leave with a full brain, aching muscles, somehow sore legs from sitting. but it's a verbal endurance test.

A bit awkward, yes. Slightly tangential in delivery, yes. But not excessively hard or punitive. Taken several classes from him and, despite the fact that the "doesn't give many 4.0's" I earned three from him. Attend the lectures, actively participate and take ownership of your learning. Most who didn't do well expected the prof to spoonfeed them.

There was some confusion earlier in the quarter, as it was his first time teaching online and using Canvas, but overall it was an okay class. I loved the subject and the readings. But I found it hard to engage with the lecture due to how long he talks. He is very open to answering students questions. So ask a lot and make the class engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dan is scatterbrained and imperfect, but incredibly knowledgeable. He's in his element when he doesn't rely on his powerpoint and just lectures. He's easy to engage with, but you have to be willing to engage. I have taken multiple classes from him now and they were interesting and informative, but do require some significant effort on your part.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not say this class was particularly difficult, but it was confusing. Prof made it clear at the begining of the quarter that he would rather be doing research than teaching. His lectures seemed unplanned. He often would ramble and not start lecturing until 30-45 minutes into class. Reading and homework had nothing to do with lectures.
Gives good lectures, understands that life happens and is willing to be flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jacoby is passionate about his work--I'll say that. But, he has a very hard time communicating his thoughts and the concepts of the class. Often, we had to ask him to repeat or rephrase. What I disliked most about his style, though is that it was dry and repetitive. I do not believe I learned anything substantive, and I am sad I chose his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: terrible handwriting, lectures aren't relevant to assignments, only used the book twice, doesn't reply to email's, hell doesn't READ his emails. Puts assignments up the day their due, his instructions are trash actually doesn't even bother spell-checking. You also have to pay to read or watch things he assigns. Randomly assigns papers, no warning.
Worst decision ever was to take this class....

He said, "I rarely give 4.0s". If you need a high GPA for grad school, skip taking any class from him. He is not helpful, cryptic lectures, and very subjective with grading. Even if you're an awesome student, you'd never know it after his class.

This was probably on of the worst quarters I have ever had. The book is used in conjunction with online quizzes and homework which do not correspond to lectures-unplanned lectures that also just confuse and leave you to educate yourself and hope the tests cover what you learn. This is a waste of time and money.

I personally love Dan; he makes the content easy to understand while also adding personality to his class. Not only is he a great professor, but he is also always at student events, helping out and talking to everyone. LOVE HIM.
Great professor and encourages student to engage
Great professor, tries to engage students and work is fair.
he's chill fr
Lots of things you'll learn and easy grade!
Super fun professor, makes class engaging, great guy in general. Not much homework.
One of the best professors I've ever had! Super energetic classes, and not super homework heavy! Respects your time, and I was out of class early most days.

Dan is a great Operations professor. You will learn a lot of random excel stuff in this class. He takes the time to make sure the slowest students are able to catch up-- which can be frustrating for the students working at a faster pace. He is also very chatty and gets side tracked a lot, but I don't consider that a downside.

Professor Daniel is such a nice and kind professor. I took BBUS 340: Operations and Project Management. He brought an incredible amount of energy to every class and made Excel exercises and heavier concepts feel approachable and fun. Kept the class engaged with real-world examples. Has a great sense of humor as well. Definitely would recommend.
