reviews.comment: I threat him that he will have to see me again next quarter if he fails me. Hope he will give me at least a 2.0 so I don't have to do operation or supply chain EVER for the rest of my life.

Really knows the material and high energy class. Rarely read off the slides, interacted as much as possible with students. Can be a little much at times but brings good energy. Homework is assigned in a 3rd party website that costs $. Most HW is due spread out through 3 or 4 days in the quarter, very much work at your own pace.
Good prof, knows the subject well. Very lively and high energy class, would recommend.

Cool feller gives a long half hour break, having him is like having a old teenager  with ADHD and sugar high teach a class, but its great. 10/10 recommend him if you extroverted and needs to yap about stuff after class
cool feller, having him is like having a old teenager with adhd and sugar high teach a class, and does very well at teaching it.

Very chill and reasonable when it came to assignments. This review is for a BCORE class meaning that it's just an entry to college level class and things aren't taken to seriously. Hosted class potlucks and made jokes with the students and the class was more about hanging out.

Dan is an excellent professor who clearly knows his material and does a great job teaching it. Everything you need for the exams is thoroughly covered in class, so attending and paying attention is crucial. The textbook and supplemental homework are helpful for reinforcing concepts but aren't mandatory for success. Come prepared & ready to engage.
You are not required to attended the class, however he gives in class quizzes randomly.

Great Professor! TAKE HIM! Honestly if you just semi pay attention and follow his excel examples for formulas, you will be more than fine. Really nice, funny, and understanding. 1 homework a week (unlimited attempts) if that, quizzes once a week (maybe), group presentation, potlucks, and a pretty interesting course.
W

Professor Dan really knows his stuff. He often taught part of the lecture using just a whiteboard, showing he didn't even need PowerPoint slides to explain things well. The class moves decently fast, so get ready to take notes. However, Dan gave us at least a 15min break every session, making learning the content completely manageable. Great class!

Great teacher! Hard class, but he made it easier, gets rid of lowest hw grades, gives long time for completion, take home tests, notes posted. He does what he can for you to succeed. Class is through excel, but he teaches everything you need. Pop quizzes, but easy grading, and easy questions. Never a stressful class, I definitely recommend Dan!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Having Professor Dan for Operations & Project management has been such a blast! Yes, the class is quite lecture heavy and pop quizzes happen often. However, his enthusiasm for teaching and his humorous nature make him a well-rounded professor. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I recommend showing up to all classes to understand the material better.

He's a great professor. He makes jokes throughout the class to keep students engaged. He's a great guy. The content itself is okay. The class is pretty boring, it's lecture-heavy and has a lot of excel class work. The only thing I didn't like was the random quizzes. We never know the topic of the quiz, when he will give them or what format they are

I was able to keep focus like 40% of the time in class because I have ADHD and I still got a solid grade. He takes a bit to grade assignments and isn't super involved for homework but that's fine. He is hard to reach outta class. If you wanna do well with him just pace out the homework, come for the quizzes and contribute during group project.

Professor Dan makes the class interesting.With group projects and course related games , the class is more fun than usual. It can be inferred he has put in much effort in his teaching . He is easy going with good humor .The class isnt hard ,as long as you participate in class and complete the homework. Bonus point,he gives a lot of extra credits .
Very good prof. Need to buy the Pearson course but don't need the textbook.
very fast paced and difficult material.
The midterm was not very good and the homework is through a costly 3rd party site.

Dan was one of my favorite professors at UWB! Even though statistics wasn't my best subject, he helped create a clear understanding of the topics. He's super nice and approachable and would always help me out whenever he could. Assignments were through Pearson, and we had a couple of group projects throughout the quarter.

has a condescending demeanor he thinks is "relatable" to students, but treats students like preschoolers. So far this quarter hes been very behind on assigning groups and quizzes. Everything weve done so far is automatic premade assignments through a $120 coursework website

Easily the worst professor at UWB. Just dives right into using Excel in lectures with none of the students able to follow along. He uses advanced key shortcuts and commands and refuses to show the students what they are because "they should google it, it's a stats class not an excel class". Horrible fake personality, does not care about students.
Hard class, not understood his quizzes!
Very humorous guy and makes lectures bearable. Participation and attendance is really important, since majority of the work is group work.

Was unable to properly facilitate group projects within a stats class, a few of my peers and I had to do our team's project all by ourselves. When we approached him, he basically said he can't do anything about it ("Honestly, I don't care"). He's a fun and relaxed prof usually, but I would never take his class again. Grading scale was weird too.

Absolutely loved Dan, he is such a kind person and is very passionate about supply chain and honestly makes you want to learn. He uses Pearson for HW but you do not have to get a textbook! He also responds super quickly to discord messages (yes he is on discord). Overall super funny guy and a great prof

He is hands down the best professor I have ever had. I would even call him a good friend in the business world. He is super passionate about Operations Management and enjoys talking with students or taking any questions. Lectures are great and exams are fair enough for us to really hone in our knowledge of the material. Please take him if you can.

Please take this professor for Operations Management. He is the best professor I have ever had and he is amazing in explaining the material and making sure we do well on excel and the class itself. His exams are reasonable and do provide excellent practice on the material. Two group projects but super lenient. 100% would take him again.

Professor Dan is extremely nice and makes the class fun, he truly cares about the student's learning and warn you in advanced to prepare. He is available for questions after class or during office hours, and he will explain things again if you ask during his lecture. Knowledge of Excel is extremely important to succeed in this class.

Professor Nielubowicz really cares about helping his students learn statistics. You can tell hes really passionate about statistics and wants the best for his students. It does start off as a slow class, but dont let that fool you into thinking you can skip classes. Near the end theres a lot of new material, but he explains everything very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Nielubowicz was amazing for BBUS215. You can tell hes really passionate about what he does and has solid knowledge on the subject. He makes class interesting and it was just fun being in class. I highly recommend showing up to class as slides are confusing by itself. Excel knowledge is needed but he goes over it through examples.

I had Professor Nedita for 3 Classes (B BUS: 220, 221, and 301). At first, I found his flipped course (watch the lecture before class and practice during class) weird, but I actually really liked it. The expectation is pretty clear, and he's very approachable. He also lets you out of class 45mins to 1hr early which I really liked.

One of my favorite professors great at answering questions and explaining concepts. Usually lets class out 40 minutes early. Tests and quizzes make up a large portion of the grade but aren't too difficult, and the grading system is fair. Overall not a difficult or time consuming class if you ask questions and do the homework.

Really easy class! It's a flipped course, and most learning happens before class, which may not be for everyone, but it was good for me. Quizzes and major tests were easy and pulled from lectures and class sessions. Class activities can't be made up, so attendance is necessary but still lenient.

High expectations from students - recordings are hard to watch with someone who has ADHD. Attendance will impact class exercise grades. Not accommodating when it comes to students with Disability. Professor is very nice but students with learning disability might find this a harder class. I dropped.

Professor Nedita is the best professor I have ever had. He gives great lectures and he really cares about his students. He's always avaliable for help and gives great feedbacks. Midterms and final are easy if you paid attention in class and do the work. Would definitely take him again if I could.

Prof Codrin Nedita is easily one of my favorite profs ever at uwb. I took him for both micro & macro. As long as you show up, take notes, ask qs, and study, you'll do well! If you see him listed for class, just take it :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had!!! You will easily pass if you watch his lecture videos and take notes. Drops the lowest quiz and exam score and always ends class about 45-60mins early. Assignments in class are done in small groups and are fairly easy.

W PROF!! watch the lectures and take notes, they'll be super helpful for both midterms and final. go to office hours but most of class work is from lectures, the practice tests were very helpful for the real thing.  You probably won't need the textbook tho :)

One of the best professors I have ever had. Prof. Nedita is very knowledgeable and is very clear on what is expected of the students. He's very kind and understanding and his flipped structure is excellent for my learning. Drops 5 lowest in-class assignments, 2 lowest quizzes, and the final could replace a midterm score. Overall, amazing teacher.

One thing to know is that the class is flipped so lectures must be watched before class. The professor himself is a very nice guy and I'd say fairly lenient and understanding. The quizzes and exams are all multiple choice which I feel helped me succeed a lot.
He's alright not my style of teaching. My fault I got this grade, you should take if you need a Micro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: professor nedita is a very good econ professor. layout of class was odd at first but you'll get used to it. class has 2 midterms and a cumulative final. In class you'll review everything you learned from the lectures he has recorded and answer the clicker questions attached. not hard but interesting class, id recommend nedita!

Best micro/macro prof at the school, well-versed in the material and very straightforward format for the lessons. take notes, there are 2 midterms and a cumulative final, but should be easy if you pay attention and take notes.

Codrin Nedita's reviews are very misleading. The majority of my class ended up getting below a 3.0 GPA. His Cumulative Final has a short time limit, is in person, no notes, 80 questions long, and covers roughly 10 chapters worth of material. Every person I know who took this class regrets taking it due to the complexity and length of the exams.

This is the third time I've taken one Codrin's classes. Not necessarily because it's an easier class but his teaching style makes any topic very simple to understand compared to other professors. If you are trying to decide between him and another professor, PICK HIM!!

100% gotta make sure to do the out of class video lessons, its possible to figure it out without them but is hard. Grades are complicated but at the same time super easy to understand. Overall very caring an helpful.
He might have a slight accent that could be a little hard to understand, but he is awesome, compassionate, and really cares about his students. amazing professor!

Great class and professor. Assigned a video anywhere from 30 mins to an hour or so long prior to class, along with 5 or so "clicker questions" worth a point each. In class was typically used to go over the material and answer questions, and would rarely run over 75-80 mins. Very open to answering questions if you have any.

Amazing teacher!! Class was used for going over practice questions and before class, you just needed to watch the lecture videos. I never had to spend hours going over Rcommands unless I was exam studying because he teaches and goes over everything so well in class. 5 HWs every couple weeks and we had in class graded exercises that weren't too bad.

You can tell he truly loves to teach. He's a very patient teacher and always encourages people to ask questions, he will never make you feel dumb! His grading policies are also very reasonable, so you should def be able to pass the class with flying colors. Highly recommend!!!

He assigns 45-50min long videos to watch before class, and then goes over the material for an hour in class. Although the videos are sometimes annoying to watch, they actually really help with my understanding of the material. He includes graded "clicker questions" that you answer throughout the video (super easy, multiple choice). I recommend

Had him for 220 and 221 and can easily say he is the best teacher I have had in my entire life! Spends an hour going over material and always asks if anyone needs help understanding, then the next hour of class is office hours if you need additional help. I've never had a more clear understanding of a topic or class and he is very easy to approach!
Legend. Best professor I've ever had.

Took him for both 220 & 221, hands down the best prof I've had so far. As long as you put your time into taking notes on lecture videos outside of class, going to class just reassures your understanding of the topics (which are explained coherently). All quizzes & exams are 99% like the practice ones, so if you work hard enough an A is attainable!

Codrin is an amazing professor. The recorded lectures are very clear and subsequently he lets his students out of class 45 minutes early. He also drops your lowest grades for certain things to give you a better chance to succeed. I wish he taught higher level economics courses so I could take him again.

time and effort = easy A. Final and 2 midterms are based on hw quizzes. hw quizzes are based on hw practice quiz. If you remember this and understand the concepts and how to solve topics you will do well. Extra credit on test and group work / clicker questions about lecture videos are very forgiving, count top 20 only or something like that.

Great professor, and I loved how the material was taught. Lots of outside-of-class time, 1 hour in between classes at minimum (not including study time and extra learning time). Drops lowest grades which helped a lot, but final and midterms were heavily weighted, if you do poorly on these it is impossible to save your grade, primary factor of grade
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nedita is really invested in each student's success. This class is really easy if you watch all the Panopto lectures and answer all of the clicker questions. Take diligent notes on the recorded lectures and participate in his questions in class. Take advantage of all of the extra credit he gives via poll everywhere!

One of the best 'teachers' i've had. I felt like I was actually learning material every class and it was thanks to his teaching style. Super nice and wants you to succeed. Explains topics to the point where you're an expert on the subject. Would recommend to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He makes everything super understandable and him having the recordings before the class is meant for his lecture to support and reinforce his lesson plans!

He wants everyone to get a 4.0 and uses the same example, which helps you understand the concepts. I solved all the exercises, homework, and practice exams until I got every question right and was averaging 90 on every exam. He loves every question he gets, especially his exam Q&A sessions. Taking macro with him too. Good professor and person too!
super lenient, very organized, very insightful, knowledgeable professor, amazing professor overall. Had him for Micro and Macro best professor i've had at UW bothell so far. Highly recommended!!!

Honestly one of the best prof at UW Bothell. Most of the practice problems will be on quizzes, midterms, and finals. As long as you do the work you will be fine. Focus on receiving a 100% on ALL the practice quizzes, midterms, and finals problems sets and you'll get an A+.

BEST PROF EVER! I knew nothing about microecon but solely watching his lecture videos by myself did wonders. Coming into class just reassured I understood the content. Everything is well-taught & straightforward. Quizzes/exams are EXACTLY like the practice ones on Canvas. He's a sweet prof, it is almost guaranteed you'll get an A if you really try!

BEST professor I have ever had. Take him for micro/macro. You will actually learn concepts and understand economics. You watch lecture videos before class and then go over them in class. Quizzes are very easy, and so are exams. Answers all questions and CLEARLY explains answers. Wish more professors were like him. Miss his class.

Professor Nedita has become one of my new favorite! He is caring and really wants to see his students do well in his class! Two midterms along with the final, recordings to watch over and take notes. Definitely recommend taking notes and knowing the material as soon as you can! He made the class environment feel comfortable to ask questions.

His lectures are good, he calls it a "flipped" class structure where you have to watch the lectures as recordings he made for his COVID time classes and you do exercises in class.
Tips:
1. at least half of the questions on the quizzes are the same as the questions in the homework(quiz prep)
2. Same goes for the tests

Super understanding and overall amazing professor. Already ready to answer your questions, lectures, both in class and recorded were easy to follow. Effort is needed to succeed in this course but it's all very straight forward and if you take notes and do the homeworks the tests are the ame questions from the homework. Would definitnely recommend.

This professor is a top 5 teacher I have ever had. He makes getting an A in his class super easy. Practice exams are super similar to main exams and lowest grades from each category are omitted. Honestly easiest 4.0 's of my life. If you fail with this professor consider community college cause this professor is clear and super helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Would recommend him over any professor in the entire business school tbh. He's brilliant, and he knows exactly how to help students learn, not just make them listen. Grading is as clear as it gets, and a lot of assignments get dropped at the end of the quarter. Definitely prioritize getting his class over any other class in your schedule.

bro is the best prof ive had here. i took micro with him and his 8:45 am class was painful but worth it. he answers every question with detail and different examples, always making sure you understand before he moves on. i honestly love him so much and i wish i he taught more classes. def take him over any other professor teaching micro/macro
Best professor at UW. You will pass with an A if you put in time and effort outside and inside of class. Communicate with him as well, his at home lectures are the best.

I was super nervous to learn about Economics, but I am glad that I got to be in Professor Nedita's class. He is very understanding and his instructions are super clear and easy to follow. Great teacher!

Nedita is a great professor. His video lectures are straightforward and the fact that he reviews them in class makes understanding the content really easy. He cares for his students and genuinely wants them to pass. Everything in this class is equally weighted. Exams are not tricky, and as long as you show up and participate, it's an easy A.

Professor Nedita was really amazing! Clear lectures and was very willing to help and very good at explaining problems. His videos and classes are helpful. His exams are not tricky, they are very straightforward and as long as you watch the lecture videos and do the homework they are fairly easy. Would definitely take his class again.

Professor Nedita is very educated and clearly understands the course well. His lectures are amazing and the class organization as a whole is great. I'm not saying he's an easy grader - the class does require effort. As long as you actually try, you'll do great. He is very accessible and is always happy to help answer questions/clear any confusion.

Mr.Nedita definitely shows that he cares about his students learning. In order to do well in this class you need to watch the online lectures. As long as you do that you will have success in this class. It is a lot of material so know if you fall behind even once, you will not be able to catch up. Take it seriously from the start .

My favorite teacher at the school! His teaching style is something that I like, watching lectures and reviewing the material in class later. Clicker questions, quizzes and exams were fairly easy. I would 100% take him classes again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Some of the clicker questions are tough but fair, he's a really good teacher though and does office hours in the last half hour of class which is really helpful if you have questions because you don't have to go out of the way.

The class material is really easy, however he overcomplicates it by giving the student 1-2 minutes on each question. The final has more than 80 questions, and half of them require calculations. Calculating 40 questions surely will take more than 1-2 minutes for each one. Time has no correlation with understanding the material, and he doesn't get it

I could not have asked for a better prof for macro. You could tell he was actually passionate about the material he was teaching as well as really nonweldable. Biggest tip for his class is to take notes on the preclass lectures and you'll naturally learn everything from that.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Literally the best professor ever. Don't hesitate to take him. Macroeconomics is hard but he explains it so clearly. We have an hour prerecorded lecture then he lectures us again in class. All we have to do is take the quizzes and good notes. Rest of it is all easy after that. I highly recommend him, I would take him again for sure!

Amazing lectures, class organisation, and teacher! Honestly, one of the best profs I've ever had. Practice, practice, practice is key in this class. This is important to clicker questions, quizzes, and exams. If you do, you'll do very well in the class. There are extra credits in the class.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Our class was supposed to be in person but was online. He prerecorded lectures and each lecture was detailed and clear. I absolutely loved them and they were my biggest help. The professor makes projected grade reports and guesses what the final grade is projected to be which is also so nice. Motivational.

I really enjoyed his teaching style for this class. I have nothing but positive things to say about my experience. If you needed help or had questions, he would make sure that they were answered. The lectures were well put together and you didn't need to read the textbook to make sense of what he was explaining. 120% would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Nedita is a great professor. As long as you watch the lecture recordings before class and do the problems, you will have no issue with passing this class. The textbook was optional, but he does a great job explaining everything in the lectures. There are two midterms and one final, he is pretty generous with the time limit on it though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's one of the best profs I've had so far! He includes many examples in his lectures, so we'd have a greater understanding. He's helpful. Quizzes every week and based on HW. Doing many practice problems helped me succeed in the midterms and final. Clicker questions mainly suck cause they're timed quick, so I'd review my notes and do HW beforehand.

Professor Nedita is a great professor who is very clear and prepared to help you succeed. He does make you work for your grade if you want an A. Weekly quizzes which are pretty similar to the HW. Quizzes corresponds to the exams as well so they were not too difficult. Panopto recording are super important and the clicker questions in them suck.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor. Had him for both microecon and macroecon, he gives tons of materials to prepare you for the midterms / finals. His lectures are also v clear. Def take him for econ courses!

prof codrin is too good for this world. i took econ 200 at uw seattle and was looking for an easier environment to learn macro... didnt think id be signing up for one of the best teachers ive ever had. he is incredibly understanding, straightforward, and super patient. he works very hard to make the content easy to understand!! such a good prof!!!!

Lots of group projects. But if given the option between him and another professor, choose him. He's genuinely caring and wants to make sure you understand the material. He always has a great attitude and is excited to teach.

One of my favorite professors ever. Extremely knowledgeable about his subject and always willing to help if you're struggling. Clear about his expectations up front, and even gives students the opportunity to make up for bad grades on previous tests by only counting your top quizzes. I highly recommend taking his class!

He explains every single detail and does not get mad when you ask questions. He's genuinely a great guy and if given the opportunity I would take him again in a heartbeat. He lectures and we do group activities at the end of the lecture so you do need to be present for class. If you're on the fence about him, just take the class. It was fun.

Best teacher I've ever had as far as course structure, teaching style & pacing go. So patient and cheerful. Minimal homework. No reading/textbook optional because you will only ever be asked questions from his lectures. Uses fun movie clips to reinforce concepts/break up monotony. I'm not a business major but he makes me wish I was!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really didn't like this teacher at the start. After taking two courses with him, I found him to be a very good teacher. If you plan on going forward with a business major, I recommend you to pay attention to his class as he explains concepts really well.

This professor is not forgiving. He will deduct points if you submit you work on exams for his entertainment which can bring your grade down a full letter grade. He is not understanding of technical issues and expects you to upload all the pictures for his lengthy exams with no grace time. I wouldn't recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice Professor, do practices and hw before the quiz and exam because they help you to have an idea of what will be on the exam but You need to actually understand the concept in order to do well on the exams because a lot of the questions are opposite of the practices.

I liked Mr. Nedita, while i had a hard time on the quizzes in the beginning he did teach some valuable lessons (Such as read the question a few times before you answer). He was a real help at office hours and his midterms, while large are pretty easy to do as long as your organize your notes and take good care that you study. hard but fair

Codrin Nedita is hands down one of the BEST professors at UW Bothell. His teaching strategy really keeps you on your toes because of "clicker" questions where he mildly tests you on concepts to make sure you're paying attention. He also makes each student custom check-points throughout the quarter to make sure you're on track with your grade!

If you can make sure to take him for BUS 310. He is way better than all the other professors! Yes he does have quizzes but they are super easy as long as you understand the homework which he posts detailed answers and explanations for before quizzes. If you don't understand something go to his office hours he is super nice and helpful!

He's an amazing economics professor. I didn't really understand econ before I had him, and my econ prereqs were the lowest scores on my transcript, but after him I get it. He's always careful to take time and explain things many different ways.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor, his lectures are clear and he makes sure that the class understands the content before moving on. Quizzes and tests are easy, participation matters in the sense that he does a ton of clicker questions so you have to pay attention but they aren't difficult in any sense. He really cares, even takes the time to get to know students.
Solid professor and class. Really liked it especially the second half.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: By far the best teacher I've had in my academic career. He clearly cares about his students, and their ability to learn based on his lectures. He is passionate and knowledgeable about economics. HW wasn't graded but we had quizzes on the "due date". Great class if you have work hard, study for quizzes/exams, ask questions, and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: got like a 2.5 in microeconomics took his class and ended up with a 3.5. if you attend every class and pay attention you'll pass with at least a 3.0. he's a really good teacher

The best prof at UWB. He has a perfect teaching technique. He explains all concepts clearly and is always asking if anyone needs further clarification. I will really miss having him I wish he could teach every course tbh.
Best professor I have ever had, really clear with his topics. He made everything super easy for student to digest.

Codrin is the best professor that I've ever had at UWB. He's extremely kind, and genuinely cares about your learning. He does anything he can to make sure everyone is with him and understands the material. Textbook is not necessary because he does such a good job at explaining material in lectures. Tests are based on practice exam/quizzes.
He's simply the best professor. I recommend that everyone take him for economics.
Nedita is an amazing professor whos very passionate about what he teaches. There are literally no problems with the way he teaches his class. One of the best teachers on campus.

Professor Nedita is very knowledgeable when it comes to economics. He's clear, funny, but he makes you work for your grade. Exams are much harder than other assignments. We have to print our notes, but I personally never used the textbook. The course consists of three exams, daily clicker questions, and quizzes based on homework.

Codrin is by far the best professor I've ever had in my life. He made learning economics (both Micro and Macro) a lot easier for me. His lectures and explanation on topics were so clear, I didn't even buy the textbook for the class. He does anything possible to help you learn and succeed if you put in the effort. He is also very sweet. Love him!

In all my time at UWB, Nedita is one of my favorite professors I've had. I took him for both Micro & Macro and he's definitely the best professor to take those with. His clickers are easy if you pay attention and the quizzes are straight out of the homework. Nedita actually cares about your understanding and you as a person. Fantastic prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class builds up anxiety and pressure through clicker questions. You are constantly being graded for everything you do in class. However, he makes the problems easy to understand and explains them well. Well-respected and willing to help outside of class. Keep up with the coursework and in the end you should be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very clear and concise in lectures. Simplifies complex concepts so that they can be easily understood. Offers lots of opportunities to pick your grade up. Class structure was super organized and the printable notes were awesome. He's super funny and makes you enjoy the class even if you aren't into economics. Do all practice Q's and HW's!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Codrin posts his slides on Canvas with some blanks to fill in. Print this out and use it to take notes, it's by far the most helpful resource in the class and helps a ton during lectures. Codrin's lectures are extremely clear, he simplifies things down and does well to give examples and check for understanding. Never opened the textbook, don't buy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Codrin is a great teacher! He is funny and does a really good job explaining the course content. He is always happy to answer questions and interacts with the students. Take this class!
Immersive involved descriptive

If you are taking Micro/Macro, take this professor! You are graded on weekly quizzes, clicker questions, group projects (answering questions as a group) and Exams. Honestly, if you show up to class, pay attention, and do the homework (not graded but great for practice problems), you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nedita is hands down one of the best professors Ive had the pleasure of taking at UW Bothell. If you need to take micro/macro econ, take his class!! Hes so easy to understand (besides his awful handwriting lol) and really cares about his students learning. Super nice guy with clear and concise lecture style!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The subject is tough but he is a fair grader, he is available to his students if you have questions and has daily office hours, the tests are tough but if you do the homework and study you should get a decent grade
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Nedita is one of the nicest professors I've had in my 2 years here at UWB. He is very clear in what he wants and what work you need to put in to succeed in his class. Almost after ever lecture, he emphasizes to take advantage of office hours if you are having troubles. Quizzes are exactly like the homework  - make sure to do it and you'll do great!

Codrin is so nice and will help you if you need it.  The class consists of three tests, group exercises, clicker questions, and weekly quizzes on the chapters.  He expects you to print the slides out and use them to take notes on.  The book is not required for class but it definitely helped me out a lot.

I've taken him twice, and I love him. Has a Romanian accent, but he's pretty easy to understand. Definitely have to work, but he makes it really simple to succeed if you put in effort. Super nice. Really easy to access outside of class. Posts power points on Canvas. Gives awesome explanations if you're confused. One of the best professors I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Although I did not get a good grade in the class he is an awesome professor. He expects you to print out the ppt slides and come to class to take notes on them. Some of his lectures are long but he generally throws in a video or two to make it interesting. We also do clicker questions and group questions during class. tip: go to office hours!

One of the nicest, caring professor's I've ever met! Always makes sure you understand the subject before he moves on and is willing to slow stuff down if you don't. Makes notes in class super easy with handouts. You have to come to class due to clicker questions which are a major portion of your grade otherwise a simple and easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: prof wasn't as bad as everyone said, he does talked for a bit ngl, but he will do everything support/ help you if you reached out to him. Not a bad prof if you just want to pass the class for putting a reasonable amount of effort. Unless you want to take the other one for having to put extreme efforts to finish all weekly assignments.

Pretty cool professor. He cares about your learning and engagement with the class material. The assigned projects are alright, and you just need to read the case studies and do some write-ups. His lectures are pretty boring, and he gets off track easily, but it's not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Be prepared to listen to him spend the first 30 minutes of 120 hour class every session on ranting about Trump...
grading papers by word count only.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The professor just goes on tangents constantly. It's 2 hours of nonsensical rambling. Even his project instructions have tangents, I've resorted to putting his instructions into ChatGPT and asking it to simplify it and cut out all the fluff. 
All he talks about is Trump and British news articles. Absolutely nothing productive gets done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I didn't get feedback/grades for my assignments until the next quarter had already started. I don't understand why it took so long because his feedback is rarely over 5 words and won't point out specifically what's wrong. I think he's fixing the gradebook to match whatever course average he wants for the class. Complete waste of time, don't bother

This was the worst course at UW I've ever taken. You can expect Professor Shaw to take over any in-class discussion, frequently going off on tangents to share his unwanted life story and voice his absolute contempt for Trump. I ended up just doing the Global Business Plan during class with my airpods in to make my required attendance productive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took Professor Shaw for 480 for the summer quarter. The man knows some stuff and isn't afraid to talk about it. He does require a lot of case study and assigned readings, However, the support and resources offered along the way makes it the easiest 8 weeks I have had for a summer Quarter.

Do not take this professor. I have never in my four years at a University had a professor who talks so much. The class was during the summer so it was 2.5 hours each class period. He never stops talking. Even during the 10-minute break that we get, he still continues to talk. He goes off rants and talks about his life history rather than content.
It's one of those class that's just so easy to pass. Work each week is minimal.

Incredibly mean and condescending and the absolute worst at explaining anything. Homework is just busywork and only graded on word count. His lectures are boring, and he constantly goes off on pointless tangents. Your canvas grade is not your actual grade and he doesn't show you how your final grade is calculated.

I don't understand his bad rep; I honestly believe that people that complain are just lazy af. He can be a bit disorganized at times but he's extremely caring and puts a lot of effort in his classes. He's very accommodating too! If you actually want to learn, you'll enjoy this class; do the readings and work and you'll get so much out of this class

I'm not even done with the quarter but the amount of useless talking he does is just way too much for me. It's a hybrid class but doesn't matter if we're in person or online he just talks. He's disorganized and he just repeats the same stuff every class. I've been confused half the time. This could easily be an asynchronous class. It's so boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class time consists of pointless case study discussions that serve as Shaw's ideological soap box or as an opportunity to practice his poor stand-up. Doesn't grade your work based on quality, but rather word count and similarity score. Overall do not recommend. Lackluster professor who is disinterested in you and makes this disinterest obvious.

I got 3.8 as the final score. But he didn't even grade the two biggest project of this course: the CST and GBP. I had put so much effort into these projects. But he didn't grade them but still released the final GPA anyways. He won't read your case study, just have word account above 500 and low similarity score you will get full score.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tough grader, "Only God gets 10/10" Lol. His lectures are interesting enough as he tries to keep material relevant. Textbook chapter quizzes, 10 case study write-ups, in class prezi, global biz project, midterm, final... yeah.

His grading techniques are very confusing and not helpful for students. Had to buy a textbook that was rarely used, only for quizzes that weren't beneficial. Never gave us a lot of in-class time to work with our teams. Grades on a curve, which I guess is helpful, but you won't know your grade until the end of the quarter. Not super organized.

I had a chance to take professor Shaw for his (quarantine) 480 class. He is a neat professor, that put in a lot of effort to make the Zoom lectures interesting. His assignments and readings are relevant, interesting, and closely related to the textbook. He is an academic, so if you take this class, be careful to spellcheck and use good sources.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Chill guy and grades easy as noted in past comments. Weekly case studies are easy. Lectures are quite boring but you don't need it to pass the quizzes. Quizzes are two attempts, unlimited time. Only challenging part is the project, but even that he tends to give out average of 3.4.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Doesn't read what you turn it, he just checks the length. Grades feel super arbitrary like he 'feels' like he can't give out 100%. The content is 30min of lecture crammed at the end of every 1.5 hour 'discussion' on tangents. Content is expressed in online 'exams' but the answers are on Quizlet. No exams. Grades on attendance, but a waste of time.

This professor was utterly the worst professor I have had in the School of Business. Unforntunately, from unclear grading criterias to full on not really learning anything from him. Professor Shaw is what I would dub as one of the teachers that grades on if he likes a student or not and not on the content of their work. Do not take this teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the worst professor Ive ever taken. Youll learn nothing from lectures or textbooks. He didnt start grading assignments until the end of the dead week. Plus, he's hard to read and you don't know whether or of you are performing well in the class. As long as you raise your hand during case discussions and presentation Q&A you'll be fine ��
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course content is easy but he doesn't grade anything. At the end of the quarter, with no explanation and no grades on Canvas, he gave me a random final grade. He says he aims to make the class average a 3.5 so not everyone will get a high grade. Also, he talks about himself more than he talks about the course and he never responds to emails.

Class was overall fairly easy work-wise, but he refuses to let you know your grade in the class. Grades are due in 2 days, and I just now got my grades back for the case studies, and nothing else. Absolutely no chance to know your grade or improve in the class, zero feedback and are completely left in the dark throughout the whole quarter.

David is a nice enough guy, but I didn't learn much from his class. Lectures were dull, but he gives pretty much everyone between 3.5 - 3.9. Also, he is sensitive and gets his feelings hurt easily. He won't take it out on your grade, but he will definitely be passive aggressive if you don't agree with him. Take his class if you want an easy A.
just show up and talk. give your opinion and everything is good. you won't get a 4, but you'll get somewhere close as long as you do this
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very autonomous. May talk for a very, very long time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Took 2 of David Classes in the same quarter. 470 and 471. Both with a 2 pages case study weekly and a final project. As long as you turn in the case studies on time and meet the 2 pages requirement, you will get full credits for all the assignments. Extra credit towards the end of the quarter. Lectures are pretty boring. He could be funny though.
Easy case studies every week. Lectures are pretty dry, but sometimes interesting. Online quiz with two attempts, if not unlimited.

his grading system makes it hard to get a 4.0, and he does not care. He thinks a 4.0 is only for if you go "Above and beyond", not if you do every single assignment, turn them in on time, and learn the material

The class itself is not extremely difficult, he's weird grading system is. He doesn't believe in traditional grading so he came up with his own unique one. In my opinion it is poop because he will not let you know your grade until the end of the quarter. Throughout this whole quarter my course grade as been locked so I have no idea if I am passing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really odd grading style that makes it hard to receive an A. If your taking it because you think its an easy A, its not. Majority of grade comes from 2 assignments and you won't even know your final grade until the end of the class. Dont bother emailing either he doesn't respond :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fully asynchronous class. Clearly outlined assignments that are easy to complete and don't take too long to do. Gives clear feedback and allows you to resubmit papers for regrading before the due date for full credit. He wants you to succeed; you just need to do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This is the second class that I have taken from Professor Goldstein. On a usual week, there is a documentary to watch, which is followed by a discussion board. I personally really like his mastery grading system because he allows revisions for big assignments. This class is an easy 4.0 if you do the work on time.

This class is based off of completion until you reach the final essay. Meaning, you just have to successfully write about a certain discussion based ques and respond to someone else by the deadline and your set. I did this class for the credit and got an A, so I think you just have to be on top of the work 2 times per week. Take it if you need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The grading system is very, very weird. It would be better if he just did a traditional grading system. Some films are interesting, some are not. The TA does all the grading, which kind of made me feel as if he doesn't participate in the class. Key for getting a good grade: REVISE! Revising the essays is the best way to get the maximum grade.

One of the easiest classes I've had yet in college. Gives a set schedule for his students to go off of for the weekly work he assigned and it made everything stress-free. Only annoying thing: weekly chapter quizzes (it could take you a long time to get 100% on them). I enjoyed him as a professor and will be taking him again in the summer. Easy A.

BIS300 is required for IAS major.  Took this online and I'm glad I did.  Class uses "mastery grading" so you had to go above and beyond if you wanted that 4.0.  The work was all reasonable.  My group coordinated our group project over Discord & one Zoom meeting, which worked well.

Get ready for a lot of reading. His 'Mastery Grading' means you must complete almost every assignment before the deadline or your grade can suffer. 1-2 essays throughout the quarter. You are also required to buy a textbook to access the readings so something to note. Overall not bad, but is easy to miss a discussion post and fall behind
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This course is simply watch 1 movie a week and write about it. Prof does 'Mastery Grading' which can be good but if you miss any discussion deadlines, there are no late submissions and can be bad for your grade. If you can guarantee you do all assignments, I would recommend. Otherwise, your GPA may slip. Beware. 1-2 Essays are involved also

I disliked the mastery grading system & found it somewhat frustrating that if you forgot to reply to someone else (replies had to be done on a different day and between Wed 10pm to Sat 10pm) you'd get a 0 even if you did initial prompt. No late submissions for discussions and some prompts were strange, but course itself is fine.
He was the best! Everything is explained well and very interesting. Would take his class again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literature genres class on American plays - online. He really knows how to teach online in an engaging fashion. He was very excited about the stuff he was teaching and it carried over in the video lectures. VERY clear about grades (scales, points, etc.). There was a medium amount of reading but the books were so cool. Take him!

I've taken two literature classes with David now (BIS 379 and this), both online. He has a very unique approach to grading and to lecturing on the subject matter, and gives us a lot of interesting activities and writing prompts around each book. Highly recommend going to his online office hours, they're really helpful and he's very kind.

Honestly one of the best well-structured courses I've taken, he's also very progressive by trying to implement a different grading style despite it not being the easiest to work with Canvas's outdated grading style he keeps you up to date and on track. The films he chooses are both relevant, enjoyable, and thought-provoking! Loved his class.
Easy and interesting class. Unique way of grading. Good video lectures and nice books to read.

Caring professor and seems very knowledgeable, but his assignments (online course) were a bit unorganized, instructions in canvas were a bit all over the place, and his way of grading was confusing at first. I do wonder if this class may have been better in person. On the positive, he was easy to reach and very understanding if you are struggling.
STAY AWAY..

This class promotes critical thinking and writing about literature. He is very well-informed and encourages that everyone participates. Classes are lecture-based and graded based on a few short papers. He is a great guy but his somewhat old-school teaching style may not be for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is indeed very responsible, but I feel that I have been targeted. For those who want to take his course, you need to pay attention. Whether you take this course or for IAS credits, this course is not so easy. Good Luc k

I liked him. He covers a lot of material, but, at the same time, he does it in a way that you are able to retain the information well. Really cares about student's learning the material. He listens to student input & reactions seriously. Very available for interaction.
Excellent professor, helpful when students needed and very inspiring teacher. If you want to learn useful information about films and movies, he is the best option for you!e

This was my favorite class at UWB. You do need to study the terms and the (online) textbook is rather helpful. David is very nice and knows a lot about film studies. He uses a website that has film clips and mini-lectures with scenes from the movies. It's a really good experience. The only thing I don't vibe with is his harsh grading scale.

Awesome guy, very personable and he made in class discussions fun. The only thing I dont agree with are his grading policies. According to him he graded using the UW scale, and my final grade was above a 95, which should technically be a 4.0. He gave me a lower GPA, which I felt was unfair.

Definitely one of the better professors for the CLA core (Caplow sucks). He's aware of the small humanities representation on campus and does his best to make sure everyone feels safe and respected in class. Also he's a man of culture with his taste in music and movies.

David is a nice person, but not one of the more impressive profs I've had at UW. His instructions are detailed to the point of being confusing and overly complicated. He let class out early every day, which gave me the impression that he was not interested in lecturing or getting deeper into discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I heard from fellow classmates about how easily structured the class is to how carefree and relaxed Goldstein is, which to his credit were true. However, his grading is inconsistent, readings are nauseating, & feedback he gives is vague and even through numerous visits to the WaCC, assignments never quite met his expectations. Overall, okay guy.
What a good man. Take his class. He's caring and funny and doesn't treat you like your a child. The class moves at the perfect pace

Prof. Goldstein was one of my favorite teachers at UWB. BIS 464 was a film class and the discussions were engaging and useful. He made it easy to participate and was clear with directions on assignments and gave great feedback! I would definitely recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: David Goldstein is a great professor who understands his students. Our class was fun and consisted of a bung of group work. We read a lot of books but none were challenging (just long). One short essay and one long essay which you could redo if you needed to for a better grade. Take Professor Goldstein, you won't regret it.

This is one of my favorite professors at UWB. His classes are always extremely easy, especially this capstone class. We do the same amount of work as all of the other capstone classes but on a much easier timeline. It is an easy A if you do all of the assignments. He is so chill and doesn't care about laptops or even phones in class. BEST teacher

One of my favorite teachers at this school. Probably the easiest class I have taken in college thus far. Still really interesting course though. He is so flexible and understanding especially with late assignments. The other teacher that teaches this gives quizzes every week, this teacher does NOT! Show up to class and your good. Fantastic teacher!
Regarding instructions, prof says one thing and grades favorably on what he urges not to do. Highly inconsistent.  He says that he is "not very well liked."  Trust your intuition!

I would never recommend this instructor based on my class' experience with him. By far the most inconsistent grader at UWB. Gave the class instructions then gave higher grades for what he told us not to do. I asked for feedback to help improve my projects and was told to get it from my peers.  He failed 3 people.
He was pretty good.  Class was a little bit to long and talks alottt but i would rate him a pretty easy grader
Good starter class for the BIS program.  I got to work at my own pace mostly though you do need to do some work.  I did think I'd learn a little more when it was over, but otherwise no complaints.
looking forward to taking another class with him!!

I've taken several courses with dr. goldstein and each time it has been a very pleasant learning experience. i was able to revise a paper that i didn't do well on and he was very helpful.  this quarter we only attend class for half the time, the other half is for working with groups on our own time.  it's very convenient and thoughtful of him.
Dr. G is DA MAN!  If you ask then you will receive.  Don't expect to go home empty--he will fill you with knowledge.  Lots to think about, little to lose.  I say go for it!@
No Comments
Interesting course, not to much work.  You can pretty much choose which books to read then write on them.  Professor is very clear when he lectures.

This was a course we HAD to take so it could have been gruesome, but Dr. G kept things simple and taught us the basics of writing and thinking.  This was a great intro to the Interdisciplinary Studies program without too much stress.
This was my "core" course and it was a great introduction to the program.  Grading was very generous and all instructions were clear and available in advance on the web.  Good basic writing course.

This was a literature course, which is not my fav, but it was OK.  Goldstein is a nice guy, doesn't talk too fast, and teaches you something.  Grading is more than fair.  Books and stories were generally fun, and the amount of reading was reasonable.
Great guy--very helpful, works through every step of the writing process.  Cares alot about his students.  Not that challenging, but you do learn how to write in this course.
Loved his teaching style. Loved the discussion groups .. Very clear .. Great teacher .. one of my favorites!
Very nice and down to earth teacher, was helpful and understanding. Definately a teacher you want

A little slow at times for my taste (David wants to be sure that EVERYONE understands the material), but it does lead to better discussions, I think.  The work is very manageable and the readings are interesting.  Grading is more than fair.

David makes learning fun and provides a lot of support.  He lets you rewrite a paper if you want and that was very helpful for me.  The films are generally very interesting.  A few of them are freaky but worth watching.
Thank goodness it's over
Very cute. Very smart.

I learned a lot in this class.  I've never taken a lit class before, but he was very good at teaching the basics while not being too boring or simple.  He was very excited about the stuff he was teaching.  He's also VERY clear about how your earn your grade (scales, points, etc.)  There was a medium amount of reading but it was usually interesting.

He was very unclear mostly because he believes in problem-posing education. If you don't like discussions and like the teacher to tell you what you need to do to get a good grade then he is not for you.

Has a very specific style he expects others to conform to. Does not actively practice what he teaches to be the beneficial or ideal learning environment. Group discussion with other students was the best part of this class. Possibly a better instructor if the subject was something he had interest in teaching.

This professor has favorite students. If you are not a favorite, don't bother trying to contribute to class discussion. This is a professor who creates an "in" and "out" group instead of a positive classroom climate which respects all viewpoints (conservative or liberal or somewhere in between).

A great professor, very understanding, very helpful and down to earth. He is very available and ready to help. Very clear, takes the time to explain, enjoys what he does, which makes a huge difference for students. Does not like slackers though!

Best professor I've had by far. 3 midterms that are super easy if you study and one of them gets dropped. Final is a bit harder though so you'll have to prepare yourself. Lectures are straightforward and easy to understand. Only thing I wish is that he would be teaching other calc classes.

He is the best cal teacher that I have, 3 midterms, the lowest one got drop, one final, but it so hard, all midterm is easy if you study. Homework is a lot, need to spend some time for it. The lecture is so easy to understand, easiest 4.0 class ever in this university.

Homework is due on every midterm day, and you can do it all in around a couple hours. There's 3 midterms, and one midterm is graded at half the points. (i.e. if you got 20/40 then you actually got 20/20 and the weight is the same).
Lectures give you everything you need, and there are videos if you miss the class.
Goated professor.
actually the best professor I ever had. He needs to be rewarded for the best teacher award because I never had a better experience in math until him. Please take him.

I don't think I have a words of how great of a math professor he is. I swear if he was my math professor for the rest the time I am in college, I'd practically be going to heaven. I have never met a better professor than him. It's unfortunate that he doesn't teach calc 2 or 3 I really wish he did.

Literally the goat. Lectures were so informational. I had trouble learning calc 1 in another course, but when I took it with Professor Hockstra I understood everything. Only thing I didn't like is how he couldn't be my prof for Calc 2.
take this guy, if you see his name just sign up for the class whatever it is.

He gets straight to the point and takes his time making sure we understand the material. He's also a very easy lenient grader and is passionate in teaching. Homework is often due every 2 weeks so you have lots of time to complete it. Drops one midterm and also adds 25 extra points if you turn in your hw on time. Had fun learning in his class!

He is easily the best professor I have had in my few years of college, the reason the difficulty is a 2 and not higher is because of how well he teaches, if you have questions or don't understand something, he is genuinely excited to teach you so its comforting. Great person, great teacher, if you have the opportunity to take his class, please do.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It's like finding a needle in a haystack. I'm so lucky to have this math professor over any of the others. It's so refreshing and heart-warming to have such a great professor for math. He's basically motivated completely by passion to teach and help students learn. He literally takes a fairy down to UW every day just to teach his students.

One of the best math professors! Outlines of what will be on the tests. Study guides, and in-class assignments help immensely with the exams. Workload is very manageable. The Final was a bit harder than the midterms because it's department based. Wonderful personality and energetic in class. I would recommend going to his lectures.

Professor Hockstra was probably the best professor I have ever had. He is so caring about his students, and his in-class lectures are so fun and engaging. It is hard not to smile while he is teaching because you can genuinely tell he is excited to be there. No matter what question you have, he will not make you feel stupid about it. THE GOAT!!

Mr Hockstra is a sweet and understanding person. Definitely an easy grade if you can put in the work for it, which is not even a lot compared to other classes. Homeworks had good deadlines, dropped one midterm grade, answers email fast, a great person overall.

A lecturer who really cares about his students understanding of course material. Tests were straightforward, and he was very accommodating when a cyclone hit our campus. I could understand the material really well because there was no external stress related to this class. Homework was flexible, I recommend this course if you have a busy quarter.

This is the best Math professor ever. He is so sweet and as long as you do your HW and to pay attention to study material you will be perfectly fine on test. He even let us drop one of the midterm score. His lecture might be a bit boring but honestly it not a biggie. The final may be harder cause I think all sections take a similar exam

This man is a treasure and must be protected at all costs. If you get a bad grade and find yourself blaming this professor there is likely something wrong with you mentally and spiritually. His lectures are easy to follow, he clearly outlines what will be tested, and his exams aren't the typical "gotcha" questions that lesser profs rely on. AAA+
Professor Hockstra is amazing to take for Calc 1 if you want to a good grade in this class. TAKE HIM!!! His policies are really good and he is really really nice!!
Overall just a really charming man and explained the concepts of calculus very well.

Professor Hockstra is a kind and compassionate educator. He is very thorough during lectures and goes out of his way to make lessons enjoyable. The work is not too burdensome as homework is assigned every lesson and takes an hour. He accommodates his students well and is overall a great teacher!

He's a very sweet and kind teacher. Cares a lot for his students. I'll give him the benefit of the doubt since he's a new hire, but struggled with Canvas and inputting grades in a timely manner. The curriculum for Precalc II is very well done although its mostly self-taught. Tests are straight-forward!
Very caring instructor, cares about student success. Highly Recommend Professor Hockstra
Very cool dude. Very patient with helping students. Also has a good sense of humor. As long as you pay attention to the lectures you should be good for tests.

The class was great, I actually ended up learning some stuff that I will use in the future about civic stewardship. I won't say that everything will end up being useful in everyday life, but I recommend Professor Dailey for this course. She really cares about her students and the course material.
The class is very disorganized and the instructions are unclear.
AI generates lectures and quizzes, but the coursework isn't hard or heavy.

I really enjoyed CSS211, prof made it fun and engaging. A few big projects but they never felt like busy work so I enjoyed them. Be prepared to be social and present up in front of the class so if thats not your thing beware. Prof very passionate about subject material so i actually learned alot
Light course work, many discussions. Be prepared to be engaged and participate. She will often put students on the spot regarding feedback. Supportive and passionate about the subject matter.

If you're looking to actually learn CS, don't take this professor. If you need this class to get by, then she's alright. She gives A LOT of HW assignments. Does not know what a return function does, enough said

reviews.comment: Professor really cares about her students. Lots of assignments but they're really easy to do. Easy A. Group project was fun and you learn a lot from this class.

Dharma was great! class was relatively easy as long as you pay attention in class, she's a bit strict with grading meaning that if you submit an assignment like even a couple mins late she'll take off 0.1-0.5 marks off. reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dharma is extremely charismatic and clearly loves teaching... but that doesn't make her a good teacher. Our cohort all struggled through this course. We would ask a question and get a million non-answers. She was all over the place. Her expectations were never clear, and many students' grades suffered because of it. This course was a bummer.

Dharma is always nice and helpful, yet this class is a bit boring and most people zone out during lectures, as they can be a bit long and dry. Daily in-class exercises are done so it's important to show up. Mainly group assignments all quarter with a final presentation. No tests. As long as you do the countless small assignments, you'll be fine

I enjoyed the class and its content, but the instructor was a little unorganized on Canvas. Although she uses powerpoint more often than many other teachers she is still a nice and engaging teacher. I liked listening to her lectures and she's easy to pay attention to. A good class overall.

Dharma is very understanding of students and just a very kind teacher. This class was very interesting and engaging, and had awesome class material and readings. I feel bad that there were some students who just didn't care or didn't show up.
This teacher is very easy to talk to and always there if you need any help. As long as you stay on top of your work it's a really fun class and pretty easy.

She's a caring and sweet professor. Lots of assigned work, but she teaches well and gives very helpful feedback. Quizzes are hard but worth little. Paper criteria and grading are fair and clear. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Great teacher. She really cares if you learn and understand the topics. Get a good group and you'll be solid.

I am taking her tech writing class and it's really good. There is a lot of work but Prof. Dailey is really easy to talk to, really helpful, and always here if you need any help. Do the readings, pay attention to lectures, and stay on top of the work and you'll be fine. You can tell her undergrad degree was in English in the way she teaches writing.

I really enjoyed this class. Prof. Dailey was accessible almost 24/7 and gave great feedback on all the assignments. She's understanding and accepts late work, at least in this class, so you will get full points as long as you put your best effort into it.

I am currently in Dharma's 301 class, and she is very good! I've heard other professors make it extremely difficult but she explains clearly and is so nice! reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great and caring prof for 301. Lectures are insightful. Lots of HW, but they're not difficult. Gives good feedback on papers. Quizzes are written by other 301 profs and are awful, but they're worth a few percent of the grade. Allows 1-3 sheets of notes on exams. Highly recommend her if you want a 301 prof who cares about students and teaches well.

One of the better options available for CSS 301. The class is still 301, though, unfortunately, which is why I can't give super high ratings.

Dharma is so kind, so caring, and extremely responsive. She listens to your struggles and questions. Class is easy to follow: there's no tricky questions, and no way to make you feel like you're in a dead end. Her lectures are really helpful if you want to learn about HCI and UX Design.

Professor Dailey was a really good teacher for the media design class. If you meet with her during office hours she is extreamly helpful. If you collaborate well on the group projects and participate in class you will get a good grade.

Out of class assignments took around a month to receive a grade.

The professor is always late to class by 10+ minutes, most times without notice, and has poor planning skills. It takes forever for her to grade projects. I learned the most from my table-mates and the peer facilitator than from the professor. Made many mistakes when grading and on worksheets.

I strongly dislike Oliver, it's only my first week in css142 and i feel extremely frusturated, she would tell us to ask if we had any questions, and when I do, she does not want to answer them or help me through the problem. This class was the absolute worst. Tho prof does do office hours, so there's that.
