reviews.comment: Course content taught very well, you can probably learn everything by making sure you just participate and pay attention in lectures along with doing the homework. Exams are straightforward to study for and are easier than the worksheets.

Dr. Gismervig was literally a breath of fresh air as a prof. She is obviously very knowledgeable in the subject but makes concepts super clear and understandable for every student. There's literally nothing even remotely bad I can say about her course. Can't recommend her enough!

I've struggled with math my whole life and this was my second time taking Calc I, but her class really helped. She made her own textbook and notes, gave weekly quizzes to test you, and the best part—if you did poorly or missed an exam, she still gave 50% automatically. exam/quiz was very similar and the problems are from what she teaches you.
If you take her math classes, be ready to structure your entire quarter around them. She is a good teacher but requires mountains of work, and her finals are incredibly difficult.

I didn't really like was that most of the lectures and practice was done online. I would've liked in person lectures rather than watch videos on my laptop for hours. She likes to beat around the bush when answering any clarifying questions about specific answers, but she seems to be genuinely passionate and care about what she is teaching.

Homework everyday. Learn from lectures on your own and practice problems in class. PARTICIPATION MATTERS! Justifies the wrong answer first and gives brief explanation for the right one. Super confusing and picky on how you write down answers (got points taken off for writing the right answer in a diff format). 
Taught myself and others the lessons.

DO NOT TAKE HER! 

* consider this your warning

My time w Prof. G was great. She offered a decent amount of extra credit opportunities; the workload (lectures, MyLabMath) was manageable, especially if you have decent time-management; and her instructions/communications were really clear, plus she remained available for feedback/clarification. 
The other reviews are accurate, students love her.

Prof. Gismervig is caring and dedicated to her students' learning. Fantastic class structure composed of previewing lecture content beforehand with concisely outlined videos and collaborating with peers in-class on group activities. Quick and helpful feedback from exams and quizzes. Clearly defines content to appear in exams and allows notecards.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I had difficulties in AP Calc so this was my second attempt and with Emily it was AMAZING! You'll mainly rely on lecture videos, which are concise and super helpful. Prof will make it clear what WILL be on the exams so no need to over-study (plus notecards are allowed!). In-class group activities were the main contributors to my learning too.

Drops lowest grade in some categories (not tests) which is nice, but her online lectures are hard to understand and she is terrible at answering questions. Her tests are also nothing like practice tests she gives or half of the material that she spends time looking at in class

She is ridiculously picky about your answer and docks you for some extremely dumb reasons. Doesn't help that she also messes up questions on her own practice exam. Aside from that, she is a good professor. Worksheets are easy to follow and she lets you use a notecard on exams. Isn't great at explaining why things work, just expects you to get it.
I LOVE HER SHE IS SO NICE AND GOOD AT TEACHING MATH

Her lectures are super clear and helpful! You can tell that she really wants you to succeed and know all the information. This was my second time taking SMATH 124 and it was so much better with Emily! Take her if you can
She honestly is a pretty good professor you just have to go to office hours and never skip an assignment .

You can tell that she really cares about her students succeeding and wants them to know all the information. Her lectures videos are amazing! The review was just like the midterm exams and was very helpful. Would recommend
Slow grader. She didn't provide the work process for the final exam review and some of the answers were wrong. It was stressful, avoid her at all costs, I do not recommend her.
A lot of homework, definitely tough grading you really gotta study in order to pass this class. Some review guide answers were wrong so it was kind of confusing so yeah.

She is favorite professor that I've had so far. She's fairly lenient on grading even if you don't get the right answer, just showing as much work as possible is good. She also has good lecture videos that are really easy to understand. Her office hours are also goated and she gives you exam review that is exactly like the midterms and finals.

I've taken Calculus the quarter before and dropped it during the last few weeks as my grade was too low to justify keeping it. I thought retaking this class would be a struggle once more but Emily made this class seem like a breeze. Clearly defined concepts and always willing to answer questions. If you struggle with math, take this class with her.

2 quiz drops, extra credit for every exam just read instructions, she's very fair. In-person class is groupwork heavy, no lecture at all, hope you have a group that won't speed through the worksheet without you. All the lecturing is done through videos due before day of class, paired with a worksheet. If you want to learn calc take it with her.
Probably the best math teacher I've had, she spends a lot of time in class going over prerecorded lectures and makes sure the material is explained
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Emily is a great Calc professor and can make the most difficult topics easy to understand. Lectures are fantastic and she prioritizes student needs first. I would note that she has definitely read these reviews and has resolved all of the issues brought up, which not many professors do.

Solid professor. She tries her best to make sure that her students are understanding the topic, She grades VERY quickly, and she is a hard worker. She is a bit of a picky grader and the class time is spent on practicing only. You are given videos to watch before class time which is convenient, but I wish there was more done in class

Great professor, helped me alot when I struggled. Very test heavy though, and you are expected to complete alot of work (both classwork and homework). Emily is the type of professor to always offer her help whenever you reach out to her. Don't be afraid to take her class

Things I liked about her class were that she had prerecorded lectures, live lectures, and step-by-step ways to solve a math problem. The only thing I disliked was that she accused me of cheating MULTIPLE times. About 3 times I was accused and each time she took points off even though I had only solved the problem a little differently. -Taken Online

Professor Gismervig's STMATH 307 was the absolute best class I have taken since the pandemic forced all classes to be online. The course structure is well-thought. Lectures were pre-recorded, allowing playback at higher speed. Class sessions were a combination of group/solo problem solving and instructor-led solutions.

She provides high-quality pre-recorded lectures, so you don't really need to attend her classes to be successful. Her quizzes and tests are much easier than the HW assignments. She is EXTREMELY ACCOMODATING. She offers crazy-long extensions on assignments, as well as a one-day extension on quizzes and exams. This professor is a real gem.

Professor Gismervig grades very harshly. Putting the wrong sign will lose you half of your points on an exam question even if you have the concept correct. She also takes away points if she thinks you are cheating which is extremely unfair, and should not be allowed unless proven. If you want success, don't choose this professor.

Accused many students for cheating and tried to coerce them into admitting that they cheated , when many of them didnt. I was accused for cheating when I made a simple mistake while solving a problem, and had gotten the answer right. On top of that, homework every single night.

She makes you do 4-5 assignments per week, she won't teach, you will watch 20 min to 90 min of lectures on wamap and then in class do problems. She will try and accuse you for cheating any chance she gets, say you skip one step on a problem or don't write a variable you will lose a couple points or be accused of cheating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't know why we had to buy the textbook, I didn't really end up using it at all. Went on a tirade and accused multiple students of cheating. Even if you didn't do anything you still had to have a zoom call with her if she suspected you of cheating. Overall not a good experience and left a bad taste in my mouth. She is decent at teaching though.

Not accessible outside of class. You have to do a zoom call, don't try a Canvas message she will NOT reply. However, she's a good teacher. Major problem with her is that she sometimes over explains concepts or teaches the more difficult way to do it when there's an easier way.

If you don't hate math already, this class will definitely change your mind. During a time of difficulty and while a pandemic was going on, Gismervig did her best to accuse anyone of cheating on the smallest red flag. It tanked the entire class's grades and took up so much of our time to try and explain ourselves. Hands down worst math teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Emily is perfect for online learning, no zoom classes at all, everything through online website and there are videos 5-10-20 mins lectures and after each video there are questions which makes you digest the topic with question solving related to topic of the video most of 5 videos per hw and 1 proofs hw and peer grading every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She wastes no chance to deduct points. She literally deducted points in the tutorials for using the tools in the class. The class is a penalization game. When you ask her for an explanation, she answers with "it works" or "didn't I say this before?" It feels unsafe and hostile. How can I learn if I will be shot down for asking?

Emily is an amazing professor that is fair and effective with her teaching style. She is also very understanding and accomodating to students that are trying even if it means she may need to quickly repeat some simpler Algebra concepts since not everyone is on the same page. I used to hate math but Emily has made me feel less intimidated by math :)

Emily is very fair and is can be lenient if you put the effort in. She'll give points back if you have a reasonable excuse, she will post exam review sheets online that give a good overview of what's expected to be on the midterms and the final exam. She also posts the key with work shown to show how she got her result (IMO helps a lot).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's very nice but the math class I had her for she was pretty hands-off throughout the class, it was more of a seminar taught by grad students but they needed a teacher supervising.
Grading is not fair at all. During the class, she will teach around the quarter of class and let us do the work by yourself and really waste our time.

One of the best math professors I've had at UW Bothell. She really cares about her students succeeding in her class. Always welcomed students to come to office hours, and if you can't make those she was always willing to accomodate on other days. Grades fairly, and overall just go to class and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Gismervig was a great professor for pre calc. She took time to understand names and created a personal relation with students. Take advantage of her office hours, as she gives specific feedback as to what will be on exams. If you do homework, study, and get feedback exams are easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I wouldnt recommend Emily, she is hard to understand while teaching and also when asking questions in office hours she can make you feel dumb for asking a question. Her grading is very unfair to the fact that if you dont round up on the test when it says nothing about it she will take off full points.

Great teacher for those who struggle with math, teaching slowly and making sure that everyone has understood. However, having a preexisting understanding of higher level math, there were moments where her teaching further confused areas I had felt comfortable. Nightly homework is too minutiae but disproportionately decides your participation grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Emily is hands down the best professor I've ever had, and i would 100% recommend her (especially if it's your first year). I personally don't like math and never really got it, until I met with her. She's very knowledgeable, caring, and goofy! She spends class time wisely, 20% lecture 80% with your group. TAKE HER!
Emily was the first professor who made me understand math. I usually struggle a lot with math but she was a very clear lecture and very much wanted all of us to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very helpful in and out of class hours. Clear lectures and class is pretty straightforward. Would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: First off, I HATE math.  I've learned to enjoy it in Emily's class.  She is a very caring person, and wants you to succeed.  She extends her office hours before tests, and is more than willing to help you.  Attendance is necessary; the participation points add up. She isn't teaching BMATH 122 in the Spring; I wish she was.   I definitely recommend.

One of the best math professor I had. She teaches the material well and does not overwhelm the student too much during lecture. Homework and quizzes are straight forward, pay attention in lecture and you should be fine. Take advantage of her office hours because Emily is extremely helpful with anything you don't understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Emily is hands down the best math professor I have ever taken and she's also one of the greatest professors in UWB. Her lectures are clear and she knows how to lecture. I would take her for all of my math classes if I could. She's AMAZING. I definitely recommend taking her!
I really enjoyed Emily's class. Going to try and have her again in math in the future!!!

Emily is an amazing teacher who cares about wether not you're passing or not. She and the other teachers (it seems more like her though) are trying to have a "No 0" policy to not let anyone fail their class. You have to come to class and participate to really understand the math.
She helped me a TON. She is always available for office hours and answers any question, regardless of how dumb it is. One of the best math professors at UWB.
She is very helpful. If you go in and talk with her in her office hours and work with her, she is very understanding. I really enjoyed taking her class.
Pay attention in class and you'll do well. Finish the homework and study a little, and she will give you the benefit of the doubt. Good professor, great class.

She is pretty nice and is the to help whenever you need it and actually explains things very well. But gotta admit she's really strict on grading!! And she didn't give us enough time to get ready for our final. The last week before the finals she taught us new material when she should have given us the review sheet to get ready for the finals.

I was very disappointed in how little help she provided. She is new  to UWB so she is clearly still learning. The amount of assignments she gives is ridiculous and even if they are easy she is ZERO help. I definitely do NOT reccommend taking her. Spare yourself the bad grade and useless material.

Professor Graham is extremely hilarious all this homework and exams are all held on Canvas. They're open for some certain number of days to get done and they're all open noted. He's extremely responsive. He has labs nearly all the time on R and he would try to help when and wherever you are especially even on Zoom.
great professor would recommend him. He is so kind and caring!

Professor Graham is amazing! You can tell that he's passionate about the subject matter and really brings it to life. He genuinely cares about students, not only success in the class but our mental health and our time. Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Graham is a super chill, nice and hilarious professor. Class is lecture heavy but he puts a lot of work into them, entertaining & informative. Tests are online/take home & open note. Use of programming language R but its straightforward (i have programming experience, without any it shouldnt be bad) Simple cmds and he gives many of them.

Clear and eazy understand teaching, best cal intro teacher. Exam review is harder then the acual exam. She is very caring about her student. she makes sure that everyone understand the concept. I wishs that she teaches cal 2. If you complete everything, like the lectures on time you will do good in class.

She's alright, she's prone to ranting every now and then but it's clear she cares about her students, there's tons of homework and she can be a little overwhelming sometimes. She's a nice person but can be a handful.

I literally cannot stand her voice for the life of me and its even worse when she goes onto belittle you in front of the whole class. Prepare to be treated like a child, and to give up your whole week due to the fact that this lady doesn't care that you have a life. Assignments will unlock on due date. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF WORKING FULL TIME.
taking him for fieldwork in health, and he has not graded anything as of week 7 but he is flexible and accessible outside of class.

I had him for B HLTH 179. This was an extremely easy class - all you had to do was read the textbook and take a canvas quiz on it. You get points for showing up, but in class he just did some freestyle talks/lectures and we spent a lot of time talking with each other about interests/hobbies/etc. He is one of the most caring professors I've met.
Easiest class I have taken here. Work was very little and professor was easy and fair at grading. As long as you follow the syllabus and assignment prompts closely, you should be able to do well.

Anderson is an excellent professor. I took his Interpersonal Communications course, which had a "Dead Poets Society" vibe. If you enjoy engaging in or listening to group discussions, you'll love his class. However, participation is key—it makes up almost the entire grade.

Anderson is an excellent professor. I took his Interpersonal Communications course, which had a "Dead Poets Society" vibe. If you enjoy engaging in or listening to group discussions, you'll love his class. However, participation is key—it makes up almost the entire grade.
He is a very nice person. Talk to him if you need help. The class is very easy. Do the assignment and you will get 4.0. This is the easiest class I have taken at UWB.

reviews.comment: If you want a class that's a joke, take this class. It's basically a group chat with no feedback and you get the grade he feels like giving you. He doesn't update assignments and doesn't grade them until 2 weeks before the quarter ends.  You're welcome.

Great professor! Mentor energy, approachable and knowledgeable. Focuses on real-world application and has extensive industry experience. The class was mostly dedicated to weekly group projects. Less reading than 506, but there is an optional textbook you will want to read if you're not familiar with web app development. Pretty lenient with grading.

Straightforward and fair. Provides excellent insights on the current industry based on extensive background (and continued work?) in the professional environment. Interact, ask questions, communicate with your group project team, do your readings and you will do well in the class.

Fun lectures with weekly hands-on group projects. Great lecture style: no nonsense, straightforward yet friendly and compassionate. The instructor brings lots of industry experience so we get valuable stories and insights. Projects/tests focus on the main objectives, with transparent expectations throughout. Promotes team work. Highly recommend.

Professor Eric is an excellent professor. The course has a LOT of reading, but in his classes, he focuses only on the things that matter in real life. He also shares many of his experiences working at Microsoft, which is cool. Be ready to read. FR.

Eric is a great professor! CSS 506 has a lot of reading, but 507 and 508 ramp down on the reading. All the projects are done in class, so no outside hw besides reading. He is extremely knowledgeable and I felt like a learned a lot of relevant information. His exam expectations are clearly explained, so no surprises on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Eric is one of the best professors I have met. He is very nice, patient, experienced, professional and responsible. If every professor in UW is like him, it would be every student's honor. I wish I could take his class in the future again.

Eric made the most slow and boring possible class to the most energizing class.
I value his innovative way of creating the class being part of learning experience by incorporating the material into tangible experience.
He created a learning environment not only unforgettable but also fun. 
Learning cooperation and adaptability was a bonus.

Professor Brechner is knowledgeable and has lots of real-world experience. His lectures are interesting and have a sense of practicality to them that a lot of other professors lack (he tells you if you don't use something in the field, etc). Class is easy if you show up, and your test grade is determined by a good cheat sheet. The reading sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures and demystify a lot of concepts. Read and make sure to focus on the lecture and you will be fine for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor, the way he teaches makes the lectures not boring at all but the text is very heavy, so get ready to read. His experience in the industry and his honest comments on each topic gives you a better understading of what to expect in real world. The class is mostly a review of the readings and open book quizzes, which makes time go fast.

Eric was clearly a knowledgeable professor with lots of practical knowledge to share. The course isn't too difficult, although the mandatory textbook readings are very dry. If you show up to class you will do well on the daily group projects. The professor provides study guides for both the midterm and final (the final is not comprehensive).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor's lectures are fun to listen to and are not boring.  The course was relatively stress-free, which is absolutely needed to balance out the coding/math intensive CSS501.  Expect to work as a group/team for every class (except for midterm/final) -- great way to meet and make friends within the program.  Expect to do a lot of writing!

Eric is a seasoned professional with many years of real-world wisdom to share about the software engineering industry.

He is also an excellent orator and makes it interesting.

Overall this was time well spent.  I highly recommend taking classes from Eric.

A knowledgeable professor with real-world experience as a manager at Microsoft. Best part of the class is the in-class group projects where we simulate the various development processes (Waterfall, Scrum, Kanban, etc.). Overall, I had a great experience in the class.
Class is almost purely group quizzes that simulate the development processes.

This course is about software development processes (waterfall, scrum, etc.). Class sessions were built around groups filling out quizzes under rules designed to simulate those processes. It works pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He did an excellent job to design and organize the class.
He is my favorite and the best teacher in the Graduate Certificate in Software Design & Development. I really enjoyed his classes

Professor provided a high level overview of the class topics but struggled to explain the more technical details when asked for more depth. There was a generally low level of technical expectations from this professor considering it is a graduate level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is a very knowledgeable professor. His expertise and industry experience can be really shown in how he teaches the course. He emphasizes on the customer and business impacts of each topic, which are very important concerns when being in the industry.

He has an energetic/excited teaching style. In-class reading, lectures, and projects are not technical in nature. There is no homework assigned that solidifies class concepts with usable skills. Half of the test answers are direct bullets from the book that don't really test understanding. Write an exhaustive cheat sheet for an A.

Class projects make attendance necessary for grades. Reading material will cover needed info and then some. Class was well organized and mostly free of homework aside from reading. Absolutely desires that you extend your answers to questions/tests beyond the reading. Funny and casual (some might be surprised at the color commentary).

This professor is definitely someone you should take a class with. He's passionate and does a good job of structuring his lectures cohesively. Most importantly, his tests are fair and impartial. He should continue teaching the way he teaches!
This lecturer is passionate and logical, and the projects in class are very interesting.

Professor Brechner's classes have been very informative. He provides industry specific, real world instruction in a fun, engaging, group project and discussion format. These classes have been a highlight of the GCSDD program.
Very good teacher, but you absolutely need to attend class and do the participation exercises to get the benefit of it
He goes over the topics to make sure that they stick in your head with funny anecdotes.

Gave me a new perspective on the possibilities of web services development. His industry experience as conveyed in the lectures was invaluable and his articles really brought the subject matter to life. Group projects in class were a great way to interact and to know fellow students. Likable on a personal level as well.

Great insights & industry-insider anecdotes, which are probably just as valuable as, and integrally related to, the coursework. For 506 expect to adjust to some really unusual in-class activities and grading principles, but in a good & refreshing way. (negative points for getting an answer wrong, possibly running and jumping over tables :) )
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Class time goes by extremely fast with his teaching method. The quizzes can be very stressful given that your score can depend on other groups if you don't have time to answer a question on the quiz.
I really enjoyed learning about software methodology from the professor. He made it fun, interesting and peppered it with a lot of great anecdotes

His enthusiasm for the subject matter was infectious and his real world experiences with software development that he conveyed in the lectures was very informative. The varying format of the in class group projects did give one a sense of the different models of commercial software development being practiced. The textbook was dry/uninspiring.

While I found his real-world, industry-experience-based lectures the most helpful, I thought after getting the hang of the group work that it bordered on busy work a lot of the time. I would prefer more time spent in class discussing the concepts - maybe not spend every class doing group work or make its percentage of the class smaller.
Good class, but difficult tests, and in class projects are a lot of work/effort but you'll do well on them usually.

Passionate, super knowledgeable, willing to assist, humble, delivers his thoughts on the subject and the lectures really well, and you would enjoy his method of teaching and being in his class. Very rare amongst CS faculties.
I like the class project, learn from it a lot.
Overall great quarter and really enjoyed Professor Brechner's enthusiasm and application of real-world problems in software development.
I enjoyed the class. Fun group projects.  Great interview preparation.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Brechner does a great job breaking down the content and revealing the real-world application of each topic.
Great examples from industry experience.  Makes dry concepts easier to learn,
Great opportunity to learn from someone with strong industry experience.
Great professor of good personality! Humorous and well engaged!

The classroom quizzes are so good that made us to change the perspective of how to look at the book. He made sure to upload necessary files in advance, bring materials needed for classroom quizzes, provided explanations relating to his past experiences, welcomed team's thoughts, promptly graded after class and provided clear format for exams.

Professor Brechner was great at explaining and covering topics that are useful in industry. He brings a wealth of industry experience and insight to make his lectures more interesting. The weekly group quiz was great at teaching us the format and purpose of the most popular software development practices. Overall, an enjoyable class.

Before class, we have to finish readings; and on class we take quizzes, but this is a team work. I think this method is excellent. Because every time, we use different software engineering models, like Waterfall, Kanpan, Scrume etc. It is really a good way for us to be familiar with these real world models, which will be contributed to our job.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Overall great professor and very interesting class! The group projects provide hands-on experience for real applications used in the industry.
It was fine.  Useful content, dry reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class is attractive and not boring at all.

Wow!  Very fun class with an enthusiastic instructor.  Yes, we do group projects putting into practice the reading material on software processes.  What a rewarding experience.   One of the best instructors I've had.  He should win teaching awards.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Eric is the best teacher in the Certificate program. He comes prepared with real world knowledge, theory, and humor.  The first quarter is the most intense of the three since the amount of reading required is significant, but after that, the next two in the sequence use the same book. Happy Customer :)

Brechner is a great professor - very easy to listen to, funny, and knowledgeable. He gives a ton of feedback so you are never, ever in the dark. Taking a Monday class 8-10pm is worth it if you get to take it with Brechner.

His experience and knowledge are keys to what makes him a great teacher. I learned a ton in this class even though I came into it with industry experience. Group projects are a little intimidating, but learning to work with others is part of what it's all about. Would take another class from him.

Professor Brechner is really passionate about the class. His industry experience and inside about what works and what doesn't brings invaluable experience to the class. Also, his sense of humor makes the class enjoyable.

I looked at the timing of this class with disdain (8p-10p) until we had the first day of class! Very fun group work every class period. Your group is a great opportunity to make friends with members of your cohort, take advantage of this! Brechner leverages his industry experience to teach about the real world; STUDY his slides, they are important!

Brechner assigns in class projects that you work on with your classmates. The teams are selected by random and are a large part of your grade. Everything from his lecture and the class projects are fair game from the exams so expect to see them. His lectures are fun and easy to understand.

Eric is an awesome professor who really brings his years of industry experience to bear in his course design and lectures.  I learned a ton about all different kinds of software development through the different group projects we did in class.  He was hilarious and inspirational.  I would love to work for someone like him when I graduate.

Eric was very engaging and has a clear passion for software engineering the translates well to the classroom. If you show up to every class and participate in the group projects, it will be hard for you not to succeed, and he leverages his own experiences well during lecture. The textbook is about as dry as a Tattooine desert.

A considerably less interesting subject was made engaging. There are no homework; readings only. Group projects were done during the class with short lecture; everything well timed. Professor Eric is quite erudite and passionate about the subject and presents very good explanations to any question asked. I enjoyed his class a lot.

Eric was able to take a fairly dry subject (and textbook) and teach it with enough passion to make it both valuable and interesting. He is extremely engaging, and always gives extremely insightful answers to questions. His knowledge is deep, and he has enough industry experience to speak to the subject's real-world relevance and value.

This course was a little light on readings / work outside of class, even for a 2 credit course. In class projects exposed us to a lot of new design activities and the software design process, including profiling, scenarios, architecture, and test.

This class made a dry subject come alive. No homework for the class; readings only. Class time was largely group project work, with limited lecture. Eric was passionate about the subject and was very effective at highlighting key points.

Eric uses in-class projects to simulate the development processes the class is studying. This makes the subject matter more engaging than any textbook, gives us a more tactile feel of how the processes work, and the rush to finish projects in time keeps your blood pumping even at 8:00pm. No coffee required!
Eric makes the learning environment an engaging and fun one.  Each week is a project that is directly related to the topics from that week's reading.

It's hard to look forward to an 8-10pm course on a Monday night, but I enjoyed the class. Brechner organized the class as a flipped classroom, with each week's reading informing a group exercise during class each week. It was challenging and engaging, and an extremely positive group experience. The textbook was a bit dry, but was great for content.

I'm grateful I was able to take her class, everything was organized from day one and she's very nice. Attendance isn't mandatory. There's group assignments you do in class, & the quizzes and HW are framed in a way to help you learn and there was no final exam, but a presentation. Very informative class, other professors should learn from her.

Very easy and nice proffessor. Lots of the lectures are pretty boring because talking about climate change on a powerpoint isnt the most exciting but you were in groups a lot and makes class go by quicker. So much extra credit. I honestly dont even know how you could fail this class, just show up and do the assignments. Shes an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not great, not terrible. Lectures aren't the best so I stacked up on the in-class worksheets for extra credit. final project was easy, quiz every week or two, canvas assignments weekly also. TAKE NOTES while she's lecturing, and read the textbook. GO TO CLASS for extra credit!! like a 6/10 class overall tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Fields' lecture, despite it being long. As long as you take good notes and study the material, you will succeed in this class. I would absolutely take another class with her again, as she is very knowledgeable in her field and always answers questions thoroughly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think he is a wonderful CS professor, one of the best I've had! He is very kind; gave me every extension I asked for (I asked for a lot). I found his lectures and answering question super helpful, he definitely knows/explains the material well.

Have one assignment/quiz a week. Do not turn it in late. He does not care what you have going on in your life, you better get it in on time. Even with DRS accommodations, he won't give extensions. Nice guy at first. Don't try to take notes during class either. He switches slides back and fourth every 10 seconds.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Arian, is a very nice guy you can tell he's passionate about CS. Class consists of 4 labs, 5 weekly quizzes and inClass labs. His directions for labs are not very clear and doesn't clearly list the expected output. His lectures are very math heavy on topics like proofs, propositions, quantifiers, recurrence relations etc. Be sure you know C++

I took STMATH125 with him in Autumn of '24, and it was rough. His accent makes it difficult to understand what he's saying at times, there's no work to study apart from the homework, the lectures are not recorded, he's intimidating when it comes to asking questions.

Empathetic, cheerful, engaging and helpful. Would thoroughly and patiently explain problems and concepts if you ask, and is easily accessible and available. Willing to help you if you ask questions and holds multiple office hours. Attend his review sessions for the final and midterms and review both midterms before doing the final. Take notes!

instead of a midterm he had 5 shorter quizzes which were easier to study for and were based off of inclass practice assignments. Lots of self learning. His lectures/explanations were difficult to understand but he encourages students to ask questions. 4 labs make sure to start early on them! its helpful to understand C++ before the course

He doesnt provide proper resources for the exams and also no review nothing. But I think his grading is good the exam would be out of a 80/100 but in canvas he would put it as out of 25/35 so that helps even when u get a bad score out of a 100. The trick is note down the exact problems he solves in class and study them I think the exam is similar

He gives no resources to study, besides referencing the textbook's practice problems. There are no practice tests for the 2 midterms or final exam. You are only given what sections from the textbook will be covered in the final, outlined in the syllabus. Aside from that, its up to you to tryhard and do the hundreds of problems in the textbook.

Overall a great professor. All the negative reviews of him being rude and the class being hard etc. are incorrect based on my experience. If you attend class and work hard on homework and studying you will do good. Almost every class has a lecture (besides exam review days) with new content so pay attention.

Your grade in this course will be made up of two midterms worth 25% of your total grade each, a 35% final, as well as 15% homework. Dr. Eyal tends to skip steps in his examples and expects students to not need review on topics surrounding calculus and previous math subjects. If you are rusty with math or don't do well with tests, he is not for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Disrespectful and negative attitude. If you manage to access him outside of class, it's a waste of time to ask for help as he goes to criticize you for asking before forgetting to address your question. He does not provide practice exams so study the exam questions off of the SOA P exam site. Class was heavily curved due to a failing exam average.

Not a professor I would take again. He has a clear understanding of math and theory but does a terrible job at explaining it. Often speaks in a low voice and is not engaging as a lecturer. Sometimes had an attitude when answering questions. Easier on grading program assignments than other professors and has more but shorter quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor but cannot teach in class. You can tell he is knowledgeable about this course and wants to teach but has short temper. Also, he has a tough time explaining certain topics such as Big-o.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took him CSS 340 he's a down to earth guy. Will push back assignments if needed and not to harsh on grading the In class assignments are close to the Quizes. Does not have office hours but will respond to emails.

He teaches fine, but the class is not planned out or structured well. He will push assignments back and listen to students if they speak up. He can also be very blunt, but in an honest way that is not necessarily mean spirited.

DISRESPECTFUL. Prof comes to class with negative energy and teaches quietly like he's teaching himself. Students correct most of his teaching, if you are fluent in c++ take him. But if you want to actually learn DO NOT TAKE HIM. Probably the worst UWB Professor anyone can take. I should have listened to these comments before taking him.

Calculus is not an easy subject you have to put in time and effort for a good grade. Most students go in underprepared, I was one of them. When I took calculus with Professor Arian, I was able to grasp concepts I didn't in the past. He is blunt which tends to intimate most, but he will take the time to explain the problems if you ask for help.

He was rude. I felt really uncomfrotable in his class which is why I dropped out. The class was shaping out to be something I couldn't handle because he was slow and disorganized. I took his class for only 2 weeks and within that time our class had a low average on the precalc quiz and he started yelling at us saying "you shouldn't take this class"

Worst Professor I have ever had in my entire life. He does not know what he is talking about, and proceeds to tell you that you have a bad work ethic. He is not helpful at all, his tests are complete BS, I have never had such hatred for a professor in my life. Class failed midterm and Final and he does not care.
Hasn't quite figured out the online teaching thing yet. A lot of wasted time during class. Had to spend quite a lot of time learning from YouTube lecturers instead of the class lectures.

Do not take him for CSS 340. This is the worst professor I have had in the CSS department at UWB. He is not understanding about anything especially during Covid and gets really frustrated that students don't understand what he is teaching but does not do a better job at explaining things. Very rude professor who is terrible at teaching.

His explanations can be a bit confusing because he knows so much about everything, but as long as you ask a question, he will explain it perfectly. The homework was very helpful for the tests. Consisted of half MyMathLab with plenty of attempts to get 100 on each homework and 5 written assignments that were perfect practice for exams.

Arian is a good guy and a decent Professor. He assigns a ton of homework but they're fairly relevant to what is covered in the textbook and what is covered in class. On average, you should expect to spend 10 hours a week outside of class in order to get over a 3.0 in his class. His exams are fairly difficult and extremely long (8 pages).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was the worst professor I had in my 4 years of college. Incredible tough grader and he was super rude. Im a 3.8 student and got an F on 2 of his tests so I had to drop it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Arian is one of my all time favorite math professors. He can be a little tough on grading sometimes, but he's exceptionally well versed in maths, and has a genuine passion for it. Further, he was always accessible outside of class, and is just a stand up guy. Don't be afraid to visit his office hours, he's super nice!

Best math professor I've ever had. Cares a lot about his students, and will gladly explain anything you didn't understand. His tests are very reasonable, and he curved most of them. He also has weekly quizzes to make sure you're keeping up. He also tries to explain how the material relates to real-life applications. Overall amazing professor.
He was super rude and disrespectful. Over 2/3s of the class failed the midterm. Then he proceeded to tell us well never succeed in college because we have no work ethic.

Seems like a decent person, but his teaching mechanics are definitely off. For classes, he just goes over problems that you already solved, nothing that is insightful or helpful. Then, when quiz grades don't turn out good. he rubs the blame on the students. Pretty much, I can read the textbook for 10 mins and learn his 2 hours worth of lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures are math heavy. He likes to prove everything mathematically and expects his students to be very math oriented. He disapproves of "alternative routes" of understanding the Big Oh notation. His method differs a lot from the methods of other CSS342 professors. He takes all the time necessary to help students understand concepts.

He is a math teacher, so he teaches the mathematical concepts really well and focuses on them more. His tests were really hard, far harder than his in class examples, but he cares. This was clearly his first time teaching this course so his class was unorganized and he relied too much on his graders and didn't always explain programming as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kind of hard to understand sometimes, but really organized and helpful when you need it. Lots of homework too. Took it first year because I didn't need it for my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great teacher. You can tell he really cares about how much his students understand the material, and he is there to help you outside of class if you need it. The only negative reviews he receives on this are based on the difficulty of the class. Choosing him will give you the best opportunity to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher, if you want to fail take him.

Really good professor. He cares about your understanding of the material, even if sometimes he seems like he doesn't. He gives short quizzes but they're for extra credit, which really helps if you miss a few points on the exams. The exams are just like the practice problems from class ,with some adjustments. GO TO CLASS & you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Really thankful that he gives short quizzes sometimes that are for extra credit which is an awesome way to boost your grade. I cannot read a math textbook for my dear life so I attended all the lectures and they really help. He also puts up practice exams on Canvas and they also help a lot. My advice is brush up on your algebra!!!
I would highly recommend going to every lecture, as Dr. Arian's examples and explanations during lecture are second to none. Completing the homework is also critical to success in this class.

Awesome math teacher, his lectures are always very clear and on-topic. All the homework is relevant to the lectures which are relevant to the tests. I didn't even need the textbook, which I think shows how well organized it was. He also genuinely cares about all the students and offers office hours and will answer all email questions. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Though Professor Arian is good at his job, I don't see him improving. His class is too lecture heavy. There is almost nothing to the class other than him showing examples. He also states that if what he teaches isn't enough, then study groups should essentially be half the experience. The homework is either irrelevant, or easier than exams/quizzes.

A good guy and pretty decent at explaining concepts, especially if you ask every time you're confused. He's very good at going back and explaining exactly why he's taken the steps he has. The homework is a MUST to understand the concepts, and even then the topics can feel difficult and rushed. Tests are much harder than homework.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you are stuck with the problems, professor Arian is always willing to help you during his office hours. I succeeded in this course thanks to his help!
100% lecture, 0% discussion and group work. If you don't pay attention in lecture you're not gonna have a good time.

This prof is very good with math and has a few cool stories to tell about his time working in the industry. A lot of self teaching might be required to supplement his lectures. Be prepared for a very exam heavy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a very good teacher and definitely knows his calculus. However, sometimes he does skip steps without much clarification but all you have to do is ask how he got to point B from point A and he will make sure you understand it. He does often help students after class and does care for his students. Very good teacher.

I have never come across a math instructor who is as passionate as Dr. Arian about the subject matter. This is a lecture-heavy course, but he really takes the time to clarify every detail. If it gets confusing, he is always available for office hours to help out. He solves complex algebra problems in his head, so know your algebra well.

One of the easiest classes I've taken. The professor is great, very accessible, accommodating, and a very lenient grader. There's a decent amount of reading, but overall it's manageable and not too time consuming. Would 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very nice teacher, work was easy, there are daily in class activites you need to do with people but it's pretty easy. She's so enthusiastic makes class not feel dreadful and boring.

Professor was great in enhancing and supporting each student. Made the class feel more at home and laid back while still learning and enhancing writing skills. Readings may be a bit long but not too bad as they actually help you. There are 2 writing projects which she gives lots of time for and project builders to ease the process. Great Feedback!

Overall a good professor, though can get sort of monotone and repetitive at times. A lot of freedom given  to students for the overarching project. Much of the class can be lecture heavy with a couple activities sprinkled through, though when it is lecture, the content is often repeated 3-4 times in different ways through the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a nice person who tries to be accommodating. However, I took her BIS 164 class and all of the books were depressing. It was very clear they were selected to push political messages rather than show and appreciate the writers' skills. If you want an easy 4.0 take this. If you want to discover interesting and unique literature, you'll be sad.

She is caring kind and great Professor. As soon as you do your responsibilities in basic level and attending the activities you don't need to care about grading. She wants you to learn and apply topics in class, and giving caring feedback always. Definitely want to take another course from her!
Overall great professor communicated well and gave great feedback.

I loved taking Professor Ferreira!! She is so understanding and kind. She grades purely on completeness and effort. She gives good feedback without making you feel incompetent. I genuinely picked up useful lessons to become a better writer. Course load was extremely manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is easily one of my favorite professors at UWB. I had her for BWRIT 132, 133, and 135. Shes enthusiastic, gives thoughtful feedback on your assignments, answers all your questions, lenient, understands students, and even funny. She uses a Grading Contract which I prefer. She even let us change it to how we wanted at the beginning of the quarter
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I recommend taking her! She is such a sweet and very helpful professor. The class workload is typically only 2 assignments per week, that only take around 1-2 hours to complete. She grades differently than other professors but you can easily get an A in this class if you do all the assignments by the deadline.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was shocked at how good this professor made a class as seemingly uninteresting as BWRIT 135. Her feedback was truly top-notch, she was kind and had an excellent grading system, alongside interesting lectures and group work. Even though I've already done a lot of writing, I learned a lot from her.

THE BEST ENGLISH PROFESSOR EVER!! She gives the best feedback to your papers and what you can improve when revising for the final portfolio as she records a video of her talking about your strengths and weaknesses to help you! She is very caring and approachable and is very willing to help. Show up to class, participate, and work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I think she's nice and really helpful with writing skills, but the content of the class could have been better. I loved learning about critical theory for my major but if we read any book that wasn't Great Gatsby it would have been more interesting. Lectures were good but I really think the material detracted from it.

Prof. Ferreira is a satisfactory teacher for what she does. I was in Bwrit 134 and going to that class was never a burden and the time scale and how assignments are turned in is fair and enough time is given to complete projects with enough time. She is also very understanding and gives good feedback if you ask for help.

(There's no BWRIT 135 option?)
Clear, easy grading criteria. Provides nice feedback.

Class is fully asynchronous (no Zoom) so you have to work at your own pace. Books are interesting, but the essays are somewhat challenging based on her grading. Shes a nice teacher when you interact with her.

The first class I ever took at UWB was with Dr. Ferreira. It was a fantastic experience and a good introduction to college writing. It's literature-based rather than article-based like the other comp classes, but it's overall one of the better ones. She makes you write, but her feedback is meaningful and prepares students to be better writers.

I really enjoyed taking B WRIT 132. It allowed me to write about myself. It really cool experience from a transition to high school to UWB. If you are undeclared, I highly recommend taking this class.

I had Professor Ferriera for my first college writing course, and she made it a fantastic experience. The essays she assigned were always completed in three steps (proposal, peer review, and final draft) and she gave great feedback that was very useful for the next steps. In class work was almost always done in groups and was structured very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Definitely challenging to get a full mark on your assignments, got a 4 hour size exam based on the reading, tough grader. Attendance is part of participation grade, which is 15% of final course grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The course consists of 3 small 2 page essays, 3 longer 4 page essays and a final Portfolio/reflection. Doesnt have strict assignments and lets you write about what you want, which is awesome. She gives good feedback after every assignment and answers emails quickly. Grading system is a little annoying since you need above 99% to get a 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is a nice teacher and the class is super easy. However the grading scale is completely ridiculous for how easy the class is and she never gives 100% on anything. in order to get a 4.0 in this writing class, you need to have a minimum of 99%, and she makes it basically impossible to get. The work is easy, but she doesn't care about the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: So nice and willing to help you if you need it!  Her grading scale is a little frustrating, only a 99-100 counts as 4.0 and 98-99 is a 3.9 etc.  She's not a harsh grader though and all of the assignments were clear and easy.  Participation does count for 25% of your grade though so you need to show up and contribute in class to do well.
Great friendly teacher! Definitely, take her for BWRIT 134!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You might go a lil coocoo taking CSS422, but I think this is agnostic to the professor. We had final, homework and final project due at the same week. Prof is really good  and he knows his stuff

Was very diligent and lax grading, offered a lot of extra credit opportunities and gave very clear feedback. If you were unsure about your grade, he gives up to a week to talk to him about it and get a grade change.
There was no racism.

He encourages participation with in-class discussions that are actually helpful for understanding course material. He also gives hints to homework and exams if you attend lectures. Finally, you can ask questions and he will give useful answers. My biggest complaint is that, even when I sat in the front and he had a mic, I could barely hear him.

W professor who knows his stuff, and if you are into this field of work, then you will love him. If you just care about passing 430, there are probably easier professors. Participation is graded, hw is light, exams are tough, no extra credit, and lectures can sometimes get hard to follow due to pacing and sound (Japanese accent + directional mic).

He was the meanest teacher ever. When I said something that made him mad, like telling him I didn't understand his explanation and asking him to repeat it, he started to hate me. After that he kept an eye on me all the time. He is also racist toward his asian students.

He is very knowledgeable and knows what he's talking about. It is clear he is experienced with this topic and this class. The grading was pretty lax, as long as you showed that your program worked and you had the right idea, he would give you points. Try to participate in lectures and in-class activities; it helps a lot, and you get extra credit.

This is a review for the course CSS534, Parallel Programming In Grid And Cloud, as I could not find it in the list. Professor Fukuda is very dedicated and responsible. He provides detailed descriptions for both assignments and exams. He is also very patient with students' questions. I think this is one of the best graduate courses I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you show up to his lectures (which you need to as there is small problem sets to do for grade in the last 30 minutes), you should be fine. The practice tests are almost 1-1 for his actual tests, and he even allows using class resources/slides/notes on tests. The final project was extremely difficult though, but if you start early, you'll be ok.

The only thing you need to know is class is not that hard. 
If you feel it is hard using his office to boot up your skill

I took this class winter quarter - While this class was very challenging, Fukuda was genuine and was always eager to answer any questions I had. He was very kind to us and was pretty flexible with the homework. The midterm was pretty rough, but he made sure we were well prepared for the final. Very passionate professor!

The exams are essential parts of this course. It cannot reflect all of your efforts. Yes! There are exam rehearsals, but the prerequisite is that you must quickly understand and solve many problems on paper in two hours. Otherwise, you mess it up for sure. The problem is to understand those concepts in class is reaaally hard.....
This class is challenging. The pace is too fast; concepts need to have better explanations. It is dangerous to take it if you are not ready for a tough journey.

While Fukuda knows his stuff and is very nice, he often doesn't explain difficult concepts and topics enough/much at all and moves on quickly, which is dangerous in this course. Make sure you start your homework as soon as possible and form groups to work together. VERY exam heavy (50% of final grade) but are almost identical to his practice tests.

He is very knowledge but 422 is very hard regardless. Like said before, he doesn't explain tough concepts well at all which is kind of needed in this class. He does give hints and his practice tests are almost identical to his real tests. Would recommend another professor but he isn't the worst option. Make sure to work/get help with others!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Has an accent which makes him hard to understand sometimes. I thought he was very caring to students and made sure students understood what was going on. During coding examples he'd go kinda fast though. He records EVERYTHING which is very convenient, but he expects students to attend class and asks students to email him if youre not.
Great professor. He gives hints for every assignments. Sample test for midterm and final, you can get good grade if you do the sample test.

The class is tough, not because of the professor, but because of the sheer amount of material in the course. Professor Fukuda does his best to help students with keeping up - his lectures are clear and well prepared, he is extremely responsive to questions in office hours and through email, and he grades quickly, clearly, and fairly.

I have taken every undergraduate class that he teaches. He is remarkably consistent in his teaching style, he gives very clear lectures and explains assignments with great detail. He has been one of my favorite professors so far, cares a lot about the success of students and is very knowledgeable.

Definitely, not an easy class. You should expect to learn a lot. He knows about his stuff and he is very eager to teach everything to students. If you are looking for an easy A class, do take other prof's classes. But, he is very understanding and flexible. Grades will be curved if needed and he responses to emails very quick. Great classes I had
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Decent professor, does not explain difficult topics well. You will have to do learning on your own but the in class assignments were helpful in determining our understanding of the materials.

CSS 434 is one of the hardest courses in UWB. So, if you are expecting something like an easy A 400-level course, this is not for you. However, if you are looking for a class that you can learn a lot, you must take this. It's a very rewarding class. He has an accent, but not too heavy to understand. He is very willing to help students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Fukuda is difficult to interact with. His accent is difficult to understand, so you might have to hear him multiple times to know what he is saying. But if you ask him questions, he gets frustrated with you and gets aggressive. He also makes it his duty to judge you. A terrible experience. Do yourself a favor and void him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but was not great at explaining concepts. He will show you the process for solving a problem, but doesn't give context for actually understanding it. He used questions and tests from other instructors, so what you were tested on didn't match up with what he covered in class. He is super nice and accessible during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The accent wasn't an issue as I am a second language student. The real issue was that not enough practice given in class. He lectured all the way except the class before the quiz, he will give about half an hour to practice. Grading was good b/c he gave points as much as he could not matter the answer is correct or not.

Best computer science teacher, I've had so far! He's extremely organized, and gives class exercises to help learn the tough material. He notices if you're not in class and actually cares if you're successful or not. A bit hard to hear, so sit up front!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Going into the class, reviews made me skeptical, but after actually taking his class he has really grown on me. The material is not easy, and no matter how good his lectures are the programs/exams will still be tough. He provides recordings of his lectures which help tremendously. One of my favorite professors so far.

Hard to listen to his accent, his assignments are a bit ambiguous- sometimes he comes in late during his office hours. He's a nice guy, will tell you to drop the class in advance if he thinks you need to retake it. Difficult to predict :) Has a lot of experience in the tech industry, even tho I'm an asian- I still can't hear his accent. Sorry!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a good teacher and explains some concepts well, but others not so much. I had particular difficulty with all of the mathematical concepts. He didn't take a lot of time to talk about them, but they had equal weight on the quizzes and tests.  We spent a total of 2 hours out of the whole quarter on it, but needed to know it as well as programming
I feel like he was a good instructor, but I'm not really sure because I could only understand about 1/4th of the words he said (accent was the issue).
His voice will confuse you.  His exams will destroy you.  Are you ready?

Fukuda is very enthusiastic and makes lecture pretty interesting. It will take a bit of time to get used to his accent though. Issues with the class included lack of directions and communication and using VERY OLD code. While he's really lenient on grading, his assignment will probably make you panic from time to time.

Very helpful instructor. Knows his information well. Not an easy grader. However, if you study and put time into his class like you are expected to do, you will do well. Tests are very hard, but manageable.
Knows his stuff. Has very entertaining and relevant stories to keep lectures interesting. Homework seems to be graded a little easy, but the midterm and final aren't.

Very professional and helpful but will not babysit you. Homework assignments are excellent -- very interesting and instructive. Will not grade on a curve. Difficult but rewarding class. Power point presentations often had errors -- I've experienced that in all my classes at Bothell, I don't know why.
Computer science is difficult class. I recommend not take a his CSS 161 class. He brings power-points in class, but it's copy from the book. Poor explaination, and careless
Soft spoken, but uses a mike. Sometimes difficult to understand, but encourages questions.  Hard but fair exams.  Really knows his stuff.
Excellent professor, eager to help students. You really learn stuff in his classes.

Fukuda is very open to explanations and is a very intelligent professor. All of his assignments are relevant, effective, and interesting. Concepts are discussed in detail, assignments are reasonable he is an incredibly fair grader.

Really good professor, took BEDUC205 during winter 2023 and I feel like it was a really fun class. He's a tough grader so prepare to do a great work on the group projects even that there's a few of them. All classes were online so it was easy to be flexible.

Loved Dr. Alcorn, just make sure to take him in person. Online is rough.

Class structure was unorganized, assignments don’t make any sense, includes extra unnecessary words on assignments that don’t make sense, the only thing that was helpful are the student examples he provides us

reviews.comment: Professor is clearly very passionate about what they teach but it just feels very confusing and haphazard. Dr. Alcorn is a well researched, understanding and kind professor. Although, a little loose in his structure and slightly confusing at times. He is always open to questions and clarification. He is disorganized person because he is not a tech person, he is quite old.. He is hilarious & inspirational. I love this prof!! He is super nice and open to help all his students. If you have questions on the exam he will help you if you talk to him. reviews.comment: By far the easiest class I have ever seen. He is an extremely nice grader, as long as you participate he will like you. There was 4 homeworks and only 3 are graded. Great professor!! This class was interesting but with the wrong professor could be boring. With Francetich though the class was easy to understand, he gives thoughtful explanations and always has a smile on his face! Only a few homework's throughout the whole thing and the final is easy!

Ignore the course I chose, I had him for BCORE107 and he's genuinely a really nice guy who will give feedback and help if you ask. Only reason I rated him a 4 is because his lectures can feel a little heavy and often over-explained. Overall, a good professor.
This is my favorite professor in UW Bothell, and I've took his classes twice. He's very patient and would teach you on the problem you are still confused!

reviews.comment: the study guides and homework are extremely helpful for learning the material. the midterm and final exam are very similar to the hw/guides so as long as you put in the effort and not cheat on those you will be good. i found his lectures clear to understand despite the accent. very organized and moves at a reasonable pace

Professor Alejandro was a wonderful teacher! It was his first time teaching this class, but he showed that he truly cared about his students' success. His teaching was a bit slow, so make sure to pay attention or you might miss some things. Study on the study guides, and you will be set for exams!

He is one of my favorite professors, his lectures are quite slow but he will make sure that all the topics will be covered. He answers all questions and emails very promptly. I really highly recommend you take his classes as he is one of the nicest professors I've come across.

I would definitely take him again. He was kind, accommodating, and answered any questions to the best of his ability. slower pacing. homework is helpful for learning. gives study guides, and similar to the exams exams. He also offers extra credit!  I always got C's in my econ courses but ended with an A- with him. Alejandro is a very nice and likable professor. Almost all of class time is taken up by lecture, participation is not required, there is a homework about every week, and there is a midterm and final exam. The class is difficult but you can tell he truly wants his students to learn.
Best professor for Economics!

This professor is great, he's really straightforward and gives you all the materials and opportunities to succeed. Nice guy, but the lectures are so boring and I often find found myself zoning out. The homeworks are worth way much more points than it should be , and office hours don't teach much. Also the homeworks are way harder than the exercises we did in class.

Nice guy. Helpful over email and during office hours if you get confused. Quiet voice with a bit of an accent so you have to pay attention.

Hes a great person, really cares about your grades. He helps students whenever they are struggling, and he has a lot patience and willing to change your grades when theres a mistake on grading. Its easy to get a good grade if you are willing to study the slides and the mock exam he gives you.

Professor is really nice and can be pretty lenient on grading homework, but his lectures are incredibly boring. Be prepared to self teach if you have a low attention span such as myself. talks very fast during lextures which makes it hard to keep up, but does her best to support everyone's learning. Both exams and quizzes are harder than you would expect, especially for an intro to marketing class. Class average stayed pretty low.

cool new professor to UWB. not easy class but not hard. lot of different concepts to remember but all tests are open note and quizzes are take home. textbook not required. lectures could be slower she talks really fast but class is overall interesting and she curves grades at the end take her! :)
relaxed professor, very chill, exam grading very forgiving, allows laptop/matlab for exam + final. take if available.

Ghofrani is just great. He solves all the problems on the board. Lectures are very helpful for homework. The exams are just like the homework and practice problems he has posted. Before each exam, he has a review session, which is very helpful. He really cares for his students.

Ghofrani is prob the 2nd best EE Prof. just his lectures are very work heavy rather than concept heavy. I feel like sometimes we get lost doing work rather than understanding why we're doing. Are you guys paying attention?

one of the best teacher I had ever, clear lecture, logic grader, full of acknowledge. I passed theory of circuits and power system with him.

Prof, Ghofrani is great, he really takes his time to make sure you understand the materials if you put in the work, if you dont then he will not go the extra step for you. He works on quality over quantity. Exams are moderate but they are a lot of work. He is a fair grader.

This professor is great. He taught this class as if you forgot everything from 215,  and brought you up to speed on everything before you charged forward. Good professor. He is good lecturer, but he sometimes gets attitude and changes from good guy to rude. Knock his office and he will listen you while he is inside doing nothing. He is the best teacher ever. You can ask him anything you like and he ll answer you. He is top of the subject teaching it. He is the best in EE bothell.
Dude's a stallion and one of the best teachers I've had in this department. Actually learned during lectures.

idk why hes rated so highly...his instructions for essays are vague and he grades tough. and his canvas is hard to navigate. attendence is required but the lectures feel SO long because its so boring. hes got a very monotone none engaging tone that makes it hard to stay paying attention

group project is tough but the professor is helpful and nice. Most students taking 470 and 480 right before their graduations, and he did not give us hard times. Farewell, UW, Fleming is a great professor.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleming was a great professor. He was personable, understanding, and enthusiastic about what he was teaching. It was refreshing to have a professor as invested as he was at this point in the MBA program.

Readings and case studies were tied in very well with the concepts and methodologies that were taught. Professor Fleming made excellent use of class time and provided detailed feedback before grading that ultimately produced better work and better learning. Instruction effort was above and beyond!

Brandon Fleming is an awesome professor! I highly recommend him. His lectures are amazing. He gives great feedback and he responds to emails in a very timely manner. Attendance is necessary for his class as you need to know what is going on and what is coming up. If you don't understand something, talk to him or send him an email. He is amazing!

Stay up to date with what's happening in the world. Professor knows a lot about various companies and industries, along with his speciality - startups. Strike up conversation(s) about career interests and you'll get some insightful advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Brandon is passionate and has a very good understanding of business. You will learn a lot, but if you are taking the capstone course with him, know this: -He makes you write a lot (5 essays total). -He is the harshest grader I've ever had. -Unlike most classes, you HAVE to do his readings. The reading concepts stay relevant for the entire course.

WORST EXPERIENCE. It was text heavy with a requirement to read 200+ pages per week. Course load was equivalent to a masters class rather than an undergrad. Were required to do "video" essays as a precursor to "video job interviews" - been in the working world 6+ years and never had a video interview. Professor continually touted himself. RUN!!
