reviews.comment: No problems with him, pretty cool guy.
He's a good guy. You can sort of tell that he's new, but he's also trying hard. He's overall pretty good!
Good professor, handcuffed by material and curriculum at UW Bothell. Reasonable and down to earth guy. Best technical writing instructor at UWB.

You can tell this guy is a new teacher. Rubrics are unclear and he isn't good at explaining it when you ask questions about it. I didn't know of anyone who got full credit on big projects/final project. Will find places to take points off if he doesn't like you.
BEST TEACHER EVER!

Mr. Porter is a pretty easy grader so long as you meet his clearly stated requirements.  There's a lot of reading, but the homework and assignments are pretty manageable.  He really values participation though, so if you don't care or slack off it'll show in your grade.
It was good.

Ian Porter is a disgrace to the University of Washington staff. His expectations exceed every standard and does not know how to evaluate student's work. I will never take another class from him again.  Not only does he randomly grade work by favorites, he never sets clear expectations. DON'T TAKE AND AVOID IAN AT ALL COSTS.

Although his lectures aren't mandatory, I still went to almost all of them, I enjoyed them, and they were quite engaging. As long as you do around half the extra credit stuff, you can get a 3.6+. He lets you revise all of your essays as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He has a grading system where a 3.0 is extremely accessible. In his class, a 3.0 is 100%. You want a 3.5? Well, prepare about 50 points in extra credit, or "UP" assignments. A 4.0? That's 180 points. If you're not willing to go the extra miles for a 4.0, take another 134 class. If you don't care about your GPA, this is the one.

You can't earn above a 3.0 without extra credit, which is just more busy work like the regular assignments. Doesn't teach anything besides organization strategies that are done through video lectures. In person, he just does "workshops" where he asks people how they are doing on their project and then he talks for 90% of the time with direction.

-Offers extra credit in assignments (lots of writing, 10-65 pts)
-Assignments are watching videos, noting observations, reflecting, and peer reviewing
-Allows all assignments to be done until the end of the quarter, but it is recommended to stay caught up
-2 blog posts, requiring one long-form (1600-2400 words) and short-form post (500-800 words)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is lots of busy work and he has a labor based grading policy (more effort put in more points). There is 1 group project spread throughout the quarter (pretty easy). One big final paper due at the end of the quarter (hard). He does not give clear instructions on basically anything so ask him lots of questions. He is very kind and approachable

took a year ago. hs/AP style teaching, cares for your fundamentals. may be difficult if you have no experience, but he is a great lecture-er, makes things interesting, might be a little intimidating, used to do cold call/pick on students. funny guy.

Exams are very difficult, homeworks are extensive and time consuming. Funny guy, treats his students like high schoolers though (somewhat justified). Don't expect a good grade unless you apply yourself. Exams are curved.

I would not recommend any of his courses. Although he tries to appear humorous and caring toward students in front of a large audience, he often speaks to students in an unfriendly and condescending tone at other times. He tends to distrust what students say. This stark contrast in his behavior is deeply unpleasant and makes me feel disgusted.

He's not a bad teacher, he allows some extensions and extra credit opportunities. He does make jokes in class and admits that he doesn't know some things when teaching the lecture; maybe some students find that upsetting. For a computer science teacher, I would rate him well; unlike him, most professors are bad at explaining and hard to deal with.

He's generally a pretty nice guy; however, he loves to cold call and try to embarrass or mess with the students to a certain degree if they don't get the answer right. He also makes a lot of mistakes and unclear questions on exams and the "exit tickets". Aside from all that, he can be pretty funny and he does a good job of teaching the material.

Jeff is, unfortunately, the least effective instructors I've had in my whole life. NOT recommend taking his class. He tries to be funny, but the lectures mostly consist of reading directly from slides and end up feeling very dull. The lectures offered little help in understanding the course material. Exams require writing full code by hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: i'm not here to simply dog on a prof, but stride is the worst css prof ever. i've taken 3 css classes at my time at uwb and i don't think i've had a worse prof. his lectures are all over the place, he cold calls in class all the time, he's very passive aggressive and has no remorse for his students, even when they are going thru a difficult time
His classes are difficult and he's a pretty tough grader, however he is also a pretty great teacher that seems like he really enjoys teaching his class.

Don't take him. Very difficult grader, purposely intensified material and constantly reiterating that this class is a “weed out class”. Test heavy, tries to always catch people cheating, even though he wouldn't have to worry about that if tests were doable. If you are stuck with him, pick a god and start praying, you're gonna need it 💀
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
I had him for 490, he made it very clear UW had him teach this class (which changes topics each time) last minute so that's why it seemed all over the place, don't blame him.
He definitely teaches like we're young hs students but put your pride aside, let him teach, and you'll learn. I loved his lessons on multi-threading the most.

I had Stride for 490. Don't take this class with Stride, his class structure is all over the place he changed the final multiple times. He provides very little info to help you understand material, all you get is slides and that's it. Goes super fast in lectures and is confrontational when you ask him questions.

I had Stride for 490. If you liked high school and the getting talked to like a kid then you'll like Stride. He means well and cares which i appreciate but he believes that everyone is as passionate as him about 490 which is annoying. His exams are difficult and structured poorly, you can't go back after you answer a question. Would not recommend
Really enjoyed 143 by Prof Stride, would definitely take again

stride is a great professor. he's very much tough love but he genuinely wants you to succeed. his lectures are helpful and, if not anything else, memorable. he's a really funny guy and makes a tough class much more enjoyable. there's a lot of projects which can be hard if you're someone who just started programming. tests are curved VERY well!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Stride is a great teacher, but the class isn't easy. Homework isn't always 100% unless your code follows the right format. Tests are 70% of your grade, so studying is a must. If you put in the effort, you'll do fine. He's super helpful in office hours and makes the class fun with his humor. Would definitely recommend!

Professor Stride is honestly a good professor if you decide to put in the time and effort to understand the concepts. Lectures are whole class periods and I recommend to look at the lectures on canvas before classtime a bit so you know the general idea. The hw category is not a free 100%, and study well for the midterms and finals as they are hard.
A very challenging class. If you put in the effort you can succeed, but the exam grading is brutal and often the lecture material is not sufficient to study with. Be prepared to participate in class.
Lots of reading and doesn't adhere to his own time schedule sometimes. But he's flexible and is easy to work with. If you put in the effort he'll notice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: out of the two 1 star reviews one person is complaining they got caught cheating (lol) and the other says it is a very difficult class (true but expected). Professor Stride is funny and helpful and makes class something to look forward too despite the difficulty. The homework assignments can be hard but translate well to midterms.

Prof Stride is great. He cares about your learning, going to his office hours helps. Class is test heavy with 45% being midterms but literally any class u take for comp sci is going to be like this. 82.67 or 83 flat is a minimum to pass which again, BARE MINIMUM for most comp sci classes. People who complain about him are just bad at studying lol.

Super difficult class, tons of homework outside of class. Professor is a great person no doubt, not too sure about teacher. Midterms are worth 45% of your grade, make sure to do well on them. 7 homework assignments that are quite hard, ZyBooks assignments that are easy; 5 late days are given to use on homeworks. Very tough class, 83% just to pass.

He cares a lot about cheating, which I get, but his way of handling it feels a bit extreme. He's more focused on catching students than actually helping us learn, and his learning style is really bad because he randomly calls on people and his lectures are pretty boring. DON'T take him if you want a good grade in the class.

Jeff is a great professor, his lectures are engaging and he knows what he is talking about. Yes, the class is very hard 75% of your grade is based on midterms and a final. Grading on homework assignments gets harder as the quarter progresses, but all homework has feedback. If you ask for help and go to office hours he will help you!
Test heavy class with hard grading system. Handwritten tests and minimal feedback. I do not recommend this class if you care about your GPA!

Class is DIFFICULT, like really hard. Tests are handwritten, lectures are the whole class period and can get confusing. Many people say this professor is really great literally only because he makes the class laugh and tells jokes, which is good, but it's a HARD class and don't take it if you expect an easy grade, I'd say stay away!

Very chill professor who knows what he's talking about! He spices up his lectures with jokes and real life applications of what he's teaching and engages with the class in a very unique and interesting way! The class was very hard but he made the experience of a weedout class extremely enjoyable!
Best professor I've ever had

I took him for CSS&143, my first quarter at UW-Bothell and he was outright amazing. He made the class feel like it was less of a weed out class than it actually was. While the course itself if tough and you need to put in around 20 hours per week, I would say taking Stride makes it much less stressful since you can learn way better if you take him.

Mr. Stride cares deeply for the class content and students. He spices up lectures with a good dose of jokes and real-world experience in the industry. He is very experienced and one of the best teachers I have had the fortune to learn from.

Professor Stride made the material super easy to understand and was very engaging throughout his lectures. He made the class enjoyable, when I heard bad things about other professors for the same class. Definitely want to get him as a professor.

Professor Stride is a wonderful newcomer to the CSS dept who demonstrates enthusiasm through combining profound knowledge of the software industry and prior teaching experience. Mr. Stride teaches how to actually innovate through meaningful, challenging projects and lectures. He has been the best instructor at UWb I've had so far. Please take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Glad I didn't listen to the bad reviews. He's a kind and funny professor that teaches the material just fine. Grade was heavily weighed by comprehensive exams so it's really going to depend on how well you prepare for that. One sheet of notes was allowed as well. Grading for group work was lax and I believe most of my class walked away with As/Bs.

Exams are 50 percent of the grade. It's  best to study the homework, exercises, and do a lot of outside learning. Professor goes through slides and exercises, but it's hard to comprehends the topics he goes through since he mumbles a lot. He's kind but not the best at teaching
I'm not sure why Jeff has so many bad reviews, but he was a pretty chill professor who graded fairly and even gathered and implemented student feedback on what the class average should be.

Classes are very lecture heavy, he expects you to know the code already to do the assignments (this is a beginner class). There's a lot of homework to finish before class and he doesn't go over questions given and he didn't teach us how to code! Most of my learning came from youtube. A plus side is he gives answers when we take quizzes in class.

Not sure why he has such bad reviews, hes a good professor and a nice person, show up to class, submit work on time and you'll be good. I also see that he teaching outdated concepts but thats not his fault blame the CSS head lol.
If you love yourself DO NOT take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE. DO NOT take Jeff unless your life depends on it. He's a very stingy grader, lectures are more dead than a cemetery and he grades like the points are coming out of his paycheck. TERRIBLE. Easily the worst professor I've taken at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Teaches outdated concepts and gives subpar feedback. Expects a lot out of his assignments while simultaneously not teaching us all that much during his lecture. Online materials are hard to follow and his office hours are very much out of people's network. Overlap in assignment due dates and unclear rubric. Stray away.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF!!!! He was never consistent in terms of the rubric for assignments. NO REGRADING and only feedback is given. Feedback was never useful.

There was one class where he talked about the low grading in class and mentioned "You have to be actively trying to fail to fail this class"

Would NEVER take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the most frustrating class I have ever taken in my entire life. Incredibly unclear rubric and assignments, harsh grading, and incomprehensible feedback. Does not take his student's concerns seriously. Impossible to understand. The average for the midterm was 32/50 and he said we did WELL. Avoid him at all costs. Seriously. I warned you.

Took it in the summer, he's a nice person but not the best at explaining programming concepts. I like the online resources he shared with us to practice programming, they were very useful. I think he's a caring teacher but doesn't teach in a necessarily effective way.

If you think the class is important, you should take Kim, but I found it to be pretty useless. His office hours are never available. If you don't have a good team, you will get like 70% on your group assignments. Getting feedback from him before a homework submission only confuses me more. The grade in canvas was the actual grade I got.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the actual canvas grade doesnt really reflect the grade u will get on ur transcript. He is very lenient when it comes to those things which is why I rated him so highly. He gives a lot of work and is a harsh grader with ambiguity in what he wants for the assignments. Overall, he gives decent feedback and you do learn a lot in this class.

Worst professor I've had to date in the Computer Science program at UW Bothell. One his lectures are boring, two he can't even write a proper assignment rubric, and three he will let his emotions grade. DO not take this class, seems nice but is extremely petty and disorganized.

Jeff Kim is one of those "awesome person, ok professor" dynamic. His grading criteria was very confusing and HARD. If you do take him, before submitting, try and ask to get it proofread by him to make sure everything meets his criteria, because your grade can tank heavily. Lectures are quite boring tbh. He was a cool guy, but his class was hard.

I took him twice because the sections best fit my schedule, for 360 + 350. He's a really nice guy and is willing to work with you and cares a lot about your understanding of the class. Not the teacher for everyone, his lectures ARE kinda boring but he really wants you to attend and participate. Not a GPA killer, just do the work and you'll be fine.

The worst prof at uwb. He does not respect his students, he acts like he is superior. He literally refuses to meet outside of class. His teaching method is horrible, he does not make sense at all. If it's not teached by him, take the class if you're new to coding. If you already code, THIS CLASS IS A WASTE OF TIME, it will not prepare you for 142.

This professor is extremely unclear about grading it's a bit unbelievable. During a test that we took, half the students complained that he didn't give proper instructions on what he wanted and he still marked us down on those questions. Very boring lectures; it's almost impossible to keep up with what he's saying for a whole 2 hours.
Worst prof I've had to date. Teaching non-relevant topics and outdated practices. Unclear and ambiguous requirements. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

He's a really nice guy and is very open to student feedback, but I could be more engaged watching paint dry than I am with his lectures. I will say it's nice that he curves, because the quizzes are hard. Lots of group assignments/quizzes, so get in a good group, as a good group can make 350 the easiest of the CSS core classes.

Oh my God. There are few instructors that can bore the paint off of walls like Dr. Kim. Gives the absolute least amount of effort possible in teaching his class, and acts like you should come in already knowing Java. (which I did, and honestly, I got better grades once I stopped paying attention to him and just did the assignment the way I knew)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take these reviews with a grain of salt. Jeff Kim is a great professor. His lectures can be VERY long winded (watch panoptos instead), but you can tell he really cares about his students and his work. Even while taking his class online, I felt a personal connection to him just by showing up to his zoom lectures. Nicest professor ever

People asked me about online classes and what profs were best/worst from spring so I am putting Kim down as a no-take. Even if CS is life for you, this guy is so boring and tells you 0 new and is useless things online. In-person for CS 142 he was a little better but seeking him out is a joke that is not funny. He goes on & on in a monotone voice.

Seems like a great guy. However, grading is somewhat slow and by a grader. Disputes with grades are longer to deal with. Grader also isn't detailed with explaining wrong questions. Lots of homework. Sometimes two assignments due at the same day. Lectures are long, boring, and some only needed to know for exams. Groupwork expects too much

Lots of homework, group work, and reading. Unclear expectations in assignments and quizzes. Very "rambling" style lectures. Nice guy, gives lots of feedback and is communicative outside of class, but overall a class with lots of work but little to no actual learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Jeff expects a lot from his assignments. most are group work. There's a final project and presentation. The lectures can get very boring and hard to follow. He always has connection issues with zoom. Jeff does try to show enthusiasm in his lectures but the overall material in 350 is unenjoyable. he seems like he would be somewhat better in person.

Professor Kim is a really nice and understanding professor. If you have questions he will clarify to the best of his abilities and the quizzes are there to help you. Homework is the top priority for your grade. If you don't go to class you won't get the quiz codes or exam codes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Kim is a really great guy. I'm taking his css 101 class right now and honestly he's not given enough credit in these other reviews. He helps you with any homework questions you have if you email him and he makes sure you understand the concepts. The class itself isn't too difficult, it's a very good class to take if you're new to coding.

Professor Kim was very nice and caring toward us students, especially in the wake of COVID19. However, I believe that his lecturing could be improved, as I felt that his lectures were spent too long on loosely-relevant examples in the PowerPoint and/or ended up rambling -- allowing less time in class to go over student work for future assignments.

Such a boring and easy class. It's like the intro to the concepts you end up learning in CSS 142/143, which makes it pretty skippable tbh. I wouldn't take it. He's a nice person and all, nothing against him in THAT capacity, but I don't like his teaching style.

Graded on a curve and you have group projects and quizzes that are graded as a group. Average is a 3.1. Workload is massive and don't hope you'll know what he wants you to do. Grades on participation as well. Fun guy but so, so not worth the pain and suffering. Take literally anyone else and I'm sure it will turn out better for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Accessible outside class but that's basically it. Mostly just boring and not as interactive as I'd hope.
No work whatsoever and really boring. I don't even know why I took this class. Take this (BIS 111/CSS 101) with a hard schedule like I did.
Mostly just boring. He's a nice guy but as a professor he wasn't very good - he assigned lots of busy work and didn't integrate IAS things such as the portfolio and research that much.

Not good. Half the time it just didn't seem like he cared and half the time he just assigned us with busy work "cause he felt like it" while grading it extremely easy (90% of homework was graded on completion). At least you can find and talk to him outside class if you need to.

This professor was among the most frustrating professors Ive ever had. Unclear quizzes that are just memorization, and vague enough to make you think its based on the content or your thoughts. Condescending responses to questions, as well. If you can, avoid taking him for classes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Most vague teacher ever. Good luck getting a good grade on any quiz. If you're going to be that specific with what you want your answer to be, ask a more specific question. Grader does all the work, he just has us present in class. Also, fix your paper criteria. There's a reason we email you asking what you're saying. Do better, we pay for this.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim is a nice guy and a good professor. All you have to do is pay attention and apply yourself. He's willing to work individually and make compromises if something goes wrong in your life. The class I took was CSS 101 but that was not an option above.
This guy is hilarious!!! He also is very nice and explains things well. I have had so much fun learning about computers this quarter!!

Jeff Kim is one of the most frustrating professors ever in the CSS department. Drones during class lectures, grades super harshly on exams, homework not clear, you name it. Avoid him for 350 and 360 at all costs unless you really want a professor that 1. makes subjects harder than they look and 2. Makes you feel super stressed out over your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but terrible teacher. He is very vague and adds a lot of fuzz to his lectures, making them confusing and difficult to follow. Half of the lectures were also student presentations. Be prepared to do a lot of learning from your readings and memorizing key terms. He looks for exact terms on tests and grades harshly. Don't expect full points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is very inconsistent when it comes to grading, especially the midterm and final. He assigns homework without giving any instruction whatsoever on what his expectations are. I would not recommend taking this class unless you want to play russian roulette with your GPA. My worst class experience in college to date.

This guy isn't the best choice when it comes to intro CS classes. I only succeeded because I had taken this class previously as an AP class in high school, and had a basic grasp of the concepts. His belief that you should read 15+ hours a week for an intro class? Come on. Poorly explains concepts, expects the textbook to teach for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very interactive lectures, you must read the textbooks and memorize any important diagrams in them to pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Got a 1.4 in his class, then took the class again with another professor and got a 3.7. Before he failed me, I talked to him and he suggested I change my major. I'm not even a CS student. I needed the credit for my Business degree. MIS major....

So unpredictable. His lectures are mostly explanations, but when you ask a question because you don't understand, he just says there's no "answer" and just "think about it". Thought I did great on the final, got like a D. He's quite laid back though and is nice in personality but not a great lecturer or explainer.
Seems like a good guy, but he's teaching a hard course very quickly. He seems knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, but his instructions are confusing sometimes.

Jeff was stubborn with his helping of students, often criticizing his students when asking questions about how they didn't learn the material the first time around. His teachings weren't horrible but they were also unclear and his quizzes are toughly graded. If you manage to do well on the midterm and final project, graded by a TA, then you'll pass

Jeff Kim's class was probably one of the most frustrating I've taken at UWB. He wants to believe that there are no "correct" answers to the vague and unremarkable topics that are covered, but when it comes to test time, get ready to give exact answers.

What can I say. For me, this course in itself was in a sense, hard to concentrate on and dry. The material takes some patience to grasp. The professor I think was witty and explained some things clearer than others. He grades difficult, he can be unclear on what he's looking for on quizzesHW. Get ready to read alot as well.
He was very enthusiastic to teaching and very helpful when you ask questions. However, it is very hard to understand how he graded on exam and quiz. He deducted too many points on subjective answers.

The lectures are great and he is definitely excited about the material he is teaching.  He does a great job of providing a variety of content for all the topics covered in the course. He doesn't provide a clear rubric for assignments, even when you ask him, which can make them pretty toughfrustrating.

I thought 301 was bad, but this class is hands down the worst class of the entire major. Was super boring and Jeff  bans all electronic devices so you have to listen to him drone on in class . He grades completely randomly and the median for the final was 62%. It was so easy, but he just took off random points to bring the average down. Never again

Jeff is a great professor. This was my first CS class. I would ask questions all the time & he would take the time to clarify. The HW is not that hard, I would finish them in one day (~8 hours). Beware though, his tests are extremely difficult, but doable, I got good grades on them. I definitely recommend Jeff though!
Don't take him if you want to get a good grade. His exams and homework are extremely difficult. I definitely do not recommend him.

I thought Management Principles was going to be a very boring class, but with this teacher it became a very interesting course with practical advice and discussion about the work environment. Tests were a bit keyword-oriented, and it is heavy on group work so make sure you like who you're with.

Loved everything about her class. Records lectures upon request, gives 5 point extra credit project, has clear grading criteria, prompt responses on Canvas messages and emails, actually cares about her students and teaches very well. Lectures are all easy understand, and very relevant to the homework assignments. Given note sheet for exams too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Joanna is theee GOAT of the UW CS department. I wish I could take her for everything. She doesn't skip anything and really makes sure the class understands concepts. Exam also allowed 1 sheet of notes and grading is very fair. Her exam prep was also consistent to what was actually on tests. Couldn't recommend more!!
Really love this prof.

She made the concepts of 343 so easy to understand - I wish I could take her for the harder class like 422 and 430. She mainly tests your understanding and logic. Her lectures are worth attending but she will record them if you ask - and puts her best effort into the quality of those recordings. Puts a lot of effort into lesson plans too!

Professor Wang completely reinvented CSS 350 into a practical, engaging, and thought-provoking course. Everything she taught, from Agile and Jira to group leadership and ethics. was directly applicable to real-world work, and I've never had a UW Bothell class prepare me for industry like this one.

She's a caring professor who makes the tough concepts in CSS 343 much easier to understand. Before each of the two non-cumulative exams, she held helpful review sessions. She's always willing to help and happy to answer questions.

Professor Reinnoldt is extremely knowledgable in business and ethics. He is very understanding and puts quality time and effort into his classes. His non-profit, TeachersforTomorrow is dedicated to improving Cambodian education acts as an example to students for how they should approach the world.

He's a good professor. He makes participation a requirement which really isn't that hard to follow through. He has a clear structure of how he wants his assignments submitted. After about a week are 2 it's very easy to be accustomed to the pacing of the class. Pretty laid back and chill class, if I could take it again I would. Very easy class.

Professor Reinnoldt was great. He has a ton of real-world experience in his field, allowing his contribution to the topics to be much more meaningful. He connected ideas to real-world scenarios, making everything easier to understand. Attendance is mandatory, and there are weekly assignments. As long as he knows you understand, you'll have an A.

He's a great teacher who knows what he's talking about. He uses very interesting scenarios that he's had to deal with in the past in business to teach the class. Beyond that, he also just has a lot of practical advice for the class. The weekly writing reflections can be a handful, but they're manageable as long as you don't wait until last minute.

Lectures are so interesting. Tells a lot of stories about his life and careers and travel which was cool. Lots of assigments which can be a bit overwhelming at times, but I would say doing them as soon as possible helps a lot. Uses a lot of the Canvas textbox for assigments which can make it difficult to import  pictures but that was my only issue.

Good lecture material. If you follow instructions and actively pay attention, you will be successful in this class. Many points can be missed simply by failing to follow instructions or carefully doing your assignments. Group project was okay. Due to the nature of an online course, many people are unmotivated including potential group members.

Overly political and stubborn. Spends a significant portion of time complaining about Trump, when it isn't relevant to the course material. 

Very stubborn on grading, and takes miscommunication personal. Harbors no leniency, even if you may be in the right. Unprofessional, would not recommend signing up. Missing a single class exempts credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Went on his CSR study abroad program in 2024 to Thailand and Cambodia and had a great time. The work for this class over the summer was extensive preparation to learn the history of the areas we were going to. But on the trip, I had a great time and really enjoyed learning from him and people he brought to guest lecture.

Condescending, uncaring, and unprofessional in class and via email. Can't plan according to his schedule b/c he often adds assignments, sometimes 1-2 days before they are due. Not tech-savvy. Didn't know how to efficiently operate his class over Zoom, and we constantly had to wait on him. Threatens his students with academic dishonesty every class.

Professor Reinnoldt is very wise and inspiring. He uses real-world examples of business and ethics. All assignments have a strict, clear structure and you can get good grades as long as you follow the directions. There are some group discussions and projects, but not many.

If you are interested in business definitely take this professor. He has a lot of real world examples and stories that can be boring at times but it's still a good class to take. Final project was a presentation and we had 1 quiz throughout the class which was easy. Overall Easy class if you just do the work.
This professor has a unique teaching style, but if you engage with it, the class is very worthwhile. Use unstuck study and the free textbook to prep - it really helps.

Do not take this class. He has a lot of real world experience and is not afraid to talk about it in depth. Despite this being an online class, every interaction I've had with him has made me uncomfortable. He's an Ethics teacher he will constantly threaten you with academic dishonesty on every assignment. I wish I took a different course.

Professor Reinnoldt is one of the best I've ever had. He is a very genuine person, clearly knows what he is talking about, has fantastic stories, and is more than understanding that things sometimes come up. The work is easy and relevant, the group projects aren't too bad, and the final(s) were quite easy too. Would take again 10/10 times.

The instructor has a lot of practical, real-world experience. He brought in some helpful guest speakers also with practical, real-world experience. Material was challenging since I don't have a lot of background in globalization, but instructor wants students to succeed. The work load was reasonable.

This is one of the easiest classes I have taken. Grading is not harsh and the assignments are not difficult, the professor really does try to help you get the best grade possible. The professor also gives good advice for things beyond college, he genuinely cares about his students. I recommend taking this professor if you can.

I think he is a fantastic teacher. Everything is very clearly outline in terms of his expectations. He has a lot of knowledge about current events and the way the world works, and he clearly explains them using different frameworks. He is quite clear and what he expects everybody to know, and bases the examinations on the concepts.
I am now in his class. So far, so good.   Good assignments.  He has a lot of experience to share         Very worthwhile class I think.

Just took marketing management with him.  Great class.  He shares so many experiences. 
i would take him again anytime

Class is easy but the guy is very passive aggressive and rambles off a lot. You will hear about his very wealthy brother and his friday cold swims a lot. He has an old-school approach to his guidelines. If you are patient, this class is for you, but if you are an efficient person you will lose your mind. Also make sure to enter from the backdoor.

His Intro to Marketing class is one of the best classes I have ever taken. Be sure to get a good team!

Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took business ethics and business writing. Great classes. Learned a lot about current ethical issues. He has a lot of experience to share.  Be sure to take good notes and attend the study review sessions!

He was great. Good example of business experience and relate it well to class material. He also talk a lot about career advice like interview skills and being an effective new employee.  Just be sure to be on time, take good notes and participate and you will be fine in this class
His lectures were the best of my education.  He is very professional and maintains high standards in a manner that clearly simulates the business world.

I have never met a professor as unprofessional as he is after years of going to various colleges around the west coast. I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw how condescending his tone was when he replied to my email after letting him know that our group ran into some issues.

Professor James is pretty intense. He does give a lot of valuable work experience that ties into Ethics and Writing. The assignments are helpful but he is all about concision and clearness. Weekly quizzes on lectures and readings so pay attention. Attendance is mandatory to get a good grade. If you do the work, you'll do fine. Detail matters alot
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great classes Great teacher. Real-like application of key lessons. On-line learning is not so good but still a great class

He has a lot of business experience that he shares and relates to marketing theory. I have taken two classes with him. Overall a very effective professor. He gave us mini quizzes each week that were not too hard if you actually did the reading. Very worthwhile and highly recommended

Class is mostly lecture-heavy and lots of group assignments. He posts his PowerPoint, but they don't include all of the slides sometimes. He does not record his lectures. He has clear criteria and is not so accommodating/flexible towards student's personal situations. Take this class only if you aren't busy with other things.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Yes greatly agree with the last comment: He is a GREAT teacher. Great lessons. Really committed to making his students become successful. But, if you miss class or miss assignments, your grades will suffer. That is the way it works, huh?

Ignore the students that gave this Professor bad ratings. If you do the work, you will have NO PROBLEMS in this class. I learned the MOST in this course. I have used the assignment materials from this course to get internships and now I get contacted by recruiters every week. I have become a much better writer because of this class.

Really good classes with him in marketing and business writing. He is very current on global issues and trends and will incorporate these into his classes and lectures. Very useful tool skills learned in business writing
This is the second class that I have taken with him. He is quite demanding but clear and reasonable in his expectations. Great examples and stories
His class is the best I have had since high school. Learned so much about business ethics and business writing skills. Group work can be a drag, though :-(

Please do not waste your tuition money in his class it's not worth it. I know its mandatory but do yourselves a favor and find a different professor. Honestly, you will not learn a single thing. James Reinnoldt, requires three group projects without a rubric or clear direction, then grades with an iron fist.
Best class I have taken. learned so much especially from his experiences in Asia as a consultant and airline executive. I would be happy to take his classes again

His Business Writing class this past quarter was amazing. Great examples given and great skills passed to students. It is best to attend every lecture if you want to do well on the assignments. No final exam :-)
His Business Ethics class was the best I have ever taken, despite it being an online class. He is quite fair but very demanding. Great business stories and cases!

this teacher is seriously one of the MOST UPSETTING teachers I have ever had. his grading is really poorly outlined, he's condescending, unhelpful, impatient, and overall rude. he seems to have a superiority complex and hate for students who miss small details at times. he constantly gloats about being an ethical and fair person (which isn't true)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed his classes. You have to do a lot of work but it is well worth it. He uses a lot of slides so take notes!
Really liked his classes. This was my 2nd one. He is very interactive with the class and very experienced. Shares a lot of career success tips
Great overall. Classes are run like a business. Learned a lot about ethics and writing tools. Highly recommended. (but need more guest speakers!)
Excellent class. Unfortunately we were doing this online so it was not as personal as it could have been, but still very worthwhile. Learned a lot!

Condescending. Inconsistent. I took every opportunity to get the best grade, worked hard. At the end of the class he sent me a personal email critiquing my appearance. Highly unprofessional. I came to class in work attire regularly. Even if you get 100% it isn't good enough, he will feel threatened and find something wrong with you. Avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Reinnoldt is excellent. He uses the business world to frame his classes which gives us a good sense of how important skills like communication can be. He is not an easy grader, but if you meet the deadline and show effort, you will do fine. Many students complain about this style because, simply, they don't do the work and they get bad grades

I took Prof Reinholdt's ethics and managerial comms class last year. His class was not too hard but he is strict about deadlines and standards. But, overall it was a great class. He helped me with career directions and advice

I took Mr. Reinnoldt for Global Business BUS 480 last year. Best teacher I aver had. His classes require team projects and quite a bit of writing. Never really used the textbooks but his own material is great. Alot of experience that he shares

I think he is great. He knows his material and can explain it clearly. Yeah, there are deadlines and strict writing standards, but the jobs I have had also have deadlines and strict writing standards. It is the real world. Some students are definitely not ready. This class helps prepare for it
Learned a lot in his classes. Very personable and helpful. Classes have a team project. Be sure to select a good one
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class wasn't so hard but the online learning challenges were great. I think prof Reinholdt did a great job in the end.... He has a lot of global experience to share

This is the 2nd class I have taken with him. He is really knowledgable and went out of his way to try to teach this class in a highly effective manner despite the first time transition to online learning to COVID. A few students have dissed him in an unreasonable manner. I learned so much in the end.

James Reinnoldt has no business teaching whatsoever. He is the one of the most condescending, uptight, stubborn, asinine, rude and self-absorbed people that I have ever encountered in my life. Wanna learn something in marketing? Read the book and go watch YouTube videos. Hes that one person that will always dump on you if you ask him for help.

Avoid this professor. He is rude and unreasonable. No exams but weekly quizzes suck. He doesn't release the answers so you never know what you're doing wrong. No way to contact him except video office hours (no thnx he's mean) or a class discussion where he likes to embarrass students. Group project sucked no clear expectations. WORST UWB PROF EVER

I would take his class again but only because it was easy and required very little work. The professor himself is terrible, has extremely harsh grading criteria; not the right font, lost 50% of the assignment grade. Hard to get in contact with to the point where it's not worth it.

He did not want to be contacted directly. You had to ask him questions through the discussion board. He was not helpful and was angry a lot of the time. He showed us his feet. He made group projects of 10 people that were not in the same section, time, or day. I got a decent grade but I could not listen to his whole 2 hour dry lectures.

He is inconsiderate when it comes to his students. He is hard to reach and out of touch and thinks he is always right. I have never felt so dismissed or disrespected by a professor. His material is not hard but he goes out of his way to call out students, make them feel small, and confuse them, turning the entire class experience negative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Attend class everyday(esp first two) and you'll have a great quarter. Amazing professor, would take again, very interesting/stimulating lectures. Do the online readings. Group project heavy, so be warned on that side and try to work with good people. One of the best I've had at UWB.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: James is an amazing professor, you will learn a ton from him in any class that you take. If you are able to closely follow directions and do what he expects at the level that he expects, you'll do great in the class. If you get to know him he can be a really caring guy! Could probably help you get a job in any place you wanted if you connect w/ him
Great class. Learned a lot about the fundamentals of marketing. Great personal stories. Be sure to pick a good team
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pretentious person who changes his mind a lot, but not too difficult of grader. Tests/quizzes not hard as long as you pay attention. Follow his writing guidelines and you'll get full points. Choose your project team wisely as marketing project worth a lot of points. My group didn't communicate well, and I had to do many of the parts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great teacher although low key still scares me. Not afraid to call people out during class. DO NOT COME LATE. Shake his hand at the start of the quarter and introduce yourself. Pick a good group for the project. Start working on the brief early. Read guidelines and go to office hours to find out what he wants for assignments its insanely specific
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took him for 307 and 320. His lectures will often make you envious of the fun life that he's lived! He inspires to reach further in life and dream bigger. Always willing to help you outside of class. I got 100% on all of his individual assignments, but the group project is what lowered my grade in both. MAKE SURE YOU PICK A HARD WORKING GROUP!

Professor Reinnoldt is a very respected professor and has incredible lectures. He has lived a really interesting life and looks for ways to incorporate funny and crazy anecdotes into his lectures. Strict and tough grader though, looks for any excuse to take off a point or two (on five point assignments). 8/10 would take again most likely.

Professor Reinnoldt is incredible. Distinguished, intelligent, articulate and amusing. By far my favorite prof in the 2 years and a quarter at UW. His lectures are geared towards current events making it easy to connect the discipline. Everything you learn in this class will be used in the real world. Incredible story teller. Take him for anything.
Great class. Huge amount of work but very relevant. Learned so much. Project teams were a drag. He also really helps students prepare for career skills
Probably the best teacher I have ever had. Interesting stories but alot of focus on airlines and Asia. Fair grades. Alot of work
Great teacher. Great class. Tough grader. But like anything, you get what you pay for. Class project was a lot of work.

Prof Reinnoldt works hard at helping students learn. He knows marketing although the classes are more slanted towards the service industry than consumer products. The class project is okay but you need to pick your classmates well. Textbook use not so important
First time I took marketing class. Was great. Learned alot. Mr. Reinholdt is kind of strict but he simulates a biz office so that is great training.

Great class. Tough grader but learned so much about business communications. As he said at the beginning of the quarter: If you can handle the challenge, take the class. If not, then drop it! I'm glad I stayed
If you are considering taking his class, good luck!
I took business writing with him. Very interesting class. Learned a lot about proper report writing which is very useful. He talks very fast sometimes but just take good notes!
Yes, James is an lenient grader and his workload is manageable. However, he wasn't the nicest professor. He was very condescending. I don't like him
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Am currently taking Business Writing with Pro Reinnoldt. Probably the best class that I have ever taken. He is tough on some people but if you come prepared you will do well.

I have had two classes with Professor Reinnoldt (marketing and ethics) and they were the best of my college career. His classes are a lot of work but very worthwhile nonetheless. Be prepared for group work, and select a good teammates!

I got a 4.0 in the class, did every additional assignment, always sat in the front and participated. At the end of the quarter, he told me I need to smile more to be taken seriously in the business world. So insulting, I was so shocked at how condescending he was like he had to find something wrong with me.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Reinnoldt is amazing. He truly cares about his students, and he goes above and beyond to help his students. I took 3 classes with him and I would take all my classes with him if that possible.

he is a bit intimidating, but a very smart teacher about marketing and he has lots of real world experience that makes his class more interesting. Make sure to never be late or not come to class he is strict on that. Pay attention, pick good teams, and you will do great
Very good teacher. One of the best I've had over the years.   Learned about writing tools for the corporate workplace. Just don't come to his class late and take good notes and you'll do fine

Prof Reinnoldt is a great teacher. Knows business theories and how to apply them. He has a very different teaching style. He NEVER uses notes. Teaches the whole class from memory it seems. He won the Teaching Excellence award two year in row from what I heard

Class is fun as he always gives lectures based on his personal experience. Make sure you take good notes + read the articles he assigns weekly. The marketing plan project requires effort so make sure you pick the right team. His marketing class is more challenging than his 307, but the class is worth it. You'll learn a lot from him.
Knows his stuff. Just listen and take good short notes that will help you on test. Be honest and enjoy his real world stories.

Great lectures full of his experience.  He is clear on his expectations so make sure you read them and follow them carefully.  Take good notes in class. Read ALL the articles cause they will show up on the quizzes and exams.

Pretty good teacher and I looked forward to his class. Assignments are not difficult but, you have to think critically. Lectures are not boring. His experience, engagement, and knowledge about the subject made the class very enjoyable.  You don't really need the book because every question on the final quiz can be answered using lecture notes

Simply speaking:  Great class. Learned (finally!) how to write a decent marketing plan.  Good teacher too (just don't be late for his class!   Textbook waster of money but good that we could buy used one

Great class. I didnt learn anything in my intro to marketing class last year so this class is really helping me. No exams. Lots of guest speakers. He is a great teacher. No wonder he won the business Professor of the Year award last month.

This is a great class. He is a tough grader but hold you to a high standard so you perform well and get prepared for the business world The marketing plan project really helped drive home the key points.  We did not use the textbook very much so it was kind of a waste of money

No respect at all. Mean! 10+ extra credit, each worth 0.05-0.1. Not allowing his student to be late to class for any reason, yet he came to class late for 20 minutes. Double standard. Discrimination. He is helpful, yet I don't think he is a good person. He teaches you how to be ethic but he is not an ethic person.
Best class I ever took. I now understand marketing.  His feedback is direct. Some students can't handle it. Any they won't in the business world either!

Ok teacher. I enjoyed his class in the beginning but when he says "you work will be evaluated against what other students submit," I begin to question just how ethical of a person he is. Easy grade, but may lead to a lack of interest in Marketing given his unwillingness to provide CONSTRUCTIVE feedback - his feedback his aimed to belittle you. GL.

If you're serious about being successful in the business world it is important to surround yourself with people like James Reinnold. He teaches his classes from experience, rather than the text book, giving students a real world look on things. Be your best, work hard and he will reward that ethic.
Real-world. Great professor.
This professor  is a priceless jewel. His class is the greatest gift I have received during my professional education.
This professor is "AMAZING", with capital letters. Do not leave the school before taking a class with him. Best teacher I took at UW.

He's a good teacher. He doesn't give out tests for one thing and the majority of your grade depends on his writing assignments and the final project, which is a TON of work (and time-consuming of course). But overall, a very bright and helpful teacher. I'd recommend him.
This is BEST of he BEST professors I have ever taken in my entire life. Teaches what you are going to need in life. REAL STUFF!
Very good teacher.  He is very clear and highly focused on helping students be successful   No exams bit a lot of writing! Still worthwhile
This was a great class.  Instructor really knows his material.  Does a great job of relating theory to real world.

One of the rare extraordinary instructors who can balance academic content and practical advice for real work in business. His class is always interesting. Not a lot of assignments, but his expectation on the quality of your work increases over time.    He has lots of experiences and  is happy to share all the tips/lessons to succeed in real life.
In class right now in short quarter. Love every minute of it. Tons of work and stupid team members but all in all very worthwhile.  I love the way we discuss current events before each class
Learned so much. Great class. Great teacher. Very practical skills for job market
Good class. Learned alot. Good projects. Team members were a bummer.
Best class I have ever had. Very useful material. I am now prepared for the job market
Very interesting class.  Professor made the material thought-provoking and fun.  Best teacher I've had in all of my schooling!
What a great class. So much experience and an ability to convey stories. He is not easy and will cold call on you but that's part of his style.  Overall great class

I really liked this class and instructor. He is quite fair but expects alot of work from everyone. Still you will get a good grade if you work hard and speak up in class. He has some amazing stories of global business.
Excellent classes and instruction methodologies. Experienced in global business. Great connections between theories and business practices. Well worth it
Interesting. I am an engineer and never really understood marketing. Now I do! Very clear. Good global experience
Liked class alot. Interesting. Stimulation. Teacher has some funny habits like always keeping doors closed. Professional environment. Lots of work. Textbook not worth the money
One of the best classes I ever took was marketing management. Comprehensive, timely and very clear content. Very fair as well: You do well, you get a good grade. If not, well..
Judge students based on personal preference. Biased towards international students. Gives unexpected low scores to students he does not like.

Great class. Very helpful. Really supportive of the students.  Real-world applications towards getting a job, communicating effectively in the office etc. You have to work hard to get a good grade but he is very fair.  The textbook was not used very much but I'd rather listen than read

PROS: very nice, clear and helpful. You will learn a lot from his class.                    Cons: Mocks you in front of the entire class. He gave us our final grade point ONLY and told us to add up whatever papers we have, so good luck finding every one of them.I am 100% sure that I have more points than what he gave me. though I got an A-
Definitely one of my favs so far. If you show dedication and interest he will invest time into growing you in school and beyond that into career goals and objectives. Highly recommend!

He is by far one of my favorite teachers. His classes are interesting and he really knows his material. He also provides a lot of "real world" information. There's a lot of writing in his class and attendance is mandatory because he throws pop quizzes. He is very helpful and wants to see his students succeed. I highly recommend this teacher.
He really works hard to keep the material updated and his lessons relevant. He IS strict on punctuality but so are top employers. I give him a top mark.
Went on an Exploration Seminar to Asia with Prof Reinnoldt. Five countries. Great experience. So much knowledge about Asia and business. A life-changing event!
I took his class last year and can still remember many of the details that are so helpful to my career. Best class I took
Excellente! Hard work but learn so much I did
Absolutely positively the best class and instructor on campus!

I fully agree with the previous comments. Hard work but you learn a huge amount about global buz, global affairs and the like. There isn't a topic in which he is not fluent it seems. He is indeed a stickler for being on time but so are top flight employers!

Great class. It really keeps you updated and aware of global events. Prof is very strict about showing up on time for class and after break.  Tough grader but it's a capstone class so deal with it; if you do really good work you will get full credit for assignments. Prof has high expectations of students. He is always willing to help if you need it
Great teacher and class. Helps me keep up with global events and news.  Textbook not helpful. Great stories. He could write a book
good all around experience. the homework and projects are a bit overwhelming but on balance u learn so much
Taking MBA global buz. Great material but class too short. Good lectures. Lots of practical experience. High recommendation!
Lots of work but great global experience. He really cares about his students. Great project. Best class in my education years
Best class   best teacher  best learning...on campus!

Just complted the quarter with him. Got a hard earned 4.0. yeah It's a huge amount of work but also a huge amount of learning about important topics. Some students gripe about him not being fair but those are the slackers that we all know. I would take a class from him any time and any day!

Over emphasis on attendance. He would publically point out a student?s tardiness or absence in order to make examples of this behavior. He condescends students who do or say anything outside of his way of thinking. Poor teaching skills. Good content. I would never take another class with him again!

Excellent overall academic experience.  Great teacher and class. Learned a huge amount about some interesting and complex topics.         P.S. I am quite surprised at the previous comment because WE ARE GIVEN THE EXAM QUESTIONS AHEAD OF THE FINAL so how hard can it be to study?

AWFUL professor. His slides are awful and he talks too fast to take notes. Studying for the final is very hard. The rest of the class is a lot of work and is doable but he is boring and self-absorbed.
Took Global Business (MBA) last year and my work this quarter reminds me of how much we learned.  Great insights and knowledge. Great instructor. Great class

Good class. Lot's of work. Keep good notes especially living cvases and u will do well.  Also helps to have a good group as alott of class in grp work. Beset class I have taken as info is uselful to life

Am about to finish this class and it is one of the best ever. Instructor knows so much about those areas of the world that really matter: Asia, China, Middle East.  You have to do alot of work but it is well worth every minute.

Just an overall awful class. Professor Reinnoldt picks favorites big time and has a huge bias, talking only about the countries he has experience in and travels frequently to. He treats this class as if it were the single most and only important thing on the face of the planet. I would never take a class from him again.
Just finished a quarter in this class. Great experience. A lot of work but 99% of it is very useful to one's career and lives.  Great final report but you will work for your grade!
Great class. Learned so much.  Especially relevant focus on China and India in light of global events.  Best class I have taken to date.  Be prepared to work!

Has the unique great ability to connect with students individually that is rare in education today. He truly motivates you to succeed almost as if you do not want to disappoint him because he thinks so highly of you. Best overall instructor I've ever had. Best overall class I've ever had. Listen to him, he will change your life!
Went to Thailand with him on an Exploration Seminar. Best esperience of my life.  Great teacher. Knows Asia better than anyone.  Highly recommended professor and class!
Useful, relevant topics. Incredible pace. Be prepared and you will do fine. Great learning opportunity. Every college student in America should take a class such as this

Wonderful class. We cover so much material of so much global relevance that it. seems like the lasted 6 months. Class was scary at first but later I adjusted and looked forward to attending every one. Such a smart man that speak clearly
Great teacher. Really pulls in global events to the classroom. Has professional experience that no one else at UW can match. Best class/prof I have ever taken

Went on a UW Explore Seminar to Thailand with James in August 2007. What a great experience! Knocked our socks off! He is quite demanding but at the same time we had adequate time to learn for ourselves. He is also one of the most fair teachers I have had. Expectations are clear and you are evaluated against those. Overall great experience

By far the most impressive professor I have been a student of to date. Jim's ability to not only teach but to facilitate an excellent learning experience is top notch. The golden nuggets of information and wisdom that he so tactfully shares with the class have served me well in my professional career. Don't miss out!
Took MBA Global Biz class. Great class and prof. Needs to be a longer course. So much to learn...
Great class. Best one at UW. Lotta effort but we learnt soooo much
Excellent class and prof! Amazing experience and stories. Just come prepared and you will do fine. Emphasis on comm skills. Iheard he is not coming back next fall. What a loss for UWB
Intense but interestig class. Keep good notes. Project alot of work pick good team members. he has so much experience and tells it well! Highly recommended prof!
Best course and instructor in the MBA program. No one comes close. Just be ready to work your butt off and don't slack. he has a knack for knowing who is with it and who is not
Best class and instructor I have ever taken. If you screw up you will fail-just like thereal world. Learn the lessons now.

Just completed MBA Global Biz with him. Of all of the MBA courses I have taken this was the best. He has an amazing breadth of knowlegde and can uniquely combine it with his experience in 30+ countries over20 years. GREAT Prof!
Class is over but we learned so much. Project killed us but well worth it. Great instructor. He should have won the outstanding faculty award!
No Comments

Great class and very fair. He puts a HUGE amount of effort into having a great class but also our career development. Reinnoldt's classes are among the highest rated in the UW system at 96% "Excellent Course" rating. See this on https://www.washington.edu/cec/b/BBUS480B1104.html
Good class. Tough but fair. Great stories.Either you make it or you don't-just like the real world!  Go for it!
Great professor! Never lose interest in class!
This class rocks! Great prof. Great discussions about world events. Amazing stories, Allota work but worth it. I will take a class from Prof Reinnoldt anytime!

INSTRUCTOR: Knowledgable but arrogant. Assnmt details are overwhelming.  Petty - takes points off 1 min late paper. Controlling - you can't talk; he has to call on you.  He's anal & don't believe him - he's not flexible OR open to feedback.  LECTURES: fast (hard to take notes).  QUIZZES: focus on minutia.  Req'd HANDWRITTEN-time consuming-journal.

Greatclass. Real world application. Instructor's demands area  bit excessive yet he has worked for some world-class firms so I think they are realisic. He likes to play Alex Trebeck of. Jeopardy which is amusing ... Overall a great teacher

Best teacher I have ever had. Awesome content and fantastic experience that he shares with the class.You have to work hard but you will get as much out of it as you put in. Some slacker students who can't handle it see their grades impacted-but they deserve it.

Worst teacher on campus. Unethical. All form and no content. Completely uncompromising. Missing a single detail will cost you several percentage points of your grade. Don't be absent or tardy, you will "pay the piper" as he says irrelevant of circumstance. Will isolate & humiliate individuals for minuscule things. No laptops. No eating.
This guy does not mess around. You get EXACTLY what you deserve. Immense real world experience, and he's an amazing lecturer. Read the homework and you'll love it. Awesome prof!

Strict guidelines for report formatting.  Very interesting real-world stories, however, quizzes tend to focus on minutia and trivia.  Overall, excellent instructor, but be prepared to work your butt off.

Great teacher. Extremely considerate and goes out of his way to not embarass the students if they come up short on answers. I'd take a class from him at any time. Great professional stories. His "Mulu Lulu" research simulation a real gem.

Great professor. Great practical experience and really goes out of his way to help students. Highly recommended  (the comment from the student below was made due to a poor grade; never came to class so only sour grapes. Too bad one has to resort to this).
Honestly, I have never been more disrespected and walked over in my entire college career. If you can avoid this teacher at all costs.

One of the best instructors on campus. Pay attention and come to class and you will do fine. Pay attention to the particulars of the assignments and you will avoid a lot of problems. Reinnoldt is great because he is williing to do what ever it takes to make you a success in an outside of class.

Great instructor, the best I have ever had. His projects are a pain but pretty simple, just follow the outline to the letter, presentation is everything!!! I would take any class taught by him in a heartbeat.
One of the best professors at the campus. Will give you plenty of work to keep you busy but you will appreciate what you learn at the end.

Such interesting real life stories from his work experiences. Excellant speaker and you will never be bored in one of his classes. Very valuable class that will add to your wealth of knowledge. Professor Reinnoldt pushes you to excellance knowing that each and every student is capable of producing such material. EXCELLANT PROFESSOR!!!

Unsurpassed experience outside academia. Rationalizes and subtantiates his point of view - even though we don't agree on some things, I respect his POV. (He could supress his political innuendo) One of my favorite profs. He has a genuine interest in your learning and fosters a safe environment for doing so. Keep up with the class schedule!
Awesome teacher! keep up with the work and you'll do fine!  interactive and knowledgeable!  a must take to finish your business classes off!

Reinnoldt has a lot of real-world experience. He is eager to share and you will learn a lot from his successes/mistakes. His stories and lessons can not be taught in textbooks or reading. Assignments aren't too tough. The mini assignments lead up to the final paper, allow plenty of time to do it.

absolutely hilarious teacher, i swear i was laughing in every class. extremely lenient on grading. topic and exams were hard but you gotta put in the work and youll be fine. participate and show up and youll do fine.

Lakshmana is a really kind hard working professor who uses his depth of knowledge to provide in detail explanations and his humor makes the lectures lots of fun while being mostly well focused. While participation is not mandatory it helps immensely to attend lectures as often as possible.
Wonderful professor who cared about his students learning and made accounting fun. Looked forward to this class every Monday & Wednesday night.

Super friendly, his humor made lectures fun! Homework is pretty heavy but it's a hard subject in general. Exams weigh a lot but are mostly multiple choice. Truly cares about student, good office hours and GREAT response time.
amazing prof, very reasonable, but the class still requires you to put in some work

This professor clearly has deep knowledge of the subject and a true passion for teaching. I would gladly take another class with him. He has a great balance between encouragement and challenge, always pushing students to do their best. Although the course was not the easiest for me, his support and humor made it a great experience.

Prof Lakshmana was amazing. His lectures and exercises are clear to understand and help you on the exams. He is also extremely accessible both online and in-person if you have a question. My best advice is to ask questions, answer his questions, and show up and participate. You really stand out and he remembers that. You also understand more!

Prof was fantastic. Canvas is well structured and has many outlets for learning. There are recorded lectures, in person lectures, slides, notes, solutions, and more. Really cares about his students, and is genuinely a fun professor. His passion for accounting shines through in his teaching. Finals and midterms are fair and well structured.

Problems in homework are not that based off of lecture material, more from the reading. This is important because the grades are 35% hw, 30% midterm, 35% final. The homework isn't that great for making sure you understand the material so either do the supplemental practice problems or find others because there is not much in-class work

The professor is nice, he really cares about his students and always asks if the material makes sense. The grade in the class is based off of homework, a midterm, and a final. Only downside to the class is that the there is a lot of material to study to be prepared for the tests. Go to lecture and do practice problems and you'll be alright.

The professor is nice and he really cares about his students and always asks if the material makes sense. The grade in the class is based of of homework, a midterm, and a final. Only downside to the class is that the there is a lot of material to study to be prepared for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very nice person and also cares about his students a lot. He will round grades and gives extra points on exams so it is not difficult to get a good grade in the class. His lectures are pretty hard to understand. If you can not teach yourself a concept do not take this professor. He is more a resource to answer questions than to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Moorthy is a traditional teacher, so if you are not mentally tough and disciplined you will be frustrated, this class is for real so if you have a bad grade it is absolutely your own problem. I like him because his teaching style pushed me a lot so I have had many accomplishment in this class.

He is amazing in terms of his enthusiasm and passion for Accounting. But very tough tests that are very heavily weighted with 2 tests being to 65% of the grade. Lots of info in 17 to 20 lectures depending on Quarter. To get the most out of class go over all of his handouts and additional questions. Asking questions during class is critical.

He's an okay professor and you can tell he wants good for his students but his class was just so disorganized. The lectures are absolutely terrible and are all over the place. His exams are heavy on your grade and if the lectures don't help you then you're never prepared for the exam. The HWs are just there and don't really offer any help either.

He gets a bad rep for no reason. The grade depends heavily on the 2 exams (65%) but honestly, it is similar to the practice exam and the HWs. He grades very generously and genuinely does care about students, offers many resources, and tries to make lectures fun.
Homework ok, the exams are hard, make sure to study and do not miss the class!

There are 2 exams of 5 chapters each, it is just impossible to remember the 5 chanters for taking the exams in person on paper with just one very small note allowed. Homework doesn't mater if you don't pass the exams you don't pass the class. Extremely hard class.

He tries to keep things lighthearted and fun, but if you aren't very good at accounting, he may not be the teacher for you. The structure of the class is confusing and leaves you with more questions you have in the first place. Needless to say, he made me cry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Assigns assignments on very short notice. Can not work with technology well enough. Yells and gets frustrated for things that can be easily fixed. Does not respect time of students by assigning work last notice. Teaches about technology policy but doesn't like/inadequate at using technology.

This is the worst prof I have ever taken. When you miss class, even if you're sick or excuses she doesn't let you make up the credit. She is incredibly condescending in class and will yell feedback across the room about why she doesn't like something. Very vibes based grading. No organizational skills. Not clear with instructions.
After every quiz or exam students form a line to negotiate their grades with her. Also, most of the class still hasn't been graded and we are on finals week...
The research project specs were dropped this morning 2 hrs before class. First draft is due in ~1 day. We are > 2 weeks behind. God help us.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class often felt disorganized. The instructor occasionally arrived late, which affected the flow of the lesson. In-class time was not always used effectively, and some material felt rushed or lightly covered. Students should be prepared to stay organized and keep up with course content independently.

This professor is very rude. Does not grade well and doesn't have rubrics for assignments. The midterm and quizes do not cover class content well either. Get ready to show up to class every time for attendance points and inclass points worth half your grade. She thinks she's always right. Save yourself and don't take her classes.

I took a quiz and she lost it. She said that she would send me a photo copy so I could study for the exam with it. She straight up lied and never returned it to me even after several emails. Avoid at all costs.
Please run.
Grading would often be a month or more behind

reviews.comment: I came in smarter. Assignment specs & slides miss key points, but is coherent in office hrs (most valuable time). Refuses to annotate digital submissions and dislikes digital notes.
