Lectures are absolutely awful. The vast majority of his lectures make no sense and mostly just reads off the slides. He provides no deeper explanations and even when he does it's not helpful. Assignments were miserable because he barely ever properly covers how to actually tackle most problems so you just have to figure it out yourself.

Clearly not Pisan's favorite class to teach. Lectures were mostly dull and never particularly helpful. Exams were relatively easy (especially compared to other 422 sections). Final project is mostly a guessing game of trial-and-error. Class is frustrating because it could be so much better, but instead ends up being boring and tedious.

Pisan is a very nice person? But his lectures just consist of him reading off of the textbook. So class is pretty boring, and he has participation points each class as well. I think he's a nice person, but his classes tend to be very boring and un-engaging.

Professor Pisan is knowledgeable, but sometimes he could be vague. He tries to prepare students for the technical interview. He is a tough grader and his exams are tough-- half of the points are from programming problems similar to Leetcode. I will not recommend it if you plan to get a 3.0+ GPA unless you use outside resources to study.

lectures were fine. some leetcode questions after learning topics. midterm was a good difficulty. topics learned after midterm were not very thorough and i did not enjoy them. final's difficulty compared to midterm was greater, did not like the question distribution. you only do projects and exams, no homework or any activities during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BE WRIED, THE TEST IS NOT THE CLASS LEVER LETTCODE READY FOR YOU ON THE EXAM

General advice: Practice LeetCode especially fundamental ones such as string manipulation and hashing. 
Start projects early and you will be fine. Running into errors and not knowing how to start is common, but learning how to cope with this is essential.
Ask questions, he will go into depth as long as you come up with thoughtful questions.

He have a clear guideline of what your project need to accomplish and use Github to do project. His exams are tough but he does help you prepare for it very well. Pretty much always available on discord.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The content for this class was made much more digestible because of Prof. Pisan. The class is still difficult and you're probably gonna need to study on your own time (esp if u don't have exp working with C++). However, Prof. Pisan provides plenty or resources and as long as you focus during his lectures and work outside of class, you'll do great.

Tests are weighted heavily, but you are given a one-paged note sheet on exams so you can take advantage of those if you are not confident. There is a textbook, but much of the information on it can just be found online so I wouldn't say it's required, you just have to know how to Google Search. Overall great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting class, we had a few intro projects to get used to Unity and C#, and then group project for the rest of the quarter to make a game. He also had a lot of guest speakers. The projects can be time-consuming but fun if are into art or like coding. Lectures can be boring. I wish he did more examples in class.
Challenging class with a nice professor who really cares. Lets you be creative with your code, which I like.

Straightforward yet challenging professor. Pisan allows you to work in pairs for assignments with VSCode and Git. 

Pisan introduces you to technical interview questions through leetcode exercises as a great addition

Only complaint is class material is rushed during this quarter and some ambiguity at times. Exams are difficult, so be prepared!

He gives many practice problems throughout his lectures which are very helpful. He can be confusing at times so reading the book, asking for help, and watching videos on the concepts will help you through the class. This class is not so beginner-friendly, so if you have no experience you might have a hard time at first. Overall a good professor.

As someone who is just learning how to program, I had a pretty hard time in his class. It's very book-heavy, so if reading for long hours is tough for you, you might want to rethink taking this class with him. Not very much teaching happens during lectures, mainly review from the tb. He is a harsh grader. I struggled a lot and was often lost:(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If he has lecture slides posted beforehand, it helps to look at them before he teaches the topic. Tough test grader but if you do the practice problems in class with him, the problems are quite similar. If you are stuck, ASK HIM FOR HELP. He will always guide you to a clever solution. Chill class, I grew to like his teaching as the quarter went on

Honestly, he is a good professor, just know that you need some knowledge of the course before you come to this class or you WILL have a hard time. Also, if you are new to programming read the book cause it is really helpful. If you do what Professor Pisan says you will do well in this class. Just put in the work and your good. Do Extra Credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Has all the attributes you want in a professor: - He knows what he's teaching - He knows how to teach it - He cares about his students - Very Friendly Easily accessible outside of class, has no trouble with emails, and has an active discord where you can reach out to him, the TA, or your peers. His PPs are accessible in Canvas for easy reviews

He has a class discord which is really nice for students to ask questions. I really wanted to give him a 5, but he screwed our section over in the end. The other 343 section got an optional final, while our final was heavy on stuff that we barely covered at the end (discrete math). Course evals also ended way before the final which is sketchy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I've really enjoyed professor Pisan. He doesn't assign work that isn't helpful. I had a good bit of coding experience prior but not in low level languages like C, and I feel like Pisan really rounded me out and made me feel like a competent programmer. Also just an overall good dude. I look forward to taking DS&A with him.

Professor Pisan is by far the worst instructor I have had. The homework assignments take the entire 2 weeks to complete (and don't count for much of grade). Your final grade is based on exams. In addition to being difficult, confusingly worded (he doesn't answer questions), they cover topics that were barely covered. The study guides are a joke.

If you need help? If you have problems with this professor? Talk. To. Him. He will listen to you! He cares a lot! He changes his curriculum based on feedback! We're so lucky to have a professor who does this. I took CSS 342 with him. I did not get a 4.0. Didn't even care because that's not important if you want to get a job, and I learned a lot.

Take this course if you want a solid foundation in CS taught by a caring teacher. If you engage, there is nothing he will not do to help you succeed. I have taken 4 of his classes and researched with him for 3 quarters. He updates his syllabus when I give feedback, maintains a wiki of CS info, and all his course evaluations are on his website.

If you want nothing except an easy A, dont take him. if you work hard and want a solid understanding in data structure and algo and C++, take him. He cares about students and will try to make complex topics easier for them. Solving leetcode problems in class is a plus. Highly recommend taking 342 and 343 with him. Be ready to read and work hard.

I had Professor Pisan for CSS 343 and CSS 342. I will say if you are looking for an easy A with no effort, you will struggle in his class a lot. However, if you are a dedicated student to pursuing an education in formal Computer Science, you will really love his classes and your hard work will pay off. One of the best teachers I have ever had.

During internship I had a few challenges. Professor Pisan was very quick to respond to my questions, make time to meet in person and offer sound advice to navigate the situation. In preparation for doing capstone presentations he gathered all the students for a practice run and give constructive feedback on slide deck. Excellent for capstone.

Professor Pisan is the reason I have such a solid understanding of data structures & algorithms. I found his lectures to be very engaging and insightful - it is clear he has had a lot of experience teaching and is very in-tune with his students' level of understanding. The in-class activities really helped solidify my understanding of the concepts.
He cares about students' success a lot. The class material is definitely hard, but he tries a lot of ways to make it easier to comprehend. His help outside of class hours is amazing.

Organized relative to other professors, but assigns a lot of work. Quarter-long group project based on a Unity game, but hard to finish if never used Unity before and only 10 weeks. Often gives unclear instructions or makes mistakes regarding assignments, and is unresponsive until the next class after when it is due. Can be mean sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Make sure you ask the professor what gonna be included in the final or you gonna fail this course.

Class is difficult so make sure you stay on top especially the first half. Pisan is a really good teacher and his informative lectures are great. He will go out of his way to answer every question. There are 5 assignments in 10 weeks. Be sure to start early. Tests(55% of grade) are harder than the classwork and practice midterms and finals.

Super nice guy, but did not teach Operating Systems very well. Heavily relied on outdated slides from the textbook which at times were out of order, had vague, conflicting, or even MISSING information. Reading the textbook was a pain as the author would go off on tangents for several pages at a time. Prepare to heavily use StackOverFlow/YouTube.

Pisan is a very kind and caring professor. He goes out of his way to help students and treats any questions asked in class respectfully. He is happy to go over any topics where students are confused. He grades the exams with more scrutiny than the assignments, so be sure to triple-check your exams. The exams are similar to sample exams.

* Lots of class exercises, make sure write them all in your note (it will help you get better grade on midterm and finals) * Attendance is not mandatory but highly recommend you to go class due to class exercise. * Of course no extra credit lol * I personally do not think he is a tough grader, he is actually generous. * Had Fun

Great professor IMO. Had him for CSS 342 and CSS 343. I found 343 to be easier than 342. The class is very test heavy, about 55% of your grade I believe. Provides test guides before each exam and goes over any questions in class. Lots of in class examples for 343 which were similar to questions on the test. Accent takes a little getting used to.

He's an awesome dude, and really cares about what he's teaching, not super great with feedback on the assignments and sometimes expects you to know material that he hasn't taught yet. Grade is extremely test heavy and the tests are way harder than the assignments. This class was time consuming and his lecture's weren't always helpful.

Quiz takes up 20% of the whole grade. It is a game development class and half of the quiz are on history of games. Watch Youtube tutorials on Unity; it is where youll learn the most out of this class. Read the book to find out why past game developers are important and what are their contribution, and the rest you can get from the lecture slides.

Very good professor overall. Lectures are clear and he explains most of them while walking through examples on the board. Midterm wasn't the easiest but it was fair. 2 weeks per homework with most of them only taking 3-4 days(10-15 hours) a lot of the people complaining started on the last couple days. Practice tests actually mirrored real tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For those saying he's hard, are you kidding me? He's an easy 4.0. For most assignments, he sets everything up for you so that you only have to write the algorithms. I'd say you should have learned at least half of the material already from previous CS classes. Final exam took 40 minutes to finish.

Lots of HW with limited time even if you get started right away. Tests seem easy but meh not really close to easy to ace. The whole class uses slack to communicate. The grader for sort of helps with the questions on HW on the day its due. Both grader and professor disappear before hw due and test days so no questions will get official answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. He has very neat slides and goes over practice problems in class. Grading is very clear, especially relative to other professors at UWB. Good HW specs and tests didn't seem too hard to me. HW took time, but wasn't too hard. Definitely go to lectures. I didn't have to do much studying outside of class. Not the easiest but still solid.
10/10 would take again

Professor Pisan is very caring and he gives good lectures that are directly related to the assignments. He also does class exercises that are VERY helpful. He only has a few assignments that aren't hard but are time-consuming. He grades fair on assignments, but he's a tough grader on tests. Fortunately, he curves. Overall he's a great instructor!
Homework not like the tests. Office hours are not good. Class average for midterms is 60%. Harsh grader. Failed a lot of people. No material to prepare for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach well. He assumes that everyone in the class is in the same pace or level of knowledge, thus this class will favor those who likes programming or majoring in CS. And most importantly, the weekly homework are tough as hell. Exams aren't that tough as the HW, but points are easily deducted because he is a strict and tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the worst grading scales I've ever seen in my entire academic career. Unless you are deeply interested in paleontology, a lot of the material is a nightmare to go through. Micromanages a ton of the work done and will nitpick the smallest details. Nice person, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not a bad class, had its moments but I learned a lot.

Work is difficult, especially considering it's a required course for a major that has nothing to do with the subject. Grading is extremely picky, grading guidelines un-clear, and grading scheme for the course is complicated and makes the course more difficult. Don't pick this course with this prof!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class can get tough, and her course starts off difficult, but you get many chances to redo your work to which she grades for full credit. Honestly a very sweet professor. If you need help, she will do everything she can to help you succeed; you just have to put in the effort!

I'm surprised to see that she is rated so low. Although the coursework is challenging, she encourages office hours (please just go to them, they're helpful), and she is very lenient on us catching up on missing/late/ incomplete assignments. She just wants us all to learn, rather than being a stickler about late work & I appreciate that a lot.

She makes us read assignments with over 70+ pages, and expects us to annotate all of it from start to finish. And the annotations have to actually be to her standard, so short sentences will not do. Not to mention, we have multiple of these assignments all in one week. I also did not enjoy that she talked to us like we were little kids.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was overbearing and treated me like a child. She was over the top on sensitivity, like we do not live in the real world. I did not learn one thing within the first two weeks, not to mention any assignment we did did not correlate with anything in class.

Although this was probably one of the hardest classes I've taken, Dr. Price was one of the best professors I've ever had. I didn't get a perfect grade in this class but I learned so much and was able to successfully write a research paper! Dr. Price spends a lot of time meeting with her students to help us retain info and ensure we've understood it

reviews.comment: good professor, super hard grader

reviews.comment: Class felt kinda pointless and business centric group projects for almost every homework assignment. Professor was nice but didn't really feel like he was prepared for a group project class, doesn't enforce or provide much support for group members who don't participate or issues with groups. Overall very nice but not a good prof for group work!
Get a good group and you will love this class. It was fairly easy and the professor makes lectures fun and engaging. Hes also very communicative and knowledgeable which helps a lot

Lots of assignments felt like busy work. Randomly selected group projects with a lot of assignments feeling 75% similar to the last one. Lots of assignments require 2 pages of writing. The quizzes are online and outside of class time, not too bad. So many random busy work assignments though.
One of the best professors I've had at UWB. Very easy to communicate with, and his class is really engaging. Would definitely recommend. Oh, and he gives free snacks

I took CSS350 with him not CSS110. Proffesor Pyle was hands down my best professor, he truly cared for student success and this class was super easy. Online quizzes no midterms or finals and best of all, he brought amazing fun snacks for us everyday. 10/10 oh and great lectures

Quizzes every week based on readings, super easy and usually knew by memory. Doug is really nice, chill, and easy to work with, had an extensive background with big tech companies. Mid-term was closed note and was the one that stumped most. Studying extra hard for the midterm payed off, but the average was low result in an open note online final.

His class had weekly open-note quizzes and biweekly homework, which was easy with high averages. The professor seemed decently knowledgeable about Cybersecurity but was often caught off guard by questions. However, the one midterm stumped the majority of the class, and the class didn't adequately prepare students for it resulting in an online final

Open-note weekly quizzes, but the midterm was closed-note and difficult, with the class average at 80% after a 15% curve. Due to poor grades, the final exam was made multiple choice and open-note. The grading scheme starts at a 4.0 for 97% and decrements by percentage from there. Pyle is a chill guy, but his class was a death trap. Beware.

reviews.comment: This professor was just not my style! i would recommend taking other professor!

reviews.comment: GPA TANKER: If you have to take this class, save yourself and wait for a different professor. 1 chapter a class and exams every 4, and exams are stressful (50 questions, no going back). Homework is the only practice you'll get, not helpful.Grading is strict with no partial credit, and he makes sure you know that earning a high grade is impossible.

Please don't take this professor he don't know how to teach this class 
He don't give anyone good credit if missed the assignment you will receive 
-50 of credit a lot of requirements for group projects you have to email him on weekends if you have your assignments on Monday he is so boring
Absolute boss 10/10 would take again

Rob engages in scare tactics, but is really a big softie. He would remind us again and again that his exams were difficult and that he graded presentations harshly, but the class avg on exams was over 70% and my group got an A on the presentation when we really shouldn't have. If you study hard and make good note sheets, you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! Learned a lot from him. He makes it very clear that the class is intense and requires efforts. But if you put in enough time and efforts, you will learn a lot from him. In his lectures, he highlights what you need to know for the exams, so class attendance is recommended.

If you wanna study and really know about finance take this class. He is clear that you gotta put in the effort. Your GPA is dropping after this class most likely but if you grind alot you can succeed. he doesnt really go though alot of numericals in class he just lectures alot but his tricks for using the financial calculator make life easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
His coursework is straightforward forward and all the exam answers are multiple choice so you have a 25% chance of getting the correct answer per question. 

My only advice is to not let his scare tactics negatively affect your test anxiety. He will put pressure on you to drop the class. He is easygoing once you decide not to drop his class.

453 + 454: Best professor I've had throughout my years in college. Very caring guy with a lot of knowledge in the subject as he works in the industry of finance. Test heavy classes. Do the homework for free points, make a good note sheet for tests, read textbook and come to class.

The amount of times he says "This will be on the exam" to only then speed through lecture slides for an hour is extremely infuriating. In addition to that, he expects you to read the textbook front to back in prep for exams when he could obviously explain the material himself. Honestly, he ruined my overall morale for my remaining quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Rob is great. Success in his class is predicated on effective time management skills and reading the textbook. Study for the exams and put in the effort, you’ll be fine. He’s very organized. I got a 3.9, work a full time job plus a part time job, had 3 other classes. Rob’s class was hard but not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do not recommend. Take someone else. Okay personality, terrible professor.

Exams are extremely difficult, all multiple choice. Treats class like we are all finance majors when in reality it's just a core class for business in general. Goes through lecture slides fast and gets off topic talking about his own clients. Not aware of pandemic. Midterm averages were 60-70%....
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst business professor at UW. This class is self-taught, he goes through lecture like we are PhD students. Exams are extremely hard. The main issue is that he has no empathy for people who have other things going on in life (even during a pandemic). No late work accepted and expects you to read every page of the book for a FINANCE class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I think he does teaching as a side gig as his main job is a finance advisor. This class is all self taught as he goes through lectures fast and unclear, expect 10+ hours a week of outside learning because you literally have to read the book page by page to understand concepts. He admits his class is hard but fair, in my opinion it's time consuming

Got 4.0s in 3 of Rob's classes (350, 451, 454). He is a smart, caring man who does his best to make sure everyone understands the material. His test aren't easy but they never have any curveballs, and are extremely similar to practice exams he provides. The homework is free points. If you pay attention and read the book, you can expect a 3.7+.

Professor Wright is one of the best professors Ive ever taken. He goes out of his way to make sure whether or not students find his methods affective and responds to it. Everything is easy EXCEPT for exams. Reading the textbook carefully and comprehending material will help you with exam prep. Its not an easy A, but Robs class is worth it.

Rob is awesome but his class is so hard. His exams are way hard. His lectures and homework don't help. I guess you need to be too good in finance to take his class or do well in exams. I study really hard for his exams but I do bad. Even though I'm an A student in other classes. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor.

He is a caring, respectable professor. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students' success. He met with many students outside of class and was there to give career advice and feedback. He is extremely clear with grading, and there are zero surprises when it comes to tests. He is a solid choice and will help you with career advice! Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor. But be ready to put in work. A lot of material is textbook heavy. He goes through slides very quickly. But, if you don't understand material either send him an email or meet him during office hours. Exams are slightly difficult but he gives practice ones that are very similar. So there are no surprises to that.

Robs extremely dedicated to the success of his students, and goes above and beyond. If students dont comprehend something, he is extremely approachable and responsive. He provides all resources to make sure you do well on his exams. Your grade is really a reflection of the effort you put into the material. Very responsive and approachable!

Rob doesn't thoroughly explain problems on the slides. I saw this class as a self-taught course. He goes over the concepts very rapidly making it had to grasp his lectures. Nice guy but hard to follow

Lectures are extremely dry and the concepts presented are not really clear. All the tests are multiple choice but they are not easy. Tip: Read the book page by page and try to memorize the concepts with your best ability.

Rob is a likable person. Half of your grade is based on 3 tests, and they are VERY VERY HARD. Attend class everyday, take tons of notes, watch all of the Pearsons Finance video lectures, do all of the homework twice, study like mad and you might pass.

Best teacher I have had so far. Rob really cares about the success of students and presents himself as a resource only for help with the course, but with letters of recommendation and connecting students with jobs/internships. The class is one of the most difficult I've taken, is lecture heavy but he makes a great effort to make things interesting

Rob is hard but he's smart. If you really want to learn finance and know what you're doing - take this man's class. If you want an easier grade, take someone else's class. His lectures are him going over slides, its your job to actively watch and listen and learn his techniques by watching him do them. Tests are extremely time crunched.
Doesn't do a good job explaining the material nor does he give you enough time to do them. Assigned over 50 questions on exam day which you need to read the book to answer, I DO NOT RECOMMEND!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Rob for two classes and he was great in both of them. He was always accessible and easy to get in contact. His lectures were always very focused and understandable and he was a fair grader. Rob was easy to talk to and get along with and I can say personally he cares about his students and helps them even after finishing his classes.
Really nice guy but he doesn't know how to teach the material. Lectures consist of powerpoint slides with brief unclear explanations. Can be a stickler.

Best professor I've ever had in college. Has high expectations of students and of himself as a professor. Cares a lot about students succeeding and genuinely listens to feedback and implements it as fairly as possible. Great personality and has a lot of experience in Finance making lectures very entertaining. Definitely a must-have professor!

A great professor. It was a demanding class, but not ridiculous, being a 400 level course at this university. He is well rouned, has a great personality, and good teaching style. I greatly enjoyed his class, I would definitely take another from him. Offers good advice and real examples, the type of professor to stay in contact with.

Rob is a really great professor. He takes the time to make sure that his students understand what is being taught. He helps you with the homework, and will do some extra problems in class. I really recommend taking Rob's class. He also is a great mentor, and will be there for you even after you have completed the quarter. 11/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Rob was by far one of the best professors I had at UWB. He takes the time to make course content relevant and interesting which made going to class a joy. I would suggest doing all reading and course work completed before class to have meaningful coversations. I would highly recommend Rob as a professor and taking classes with him.

Professor Wright is the best Professor you can ever take at the University of Washington. He goes belong his job as a teacher. If you have any questions about class work/life/career paths, he will take the time out of his day to give you the best response/advice as possible. In ways he is more of a long term friend and life time mentor.

Although this was one of the more difficult classes I've taken, Rob was BY FAR one of the best professors I've ever taken! He is very clear about his expectations, willing to meet with you outside of class & genuinely cares about his students. Rob is super quick in terms of e-mailing back and posting grades. If you want to actually learn, take Rob!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really amazing teacher super nice guy and really really cares about his students. He gives you hints on the homework but, that doesn't mean you don't have to study they are on the exams. The only reason that I got an A in the class was because I read all the material and studied hard. Make sure you participate.

Professor Wright was one of the best professors I've ever had. He has a lot of knowledge about the topic of this class and definitely knew how to communicate it over to the students. His class wasn't easy, the topic of Financial Planning & Policy is pretty dense, but Professor Wright made it more bearable by always offering help if you needed it!
put it on wallahi bro say wallahi

Not the professor's fault, although structure of class was extremely poor. Grading criteria was extremely confusing, each assignment had 3+ grading rubrics-expectations not at all clear. Attendance is only mandatory for half the quarter. Lectures not at all relevant to course content, professor often went on tangents in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the best professor I've ever had, I always enjoy coming to class every week! Dr. Zak makes the most out of the curriculum while giving us a valuable learning experience. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She also gives out free energy drinks, and is easy to talk to if you need help or an extension.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Don't penalize them for a poorly structured course (it's BAD, but they didn't design it). IMO they made the most of a bad situation as a new prof. Extremely accessible outside of class and has a lot of really valuable industry experience they're willing to share. Precise but fair. What some describe as rudeness I just took as them being direct.

Nah. Very poor class design made by a different prof, and Zak clearly had no interest in the class itself. Often went on tangents and grading was wildly inconsistent. Snarky remarks to questions and was kind of rude. Lectures weren't *that* relevant to the work. You will leave this class with character development.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Zak was a fantastic teacher can be a bit tough but as long as you follow the material, she's fairly reasonable. Overall class wasn't bad and I would take again.

Pretty rude lowkey. Not going to place blame for the class structure because Rubin didn't design it, but I don't think Rubin even understood what they were supposed to be teaching or what was expected. Main issue was that the the grading criteria was unclear and rather than clarifying, Rubin only redirected.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The professor is unclear as the rubric and instructions consistently contradicted each other, and when asked for clarification, you're met with VERY RUDE responses. The only positive is that they review a couple of questions on the actual exam during class beforehand, + the questions on the final exam were very easy (more reflective than testing).

STAY AWAY. Course is poorly designed by another prof and all profs blindly follow it. Instructions, book, and rubric contradict each other. Grading is inconsistent. Questions are dismissed instead of clarified. Lectures go off track and don't help in class, though she shares valuable professional experience. Very hostile learning environment.

Her class was fun and super easy! However, I do think she could spice up her lectures to make them entertaining, but it was prob the easiest class I've taken, so I can't complain. Otherwise, all the information in the class is very eye-opening. Def take her classes!

She was a very kind professor and gives a clear guideline of what to expect for the quarter. There is a lot of reading and weekly quizzes but it's not a lot and pretty easy since it was online quizzes and you can use your notes. The lectures every week though felt boring as it feels like she repeats what we read in our textbook (Homework Notes).

This is the second class I've taken with Professor Richards and she is lovely. Super easy grader and assignment load. We had chapter readings that go along with the weekly homework assigment and weekly quizzes. Attendance is needed if you want full credit for the in-class assignments. She emails back quickly and is very sweet! I highly recommned!

Easiest grader ever, no final (just weekly 8-question quizzes). Provides free textbook, very textbook reading heavy homework but overall not too bad. Lectures are a bit repetitive to what we read in the textbook but interactive activities every lecture. Super understanding, allows late work. So so sweet. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor seemed pretty knowledgable on the subject, but not how to teach. He was not great at interacting with the students, answering the questions, or helping you if you fell behind. I'd highly recommend a different professor.
Professor does an alright job of teaching the material, but it is quite obvious that it is his first time as a lecturer. Class could have been better organized.

Look, I agree that this class was not organized and maybe could have been handled better, but if you take Professor Rajanna, you will be met with someone who genuinely cares about you as a student, is always offering extensions, goes out of their way to make sure you learn (but you need to go out of your way and ask for help), etc. Loved CSS478.

Madhu is a pretty chill guy. If you go to his lectures, he does try to make students participate as he tries to make it interactive. The more people participate, it actually gets the ball rolling and he teaches really well. He's pretty nice and enthusiastic about teaching. If you show him enthusiasm and participate, the class is actually p fun.

This class probably shouldn't be offered in its current manner. It's about a week or two's worth of content stretched out over 10 weeks. Professor is nice and he does a good job of explaining things. Quizzes and exams are embarrassingly easy and the class is so easy it makes you feel bad for taking it. Course Canvas is badly set-up, though.

Tough grader and very disorganized. Terrible at teaching and extremely hard to understand. Gives tons of homework but takes forever to grade and gives no feedback. Save yourself a bad grade and choose a different prof.

This was Professor Rajanna first time teaching BIMD233, and yes it was obvious but he was always willing to help and answer questions if needed. The grading did take forever, but that was more on his grader. As long as you attend the lectures and ask questions!! you will succeed in this course.

Fair grader, a lot of assignments, but he is very understanding towards students and is willing to move deadline dates if circumstances call for it. Overall, a flexible professor. You just need to try in this class to get a decent grade.

Although the course starts with a LOT of individual work and assignments may be a little vague. He was easily reachable and understood his student's frustrations. The final Project and Report was also straightforward and fairly graded. He has in-class exercises/quizzes that help you understand the material a lot better as well.

Don't! Just don't take his class. Lectures are boring, heavy workload, hard grader, very unorganized (you don't know what assignments need to be submitted), he doesn't give feedback on assignments, and he takes so long to grade past assignments. Exams are easy though. The class structure was hard to follow. Just don't take his class.

Genuinely the best CSS lecturer ever! The way he lectures while doing code alongs makes the most difficult concepts easy to understand and remember. I wish he taught more classes so I could take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very practical professor who integrates Discord and GitHub, so you end up building your portfolio while doing classwork. The structure is clear and easy to follow, and the exam comes straight from lectures. He genuinely cares, and if you reach out he'll go out of his way to help. By far my favorite STEM class.

If you see him as the instructor for a class, sign up asap!!! Run do not walk!!! Seriously the best prof ever! You can tell he really cares about students and he wants to set us up for success, and he has great lectures that are fun (as fun as coding can be!)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Peng Dug is really the GOAT, everything taught in lecture actually coincides with homework, great extra credit opportunities, you are taught a lot of useful information that applies to a career in CS. Professor also pays good attention to the class and notices if the class needs more time with homework, very understanding and fair.

Easily the best CS prof! Teaches practical skills you will actually use. Is extremely accessible outside of class on discord and hosts study sessions in person on Sundays. His lectures are easy to follow and he's really generous with extra credit. Everything on the exams are on the study guide so just study that and you'll get an A.

Peng Du is the best professor Ive had at this school! Very caring and helpful and wants to see students succeed the class is mostly over discord but that is amazing as he responds super quick and is always happy to answer questions 10/10 professor will take classes again!

AMAZING professor. This was my first time taking summer classes and I only did it so I could take Peng for CSS 143 because I have heard from other students how he gives very good lectures and is a great professor. They were all right. He is so understanding and amazing at his job. I heavily recommend taking him if you can. Lots of Extra credit!!

TL;DR: Prof. Peng is fantastic. Just go to class, code along, and you'll be fine. As a business major, I didn't expect to get so much out of a CS course. Beyond Java, I learned real interview tips, practiced Git commands, and learned how to write solid code. He's easy to reach &always open to chat, which made the class both practical and enjoyable.

Professor Du is the best CS professor ever!! Whatever class he's teaching that quarter, take it. His lectures and code alongs are engaging, homework and exams are reasonable, and he's always available to help you on discord even if it's late. He makes difficult concepts simple to understand. Seriously do not hesitate to take him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Beware of his rude and disrespectful responses to students on Discord, made me and others afraid to ask questions, demeanor is inappropriate. Notifies about quizzes the day of, making it difficult for students who have evening classes. Changes his mind constantly/last minute.Take him if you don't care about your tuition and want to teach yourself.

reviews.comment: Ignore the guy that gave Peng a 1.0. I think I know who he is and he was a bad student. Peng isn't perfect but he gets close to it. His tests are hard and weighted heavily like all coding classes. Studying for them is easy, he records his lectures and bases his tests off his lectures.

reviews.comment: He barely taught, he showed us videos of cars and pictures of cats most of the time and had us do a quiz on improv. He was disrespectful to students in the Discord and would never answer questions. He would always say "ask ChatGPT." He assigned things late and wouldn't give extra time and changed his mind on the lessons last minute. Do not take.

reviews.comment: The best and most chill professor at UWB by far, would recommend taking one of his classes (even if you don't need it).

He's the goat, even though the final is take home now, he allows a cheatsheet and the problems are really similar to the midterm and the final study guide so as long as you review that stuff, you will do good. So much extra credit opportunities and lectures are recorded so you don't have to show up. Take him if you can!

He's great, but I think this quarter he's started to bump up the difficulty for his classes. His midterm and final are now in person handwritten, and he has pop quizzes in class almost every week. My friends who have taken him before had said that he has never done that. So, I think he's trying something new. Just needs a study guide for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Oh yeah, he's just a chill dude.
Amazing, would enjoy taking more classes with him!

Best professor I've ever had. I was stuck on a bug and Professor Peng stayed on a Zoom call with me until 11 PM to help me understand where my implementation was going wrong. I don't know any other professor who goes to that length to support their students. Truly the GOAT—genuinely caring and dedicated.
If you can get his class take it over any other prof. Peng du is the CS goat
Hes the goat

MUST TAKE. I absolutely loved this teaching style, he worries less about grades and more on students growth. He does allow ChatGPT use which can be good and bad but if used in intentional places great course. Lot of extra credit oppurunity, post finals grade I had an 101.35%
Best CSSE professor at UWB by far

There is so much I can say about Professor Du.  He once met me at 10:30 pm to work on a problem with me.  His coding assigments are applicable outside of class.  He also exposes you to tools like git and AWs and linux during class.  He applies lecture to real life concepts and interview questions.  He is the most dedicated professor I have met.

Professor Peng has to be one of the best professors at uwb especially within the CSSE department, he uses practical examples and simplifies content which caters to each students learning. He is also active on discord even at 12am which makes contacting him super easy. His grading policy is niceas he wants students to learn and worry less on grades.
Literally the best professor I've ever taken. Literally took a summer quarter just to be in his class. 100/10, wish he taught every class. Super helpful and knowledgable.

6/5, great lecture slides which are not dull and static. Code walkthroughs and many demos for understanding. quizzes are built off of demos to really set that understanding. Insane amount of extra credit. Loves rallying and photography with a cool background in tech. Wish he just taught everything tbh

Professor Peng Du is one of the best CS professors at UWB. I would highly suggest signing up for his class early because his classes fill up quick. I took him for CSS 143. His class is not too hard, but some assignments might be tough. If you took CSS 142 at UWB, this class will certainly be a lot easier for you if you take his section.

I love this man! He is always willing to help, very accessible over discord at basically anytime (along with the grader). The homework is difficult but he gives plenty of time to complete and is always willing to help if you have any questions.

Amazing CS professor. Will clearly explain a topic to you and makes sure you understand it. Very accessible over Discord and will get back to you as soon as he can. Exams are online, only rule is don't collaborate with other students. Final project is in groups. Homeworks are hard, but he has tests which tell you exactly what he wants. Take him.

Professor Du is truly a very good teacher, and I'd recommend anyone to take him. Not only does he teach in engaging ways, but he streamlines everything. He uses code repos on github and does an initial autograde with an AI made by him. He has an AI bot for questions about the class and makes communication very easy with him, and graders on Discord.
He's the goat teacher at UWB good luck if you can get into one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Excellent professor! The most accessible professor outside of class that I've ever had. He helped me over Zoom after a nightshift around midnight! He's the GOAT! Very understanding about attendance. All lectures were on Zoom and recorded but going in person is encouraged. Plenty of time and available help for assignments. He also allows teammates.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Du's lectures give you hope for the future in CS, not only does he teach well he also makes an effort to explain it through real-life examples(Which is usually missing in other classes). He is always available outside class and is ready to help us through any means necessary. Seriously, I would close my eyes and blindly take his class.
Seriously enjoying this professor. Really wish I could take him for CSS 342! His explanations are extremely clear and helpful. Really wish more professors taught like him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best Professor/Educator/Mentor I have ever had! His lectures go very in depth on topics and utilize plenty of metaphors and examples to explain these topics in a very tasteful fashion. Class has a textbook but you can get away without it just because of how good his lectures are. 50% of final is group project i wish i could write more BEST PROF EVR

Doubt there's a class more student-friendly than his. It can be hard for some, but he does a lot to make the student experience great. Lectures are filled with helpful demos, and are accessible to watch on zoom or recorded for later. He provides plenty of extra cred opportunities, & is super accessible on discord . If you can take his class, do it.

Professor Peng Du is very good at demonstrating concepts to students being introduced to java. He is also very accommodating for his students and is easily accessible outside of class. If possible I for sure would take him again in the future.

Professor Peng Du is really good at explaining concepts to people who are having their first experience with java. He's also very accommodating as well as accessible outside of class. Will for sure take him again in the future if he is available.

Peng is a great teacher who is both very knowledgeable and able to understand the perspectives of students who are learning material for the first time. It is very easy to not do much work in his class and still get a good grade, but if you attempt to understand the code he presents and pay attention to the lecture, you will learn a lot!

Uses lots of analogies to help explain topics and offers a ton of extra credit. He's also extremely accessible outside of class through discord. Lectures are recorded so you don't have to worry about missing anything. Uses Git and GitHub for homework rather than canvas. If you don't understand version control, you will after taking him.

Best communication with professor and classmates through Discord! Professor Du is always available to help and often hosts office hours. Homework is in bulk, every 1-2 weeks. Group work is optional, mostly to make your life easier. Lectures are available online if you missed attending in person (be sure to watch the material). Lots of extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Out of every single prof I've taken, he's really fun to be in class with. We use github, intellij, and discord to run the course. He tries to make his lectures relatable in a way that makes the concept easier to learn. If his course is on the waitlist, be on that waitlist. He really is a great professor.
Take whatever class Peng Du is offering, he will make your life and your college career so much easier.
Easy
You will never regret taking his class. Amazing teacher!
He has a great teaching style with relevant topics and very clear grading criteria. The best part, he is always available outside of class to help.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Du is an amazing instructor. He is overflowing with knowledge, and knows the best ways to not just tell people the answers, but allow them to learn it for themselves. He is extremely personable and friendly and his lectures are incredibly informative. Would take his class again in a heartbeat.

We need more professors like Prof.Du at UWB. For every lectures I learned something important/practical/applicable irl every 15ish minutes. He uses GitHub instead of canvas (if you don't know git, take him), extremely well organized, responsive, genuinely a good person who cares about his students, and a cool guy. He does car racing on the side!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Peng Du was a fantastic introduction to the major for CSS 342. The programs themselves weren't too difficult, but they weren't easy either. Online solutions helped supplement some of the more difficult parts of class, and Professor Peng allowed them as long as sources were cited, which was a big help. Very accessible through Discord.

The assignments are pretty hard starting from week 3, but you can find most of the code online. You can receive full credit as long as you cite the solution. You learn a lot of very practical algorithms. He is very accessible via discord. A lot of extra credits in assignments and tests. Easy A as long as you do all the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: genuinely one of the best classes i've taken at UWB. i took bismcs 333 and genuinely felt like i learned something. YAY seriously in my professor hall of fame. quarter long group project and weekly small group meetings, no quizzes but weekly assignments (250 word application of concepts, really easy if you did readings or paid attention in class)

Mr. Krabill is a great teacher. He is very engaging and cares about us as students. The coursework is light just some readings and discussion post. One group project and essay at the end of the quarter. Very chill but still very informative!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Grading was completely subjective, do not take if you don't have to. (If you care about your GPA).

BISMCS33. Ron Krabill was honestly the first professor at UW Bothell that I have ever really liked. He was caring for his students and the class was discussion based which typically I hate but I found myself wanting to participate each time. If I was not graduating I would be taking Ron for any course possible!!!

From what I've heard of other professors for this class, Ron is one of the better ones. I liked 300 with him, but wasn't the biggest fan of the way he graded group work or writing. He was, however, always clear on what he wanted from assignments and assigned fair work. Very nice man and I'd love to take another class with him with better structure.

Great instructor, does a good job of introducing difficult topics and sets the stage for his class to not only take part but lead the class room discussions. Is a bit of a tough grader but that is because he wants to see that information is being digested and processed and not just memorized. He gives students support and am personally thankful.

Prof Krabill was such a great guy to talk to and his lectures really opened up my perspective on specific social issues. Always willing to make time for students and is understanding. All group discussions during class about the readings. Tough grader, really challenges you to think outside the box and to fully read the text. Participation matters!

The class was about human rights issues; on average 30 pages of reading were assigned weekly. You will most likely meet a bunch of cynical Democrats who care nothing but "social justices" regardless of the reality. Cynicism caused by the media was never addressed in the class. Accusations without valid clues were made constantly.

Krabill actually cares about the subjects he is teaching, especially with media and human rights with the class that I took. He is relatively easy for a level 3 interdisciplinary course, but the work load still wasn't the easiest I've had. Mostly class discussion is required for daily credit, but also a big group project in place of the final.

He was an amazing professor, really connected with the class, and was very accepting of everyone. Never once did I feel like my opinion was invalidated in the class. The atmosphere he created motivated me to engage in class despite being introverted and having anxiety when speaking in a class. I would definitely recommend taking him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ron is very passionate about teaching and his subject. Very easy to listen to and talk to. Lenient on deadlines. Very interesting and engaging class, as hard as it is it's easy to succeed if you're interested. Honestly one of the best classes I've taken at UWB.

He's really sweet and does want students to succeed. There are weekly readings and in class assignments, so as long as you participate in the discussions, your grade will be fine. The final is also a group project and paper, so make sure you prepare ahead because he only gives the groups 3-4 times to work in class.

Professor Krabill is one of the best scholars at UWB. He is clear within his instructions for assignments and cares about how much EVERY student learns and succeeds in his course. With all that being said, his class has a lot of work for you to do and you better not fall behind otherwise...

He's a nice guy but you will have to work for your grade. Engaging lectures and a TON of resources available to you. Participation matters and there's lots of writing and projects to be done. Feedback on assignments is timely (often early) and EXCELLENT. Great intro to IAS resources in general too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. Genuinely cares about students and wants everyone to succeed as much as they can. His senior seminar was difficult but rewarding because I was able to find new academic interests this late in my degree (AES) and he helped me apply to law school/UWB MACS/UW MPA.
Awesome professor. Gives great feedback, appreciates students and they appreciate/respect him, and loves working with everyone. I highly recommend.

Idk what the previous rating is all about. I'm in BIS 313 right now and I have to say, it's super quality. Maybe some don't like the structure because he doesn't do much lecturing. We have readings, discussions, and lots of interaction/ participation. I love it. He's brilliant, extremely knowledgable, and genuinely cares about people.
Not a good professor. Learning is nonexistent and the guy doesnt appear to know what he is talking about. Unclear how he got a job teaching. Regret taking course.

One of the best professors I've ever had. A true educator. Brilliant, unpretentious, and caring. Make an effort to engage with the work and there is no reason not to do well, but he will challenge you to do your best work.

Professor Krabill is by far the best teacher I have ever had. He cares about his students and encourages participation. He provides a safe space for thoughtful discussion. His class was intellectually stimulating and if you have the opportunity, take any class you can with him!

Great professor but you will work for your grade. Participation matters and there's lots of writing and essays and reading. If you want to learn take this class with him. Is a great resource overall as well.

Ron is a tremendous professor, and a tremendous guy in general. He is so friendly and lively and truly cares about everyone in the class. He wants you to learn and engage first and foremost, and is very flexible in how you do so. He respects all opinions, but also isn't afraid to tell someone when they said something they wrong. Take him if you can

Ron is sincere and engaging.  He is the one professor I kept hoping he would lecture more since he is extremely competent on media and human rights.  I looked forward to the class discussions.  There was no textbook assigned which I appreciated.  There is quite a bit of reading with articles and two group projects.  I enjoyed the class a lot.

Difficult class with TONS of reading. However will keep you engaged and interested in all topics as long as you have a single care about the subject on hand. One of the best and meaningful classes I've taken in years.
He is really intelligent and you will have deep meaningful class discussions. I got an A but I worked VERY hard for it. It is not an easy A but he is a fantastic professor.

Professor Krabill led my study abroad group in South Africa. It was an amazing experience. He expects students to be driven by their own interests and to partake in class discussion. If that's not your thing then you won't enjoy his class. It can be quite rewarding for others.

He is really good at encouraging you to draw out deeper meanings. He's extremely likeable, engaging, and fair in how he assesses things. He really likes to hear your side of things and makes every discussion interesting.
Very engaged, cares deeply about his students and has a great passion and deep knowledge of cultural studies. Top rate professor take him whatever the topic is, you will not be dissapointed.

There is a very steady pace in this class. I learned a lot about video production and he was always willing to answer questions and give feedback. This is an advance class. Expectations are heightened up, but if you listen and follow directions AND if you know the basics, you will sure excel in his class. Make sure to study for the quizzes though because they are quite tricky if you don't know the stuff. Overall, it is a very amazing class. Would love to take a 500th level if it was offered..
Most fun I've had in production class on this campus. The prof has a system that keeps you busy but assignments let you create original videos with partners. Great class.

This beginner's class is called Working with Video and that's what we did. A lot of short assignments but he does give detailed and clear directions if you listen and read all the prompts. If you follow instructions and keep up you will come away with lots of experience and skills in basics. It was a lot of work for a 2 credit class but worth it!
He is not a good/clear teacher. His 2 credit class was pretty much a 5 credit class. Wants things his way or it's the highway for your grade.

He has no clue how to explain what he wants from you, often saying one thing then grading hard on unknown criteria. Asking for help is useless as he just laughs and says to try harder and/or follow the directions. Also, it's a 2-credit class but he wanted us to spend hours upon hours outside of class, giving no real in-class time.

If you are going to take video production, do not take it with this instructor. You do the same amount of work for a 3 credit class that you would do for a 5 credit class. I didn't actually learn anything in this class that I couldn't figure out given enough time with some youtube tutorials. Not worth all the work. and the projects were boring.

Don't take this teacher. He is VERY vague in what he wants, but then grades very hard if you don't write exactly what HE wants and thinks. No syllabus for paper, yet graded it down because I did not match his criteria. Very ambiguous in expectations but grades hard. Do NOT take him, unless you want to be bored to death for 4 hours a day.
He is very unclear and is a VERY hard teacher.  Expects you to do way too much reading and the way he grades is very very hard. Do not take BIS 341

First quiz down and our class average was a D.  The material is not that difficult.  He is not does not make his expectations clear.  Repeatedly interupted a group presentation today and kept re-directing it.  What's the point of hearing from others when he's just going to put his spin on it?  In week 4 and so far NOT impressed.

He is very laid back and helpful, ask him questions when you don't understand, he will be there to answers it.  As long as you are doing your work then shouldn't hard to get an A in his class.  Take him when you have a chance.

Not a great lecturer, but he doesn't need to be. Does keep track of how often you show up. However, this class is incredibly easy. Watch movies, two quizzes, three papers, lots of extra credit and a group presentation. Odds are if you do it, you get 100% Easy A.
No Comments

Sam Yum is a great teacher! He's really laid back and just a plain cool guy. His work load isn't that bad, and tests are easy if you keep up on the reading. I loved the video project part of his class. I recommend SAMUEL YUM!

I had Professor Trujillo for B DATA 412 and really liked the class. The class is Group Project-Based (so choose your groupmates wisely) and no exams. Workload can be overwhelming, but they're pretty easy to do as long as you stay on top of deadlines. Very nice professor and really cares about the success of his students. Would highly recommend!

He does not teach the content nor assign homework relevant to Tableau, which is the purpose of the course. His lectures were very off-topic and class felt like a huge waste of time. All learning is done through LONG online videos that info dump everything at once, rather than over time. The assignments were otherwise very easy, just irrelevant.

If you want to learn anything in class don't take him. He goes on the most random topics that barely relate to the assignments and topics. For this TABLEAU class we literally pulled up tableau once. Everything had to be learned with linkedin vids. Very unorganized and barely knows what hes teaching and what HWs are due each week so he cant help.
Best Prof at UWB!
Best professor at UWB!

Loved this class. Professor Trujillo is very helpful and understanding and is clear with his instructions which is amazing. I would take this class again, readings are not hard and assignments are a bit time consuming if you are doing it last minute but if you give yourself enough time to do they are easy.

Having a little bit of prior experience, Professor Trujillo really helped me grow. Tableau at first may seem intimidating, but he makes his assignments clear and provides you with resources to help you with his assignments. He also posts helpful YouTube videos of him guiding you throughout the assignments. Very good professor! 100% recommend

Professor Trujillo was a very nice person and I enjoyed his lectures and the activities. He seemed to care for the class and was very helpful when we needed him to be. He tends to ramble when talking. It's easy to do well in the class.

He assigns very interesting readings and projects and is very accommodating and supportive. Cares so much about his students. I learned a lot and highly recommend this class. Class is backlogged (last 2 weeks are hard af due to the final project) but not super heavy.

Gotta put up 2 reviews for this guy since I had him for BIS 232 and BES 301, which are 2 very different classes. In 232, he was a really good teacher, as he went the extra mile with his students to help them understand. It got hard at times if you didn't have a strong coding background (RStudio), but he's very patient and very willing to help.

reviews.comment: He is very boring during lectures, so you tend to doze off. The class is centered around learning Tableau and RStudio. He doesn't really go over how to use any of the applications. There's a final project where you create a data visual to support your thesis. Class is backloaded, so be prepared to do a lot of research work in the last 2 weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is the second class I took with Professor Trujilo. He's always down to help and give good feedbacks. If your code cannot run, he will be with you until the code runs smoothly. I heard someone said he's boring, but absolutely wrong, he's the chillest and coolest guy I have ever known. He does not mind go out of his way to help his students.

Professor Trujillo is amazing! He is very nice & cares so much about his students. He walks through absolutely everything step by step and he offers help any way possible if someone is confused. Although I loved this professor, the class was not for me. You have to like working w/ computers since this class works with special programs and coding.
He's a very good professor who has a passion for the subject, and is very open minded and respectful.

I took this class just for the BCORE credit. The class was light, professor was nice I completed a few reading assignments and then a group presentation for the final and, that's it. On my momma she is the best educator I've ever had. Very hilariously old-fashioned and rigid. Has high expectations for her students but can also be unexpectedly kind and humorous. You HAVE to be locked in, in order to get a good grade in her course/lab.
One of the best professor at campus!!!

Al-Noori is easily the best professor I have ever had. Her lectures are very smooth and organized. In order to do well in her class, you have to put in the work to really understand the topics but that is what makes it so rewarding at the end. If I could, I would take every class she teaches!

Very knowledge! Honestly the best prof I've ever had and is amazing at lecturing and being interactive. She expects a lot out of you and is a hard prof but if you show up to class and participate you'll be fine. Generally one of the sweetest most knowledgeable profs ever!

She is a passionate professor who truly cares about her students. Her course was very challenging, due to it being off the syllabus schedule for over half of the semester. I felt that communication and updates were lacking in this course, and previous quarters struggled too. Harsh graders, memorize slides word for word. Study guide is a list.

very intelligent. “harsh” grader, but only bc she expects the best out of her students. labs were so fun. sweet & caring. easy to talk to in/out of class. great teacher. lectures were amazing. one of my fav profs @ UWB. course is TOUGH & heavy in content but she teaches very well. very knowledgable. highly recommend taking her. great experience !

An articulate and knowledgeable professor who values intellectual discourse. While I appreciate her interpersonal skills, I found her less accommodating during a difficult time following my mother's murder. Despite active engagement, I received a 3.5 in the course. Her teaching style involves lively debates, visual aids, and substantial learning

Dr. Al-Noori is great.
Attend lectures and take notes and you will do well.

Claims syllabus is clear but really isn't. Grades LATE and very harshly and is dismissive of feedback. Not my first choice for BBIO220 but is a respected/good person overall.
Don't take this teacher! She will harshly grade your assignments.

Al-Noori is really knowledgable and she really holds her students to a high standard. However, I felt that whenever I or students asked questions, she had this judgement that was almost belittling. She's also not that clear on her rubrics and grades extremely hard.

She is an AMAZING teacher. A kind that makes me hopeful for my future! Classes she teaches are hard! So dont go into neuropharmacology and expect easy content. But she teaches very smooth. You have to engage in class which makes it easier to learn. Take her if you can!

She is an okay professor, definitely not the worst I have ever had, but her class is very lecture heavy and she will randomly call on people during lecture and lab so participation really matters. She is hard to talk to since she is condescending and whenever you ask her a question she gets irritated and won't fully answer the question.

Good at reading off lecture slides, impossible to get a clear explanation on specifics. Questions are poorly generated for quizzes, worksheets, & labs. Does NOT welcome feedback--at all. Humiliates students that ask questions. Over-answer all of her questions, her rubric expects 200-300% more than what the question implies; rubric not shared.

Dr. Al-Noori is truly an amazing professor. She inspired me to become more passionate about the field of science. Her class is organized & well structured & she is always available for her students. She does take a while to respond to emails so make sure to reach out to her ahead of time or ask questions in lecture.

reviews.comment: Pretty great professor. She knows HOW to teach. Exams are mostly memorization, very little critical thinking if any, which makes it an easy 4.0 class. Dr. Al-Noori is super caring of her students and makes sure to come around during discussions or when we're working on worksheets. She is the greatest professor I ever had. she truly cares about her students and their success. she gives amazing lectures and makes them very easy to learn.

Dr. Al-Noori is one of the best professors. She is caring and funny. Her lectures are heavy but very interesting. Great professor! As long as you attend classes, and complete assignments, you will succeed and learn a lot in his classes. He also provides lots of help outside of class time if you need.

Very nice and chill teacher for such a high level course. Lots of work and assignments, but he's a pretty lax grader and is very lenient on deadlines. The course is a lot of work and his lectures are kind of boring but other than that he's very good.

Professor Carlson is overall a really solid professor and nice guy! His lectures are clear and he gives great examples that help us understand how to do our homework really well. Easy to reach him outside of class and he seemed to really care about our learning and that we understood the content.

Professor Keskin is one of the best! His Intro to Information Systems course is super well-organized and genuinely engaging. Fair warning though: if you plan on freeriding group projects, his peer evaluations will call you out. Put in the effort and you will love this course. Highly recommend!

2 exams, 3 quizzes (cancelled 4th for W26), + group proj. (multiple assignments/pres.), cheatsheets!!. One of my favorite lecturers, hands down, really makes a different showing up. Great Professor - If you are taking IS 300 at Foster, you should do it Winter Quarter with Tayfun

This class had useful material, but the overall experience was frustrating at times. Best storyteller. Dude is so funny. Just take good lecture notes and the class is a breeze. Probably the easiest foster class I've ever taken.
This is easily the best class in the MSIS program. Seeing the final grades posted today, I am wishing I had been more actively engaged in all my classes this quarter for my future career

Best prof I ever had. All materials are very updated and class is very intresting. One time I send email about grade at night and prof replied in five minutes only. Great professor, for real. He's got solid work experience and explains tough concepts clearly. Go to class or watch the recordings, or you'll struggle. Plus, he's great at helping you network in IT. This is exactly how a master's course should be.
Great professor
Terrific professor. I chose the IS major because of him.

Very chill class overall with a very low workload. He structures the class so you won't have too much work and skips a midterm. Beware, though, the final was very hard. Gives good feedback, especially if you talk to him after class and he answers emails quickly. You get out of this class what you put into it. Peer evaluations matter. Prof. Keskin is not only hilarious but also attentive to students' growth. His class convinced me to pursue IS major. Tests weren't a breeze, but they were open book. Choose your group wisely: he assigns groups but allows swap. I'd gladly enroll in his future classes again.
Tayfun is one of the best professors who I met at Foster. He genuinely cares about his students. His lectures are up-to-date and directly applicable to real-world scenarios.

Tayfun is my favorite professor at UW. He is absolutely hilarious and cares deeply if his students learn. Very accessible outside class and a great lecturer. Exams are open note, strictly timed. There's lots of assignments, but he also gives you great feedback and the assignments aren't that hard. Lectures are useful, so attend even though the attendance isn't mandatory. Stay on top of your deadlines and you'll do well.
IS 300 is hard but Tayfun is great!

Tayfun is a fantastic professor! His expertise in systems analysis and design is evident in his engaging lectures and practical assignments. He genuinely cares about his students' success and goes above and beyond to ensure their understanding. Highly recommend!

By far the most interesting professor I have ever had. I was lucky enough to take one of his courses before I graduated. I wish I could take him earlier :(

Tayfun is an excellent professor. He's super funny and makes info systems interesting. His class is extremely easy, there is zero reason his difficulty rating should be near a 4. I love Tayfun because he is wonderful, patient and very caring. His class is very organized. I just left his midterm exam. My only complaint: he changes exams every quarter so my fraternity database for his exam questions is useless. C'mon dude! Use the same exam so we all can get an easy A

Dr. Keskin is the best professor so far here at UW. I wish he taught more classes so I could take him again. Prof. Tayfun and he sold to Information System. amazing lectures and a very lovely professor... although he makes you read the book and do a little homework every week but still the book and lectures are so interesting. Solid professor. He is very understanding and has great real-life experiences to share. I would definitely take his future classes again.

Professor Keskin is a nice person and makes the class enjoyable. He really cares about our learning and informs us what's next at the end of every class. He is hands down the best professor I have ever had at Foster. I would even call him a good friend after graduation. He is super passionate about MIS and enjoys mentoring students. Absolutely loved Tim, he is such a kind person and is very passionate about information systems. Honestly, he makes you want to learn. He uses a book but optional. He also responds super quickly to emails. Overall super funny guy and a great professor!

Dismissive towards feedback from the multitude of students struggling with the expected workload.

i really enjoyed this class. Dr. Murali can be a little hard at times because some experiments are designed like that, but as long as you prepare well on the procedure and concepts and make it to class and put in the effort in the lab you will be fine. He is understanding, and grading is fair and made everything really clear.

WORST professor ever. i go to class with my printed lab stuff, and every lab he says there is somthing wrong with the printout (such as adding a step, removing or wrong numbers). MIND you he tells us to be prepared, when he himself isn't. 
Prey you dont have a question because he will make an example of you to the whole class. VERY strict GRDER!

Prof Murali is a good instructor. People complain about how harsh grader he is but he shows the reality of the future and prepares you for the future. He's easy to reach out to and is really nice. He always helped in lab and answered any questions I had. He's the best!

Do not take this professor he's one of the worst I have ever seen. Extremely harsh grading he will dock you for anything he can think of once got marked down for missing one of the r's in my lab partners name he's extremely arrogant and truly unaware. His TA is also extremely rude and has no idea what he's talking out bottom line avoid taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors

He's absolutely horrible I genuinely wish I never took his class. If you want to FAIL, take his class. He's EXTREMELY STRICT with his grading and will deduct points for unnecessary things. His TA helps him with grading and he's also super strict and rude.
The BEST Organic Chemistry professor across all three campuses by far.
