Murali is one of the best lecturers! Ochem is hard, his teaching style helped me grasp concepts well. He can be fast paced, but if you tell him what you need he will adjust. He wants the best for his students. His practice probs and SO helpful. Tests are usually fair. just watch lectures, spend time on problems, talk to him, and dont procrastinate!

Say what you will about him, he knows his stuff and always double-checks with everyone in the class to make sure that you understand. His lectures were one of the only lectures where I was engaged for the entirety of the 2 hours, which is genuinely impressive. I would recommend it, just be prepared to show up to class!

Dr. Murali is a good teacher. Can't ask for more in a gen chem teacher teaching a lab. He gives clear feedback and it is really depending on us to improve our presentation of the lab reports. The harsh grading in the beginning helped me a lot to improve my learning, otherwise I wouldn't have changed my bad report writing habits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. This professor is by far one of the worst people I've had the displeasure to come across. He does not respond to emails, waits until the absolute end to grade things, and bombs your grade. His feedback is very arbitrary and vague, so even if you wanted to improve your lab report for next time you can't.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. His grading is terrible and he gives poor feedback and advice on the post-lab reports. He ends up changing up the experiment without telling his students. Definitely would not take his class again!

Overall a horrible professor who is extremely rude to his students and will not take criticism whatsoever. His rubrics are unclear and his T.A.'s grade extremely harshly. There is no care for students wellbeing, and will not hold himself to the same standards he holds students. Avoid his lab at all costs

Grading and feedback is terrible, rubric changes seemingly arbitrarily meaning your grade is always subject to change even if you follow it.

Does not follow written lab directions, instead telling students to skip entire sections or pieces. Then marks down the grade because the skipped part is missing from the lab notebook.

Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Muralidhara is a great professor who cares about his students but he is very unclear on what he wants on his Lab reports. He updates what he wants on the reports without any announcement to the class. His grading is reasonable but takes away points just because of small little details missed in your report.

Murali was a very caring professor in class, but he definitely lived up to the "weed-out" stereotype of gen chem 1. His class took me through the wringer for only 2 credits, and our lab reports took hours due to having unclear procedures and unclear requirements. His feedback was negligible and often was not helpful. His curve is also a joke.

Don't take this professor. He is very strict and grades harshly. But he is manageable if you put a lot of effort. The lab reports took me 3 to 4 hours to finish. I hate him with a passion. Avoid at ALL costs. Btw he is gives horrible feeback on canvas (basically a cricle with a question mark) but he will give u some feedback in his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just horrible really horrible. He graded very harshly and promised through the whole class time that he is going to curve it, but did worse than the normal grading. He gave me 3.3 for 89. Maybe he's better in other classes, but even OC students complain about him.

Graded harshly at the beginning despite unclear rubrics and consistent procedure changes. Kindness doesn't excuse arbitrary grading. Vague responses in online emails. Had Tylenol each time we had lab. I would rather pop a perc and drive blindfolded on a highway than be in another lab of his again. Considered being a mall kiosk worker after labs.

The first ~5 weeks are BRUTAL. Procedures changed without announcements (nearly every lab!), grading criteria were also unclear, and his feedback on lab reports was even more vague. Tip: have friends in his earlier labs who can warn you and ask your lecture professor for help. Lab does get easier once you learn what he wants, so don't give up hope!

A lot of people consider Dr. Murali to be a tough grader, but once I got used to his lab notebook criteria, I found his grading very reasonable. He also grades more quickly than some other lab professors. His feedback on lab reports can sometimes be confusing, so I would recommend going to office hours for a more in-depth explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grades very harshly at the start, lightens up a bit later. Often changes procedure mid-lab, don't come in with tables drawn - you'll have to change them 80% of the time. Can seem intimidating, but ask questions when you can because he's decently helpful. Feedback on lab reports is unclear, go to office hours to discuss. Reports take up to 5 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof does not give any sort of accommodations for medical issues or disabilities and class was entirely exam based grading so really hard to do well especially if you have to take any time off unexpectedly for medical issues/emergencies

Dr. Murali is the best professor I have had at UWB so far! He truly cares about his students and makes himself very available. He is very intelligent and does a great job explaining concepts in a way that is easy for students to understand. Highly recommend!!

Extremely tough,grades harshly. His grading criteria is often unclear. Changed the procedure many times w/o notify students.Not that great, just okay prof. I put more efforts in lab than lecture. I didn't enjoy coming to his lab and hate it so much. He's more chill by the end of the quarter. Wish he was like this from the beginning. Glad it's over.

Tough grader in lab, and his grading criteria is often unclear. However, he is a nice guy who cares about us as students, and I am able to understand his intention to prepare us for higher level classes. My advice would be to read the procedures beforehand, arrive on time, and learn from your previous mistakes.

In my opinion, the other ratings are trippin fr. I think he is a caring prof and if you just follow the directions, you will get good grades. Also, from what I've heard from other students (who has different lab professors), Professor Murali is one of the best and safest option is choose from all the chem lab professors.

To other fellow students: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF!! The amount of work you put in is ridiculous. Lab report is hard enuf but he makes it 10x times harder. Rude in disguise. Gets annoyed when you ask too many questions. I still rmb that one rude cmt he made. Either reply fast or ghost you. Harsh grader. Worst lab experience ever. Idk what I learn atp.
Nice guy, until he starts grading, I have never seen someone so many remove points just because they can, his handwriting on his feedback is unreadable.
I thought his rate was good, so I selected him. He doesn't give feedback on reports and he just deducted a lot of points. So you don't know how to improve and his pre-lab quizzes are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Murali is the worst possible lab instructor that believes repeating the same sentence will lead to understanding. Questions are met with vague answers and enjoys grading harshly. Requires lab prep but changes procedure without announcement forcing us to waste time in lab. Nice in lab, but lacking in every other area. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Phenomenal chemistry professor. Exams are not hard because he expects you to UNDERSTAND the material, not to MEMORIZE them. If memorizing is your method, you will likely suffer this class. If you dedicate enough practice, this course will make sense to you.

The course in general is difficult and will not be easy. I studied for hours consistently. He values participation and questions a lot even if it seems as if he does not. Ask Qns and show up for office hours. I learned a lot from him and appreciate him a lot. TAKE HIM! such a Dr. Murali is a good prof! exams are straightforward and doable.

Started with 237 and ended strong in 239 and cannot thank him enough for pushing me and encouraging me to put in more effort into OChem. I really do understand the subject (especially mechanisms) as a whole. A big thanks for him for making this daunting subject easier. Although attendance was not mandatory, attending all lectures really helped me.

Dr. Murali is a good professor, he will pause during the lectures to make sure you're understanding the topics, so much so that we were 1-2 chapters behind when the quarters ended. There are only graded exams, but the practice problems for each chapter are usually enough for me when studying. He curves the class grades at the end of the quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Murali is an awesome professor! willing to help you understand material you are unclear about. His lectures are complete, straight forward and meaningful. Provides lots of problems to practice. He wants you to know what you are doing and make sure you aren't memorizing reactions and other concepts! love his class and his passion for chemistry!

Dr.Murali is a very nice professor. He starts every lab with an overview and brief intro to what we will be doing. Pre-labs are due as soon as we enter the lab and pre-lab quizzes are due 1 hour before. Feedback is concise and he is always happy to explain in more detail about the lab report. Highly recommend Dr.Murali for chem labs!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ok professor, made efforts to positively impact the class. He did talk a lot during the start of the lab but overall pretty ok. A solid choice out of the lab professors.

Unless you are a slacker, you will learn a lot about Organic Chemistry if you take this course. Folks, it's a pre-med requirement. If you can't pass this, you won't pass the rest. I studied hard, saw Dr. Murali during office hours when I needed and was at class every session. I learned a lot. He cares a lot for his students.
Great professor who genuinely cares about his students. Gives good feedback on tests. Definitely take him again.

He puts the wrong dates on quizzes and lab reports(different from what's on the syllabus), doesn't give good feedback, doesn't respond to emails, is rude, isn't helpful, and seems nice in the beginning but he quickly changed. I hated going to his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems fun but when it comes to being preped, not good. Mistakes made (class data missing) when asked through email tone seemed rude. Teaching is more repeat the same thing 3 times as if you'll get it. Asked same question you get 2 different answers. Come preped(tables drawn) ur gonna cross things out bc last min. changes. doesnt pay to come preped.

Professor Murali is clearly enthusiastic about his job and VERY fair when it comes to grading, especially when compared to other professors such as Shippy or Sommerfield. As long as the key concepts are hit and clear work is shown/done, you'll be rewarded for your efforts for the Lab Notebook + Report. Would absolutely take his class again.

Dr. Murali is one of the best chemistry professors I have ever had. You can tell he actually cares if his students are learning the material. His lectures are very thorough and he shows lots of enthusiasm every day in class. As long as you pay attention during class and do the practice problems before exams, you will do well in his courses.

I had high hopes for this professor, but he doesnt listen to our class needs. Lecture-wise, his pacing is all over the place and its hard to follow what his big points are. He encourages us to go to his office hours, but when we ask Qs, he doesnt have the attitude to help his students grow and he tends to be really harsh/rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Genuinely cares that you learn the material. Frankly, he's an organic chemistry genius as far as I can tell--how much you interact with him directly results in how well you learn OCHEM concepts. He's insanely accommodating for students--almost to a fault. HW due at end of quarter. He doesn't do the 'bare minimum,' he just expects accountability.

Murali is one of the worst teachers I've ever had in my college experience. I was told that OCHEM is one of the most difficult courses offered but this teacher gives the absolute bare minimum effort. He hasn't responded to any emails this quarter and often responds disrespectfully to students with questions in class. He doesn't deserve this job IMO
All around awesome guy. I recommend doing his practice problems a bunch and going over the practice problems in his lecture packets. I recommend his office hours too, hes very helpful!

He is amazing. Just do his practice problems, do the questions in his packets and go over his lectures. If you need any help look over his Panopto or attend his office hours. Hes very helpful during office hours. I dont recommend watching his pre-lecture Panoptos because he focuses on what you need to know in his lecture.

You can tell Dr. Murali is very enthusiastic about this course, however, he did not make the exams easy. His practice questions are all super easy, but the free response on the exam would be super duper hard. The class average was usually around the 50's so he gives out extra credit to help out which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Murali is my guy bro. Yall just a lil dense if you think hes a bad lecturer. Makes the class very easy to 4.0 if you actually have a decent understanding of the basics of Organic chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Nice person but office hours are crowded and can't ask questions. Exams are fair if prepared

His teaching style is very unique but if you pay attention, everything makes sense and comes across very easy. He's very passionate about teaching and he's been one of my favorite professors ever. He really knows organic chemistry and is very knowledgeable. He is very committed so if you need help, he is more than willing to help students.

Dr. Murali is one of my absolute favorite professors. He really wants success for his students and provides all of the tools that help to succeed in organic chemistry. Don't forget to do the practice problems he gives multiple times-practice a lot. Very caring and helped me a lot during his office hours.

Great professor. Extremely knowledgeable about chemistry. I took the whole organic series with him and 4.0ed every class, read the chapter and study practice problems religiously. Just dont take with lab if youre a premed student like me, gives you more time to prep for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Professor Murali! He manages to make organic chemistry interesting and manageable. Everyone told me beforehand that I should be afraid of organic chemistry, but he manages to make the course interactive. He is by far and away one of the most dedicated professors I have ever had, and he genuinely seems to care about his students.

I just think he needs to hire better graders!!! Less condescending and thorough, please. WAY too many people constantly complain about their graded exams and manage to get so much points back. Think he got so stressed by this, he just became a completely different prof than when I first took 237 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Personally, I loved every bit if the class. He comes to class excited to teach. Cares about student success a lot. Other class mates didn't like his style of teaching, but it worked very well for me. I learned a ton, and enjoyed every bit of the course

great person, very knowledgeable, and genuinely cares about his students. This is a rarity in universities and should be acknowledged. Con: don't take lab with 238. There is so much hw it hurts my study time in both classes. Check your tests, as right answers are marked wrong often. He's confrontational when you need help, but helps you anyways.

Great Prof! Lectures are interesting and he makes the class fun. His classes are painless and you learn a lot including lots of life lessons. The more you interact the better off you are. He is very helpful and will answer any question you might have without making you feel stupid.

THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!! Dr. Murali is such an amazing person, his lectures are always entertaining and he is genuinely passionate about his job. OChem is a really hard subject but he makes sure you really learn it. I absolutely loved him. He gives lots of problems to practice. I definitely recommend him! He's the best!!

Murali is very disorganized during lecture and often mixes up what he says. He holds study sessions on Saturdays and they are helpful, because he does a lot of practice problems. However, he doesn't give enough time during the tests, and talks a lot while the test is going on. Test averages are usually 60%, but he curves the class in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: So its true that his class can be a little disorganized... he has a syllabus with a  schedule, but he tends to go off track sometimes, and then you have to cram information later. That's the only downside in taking his class, otherwise he's extremely caring, and will do his best to help you understand ochem. He's funny & uses desi analogies

Best teacher at UWB! always comes into class happy and excited to teach! understands his students and strives for his class to be very stress free! His teaching style helps yo remember everything for the quizzes and exams. I am happy that I leaned OChem from him and would love to take any course he teaches at UWB.

Avoid this teacher. He is disorganized, unclear, and makes so many mistakes that it confuses the whole class. He often goes on ridiculous tangents and talks about philosophical and personal subjects that are not at all related to chemistry. Additionally he will go at a snail pace during the first two weeks,  then rush through the rest of the weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I've taken both Ochem Professors at the University of Washington and Murali is definitely the "easier" of the two. While most people say that he's easier.. take this with a grain of sand, as the subject is very tough and will still require you to put a lot of work in on your part. If you  STUDY the practice problems you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: OChem, regardless of the teacher, is really a tough class. With that being said, I had Dr. Murali all 3 quarters and I liked his class and I learned a lot from Dr. Murali. He is very enthusiastic and interesting professor and is always willing to help you out. Like he told us almost everyday, you just need to connect the pieces to make it work.
Murali is a disorganized mess, who is really nice and means well.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is phenomenal as a professor and as a person. He is exceptionally clear and explains things really well, always pushing you to try harder and challenge yourself. He always answers questions. Do the work and you will be fine.
Awesome professor. He never disappointed me. Classes are very engaging and lots of information with plenty of examples with life experience connections. Definitely would take again and recommend.

Dr. Mural was excellent and the rigor of the course met up to my expectations. He was very encouraging and always willing to help out students. It was definitely a pleasure having him and I can't wait to have him again in the next quarter. I could tell that he loves what he does and he is definitely a pioneer  in his craft. I recommend him.

He went over one chapter for a week and then would cram another 2 chapters into one day, usually right before the exam. No way to know what to expect on the exams. Review sessions didn't help because it was just more lecture - no engaging or giving practice problems EVER even when asked. Knows his stuff, but doesn't know how to teach it.

So far into this quarter, he is VERY unorganized. He never follows the schedule that he made  on the syllabus. Be prepared to be taught on one chapter for 2 weeks and rushed through another chapter in 1-2 days. This class really does require a lot of self studying. Plus he spends a lot of time talking about  irrelevant subjects. Avoid this class

He is a kind helpful person who curves grades, he expects too much from his students, even if he's teaching a class where they do not know chemistry - he has tested us on material we barely go over because we are behind in our studies. Overall I suggest taking him if you want a challenge or only if you have no other choice, but avoid otherwise.

Ochem is hard. Murali is an awesome teacher, he has a respectful teaching philosophy and cares about his students. On 3rd qrt, he gets a little cloudy, but thats the same for all ochem profs. Get to know him, don't slack off, practice, practice, you will do just fine! Hes great in lab as well! Expand your thinking!
Best Professor in UWB. I recommend him for everyone to take him. He rocks and helping many students to understand. Gives good examples and makes you understand the concepts.

Murali is a nice person, but a scatter brained professor. His lectures are everywhere, he'll spend an hour on one question and the tell you its wrong. He doesn't have a style of teaching yet, as he is newer to teaching at UWB. He makes you do entire chapters on your own without going over in class, and he is always behind the syllabus schedule.

Professor Murali was the best professor I've ever had at UW. He always explained things clearly and made sure he taught in a way his students could understand. Tests were pretty tough, but if you put in the effort, it's not too hard to get an A in his class.

B Chem 237,238,239, 241 Passionate about chemistry, and wants students to love this subject too. However, he doesn't try very hard to help students achieve success in his class. Grades in his class are pretty much based on exams and a very small % is earned from the HW. You can skip all his classes and still get an A if you study.

He explains things clearly and very enthusiastic! He is very approachable so it's easy to get help when few concepts are unclear. He definitely makes chemistry a easy one. I definitely recommend this professor.
I enjoyed his lecture. It helped me understand lot of fundamentals in organic chemistry. I would definitely take his class again.

Excellent Organic Chemistry Professor ever had in my life. He is very helpful, and explains the stuff in a clear and in an easy way. If you attend all his classes to understand the concepts and do all the suggested problems, you would be fine. I was lucky that I learnt the organic basics from him. Take his class, he is awesome.

He's a very nice person but not so much a great organic chemistry professor. He speaks too quickly and doesn't cover important material. Every lab lecture he has given this quarter has gone over time by at least five minutes, and is often unfinished. Topics that aren't covered in class due to lack of time management skills are still on the exam.

Grades tough, adds no valuable info to class, I could teach this better, cares more about expressing his political views than teaching. Canvas will be your teacher and you should heavily rely on ChatGPT. He hates AI, and u can use it to pass every test or make ur assignments. Run.

Professor never really explains ANYTHING, and very much expects you to figure things out via Canvas. Not much help most of the quarter, and you really need to collaborate with other students to even understand the point of the class. However, by the end of the class, once you understand it all, he is very easy to connect with. A bit annoying too.

Don't get me wrong he is very passionate in what he teaches, but with that said he assumes we understand everything as if we were him on assignments, on simple vague questions, and on so many other things. He doesn't actually answer questions straight on but rather In a confusing way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Let me preface, don't take this class unless you have to. Not a single person in my class had any clue what was going on the entire quarter. Professor Toft grades really hard and offers little feedback. Anytime you ask for clarification he uses a lot of words to essentially say nothing leaving you more confused in the end. I learned nothing.

Great guy, friendly and WILL help with your work if you ask. Going to class does matter as there are in person assignments, and he will give you extremely detailed feedback with work he doesn't like. I will say however he is an TOUGH grader. Some of it is really frustrating as it is more so his opinion and not due a failure to follow the rubric.

His class has been awful especially towards the end of the quarter. He assigns a lot of reading with more than 25 pages to be done before class. He makes every assignment due right before class and doesn't take into consideration other classes and jobs. He grades with a standard of perfection and his very critical of students who are beginners. RUN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Toft is a great presenter and I did learn a lot about public radio. That said, the work was insanity level. Am I better for having taken the class? Yes. My limits were pushed and I grew. Don't take this course if you have a full time job. Do take this course if you love podcasting and want to really improve your skillset.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Run.

This professor is appalling. he is unclear, confusing, and downright creepy at times. if you have the option to take another professor, do it! his class was an elective for me and it took up 90% of my study time, and i still only got a b-. save yourself, dont take this professor.
Not a easy A class even if you do well on the assignments. Lost of complicated works.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I easily recommend Amoshaun Toft, he is opinionated but makes his lectures a discussion. assignments are interesting and thought-provoking. while I don't always agree with him I have nothing but respect for him and his teaching style. if you are looking for a media class to take look for his name you will definitely get your money's worth

He's a nice guy but his instructions are always worded weirdly to the point you become very confused. Always has "activities" that are quiz-style based on your reading from the night before, these are always open for discussion. Makes it difficult to receive full credit for your work. You have to volunteer 3 times within the quarter.
There's often ambiguity in the lectures, but more than anything the amount of homework for a 5 credit class is outlandish.
So many lecture, podcast with no text

Updated my fall courses immediately to remove a course with him. I normally excel in classes like these, but Toft is never clear in what he wants. When you ask for clarity, he stumbles and backtracks. If you include everything he wants, youll end up with a 16 page paper when he only wants 5. I dont think he even knows what he expects from us.

If I could give the rating below 1 I would. Not clear on his expectations or assignments. Quiz questions are completely different than what he asks for if you ask him to explain. There is heavy reading, at least 20 pages per article, and a really tough grader. You're your own professor, he doesn't teach you anything. Your brain will be mush.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Clearly passionate about the class and its material. Not very difficult in theory, but his grading scale is ridiculously hard for no reason - even if the feedback is helpful and constructive you still need to put in the work. You need to put in a lot more work than you think you'd need to. Very accessible and helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is well run, but Professor Toft cares WAY TOO much about the subject material over your ability to understand it. If you come into the class and it's a subject you do not know, I suggest another teacher. His instructions are very confusing and he doesn't do a good job explaining. He also grades for PERFECTION, so keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grades your assignments not based on if you met the criteria, but rather if he just "liked" them or not. Never posted a syllabus or set class rules and expectations. He treated this class as if we were his employees and not his students. If you really want to take this class, wait until school is back in-person.

I honestly dont even know where to start with this guy. The copious amounts of reading that you only have time to complete if you have nothing else happening in your life... or the vague and harsh grading criteria, that he uses to tear apart your every assignment. One of the worst profs Ive ever had the horror of taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The Media & Communication major's "core class" is actually pretty easy, but the rubrics and guidelines in Amoshaun's version can be confusing. He's a nice guy but the class is honestly all over the place, even if it's interesting enough to be engaged in. He definitely knew what he was talking about and adapted the class very well to COVID-19.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He was very confusing on his instructions, and only focused on one subject. I would not take this class again. It was very lecture heavy, and a lot of group work where everyone was confused. If you take this class, just be ready for A LOT of readings, and he's a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is quite passionate about the lectures but no one else know what he is talking about. Very tough grader, insane amount of readings, and very unclear assignment descriptions. Would not recommend to take his class unless you want a challenge

He looks for connection to EVERY reading that was related to the paper, so even if it's a small one, try to put it in your paper. Replies emails pretty quickly, but he can be confusing, so I really suggest using his office hours and have him explain things to you in person. Not an easy class, grades fairly when he sees effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: 5 short papers, a final group project, no quizzes. LOTS of readings, and looks for deep analysis and understanding in your papers, but fair grader. What I don't like is after the paper is due before class, instead of talking about the readings related to the next paper, he keeps talking about the readings related to that submitted paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: To me, he gives fair grading when he sees your hard work in effort but overall, he's a very tough grader with so many papers, heavy lecture which he doesn't seem to focus on other communication fields other than radio journalism throughout the quarter as a project.  I agree with person below me. enough said

Rather than allow the class to discuss and get to know each other, all of his focus is on the ridiculous amount of papers he has you write, all of which HAVE to draw heavily from each of the million readings he assigns for each one. Most prompts don't even make sense. Good luck passing if you work or have literally any other priorities in your life

I had him for an elective class, and for an elective professor he was a very harsh grader. I took the class because elective classes are usually easy As, but the class was definitely not one of them. A LOT of reading, reading responses due every week, and if you do not put in 110% in group work he will dock you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: LOTS of reading required.  Lot's of writing, but it isn't hard.  He provides a LOT of feedback with grades on assignments, which is awesome :)

Was very passionate about the subjects but it does not transfer to the course or to the students. He assigned a lot of readings and we spent most of the class days having to talk with other students about the readings while he walked around and listened to us. Throughout most of the quarter he probably gave 3-4 lectures. Very confusing course.

Toft is extremely passionate about everything he talks about during class which is nice, however he has really high expectations. The amount of reading is ridiculous but the material overall is quite interesting. If you like a challenge take the class, if your looking for an easy A, you won't find it here.

Amoshaun is great at what he teaches. Like the previous reviewer said, he is indeed about power and cultural movements, but using media and other means of communication as a tool.  The pace and reading (as well as videos) are incredibly ridiculous, but you will learn quite a lot. The project was fun as well, but slightly unclear at times.

He's quite interesting, though his approach is a little different than your vision of Media and Communication. This class was more about Gender, Race, and Class as well as culture. All in all though, I noticed that sometimes he gets lazy grading papers and I randomly get a perfect score. Also, the pace of this class is mediocre.

The pace of this class is absolutely unforgiving. While I learned a lot, some of the assignments were totally arbitrary.  Mindlessly heavy course load. Because of the rapidness with which media assignments are due, I would not recommend this class to anyone who works, has kids, or just a busy life in general.
I learned so much from this guy and am very glad I took it.  A bit quirky maybe and definitely demanding, but worth the time you put into the course.

By far the most confusing prof I've ever had! You can tell he knows what he's talking about, but no one else knows what he's talking about. By the end of the quarter I was still totally confused! And his office isn't even at the Seattle campus!

Took Realities of Inequalities from him and absolutely loved it. Be prepared for a ton of work--meaningful work--and to learn a lot. Go to class every day, be prepared, and don't even try to phone it in. He's a fantastic and sensitive teacher, and I am thoroughly impressed. It was worth all the work. Also: what a hottie!

Toft was very knowledgeable about the subject matter, but the class was extremely boring. He was not clear on directions and a lot of people are still confused about the class project. You have to learn as you go along. Attendance is mandatory to do well in the class. But you don't have to do the reading to do well. I took his class at UW Seattle.
Don't take his class PLEASE! It is not worth to risk you grade. He is extremely hard, no clarity, ton of readings, quizzes are lame.

Gives readings/videos,some over 70 pages and most videos are only available on netflix or library (he gives pop quizzes)In class he uses powerpoints (not online) that are very hard to keep up with while listening to him talk and taking notes.  Find a different teacher, I hated this class&got nothing out of it but a mediocre grade and a headache.

He knows his stuff, but this class is super boring. None of his instructions are clear and you have to figure it out as the class progresses. Most of the students in my class still don't understand what is going on. He gives lots of busy work and materials that you have to read which are dense and a super headache to read. Some are irrelevant.

As long as you keep up and do the work, you will do fine. He is pretty clear on his expectations. You can get extra help from the DML tutors. Pay very close attention when he goes over ProTools. You would definitely not want to miss any classes that are scheduled in the DML.

Lots of busy work. Required to do weekly posts. His expectations are high but doesn't give enough instruction for certain aspects of the class. He is a nice guy and offers help but just be prepared for a lot of work.

This teach is truly inspiring. He is so passionate and compassionate and it shows through his innovative teaching techniques. He will challenge you academically and allow you to see your potential. I loved this class, hoping to take another from him again soon!

I love this teacher. Had him for Realities of Inequality.  He has a warm heart and is passionate about inequality. He is funny and really knows his stuff.  The material is life-changing - amazing! The only bad thing about him is that he doesn't give feedback on assignments and only gives grade updates 2x/qtr.
The work load is inhuman, but Toft has a lot of information to share.

The work load is over the top, the activities and homework don't connect, and the information is difficult to absorb because it is so disparate. That said, I think Amoshuan has interesting ideas to share, but I would never recommend his courses to someone I liked.
Amazing class! Amoshaun really knows his stuff. Class was interesting & fairly easy as long as you read every once and a while and do the fieldwork.

Dr. Tewari is a great teacher. If you're ever confused about smth just ask him, he's always ready to help. The course uses excel, so learn a bit before the quarter starts. Exam questions were very similar to the hw so if you know how to do the hw you're good. There are a few graded workshops, so be sure not to miss those, and a short group project.

Professor Tewari is obviously passionate about what he teaches and wants students to understand. Sometimes his lectures are a bit fast but he always is wiling to explain further or go back. There were multiple opprotunities to improve your midterm grade which was very gracious. Show up to class-not mandatory but you will be confused if you don't.
Very passionate about what he teaches, can be confusing at times but honestly not too bad. Be prepared to know how to use excel before you take his class though.

He is very passionate & knowledgeable but sometimes sounds confusing. Using Pearson is crucial to success and playing around with excel before taking the class would be quite helpful to understand what he is saying. If you have a Mac be prepared to be a bit lost, he is used to windows and excel being easy to use. Homework/Exams aren't bad.

Took Dr. Tewari for the MIS Capstone 489 and it was overall a good class, he has an accent so hard to understand at times. The project is IT based and I felt like it was very beneficial for me as an MIS student
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took his BBUS 489. Lectures are long and pointless. Some assignments doesn't even have instructions. He also wants you to answer MCQs, SAQs, and write a whole page essay during one midterm in two hours. Don't bother emailing him for questions, he doesn't bother reading much less answering what you're asking. Avoid this professor at all costs...

He is a kind person who means well; however, his class isn't super engaging. It's difficult to follow along, and certain concepts were explained in a way that made them more confusing than they actually were. I showed up three times and got a 3.8 and taught myself most of the content.

Very easy subject, and this guy very clearly cares about teaching and is knowledgeable, but isn't the greatest at teaching. tends to make things more complicated than they are, but it is very easy to figure out on your own. kind guy who is ready to help his students. lots of homework though. was basically an online self taught class though.

He has a tendency to make concepts sound significantly more confusing than they actually are. If you can decipher what he's saying though, the lectures are very eye opening and worth while. Homework is not heavy but often doesn't reflect even a little bit the material that is gone over in lectures. Overall he grades fairly and is there to help.

He means well and is a good man like other ratings have said. However if you actually want to learn be prepared to teach yourself. Lectures are hard to understand and follow. Most people don't even show up to class because they would rather teach themselves. Wished I dropped it early on. Easy subject, organized poorly.
Very nice man, love the dude, easy class, literally let me cheat on his midterm with no consequences cause he knew i was struggling

This dude actually has the worst lectures in the game. They are jumbled, unorganized and he jumps around way to quickly. His examples make no sense and he is hard to understand. To put it in perspective, this is the only class that has broken my 4.0 record.
His lectures were quite hard to follow sometimes but he would answer any questions you asked him or any clarification.

Took him for BUS 489 MIS capstone.
Good guy but the lectures are heavy and quite honestly boring. He means well but goes about it poorly
did not grade any assignment until 2 weeks before the quarter was over but gave it all 100%.
Most people (about half) don't go to the lectures.
Overall a good man, easy grader but misplaced values / practices.
He is great overall, is passionate ab

Small complaint but he does have an accent that sometimes I find a bit hard to understand. He is passionate about teaching, but he isn't very used to teaching in the U.S with canvas. He tries to make lectures engaging, and he explains concepts in a way which is relatively easy to understand. He's also very nice.
He was very hard to follow in lecture

I think the prof was great, the class was overall boring but he made them pretty easy to understand. I feel like the class had tons of homework but he will move the deadline if you give him enough time in advance.

I stopped coming to lectures after realizing everything was done online. In-person lectures consist of the prof. talking with little engagement. He wants us to use Excel but doesn't explain how to use it. I can tell he loves to teach but the information just isn't received well, his lectures are a little messy. However, it's easy to get an A.

Does a good job at explaining concepts clearly, and in a way that is easy to understand. You can tell he is very passionate about what he is teaching. Overall, he's pretty chill. Would definitely take a class with him again.

There were no complaints about the grading criteria. This course is Excel-reliant and requires you to be technology-reliant. His grading is easy; just do all my lab questions, and you can pass. You can skip his lecture and teach everything yourself. Only con is he refuses to record his lecture and doesn't share his excel formulas.

Best taken if you're a senior in biology as there's a lot of content that's review, but not super well explained in this class. I took it as a senior and knowing a lot of background info really helped me, and I'd suggest that you study with the study guides after each lecture as to not get behind. Worksheets based on completion. 2 projects. 3 exams

Bad prof, take if you're looking to get a review of bio basics.
She doesn't understand the concept of teaching. She expects you to know everything and then goes ahead to teach you the basics. 
She will go ahead and invite her old colleagues that are in the job market to present for the class, wasting time and resources of the school and students.

She made attendance mandatory in the middle of the quarter. Does not know how to teach, I got nothing from the lectures. The exams do not resemble the worksheets and she grades harshly. She also did not grade my assignments fairly which I messaged her about and she ignored me.
Do not take this class if you want to learn something about microbiology. Take it if you do want to be frustrated and feel unvalued.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: New teacher, and I like him even if it may not be the best class for how I learn. As others have noted, his class is very interactive. Lots of group work and interesting assignments. He prepares us well for exams and even interviews. Generous grader. Giving a 5 rating to offset the 1-star ratings, but truly a 4-4.5 probably.

One of the few teachers that actually cares deeply about his students.
Took him for CSS 360 Software, he teaches practically and is VERY open to feedback.
He brings in food, his dog, likes to do activities outside of class with students if asked.
Lecture heavy but he knows what hes talking about.
a must take if given the option.

Honestly ignore any bad reviews on here i had to retake cs and i took it with ethan and it was amazing. He is very understanding and a good professor. From someone who went from failing 142 to passing it with a 3.9, take ethan hes really good
Professor deletes any negative reviews on rmp even if it follows guidelines.

I got an A- without touching the book at all. The prof had some duplicated questions on his exams so he gave extra credit and curved which helped me a lot. The class was challenging but rewarding. If you attend lectures and take good notes you will be fine. I wish I had him again for 143 this quarter!

Man this guy really knows his stuff. The class wasn't too hard but dang the exams had hundreds of questions. Good thing he curved. I got to know Ethan more throughout the quarter, he's very chilled and casual. Sometimes I forgot that he's my professor. By far the most practical course I have taken.

Ethan is one of my favorite professors! I liked how he would always explain alternative ways to implement certain things. This class is very broad so you will learn a lot. Don't take this class if breadth is not your thing. The final group project is probably my favorite because you get to really build a full stack application.

I like Ethan's way of teaching. It's more practical than my other classes. Towards the end of the quarter he started to use the whiteboard more which was very helpful. Aside from the slides he uploaded on Canvas, he also shared his comprehensive lecture notes which I used as my study guide. Overall, he's a very caring guy and I'd take him again.

Unlike other CS professors at UWB who just read off the slide show, he teaches you how to implement code more realistically. He's very casual and greatly cares about his students. FYI, he will have a bring your dog to class day if you're lucky. He's also an expert in the field and he encourages students to consult him regarding their career plans.

Prof. Valdez's criteria/expectations for her assignments are not made clear. In order to get a good grade, you have to be IN CLASS. The guidelines for assignments do not cover everything she wants students to accomplish, and her email responses to questions are vague & unhelpful. Participation points are easy, but class time is not used effectively

Worst professor I've had thus far. If you must take BES 301, take it with someone else. Nobody had any clue what was going on until Week 8. She would say we were going to do all these different tasks but then talk for 2 hours straight. No sort of organization at all either. Big fat waist of time and energy. Made the class way harder than necessary.

She is a passionate and great professor. Not a lot of assignments, just a big group project at the end of the quarter but she would give you some time to work on it. Get ready to do a lot of research for your exams because the exams are open book and short essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Primarily project-based and discussion-based B CORE section. If you manage your time well, do the (fairly short) readings, participate in class, and put genuine effort into your work, you will be rewarded. Would recommend taking advantage of the small class size if you are interested in biology; Dr. Valdez is enthusiastic about undergrad research.

Pretty simple class you have to do a big group project at one point. As well as work on projects that are due later on in the quarter like the Bird Journal and the Bird Photo Gallery so if you don't like later due dates maybe not your class. Also reading simple journals assignments and in class participation counts. Overall an easy class to take!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Expected the worst but pleasantly surprised. Pros: Understands life's hurdles IF INFORMED. Key to success: get on her good side = PARTICIPATE, listen to her feedback, & at least skim the assigned readings before class. Cons: Unorganized. Can be rude but only w/ students who don't participate or don't pay attention/on their phones. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I genuinely really like Dr. Valdez. She is very kind and her lectures are interesting and engaging. She's kind of a tough grader, but she gives amazing feedback that can be used for future assignments. She also replies to emails quickly and is generous to help with anything.

You can tell she genuinely wants you to learn the material/ be able to apply it outside the classroom. Lectures were clear and simple to understand/follow. LOTS of extra credit opportunities, be sure to take as many as possible! Sometimes slow grading, but gives good feedback! I don't understand why people rate her so harshly, genuinely a good prof

Take home exams. You will spend alot of time researching. Sometimes questions on assignments aren't specific, but overall ain't bad. Fair grader, gives good feedback. Sometimes forgets to make assignments available on canvas but gives adequate time for us to work on them when they are. Attend the whole class period-don't miss out on participation

The organization is terrible and confusing, one of the slowest graders, and a very hard grader. Expects you to give out high-quality perfect explanations on assignments while having terrible instructions for the work you are given. Also waits until the last minute to allow you to work on and submit assignments. Worst class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I can see that professor Valdez is enthusiastic about the subject and wants her students to learn however she is not clear on what she wants out of you for assignments, and she is often unorganized, posting assignments late (like Monday the week of) so it can be difficult to plan for them especially if it is a group project.

Extremely unprofessional unorganized work in canvas. Doesn't actually know how to efficiently use excel features such as filter, and rants at student when another idea is suggested. When giving feedback in zoom/person she loves to rant about the same things over and over in the most negative way possible without a shred of positivity.

consistent with the other 2 classes I've had with her. unorganized, typos, inconsistencies, etc. It often feels as though her class is just one step away from falling apart. I have done well in all of her classes, but it seems like she fluctuates from crazy hard grader to "I'm too tired to grade your paper so here is an A". Avoid at all costs.

I gave her the benefit of the doubt for this first class, but my experience has been consistent. None of the assignment explanations are clear. There are constantly typos and inconsistencies due to assignments not being updated. All of her classes are unorganized. I'm not the only one here, folks. I don't understand how she hasn't fixed her classes

I will never take her again. I tried to give her the benefit of the doubt because I thought she was a nice person but the worst professor I have ever had. 4 take home exams, dont be excited because she will never give you full credit unless theres some sort of extra credit, very little points, and sent me passive aggressive emails to questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Tough grader--Group projects

reviews.comment: Will dock points if your responses arent exactly catered to what she wants, even if its correct. Doesnt track attendance and missing class is ok but she likes participation+keeps track of that for final grade. Odd grading scale 97 4.0, 84 3.5. Somewhat difficult to get a 4.0. Take-home exams take hours(open note). Would take again only if I have to

This Professor tricks you you into thinking that you will have any kind of independency when doing research in her classes. Its very rigid in ways that she wants you to think specifically that caters to HER understanding rather than having her course be a learning experience that prepares you for real research. Beware.

The BCORE class was All Things Crows. However, in a 10 week quarter, more than half of it was spent on a project not even closely related to crows. As a teacher, she's also not great. She is unorganized & the canvas is difficult to navigate. She also expects high quality, huge effort drawings for the bird journal. Way too much effort for a BCORE.

As far as online classes go, it's meh. She seems nice and very knowledgeable. For a 300+ class it feels kind of basic (easy and boring). has very strict guidelines on availability but I can appreciate that. I will NOT answer calls from my job past the end of my shift. Acceptable level of assignments/readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Valdez is honestly one of the best professors I've worked with. She is strict and wants you to learn. It is really easy to get on her good side if you need a letter of recommendation, all you need to do is participate in class and ask questions. She does give out homework and expects you to hand it in on time (she doesn't take late work).

Ive had professor Valdez three different times over my time at UWB and Ive hated every experience with her. She is overly nit picky about things, and if your thinking or explanation isnt exactly as she would put it, youre totally wrong. She waits to assign work until the last minute, and does not respond to emails. Worst professor Ive had.

Dr. Valdez had zero assignments for the first half of the quarter. The midterm was not graded until the 2nd to last week of the quarter - upon which the entire grade was based upon. She was routinely late to class, and yet expected attendance and participation from students. She was disorganized, and extremely slow to respond to emails.

Class was so poorly organized. Assignments weren't posted until she wanted to add them, which made it really hard to know what was expected of us. She would make NUMEROUS of announcements with links to readings and google docs which were hard to understand. Then you had to dig through files to just find what you needed to do. AWFUL!

If I could give her a negative rating I would. Worst teacher Ive ever had at UWB. If youre a bio major take bio 471 with Chang instead. Her grading is harsh, she wont reply to emails ever, lectures are boring, if you dont agree with her opinion on an exam youll be wrong no matter if you got evidence to back you up.

I liked Professor Valdez, you can tell she really cares about the subject and her students learning the content. She can be unorganized at times but accomodates for her students. Wasn't too much homework and was an easy A for me

Professor Valdez is awesome. I had her for ecology and she was so passionate about the subject. She made that class a fun experience for me. There was a lot of reading and a lot of participation, but she's just making sure your engaged. Would definitely recommend she's great!

I was frustrated the entire quarter. Instructions aren't clear and her voice is hard to understand. Lectures and grammar were not college level. She is kind, but assignments are all busy work consisting of two article worksheet/week, and she only picks a couple to grade. So you better do all of them. It was difficult to figure out what she wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is not a hard class, but it has ridiculous amount of work to do. It is only a 100 level class and it should't be that loaded. Also very unorganized. Would not recommend taking.

Professor Valdez might be a little bit tough on grading. However, for students who are interested in the topic, the experience of taking a class with her would be unforgettable. Her passion for wildlife biology and conservation is unparalleled. Also, the way she teaches her classes really gets you think critically about many global issues.

There is to much homework, this class has made this quarter hard by the amount of work I have to do for it. This class gives the amount of work of like 2 classes. Having to do  CBLR project , blogs, perfect journal entries on your own and doing long readings and answering 5 questions every week. It takes work time from other classes. Avoid taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Took her BIS 141 class, requires 18 hours of CBLR, 5 blog entries, read a book within 2 weeks and prepare to present it to class, journal every week which you have to follow her instruction to get full credit. She expects too much from the students for 100 level class, it feels like 400 level class. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS !!!!!

Her powerpoints were filled with pictures which made it easy for visual learners. She is fun and easy going. Final exam was difficult but it was take home. We had class outside once which was awesome. Her accent is barely noticeable. She is very willing to help you succeed, always offers help and is a fair grader! *read the textbook for xtra cred

Do not take a class with this woman. Her lectures are a terrible, she expects way too much work for a 100 level class and she has a habit of assigning (pointless)assignments the day before they are due. She gets very anal about following her directions, which is almost impossible because of her vagueness and inability to explain anything clearly.

This is the worst professor I have ever had. Her English is terrible, she treats the majority of her students like high schoolers, and her lectures are uninformative and boring. She  won't accommodate students if they need to miss class for a doctor's appointment or any other necessary reasons for an absence. I'm not sure how she even got this job.
Prof Valdez clearly cares about what she teaches and engages her class to not just textbook learning but applied learning.

One of the worst professors I have had. Power points are grammatically incorrect, have an absurd amount of incorrectly spelled words and do not make sense, and mosts slides look so unprofessionally cut and pasted with images, that I am surprised she has a PhD at all. Her lectures are long and boring and don't really make sense a lot of the time.

This class was an easy A for me but her grading is very picky and vague, so I feel like I just got lucky. Class was boring but the material was basic. No reading or studying required if you've taken intro to biology. There was A LOT of group busy work which was a pain in the ass. I like her as a person and researcher, iffy as a teacher.

Alot of busy work. She does have a thick accent, but it never bothered anyone in my ecology class. Lectures are loooooong and she will spend every minute covering it. Some had more than 70 slides per class! Note taking is very difficult and she is unorganized. I liked her as a person, but as a teacher... No. However, it was a grade booster class.

The WORST prof I have ever had (and I've finished my BA). Expected way too much for a 100 level class: tried to require our summer class to attend an overnight field trip and when no one could attend, she added 2 extra CBLR hours to the class requirement. 8 hours of farming in 4 weeks! Completely unorganized, unclear, rude, and flaky. DO NOT TAKE!

She is completely disorganized & unclear (instructions are vague & her accent is annoying). When you ask a question, she makes the answer 100x more complicated & confusing. She's rude when you ask questions. My grade literally dropped 6% b/c she didn't like my work, when she was unclear about what she wanted. Do NOT take her class!

Shes completely unapproachable as a teacher. She's unclear about assignments, has a thick accent which makes her hard to understand, and is completely disorganized. One of the worst teachers on campus

If you want a very easy 4.0 then take this class. I took her crows class and it was very easy. Do your work and you'll pass with flying colors. She also gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit. The only downfall to this class is that her classes were repetitive and she was very unorganized. Expect assignments being created one day ahead.

She is very unorganized and made up the class as the quarter progressed. I think she is a great person, but her teaching is terrible. She is a really easy grader as long as you put some effort in. She did assign things the day before they were due, and should have had a better syllabus that said what the assignments were going to be. She made it up

Very disorganized, and not helpful at all. Not understanding if you miss class or an assignment. You have to call her Dr. Valdez or she will get mad. You can't really understand what she is saying a lot of the time. The class is very boring. Again, she is very disorganized!!

I took the CROWS class. She is so disorganized and confusing! She assigned stuff the day before they were due. Her whole thing about having us be creative as well as scientific is annoying. Field-trip=waist of time. Class content is repetitive. Journal=useless. She is nice, but when it comes to the class boring and annoying. AGAIN, SOO disorganized
Worst professor during my time at udub. Teaches super slow, never seen him answer any questions confidently or to my satisfaction. Often gets confused while teaching.
He's very impersonal, but extremely care about your learning. As a no-frills student, I love his style. His teaching is superb also .
He's a NICE guy but a TERRIBLE teacher/lecturer. If your into theories, you'll be fine but if not, it'll be hard to understand him. Also, he has an accent that can be hard to understand.

Do NOT fear him! Please! Very clear in explanation and genuinely cares about you when approached. He even provides Scantron forms during final exam! Take notes and listen to him and do homework. You should be fine. Again, do not fear him. Prof. Hetmaniuk is what Kevin Flynn states in TRON: Legacy. "Like flowers in the wasteland."

Ulrich doesn't really teach the class. He only just comes in on a weekly basis for an hour lecture. Other days are led by TAs. The class is said to be doable for anyone with just Math 125 knowledge and that no prior programming experience is necessary. This is true, but its strongly recommended that you know some CS and Math 307 and 308.

I took AMATH 301 with Professor Hetmaniuk and it was a straight forward class. There were 5 homework assignments and 5 quizzes and one final. Homework makes up 50% of the grade, quizzes 20 and the final 30. Final is just like the quizzes and as long as you watch the video lectures you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Hetmaniuk really doesn't teach well, or care about student learning. Most of the time he wasn't even there, there was instead a graduate student.  When he is there, usually he just writes equations on the board and ignores the students. The homework isn't too  bad, and tests aren't either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is really impersonal. But he is helpful enough to answer your questions online quickly (not thru email). Tests are okay if you understand the material.

Very knowledgeable, but extremely impersonal, and practically unresponsive to students' questions and concerns.  Blasted through most of the material without giving students much opportunity to work with and explore new concepts.  HWs required many hours, and little of it was covered in lectures. Tests were similar to HWs, but with limited time.

Had a really positive experience with this professor.  Excellent use of technology and making resources available to students.  His explanations in lectures are excellent.  Probably one of the best professor's I have had at UW.

An exceptional math professor, (maybe the best I've had). His lectures are clear and concise, his class is extremely well organized, utilizes technology well, and comes with no surprises. After being extremely disappointed in the teaching quality of my 308 professor, this guy renewed my desire to learn the subject matter. UW is lucky to have him.
Difficult class, but he does a great job. I definitely recommend him.
Take this class, best professor at UW!!!
Love Him!!
Best use of technology I have seen in an applied math course. Although not a pre-rec, you should take math 308 prior. Bonus: he has a beautiful french accent!!

Thought it was going to be a great class taught by a great professor with Microsoft working experience. Good at work doesn't necessarily mean good at teaching. He was basically re-state what was on the lecture slides. Each test covers too many & too broad topics, and most of them are listing & theoretical. Does not have grading rubric or guideline
Assignment was so vague. You need to memorize everything  in the slide for exams.

Horrible teacher. Very vague in giving assignments and boring. He does not possess any teaching skills whatsoever and reads off the slides every single day. He gets extremely defensive whenever you ask him questions so don't bother :/ WANTS your grade to be horrible, claiming it's to make you work harder. Do not take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are not clear at all. He will have multiple classes in a row where no information will be taught and then once class he will throw every bit of information at you. He lectures wo powerpoint and when he writes on the board he abbreviates everything. Very hard to follow. Only two tests in the whole class. TAKE THE OTHER FINANCE PROF!

UGh, where to start.  Couldn't keep to official course calender, didn't get our midterm grade until 2-3 classes before final, didn't get our project grade till after final, lectures are BORING and DRY, he went on for 60 minutes about something that took about 5 minutes to explain.  If you are a good self learner, you will do well, if not, stay away

He's VERY SMART, but VERY BORING. There are some goods and bads with this guy. THE GOOD: Extremely helpful, willing to help for as long as you need.       THE BAD: very very very very very dry lectures. ZERO out of book lecture, very little real-life experience.

Very good prof if you are prepared to talk about finance or economic based topics. If you don't do the homework you are screwed. If you don't listen in class and take notes you are screwed. He tests on the book, homework, and lectures. Class was challenging but very rewarding.

Trust me you do not want to take this class.  This is my last quarter of college and I have only had one other professor who was as bad as this guy.  Late to class, unorganized, doesn't get assignments graded quickly, LOTS of errors when he works problems on the board.  He gets a D+ in my grade book.
He knows the topic and is able to explain it well.  Be prepared to listen to an accent and ask questions.
Very nice guy.  Horrible teacher.  I LOVE investments and still hate coming to this class.  Some people weren't cut out for teaching, he is one of them.
Best Professor I have ever had. Very good at explaining and always willing to help. Class was kind of hard but very fair if you studied. Can't wait to take investments with him next quarter.
Great guy and a wonderful teacher! I learned a lot in his class.  Don't slack if you want a good grade. Ladies, he is cute too!
One of the best teachers at the campus. Does a great job clarifying topics.

I was going for a concentration in Finance until I took his class. He is very smart - just has a hard time conveying his knowledge. No control on class; he couldn't keep an entire gaggle from talking the whole quarter, despite numerous complaints. Tests are reasonable, not enough time to "work" through challenging questions. VERY frustrating class!
Great class, learned a TON about finance!
Best Prof. Ever!

I actually really liked this teacher. He went at a slower pace and taught a lot of accounting basics, which was great for me. Classmates complained of tests, but I found them to be easy so long as you did the practice test beforehand. Good teacher.

Some will say they hated this professor because she's bad at teaching, and I'll admit she does not provide the best explanation but if you read the textbook before class it should be easier to understand her. She is an incredibly nice  professor and even lets students use their textbooks for the exam, and gives EC. Easier than other professors IMO
She is great i learned way more from her because i like to learn from the professor not just my book

You have to listen pretty hard to understand what she is saying, due to her accent, and she has trouble explaining things in understandable terms to begin with...  I just read the textbook and I was fine.  She's really nice, and a super easy grader though.  If you go to her office hours, she'll practically do your work for you!
such a sweet professor and veryyyyyyy passionate about what she teaches :) very chill and educational overall.
She was very passionate and a fun professor to listen to during lectures, I feel like the overall class structure however could be rearranged to make it more engaging

Just show up to class and do the projects for credit. Readings weren't required but they were easy. She stated that she doesn't make students buy textbooks. Super caring and knowledgeable. She is easy to understand and made learning fun!

She is so amazing!! I have taken her for 2 classes now and I love her more every time. She brings a warm and caring teaching style and makes safe environments for learning. 
100000000% take again
She's so amazing! You'll learn a lot about project-based teaching and student engineering. Her lectures are really interesting and the projects are super fun! You should take her class!
Very caring, and passionate Professor. Learned a ton of information about STEAM. Would love to take Veronica again :)

He is a really nice person, and I was genuinely fascinated with his FBI stories. Unfortunately, his lectures were dreadful and painfully long. At one point, there were only roughly 7-8 students a week. I couldn't tell you a single thing I learned, but it was a very easy 4.0 because every single assignment, quiz, and exam is online.

I think the prof. made this course really fun. The subject was meh but all the real-world connection to the lectures made them interesting. Really cool guy and def worth to take his classes if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ethan's lectures go by pretty fast and you won't have a single chance to write anything down. But, it doesn't really matter because the homework is all the notes you'll need. Overall, the class is fairly easy. My biggest issue was his TA Gary. You can do well on all the assignments but Gary's grading on the Excel work will screw you over. Be wary.

Bro is the goat. Let us pick whether or not to come back to class, he switches his classes with lecturers and in class work which I find freshening, hes hella funny and his TA Gary is the goat. They help ease the stress of Managerial accounting and make it super easy to learn. Hes very new, but I think UW did somethin this time, great class.

I loved her developmental psych class! Very clear grading criteria and a very friendly teacher. Clear expectations throughout and cares about our learning. Work isn't terribly hard but you HAVE TO do the readings to do well. Most of the class, or at least the friends I made, put in effort and got 3.5+.

Honestly, I wanted to like Professor Udell, but they made it incredibly difficult. The seem to have a big ego, which clouds their ability to fairly handle conflict, and carry out ethical judgement. That's surprising to say, especially given their educational background, but it's what I witnessed. They're likeable, but struggle to respect students

Professor Udell is a tough grader but Her feedback is reasonable more often than not and always sees room for improvement. This class is less lecture based and more group/independent work. If youre struggling, reach out to her! She will work with you if needed
She is definitely a tough grader but she is very good at teaching. If you're taking this class, ATTEND THE LECTURES they are important to all the exams and the overall understanding of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Why on earth would a professor give us a next chapter quiz on the same day as an exam for the previous chapters! i mean we suppose to take the exam and then take the new chapter quiz after couple days or so. How the hell will we have time to study for the exam and for the new chapter to take exam and quiz the same day! your grade will suffer

Shes a tough grader man, and this class is stressful so much. She isn't fair with grading and her exams are way too hard too. She tells you she won't ask for definitions in exams, then BOMB a lot of definitions are asked on the exam. You only have a very short time on exams, if you have anxiety. good luck....
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's an okay teacher. She will help you. But when it comes to an assignment no matter how much effort I put in it I get less than I deserve it's hard to get an A, this class will definitely affect your GPA. If you put a lot of effort in your assignments you will not get full points as you think way less than you think you will get. Terrible class

There's a lot of work it's a fast-paced class. you don't have time to study enough for exams or read the chapters on top of that you have assignments due the same day as exams. BUT she is the most caring, nice teacher, I have ever met. if you ask for help she will be there and be supportive. Exams are tough and the grading.

Professor Udell is pretty good! Expect an all lecture, reading/hw heavy, group work oriented class. The hw isn't hard, you can collab w/ other students on it and the answers are easy to find in the text. No final just one midterm, one essay, and 2 hws a week. She built days off into her curriculum, which was really nice. She grades kinda hard tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor fails to mention assignments that she omits from the course on the syllabus to incoming students. She disregarded my concerns & failed to give me grades for an assignment that was in the syllabus after saying it was required, then saying it wasn't after I had completed it. My GPA DROPPED taking this class. She's an Ivy league mess.

I am doing u a favor by writing this review. I always get 4.0's while taking 25-30 credits a quarter, but this prof wrecked my GPA. She may be good in person, but this online class sucked. She is the most harsh grader I have seen in my life and doesn't even care when we try to talk to her. She is really mean, so don't take her unless u want to fail

I feel like shed be an ok professor when schools normal but with COVID and all the riots, shes been absolutely dreadful. Tests and hw you only have 3 days to complete with no way to move ahead because she doesnt post things ahead of time. Im working and struggling and this class is so unreasonably difficult. On top of that she grades SUPER hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm sure she would be a decent prof in person. But her online class is the worst. She is not even considerate of COVID-19 or the riots going on, or how her students are being affected. She continues to harshly grade assignments. If u want a good grade, stay away from her. Trust me.

She is literally so mean. Such a harsh grader, and grades you based on your opinion in discussions. I am a straight 4.0 student for the last 2 years while taking 30 credits at a time and this is the hardest class I've been in. If you want your GPA to tank, then go ahead and fail here. I literally worked so hard to barely make it to a decent grade.

Taking this class during the pandemic so online class is hard to grasp for me. She is a really tough grader + marks down for the smallest things. Lots of tests and quizes. She is transitioning to online teaching well I would say, she provides video recordings for going over material which helps. She seems nice but still a somewhat tough class.

Super chill and funny prof. She goes through her lecture and makes sure you understand the material. Her class is based on group work and slides. No exams, just quizzes (7 of them). They're not hard unless you don't study. One final paper about a movie. Overall amazing professor and very interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super nice and definitely explains questions you have. This class was oriented by what you did on the outside of class as in reading from the required text, then asking questions on canvas to your group (work in small groups) and in class we discuss the material we read and answer questions. Also there are frequent tests, however they are 16 ?'s
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shes funny, and very good at going through and talking about what we read. And answering any questions anyone may have.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious
