She is knowledgeable of what she is teaching and assigns readings which really expand your thinking and provides good feedback. Readings are fairly simple and the workload is manageable. I honestly don't know why her rating is so low on here, students on campus loves her!

The content of the class is great, Ive learned a lot. BUT- she can be quite curt in her communication, her expectations for the mid term were super high, and she seems way too obsessed with certain details- she makes you add a very specific check list to your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's very unprofessional, unorganized, don't reply email on time, very biased, and lazy. She does not prepare for students success. She failed to complement the goals of UW to students, and failed to maintain the school value. Most importantly, her class is not student-centered class. Whatever she says, she wants you to accept that it's the truth.

While the class is genuinely a hard one to take, the concepts are well defined and the readings are interesting to go through. She provides lots of commentary on the work and provides guidance on readings in class. I would take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was very organized. She was always willing to help students who have trouble  or question about the class. There were some readings but it was doable. 2 exams, 1 group presentation. I would take her class again.

She gives clear and helpful lectures. There are a lot of readings, in which a lot of the readings are dense. She will clear any confusion and is very approachable when concerning questions. There is a group project and presentation towards the end of the quarter.

Dont do anything in class besides talk about readings, watch movies, and talk about future essays. basically dont need to be in class to pass  just  have to do the essays which are ALOT of ESSAYS slow moving class. But she is really nice
This professor fails to give feedback and gets mad if you ask about grades.

Good professor, but you need to lock in to get a good grade. Final grades are given on a curve. I thought I was gonna get a 1.7 in the class, but actually ended up with a 3.1. I for real left half of my answers blank on the final and did good. Just make sure to get a 100% on the pearson assignments.

I enjoy attending class with Professor Xiahua. She is knowledgeable and explains concepts clearly. However, the exams can be tough, so be sure to review all the class material and notes she provides. Overall, she is a great professor for students who are willing to put in the effort.

Midterm (30% of the grade) and final (another 30 % of the grade) are in person. Attendance isn't mandatory, but 10% of your grade goes towards the Participation points. Math heavy. Mostly algebra level.

The midterm and final exam are weighed very heavily. The final is HARD. She is a very nice person and will help you during her online office hours. However, her in-class lectures DRAG ON. She gets distracted very easily and goes on multiple tangents. One class (2 hours) was just spent on her talking about our midterm grades and her college stories.

All the content to be tested in the exam is already in the class notes and copies are provided, the practice homework can help you build your abilities. The textbook does not need to be read because it is not very helpful. She is very tolerant of exams, she will give you a whole page as notes and all exams are based on class notes only.

I enjoyed professor Anny's class. She is very knowledgeable and encourages her students to be the best they can be at UWB. I will say this class is not easy and if you do not show up to the lecture you will fail. The tests are heavy but there is room for extra credit. I
There are lots of things need to learn by yourself. It is Overwhelming

Midterm and final are weighed 30% each. There's a lot of material in this class so you're given a lot of information in every lecture. To get a good grade in this class, you have to study on your own a lot, especially before each test. Other than studying on your own, the weekly workload is fairly light.

She truly cares for her students and wants them to succeed. This class isn't for everyone though, you should only take it if you really want to learn/improve yourself. The class is pretty difficult, the average on both the mid term and final was around 60%, but the class is curved. Talking to her in office hours was very useful, she is very wise.

Professor grades class on a curve. So not know your grade until the end is hard. Tests are worth 30% each, so be sure to study hard and pace yourself during the exams. One the down side, professor created almost like a competition of who can get the best grades and to be over prepared for tests.

Annie was my favorite professor in the beginning but became my least as time went on bc of how rude she acts towards other students & myself. When people attempt to participate in class and their answer is wrong, instead of encouraging participation she nags about people not getting things right. There is no psychological safety in this class.

Great teacher, but you have to work hard, she loves to teach and cares about students understanding the concept. 2 heavy exams, 30% each. The class was curved, so not knowing the grade until the last day on my uw. She is super nice teacher!

Midterm and final exam are worth 30% EACH so this class is super heavy on exams. All the time spent doing homework and other assignments don't matter but she does love participation. No one finished the final exam because the content was so hard but she is a sweet person overall so it's hard to not like her. Just the material is tough. Get ready

She's a great person and genuinely cares for your success, but I have never been so confused in a class. Pre-Class quizzes are given even before you go over the topic. Homework is very confusing. Study hard or you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Anny is probably a great person but as a teacher, she really lacks proper pacing in lectures. Goes over basic concepts extremely slow and sometimes overcomplicates things for students. The grade is pretty exam heavy and most materials in those exams come from a strong analysis of concepts she never teaches you. If you want a good grade, STUDY!!!

Professor Wei is a remarkable instructor. Her economics class is not a walk in the park. To get a good grade, you have to earn it. I didn't have a good understanding of economics before taking her class but having taken her class, I definitely have a better understanding of it. Definitely recommended.

Amazing professor, tries very hard to be accessible, genuinely cares about students and wants you to do well. Class itself can be hard so go to class, but it's an easy A if you show up and put some amount of effort into class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Xiahua(Anny) is one of the best professors that I have ever had. She wants her students to succeed and will go out of her way to help them when in need. Put in the work, be genuinely curious and you'll do great.
Nice person but hard exams

She's honestly amazing & really committed to helping you do well. That is not to say that her class isn't hard. Do ALL the Pearson HW, pre-class quizzes, in-class exercises, and practice homeworks if you wanna do well on tests. Go into her office hours if you need help. She knows the class is hard but is there to help you. 1 pg notes on all tests

Amazing teacher. Definitely a tough teacher but she works super hard to make sure we understand the material. Sometimes there were days where I wished class would go a bit longer because of how interesting the material was. Definitely not a class you can slack on though, My hardest class this quarter but also the one I enjoyed the most!

Professor Wei works very hard to make sure that her students learn the material. She goes out of her way by extending office hours, hosting study sessions on weekends and responding to emails in a timely matter. Her lectures are helpful/easy to understand, and is she is great with answering questions/clarifying. Professor Wei is very knowledgeable!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a really nice professor. Her lectures are easy to understand and her test is not too difficult. There is a final group presentation, and it worth 50%. If you practice her practice homework, then you will get a good grade. She always provide us a lot of information. Overall, she is a nice professor and i will take her class again.

Econo-metrics (Statistics) was challenging for me but this course was intellectually stimulating and useful for my future career. Professor Wei is professional and full of knowledge. Her class is tough but not impossible if you work hard. She wants everyone to succeed and is encouraging. We are lucky to have her at UW. I'd marry her if I could...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Class is okay. Exams are hard becuase its not receprocated off the homework online so the formatting isnt the same. Make sure to study. Very easy to talk to and understand needs and concern if you talk to her. Helpful in terms of that but other than that lecture is heavy and attendance isnt mandatory but you should go to class to understand
Unbelievably difficult and heavy workload!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Wei is great. She is very fair but does expect that you are prepared for class and will call on people to ensure that. Do not be afraid to ask questions in class. Homework is easy and short and not very much. Very accessible with office hours and creates additional hours if necessary. Exams are pretty tough, definitely study!

Professor Wei is highly engaging and deeply cares about our learning. She has a lot of open office hours and does a lot of 1-on-1 engagement with us to help us understand economics. Economics can be challenging but if you are willing to put in the work, Prof. Wei will be there to help you and you will succeed. She has my recommendation.

Phenomenal instructor. The material is more difficult than what some might be used to, especially if they transferred from a community college. But it is critical to experiencing success in subsequent business classes. Xiahua knows the content, she is organized and methodical, she  and she cares about the success of her students.

Unbelievably difficult. BBUS 310 is a difficult class but Prof. Wei made it impossible. I failed, first and last class I will ever fail. Excessive and unhelpful homework assignments, confusing powerpoints and in class exercises that made little to no sense. Stay away!!!!!  Retook the class with Prof. Campbell the following quarter and got a 3.7.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: We consistently fell behind in the course. Topics we were supposed to cover in 2 separate 2 hour classes we ended up covering in 1 hour of 1 class period. The tests are worded very bad and there is not enough practice material/homework. Also, the homework is all online while the tests are mostly handwritten. She's nice, but this class needs work.

This course is VERY math intensive. Know your algebra and calculus. Her accent can be a little distracting. She does a lot of practice in class and that really helps. However, she fell behind on her schedule and would still test us on material we barely covered.
Worst. Professor. Ever

If you come to class and read the assigned chapters, do your homework online- you can easily pass this class. I would highly recommend this instructor. She is very helpful and can accommodate her office hours if students have questions.

She is my favorite teacher at UWB so far. She is "tough with a smile". Face it, there is no way to make 300 level econ a walk in the park for everyone. Her thought process is crisp, and she usually understands your questions right away. The assigned research paper is a unique opportunity to do something cool.

Anny can be demanding of her students, but she wants them to succeed.  Pay attention in lectures, because that is the material she will quiz you on.  Anny is more than happy to help after class, and is very accessible by email.

She expects you to know a topic inside and out (i.e read the book) before it is gone over in class and she only minimally covers key concepts during lectures. There are many different equations requiring lots of calculus and she never goes over math in class (most of us took calc over a year ago) making the class that much more difficult. RUN!!!
I will admit, she is extremely difficult on her tests/quizzes but on everything else (homework and projects mainly), she's easy-going. She's also a fair-grader and she answers emails very quickly.
She spent a lot of time on teaching and helping the students. If you review her PPT slides after every lecture, you will find all the questions on tests are similar in her lectures and homework.

She was very lenient in grading. If you listen to her lectures and review the PPT slides carefully, you can get A+ definitely! She gave us a lot of extra credits. All the questions on exams she did teach us in class! Don't miss this great professor.

I know people were complaining about her, but she was not as bad as other people said. Yes, her first "quiz" was horrible. But she ended up taking one of the sections away. As long as you read over her ppt, her quizzes were doable. She may not have been one of the best prof, but she was definitely not the worst.

A very confusing class. We had 1 hour to take a test involving: Online multiple choice, a packet, and an Excel spreadsheet. No one finished. She defended herself while the class raged for 30 minutes about why the test wasn't fair.
Exams are impossible to prepare for. Once you've taken her class, you won't leave the same person again.
By far the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. I am a 4.0 student and her class is impossible to do good in. The exams are only 1 hour and they are impossible to prepare for.
The worst professor ever!! The exams are much harder than the hardest problems in the homework.  Please, DON'T WALK FROM THIS PROFESSOR >>>>> RUN!!
Unclear! Really confusing throughout the quarter
the worst professor I have ever had
She is unclear but she tries to make everything is clear. Approachable. Lenient in grading.
Yes the class is difficult but Professor Peng is willing to help you out tremendously if you visit him during office hours. I also did my capstone with him and he was very chill. Great guy!

He does a very good job keeping a reliable schedule, so it is very easy to keep track of the work for this class. His lectures can be long, but he does gives adequate breaks through the two-hour period. He is very knowledgeable with the subject so any question you have will likely get a great response. Rubrics were also very straightforward.
Lecture was detailed and cover many contents. However, it could be boring toward the 2nd hour of the class. Programing assignments and exams have clear criteria and graded on time.
Homeworks are unrelated to the lectures. Strict heavy penalty for late submission. hard to understand the lectures cause of the heavy accent and teaching style.

Quiz every class, I wouldn't say quiz hard. He is great guy, but very hard to hear what he is saying due to his accent. If you are median of class, you're guaranteed to get 3.5. Final project part 1 and 2, part 1 is easy, part 2 is a disaster. Pay attention to practice quizzes and exams. Go to QSC center for helps with project and homework. GL!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every other class had a quiz to make sure students understood the previous lecture. He'd go over quiz answers + explain topics well imo. He did go over coding problems with the class, but not a lot. I will say that you should read the textbook to pass the class and most students did not lol. has an accent..i thought he said SQL instead of C code..

CSS 422 itself is a challenging course. The final project and exams are definitely challenging, but I don't really blame the professor for the difficulty. He was flexible and modified the content on the final because he was sick. Answers questions if you can catch him in person. I liked his lectures too, though they were a bit dry at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's an...interesting professor. You can tell that he wants you to succeed but it feels like he'd rather get through all the content needed to cover rather than make sure the class understands before moving on. Assembly is not like Java to C++, it's a brand new language but he just commentates over slides rather than do in class coding examples.

Speeds through lectures and gives no coding examples to help you understand a brand new programming language aka Assembly language. Midterms and finals were incredibly hard with averages close to 50s. He provides no suggestions on building your final project aka the disassembler. Office hours were useless. You're pretty much on your own in class.
Caring guy, but very thick accent, had trouble understanding him, nice thing is he records his lectures which helps....

During the in-class lectures Dr. Peng always gave me the impression that he cared very much about our success in the class. He paid close attention to the parts of the lecture that students did/did not understand. He explained Karnaugh maps in class in one hour, and I'd read that wikipedia page at least 5 times before then and never got it.

No need for textbook. Difficult class. Other ratings under "Peng Yang". DO NOT FALL BEHIND. It will take you forever to catch up. Not a forgiving teacher - if you turn in anything late or not in proper format - huge impact on grade. The "MarkeyJester's 68k Tutorial" website can be found on Google - will be your best friend throughout the quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Peng is very experienced with C++ and is willing to help you learn more than just the basics. He will help you understand WHY things are done a particular way to prevent possible bugs or errors. He really helped me grasp pointers and the STL. I highly reccomend this class with Professor Peng.

He goes off-topic A LOT you will most likely find yourself fighting sleepiness. He is a harsh grader, but the curve at the end may bump your grade up quite a bit. Part of your grade comes from how well you do on a board game that is partly depended on your luck. The extracurricular to make up for the points lost is also from the board game.

Snooze fest. His lectures are long and off topic. Every time I attend class, I wonder if we really need it. His grading is tough as if you are late then you would lose 33% for that assignment. He also makes us play a board game for our grade. And if you do bad in that board game, then your grade in that class will drop heavily.

Just a very boring teacher overall, he also is very very tough about deadlines and has no leniency with policies of lowering the grade of an assignment worth 15% of your course grade by 25% if late my mere seconds in class

Out of all the Bcore classes, this one was definitely the best. Super interesting topic of risky business, little to no homework, and overall a great professor who enjoys what they do. If you are interested in business or stem I'd recommend it.

The professor himself is a nice guy. He's always enthusiastic and has his camera on. However, his class is not one to take if you are a full-time student. It's content heavy for an "intro" class, leaving me confused the entire quarter. Lecture isn't spent effectively as he just goes over readings in class, which we have to already do out of.

Ive never felt so lost. not only is he very disorganized, but the later assignments are hard and crammed with the final project presentation. Yes you can schedule office hours for questions and feedback, but the class time is not used to help us build our projects and understand the assignments. None of the assignments are graded, final's next week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Enthusiastic about his work and takes time to make sure everyone is on the same page. Definitely a great personality and is very open to further discussions on class topics. A very helpful guy, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: i absolutely loved this professor, he was very nice and caring. he is passionate about what he is teaching and helps a lot during office hours. very easy grader but grades the day before quarter ends
Very good professor, he mainly focuses on 2 big projects (no exams). Professor gives good lecture and feedback to his students, would take again.

Doesnt respond to emails but if you schedule office hours or ask questions after class he will answer them. Hes very kind and cares about your success. He is one of the better Bio teachers at UWB imo. Hes passionate about this class and hopes to further research experience for students taking it. Dont take this class tho if you know you hate coding

He's not responsive to emails, but he's very helpful about meeting outside class! (As long as you schedule office hours at the end of lectures) He also didn't grade any assignments until the end of the quarter, so if you needed feedback or help on your project, you'd have to go to office hours.

Okay so I don't really care how he teaches but he doesn't grade any assignment even at the last week of the class. Never responded to my email or my classmates. This is important for professor to do, give feedbacks on the work and grade accordingly. I'm not even sure how well I'm doing since I didn't get any of my grades back from any assignment.
This was such an interesting subject (bioinformatics) and you can tell Jesse is passionate about teaching it. He's really helpful outside of class. The class is jointly offered with a CSS class.

1 grp project, 2 exams (1 dropped), & 1 final. Gave the option to attend in person or watch online if you were iffy due to covid which was so considerate. Jesses not harsh grader either. If you got a wrong answer but explained your reasoning he gave you points still. He wasnt the most organized but still amazing. Loved his class! Solid choice

The class is very disorganized and takes a long time to give grades on assignments. It appears he doesn't try very hard as a teacher, and ignores emails. Rough class to experience. I would try to avoid in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a good caring professor if you are willing to put in the work and study hard as you should be for a 400 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A really good professor, straight forward exams.

Words cannot even justify my frustration with this professor and this course. His teaching style is actual dog sh*t - and that's the kindest way I can put that. Oh, you like organized class structure? Too bad. You want a clear and well-constructed answers? Sucks. It is so hard to do well in this class given how he "teaches"... all outside learning.

Fun person, very poor professor. Unclear, rambling, doesn't prioritize getting grades back to students, syllabus isn't followed, and exams are difficult to predict. I strongly recommend avoiding taking a class with him.

This was his first quarter teaching so I don't know why everyone is being harsh. Yes he could have taught some things better, but we're in college. We are expected to self-teach ourselves. Reading the book ahead of class time will help a lot. There are two exams and a final and he was very generous with the curve. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: This was his first quarter teaching evolutio. He is improving, but many of his lectures were hard to follow and we didnt do most of the assignments on the syllabus. I think that he will be a great teacher in the future! But this class was rough. He also does not explain much of the math because he is also a prof in computer science.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He taught us model training step by step and showed us useful methods to read papers. He always encouraged us to keep learning. Really learned a lot from his guidance!
He guided me through my first research experience, and under his mentorship, we achieved first place in the first phase of the CBVCC competition!

His course materials are thoughtfully prepared. During lectures, he combines traditional board work with multimedia content to explain complex concepts in depth. The homework assignments are well-designed and provide valuable hands-on experience, which was incredibly useful for my job search.

Highly recommended! The professor's lectures are coherent and structured, with well-prepared slides and visual aids that make complex concepts more intuitive and easier to grasp. Additionally, he provides comprehensive materials to ensure students fully understand the content. Every aspect of the course reflects his dedication and professionalism.

His Computer Graphics course is amazing! He explains concepts clearly and makes complex topics easy to understand. The lectures are engaging, and he provides practical examples that help reinforce the material. Highly recommended for anyone interested in this subject!

He's known for being an easy grader, and I agree. Really nice guy and he genuinely cares. However, at the very end, the ENTIRE class emailed him regarding our GPAs. Most of us got very very low grades despite 100% on the essays. It was fixed, but hassle makes me hesitant to recommend him to someone else. Nice guy, but it was a bit stressful.
No need for textbook. Easy grader. Never missed a point in the class. Don't learn much about the topic but he talks about important lessons for future CS students.  No tests. Fun class.

Bryan talks about a lot of things not related to the course and often times remember that he has to discuss something about it. Just remember to show up, submit your homework (late submissions are usually accepted as long as you submit it before the Final week), and you'll get a great grade.

He is disorganized but only because he is newer to the Canvas format.  He does talk about other things during class but when you ask him a question in or out of class he is very helpful. He wants you to succeed. He adds his own spin on things. Don't worry, do the assignments and you'll be fine. You don't have to show up to class but you should.

Zetlen rants about random topics, rather than lecturing about what is relevant for the class. He is very opinionated, which is fine, but aggressively shuts down opposing viewpoints. In any given 2-hour class, max 30 minutes is related to 370 material. He's very disorganized about assignments, and can't get Canvas to work. Wish I had any other prof.

Totally awesome Prof, she's snarky and hilarious. Really, really enjoyed this class. Grades are solely based off of weekly online quizzes and presentations, no midtermsfinal. Her quizzes are tricky and definitely take time, but she genuinely isn't trying to "trick" you and feels bad if questions are confusing. Definitely recommend the class.

Grades made up of only presentations and catalyst quizzes. Presentations were not bad, but quizzes kind of stressed me out even though you could work with other students. Just do well on your group presentations and fairly well on your catalyst quizzes and expect a high grade. She is sassy, awesome, and fairly lenient on regrades. She's great!

Dr. Zeman was a great lecturer and shows a lot of passion in animal physiology. However, her exams can be a bit tricky and application is necessary. Bio is a hard course anyway, so studying is indeed a must. She even visit students in labs :)

AWESOME PROFESSOR EVER. Her classes are tough, but she will commit enough time to explain every detail you need to know. Her office hours are very helpful, and she will never turn you down if you just walk into her office with a bunch of questions at any time. If you take her lectures seriously and read textbook, you will do great in the exams.

Absolutely amazing. The amount of effort she put into this course was unbelievable, and she truly cared whether or not we learned. Exams were pretty tough, but she graded very liberally, focusing on how well we could defend our observations. I've never had a prof be so enthusiastic about the material. By far the best prof in the bio dept.

You'd think that after decades of teaching, she'd be a bit better at it. Her teaching style is completely different from the norm. She has quizzes in addition to midterms and the stuff is cumulative. Her test questions are impossibly difficult. Avoid at all costs. Her class will kill your GPA & any desire to take another bio course ever again...

She's really helpful in office hours, but exams are more like solving engineering problems.  Do NOT expect to memorize stuff and be able to pass this class. Be prepared to think like a scientist, know *processes* instead of facts, and you should do ok. Professor Zeman knows A LOT about physiology, don't be afraid to ask questions. :)

Nice professor, awful class. Class is extremely exam-heavy (exams worth 50% of your grade). Many of the exam questions are not on the exam-specific provided review materials; be prepared to review all homework assignments individually to feel even remotely comfortable on the exam. The final exam was moved up a week with little prior notification.

Worst teacher I have ever had. If you ask a question in class she will trail off mid answer and say she will get back to you and wont. She spent the first half of the quarter showing you how to solve problems with excel, which you cant use for tests. Moved the final up a week because students were traveling and would not make exceptions.

Class was challenging, so I suggest spending time in class to learn the material, especially considering the homework you receive. If you do poorly on the midterm, it's cooked. Exams are wordy, which makes it difficult GL.

This class was pure torture. The workload was overwhelming, with a group project due every single week. It felt like no matter how much time you spent, there was always more to do. On top of that, the professor was completely unhelpful, leaving us drowning in assignments with no feedback. Save yourself the headache and avoid this one.
She is okay
She is a really good professor. She provides all the help needed and cares about her students. If you study all the assigned homework, you will get a decent grade.

The professor assigns WAY WAY too much work. Expects a final report but getting data requires you to be on campus. Inadequate teaching via unhelpful videos, no guidance, and high expectations. Fails to address questions and reads word for word in her lectures as others mentioned. Extremely dissatisfied with this teaching approach. Terrible prof.
Great professor! very knowledgeable and passionate about Finance. Also very kind and personable as well.  Would highly recommend!

She is simply fantastic! During finals week, I got sick and couldn't attend the final exam. She was incredibly understanding and allowed me to reschedule without any issue.

Her genuine concern for her students success is there. I highly recommend taking her for 451

I don't know if she is a better teacher in person but it was horrible online. Does not review everything from the assigned readings. Lots of group work so choose your group wisely. Does not explain very well in class, lecture time is used mostly to do practice problems, so a lot of self learning.

Professor Ying is wonderful. She is my favorite professor so far at UW. All of her lectures are organized and pre-recorded on Canvas and she tries hard to make students understand concepts. I was dreading this finance class, but now, after taking it from her, I want to add finance to my concentration! I hope I can take her future finance classes.

This is a hard one, the class is incredibly easy given its online now. However the professor is easily confused by student questions and technology. Routinely is flustered by Zoom. For the first half of the class she didnt share her power point presentations. Grading criteria is anyone guess. She might be better in person.

I've never been so confused on how to rate a professor. She's an easy grader for the group project, gives u multiple opportunities to makeup work, but i feel like I didn't learn anything from her. She's so confusing. Also her grading "on a curve" is unreasonable. Even if you get a 95% in the class, be ready for a 3.5
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you show up to class, participate, and understand the homework and in-class problems, this class is not bad. She is not afraid to call students out, and she definitely can be intimidating at times. Be prepared for open-note group quizzes, half of the midterm and final is online, and the written portions of the tests can be new and difficult.

Ying Li is the best professor I ever met in UW Bothell. Her class is well prepared and easy to understand. She cares for everyone in a class. If you pay attention to her class and do your homework, you would get a good grade.

I like this professor because she always tries very hard to help every student understand the concepts, she made reasonable homework for you to work, and I feel I was treated very respected as a student. Her lecture is easy to understand, if you have questions to ask her, she is always helpful. I will definitely take her class again if I will.

I don't know if she lowered the level of difficulty in summer quarter. HW were all in myfinancelab, and they were very easy. Group should do the case studies (4 calculation question) very week, but those questions were not very difficult. 3 exams and 5 quizzes. Each exam had 10 multiple questions and 2 calculation questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: very tough grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Her lectures aren't helpful and the heavy workload only brings more frustration.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Coming into to this course I knew it was going to be challenging, but Professor Li is very dry. A majority of the grading system is heavily relied on the midterm, and final. She offers 4 bonus opportunities, I recommend doing them to boost points. She does her class by a 1,000 points based off system. She is intimidating.

Initially I was scared to take the finance class but she made everything so clear. Pay attention to learning catalytics and the practice long answer provided for the exam. Participate because it will really help your overall grade. Most of the time I didn't even have to read the textbook she explains it very clear. Power Points are super helpful.

Ying is one of the best instructors at the UWB Business School. I learned so much about the finance industry, and would recommend everyone to take this class with her. The class is a piece of cake if you are motivated.
she is challenging, but super nice. pay attention, PARTICIPATE!, and ask questions and you should do fine. i really enjoyed her class and i definitely learned a lot

Ying Li wasn't a bad teacher per se; she was fair and honest in grading, assignments, and generally sort of helpful, but she was terribly boring. Class was lecture only, we never had any group projects, discussion, or anything but her dry lectures. If you can sit through boring classes, she's great. Otherwise, you'll just be bored every day.

I don't understand all these low ratings. She is helpful, and really not that hard of a grader. I learned early on that reading the textbook was a waste of time. Make sure you go to lecture and understand the HW and online quizzes. The only area that she needs to work on is to be more clear about what she wants on the group research project.

She is a great profesor with a great personality, very friendly and always happy. She is always there to help. The material is not very easy but she makes it a little easy to understand but you have to study a lott. I will def take another class with her.

Great teacher. Not sure why there is so many negative ratings. BBUS 350 will help you not only get your business degree, but it will supplement your financial life. Class is straight forward. Be in class, participate, do the homework, and you'll get a 4.0.
Very hard to understand.  Confusing in delivery.  It's best to read the book and understand it than attend class.  Anonymous comments are not anonymous.
She is a very nice professor and will help you if you ask. There is a lot of group work.. make sure you have someone who is good with finance in your group or your grades would suffer.

Professor Li is a great researcher with a PhD in her pocket. Other than that she is not a teacher. She does not care much about your learning or your effort. The worst teacher I have had in my life. Simply do not spend your time and money trying to make Finance your worst enemy. This class with this professor will damage your GPA.

Professor Li was hard to understand at times due to English being her second language. The material taught in class is not what she puts on the exams so be prepared to read the text a lot. She has a variety of scarves that you will notice throughout the quarter and she is very approachable.

She seems mean in the beginning of quarter, but gets friendlier as time goes by.  Exams are open book and with notes.  Quizzes are done at home on BlackBoard.  Lots of groupwork to do.  Lectures may not be the best, so use this time wisely by reading the book or doing homework.  Attendance is mandatory, 5 unexcused absences=incomplete.

Excellent professor. This is generally considered one of the harder classes in the CSSE major, and I felt like I understood the material well and ultimately got a decent grade. She's super helpful in office hours and is usually fairly generous with homework grading.
Professor Afra is inspiring, and she cares about her students. Her lectures could be vague sometimes, but she can be available to help outside the class.

Prof Mashhadi is extremely knowledgable in machine learning and she is very good at explaining the concepts. Tests/quizzes can be difficult, due to the specificity of questions, manage your time and you will be ok. Be on time, she does not appreciate students being late. I loved learning about ML and how fairness is involved overall good experience

Afif is only grading you by a few things. Everything matters on the final due to it being 45%. Hard multiple choice questions and likes to trick you. Have the class was failing so he had to curve everyone grades. Wouldnt take ever again due to the stress of the final

How does Professor Nassif have such bad ratings? Was totally expecting him to be ranked high. Im currently taking his negotiations class and Im learning so much. I think the work he assigns is appropriate; yet, hes passionate about his lectures and teaching of skills. Definitely recommend and no he is not a tough grader, at least for this class.

we took online classes during the breakout time, in his class, I did not learn anything from him, the only thing we need to do is read the book and discuss in a group, in every class, he talk with us not more than 10 minutes. definitely do not recommend to take his online classes, and his grading is harsh, be careful and if you wann take his class.

Easy class, great professor, very little homework - 20 minutes a week. Only complaint is that some parts of his tests aren't explicitly covered in class and this class is very test heavy. Still easy to do well though.
Stay away from him. Tests are extremely difficult, requires you to memorize 8 sets of slides for the exams. Surprised that he gets to continue to teach at UWB.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not an easy Professor, he makes you work for. As long as you put an honest effort, seek him for help, youll do fine. Ask him questions during lectures & integrative cases for his feedback. Study the lecture notes (in-class notes - NOT writing slides word-for-word, online examples, etc.) after EACH lecture. These are KEY to passing his class.
Ron is one of the best teachers at UWB. His lectures are engaging and he is happy to explain concepts in different scenarios to clear up confusion. If you have the chance take him, he's the best.

Ron is extremely knowledgeable in the field of accounting. He is a caring professor and teaches accounting with enthusiasm. His tests and grading criteria aren't unreasonable, but you need to spend time and effort to get good grades. I really enjoy his teaching style, he is always helpful to students. Please do yourself a favor and take his course.

He's the best accounting prof I've ever had. He's very friendly helpful and caring about students. And he loves Costco so much. His exams are heavy but if you read textbooks/slides and study well it's possible to get A for this class. Homework is a lot and sometimes it is hard but he explains it in class. Must take his class!:)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ron is the man. The best professor I've had at UW Bothell and a genuinely kind person. He can be a tough test grader, but never unreasonable. He's always willing to help outside of class, always sharing good opportunities for careers in the accounting world. Ron loves accounting and made me love it too. Study hard, read, and go to class.

Ron is a great instructor at UW Bothell, he is enthusiastic about the course material and always helpful. As long as you do your homework and utilize the exam study guide, then you'll perform very well in his class. The case studies were a good opportunity to practice your accounting skills and learn about real world examples. Overall,Ron is great!

class was not hard with this professor because the exams were mirrors of the homework and the study guide. To succeed, ask questions, do homework, read the book or use power points and do the study guide. The case studies were easy as well.

Best teacher I've had in my college career. You show up and pay attention and you will get a good grasp of the material. If you have the opportunity to take Ron's class, do it, you will not regret it.

Great professor who knows the material very well. Very clear in delivering material. If you show up, pay attention, read and do the homework you will do very well. One of the best professors at University of Washington.
He is one of the best professors at UW. His tests are hard, but if you do the homework and pay attention in class, you will get a good grade. Everyone else at UW should have been like him.
Best college professor I've ever had. Show up, try, and pay attention and you will succeed! Need anymore be said?

Very nice person who knows how to teach! I would take all my classes with Ron. He has an amazing teaching style. He solves all possible problems, and always ready to help. Ron is an example of a perfect university professor. His tests are not easy but he teaches you very well and you are prepared to pass these tests successfully.
Great lectures. He cares about students learning. He shares his business experiences in his lectures in helpful and interesting ways.  Homework is reasonable and helpful for success in class.

He is amazing. I took 2 accounting classes with him and he made everything look so easy because he always shows examples on the board.  Tests are hard, but if you go to class and pay attention, you will do well.
Best accountingmath professor.  Funny, interesting lectures.  Very helpful with homework.  Tests are tough but fair.

Ron's the man, very helpful, receptive to feedback, will clarify anything, has great business experience, educates through personal experience, SHOWS how problems/issues are worked out . . . overall best professor at UWB

Great professor! The material can be difficult, but there is a reason accountants are paid well. He is super approachable and does a fantastic job of teaching the material in a well-understood manner.

Ron is the best teacher I've had yet. His enthusiasm for the subject and for helping students to understand it are clearly on display in the classroom. He has the ability to break down complex issues into easily digestible pieces. Study hard, it's not easy. Use his templates whenever possible. It translates into better exam scores.

Best teacher I have ever had. He knows how to explain the material very well. I would HIGHLY recommend taking a class with him...I have never met anyone that has not loved him! Be prepared to study but look forward to him making the material/class fun and intersting

Best Teacher Ever!!!!! Should be teacher of the year!!! He is very good at teaching hard difficult material!!! Knows his stuff and is ALWAYS willing to go above and beyond!!! Active in the school and professional community!! Awesome person!!! I wish he taught all accounting classes!!! Be warned, the material is hard so study accordingly...
Awesome! Best professor I?ve ever had. Gives awesome examples in class and you actually learn from his lectures. His tests are tough but if you have gone to class and done the problems its easy.

I AM an accounting student, and I agree that I'm very lucky that he'll be teaching some of my required courses. To get to the point, Ron is kind, patient, clear on what he expects from students, easy to follow during lectures, and very helpful. He also has a good sense of humor.

Probably one of the best teachers at UWB.  He is VERY PATIENT (I can't stress this enough) and helpful.  Accounting students - you are very lucky that he will be teaching the accounting courses next year and not the finance courses.

He is my favorite teacher so far.  He takes hard concepts and makes them easy.  I wish he was teaching another class I need.  He will make you love the subject whether it is Accounting, Finance or whatever.  He is very funny and cares about your learning. He is probably the best in the school. He is well like by students. Students gossip about professors, but he is 95% of the time given a positive review. He is my inspiration.

He is great.

One of the best Prof ever!! The man luvs 2 teach, u wil learn!
fabulous!

Ron has an exceptional ability to convey challenging accounting concepts to students.  He is always ready with alternate explanations and has a great sense of humor.  His tests can be difficult, but only if you don't study.  (One page of notes is always allowed.)  He truly cares about seeing his students succeed.  One of my favorite instructors!

A very devoted professor. Always has an open door if you need help in understanding your course work. Should be teacher of the year!!!!!  Wonderful professor, wish all of them were as devoted to the profession.
One of the best professors at UWB. Projects reiterate and clarifies concepts in class. Tests are straightforward and you get a page of notes.
Funny guy...extremely willing to help...not the best at explaining concepts in class but one-on-one he does a pretty good job clarifying things
Great professor! More emphasis on conceptual stuffs than how you calculate the answer. Always avaialbe to help students.  Very patient guy!

Hes nice but he doesnt know how to teach, even with a  microphone you cant hear him, he often babbles to himself for minutes trying and expects you to know everything, get ready to teach yourself all the stuff. She is a great teacher, very sweet and kind. The class has a heavy emphasis on group work but it's very easy to get a 4.0 if you show even some effort and commitment. She cares a lot about you and your learning.
Awesome teacher! She is extremely helpful and open minded. Go to her office hours because she's always there to give good advice. One of my favorite classes ever.

Professor Borsuk has been (by far) the best teacher I've taken at UWB. She's very caring and understanding of many things including student responsibilities, personal life, and self-care. Her class is very welcoming and a space for students to feel valid. Work load is fair and her grading/feedback is very considerable.

Amaranth is so kind and gives amazing feedback. I was nervous about this class as I have limited experience with poetry but she really made it as an art form feel very accessible to beginners. Shes very encouraging and understanding. Totally love her, Id take another class with her if I get the chance!

Very VERY nice teacher. She cares so much about students, and is accessible outside of the classroom for 1:1 meetings. Grades everything on completion but weights weekly assignments way more than the final. EZ 4.0 tbh.

I also took BISIA 207 with Amaranth. She is a great teacher, really cares about students' well-being, and gives good feedback on students' creative skills. In all her classes there is heavy emphasis on working with peers.

Amaranth is the BEST teacher I have ever had. She really understands students' needs and is so approachable. She's a fair grader who values effort, lets class get out early, and teaches in a way that everyone benefits. So good.

Amaranth is amazing! She is so caring and understanding with students. What I gained out of her poetry class was way more than I expected. She is not a tough grader because she values our engagement and effort.

I'm presently taking a course "team-taught" by her and two other profs. During her 3 weeks teaching us, Amaranth was excellent at making the subject matter interesting and at building a community from the class. She is also very nice and gives very helpful feedback.

I always looked forward to this class as it was the most interesting class I had that quarter. Amaranth was very kind and always encouraged group discussions and inputs from everyone. Her office hours are very helpful. She's a little slow at grading and responding to emails, but I still would've taken her class even if I knew that ahead of time.

Very sweet and kind lady and very good teacher for this class. She grades based on effort and is super flexible. She will work with you and give you lots of helpful feedback. This is a great class to take if you really want to read poetry. I like hearing the sound of her voice and her laugh. Also she's low key cute.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She is awesome! Extremely helpful and open minded. Go to her office hours because she's always there to give constructive advices. One of my favorite classes ever.
She is a nice teacher and the class is super easy. However her grading scale is completely ridiculous for how easy this class is.

Really cares about students and promotes true freedom of speech and opinion, as well as encouraging creativity and experimentation, in class. Lots of reading and long lectures but her enthusiasm and kindness make up for that. Would definitely recommend.
She's a great teacher - very kind, understanding, and sweet! She is also very knowledgeable about poetry and literature. As long as you put effort into your work you should do well.

I really liked her. Very understanding of the amount of work a student was capable of during a pandemic and gave us a pretty fair workload. Grading policy that is clear and easy to get behind, doesn't make it easy to get a poor grade. Very pleasant to listen to in class.

She's a nice lady and very accommodating/helpful, very willing to meet with students and spend extra time with them on writing assignments. During our conferences she helped me understand how I could make my writing stronger. I would definitely take another class with her.

Good teacher who works EXTREMELY hard to get people to understand poetry and the course texts. Very kind and pleasant person, and her voice is really nice to listen to, especially over Zoom after a stressful morning (her class was 11-1). I wasn't a fan of some of the material she had us read but creating my own poetry work was a load of fun to do.

Honestly one of the best professors at UWB. Lots of interesting stories and experiences to share with the class, lots of cool assignments too. Experimentation and effort are valued. Very sweet and calming presence and voice. Also how does she not have a red pepper.... saying this as a straight girl, she's very pretty and easy on the eyes.

Most IAS professors are great, but Amaranth is one of the top profs there. You should totally take her. Easy grader as long as you TRY (she appreciates effort), definitely knows what she's talking about, and makes long lectures fun. Very supportive and encouraging if you let her be that way. Also the app she designed/created, Abra, is really cool.

I really enjoyed working with her TWICE in my MFA, if only she supervised my thesis or wasn't on sabbatical this year. She was the most impactful teacher I had in grad school. Very helpful, optimistic, and encouraging, and really humorous too. She honestly works way more than she should, and really recognizes effort and interest.

Heard she's back from sabbatical, time to give my two cents. Honestly? I love her. She's a little quirky and somewhat forgetful/disorganized but she's one of the nicest people I've ever met. She is the kind of teacher who recognizes effort over quality but still grades fairly using both, so I enjoyed this class. Light workload and easy assignments.

She is a great professor and REALLY cares about students. While her lectures may get dry for those who are not as artistically inclined, her expectations and grading are very fair. I enjoy her quirky sense of humor and how that helps her be a more enthusiastic teacher.

Amaranth is rad. She is a really engaging and interesting person, and always fosters interesting class discussions. Her lectures often bring out her quirky humor - she acknowledges and embraces her nerdiness, which I love and honestly inspires me. Feedback is super specific and leads you in the right direction. Extremely kind and encouraging too.
Didn't do much in class, not the most engaged, but I still liked her as a person. I would totally take another course with her.

Amaranth is a fantastic professor. Not only have I learned so much from her, but she's extremely supportive and genuinely cares about each and every one of her students. If you see an opening in one of her classes you absolutely must jump in. You won't regret it!

Amaranth is sort of amazing. She is kind and composed even in challenging situations and really works more than she should. She is a true resource of knowledge and respects her students. This class was a great experience. UW is lucky to have her.
The most inspiring person I have ever met - cares deeply about her students and is a lot of fun to be around

Had no idea what to expect for the Clamor Literary Arts Journal club/class but it ended up being a great and easy experience. Attendance isn't always mandatory if you have a good reason for missing a class every once in awhile. Very nice professor and would take her again if I could.

Amaranth is one of the best professors ever! She cares about all her students and genuinely wants everyone to learn. She is very clear and helpful in her teaching methods. If you have the opportunity to take any of her classes, do it!
What an amazing professor!
Great teacher!

She's an amazing teacher, that truly engages her students. She is really encouraging and motivating to students. On the last day, every student wanted to say good-bye to her, and you could tell we all felt connected to her as a teacher! She's truly what a professor should be!

The readers that are assigned in this class are VERY long. She doesn't cover all of the topics in class, and likes to ramble on and on about random things. For her exams, there are a few questions which you MUST hand write (approx 7 - 9 pages). She is definitely a tough grader, and it is hard to get a 1010 on assignments.. The usual score is 810!
Readings were long, and in class she went off topic when trying to explain them. She wasn't very clear with instructions. Overall, I did terrible in this class even though I should have done better.

She assigns lengthy readings and expects you to participate in class. She wasted a lot of class time lecturing us about how we weren't doing our readings or homework on time. She was unclear on instructions for homework and the final project. Overall, a very frustrating class since she just kept going on about how we weren't working hard enough.

Doesn't give 1010 and will hardly give out a 9 no matter how good your paper is. Directions are not clear and lectures are usually random and a waste of time. 50 page reading that we didn't even touch on in class.
Honestly, you dont even have to show up to class, just do the readings and HW, take the midterm, do the final project and you'll get an A.
Very knowledgable about the topics covered in class. Always willing to help answer questions. Expects you to perform well but is a fair grader. Good at emailing you back.

You know how the best teachers want their students to succeed. This instructor is NOT that. You will get the feeling that she is looking for any random excuse to take away points. She will always comment that you didn't answer the question correctly and mark down for it. She is an extremely unfair grader. You will regret taking her class.

This professor has no regard for students time or well-being. She is a harsh grader, and frequently makes grammatical errors in her coursework. There are zero extra credit opportunities and it is like pulling teeth trying to get an answer regarding any questions for the course. Course content is minimal and useless. AVOID THIS CLASS

A lot of homework with Professor Appel, but she is great! She is extremely nice and really wants her students to do well. She is really caring and you can tell she wants you to succeed. If she was doing other health classes available, I would definitely take her again!

Prof Appel is nice but a tough grader. A lot of the assignments are busy work and busy reading. I basically took away how to just in-text cite and somewhat APA cite. Class is out of 120 pts so minimal room to make mistakes, only extra credit is up to 5 pts through WACC. Not a hard class, you just need to understand the prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's very sweet and caring! Go to her office hours for extra help and she'll help you on your paper. She can be a little picky on citations, but I learned so much from this class!

Hoa is a very good professor and has everything laid out for you. She tries to be humorous to lighten the atmosphere which is nice. Assignments and quizzes are not worth many points so make sure that you do well on them!

She's funny and super nice. Always willing to help. BUT she assigns WAY TO MUCH WORK. I had to take her for 360 as part of my BSN program requirements. Her lectures are pretty dry and hard to pay attention to and she assigns a boatload of "busy work" that arent worth that many points.
She is nice and tries to be funny. You are graded on a few assignments so make sure you do them well. We had 2 quizzes that were open book/notes
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Appel is very humorous and makes lectures very engaging. The class was out of 100 points which made it very difficult to make a mistake. Appel is very meticulous and will point out the smallest mistakes which will hurt your grade. I feel like I learned more about citing in APA format than I did a research proposal.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Shes a really nice and approachable professor. All the lecture notes are on canvas for you to look back. Exams are pretty straightforward and not hard as long as youre going through her PowerPoints. Clear grading criteria for your essay, and gives feedback on your draft to show what you need to work on. Do all the assignments, each pt counts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Class was good and everything was fair. She did grade our papers a little tough though.

I absolutely loved Hoa. She is amazing and tries to make jokes to be funny. She gives extra credit if you don't do well, but as long as you do the work, there should be no problem. The book isn't necessarily used, but she does reference it. I highly recommend her and would take her again.
great professor. Follow the guidelines, come to class prepared (watch panopto recordings), use the extra point opportunities and it won't be hard.

This is my favorite professor so far and I have been here two years. There is one paper that is split in two. There are labs, but everything is straight forward. She gives extra credit as well. I would definitely recommend her and take her again. I expect everyone in the class to get an A with how great she is.

Dr. Appel is the best teacher ever. The class was active and fun. Labs were fun to work with. Exams were straightforward;  Dr. Appel takes some questions directly from the lectures, labs, or even in-class activities. She is willing to help her students succeed, she is patient, respects all her students, and is available after class for anyone.
She is really caring and always willing to help.
She's a great professor. Her classes are very relaxed, and she's very lenient with grading, making it easy to earn credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Solid professor overall. Sporadic grading. Can grade some assignments instantly and others aren't touched until weeks later. Fun outdoor meet-ups and knowledgeable about ecology. Textbook heavy, so be prepared to write and cite. Can be difficult to reach outside of class, and more strict than other profs when it comes to late work, so be prepared.

Textbook heavy course, but involved and fun. Great if you like hands-on learning. One final exam was easy. All other assignments were participation/completion-based based pretty much. Lots of time outdoors and prof has cool experience in ecology. Can be slow to respond to emails and grade. Wish the timeline was clearer from day 1, though.

This was the first time she taught this course; it was chill. We went outside once a week. There is no hw and there is 1 final exam at the end of the quarter. Each week, a student will present a topic from textbook. If you had to present on the first week, Dr. Lambert will grade you lightly. I skipped the readings and did just fine. STUDY FOR EXAM

DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER. DO NOT. lectures go on forever and leave you even more confused. super unclear grading criteria, and then grades VERY harshly. little to no feedback is provided, and when it is, it doesnt make any sense. way too much work for an elective class. spent more time on this than classes for my major. PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF!

Really nice professor from someone needing art credit. Very interesting and hands-on going on walks learning about the land/region. About seven essays 300ish words so nothing crazy. Attendance isn't required but  makes a two hour class feel like one. Some group collaboration. extra credit through volunteering

Very unclear on what to do, an extremely harsh grader especially if she perceives that you aren't exerting enough effort into the weekly "sketches" that you need to work on and every lecture just left me confused. Also an extremely high workload for the kind of class this is.

I had to drop a class for the first time after taking BIS 319 with Prof. Lambert. Assignments are long, hard to understand, and graded very harshly. She does not have clear expectations on assignments, and does not give good feedback. Almost everyone I talked to in this class was hating it. Do not take!!
Great Class! BEES BEES BEES EVERYWHERE!
BEES! BEES! They're everywhere! BEES! BEES! So hip to FUQ BEES!

I used to be a renegade, I used to fool around. But I found I needed a science class, and had to settle down. Now I'm playing it real straight, and yes I got an A. You might think I'm crazy, but I don't even care. 'Cause I can tell what's going on.
all hail the bee queen

Great class about pollinators and their impacts on the environment. Really nice teacher. Future versions should have a movie day where we watch The Wicker Man and talk about everything wrong with the way it represents bees.

Dr. Lambert is extraordinarily knowledgeable and caring about pollinators. Mostly uses one textbook and lots of short documentaries. 3 different options for the final. Lectures were rare and not super insightful but a great opportunity to ask questions. Has a deep care for pollinator conser/reservation and if you somewhat like bees, take this class

Where do I start? She doesn't reply to emails, assigns too much homework to be done in little time, her assignments are confusing and don't make any sense. You have to ask her to clarify what she's asking multiple times to just scrape by. She grades SUPER harshly and expects you to know about restoration, even though its an introduction class.

I really enjoyed Dr. Lambert's approach to integrating arts based ecological restoration. This class is not typical of reading pdf's and answering specific questions. Her style promotes creative and unique learning approaches. Expect a fair amount of reading and a normal/consistent workload each week. She truly cares about her students as well!

I don't know where to begin. This professor is so disorganized. Lectures made no sense. She assigns WAY too much homework with little guidance. She doesn't post assignments to give us enough time to finish or add our best work and then is a tough grader. I didn't learn anything in her class because the readings made no sense and neither did she

Dr. Lambert is a fine professor to obtaingranted you do the work assigned in class. She does assign a fair amount of homework, but it is all doable within 1 to maybe MAX 3 hours. She responds to emails fast, I appreciated that the most (because sometimes her assignments can be a bit confusing).

I loved her class about pollinators. She is super knowledgeable and if you email her with a question about anything she will answer pretty quickly. This was one of the best "science" classes I have ever taken it was interesting and relevant! Her guidelines for assignments are pretty specific so just follow them and you will do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: LOVE this professor. So super sweet & caring. Very passionate about the class and pollinators. This class was so awesome learning and the work load was completely reasonable. Textbook is free online. I have enjoyed the entire quarter and I would definitely take a class from her again. Everyone should take BIS 360!!

Amy is a really interesting person and I enjoyed her lectures, but I found her assignments incredibly confusing. Her instructions are too long, I had to read everything multiple times. I lost a ton of points for missing one class due to illness. I generally felt confused most of the quarter, which is unusual for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Her class focus way too much on individual homework, instead of letting us work in groups. There are tons of reading for each week, and those are all scan PDFs so you have to really read through them, also, some of them were not scanned clearly. She also makes us do works that she doesn't grade on, tons of useless works don't really relate to class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is extremely passionate and high energy. If you have a chance to go to the San Juan's trip do it it is AMAZING (but actually participate don't just sit there). This course changed my whole quarter, you are outside learning every week. So have fun. But expect to learn a lot. Her assignments are hard but not impossible. JUST TRY YOUR HARDEST
Amy is very nice but her clarity is lacking. Tests questions are written to confuse you. High expectations with very little guidance.

I took this class b/c someone told me this was the best teacher they have had yet. Unfortunately I do not agree with this person. She wasn't bad and she is very passionate and educated. However, her grading is really tough and she sometimes is unclear with what she wants. The field trips and projects were super fun though! Not as much global warmin
Amy was one of the greatest teachers I have had. She is really inspiring and remembers her students. I will defiantly take another class of hers.
Amy is a great teacher and really knows her stuff! Some of her assignments are unclear but she'll do what she has to to help you out

Favorite class and prof so far! Amy gave clear instructions on expectations, followed the textbook, and challenged students to higher thinking to solve complex problems. The essay-exams were difficult, but manageable. My emails were promptly addressed. Amy has a wonderful, humble presence and is very passionate about restoration and teaching.

Amy truly believes in the spirit of Restoration Ecology, and you will be given a variety of unconventional learning opportunities. Some of the projects are pretty difficult, but it is a 300 level course. If you want to discover Restoration Ecology and meet interesting people, do not hesitate.

She's terrible! Unclear expectations, doesn't reply to emails, doesn't give timely feedback/grades on assignments, always ends class early, misquotes the material--I could go on and on. My biology and chemistry professors couldn't figure out what her multi-paragraph, convoluted take-home test questions were asking!

NW designation forced this art major to take environmental restoration - had to work hard on theory but in the end helped me to conceptualize narratives built around important topics.  Professor is fantastic lecturer and passionate about the topic - can't ask for more!

Amy is a wonderful teacher, full of knowledge, inspiration, and passion.  She is challenging, but in order to learn something we must be pushed outside of our comfort zone.  I have also taken her art/restoration class and the "self guided tours" the others are complaining about are because they missed class and had to go out on their own.

This class requires mandatory attendance or 10 points are deducted from your grade.Its hard to get an 4.0 in this class because she grades harsh esp at the end of the quarter. if you miss 50 you are down to a 3.8 (small margin gradeBut the most frustrating part of this class is the self-guided field trip, which takes the whole day, 4hrs of driving.

I've heard her wetland classes are great. She is knowledgeable and is overall good. I would not suggest taking her Art/Environment class because she is very unclear about her standards and expects professional photography skills from everyone. The class requires self-guided tours, one which took me 110 miles and 3.30 hrs of driving.
Great class!!!!!

Took Amy's bee class over summer. The material is fascinating even for non-science majors. If you can handle LOTS of busy work, are good at memorizing for her intense exams, and are willing to give up a few of your Saturdays for field trips then I highly recommend this class. If you are looking for an easy A...search elsewhere

I truly enjoyed the bee class and was excited about everything I learned. Although she's a bit vague with expectations and then marks you down! Her exams are really tough (8 page study guide) and the questions are super tricky.  I've heard HORROR stories about some of her other classes.  The bee class was great though! Don't shy from taking it!
This was a fun class.  It was work, but we got to go outside every day.

One of the hardest classes I have ever taken. I currently expect to fail miserably ( I will take the W). I think its fair to mention that I made the deans list the quarter before last and have been an honor roll student for years. Weekly quiz's with paragraph length questions, weekly written papers on top of large amounts of reading etc...

It was a 2 credit class and I ended up having more work than my 5 credit classes combined. Expects you to be a wetlands expert and doesn't explain any of the assignments or what she's looking for. Says in her syllabus that she will respond  to e-mails within 24 hours however I have yet to hear back from her. Absolutely horrible! Don't do it!
she is very clear, helpful. I would definitly take her class again.
Amy Lambert is very knowledgable instructor.
Great prof. Enjoyed taking her class.

I had her for Wetland Discovery and it was a pretty interesting class.  I was slightly bored at times. It was a 2CR CR/NC class and it felt more like a 5CR class.  Lots of reading. Was cool to get outside almost every class to learn about wetland on campus.

I took Amy for a 2 credit,C/NC class. She is knowledgeable and enthusiastic, but gave out too much work for 2 creds. She isn't good about getting back to students by e-mail and doesn't offer office hours. Hopefully that will change when she goes full time.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class and would recommend him as a professor. You can tell he cares about teaching and creates an environment thats easy to learn and interact in. Attendance counted for 40% of your grade so going to class really matters for his courses. There isn't homework (besides readings) so midterms and attendance define your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had mixed feelings going into this class, I was not a fan of harry potter or the constant use of AI. However, He had engaging lectures and lots of opportunities for extra credit. There is reading as homework but nothing you submit. 2 midterms and an optional final, he told us what's on the exam and lets you bring 1 page of notes. Overall great.

Very passionate and upbeat about his subject. He split the class into Hogwarts houses and had us compete in four teams through mini-essays with the class as a whole having a Harry Potter theme. No homework, only two written exams. The 2-hour lectures flew by and kept me engaged. The exam prep prompt he makes you do was identical to the exam prompt.

Made class very interesting, 2-hour lecture felt like it went very fast. No homework for SOC 201. Quizzes biweekly. The only part I wish I could change is that the study guide is class-made and prepared two days before the quizzes.

If you don't treat her like a king & and stay on her good side u will probably have the worst experience. Snarky. Inaccurately weighed my grades (had an F) until the end of quarter. I eventually had to report her to the dean.

Looking for a professor to teach you how to attain near impossible goals? Professor Ali is the professor for you. The class I took was not an easy grade, and it challenged me in ways other classes haven't, but the professor communicates after-hours and she worked with me to ensure I could succeed. She is blunt, but compassionate, and I am grateful.

awful. If you care at all about your mental health and GPA do not take this professor. She was very rude, and doesn't care about embarrassing you in front of the whole class. She threatens to fail you via email and cc's other classmates, even if you have an A.

There are 3 professors for this course and Anida is easily the worst one. She'll ask for feedback on a project, but get offended by any comment you make that isn't positive. Her tone is always confrontational, and she will never hesitate to embarrass you in class. She also likes to brag about her odd artwork for 30 minutes every class, so be ready!
She is nice but the class is somewhat hard and she can't use Canvas to save her life.

I took Prof Ali as part of a 3 professor sectioned class in BISIA 319. I was expecting a very harsh/strict prof based on reviews but found her surprisingly approachable, passionate and caring. Yes she grades harshly but I understand her reasonings for the grades that are given. Appreciated her ice breakers and her concern over an email incident.

I'm taking her Arts in Context class. Her class has helped me realize art is where I should focus my time and effort. 

It's not a difficult class. There's barely any required reading, and all we have to do is watch a weekly video and follow up with a relatively easy quiz after that.

Show up to class, participate, and you'll get an A.

This lady rubbed me the wrong way in every aspect of her and her class last fall. I could have sworn I was back in high school by the way she treated her students. There was no compromising with her. She was terrible at using Canvas. The writing assignments were ridiculous. Love how she "forgot" to grade us once.

The class was pretty straightforward and enjoyable. As long as you do the assignments and attend the classes, you will pass with an A no problem. She does call on people, so be prepared to share your thoughts.

Brings an interesting perspective to the classroom, and is somewhat "famous" for her art, but is not a very good lecturer. Class discussions are full of her opinions on everything. Not suited for online teaching at all, especially not remote learning. Seems like a tough grader but her gradescale is very easy to exploit as long as you come to class.

I have never wanted to make a rating about someone before. Shes a really tough grader its either a pass/fail even if you put a lot of work into something and get one thing wrong, the whole thing is wrong. She automatically assumes you dont do any reading or nothing outside of class. Very energetic which is good for morning, but also very rude.

Professor Ali is lowkey the gem of UWB. She's down to earth, caring but tough, is well known & respected globally for her art. Her classes can def. be difficult but they're IMMENSELY rewarding. If you care & put the effort in, listing your projects on your resume & linked in will literally bring your ranking up. This is a true Uni level art prof.

Stacks a bunch of work for her students in the last two weeks of class and expects her students to finish it all ASAP. It's like she thinks her students only have one class. Replies extremely slow to emails, so don't expect any replies from her for at least two days. Confusing directions when it comes to group projects.

She doesnt upload anything to canvas until the day before its due and still expects it to be done by the original due date. She also engages in political debates with students and pushes her political agenda upon students.
