reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She brings a lot of energy to the class

Kind but challenging. Awful lecturer, but fair grader and very helpful/supportive outside of class. Seems tough because she wants students to succeed, but to do it by taking risks, being independent, and exploring resources - INCLUDING her office hours, wheres she's actually very kind. I honestly think I became a better person thanks to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's not cruel or mean like the previous reviews say. Yes, she's extremely strict and very direct, but it's actually a really rewarding experience cause she's trying to teach you how the world works in her own weird way. She's like that because she wants to help you reach your potential IN class, while being extremely approachable OUTSIDE class.

She's the only professor who ever screamed at me or told me I had no talent. Very conceited too, because she doesn't listen to her students and values what she thinks and says more than anyone else. She is not flexible at all, either, and assignments are never "good enough" for her while her teaching style is all over the place.

Anida is awesome. While she is a difficult grader at times, it's because she's trying to motivate students and inspire them to take more creative risks and do better. She's a terrific performer and artist, and hopes to inspire that into students as well, and she's a very kind and supportive person. Definitely one of my favorite classes so far.

Took a performance art class with her and the first few weeks was spent wasted on lectures instead of preparing, causing us to set up late. Very tough and has no communication skills. Made a lot of the students do the work while she just sat and critiqued. Very passionate but hypocritical and will yell at you in front of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not my favorite professor, I mean she is very passionate with the subject and she'd good at it. But the grading is just.. off. She said she grades on effort, that's somewhat true, but also she can just mark you down for no reason. Unless you are really passionate in the subject like her, then I can't recommend this class.

My first quarter at UWB and taking her course was definitely the best choice I could have ever made. She really motivates you to think outside the box and be comfortable with your own opinions and beliefs. We did a lot of group work and activities. DON'T SKIP, you wont pass if you do and her class is seriously worth going to and keeping up with.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Would take again

reviews.comment: Caring teacher, and a respectable background. She's a different professor and grades pretty much on effort. She stresses artistic risk. Group projects aren't difficult. Lots of extra credit opportunities. She also does a few lectures, but lets just say that isn't her strong suit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's an artist. She's different, she wants a lot of thought, sharing ideas, people to get out of their comfort zone. She's very lively. Projects have the option of groups or alone. Project require a lot of work. I learned a lot more than expected. A lot about the world. She specializes in installation and performance art.  Good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is great overall, but Professor Anderson's grading does not align with the expectations of a 100-level course. Additionally, grading turnaround times are long, which negatively impacts performance on future assignments.

He didn't grade some assignments for a while so I didn't get feedback on them until after I turned the next assignment in, which would then effect my grade on the next assignment due to not knowing how I did. He grades pretty harsh so you have to be really specific with including everything he wants, even if it seems like you already did.

Professor Anderson is a great professor! He is VERY kind and understanding. He wants to see his students succeed and will support you. His assignments were very fun to do, I oddly looked forward to doing them. Great teacher and class set up. I def recommend

I've never had a professor who's been able to make an asynchronous online course as engaging as Professor Anderson. He is passionate about what he teaches and very understanding. It's clear he cares about his students and he wants them all to succeed!

Prof.Anderson's class was very easy to keep up with especially with the asynchronous online part. All the assignments were interesting and fun to read about, and the final paper was just going around and about a specific topic that interested us during the quarter. Very easy A if you have tougher classes to keep up with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Very engaging and interesting online class, also very easy. Christian is willing to help you with LITERALLY ANYTHING. He reminds me of Hank Green.

This professor gives more than enough time and heads-ups for their big final homework assignment-which is nice. One of the easiest classes I had this quarter, which made working 2 jobs and traveling mid-quarter for competitions really smooth. The professor is super enthusiastic about maps, and his lectures give "fun with flags" vibes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Online asynchronous course. Very friendly and engaging teacher, no useless busy work. Easy to contact and set up a meeting, especially online. I'd take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor for human geography. Accessible outside of class and also not too difficult to understand what he wants. Gives a lot of feedback on the assignments you do; he is really passionate about what he teaches. For this class specifically, there is a lot of online work. Quizzes every two weeks or so, but the lowest two get dropped. Goated
Worse Professor

I've taken 3 classes with Christian and each one has been amazing. He is a great professor and person, he cares about what he does, but more importantly he cares about his students. Thank your lucky stars if you are lucky enough to take even one class he teaches. He will go the extra mile to make sure everyone learns and enjoys learning.

Very clear and effective teaching style. He cares a lot about students, is very funny, and provides useful examples of what you are learning in class. Readings are interesting. If I see another class he's teaching, I'll take it immediately.

Took for an elective, and it was awesome. Interesting class content, clear and fair assignments and grading, and Prof. Anderson was hilarious and really inspired everyone to pay attention and participate. Only downside was there was a lot of reading.

Absolutely the best professor I have had and that's saying a lot considering this was an online course. Professor Anderson's class was challenging in the right sort of way. There really wasn't a downside to the class. All of the material was interesting and he was extremely clear about expectations.

Christian is the best! He's so smart and funny. He obviously really loves teaching. Readings can be hard but he always goes over them in class. He is really helpful in class, always willing to answer questions, and NEVER boring. This is the third class I took with him.

He is so nice and helpful, and kind of a dilf tbh. Easygoing, accepts homework late and is pretty lenient, but the feedback on assignments is really helpful and he's very responsive to emails and office hour requests! He makes the class interesting and definitely delivers in that sense.

The Prof really cares what he's teaching and wants us to succeed. Felt the class was paced well and the work we did actually had purpose! Gives lots of feedback on assignments and cares more about what you learn on the material at your own pace. Weekly assignments/readings. A fun/easy going professor that responds to emails pretty consistently.
He's confusing on his instructions and what he wants, but he is an easy professor to take nonetheless.

Christian is pretty chill and has a really good sense of humor. I learned a lot mainly from his lectures and actually doing the assignments rather than just listening to his explanations. Easy and interesting class.
Amazing Professor. It is easy to do well in his class. He really cares about students!

His cultural research 340 class from last winter quarter was amazing. Great examples given and great skills learned. It's certainly best to attend every lecture if you want to do well on the assignments. He's a nice guy and very uniquely funny and energetic, like the other reviews say.

He is a great lecturer, he is very animated and interesting to listen to. The material can be boring at times, but he is very helpful and very welcoming to questions and concerns. He always takes the time to listen to what his students have to say. I would highly recommend taking a class from him.

Christian is a sweet teacher who genuinely cares about your success in class and the way you engage with the material. He's always very excited about the content and gives great lectures. This class is easy but you still have to do the work. Attendance isn't required (I took it on Zoom) but it's worth it because his lectures are seriously awesome.

Lectures are great and he really is hilarious, and there was no confusion on what we were learning. The class is more practical than it seems at times, with the writing and research skills gained. He has really open office hours if you need help. DO THE COURSE EVALUATION for extra credit. Made online learning fun.

Anderson has a uniquely energetic and casual teaching style. Really funny guy and cares about students' needs. Readings are sometimes long, but interesting not too difficult. Work supports class concepts with usable, transferrable skills in writing and research. Class was well-organized and the work is distributed evenly across the quarter.

Highly recommend his 340 class especially if you are an IAS major who needs a Methods course. There is a lot of reading but besides that the class is easy as long as you keep up with the work. Dr. Anderson is very open minded and willing to work with you and help you if you need it, and has really good lectures that make you not want to skip.

This class is super easy as long as you put in some effort and complete the weekly writing assignments, almost all of which lead up to the final paper. He's a nice, funny guy and has very insightful lectures. He's super approachable and can and will help you with just about anything.

Among the top professors here. He's pretty lax on grading/requirements and basically guarantees you an A if you show effort, plus his feedback is helpful for building some skills in writing. Really nice and funny guy too. Wish more students, especially first-years, knew about him. Not a hard class if you participate and do the work.

Anderson is an amazing professor who's obviously invested in his subject which makes his lectures more interesting. He responds to emails quickly, can make time to meet with you, and gives really helpful feedback while being an easy enough grader. As long as you keep up with the readings and assignments you'll do well in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Anderson as the second highest-rated prof in all of UWB on this site? I love democracy! Cultural research with him was the BEST class I've taken. He teaches a much more progressive and relevant version of what you'd consider "research" methods in interdisciplinary studies, and is super passionate about working with students.

Very friendly teacher. He was always excited and energetic during class. The class is easy IF you attend lectures because he helps guide you through the work. The final project was really fun and I like how self-directed he made it.

I wish there was a 6/5 rating because he was the professor who made me love UW Bothell. He offers really interesting readings and assignments in his classes, and is really funny. Lectures really well. I also took BIS 318 (self and society) with him.

He really cares about students learning and succeeding. He is funny too. He offers to help with all work and understands when there are personal issues that come up to impede your progress. The readings were interesting and I liked the way he both lectured about them and facilitated discussions! Would definitely take him again for another class!

Nice and easygoing teacher. Always answers emails quickly. Willing to make time for you if you can't make office hours but need help. Very clear, organized, and straightforward. Class structure was very easy to follow. Gives really good feedback on work. I would highly recommend Christian, I really enjoyed his class.
Excellent teacher. He cares about effort and how much you participate, makes the class feel comfortable with his jokes and smiles, and gives really interesting reading material and assignments.

HE IS AMAZING! He's adorable and really funny! There is a lot of writing but its super chill. Weekly discussion posts on Canvas that you have to do. Random class activities that count towards participation so it helps to come to class. I would take him again. Really quick at grading/email responses and gives really thorough feedback!

Super nice guy, you can tell how much he loves what he's teaching and values the students who take his classes. He was my first class of the day and I loved starting my days with his class. His passion and knowledge are very refreshing. Definitely a teacher I'd recommend!

This class is really easy because of how interesting and straightforward it is. The readings aren't too hard, the assignments all make sense in the broader context of the class, and Christian himself is amazing at giving lectures and helping us learn -- he really cares about his job and just has a great attitude. Also there's a lot of extra credit.

I really liked Professor Anderson. His lectures were very informative and the class was not hard. When you had questions about upcoming activities and assignments he would be very clear and specific. He cares a lot about student learning and is always very interested in the topics he teaches. Zoom chat always pops off and it's the best experience.

Christian is the teacher who made me like IAS. This class material was brilliant, and Christian has a good sense of humor, a lot of knowledge on the subject (cultural/humanities research), and a very relatable, open-minded style of instruction. Gives a lot of feedback on assignments.

Easily one of my favorite professors. He's funny, incredibly passionate, and the class material is well-presented and very interesting. Homework is not very heavy but the final research proposal can get hard if you don't stay on top of things.

Prof. Anderson is a really chill and friendly guy. Just show up to class, do the readings, and try your hardest on the homework and you'll do well. This class is basically a higher-level/more advanced version of UWB's intro research writing class focused specifically on research in the humanities.

A teacher should be someone open to new ideas and a diverse array of opinions and students, and Christian was the most open-minded teacher I have ever had, and is also funny, which must be why he's a popular teacher. So glad to have met him my first quarter at UWB, he's made a really big impact on where I want to go academically and professionally.

This teacher explains every single detail and does not get mad if you ask questions. He's genuinely a great teacher and person, and I would take him again in a heartbeat. He lectures and we do group activities at the end of the lecture so you do need to be present for class. The final research proposal and everything leading up to it were very fun.

Christian is by far one of the best IAS professors I have come across in my 2 years at UWB. He models good citizenship and caring for others and encourages students to explore various online resources to support their learning. He was always very lively in class and you could tell he loved teaching us. Attendance is a BIG part of your grade.

Christian is very nice, caring, funny, and really passionate about his subject. This class definitely was overwhelming with the amount of reading and writing, but we always - ALWAYS - went over them in class which really helps. He gives really good feedback on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson grades very easily and is really more concerned that you're participating and putting in effort. Class sessions were lectures mixed with discussions on the readings and assignments. He's very helpful and communicates quickly and clearly, which I really appreciated after quarters of s*tty professors.

This is my first quarter at UWB, and it was so pleasant to have Christian as a professor. He explains complex academic concepts in a way that makes them seem simple and is really funny. He always responds to emails. The final assignment is a research paper worth a big amount of your grade but it's graded somewhat leniently.

I loved Prof. Anderson and will be taking a class from him again next quarter because of that. Lectures were very interesting and his expectations were very clear. Very accessible in office hours. Not an easy class necessarily (lots of reading and writing), but it was fairly easy to do well. He's really funny too.

This class is fantastic! Christian will often change things up if things get dull or tedious in order to generate interesting conversations. He's seriously so nice and cares a lot, really funny, and always gets so happy when teaching which is refreshing after quarters of bad teachers. Do the work, participate, and you will do well!

This class has been phenomenal. "Dr." Christian Anderson (he jokes all the time that he's "not a real doctor") makes the complexity and dullness of research exciting and engaging with his jokes and student-centered way of teaching. You would be doing yourself a disservice by not taking any of his classes if you're even remotely interested in them.

Just a really nice guy in general. Very knowledgeable and gives really thorough feedback when grading. Assignments are relevant to the real world, and the final (research proposal) is very open-ended which is nice. Lectures can feel long sometimes but he always finds ways to make them engaging. There's extra credit in this specific class, too.

Christian is hands down the best professor I've had at UWB. He's very enthusiastic and will answer any questions you may have. Very clear about guidelines for assignments and grading. I learned more in his class than I have in any other - you don't just learn about research but about how you are affected by it. I'd take any other class he teaches.

Christian was great! The Canvas modules are a super helpful and organized way to learn and pace yourself, and they excellent job of making you think critically about the concepts from class. His feedback is very helpful at deciding next steps, and the final is built up from all the previous homeworks. Also a very kind and caring person.

Professor Anderson was an amazing teacher. I am glad to have taken Cultural Research with him. He was really helpful and understandable, really funny, and worked so hard to make sure we understood the material. I recommend taking any course he teaches, and would love to take another with him.

Christian is one of the best IAS professors out there. Very nice and VERY knowledgeable, and makes complex things easy to understand. Not a hard grader, really understanding and accommodating during COVID, and just a good person all around. Connects class readings to a lot of current events and encourages students to learn more about them.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is awesome! Super fun and interesting class with guest speakers and assignments that really impacted both us and those around us. He is also very passionate about his work. Definitely expect to come to class though, it's not a class you can skip a lot of - and not really that hard elsewhere. I highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Christian Anderson is the best professor at UWB. Hands down. Only prof I have had 0 complaints about. Strongly stands by his belief of student-centered learning and student success, which is honestly really refreshing. Very clear expectations, very good feedback on assignments, very supportive, and incredibly legible handwriting, which is a plus.

Love this prof! Workload is very manageable. There are weekly discussion posts and reading reflections plus one project that is spaced out over the quarter. On the discussion post and reading reflections, as long as you answered every question he asks, you will surely get full points. Very student-centered class. Cares a lot about our learning.

Great class! Christian is a great teacher. He made everything incredibly clear, and the readings he chose are super relevant. He cares about your learning and is always there for you when you need him to be! Responds incredibly quickly to emails.

Fantastic teacher, you can tell that he really loves the subjects he teaches! Also, he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Lots of reading homework for this class, but none of it is busywork: all assigned readings (as well as all of the suggested supplemental readings) are useful for learning and completing the work.

Love Christian. He is a very kind and intelligent teacher. If research is your thing definitely take this class. If not, you might be bored. He gives great feedback, and is well versed in geography, sociology, and health studies. Work isn't heavy but the readings can get annoying because of how many there are. Very helpful and accessible.

Highly knowledgeable on the subject of cultural research, as broad a topic as it is, and has a unique approach to teaching that is more stimulating than the typical "lecture and you're done" type of class. Very fun in-class and outside activities and assignments are meaningful. Advocates for your learning. You won't regret taking a class with him.

Best teacher ever! Very invested in his students' success, both in his class and in their degree work. No textbook to purchase, he provides all the reading materials. Show up, do the readings, put thought into your responses, interact with other students during class, and you'll do just fine.

Not super hard - 2-3 articles to be read each day and reading responses assigned, and the topics are interesting enough to be enjoyed. Not a mind blowing class, but still pretty good. He is really funny, which is nice because it also helps him connect with students (something he REALLY wants to do) better. Very responsive to emails.

Christian is fantastic! He clearly enjoys what he does and is always more than happy to help you. The passion shows in his teaching and the way he uses his knowledge. I've taken 2 classes with him now (BISCLA 318 2 years ago and BIS 340 2 quarters ago) and I've loved both of them, gotten a 4.0 both times. Highly recommend.

Christian is one of the best professors at UWB. He is engaging and interesting. He fosters interesting class discussions and brings out his "adorkable" humor - acknowledging his own nerdiness. His feedback is super specific and leads you in the direction he wants to see next. Extremely encouraging and supportive. Take every class he offers!
Take every class from this man that you possibly can. But, seriously though, get ready to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Always wants to make sure students understand the material and is very willing to help outside of class. The final project was difficult to understand at first, but eventually everything came together. As long as you show him that you're trying, show up to class, and do your best, you'll get a good grade. By far the best professor I've had so far
Great professor.  It was very easy to pay attention in his class.
Immediately caught my attention - he has a passion for what he is teaching, causing me to become motivated and interested.

Christian was awesome. He is very friendly & overall an easy grader. Wish it would have been an online class, because the layout of the material could've been taught online. I would take him again! Your grade on canvas doesn't show anything about participation, but you will get docked big time points.
BIS 300 is a required course for IAS students. His class is based off of the City. His emails are rude and so is his feedback. He doesn't explain assignments well and just kind of leaves you hangin.
He is very animated and clearly cares for the subject.

Dr. Dre is the best prof ive had for finance! She allows notes on all exams, and her homework and course packets are extremely helpful. As long as u study the hw and packets, you will do just fine. I def had to put in the work/studying, but got a 4.0. She says u have to do the readings, but I did just fine without. TAKE HER!!

She's the best of the best! Her course packets are so useful. You can spend hours reading a textbook and not understand. However, she explains everything in such an easy way, it clicks right away. Definitely do not recommend skipping class as her lectures are amazing. Best finance professor out there. I always look forward to her classes.
Professor is almost never available outside office hours in cases of conflicting schedules. Not an understanding professor and is new. Don't take her classes.

Tests aren't relevant to what you learn. Only to some degree. Two group projects aren't too bad, but the tests are horrible:( Doesn't keep things organized, gives you a lot of material to study that overwhelms you. Like I studied around 20 hours a week and still got C+ on the Midterm.

This professor is freaking horrible. I don't know how she has a job at this school honestly. Her class is one of the worst experiences I have ever had in my life. Her tests are extremely hard and just do not really reflect what you have learned in the class. Take a different teacher please it'll be the best thing you do.

Very organized professor! She knows exactly what she is talking about, and doesn't waste any of our lecture time. Her lectures are straight to the point and engaging as there her course packets help you follow along. I have taken two classes from her already and would highly recommend her.

This is her first quarter teaching 451 so she did not have a practice midterm/final like her 350 class. Extremely passionate about students' career development. Utilizes course packets for students so it's easy to follow along. As a finance major, I plan to take most of my core classes with her if I can. Easy to contact for office hours too.

Truly cares for your success and will provide you with career help! Extremely organized, uses course packets. For my class it was online so open note/open book which made the midterm and final pretty easy. Homework is also manageable, just do it on time. Lots of additional videos and resources too if needed. Highly recommend Dr. Dre for 350.

One of the best teachers I've had at UW. I took another class just because she was teaching it. Her lectures are very organized and course packets are very helpful. Exams are so easy if you just show up to class and listen. I wish she taught all of my classes.

Relatively new to UWB and excited to take her class again. She gives out course packets where you can learn the content and practice it with her in class. Her projects seem daunting but she gives instructions every step of the way. One of my favorite professors!

Her instructions for projects are vague. If you try to get ahold of her to answer a specific question, she either responds with more ambiguity or adds more useless content to the already confusing question.
Professor Anthony is great

Professor Andrea was super tough. Hated the group project bc everyone gets the same grade, so you need to watch out for the rest of the team doing their parts right. The midterm was ridiculously hard, and not enough time. The homeworks are super long, you get 2 tries to get the correct answer. Prof Never answers emails/canvas messages either.

I cannot recommend her enough! I'm not really good at math and was really worried about this class, but prof. Anthony is hands down one of the best teachers. She is extremely clear, what you see is what you'll see in the exams (note sheet allowed), and makes everything interesting! She made me love finance, no joke haha

You do have to pay extra for her class though (textbook & calculator). Andrea is definitely passionate/knowledgeable about what she teaches and it clearly shows, class is structured super well. Was not a fan of the course packets though. No quizzes. Midterm/Final, but not cumulative, you get cheat sheet. Easy to get a good grade if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I don't see why she has bad ratings. She allows you to use a equation sheet on the mid-term and final exam. Final exam is not cumulative, and she really knows what she is talking about. Teaching style is very good and clear, and she really wants you to learn. I would highly recommend taking this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is ridiculous. Professor A has no idea what she is talking about half the time, and does not respond on canvas. She rarely gives feedback. Avoid at all costs
she's a great professor however I didn't like the project. Make sure you attend  and watch her zoom the classes most of the exams questions are things she teaches in class

I just don't get why she shows us the answers to the course packet rather than showing us how to do it. I've also read other reviews saying you have to buy extra course material, and I can confirm it's true. Unless you have a TIBAII Plus, you're looking at around maybe an extra $75-100 including Pearson MyLab. However, there is lots of extra Credit
Great teaching! The material is tough especially the second part. Find it interesting. The exams are hard but worth it!
Watch out! You will need to pay around $100-150 of additional material! Otherwise, decent professor. The class goes really fast though.

Very nice person! However, the lectures are poorly conducted. Rather than showing you how to do the work, she lazily goes through a completed course packet. Midterm mean score was 70%. Tests are very long and unbalanced. She also has students spend around $120 of additional course material. It's just not practical. Wouldn't recommend her

She is a nice teacher, but she moves WAY TOO FAST during her lectures. Spring 2022 the midterm average score was 77%, with 8 students getting 60 or lower. She's mentioned that students have a history of having a hard time on her tests (maybe the test scores might reflect the quality of her lecturing and teaching?) Take a different teacher for 350.

454 Investments. A very difficult online class with few lectures. Punished for not understanding material right away with zero instruction and 2 homework chances. Entirely self-taught.  Took with another professor who explains things and has lecture materials, did much better. Fine for 350, don't recommend for fully online courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was a pretty tough class, but Dr. Anthony was really good. Probably the best Finance Professor at UWB. Weekly Homework, recommend getting a headstart on those. Midterm and Final. Pretty hefty group project where formatting and visuals are imperative. Extra credit opportunities and attendance are mandatory. The class overall is fantastic!

Professor Anthony's class so far is going great! Her lectures are engaging and exciting. She does a great job with making her PPT easy to understand and adds fun facts to a lot of the slides related to course material. The examples she uses relates to the real market. There is a lot of Homework but it really helps you learn the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Amazing and very kind professor. She loves to teach and is really helpful if you have questions. She has a really unique interactive assignment, which is actually really fun. If you read and pay attention, tests are easy. Very understanding if you miss class. Overall amazing professor and very sweet.

Overall, this class is pretty easy, but the tests can be a little tricky. The exam questions don't always line up directly with what's emphasized in the lectures, so make sure you watch all of her videos. There is one midterm, one final, and a group final. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are in class group assignments for points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: one of the best professors I've had so far. she actually cares about the material, like a lot and really wants to help you understand. she has 2 kids so prolly why she understands how to help so well. mon. are lecture days and wed. is lab day. lab day is super chill and you can work with others and she wants you to get 100% on it so ask for help.

Great professor. Just make sure to attend class and study in a timely-manner. Her wording on quizzes & tests can be tricky, but overall she is very helpful and efficient with communicating to students.

Class is easy. I only read the first two chapters of the textbook and stopped because the quizzes are based off of her lectures. Every Wednesday, it is lab day; you use and excel program or use equations to fill our the packet/ worksheet. If you don't finish it in class, then it is homework (which isn't due until Monday).

Professor Stone is by far my favorite professor I've had. She is so helpful and a very good teacher. I took statistics with her and I have never been good at math, but she definitely made it understandable. I really want to take her class again. She can be a bit slow at grading and giving back labs, but if you ask her for it she will give it to you
Best professor at UWB, hands down!
A great class. Now one of my favorite professors at UWB! Love her energy!! Overall pretty easy class.
Drugs and Alcohol Dependence class. Interesting class and lectures. Work is not difficult at all. She's fun and super enthusiastic about the topic.
Her class is not that hard if u do all the work and be there every time.  She knows how to teach!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Highly recommend. Was dreading statistics but I ended up enjoying it. Very helpful and genuinely cares about students.
GREAT TEACHER! Makes sure everyone gets it before moving on.  Will stay after class and go over things again to make sure you get them. Very likable women, genuinely wants students to do well.
Good class although it was boring at times.  Andrea is a great professor and is willing to provide assistance when needed.
Her classes are fun, easy, and interesting.

by far my favorite professor. she is so understanding and makes the student her number one priority. she is just so genuine and I cannot recommend her enough..she makes you want to attend class and learn more. take her class you will be so glad you did!!!!!

Professor Stone is one of the best teachers that UWB could have!! Not only does she take her time to make sure that the entire class understand the subject, but she does so in a clear and polite manner. If you need to take BIS312, take it from her, NOT FROM CARLISLE.
Prof. Stone is really energetic and tries incredibly hard to make her lectures clear and easily absorbed. It upsets me that some students have taken advantage of her polite nature, though.

She did a great job at trying to make statics fun, but being in a computer room just didn't make sense. However the new class I am in with her rocks.  She lets you know exactly what is expected of you and works off a straight 100 point class.
Professor Lo is one of the first professors who seemed to care for her students. Her lectures are a little bit hard to grasp but her homework assignments really taught me a lot.

Professor Lo was really great! She definitely cares for her students and wants everyone to succeed. She is very blunt when it comes to your work but it helps you learn. You were allowed to resubmit any assignment if you up until the end of the quarter if you wanted to receive a better grade. tests are multiple choice based on textbook.

I don't really take the time to rate professors, but Lo is by far the absolute best professor I have ever had. Even after taking her class and parting ways, she's still advocating for me. Put in the effort into her class, show her you're motivated, and you'll have someone in your corner for years to come.

Pretty easy class. Only had to show up a few times for group presentations, but otherwise everything is online and very easy. the midterm and final you can use a sheet of notes. i will say she is not a great lecturer. really rambles on and isn't very clear. but, the course overall was organized and clear. Pearson is used for all assignments.

She is all over the place with information, you can't understand what she is saying. When you ask for help she doesn't answer your question or give you feedback on what to improve on. She always compares her students to HS students and that we aren't "smart" enough. She doesn't respond to her emails and states that she is to busy.

Alison is all over the place. I'm not sure if I learned anything new from her class. Most of her lectures were either about data analysisstats or stuff we'd learned about from Managerial Econ. Most of the class pertained to a book you chose and was group work. That being said, it was a really easy 4.0. It just felt like a waste of time often.

THICK accent. She doesn't really talk to the class during her lectures (which don't even matter because there aren't tests or quizzes, or anything pertaining to them). Class is basically group work and two individual case studies. Final is extra credit. By far the easiest teacher  class ever.

I am not particularly interested in marketing but found the first half of her class very interesting. After she introduced R Studio, it all went down hill. The lectures were very boring and she bounced all over the place. She gives you an option of what book to buy and the final exam is optional so passing is easy but curve is high.

Professor Lo is extremely helpful, friendly, and enthusiastic. Although some may argue that is is difficult to understand, she makes perfect sense and those students saying otherwise have not been exposed to asian accents. She is extremely flexible and understanding with your groups and provides frequent and helpful feedback. Take her course!!

She is very hard to listen to when she lectures. She has a hard accent, gets off topic, and  has difficulty explaining something when someone asks a question. She offers help, but again is not good at explaining things. Do the readings to learn it on your own.

She is extremely intelligent and help the learner understand WAY beyond the boring textbook. She makes marketing interesting (I was very disinterested before taking her class) and includes interesting statistics in her class. She also is looking out for the student's career possibilities and understands real world challenges.

A fabulous teacher! She recommends many non-textbook reading materials for in depth understanding without the dry tinge of academic materials. I'd never considered marketing as a potential career, and she managed to capture enough of my imagination with her enthusiasm to consider it.
boring and a hard grader. exams are 80% lectures/ 20% book. worst teacher ever as she rushes through every topic. steer clear away!!
Hard teacher. Pretty boring and repetitive. Doesn't like getting to the point and goes on many tangents.

she made the only exam really hard just to prove that we were not as good as MIT or Duke University students.  Overall, though this was an easy class because we asked for a lot of her input for our project so of course it turned out great.  we did everything she told us do!  You just have to pay attention and participate.
Great professor. She really challenges her students.  Be prepared to work hard.  She has high expectations of her students but tries to make sure everyone understands the material.

She's not an absolute horrible teacher, but if you didn't take her BBUS320 class, then don't bother taking anything else with her. She constantly reminds you how you're at a disadvantage to her other students since you have never taken her and when you don't get as good of a grade as her other students, she'll remind you again. She holds her class

Alison is a tough teacher and the work load in the class is probably more than a five credit class should have.  That said, she's a wonderful teacher who adds tons of content outside of the text book to peak student's interest in marketing.  She's very passionate about her subject and it's catching.

Liked the class and learned a lot about marketing. She will help students out if they need it. She grades hard but has high standards for students at the University level. Read the book, take notes, and ask questions before, after, or during her office hours if needed and you'll do fine. You get great marketing knowledge from this class.
This teacher has too many favorites and did a horrible job of grading based on actual work.
I like the course and Alison a lot. especially the interesting materials that you don't find in the textbook.

Steer clear of Lo when possible. Arbitrary grading and superiority complex. Too many comments about how dumb the kids are at UWB. Word currently around campus is not good, ask around! I promise it will save you a lot of trouble.
I enjoyed this course a lot! I never thought marketing is so interesting.
Alison's exams are difficult.  But if you pay attention, study her notes and study the text book, you should do well. I enjoyed her class!

Ms. Lo is very smart, and I think has a lot to offer to her students. However, the group project was only worth one test grade, but was several hours worth of work, and stress. The project was much more trouble than it was worth.
Took marketing research last quarter. She wrote me a recommendation letter that got me into my #1 choice graduate program. I saw the letter and I thank her SO MUCH.
a lot of work. I like the readings and the project. Kind and willing to help when needed.

Prof. Alison doesn't do a good job with explaining material. She likes to give tons of print outs with information that is not in the book. Tests are hard because she doesn't contribute to comprehension of the material and her requirements are high.
Very kind and passionate professor
Excellent professor, I would take it again if I have the chance. Strong Recommend. Fair Grading.

-Annotations assignments (movies and readings, on things that stood out + agree/disagree with, can be submitted up to 2 weeks post-deadline)
-2 exams (written)
-Extra credit (time stamps for theme + short answer for justification)
-Group presentation
-Class participation (do assignments in-class and online)

Truly one of the worst educators ever. She is extremely unorganized, and she simply doesn't care about her students. Good luck trying to send her an email, or 3; she will never respond or help you when you ask. Just showing up to class once a week was a struggle for me; I dreaded sitting there for two hours while she read off her useless slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: I just finished a Gender and Human Rights class with Dr. Kurian and I am amazed at how much care, preparation, and research goes into her classes. My three favorite things about her teaching style is that she keeps herself well-read to enhance class discussions, her grading criteria is crystal clear, and she gives great feedback on questions.

Go and register for her class asap! One of the most engaging professors I have had. I have really short span of attention but it did not budge in her discussions. She does not lecture. Her class was all about discussions.

I very much enjoyed having Dr.Kurian for several courses for Women, Gender and Sexuality Studies. She also wrote my letter of recommendation for grad school. She is very kind and truly cares about her students. She celebrates diverse perspectives, experiences and voices in and outside her classroom.

Professor Kurian is one of the best professors you could ever learn from. She truly cares about the material, and she teaches in a manner that is engaging and insightful. She also cares a lot about her students success, and she will always take the time to help you if you are struggling with the material, or if you need some extra guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a strong lecturer, very caring and accommodating. I learned a lot about different identities in her class. Honestly, I feel like there were a lot of people who were mean to her in/out of class and I seriously can't imagine any other reason than her being an Indian woman with an accent. It sucks that people berate her for just doing her job.

The reading amount is ridiculous for a 100 level course and most of them are boring. The class is her talking all the time and often start to bother you when you zone out a bit. Not caring and respect at all. Late work get deducted heavily and the final reflection assignment miss will significantly impact your grade. TRY TO AVOID HER IF YOU CAN.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took BISGWS 301, I really enjoyed Professor Kurian's lectures, there's a lot of in class discussions (not mandatory to speak unless its group discussions). There's weekly (long) readings that you annotate once each page, and a 10-15 min group presentation. It's a lot of heavy thinking but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lack of control in her classrooms makes it feel like the students are teaching not her, we are paying tuition to have her teach and not our peers. She also has really ambiguous wording on her quiz and exam questions making it difficult to answer and she only looks answers worded in the way she would word it herself which seems completely unfair.

The prof originally had a very unreasonable reading requirement of 2 annotations per page. Upon students emailing her requesting to reduce the workload she brought it down to 1 annotation per page. This alone made the course MUCH better and enjoyable.

Her class is discussion based but She wants to discuss alot of issues without offending people which isnt really possible. She makes things super complicated when they are not complicated.I had a major career thing clashing w final exam and she was super un-supportive about it and kept like delaying her response to me  which i found annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: attendance matters! she'll basically ask you to turn in a piece of paper at the end of every class to ensure you were there--it's counted as "class participation," which is worth 20% of your grade!!!!! so stupid considering that quizzes/tests are just 5% more at 25%.
she is nice and her lecture is usually her walking around and classroom discussions.
A really easy professor, at least for BIS 164 which wasn't listed here. Easy grader, just required 2 short stories being read and discussion board posts. Very simple class

Professor Kurian is very nice but her lectures were a bit dull. There is a group presentation in front of the class at the end. You will also be called to speak randomly in classes so if you are shy, this might not be the class for you. Overall, the movies you watch are interesting and the assignments aren't too bad. mainly a discussion class

Take this class from this professor and you will be glad you did. Prof. Kurian knows her stuff. One of the best classes I've ever taken. Professor Kurian is also very nice and easy to work with if you need any help. Just ask...

Alka is a very nice woman. The main problem that I have with her class is that it is extremely disorganized. She'll give you a 9/10 on an assignment with no feedback explaining why you missed the last point. This class is very activity-based and no one understands any of the in-class (or online) activities because she doesn't explain them.

Professor Kurian is one of the sweetest teachers I've ever had. She does an awesome job getting students engaged in the class, and is super receptive of feedback and really wants everyone to pass. I would absolutely recommend this class!

Professor Kurian is amazing, I took her BIS300 class in the fall quarter and honestly, she was so understanding and sweet. Offered extra credit to the students and it was a fun extra credit event too, helps with problems and is very knowledgable about what she's teaching. Also loves to let the students engage each other, instead of long lectures.

She is a nice person. EZ course works. I told her I was sick at presentation day. She just give me full points with it. But she is kinda tough to grade. I submit all assignments and going class everyday only got 2.5 gpa. two exams were kinda hard to international students.

She is an amazing person and very intelligent, gives great lectures but I would say unorganized when it comes to her class and unclear about a lot of assignments. Prompts were very confusing. Overall, would still highly recommend.

LOVED this course, and the professor is helpful, understanding, funny, flexible and keeps the class interesting. I highly recommend to take this class. However, you absolutely need to attend class and do the participation exercises to get the benefit of it

I took three of Alka's classes. Since her background is very diverse her classes are going to be mostly critical thinking oriented. Lots of Q&A. She assigns many scholarly article readings from scholars from South America, Asia, Middle East as well as Europe which enabled me to hear different perspectives and ideologies. I loved it!

I love Alka she was one of my favorite professors at UWB. Truly caring and very supportive of her students. If you get a chance you should definitely take a class with her especially if it is a human rights class.

Alka is an interesting person and resource of knowledge. She is a fair grader and receptive to student requests, though personally, I thought her assignments were reasonable and the requests for extensions and changes were not necessary. She will challenge you in discussions, which is fair enough. Make an effort to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I love Alka!! I have taken two classes with her and found many of my classmates have as well, she is very considerate and pays attention to the students needs, due to assignments on time and show up to class and you should be good

I loved her! She was such a sweet and intelligent professor and always encouraged our ideas. She was always so positive and flexible but made you think critically which was great. I would take any of her classes.
Alka is awesome! Love her! She is a really flexible and open minded professor, always welcome for students to correct her.
Very confusing, she is not consistent at all. Can't seem to remember what she said in her email conversations, don't take her word. It is her way or the highway.

I thoroughly enjoyed Prof. Kurian's class. She was always very helpful, very understanding, and always wanted you to succeed. She was always open to everyone's ideas and appreciated every input, even if it was the complete opposite of her own. Always very encouraging and positive.

Hwgrading: Focus in class & give answers based on what she teaches; she pays attention to detail. Classes: She's smart, passionate, and puts time into her teaching - I love learning from her :). Participation is very important .You get a short factoid assignment weekly, one essay, 2-3 quizzes, and readings throughout the qtr. Well rounded class.

Alka can be a tough grader, she expects a lot from her students (she will call on you for your thoughts if you are quiet too long!) However, she was always very helpful when asked for advice or feedback on your progress for an assignment. Don't be afraid to engage with her if you are struggling. Be ready for group projects for your final.

Such an engaging and lovely prof. Very helpful. But will randomly call on people in class. Do the readings and participate in class discussions and you will be totally fine. Prof is also very reasonable when it comes to quizzes/tests. Also you should enjoy/be interested in the course topic before joining the class. I would very much recommend her!

This was one of the easiest most interesting classes I have taken here. There is hardly any work just a reading before each class that you need to comment on, a final paper, and a group project. Participate in the class and you should have no problem getting a 4.0. She does however, bring up politics A LOT. I just ignored that aspect of the class.

I HATE THIS CLASS. She is inconsistent & rude. When I asked her a question she snapped at me. Her grading is terrible. Your answers have to be what she wants. One assignment said list what WE find interesting; she gave me 1/2 credit, apparently I was suppose to GUESS what SHE found interesting. I wouldn't recommend her or her class to anyone.

Her grading criteria is so inconsistent which makes it very hard to get a good score. To get a correct answer on her test, you must have the exact answer she wants when there are multiple. Her grading scale is also out of 4 which can deter your grade A LOT even with -1 point.
She grades pretty harshly even though the in-class time isn't too bad. She seems like a nice person and all, but it's pretty hard to maintain a good grade with her grading technique.
She cares that her students learn but not in a hound-you-about-it way. Her film class for the Discovery Core was super easy and definitely worth it.
Alka is seriously one of the best teachers you wiill ever have.  She truly goes to great lengths to make sure her students succeed.  She values what her studnets say and feel, too.

Took a Transnational Fillm Class with her. The films she chose were usually good or at least mildly entertaining. Some of them sucked. But there were good discussions. Quizzes were fairly easy if you have good movie comprehension. I never read the articles and still got an A. She's a good lecturer too.

She is very nice. Sweet, Understanding and helpful in every possible way. You can get 4.0 in her class if you are not lazy and do the work on time. She makes the learning environment very friendly, engaging and something you will look forward to everyday you leave her class. I recommend her classes. They are well developed.

Her consistency does seem to vary. Participation in class helps your grade. She is really nice and wants students to be successful. Be very thorough with your answers so she knows you understand the material. Also, understand exactly what she wants from you in writing a paper.

Great class, it was fun watching movies every week!  I really like Alka, she's got a sweet disposition.  Beware though, her consistency DOES vary which can be frustrating.  She is also a pretty tough grader.  All around though, this was a good class.
She is pretty hard. makesure to studythe textbook.

Tough grader and consistency varies. When I adjusted my writing and inclusion of referenced concepts she then wanted more of my own opinions, then it was the other way on the next paper. She speaks well, and presents the material and concepts well.
DON'T TAKE HER. SHE IS ACTUALLY GOING TO MAKE YOU RETHINK LIFE
Just don't

I took her for 124&125, I loved her teaching style. She was very caring, her lectures were super super helpful (definitely attend class), and she wasn't a very tough grader. I think my grade was as good as it was because of how helpful and nice she was.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Musselman was an excellent professor for this class! She cares so much about students and is always willing to help you out. As long as you stay on top of all the assignments, which often times she provides ample time to complete during class, you should have a great time. Would definitely take another course with her!

She is super sweet and loves to help. Attendance is mandatory. Take home quizzes are fine but make sure you add EVERYTHING. Tests are not too bad just make sure to come to class cause most of the questions on the midterms are related to class questions. Overall solid professor.

She's super caring and approachable and likes to help her students. I had her during A term in the summer and if it wasn't for the fast-paced structure, I'm sure I would've passed I'd really like to have her again. The exams were worth most of our grades, weekly online hw, and video lectures but no extra credit. Amazing professor, highly recommend!

Open-note, take-home quizzes were every other week. The textbook proper was rarely used, but an online homework system that often comes with the textbook was frequently used. Note that used textbooks tend not to come with access to the online homework system, so I recommend a new digital textbook. Note checks were at the start of most classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Solid Professor! Nothing special, but nothing extraordinary either. Stay with the class and watch the lecture videos before class and you will grasp the material pretty easily. If you put the time in a high grade is easily attainable. Ask for help, as she is great at explaining topics and is SUPER approachable and nice!

Mandatory notes, mandatory classes, you will print all of your groupwork, handouts, homework, quizzes. All lectures are online, and avg 2-4 hours total. class time is 100% just individual groupwork. Tough grader on quizzes and midterms. She seems to be a good teacher but class time is just very poorly utilized and class structuring is confusing.

Goes over problems in depth and understands most of us forget everything from precalc. 5 Midterms (kinda crazy) and 1 final are problems you've already seen before and not something crazy. In-class group work and warmups are super helpful too. THQ are harder than test IMO and be prepared to spend 4-5 hours watching lecture videos per week.

Very helpful in dumbing topics down and explaining any questions. 2 Midterms and final exam are basically based on group work and lecture notes so nothing you have not seen. Very video lecture heavy but is nice to spend class in group work and asking q's. Hardest thing was THQ questions as you have one day to do. partial credit is a lifesaver!

She's a nice person overall but there are some things about the class that make you question a lot of things. For example, all of her lectures are pre-recorded videos and some aren't even by her. The only purpose showing up to class is for her to grade you on your note taking for those lectures. On top of all this her first assignment was a THQ.

Flipped classroom format you watch video lectures before class & class is warmups & group work where you can ask questions. She's understanding that you probably don't remember precalc & trig & goes over those parts in the lectures. Take home quiz every other week, 3 exams, 1 cumulative final exam. Can use scientific calc on exams (only 125).
Really good professor and teaches things very clearly. Have to watch a lot of videos at home though because she does not do the lectures in class, instead you do a lot of group work.

This is a new class on teaching math for the Education major at UWB. Alex is a nice and approachable lady but often seems to forget she's not working with STEM majors in this class. Assignments are very interesting so far. You will fall behind if you don't attend.
Really great professor, straightforward, and the test are easy to understand if you put the effort into studying.

Dr. M is an amazing professor. Although she didn't make many video lectures this time, in-class time was effectively used to cover important stuff in each chapter. Her grading is very clear and straightforward. She's very flexible when it comes to scheduling office hours. Attendance is not mandatory. Would definitely recommend taking her.
Explains the concepts to a T. Best math professor I have had in a longgggg time.

Dr. Musselman is a really friendly and caring person. I loved attending the pre-recorded lectures, it helped me absorb the material and gave ample amount of time for Q/A sessions the next day in class. She's concise & clearly tells her expectations. If you follow them, you're in a good shape to get an A in this class.

She does not teach in class, she makes you watch videos on YouTube. Her teaching method is confusing, so you have to watch videos made by others. Overall it feels like a online class even though it is not.
Her class is basically online. You learn from YouTube videos not in class. In class is a waste of time.
Easy to understand the content if self taught, I got more confused by her explanations and had to reteach most of the material myself
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good professor if you really want to learn math. Grades justly, and tests are a big part of the class but they are also relatively easy as long as you know the material. Definitely would take this teacher again even if the class is pretty fast paced.

I think she's an "okay" option. If there's anyone better I would aim for that. She held class only once a week which is NOT enough for math especially online and within that time we only solved 1 problem which again is not helpful either. It takes her at least a week to reply to emails, she also takes a long time to grade.

Dr. Musselman is only willing to help you during study hall, she doesn't seem interested in replying much to emails. Felt she didn't really care for us as people. Her lectures sometimes do not match up with her homework in MML, sometimes I had to self teach. Her quizzes pretty close to the homework in MML and her final wasn't too easy nor hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Musselman is an extremely caring professor who is clear and concise about what she expects from you. She is a very good teacher. She goes through every topic. She gives you packets that you can use for studying for tests and the final. If you pay attention, take studious notes, and just do the homework, you should have no problem getting an A.

I don't understand why she has a 2.9/5 rating on here. Dr. Musselman is a great professor and it's clear that she loves what she teaches. She is extremely helpful and even though she doesn't give extra credit, her exams are straightforward and match up with what you learn in the lecture and hw.

Dr. Musselman is a straightforward professor. She talks very fast. However, she always asks "does anybody need me to say that again?" Not great for introverted students who don't like admitting what they don't know in front of others. I'd prefer a more personal conversation as she's walking around to check in. A good grade is definitely attainable.
Great Professor. Great lectures. Doesn't try to push any political agendas or propaganda on you. Lots of HW in My Math Lab. Tough grader. You cant pass the class without the lectures.

Not a very good teacher even though she prides herself in getting a PHD in teaching... Got pretty tired of being talked down at and treated like I was 2 years old. She likes to feel like she is in charge. You can tell she doesn't like what she is teaching but tries to cover it up. Really tough grader and I think that relates to her power trip.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor is really tough on grading but she is really nice person. You can't miss class or else she will have you learn it on your own even though you go to her office hours. She assigns a lot of hw and its due 3 times a week. The test are super hard and you're on your own if you take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I'm currently taking her now and she's is a great professor and I'd HIGHLY recommend taking her if you plan on moving forward in math. She makes sure you understand the material. Tests are based off of worksheets from class and her lectures so its straight forward! Take her even if you need to change your schedule around!!!

Extremely approachable professor for anything you do not understand. There is ALOT of material to be covered in this class. I felt the online homework, sometimes due three times a week, did not apply well to her exams. There was usually a question on the exam worth 20 points. You better hope you know your stuff!

Super friendly, enthusiastic and caring! Her office hours are honestly worth going to. She's willing to take her time to make sure you understand every single little step. She tells you clearly what will be on the test and what won't be; didn't see any surprises. Her feedbacks on exams will help you pass the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was a great teacher. I passed this class easily just by paying attention in class. The online homework was repetitive but helpful, as well as relevant to what we were learning. The two midterms were shorter than I expected and there wasn't any surprises on homework or exams if you used her notes and payed attention in class. 10/10 recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice person overall, but not helpful. Only solves half the problems in class and when asked for clearification she would suggest going to the qsc or her office hours.  She's also the type of teacher to introduce a new concept in the last 5 minutes of class and expects you to understand it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She was a good teacher overall. She was very helpful if you had questions for her. I had a long break from math, and she was very helpful in getting me back up to speed and refreshing my memory on some of the things I had forgotten. Overall I would take her class again. There was a fair amount of homework, but that is expected from math classes.

As my first professor, Musselman wasn't a bad teacher. The class felt  like  high school level which was good for people transitioning into college. But her teaching pace was not on the same page as the online textbook which was really bad because tests would always have me confused. If you pay attention and read the online textbook you'll be ok.

She's a nice teacher. She makes math alot harder than it is. Participation is graded toughly. She is also a very tough grader marking you down for simple mistakes. Even if you get the answer right you can still be "wrong". I took her up on office hours and still received a low grade. Keep in mind i was a straight A high school student. :( beware

She is a horrible professor. She grades you wrong even if you get the right answer on tests. She assigns a ridiculous amount of homework that doesn't relate to anything in class or on tests. She grades attendance which is technically illegal, and its at least 5% of your grade. If you have an option, take another professor because she is terrible

Exams are not difficult if you pay attention in class and do the work. Yet she is the toughest grader through out my college expirance. If you get the right answer she'll find something wrong with it and mark you off a large portion. She is also very confusing during class and often gets herself confused. I would definitely not recommend.

Professor Musselman encourages students to visit her office hours, which is a plus. HW amount is reasonable, there are two midterms, and a final. She gives the second midterm a week before the final, which is not convenient at all. Teaches the class at a reasonable pace.

I already took this class in high school, I just wanted to review, and thought it would be fun, getting me into the just of college, NOPE. I AM ALMOST FAILING!!! She makes everything WAY MORE CONFUSING THAN SHE HAS TO! We will ask a question, then she will ask us a question in return........ Grades hard, with no opportunity to get grades back up.

True GPA terrorist, the lectures will not prepare you for the exams. There's a lack of material to actually study from. half the class scored sub 70 on the midterm and he says he's disappointed and  the exam wasn't that hard. You don't know what is actually on the exam because there's no structure in this class, lectures are all breadth no depth.

This is the worst class I have taken. The lectures cover 30 different things with a few bullet points of information each. You are not prepared at all for the exams the few example problems in the lectures are extremely simple compared to the exam problems. It's a challenge to study due to the lack of material  and not knowing whats on the exam.

Look, you students are just students .Mr Berger, he's the devil. He is smarter than you, He is luckier than you. Whatever you think is supposed to be on the tests, im telling you the exact opposite will be on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's just terrible. He only read off the PowerPoint. Worksheets are not relevant to the exam or quizzes. I tried every method in the book to study for this class, but no matter how much I studied, the quizzes and exams were still unpredictable. Try to take this class with another professor, if not GOOD LUCK!

The burger is an interesting fellow, the lectures are typically monotonous and wont do much in terms of learning unless you're reviewing, the textbook is "recommended" but you definitely want to read it . huge difficulty spike in the content after midterm, hdlbits website . he may or may not hate women but there is no gender bias in circuitry
He's alright. You must be proactive in his class to get a good grade and most of the final and midterm is just stuff he shows on the slides

This is my second course with him and you can expect consistency. He explains things well in the lectures.. His individual help is VERY helpful, so just ask if you're not sure how to do something. Half of the class is spent solving problems. Some parts of the quizzes will come from the textbook. Do the homework even tho its not required

He isnt bad but the lectures are just so pointless. He reads through slides with very simple lectures then handouts difficult problems expecting us to understand them. Get the textbook if u wanna pass and expect to study a lot because the exams are much harder than the textbook and quiz/hw problems. Class avg for midterm/final were in the 50s range

his lectures are very confusing, so you will have to learn through the textbook. What would help more students learn is working through example problems with his students, instead of just reading the slides and expecting us to work through the problems he gives out. A little more than half the class failed the first midterm. Very frustrating

Intro circuit analysis class should be taught with examples yet he didn't draw a single one on the board. He curves at the end so students end up moving on with very minimal circuit analysis skills that are required for future classes. Over half the class failed the midterm and he berated us for over an hour saying we weren't trying hard enough.

Professor Berger is a great teacher. If you're willing to put in the work, not only will you learn a lot but he will go above and beyond to help you when you ask. He likes students that are proactive about their education. Just be respectful in-class and ask questions when needed. Just don't expect an easy class as it's not an easy subject.

Professor Berger knows the material, but has no clue how to teach it. 50% of his lectures is just him talking about what he did when he was industry and he doesn't show us how to solve any of the problems seen in the HW.

His lectures are long and boring. One of the worst parts is that he'll put a incredibly simple example in, and barely skim over it and then expect us to be able to do complex circuitry problems by the end of the week. Another thing, half our class failed the midterm and most got a C, in summary he said "do better". Def get the book and study ALOT

Berger is clearly a knowledgeable professor, this does not transfer that well to his lecture abilities. If you can self-study, and put in 5-10 EXTRA hours per week doing practice problems, this class will go well for you. If you are reliant on lectures to learn, please practice using textbook questions. I didn't feel that the lectures helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Berger is a very knowledgeable professor who loves what he does. However, he does not know how to teach students. He expects students to read the textbook and doesn't really do that great of a job explaining things. He doesn't really go through problems with the students and kind of just leaves it up to the students to do it themselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tests are difficult, but predictable. The required book, written by this professor, is outdated and has many errors. Everything you need to know for the whole quarter is in one PowerPoint, but many of the slides are unclear without his explanations. Homework and project specifications are lengthy and not divided into logical sections.
His tests are too hard. Prepare to study ahead.

Tough test but very interesting class. Mr. Berger teaches you what you need to know in a macroscopic sense but there is a disconnect between what your taught and whats on the test.  Kind of wish we spent more time problem solving with guidance.
The worst class and professor is in my scholar live. He will give you the most challenge problem, and his lecture is not helpful. At the end of the quarter, he will curve your grade. Painful memory!

Lectures are a bit boring since its a new topic and hard to understand. He tries his best and is passionate but fails to  teach properly. Tests are had due to the lack of knowledge students have about the material but the grader is very generous. I don't think i learned as much as I would have liked :(
Lectures are long and Dull. Like being tortured. monotone voice
The tests are too hard. You should do the hard problems in the back of the textbook.

Professor Lund is okay. I thought his lectures were quite difficult to pay attention to, and that I could easily go over the same material on my own. Lots of group projects which he grades fairly, but the tests are what can tank your grade. He asked some specific questions about something a guest speaker said that is almost impossible to remember.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Arnie's classes are easy as long as you do the assigned work. There are a lot of small assignments, but you typically get full credit on them. You're in a group the entire quarter to complete a lot of these assignments. Tests are pretty easy, you get a cheat sheet and he curves tests down so you can often get over 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was very disorganized. He tends to ramble about his industry experience and his lectures were very irrelevant and borderline confusing due to the information overload. That being said, you get a double-sided note sheet for all exams, and he is a very easy grader. Overall, not a good teacher, but good for industry knowledge and easy A.

Fantastic teacher. He is an experienced industry veteran. Very lecture heavy, however, you are allowed a cheat sheet for exams which is all you will need. Show up, pay attention in class, and take occasional notes, and you will 100% do well. Invites guest speakers to class to speak on the industry and group projects are very fun and educational.
practical class
wonderful class, cares about students. Even does an interview workshop to connect to real world....
Loved the class.

In tune with modern times and refreshing to see a real world approach. Bonus - does an interview workshop and helped me prep for a real job interview that I cleared! 

Really cares and spent even a weekend helping us think on our project. Highly highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fun yet engaging class. I wish he taugh more often..
Likes to talk about himself and his career accomplishments. Has unrealistic expectations on case studies. Avoid if at all possible.
Very good teacher
Great content and presentation style. Loved the case study based approach during assignments. Group work during class is great. Excellent guest speakers and it helps to have a hot professor ;)

If this class has an opening run towards it. Amazing lectures and to the point. Aseem is a great presenter and makes things simple to digest. The pace of this class is superb and I felt I learnt so much about business than my previous classes. His teaching style is relaxed yet informative. My only suggestion would be to make this two hours.

Very much in tune with the present times. Does not use a textbook but lectures are amazing! I learnt so much more - something that I can put to use rightaway. Very helpful professor, one of the best IMO.
Great course and excellent class. Its folks like these who schools need to have teaching a class - Practical, Realistic and I felt I learnt so much from this class.
He grades horribly in projects and case studies.

Very clear lectures, easy to understand. Not many assignments and only 1 exam and 1 group project. Attendance is very important because class discussions are a big part of your grade. Just go to class, participate in discussions, read the chapters and you will get a good grade. I recommend his class.
Haha. I'm joking, interesting class.
Take with any other professor if you can, otherwise the whole quarter will be miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Berger can be intimidating. The problems prepare for real scenarios with not but a datasheet. It's possible to do okay in Dr. Berger's class.
