To pass: 1) Read material in the schedule on time to follow lectures. The book is better than the slides. 2) Raise your hand & say "I don't understand that" 3) Go to office hours, or schedule something

His lectures can be boring and lengthy and the textbook is recommended but not required. I recommend looking over his slides first and then watching tutorials before coming to class. Do practice problems to prepare well for exams. His classes are a bit hard but fair if you work for it. Make sure to read the articles he puts out!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: In fall 2018, he attempted a reversed-class. He prepared the material and had us self-study. We would begin each class with a 45min lecture; The rest of the time practicing. The class was fun and we had plenty of practice. We had an extra 7% of our final grade as extra credit. He accepted late work and graded nicely. I would take him again.

If you really can delay this class hoping that litterly any other professors teach it, please do so. I litterly took the class and understood the very minimal that I could have done by watching YouTube videos or going over articles by myself and it would save me going to a class and get mocked and fun of
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This isn't going to be like your other engineering classes, you actually have to understand the topic and be able to apply your understanding with whatever he tests you on. Don't skip class and really try and focus during lecture or it will take even longer to learn it alone.

Intellectual professor, but I would recommend focusing more on the readings and homework than anything else in order to succeed. If you have the option of either going to lecture or reading the textbook, read the textbook. By my advice, you will do just fine, just be involved.

This guy seriously sucks. He blazed through 2/3 of the material in the first four weeks and spent the rest of the quarter letting us go through "practice problems". Terrible lecturer. Do you like stupid Dilbert comic strips? Then you'll love all of Berger's class material. If you can stand his dry humor and snide personality, you'll make it through

I took his class because I had no choice. This course is offered only once a year and he is the only teacher. He goes too fast. he himself said that he went to fast. We finished 90% of the material in 5 weeks. He needs to slow down. Exams are nothing like his homework. GG.

Even though the exams are 70% of your grade, you'll do fine in the class if you do the homework and labs. But remember to study a lot before the exams!! Try to do the hard problems in the textbook (transistors), there's a strong chance it'll be on the exam.

Had a different experience with Berger in EE.  He definitely knows his field of EE, but was disinterested in teaching any classes other than 422.  Repeats the same stories which wastes time.  He's the archtype brilliant guy that lacks the interpersonal skills to stick in industry. Atrocious organization and planning outside of CSS 422.

Arnie's Hardware Organization class was amazing. I received the lowest grade in my academic history from him and consider him my favorite teacher I've had, so that should say something. If you show up, pay attention and show up to his study groups, you'll get the grade (I failed to do so for the midterm) Pity he isn't teaching much CSS now :(

Lots of new things to learn in one quarter so the class is pretty hard. Do homeworks, read ahead of lectures and go to exam review sessions and you should do well. Prof. Berger is very helpful. This was the hardest CSS course for me.

His lectures and assignments are interesting and informative. The midterm and final are not good measures of what students learned. Instead they measure how well you can memorize and how fast you can do arithmetic by hand.

Berger isn't hard... the material is hard. Somewhat technical but very verbose.  Read ahead of lectures, don't miss class, and don't get behind!  25% of the class will fail, but due dilligence will see you through.  It's a pleasure to have a class where the book, the lectures, and the assignments are so well synchronised.
Very smart professor and fair grader. He expects you to work hard but you will really know your stuff after his class. Don't slack off - the material is pretty hard. If you work hard it will pay off.

A very tough professor. He knows his stuff, but he isn't the most clear in describing it, resulting in confusion. When students are confused, he frequently re-hashes exactly what he already said, instead of alternate explanations. Although he verbally expresses his intrest in helping students, he tends to have a very cold personality towards them.
heavy work load, read the books, don't hesitate to ask questons. Good luck!
Berger is a good teacher. He includes a lot of helpful resources to help you learn. Make sure you ask a lot of questions in class or you may have a hard time

Arnie Berger is a good professor that I genuinely liked.  He has extensive experience in the field from being Director of R&D at Applied Microsystems Corporation and R&D Project Manager for HP.  He knows his stuff, explains it well, and expects you to pick it up.  But, you'll learn a lot from him and you will pick it up.
A Professor who was in the IT field. Very knowledgeable

he don't really teach. he sits on the corner and students present the entire quarter except for few hrs. not well prepared for classes, assignment is not clear, grading criteria is not clear. not recommended if you care to know the material well
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Vague/confusing assignment instructions, zero feedback, and exclusively group projects (no individual work).

He seems nice but is VERY disorganized. He would consistently forget to post slides & often had no clue what the slides he copied from online were about. He is unclear on what he expects or how he will grade, and gives almost no examples for hwk. He even graded the class by ranking us on performance. Class was way harder than it shouldve been.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about programming and does a decent job explaining concepts. Main gripe with him is that he is very unorganized and obviously not used to teaching in a classroom/college setting. Things in class felt disjointed and grade scales and test difficulty was all over the place.

Amazing at articulating programming concepts. I knew nothing about programming before his class, and he helped me understand everything. He is down to earth, personable, very nice, and incredibly understanding and flexible based on the needs of the class. All around great professor. Dont expect help outside of class and office hours though.

Aseef is the reason I got to computer science. He is passionate, caring, and motivational. I would recommend taking him. It is always funny that I kept stuck on setters and getters which is a simple concepts but he has pushed me through it until I became really good in programming.

It's an entry level class. He expected you to be professional programmer. He will teach you simple concept, but his test and homework are beyond this level. And he didn't go through homework again. i.e.: he will tell you the next lesson is method, and tonight's homework is method.
get a good group/coordinate with friends, or prepare to do all the group work yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor is very unorganized, creating confusion for students. Students never know where assignments are, always having to email the professor to ask. She always responds by saying she messed up or forgot.  Boring lectures as she reads off of slides and randomly calls on students. This is not high school, relax with the cold calls.

Hazel gets the job done. She doesn't have exceptional lectures, but cares about you learning the material. Her system for group projects was solid, since you can 'escape' from bad groups after each project if needed. Overall, she will help you learn if you put in effort. Ask questions, get assistance and above all, participate.

If this class's content was relevant to current trends in the tech industry, like user research, defining tech stacks, and different problem-solving frameworks, it would be one of the best classes in the CSS program. Hazel is a great professor and great resource for future knowledge, but her lessons are outdated.

This class seemed like such a waste of money. All class is essentially answering questions from your reading. There is no engagement so you just lose all of the knowledge the next week. Keeping engaged is also extremely difficult. The contents of the class are fairly easy however. Do yourself a favor and take this in person with a different prof.
Best professor. I will recommend to all students please enroll in her course. She is the best. I learned a lot under her guidance.

I took 360 and 370 with Hazel this year. She's definitely nice and I think she does care about students, but the way she organizes this class is kinda confusing. She likes diagrams and will throw many of them your way in her lectures, particularly in 370, but they help make concepts stick.

The class only had 5 group projects, 3 quizzes, and a final, and if you watch her lectures and take notes based on her study guide, you'll do good in this class. Although her lectures are really vague and it's really hard to connect dots and apply what you know to real life if that makes sense. The lectures make enough sense to pass this class.

As other people on this site say, she is a very kind and pleasant person. But that did not equate to her being a good teacher. She makes things harder than they should be and kinda overcomplicates concepts. The textbook was kinda useless because you learned EVERYTHING from lecture.

Hazel is probably among the nicest profs in CSS, but the way she teaches and structures the class makes it kind of hard to stay engaged when learning from her. Just pay as much attention as possible, get a good group, study for the exams, and you're set. She makes time to meet with students and is open to feedback, which I appreciate.

Hazel is a nice person and decent teacher, but this class's material is somewhat outdated when comparing it to today's industry practices. Assignment instructions are very complicated and grading techniques are not the best. Despite this, she can be quite helpful in office hours and is accessible if you can't make her time.

Hazeline is a nice professor and the class is pretty easy. You can tell she cares about the students because she actually listens to the feedback the class gives her. The only unfair part about the class is that she likes to include trick questions in the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Turned in a project and received a grade of 79% on it. Two weeks later I used something from the exact same project, unchanged, on an exam and received 14/15 on the exam. This was the class in a nutshell, and she was the nut. Confusing way of learning and not the best at communicating knowledge.

I also took CSS 360 with Hazeline. She is one of the more dated professors in the CSS faculty who hasn't worked in industry since 2000. Her class is more outdated than most. The assignments are very superficial. Decent if you want to just get an A though.

Flexible and understanding professor that is keen on student feedback throughout the course and actually puts that feedback into action into changing course structure/material. Although the content of this course is outdated, Hazel has made improvements such as adding bits about REST to hit modern topics. Respectful and caring toward all students.

This class was pretty useless, to be honest. Aside from learning UML and software architecture the things presented in this class were already talked about a lot in CSS 360. Hazel was rather ineffective at teaching the material and expected extremely specific answers. The projects are better than the tests and should be the bulk of the class.

Professor Hazeline is nice and fair. Her TA's grade everything. The class is pretty easy to pass. 5 group projects that are straightforward. 3 quizzes, the lowest one is dropped. Final is 35% of your grade but only one question. Overall easy to pass, but the course itself isn't very interesting, and I don't feel like I learned as much.

Class is made up of tests and projects. Projects are easy. Tests are impossible. She grades you like an "ice skating judge" as someone else said. Questions are short- answer, super vague and expected answers super specific. If you do not write something that was preordained as correct (she has a list of "correct" answers already made) you get 0.

Issued a ton of busy work to waste your time in the beginning, then threw you into big projects and exams without much guidance. Lectures are boring and honestly skippable, but asynchronous lectures are great. Textbook is useless if you watch the videos. Exams are graded badly. Would not vouch for this prof.

Everything about this class was disorganized and vague. Her grading heavily penalizes you for simple mistakes, like an ice skating judge. Class time is not spent well and mostly just reiterates the book. When students ask questions, she tells them to pay attention more instead of answering.

Overall she structures the class really well for a hybrid class. Pretty good at explaining models and diagrams in lectures. If you choose a really good group and an easy project to work on, it shouldn't be too bad. You can earn a lot of extra credit points on the discussions, so make sure to participate. She does take a while to respond to email.

I cannot say enough good things about Hazel! Her class is really engaging, the lectures are good, and she's really optimistic and friendly. There is a lot of busy groupwork but she's willing to make time to help you and your class, and she's really available cause she's a part-time prof here.
She is not very timely with her feedback and doesnt really explain complex topics very well. Perhaps she is great at the undergrad level, but Id avoid her at the grad level.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If every CSS professor were like Hazel, the department would be so much better. She is a genuine and caring person, and her feedback is incredibly helpful and timely. Plus she understands that we all have lives outside of her class and is willing to make time for us to improve our understanding. Definitely recommend.
You will score if you study and understand the topics well. Some questions require a deep understanding of the subject. Group projects and assignments are fun.

If you like hands on, group projects, and active participation this class is great. Her lecture notes are great and most of the tests will be taken straight from her lecture notes. The class will be easy if you have a good group. There are 5 group projects that really require a lot of group interaction.
Get ready to have some group work. It is not super hard but there are some. Two quizzes, Midterm, Final, and done.

Hazel was 5-15 minutes late to almost every class fall quarter. She is nice, but not the best teacher. She doesn't give clear directions or seem to be confident in what she's teaching even though she has experience in industry.
She makes sure you understand by repeating the complex concepts a couple times. Provide a good review before an exam. Easy to approach with questions.

I took her for Software Engineering, which is a group work class so take it with people you know if you can (you pick your own group). In class is mostly lectures with slideshows that have all you need to know on them. I found myself just bored most of the time, the class wasn't bad but it wasn't particularly good either.

Very nice and genuine, she's awesome. Tips for getting a good grade: 1. Start preparing midterm/final notes early. She allows 1 page handwritten note (both sides) for midterm, and 2 pages for final. 2. No need to take notes during lecture, they're all on slides. 3. This class is more fun if taking with a friend, you'll have four group projects.
The professor has a clear grading criteria and she is vocal about it. She's strict and expects students to follow the criteria set by professors for evaluation.
Difficult to understand
She's really a nice professor. I studied Machine Learning under TCSS555. Extra credits are useful to boost your grade. Emphasis very much on feedback. The difficulty is not so much.

I wouldn't take her class she has no idea what she is doing and her lectures are very scattered. Also she updates homework assignments a day before they are due because she made a mistake making the assignment impossible. She is also very rude to talk with.

TCSS422 is an operating system class. Overall, the class content was pretty hard itself. She just made it worse. I studied very hard for the midterm because I messed up some of her random quizzes during class and did pretty good on it. However, she somehow canceled the third HW and made quizzes worth 10%(was about 6%). I lost 5% for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This professor has a firm grasp on networking concepts, but I feel like her lectures may be inhibited by materials she uses from the department. You must read the book, as there are many concepts, and note sheets are not allowed on tests. Course materials often direct us to use deprecated networking technologies, and should be updated.

This was a very easy class and I actually enjoyed it more than I thought I would!! Super nice prof although we were online, he made sure to provide help to students. I wish he was more responsive outside of class though. If you see prof Wayne Au listed for a class, sign up! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The class was easy and so was the workload. Overall, the class was chill and allowed me to learn about the topic without having to stress and worry as much. It made doing the assignments more fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This course was extremely easy because I could do it in my own time. Assignments are pretty much just reading and leaving annotations on the reading and then interpreting each chapter in a 250-500 word response. Didn't interact with the instructor much, but I'd say I learned a decent amount about Asian American education.

I'm taking him for BEDUC 201: special topics in diversity and education, topic "asian Americans in education," and the class is based on the book he published. Very easy class and he is an easy grader, the final is only 500 words and all you do is annotate his book each week and do chapter reflections, he is really nice and knowledgeable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought he was average. He definitely has the male ego thing going on.

Dr. Au is by far THE BEST professor I have ever had. I took his Education and Equity in the U.S. class, and it has changed my view on teaching. He takes the time to care for you as a student and cares about your learning. I will take all of his classes, by far MY FAVORITE teacher here at UWB.

I have Wayne for BEDUC 205 (only taking this for a diversity credit) and he is one of the nicest, genuine professors Ive ever had. He makes you feel important to his class and valued. He also made me care about education equity and make it relevant to me for the first time. The class is pretty easy, recommend for whoever needs a div credit. Easy A

Definitely the best Education professor you can ever ask for. He talks about race  culture gender sexuality immigration status bilingual education etc. and shows why talking about these socially constructed systems matter in education. He will inspire you and you will remember why you love education so much. Take him every chance you get.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Simple as that, he is REAL, he is from SEATTLE, he understands YOU! HE CARES ABOUT WHAT YOU THINK. He isn't afraid to talk about topics about race, etc. I missed class once and he was totally cool about it. If you want to be a teacher, he is the best professor to look up to and he will help you with every step on the way. BEST!

Prof Wayne is AMAZING!!!  I had him for a Hip Hop in Education class & another Ed class and I wish I could take his classes every quarter.  He is smart, kind, and funny.  He makes his students feel valued and his expectations are clear.  Can't say enough great things!  You would be lucky to get into one of his classes!
Just no. Don't do it.

Lectures are okay. Gets boring pretty quick. You lose points on assignments for not breathing right or for blinking too many times, so don't expect a 100 unless you're a perfect human (you aren't). Announces when quizzes are ahead of time.

Expect to be crying by the time finals roll around if you aren't already still crying from midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sucks at teaching, quizzes and tests are worth 65% of your grade, takes off points for the dumbest reasons. Don't take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He might know his things in physics, but he ain't good at teaching it nor explaining it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for BPHYS 121 as my lab teacher. This dude is genuinely an AI, and will make you lose points on unclear grading criteria

It's frustrating because prof. Bacon is nice but is a tough grader (e.g. 2.9/3.0 and 0.9/1.0). The class at UWB is not difficult, but he does *not* give clear or constructive feedback on the assignments and in class. He shows you a rubric but does not explain how he applies it, making it hard for students to understand his grading criteria.

Overall he's chill and checks in with groups but doesn't give good feedback. He grades hard on lab notes so grading criteria isn't that clear. It's not a hard class though cause he doesn't focus on physics aspect more about the reflection and what you learned from it. If you have a good group then you'll be ok but no one knew what they were doing

Prof.Bacon is a very nice professor, but he does not explain very well. He reads off the slides for lab, which costs us time when conducting our experiments. He's a harsh grader but if you ask and explain, his feedback can help in the next report. Chill class but you have to be present for lab. Ask about structure of report more than physics itself
very nice person, but extremely harsh grader. dropped course due to incredulous grading. avoid at all costs, at least for lab.
oh my god dude like this is crazy like he is a teacher
Don't know all the bad ratings - he changed his teaching format winter quarter and it was light and easy. My email was responded instantly. Exams were online - got an A in the end

Lectures were a waste of time. I had to teach myself the content. Never responds to emails no matter how urgent. The class is one giant group project and you cannot change groups. Individual assignments are easy and useless. Weekly discussion posts (also easy and useless). Changes schedule whenever he feels like it. Doesn't respect accommodations.

I didn't learn anything during his lectures and taught myself everything. The whole course essentially revolves around a group project, so be prepared for that. Individual assignments were easy and shallow, but as a consequence, you don't really learn anything from them. He rarely responds to your emails and frequently changes the course schedule.

Professor Bantwal is often late to grade assignments, but provides clear feedback AFTER the submission dates. Often you must complete homework assignments before they are even fully covered in class. Ask questions early and you may have a chance at a decent grade. 

Prof. Bantwal is very flexible with due dates if you or your group needs more time.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please do not take any course offered by this professor. There is very less knowledge shared in class. Teaching standards are extremely low and grading is not set on a relevant criteria's. I wish I had know the subject would be this manner and I would have never opted for it.

They have attempted to adapt a CSS475 course taught by Mark Kochanski, but fail to explain the course content. Half of the class is Hybrid lecture videos from another professor. Group projects are frequent and heavily weighted with ambiguous guidelines. A large portion of the class didn't have enough time to finish the midterm.
Avoid this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His teachings are illogical and incoherent. It seems like he expects that everyone already knows or understands everything he says in his lectures. Adding to the problem, his homework requirements are vague, which means he'll slash points without much explanation. I'd rather have someone else than this guy in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grade depends on very few assignments, has no grading criteria, no clear instructions for anything, and is not a good teacher overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would try to avoid taking him class from now on. Here's why: 1. Strong accent, I had a hard time trying to understand him. 2. He expects you to know everything. 3. Questions on hw and exam is unclear. His explanation is also unclear. 4. He doesn't grade on rubrics. 5. A lot of homework. 6. Exam and hw are hard.

His teaching makes no sense. The way he teaches he just assumes everyone already knows everything or understands everything. On top of that his homework requirements are not very specific so he will take off points with very little feedback. I would honestly take anyone but this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Uh... there really aren't any words to describe Praveen. Expects the class to know everything and seems to get irritated when we don't. Very dry teacher, although 360 as a whole consists of dry content. Take someone else please. Tbh I'd take Nancy Kool for 360 instead of this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a very friendly professor! Her class is actually pretty easy to go through with weekly assignments graded mostly on comprehension/completion, quizzes that can be retaken, and flexible grading overall. I'm able to contact her outside of class pretty well.

Lowkey never showed up but she always put effort into me succeeding. Fun group projects, quite a few readings, and a lot of just talking even if it wasn't about the subject in class. If you can take her, DO IT

Shinneman was really nice and very accommodating - if you can get ahold of her. Both my classmates and I tried emailing and rarely if ever received responses, and when we talked to her in class she usually just offered to follow up later. Did a good job teaching the course, but just don't expect to get ahold of her outside of class.

Things to Expect:
-Hybrid Class
-8 or 9 Relatively light readings + annotations (Hypothesis) 
-3 Easy reading quizzes
-6 or so discussion posts
-Various small assignments
-In-class group discussions and some collaboration
-ArcGIS story map final 

(A sweet and easy-going person. Good lectures, workload, and worth the NSc credit. Rating: 4.25)
You do the work in class, so it's pretty easy if you show up.  The class covers a lot really fast, though, I wish it would have gone slower, but I guess that's just a quarter system thing.

Very Supportive. She will give you a lot of resources throughout the quarter.
The class is interesting as well. You will learn about how climate change was discovered in the first place.
Her grading is very reasonable and kind. Reasonable homework amount.
By far the best BCORE class to take as your very first class in college.

I took Professor Shinneman for a Climate Change in History class and really enjoyed it. Only one big paper all quarter, few assignments, and just a few readings each week. She really emphasized discussion and would lecture for most the period. Very kind person who is open to discussion. Would take again.

Overall a good class. Avery seemed a little snobby at first but she REALLY cares about students' learning and making the content interesting and applicable to the real world. She is somewhat inflexible with deadlines but if you do need it she'll let you. Easy to work with her in office hours and it gets you on her good side.

Professor Shinneman was great! She explained everything in a way that was easy to comprehend and gave extra help when something was hard to understand. If you miss labs and don't make them up it will be hard to pass but she gives you time to turn in anything you have that is late. I wish I was able to take more of her classes in the future!
So happy to be back in class on campus. This was a good one.
Loved this professor! Made geology really accessible and I suck at science.

I was excited to take this class, but it was run poorly. Avery is not a flexible teacher, but demands flexibility from her students. Do not expect her to reply to emails on time. She is egotistical, old fashioned, hates phones, and wasted our time with tech issues. After the first few weeks, she kept teaching the same material over and over again.

Dr. Avery Shinneman is a professor that cares for their students, and has a love for the subjects that is infectious and spurs the students on to further exploration. She gives the student a "map" of the concepts, and encourages them to explore further. She's a good mentor for those wanting to explore further in those fields, and classes are fun!
This class should have really sucked online, but I learned a lot. There were weird technical glitches and hard webpages to follow, but they were always worked out. Probably better in person!

I had a 91% in her class but the next day my grade was 74%. I looked in the grade book and saw that she had added 3 new assignments and given my 0s for them. I sent her an email asking her when we did those because I wasn't aware of them and she didn't reply. Now I'm stuck with a grade I didn't earn and she won't reply to my emails. That's unfair.
Amazing lectures, good quality and relevance of content, and excellent engagement with students. I highly recommend her to anyone with an interest in water ecology courses or fieldwork courses!

I would like to comment on the previous reviews. I believe she isn't that strict like all what the other peer facilitator reviewers said. She never said she has any problem with technology and she is very accessible. Always responds to emails and gives good feedback for assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's nice and all but extremely strict/rigid and makes the Peer Facilitator job much more challenging than it should be. She's not bad like the previous review said, though. I'd honestly try her geology class tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm a BCORE Peer Facilitator and Avery's our staff advisor. She tries to be nice, but unfortunately she's very strict and gives us way too much busy work and is very inflexible and inaccessible at the same time. Hates phones and doesn't let students use them at all. Also pompous and acts like she's better than everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Avery is so nice. She asks a lot of questions but she doesnt always just look for the right answer, so answer even if youre unsure. She will help you learn and understand things. Science isnt my forte but she explains things well and doesnt make you feel dumb for not understanding. The quizzes are easy and theres a final project. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Way more fun than I thought for a science elective. It was pretty cool stuff, but packed in. Had to show up to keep up for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was an online hybrid course, so there were in-class lectures and outside-homework assignments. The homework isn't particularly difficult, but there are quite a bit of readings. So if you're confused, don't worry! Every question I've ever had has been answered quickly through an email response or covered by Avery's lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You can tell she is passionate about what she does and that is inspiring to see in a professor. She is very, very organized and is extremely helpful. If you ever have questions she won't just give you the answer she will work with you to find it.

OMG if you are not geologist, then don't take it!! It's super boring and ridiculous class.  You have quizzes online before class. She asks you to understand everything she said and everything in the book. Final is the whole freaking book (which costs you $100)! And it took her 1 week to answer the email...

In her Water in the West class, she had us do a LOT of busy work. There was 15-30 page readings twice a week, an online quiz per week and two field trips. The field trips were interesting, but she didn't include facts of them on the tests, and we had to provide our own transportation on our own time. We had both a final project and a final exam.

Avery is a great professor. The class very fun and was super engaging. Plenty of field trips and activities as well! There is a decent amount of work but the class is very organized and dates are deeply expressed. Over all, recommend this course to anyone. Its very very educational.
She is knowledgeable and she provides a fun learning experience.
Really good teacher, very organized and helpful. I recommend taking her classes

She's really nice and is willing to help you on the drawings. But, the course requires a lot of effort to get a good grade in the class. Be prepared to buy a lot of materials or buy in bulk at bookstore. It was a lot of work considering I had two other courses that were very challenging. The readings also didn't help me at all on getting a 3.5!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not an easy class. LOTS of busy work you can't get by doodling. She expects 110% effort into your work!! You only have a midterms and a final which is presenting your drawings to the class. Barbara is a kind and funny professor but I wouldn't take her again because of all the work I had to do in her class plus my other 2 classes. It was toooo much.

I loved this class, I got to learn how to paint and could use subjects of my choice. I liked the images Professor Noah showed us and the books and artworks she brought to class. The guest lecturer was great, too. This class was inspiring, and I plan to keep on painting on my own.

Professor Noah is awesome, the best teacher I have had. Her lectures & readings taught me contemporary art. Her feedback was really helpful. I enjoyed learning techniques & experimenting with other ways of painting as part of the creative process. The field trip was awesome! Her grading was fair. I will try to take another class from her!

Professor Noah is a tough grader but she's very fair. I learned a lot about art in her class and felt more confident as an artist when it was over. I'd recommend this course to anyone who is serious about art because you can't just sit back and expect a 4.0, but you can also come in with no experience and succeed if you put in the effort.

Barbara is very kind teacher, but she doesn't really teach anything in her class and very boring lectures. You mostly watching video and art works from some famous artists. All the techniques and inspirations are mostly come from yourself. She is a tough grader. If you never taken an art class before, I wouldn't suggest you to take her class.
Really respectful.
Barbara is a very great professor, she is enthusiastic and really care about her students.

I took this course only because it's required, and I'll never take it again. Barbara only gave you credits when you suits her preference, otherwise, you'll just get horrible score. She is also mean about your painting, her words made me think i'm not "gifted". JUST DON'T TAKE HER CLASS!!

Super knowledgeable and enthusiastic. I learned a lot from her lectures and demonstrations and loved being able to make something. Syllabus was useful and organized, and I enjoyed the class readings, discussions, and peer reviews. You have to do the assignments, but she isn't an unfair grader, same as other IAS classes. Awesome class and professor!

If you're just looking for  VLPA credits or looking for an enjoyable art experience, don't take the class. She makes you buy a list of the most expensive art materials. She gives you a low grade on your paintings if it doesn't match her artistic style - makes you change little things to fit her preference. Most disorganized syllabus, boring lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice teacher. Gives feedback, more if you need it. Two painting projects, participation, and an easy presentation is your grade. If you attend and make an effort, you will do well. There are a lot of intimidating painters, but don't be afraid. You may need to think more artistically, especially if that's not your thing.

A wonderful professor. I took 5 of her classes and went on a study abroad with her. Yes her lectures are long, but they are informative and open students up to a wide range of styles and techniques. She genuinely cares about her students and is concerned with your success in her class, your general well being and your progress in the art world.

Barbara likes to talk for a long period of time... Just pure rambling on unnecessary & random topics. Participation is a HUGE aspect to her class... If you don't talk, your grade will be very low. She gives good feedback and is fairly nice when it comes to criticism for a student's art work, but she is NOT clear on her instructions for projects!!

She is very passionate, genuinely knowledgeable and shows a lot of interest in student's work and gives good feedback for improvement.  Class time is all studio time/critiques.  Readings are on reserves but she never goes over them.  Grade is based on amount of effort and participation during studio. Outside work is needed to succeed.

I've had Dr. B for two classes now; marketing management and undergrad research. Easily one of my favorite professors during my time at UW. If you put forth a bit of effort you will succeed in his class. If you expect an A to fall in your lap you're getting nowhere. Make an impression… he is a very valuable connection to have.

He is a nice professor, but the way he conveys his lectures will involve a lot of side tracks which will cloud your overall understanding of the learning outcomes. His classes involves a lot of work but he is not a tough grader.

Insightful lectures and engaging discussions. Assignments are challenging but fair, feedback timely and helpful. Professor wants the best for his students and is willing to help them achieve their goals. Only gripe: no pick-your-team final project!

Almost every homework assignment based on textbook was on Quizlet or Chegg, but for the other assignments that weren't textbook related, they aren't clear at all. Professor never responds to emails, so you're pretty much on your own. He also calls any students out on the spot for various questions, expecting perfect participation.
He's alright. I would get very bored during his lectures. The class could've been made more interesting. Definitely wouldn't take his class again.

RUN! Professor lectures on all topics outside of the book, expected students to sort through posted lecture slides and deduce relevant material on their own. Was structured like a graduate level class rather than introductory. Expectations were not clear and because book material was not discussed in class, test questions were very ambiguous.

Professor B is definitely a professor I would take a class with again! He makes his grading criteria very clear and his tests are multiple choice. Reading the textbook and getting involved in his discussions helped me learn. His lectures are interesting because he uses real-life examples. Also, keep track of due dates.

Dr. P.V. Balakrishnan is the best professor I have had thus far. Funny too. If you give him respect, he gives you equal or more respect. He has high expectations, but he deliberately tells you what he wants and what he doesn't want, so it's on you. Very inspirational, his class motivated me to seek a double concentration in marketing... TAKE HIM!!!

Prof. B is fantastic. He's funny and genuinely cares about his students. Make sure you go seek him out for help if you're struggling, because he'll help you out. His final project is a lot of work, but it was one of those that when you look back, you realize how fun it was. I learned a lot in his class. He really knows his stuff.

Professor B is one of the best professors I've had at UW! He gave me a passion for marketing and encouraged my class every step of the way. He replied fast to emails, does whatever it takes to get you on track and to pass. His group project was fun, but you need to keep up with due dates.
Incredible amounts of busywork, mostly unrelated related to the subject.  Highly disorganized. Grading was random.  Worst experience in the entire MBA program.  AVOID!

Grades were just released today with zero feedback to students on the breakdown or what was received on individual assignments. Professor was rude to students, course was very unorganized, and assignments were just busy work so he could find a excuse not to teach. This guy seriously needs to learn how to teach or switch careers.

Disorganized. Claims Blackboard is obsolete but his communication methods are pathetic in comparison. Splatters course info over at least 5 different websites. Poor communicator. Openly disrespects students point of view. Huge, useless homework assignments and projects. Assigns massive amounts of readings that he never talks about in class. F-

Spent many hours over the weekends and throughout week on homework. Cases were did not apply to the degree. Busy work and no clarity on where to find assignments, how to complete and how to submit. I feel UW has failed in allowing this class to be presented for so long.

This guy is rude, pompous, and frustrating.  Students are interrupted and made fun of and he doesn't listen to answers or questions.  He thinks he is clever and charming, but he's annoying and rude.  He is highly unorganized.  Students don't know what assignments are due or when because the syllabus, "playbook," and numerous emails often conflict

One of the top three classes I have ever taken. Workload is heavy but totally worth the learning experience. Listen closely to Dr. B's requirements and do try to impress him with your work. Dr. B is a great person, his classes are great while I could say that students who take him do graduate with an advantage compared to others who don't.

His class is super time consuming. The work is not difficult but the time constraints are ridiculous. He is often rude and dismissive. Not a fan and will avoid taking a class with him again at all costs.
Great prof! Probably learned more from him than any others. There were times I wanted to wring his neck, but loved the class and really enjoyed his teaching.

Good teacher, fun and does everything to make it interesting. Very timeconsuming class. Likes a LOT of participation and expects students to turn up to every class with articles about marketing, ready to explain them. Long very TIMECONSUMING project. Pick your team wisely. Quiz is 100 multiple choice and a few calculations or paragraph questions.

Prof. B's class was great!  I am not in a marketing concentration, but I still enjoyed the class.  It's not easy by any strech of the imagination.  You have to put in the work, but its well worth it.  He will teach you a lot if you are willing to learn and have an open mind.

Lots of weird pop quizzes and such to make sure you attend class regularly. Lectures for the full 2 hours without encouraging nor permitting significant student participation. Big group project at the end of the class that you will most likely not enjoy. Would not take this professor again.
Prof. B, is amazing. His class is fun, intense and interesting.
Outstanding, very knowledgable, very helpful and personally kind.

This professor is great. If you would like to learn a great deal about marketing and stretch your intellect, take this course. You will not regret it. Most importantly B. is great professor. His class is entraining as well as challenging and he is very fair in his grading system.
This professor is outstanding!

If you want the free ride and an easy grade, skip his class. If you want to learn about Mktg from the best, register now. He pushes you but helps you learn - I would like to study under him post-grad.
No Comments
****in Awesome!
Prof is well versed on the topic of Marketing. Great reference, if you are on his "good side." Lectures are jam-packed full of info. Hard exams.
I learned tons in this class.  He knows alot about what he is teaching.
Worst teacher ever
No Comments
Worst teacher ever!  Cannot communicate well with students. His final was crap. Most of the questions on that test he hardly went over in class

Is intimidating b/c he is rude and big headed.  This professor is full of himself and is unreasonable in his test.  You shouldn't be tested on material you were not taught. Marketing should be fun but b/c of him, it is not my minor.
Worst professor on campus
yelled at me for no good reason.  Very boring and gives out way too much work to do in short periods of time.
Very unfriendly and unpleasant.  Does not show any interest in his students.

super nice lady, didn't learn that much but my class was really big and i think she did her best. she's very likable and sweet and seems really knowledgeable in 1:1 conversations but the class itself wasn't that great (we watched a lot of movies/shows in class). very easy and i would take another higher level class w/ her again!
Professor Berliner is super nice and encorages class discussion. Sometimes her lectures are a bit shallow and short but the class is fun.

This class was great. It was super easy, you learned a lot, but it didn't require too much effort and no frustration. The workload was very appropriate and never felt unnecessary. Wasn't my favorite professor bc I didn't get a chance to connect too much, but it was a huge class, so makes sense. She was nice and understanding.

Introduction to Analyzing Media was a great course. Learnt about the technical aspects of media analysis and the external factors that influenced the production of the media works. There are two handwritten pages due every week but the topic you write about addressing the prompt is quite flexible. There are in-class discussions for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's very nice and the material was interesting and relating to current topics. I liked that she allowed us to pick what topics to write about for the weekly assignments, and is overall easy to talk to. Easy grader, lovely prof.

Very nice person, could be a better teacher. Assignments are interesting but the flipped classroom format - and focus on video lectures - is not my favorite. I would've preferred more in-person lecturing rather than just doing activities and being reminded of due dates. Kinda left us hanging for the final.

She's nice but not a good lecturer, just reads off of the slides and recites quotes in lectures. The class is not stimulating at all, very repetitive structure. She gave us a mid-quarter survey but didn't even acknowledge it. Please take any other teacher.

Great for the MCS core class. A media studies class first thing in the morning isn't the greatest but that's not her fault. The class is mostly doing readings every week and participating in class discussions with an interesting final project. Teacher is nice and gives great feedback on writing.
This class was a trainwreck. Anyone else in this online class will tell you the same if not more. At least she seems nice and the class is easy. Just don't take her online.

She seems to be a good teacher if you take her in person. Don't bother taking 313 with her online, the class is structured terribly and the content itself is dated. She also just...doesn't communicate. This was my second time taking it with a different topic, and I preferred the other one I took significantly.

LB is really sweet and I really enjoyed being in her presence, but the class overall was unsatisfying. We rarely strayed from the same lecture/discussion style and it grew tiresome by week 3. Discussions remained surface-level at best, sometimes troublesomely so. I wouldn't recommend this class. Lots of reading and writing for next to no payoff.

I took her visual culture class last winter. Good class content ruined by the format of hyrbid learning. Limited face-to-face interaction wasn't the best. Nice teacher who is willing to work with you outside of class. Make sure you don't get confused on the Friday writing assignments and turn them in at NOON instead of midnight.

As others say, if you're an MCS major and need this class, she's the best available. Her lectures are great and super engaging. Assignments, especially writing, are very open-ended. Final project can be done in groups or by yourself, and you can do any medium for it. Attendance is required in-person because of how she grades participation.

Nice teacher, very clear with grading and feedback, but the class was kind of easy for a 400-level. Long lectures and lots of hand-holding through concepts. She does help students out a LOT which is nice.

Great teacher. Kind and easy to understand. Weekly multiple-choice quizzes based on readings that are just things she goes over in lecture (BEFORE the quizzes!), only 20-25 pages a week of interesting reading material, and a flexible final group project, with some little assignments. Really easy if you pay attention.

I have taken 2 classes with LB and she is one of my favorite teachers! I especially liked 473 (visual com). She is funny and I love her lectures! Helpful in class and offers alternate explanations when needed, and is very quick at responding to email. Assigns a lot of reading but isn't too bad and always discussed in class. Easy to get 3.9 or 4.0.

Solid lectures, very informative on the topic but she also takes the time to make sure that students understand the material. I would take a class from her again. Really, REALLY helpful over email and office hours. Put in the time, participate, follow the prompts, and you'll do great.
She brought her bunnies to class (they’re the cutest!) on Tuesday and I feel like giving her a 5 here is the least I can do. Class is relatively easy and she is very nice.

Professor LB was hands down my most favorite professor here. I took two of her classes (333 and 473) and learned so much from her. She loves what she does and that shows in her assignments and lectures, especially in 473 which is based on her PhD work. There are many readings but they're not hard. I grew a lot as a writer thanks to her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She is good at lecturing and explaining concepts, but a slow grader and not the best with feedback or facilitating class discussions (at least in this class). Sometimes I felt like I was back in undergrad with her teaching style - perhaps she is a god teacher at the undergrad level, but I would avoid her in the MACS program.

Awesome teacher, great lectures, great explanations for everything, and is super caring about her students. Lots of written work but it's not too hard. Take her class - or any with her, to be honest - if you have the chance! One of the most important classes for the MCS major and she's UNDENIABLY the best prof available.

I love Professor LB! At first it seemed like a lot of work but this was one of the best classes I've taken at UWB. The readings aren't intense even if there is a lot, and there's lots of weekly writing assignments, but she's not a hard grader. Really nice person too.

Professor Berliner is a very nice teacher who is also very organized. Helpful in office hours and stays around after class to help struggling students. Tough grader but still manageable because the workload is not heavy. Compared to what I hear about the other options for the MCS core course, she is much better.

She's a very nice, helpful, and organized teacher who communicates clearly. The problem, however, is her extremely inconsistent grading and over-reliance on exams and other objective forms of "mastery" aside from the final media project. I would have given her 1/5 for her terrible, terrible puns but she's too nice to deserve that.

LB is nice and her video lectures are informative, but the synchronous class days are useless. Explains everything really well but the examples given are somewhat outdated, which is understandable given her age. For someone interested in internet culture, this was a good enough class, though. Hope she's better in person - I'm taking her again fall.

Not accommodating AT ALL, and very hard to get in touch with outside of class. This had the potential to be a great class as the information was very valuable and interesting, but the format of the class really ruined it. Has really detailed video lectures for asynchronous days but synchronous class always ends early. I hope she's better in person.

Aside from this class being incredibly boring, she comes off as passive-aggressive when students don't do things and is extremely slow at putting grades in and responding to emails. Class is easy, just put in some effort and make sure to turn it in on time. The way she grades participation is ridiculous and incredibly biased.

I found everything about this class to be horrible. The content was boring and irrelevant to daily life. This class was more of a burden and I do not feel like there was any educational gain from it. She also requires lots of participation during zoom classes and puts people in small groups most of the time. Others may like this class but I didnt.

Great teacher, nice person, but awful grading scale. Amount of work assigned is alright, but the way she grades it is really unbalanced because she can be overly critical if it doesn't fit exactly what she thinks. The way she grades participation is ridiculous, I don't think it should be this way (everyone starts with 80% until they "do things").

This class was very interesting, LB is fun, interesting and tries hard to include everyone. There's a lot of reading and written work but I think even though the class stretched my workload I am very thankful for the opportunity! Discussions are interesting and she's very nice! If you put in the effort you'll be fine.

Great professor who ALWAYS comes to class with a solid plan. Lectures are very student-centered. Very knowledgeable on the class content and very capable of supporting students in a variety of ways, because some of the content is hard to understand. Adapted very well to Zoom.

I absolutely LOVE her. She provides a lot of examples for the concepts presented in class and is quick to respond to emails. I've also found a lot of the concepts she discusses in class to be interesting. The workload isn't too expansive and there aren't any tests but there usually is a group project by the end of the quarter (pretty easy).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Berliner was kind and had the intention of being informative on the subject of MCS, but sometimes it felt as if this was her first class she was teaching. She also seemed a bit distracted and it was hard to get her attention. Lectures were not engaging in content and class led discussions were definitely the best part. I liked the class.

I really liked Professor Berliner, she's a really nice teacher who really understood the plight of students.   She even canceled one of the papers because she felt like we had too much as it was!   attendance isn't mandatory but she often gave extra credit to us who did.   fair amount of group work but nothing outlandish.   Not to mention shes cute
This professor was good. She was clear and concise with what she wanted. The material made sense and helped with the overall class structure. Overall great class and professor.
Enthusiastic, intelligent, supportive. Loved this class, loved Berliner. Lots of work, but worth it considering the subject.
Hard grade, hard assignment. I did not learn too much in this class.
She is a great instructor.  She does give a fair amount of homework/readings, but it is not overwhelming. I would definitely take one of her classes again.
She is very helpful!
The professor is amazing, easy homework assignments but intellectually stimulating materials and concepts, great feedback, and immediate responses. I wish I could take all my classes with him.
Best professor at UWB by far! Such a kind and caring professor :)

Ben Gardner is without a doubt the best professor I have had. His lectures tend to be very engaging because he is very enthusiastic about what he is talking about. A great deal of the homework is completed in class. He has a midterm and final knowledge assessment, which have been the easiest midterm and final test I have had in any of my classes.

Very good professor, everything is graded based on participation. You complete the assignments and you will get 100% on every assignment besides the factoids which he actually grades and he is lenient with grading that as well. Can do the in-class tasks at home during the time he teaches and can still receive credit.

I had professor Gardner for  Introduction to Globalization. Little work to be done out of class. Grades very graciously. Easy 100% class if you try. Fun and engaging too, he is incredibly passionate. He will go as far as to email you to ask you if you need more time if something is late/ not submitted. So far the best class/ professor I've taken.

Professor Gardener is an absolute inspiration, and combined his expertise on Sudan with class dialogues and group projects to seriously solidify meaningful topics in students. 10/10 amazing human being, class content, and projects. Lots of reading, but it's never too hard and quite fun in all honesty.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great teacher for intro to global studies. I like how he took the concepts we were learning and helped us think about their applications in the real world, and how he always tries to engage students and make everyone feel comfortable in class. He's good at breaking down complex and abstract concepts in social science for students.

Ben is one of THE BEST professors I've had here. Humorous, encouraging, and very supportive of you and your learning. As long as you make an effort to engage with the work, there is no reason to not do well. Provides a safe space for thoughtful discussion in class. Truly an excellent professor.

Professor Gardner: - Sprinkles in humor in the lectures to make the learning process enjoyable. - Amazing lectures. Well-organized, compartmentalized, powerful orator. - Eloquent, articulate, charismatic, and inspirational. A seasoned professor, can read his class well, make adjustments, and has a clear passion for teaching.

Amazing professor. Encourages group discussions and creativity instead of simply giving long lectures. Provides feedback on ways to improve and is always present when needed. Simplifies coursework to create a better understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Awesome prof. He is really good about doing a variety of activities & engaging the class. Gives really good feedback on essays and wants to see you succeed. Two "facilitations" which were probably the most fun/painless group presentations I have ever done. Go to class, do the readings, and engage and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very good teacher and very helpful when you need help. Plus he makes the class very engaging and not boring at all. Very good teacher and would take a class from again if I can.

I thought it would be another research class (researching then writing the paper.) I was wrong. Prof Gardner makes the class engaging as a whole! He's very enthusiastic and uses a lot of interesting activities pertaining to the topic of culture. The research process was different than I expected, but it helped. I'm taking him again next quarter!

After 4 years of college Gardner remains one of the best, if not THE best professor I've ever had. He is clear in class and loves what he does. The subject matter wasn't something I was even interested in but he made me passionate about it. Can't say enough about how great he is. Still say hello every time i see him in the halls.
Very subjective grader. Seems to place a label upon people and what grade they should receive. Hard to get solid feedback to improve. If you don't feel it the first day, drop the class.

Super passionate about his teaching and the topics. He extends out to all of his students and encourages many ideas even from the quieter people. He sets the classroom up to be a fun, understanding, and respectful area and makes everyone comfortable. Great Prof.

Enthusiastic! That's the word for Ben. He enjoys teaching and it shows. The class is well organized, engaging and fun. I learned a lot, now have several good writing samples for my portfolio and made a few friends through all of the mini group projects. I recommend Ben for any course.

He's one of the best professors I've had at UWB. His classes are always well-organized and proceed in a logical manner. His teaching style is flexible and engaging. Very fun and enthusiastic professor!

Professor was very organized from the beginning. Readings were very interesting, he's energetic, and will steer you towards in-depth questions of topics being covered - without drowning students in work. In my opinion he's a top notch professor.
Professor Ben is very encouraging and energetic which makes his class a lot of fun! I went in with attitude it was "Just" a core course but I am amazed at how much I learned! Highly Recommend!
Well organized and helpful. Much to read but it is all very interesting. Very nice instructor and course.

This course was about something different than I expected. Ben worked hard to make sure the students understood core concpets. He uses a lot of different mediums and activities to teach to concepts and methods. Ben answered e-mails and is flexible with office hours. Only complaint was how long it took to get graded papers back.

Assignments not clear. Doesn't seem interested in helping students before or after class. Stay or go based on your first gut feeling on the first or second day of the class.  If you think bail, then do.

wonderful course.. second I have taken from Prof Gardner.  He is highly organized and his energetic attitude is infectious. This prof cares very much that his students get what he is trying to say, he frequently requests student input.  There is a lot of work in this class but each and every reading and assignment has value and meaning.

I think Ben is a great teacher, he always come to class in a great mood and is very organized .He is very good at engaging the class and makes sure every one gets a chance to speak up. I also like how he treats his class like a community, so if someone falls asleep or do something dumb(and people have) he will know, even if you dont think he does.

professor blancas does not grade papers that are heavy weighted until the last few weeks of the quarter, doesn't give feedback on them either until grades r due. lots of busy work and not formatted well, class is not compelling.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maria is a nice lady but her lectures aren't always compelling, feels like shes just reading off the slides. Assigns work but doesn't really feel like its meaningful. Doesn't rly provide feedback but isnt a tough grader, shes alright. Easy A class tho
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes very kind but her instructions on assignments are very unclear..  i also dont feel like im learning very much currently. we have papers to write but the lectures dont give a good base for me to write. like idk how im supposed to write about certain theories if we didnt even cover it in class.

Beware of his unclear grading system. He obviously cares about what he is teaching, but the joy of his class immediately ceases whenever you get unclear feedback from either him or the assigned grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: there was a lot of work but i appreciate his honest interest in students and the material. unlike a lot of students i see, i value actually learning about things, and i notice that students like me tend to take his classes so i did too and i didnt regret it. props.

Overall it's a ok or above ok prof. You need to put some effort to the class. The contract grading generally fit for your performance through out the quarter. If you have a better option then you may want to consider it but the course itself is quite creative and well prepared. The prof is also a easy speaking person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Berger is a great teacher and person. He prioritizes depth over breadth and encourage students to be thoughtful, creative, and reflective. He is fair in his grading and deeply knowledgeable about the class content.

This professor has the most unclear grading. You go the entire quarter thinking you have one grade cause of your completion of the assignments and your percentage grade, but at the end of the quarter your surprised on the last day. I had a 100 the entire time and ended with a 3.2. 'contract grading' Don't take this professor and save your gpa!

He is ok. His lectures are really dense but he allows you to take breaks and ask questions. He cares a lot about what he teaches, though he sometimes forgets that most people taking the class have only a little bit of background in it. Many assignments are just graded on completion with little feedback. He's a nice guy though.

This professor is extremely unclear about grading. You progress through the class thinking you're doing fine because of his feedback and then get a surprise when final grades come. He's a nice guy and class has interesting readings, but the grading was unbearable. Core class for my major in AES, try to have a different prof if you need this class.
Nice guy, smart professor, and fair grader. He expects you to work hard but you will really know your stuff after his class. His lectures and assignments are interesting and informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Lots of reading and a big research assignment at the end. Dr. Berger is a nice guy and wants students to do well, but it is somewhat difficult to get a high grade on writing assignments because of his grading methods. He tends to go on tangents during lectures. Overall, it's not terrible, but isn't easy.
His class is fine. JUST DO THE WORK! Homework is fairly straightforward. Contract grading method isn't too bad.

Most confusing grading system ever. The beginning of the quarter he has us "sign a contract" asking us what our goal is in terms of final grade. He marks every single assignment either complete or incomplete with no feedback. The last week of class he tells us what grade he thinks we got. The whole quarter we are oblivious if we met his standards
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's very nice and easy to work with, especially if you ask questions and show engagement. I like his assignments, they help me engage with material better than other profs have. This is a very good class for students interested in history. This quarter was his first time teaching this class (American ethnic history) and he is good at it so far.

I get the bad ratings - he's not for everyone. He's in his element when he doesn't rely on his PowerPoints and just lectures. He's easy to work with as long as you are willing to engage. I have taken multiple classes from him now and they were interesting and informative, but do require some significant effort on your part. Not that hard a grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I did NOT like this class. I found Prof. Berger to be pretty narrow minded and unclear with instructions. His class was also a lot of work. He took a potentially interesting topic and kinda butchered it. He was nice enough, but I wouldn’t recommend his class.

Dr. Bergers class is not an easy A but thats okay because it's still doable! If you are confused with anything, hes always happy to chat 1-on-1 and answer any questions with kindness & grace. He'll recognize your hard work and it will be worth it! Everything you read & learn is interesting and applicable to your research and overall knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dan Berger teaching the history of mass incarceration pretty much tanked a lot of student's grades. He is very for abolishing the prison system in the U.S. and if you are pro prison, then your opinion will not matter to him. He will mark you off points if you have anything that supports U.S. prison systems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I have some mixed feelings for Dan. He is a really tough grader, and sometimes his feedback contradicts with what you would like to write about, but overall he helps out a lot with developing your research questions. He also is really understanding, and quite funny. He adapted really well at the end of the quarter (all the COVID-19 stuff)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He expects you to reading a ridiculous amount and is a very hard grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very passionate about the subject and very knowledgeable but he is an extremely tough and inconsistent grader. Good luck figuring out his assignment instructions, even he doesn't know what he wants! Requires a ton of studying and if you want an easy 4.0 or just a 4.0 in general, this is not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst professor, and I learned nothing. His grading makes no sense, with little or disputable support. There was only four assignments related to course material. The assignment worth the bulk of your grade has nothing to do with class material. The instructor was confusing and pointless in my learning. If you want a suffering GPA, take Dan.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The worst, most unclear, & radical professor I've ever had. Voice an opinion that differs from his & your grades will suffer. He calls himself a prison abolitionist & when asked what we should do with the most violent offenders he avoided the question but said, "murder has the lowest rate of recidivism" & blatantly implied murderers be set free...

We had very different opinions, but he was the first prof at this school to let me speak my mind and grade me fairly, rather than allow political bias to cloud his judgement. He gave great feedback and gave me the real learning experience I wanted instead of an indoctrination session like most classes here. He was tough, but fair. I learned a lot.

I found Dan to be knowledgable, fair, and very helpful. He assigns a lot of reading, but it's worthwhile, and there are only a few other assignments you have to do (though they take some time). I also appreciate that he considers varying opinions, but also isn't afraid to challenge/correct people when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: WORST TEACHER EVER. Unclear instructions + subjective grader. Had to have like 3 books which was annoying, DENSE readings and we had to write about the readings but he was looking for an exact answer (5 discussions posts, can post more) group project at the end and it was graded individually so thank god but never again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very intelligent and well versed in subject. Extremely respectful. Always helpful answering any questions I had.  However, a lot of reading. You must do it, otherwise you won't do well. He's also a tough grader.

I took 4 courses that were led by Dan. My first course impressions is that he is boring. But I started to like him the more I took his classes. He is engaging, thoughtful and gives really good feedback. He really got me to think about my essays and how I construct my arguments. One of my favorite professors at UW Bothell.

I really liked Professor Dan Berger. His lectures were informative and concise. When you had questions about upcoming activities and assignments he would be very clear and specific. He know what he was professing and seemed very interested in the topic he was teaching. I would take this class again just to gain more insight of the topic.

He is one of the most unclear professors that I've ever had. It was as though everything on the syllabus should've been thrown out the window. I learned absolutely nothing from his class and felt like I just wasted my time. The course text book was used for only 2 weeks and the rest of the class readings were long, boring, and just irrelevant.

This guy is supposedly “one of the best professors at uwb.” I never got that vibe from him. He values his own interpretation of the “real world” skills more than the actual course material and tests on the material and expects people to do well. Not accommodating and a tough grader. Very not clear rubrics that don't explain what he is looking for.

Captain Anderson is the best Professor I've taken a class from at UWB so far. Although a tough grader, he just holds his students to a high standard because he wants them to succeed in the future. His industry knowledge, unbridled enthusiasm, and practical advice make him such an asset to the college. Can't wait to take more classes from him.
Best professor ever! He brought real life problems to the lecture.
Great teacher, knows his stuff, lectures are very to the point, he gets right down to business efficiently!
Intelligent and genuine. This is not an easy A class but you will leave satisfied knowing youre leaving with a lot more knowledge on the topic than when you first came in.
Awesome professor. Super knowledgeable with a concrete background in both psychology and CS. Pay attention in lectures and use his study guides and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Bill is a nice guy. He's super chatty, and hard to pay attention to at times. He's really chill in terms of letting you turn in things late, but your work better be high quality. He does have a fair curving policy with the quizzes. We never got to see our grades for the final and 2 final projects, but based on our course grades, he was harsh.
Lots of reading.

One of the first professors for my Grad Course, is among those few professors on earth who indeed "Mentor & Guide" the students. With exceptional Knowledge of Computer Science his lectures had a tinge of Multi-Disciplinary concepts like Healthcare, Psychology, Marketing, etc. amalgamated with Technology. ThoughtResearch based exams & assignments.
Outstanding professor with a deep knowledge of software design. This was easily one of the best courses I've had.
I loved his class. It's full of energy and very less burden. He is an enthusiastic and very helping professor.
He is a great professor.

Any class of his will be a departure from your other CS classes.  Get ready for a psychological, sociological, management and design centric whallop.  You'll feel like material is 'fluffy' until you get toward the end.  It's good value despite the right brain loading.  I took two classes and they overlapped in material quite a bit.
Great teacher. Teaches by example, examples/stories are interesting. Tests are essay based, but graded fairly. HW is minimal, and mostly involves reading. Concepts described are extremely useful.

Note this review is for CSS 497 (in my case an internship), so there was no teaching involved. He didn't respond to almost any of my emails, but was helpful in setting up my contract and preparing for my presentation. I received an appropriate grade.

Very good professor with real-world knowledge. Uses good textbooks. Lectures are very interesting, and you are given freedom in designing your own project. Fair grader. You will really know networking after his class, which I thought can be very valuable for anyone in the CSS program.
Made an otherwise non-entertaining subject (management) fairly interesting. He is very interested in the learning of his students and will always provide feedback if asked.
Erdly always has a story to tell from the industry.  Entertaining and passionate about his subjects.  This guy is like superman for the Computer Science department.
No Comments
Great Prof. you will learn.
Prof Bimal is a true educator for teachers
Join his class, really is a philosopher, takes you into a journey of true education..
Great educator, fun to have as a tough professor, humble but tough

Very knowledgeable, uses collaborative approach, gives prompt feedback, flexible, tough with policies and attendance. Very friendly and easy to talk to for feedback. Surely recommend for future students.
educated, experience and very professional, particular about time and deadlines.
Loved the readings but he NEVER talked about them. We talked about the "questions" people had about the readings and watched a video. Boring
