His class average GPA for the quarter was 1.8 and the average score for his final exam was 57%. He fails his students just as much as his students fail his class. Avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mann really cares about his students & tries to accommodate needs. The structure of this class is what fell short for me. Every day of class there is a short quiz and each week there are two 1.5-2 hour lecture videos to take notes on, that ends up taking at least 4 hours to watch. I would take classes from him again, 300 just wasn't it for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: So. This teacher has some pretty understanding of his notes. But the lecture that we are supposed to watch almost 2 every week is way too much. I would have to sit there for 2 whole hours and do absolutely nothing but stare at the screen. Another thing that I had experienced was the quiz. Some of this quiz aren't even on the things he reached us.

Okay, this dude is one of the most overwhelming professors I have ever had, and this is only my first year of college. Not attending his lectures and not doing his homework is like asking to fail the class. His tests make you think if that he wants you to fail, because the quizzes are only 90 min, his written quizzes are way different from the hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes are from the weekly homework. Exams are not easy or hard, I think it was reasonable. Be on track and you will do fine. However, I feel that he is not much interest in student's learning. Also, he won't post solutions for the homework and exams. Graded only quizzes and exams so it was hard to get a good GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's an okay teacher, good with the concepts. Tests are worth a lot. Homework is a ton of work but very little credit. Has a midterm the week before the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr.Campbell was one of THE BEST professors I've had so far, she does a great job at explaining and clarifying concepts and the lab portion does a great job tying in with out lectures, amazing lab professor
The sweetest woman ever. Beyond helpful and easy to talk to. One of the many few classes I actually looked forward to going to. She is extremely nice

Genuinely such a nice &caring lab professor! If you are stuck in the lab she helps you understand why you're stuck and helps you also understand the concept that you are stuck on. She does talk a lot in the beginning of labs but I found that helpful at times where I wasn't sure about what we'll be doing in that lab day. Overall great lab Professor!

Genuinely such a caring and nice lab professor. If you are stuck in the lab process she will help you understand why your are stuck and how to learn from it. She does talk a lot during the beginning of labs but I found it very helpful for the labs where I didn't know much about what we will do. Overall a great lab professor!

She's great and can explain very well. She's passionate and wants to make sure you understand the topic before you leave. She acknowledges every questions and does not make you feel dumb for asking them.

This is an easy A for the lab section of bio 180. There are no big reports (just 2 questions submitted on canvas). A worksheet given in class (turned in at the end of class). The professor is super nice and very approachable.

I just wanted to hug her and say thank you a million times. What an amazing teacher, super energetic, super caring. She genuinely made learning enjoyable, instead of worrying about my grade 24/7 i could actually learn in her classroom. Take her any chance you get.
Very sweet and wonderful professor, she is very helpful and gives clear explanations.

Only way you could lose big points was not showing up or not trying at all. Lab was always fun and she really wants to help you learn the material. Very accessible outside of class. The way she teaches/lectures reminds me of an elementary school teacher--very excited and encouraging. She'll help you with whatever your having trouble on in labs.

Unlike other lab professors, she was sweet and calmed me. She knew her stuff and was understanding and gave clear grading criteria. She wasn't a hard grader cared for her students and would check in during our lab assignments. If you pay attention and go to the lecture part of the class then you'll have an easier time understanding the lab work.

Professor Campbell was unhelpful, overly strict on grading, and excessively talkative. Despite acknowledging our good work in person, the grades were consistently low. Additionally, their disregard for the lab manual caused delays, making us late. Would definitely not recommend for anyone to take this lab with her.

an incredibly sweet human, very caring & enthusiastic. she adores her job & does amazing teaching lab. looked forward to bio180 labs more bc of her. would love to take her for a lecture. she's full of energy when talking about course material & it's refreshing. DO NOT BE LATE, it's the only way to lose points really. 
A wonderful person.
the Best

She is very patient and wants to help you understand. Small workload and easy class. She's also a sweetheart plus I understood most of the projects we did because she was ready to explain it even though we had to read a manual the day before, which makes sense. I would take any other classes with her if it were possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Spent most of the lab talking about what to do even when the lab manual was on the desk and you're required to read it the day before coming in. Very enthusiastic. I respect her as a person but the way she runs the lab is not how I work. I can see how other people may love her, but she is not my cup of tea. Very harsh when even a little late.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors at uwb. She's extremely understanding and is always there if you need help no matter what. She's enthusiastic and her sense of humor brightens up the room. She also gives back great feedback and responds to emails quicker than I've seen any professor do. Such a queen I love her.

Love prof Campbell!!!!!! She responds to emails usually within a couple of hours or at least within a day, quickly and thoroughly. Her husband on the other hand... Let's just say that I wish Dana had taught the lectures instead of him.

Dana is a sweetheart. Literally the happiest person you'll ever meet in your life AND she's super patient and passionate about what she does. She's a prime example on how ALL lab instructors should be like ! Like most labs, all we had to do is a pre-summary, comprehension quiz, and lab work -- she responds to all inquiries LIGHTNING fast.

Best lab prof I've ever had. Extremely enthusiastic, kind, and caring. Teaches bio with clarity and ease and responds quickly. Labs were super educational and fun because she was teaching them. I learned more from her than I did in the lecture. Slow to grade, but I wasn't nervous about my results because I was so confident in her teaching ability.

Dr. Campbell is a breath of fresh air. She puts in the time and cares about students. She gives good feedback and is super accessible over email. I just wish some things were graded a bit quicker so we had more sense of our lab grade but that was a small thing! She is pretty fair and definitely choose her for lab-the kindest ever!
She should've taught the lecture instead of the lab; she's easy to understand, enthusiastic, and I thoroughly enjoyed the labs

Take her for lab, you won't regret it. Definitely one of the best lab profs at UWB. Her in class overviews of lab are very thorough and her sense of humor and enthusiasm about the content make them fun to listen to. No matter how dumb your question is, she will answer with zero judgment. Great prof overall who creates a safe learning space.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Campbell taught me more than my main biology professor. Her enthusiasm each lab was always comforting and inviting. She explained concepts very well and truly cares about students success!

Dr. Campbell is sweet, caring and extremely responsive. She listens to your struggles, stress, questions. She replies emails at 12AM (which proves she is a kind person tbh). Lab is easy to follow, you have to pay attention and that's it. No tricky questions, or make you feel like you're in a dead end. Her small lectures are funny, she's goofy LOL
Definitely one of the better bio lab professors, she should've taught lecture instead of Chang tbh

She's a tough grader, but honestly one of my favorite professors. Her essays were a challenge :( that said, her feedback was really helpful and I improved a lot after. Her lectures are long, so be ready for that, but she's super knowledgeable and actually engaging to listen to. If she teaches another class, I'd 100% take her again.

This is for BHS 302, Celia's clearly passionate about what she teaches, wants to help you grow as a student+very transparent about grading, there is a lack of rubric so reach out to her so she can review your papers. Lots of reading but not up to her jurisdiction, but required by the BHS dept. Very intelligent and you can learn a lot from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Gorbman is the best professor I have ever had. Shes a tough grader on papers, but her feedback goes above and beyond and she allows revisions which is very generous. She knows what she's talking about and gives incredible lectures, you can tell she is very passionate. I learned so much in the class. You should take a class from her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
It says 201, but its actually BHS 302

If you cant keep up with lots of readings, or group work and you like to procrastinate, then this class isnt for you lol. She is one of the best professors i have ever had, but you need to pull ur weight, you will not get away with skipping readings or classes.learned so much, def lots of group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class was really good and ran well. Dr. Gorbman's class required attendance, collaboration and discussion in order to do well on quizzes and participation activities. Her final was hard but you could do well if you studied. She made sure we were on top of things and checked in with us a lot so we didn't fall behind.

Professor Gorbman was a really amazing professor who made this class better due to her enthusiasm and affability. She fostered a really open and great class environment where we could openly discuss important topics. I also appreciated the organization of the class as everything was straightforward for what we were doing and expectations.

Professor Gorman is the sweetest professor ever. Her lectures are interesting and cares deeply for her students; she genuinely wants them to pass and learn something out of the course. If you study off her lectures and online content I promise you will pass. I honestly wish her all the best. I am looking forward to taking her in the Autumn.

Ceri Nishihara was a very frustrating professor to work with. The canvas layout was poor and made navigating through projects a nightmare, project guidelines were poorly defined, participation was expected in class (I took her online) and her guideline for how participation was graded was "if I remember your name you will get points".

Not sure how Ceri got any negative reviews. Amazing professor that cares about her students! She's hilarious and so passionate about the material she teaches! She does care a lot about participation as she does use conversations style lectures to help tie in lecture concepts with everyday life. 10/10 would recommend! I will also take her again!

Not sure what the negative reviews are about...Ceri is your standard marketing teacher. Class sessions are discussions so bring something to talk about but she doesn't call on people. Obviously you need to read the chapters of the textbook (available for free) and complete the homework. This is an easy A course if you put in any effort whatsoever.

I've taken 3 classes with her and I would take more if I could! She's an amazing teacher, my favorite one in all UWB. It's not an easy class, but it's so worth it if you put in the work. She doesn't treat her students as dumb people, she treats you with respect and pushes you to be better; she's really open to communication. Love her!

WOW. Why do students have to pay for this? WASTE OF TIME WASTE OF MONEY. Class is an absolute waste of time, just lets students babble on for 2 hours, then she gives a quiz that is based solely from the book and stuff she has never once mentioned, oh yeah the quiz on 2 chapters is just writing a 6 page paper. wow. not a teacher. REFUND??

she is the only professor who ever made me feel down on myself. She would often ignore many things I said and made me feel like I was annoying in class. Toward the end it got worse. I had a 90+ on 2/3 exams and then suddenly the last one she gave me a 60 and didn't reply at all to requests to understand why. 10/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. I do not recommend taking her. Lectures have very little to do with what is on the exam. She grades extremely tough. Exams are all based on the book, so don't even pay attention in class. I have no clue how she grades participation, probably randomly cause she never takes role. Overall, a cool person, but very bad teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This professor doesn't provide feedback. Once you finished the quarter, she doesn't even respond emails. Hard to reach, and if she doesn't agreed with your comments while attending class, be careful, she might discount points from you participation. If you have different opinions, she will punish you. Don't recommend this class.
You think the class is easy even if you study and do all the work but then you end up with random questions on the exam that have never been covered in the book or lectures.
Lectures and interesting and straight forward. She is a tough grader, but will help you out if you're struggling.

She's super knowledgeable about rhetoric and speeches, but the reading and lectures were long, boring and not super discussion based. She's very nice, but grades hard and expects you to know small details about the speeches. I studied more for this class than my other two combined.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You need to pay attentions, do all the readings, and take a lot of notes in order to get a good grade in her class. Overall, she is a great professor. I like her class.
She does a very good job of having her students know what to expect on a test, but most of us got pretty bored because of the repetition. It was cool to read the historical speeches though.

I have never hated a class more. If u don't have a life and can commit to drawing multiple good drawings every single day, don't do it. My roommate had him as well and we both absolutely hate him. He also doesn't respond to emails. I think he gets joy from students suffering. I'd rather have a chem lab every day of the week than take this again.

This man has made me hate art. No matter what you do, he finds a way to grade you below what you deserve. I don't care if he's nice. He doesn't appreciate art unless it's the way he wants it. Don't take this class and save yourself.

worst class I've taken in 5 years of college. The online structure is disorganized, assignments were due before prior weeks were finished. More work than my other two business classes combined. Unless you're passionate about drawing, avoid this class. Too much work with 10+ drawings and weekly peer comments makes it overwhelming. you'll fall behind

Tbh half of the class submitted stick figures in the discussions and spent about 5 minutes on their weekly drawings. I'm a pretty bad artist and I was able to pull a 4.0. He asks that you spend 3+ hours each week on the drawings, but I was able to get away with maybe 1 hour for the weekend drawing and an hour for the weekly sketch book assignment.

Class is homework heavy and very easy to fall behind. Not worth taking unless you really like art or have 7 plus hours of free time a week. Materials are expensive and sometimes hard to find, especially the drawing pads. He's not a bad person, just hard to understand why he assigns and expects so much work for an intro class.

By far the most frustrating class I have ever taken. So much work every week it's horrible, all while having a terribly disorganized canvas page. 7 hours a week minimum drawing. Basically no creativity involved in this class just observational drawing. Never responds to emails. Recycles assignments made during covid. $100+ in art supplies.

sometimes he would assign a lot of random assignments all at once, be careful and manage your time wisely. theres a couple easy art projects and group projects, the group projects take a bit more effort, still easy. gary is very kind, helpful and a easy grader. gives out a lot of extra credit opportunities as well.

literally the worst ever I regret this decision so much he is horrible to work with and has some sort of artistic superiority complex that for some reason forces him to dock an insane amount of points with no reason as for why. do NOT recommend

This professor will set u up for failure, this is the one. At least 10 drawings a week, no email responses, and vague critiques make this class unbearable. He doesn't seem to understand not everyone is Picasso or has endless time for art. It's demoralizing, overwhelming, and feels like he's out to ruin your college experience.Avoid him at all costs

BCORE120: he was one of the professors. I think compared to the other professor who taught with him, he can be a little more serious with grading but had nice sarcasm & was laid back for the most part. This class was easy so it made him more relaxed. Didn't show up for the last 2 weeks of class but it's easy if your group puts in effort for final.

This professor was terrible. The first week of school I had to get an emergency surgery and I emailed all of my professors to let them know I wouldn't be able to come to my classes while I recover. He basically told me that if I could type the email then I can do the assignments.

its just busy work. he doesn't understand art is done in different ways, its either his way or the highway. If youre an artist just give him a meh piece of art work and youll get your points, he doesn't know how to appreciate art.
Lots of busy work, way too much work for the time given. I thought this class was going to be fun but it was mostly just busy work. Gave no feedback on points docked off.
too much busy work and unclear, sporadic grading

Do not take this intro to art class if you are looking for an "easy" class. Each week, you need to turn in 10 fully developed sketches; 1 fully rendered sketch; respond to 6 classmates on discussion boards, and the weekly learning activity (can be 1-3 assignments). It's so much homework for little points. Don't underestimate this class.

Attendance is highly recommended because the professor likes to spring random small assignments on you. Many weeks started with 1 assignment due but by the end of the week, you'd turn in 4-5. Don't be surprised if you miss points and see no comments on why you missed them. Many major projects were due a week after the assignment opened.

This teacher enjoys giving out busy work and will take off points without explaining exactly why he took off points. It's easy but be prepared for a lot of homework more than your other classes combined.
Professor is very good at assigning meaningless busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class and professor will stick with me for the rest of my life in the best way possible! I love professor carpenter and the ideas he spoke about during class. I looked forward to going to class everyday. As long as you do what is being asked and participate in class discussions, you will TOTALLY be good to go. absolutely amazing!!!!!!

Classes materials are clear. I like that he respects everyone's drawings and doesn't force or judge you based on your ability as I am not a good drawer. He's polite and the videos are nice. But he is so strict in deadlines which I think he should improve since not everyone has the same time schedule and life can be tough to some

Took two classes with him, the first was good but this course was challenging for an intro class. I would not recommend if you dont want a lot of homework. Hes respected and knowledgeable but I learned more from YouTube. He doesnt teach basics and expects you to get it which is hard for an intro class. Hes a good guy, but I regret taking it.

Super nice guy, you can tell how much he values teaching as well as the people who take his classes. His classes are fun, although they require a lot of creativity. He was my first class of the day and I loved starting my days with his class. His passion for teaching is very refreshing. Definitely recommend!

I don't understand why there is a rating of less than 5.0 on here. Gary is an AMAZING prof, and he cares deeply about his students. Gary is one of the professors that I wish would teach CS because of his attitude is super, super chill. Gary deserves all the 5.0s. He is just that awesome.

Gary is a very down to earth, and super knowledgable guy. I don't see why anyone wouldn't like him as a teacher- honestly. Minimal homework, creative journals every week that are pretty easy. He isn't a stickler for grammar or spelling so it's a very open ended class. He's a respectable guy and you can learn quite a lot from him.

Gary is an AMAZING guy. Very nice and caring. He gives a lot of homework which I feel is unnecessary for an intro class. But you dont have to be an amazing artist to do good in his class. Do the work, show effort, and you get the grade. If he gives you pointers/feedback try to take it and improve. A fairly easy A.

Gary is cool, can be boring especially with his ppt lectures. I did not find that necessary for this class. Attendance is mandatory. I took his class starting at 18 weeks pregnant so it was difficult for me to come to class alot but he understood. You have hw everyday but you get into a routine and its easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very easy class. You have homework everyday, but they are sketches. He does give you extra credit, which are extra sketches in the drawing notepad. As long as you do all the homework and show up to class then you will be golden.

He is resistant to those who take his class as an easy-A, but he doesn't make the class too hard. In his art courses, find and follow a passion and discuss with him your interests. Following the mechanics of an art form is only seen as a first step.  Nonetheless, he is very helpful in guiding this discovery, and I highly recommend his courses.
If you have a chance to take Gary's University Beyond Bars class, jump at the opportunity. Very rewarding!
Singlehandedly made me realize I am an artist! He may have just helped me find a new second career!  LOVE LOVE LOVE HIM!

Gary is a very nice and friendly professor. Helpful whenever you need it. Totally stress free. You don't have to be good, he likes effort. He will be lenient and understanding. Just do the art. I would say he is my favorite Prof.

Art classes are easy, just do the work, doesn't matter how good you are. I never read a thing, took him 3 times, got grades over 3.7-4.0. He can be confusing or boring, but an easy grade. He is very nice and talks to you like a person. Lenient on most things and understandable. Not a stressful teacher- a breeze.

Gary is a very friendly professor and cares a lot about what he is teaching. I really appreciated his attitude towards art and teaching it.  That said, I took the class over summer and it was 2 1/2 hrs of standing and drawing the same thing over and over again. Pretty boring at times. Beware the naked model!
Christy is a great professor and cares a lot about her students. Her lectures were fun and she will bring in snacks in class sometimes.

Great professor who made marketing easy to understand and engaging. The class was organized, helpful, and full of real-world examples. Attendance is mandatory, but you'll mostly submit answers on Menti in class. Overall, Christy is a great professor and cares about her students.
Amazing professor, super considerate towards her student's goals and outside life. She lets you redo a lot of assignments and she brings a lot of guest speakers. No complaints, loved Christy.

Johnson was sooo sweet. She is extremely accommodating and a really great ally if you try communicating with her. I think it's almost impossible to get full credit first try for an assignment but she gives a LOT of feedback, and you can redo most assignments as many times as you need. 
Most of the class we were doing our own research, no busy work.

She is good a teacher and let's u turn assignments whenever ur ready. A TOUGH grader which makes the class hard for a b core. Feedback is usually a page long. Assignments sometimes aren't clear and it happened multiple times throughout the quarter.

Christy is an awesome professor. Her content is always engaging. Be prepared to read many business cases and whitepapers in and outside class. She is the best professor to take 470 with. She uses the materials of Dr. Jones but is much nicer/forgiving/adaptable. She is a stickler for attendance and isn't Canvas-savvy.

One of my favorite professors at UWB! Christy is nice, caring and gave me a new perspective as to being an entrepreneur. Class is fantastic in terms of networking! She is new at UWB so her class structure is not perfect, however, she is willing to hear feedback. Lots of assignments that works up to a project and presentation you do at the end.

Your grade is based on the 2 exams and pearson HW. If ANY of the study guides were actually readable, they'd be useful, but deciphering hieroglyphics might be considered easier, grading system is 500 points (200-HW), (150- Exam 1) (150- Exam 2), she was passionate about the topic and cared about it, but struggled communicating the point.
Overall, she's a great professor. She doesn't explain concepts that well, but it's not hard material to grasp.

She seems passionate about the subject, but I wish there had been more structured lecturing in class. I personally did not have a very positive experience. During an appointment I scheduled with her, a comment she made came across as insensitive and made me uncomfortable. Overall, I would not recommend taking this class based on my experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: In my experience, Professor Charusheela is not like many of these reviews suggest. My biggest complaint is that the instructions on assignments were vague at times. Other than that, I had a wonderful time in her class. She is harsh on deadlines which shouldn't be a problem as she allows you to drop three assignments in case you need the wiggle room

Dr. Charu is not as bad as people make her out to be. Weekly Pearson assignment and two exams. This was a hybrid class so she had students watch lecture videos outside of class. She's a tad unorganized and doesn't always explain concepts well, but overall she's very smart. She's always willing to help if you need something.

Written instructions vague/ cryptic. Incredibly informative class lectures + discussions. One of the most passionate profs I've ever had. Office hours is an invaluable investment. Readings matter, her insights more. Say what you will about gripes, but she has my unfettered respect for her knowledge and vigor, albeit sometimes it's a bit much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For an intro class, the material should be more intuitive. The material itself is not difficult if you practice, but trying to do it yourself w/o help is an adventure. The provided materials don't always pertain to in class assignments. Teaching feels disconnected. Not asking for easy answers but it should not be this hard to figure homework out.
No compassion for anything. Do not take this professor.

Run! Unless you have to take this class for a major requirement, dont, otherwise Im sorry for you. There were almost no assignments in this class, There are two Major mid terms and a  final and those are worth 70% of your overall course grade which IMO is insane. the other 30% is Class participation and online "homework" (discussion boards)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm trying to spread my truth like people try to spread the gospel, yet my reviews keep getting taken down. Rambles on lectures, insults students, is not open to thoughts that differ from hers, her grading system is wack, gives no answers, only cryptic messages that feel like you're trying to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs.

She cares very much for the material, but the way she teaches it is so disconected, condencending, and convuluted. She tells you for the most part what you will be tested on, but to actually get a good grade or to write a good response she never goes into detail. Steer away.

her teaching style just didn't work for me (and most of the people in my class). it's almost a guarantee that she'll vent about something totally irrelevant to the course, and then try to cram all the classwork into the last 20 minutes of class.

Professor Charu is not the type of professor who will let minimal work/effort slide easily. If you are looking to learn and will genuinely put in effort, you will enjoy her class. She is a very compassionate person and wants to help her students, you just have to ask for help if you need it. Her teaching style is different but has helped me grow.

Extremely frustrating class. Manages to take 30-45 minutes to explain topics that could be explained in as many seconds. Class time feels wasted, especially considering she has long video lectures that are basically required as well. Her Canvas page is an unorganized mess, and her grading system is very unforgiving. Avoid this class at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She talks on volume 100 only; headache inducing. She does not provide any context for what will be on the exam until a few days before, which gives you no time to prepare. Doesn't weight the exams either; the mean was a 55%. She also makes you watch 2 hours of lectures, plus the homework and reading outside of her already 2 hour lecture in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: RUN

Although it was a hybrid class, she did not teach one bit in class, no ppts!! Her overall class was very boring. All she did was lecture and ramble on about random topics that never pertained to the lesson nor class. You learn through watching her weekly videos and doing in class worksheets in groups which hardly aligned with her lecture videos..

She loves to talk about herself even when she is presenting content pertinent to the class. She goes off on tangents. Overall, I can't stand her. Hardest prof I've had my entire college experience AND it's for an intro class. Lmfao. Avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's an okay Professor but her teaching style doesn't do students any good. she's very unorganized and would make you feel like you don't know anything if you can't answer your own question that you asked her. AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS

I took Microeconomics (BBUS220). She's a fair person with strong values but is quite hypocritical in expectations. Refused to give extensions to multiple students who came down with illness. Yet she delayed in grading when she became sick herself. Exam practice is provided ahead of time, which I recommend utilizing because the class is exam-heavy.

I thought Professor Charusheela was very fair and hilarious. She let us know exactly what would be on the exam beforehand for review days. We are sitting with the same table groups the whole quarter. It was fun to be with your group. For homework, she gave us a week to do it with unlimited tries. Get ready to read if you want to pass exams though.

I have mixed feelings about her. Classes are just her talking at you about random topics that don't pertain to the class. She is also super unorganized and forgot to upload assignments a lot. However, the quizzes are super easy bc they are the exact same as the practice, and the essays aren't too bad. Even so, I wouldn't recommend her.

She’s the reason why the world is terrible.  She thrives on “feeling” so smart. She’s full of it and treats people terribly, especially BIPOCs. She’s “woke”&  “progressive” but when anyone else competes for the spotlight, she destroys them. She’s no good

She never uses PPT's, all she does is lecture. She does however, give an exact outline for every exam and the exam is literally the exact same questions as the review, except different numbers. It's really hard to actually learn anything in this class, however it is an Easy A. Oh forgot to mention, she grades attendance...
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Charu is a phenomenal teacher, top 3 at UWB. Her passion for forward-thinking economics is contagious. Her teaching style, knowledge base, and care for students motivated me to work harder, she grades much clearer than other tough profs, a 4.0 is possible (I'm not a straight-4.0 student). Don't miss out on her class!

Professor Charusheela is passionate about her subject, but is horrible at teaching it. Makes really easy concepts complicated bc she expects you to learn terminology that she hasn't taught. She loves politics and the economy so if you love those two things take her, but don't be surprised if she makes you dislike them bc she gives heavy lectures.

Prof Charu only talks and doesn't use power points or anything. Most the time I doze off. She gives you the material that will be on the exam, so if you study it, then you can get an easy A. Coming to class is mandatory and will hurt your grade if you don't. There is a lot of reading, but I never do it and I expect an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very tough grader. Would deduct as much as 10 points per paper. On a grading scale of 475-500 as 4.0. That points are too much of a deduction already. According to Canvas statistics on grade, she never gives full credit on every paper. Research is worth 300 points out of 500, but yet never gave full credits even if you did your best. TOUGH GRADER!

I read the reviews before signing up for a class with this professor. Her organization style is so out of place. She makes simple concepts so COMPLEX (i.e. demand/supply). I would avoid her if you could. She doesn't use powerpoints, it's all dry lectures. Also, she's very strict with attendance, your grade will drop if you don't show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. with this women. I took it based off opium. I was totally excited but she never taught on this topic. She had us go watch videos on our own time in the library. Reading 40 pages on how to be a productive group member was a waste of time. Readings where ridiculous but the worst thing was her grading.

Very charismatic/fun professor. Assignments were reasonable and she wasn't an overly harsh grader. Three exams including the final weren't overly difficult or terribly easy, either, but each includes a long essay (think 1.5-3 full pages written out). Activities in class were a bit of a time sink - nice break in routine, but draining on the clock.

She is a very intelligent and nice person, however she is very unclear about every assignment which gets you to think about things in your own way which makes since given the class however its really frustrating because you never know how you're doing in the class or if you're doing good.I only have gotten 2 grades back this whole quarter..

Should have read the site before taking her class. Her instructions are confusing, her clarifying answers after the fact are even more so, and to top it off it takes her forever to grade assignments. I know this is a required class but if you have any other options for who to take it with do it. She is nice but not for this class

She's enthusiastic.. I guess that's cool. But what in the world? I can't figure out what I learned in this class. Her assignments are super confusing and I hate asking her questions. She never answers your question correctly... NEVER. I ask her one thing, she answers with something that has nothing to do with my question? NEVER GOT MY GRADES BACK.

Charu is very nice and VERY smart, but everyone showed up to class every day having NO idea what was going on. Her assignments are vague and her answers when you ask for clarification are cryptic. If you're like me (meaning, you need certainty and guidance), you're going to want to pull your hair out every day. VERY unclear teaching style.

Intelligent person, not a good teacher. assigns work without clear expectations. class is about critical thinking which is fine,does not do a great job of guiding the class. lectures for a long time and after the assignment in question and expectations becomes confusing. purpose of class starts out clear then becomes blurred later on in course.

Assigns lots of busy work. Lectures are long. Never clearly answers questions because the class is supposed to be about critical thinking. Grades very strict. Grades papers late. Gives assignments just days before they are due. Would not recommend taking her.
Very intelligent and enthusiastic. Good on office hours. Grades assignments late, harsh grader. Will never take her again

I took her for Interdisciplinary Inquiry, which is all about teaching people to think differently.  For those that say she doesn't make things clear, she isn't trying to. She wants you to think and come up with your own response. Very intelligent woman!!

This professor lectures, does not facilitate. Comments on work are very late in coming and often do not make sense. The course organization is extremely poor. Professor tends to ramble for long periods in class on topics of interest to her, that have little to do with the course. At times a bit hard on some students who are struggling with topics

Incredibly intelligent woman, but occasionally is unable to tailor her responses to the level of the student. A bit slow in turning back work. Overall, she's a fine professor with a passion for her subject.

Although the woman assigns a lot of work, doesn't hand back graded assignments until well after the next one is due, is vague with guidelines, get's confused about deadlines, and gets completely off course with class discussions, I really enjoyed her class! She has it set up so that all the hard stuff is out of the way by the last 3 weeks!

This prof couldn't keep up with what was due and was really unorganized. She's a really intelligent woman.. But not a great prof. She couldn't seem to get us back out first draft until after a second one was due. And was really vague about pretty much everything. AND sprung 5 papers due within DAYS.

He's honestly fine. Old man who makes a lot of errors in the work assigned and sometimes makes mistakes in lecture. But gives pretty good lectures. Workload isn't too bad, with weekly or biweekly SQL queries, two exams, and one group project. He gives clear feedback although sometimes pretty blunt but genuinely cares about students learning.

Absolutely terrible for 475. Homeworks make no sense half the time, grades harshly, test questions are clearly made 20 seconds before the test, expectations are high but gives no support to reach them. probably one of the worst professors ive had at uwb

He is by far one of the best instructors in the CSS department. 
Good - send out an "after-action report" after each class for asking anonymous questions/ suggest improvements for next class, you WILL have a good understanding of memory and pointers
Bad- course was structured 50% tests and 50% hw which made this a very hard class (may change)

Chenault simply treats all his students like professional Amazon developers (as he's worked there for many years). His lectures are so fast paced it's like a slideshow. Homework is akin to medium LeetCode SQL questions, tests are similar to HW but with a spin on it.  Would not recommend taking with another difficult class.

Professor Chenault is one of the best professors I've had at UWB. He cares SO much about his students and does everything he can to ensure that they understand and pass the class. He gives tons of feedback and he also does something unique among instructors: sending out feedback polls after each class to gauge our understanding.

Chenault has a lot of industry experience and it shows in his lectures. If you want to learn as much as you can, Chenault is a good instructor who will work hard to think deeply about your questions and challenge you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mr. Chenault is a good instructor but he has strict rules. CSS475 class you need an answer key for sure. If you don't know the answers, it is super hard to get good grades. He is also a hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have had at UW Bothell. Apparently he used to be really laid back, but now he has very strict expectations with very ambiguous assignment instructions. Also, he hasn't been able to adhere to a rubric at all. Not sure why he even uses them. Maybe he doesn't know how rubrics work? Anyways, I 10/10 recommend anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Solid choice for professor. At one point he gave an assignment almost the entire class failed, but other than that one mishap, he was one of the best CS professors at UW. He will help you understand your homework and answers all lecture questions. If I get the chance to pick him, he is always a safe choice for a good professor.

John probably cares more about his students than any other professor I've ever had. He genuinely wishes to present content in a way accessible to every student in the class, and actively seeks for criticisms of his own teaching. He explains things in a way that make perfect sense and is all around a tremendous teacher with real-world experience.

John genuinely he cares about his students. He constantly asks if everyone understands what is going on, and will repeat things as many times as needed until everyone gets it. He wants you to succeed and I respect that. Lectures were posted to Canvas, textbook says "required" but isn't, and for tests make sure to study the assessment quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You learn a lot from him! You can ask lots of questions in the class. Unlike other professors in the CSS, he doesn't make you feel stupid even you ask the same question multiple times. He is approachable, patient and respectful to students. He's not really a professional "teacher", but he does an amazing job! You'll just learn a lot.
Chill professor, and the homework load was manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very chill professor who clearly cares about us learning. Most of your grade depends on three quizzes that have the same weight as the final exam, which can be tough if you're bad at tests. Lots of group work, but he's very fair with deadlines. The most important part is finding a good team, and then Chini can be like a facilitator.

He is really nice and chill. The lectures are about 1 hour long, but sometimes not too organized or clear. The main thing is that he sometimes words exam questions in a weird way or puts stuff that we haven't covered, but he's a pretty lenient grader
97%+ to get a 4.0 for the class. No curve. Sometimes hard to study for what's on the midterm because they are not talked about or emphasized. Caring and kind, person in general though.

He's my favorite CS instructor. 1hr lecture, then class activity and you get to go home once you're done. His exams are a bit hard, but if you listen to his lectures and review the slides you'll do well. He likes to interact with students which made me like attending class more. The course is more than lectures and exams to him, he enjoys teaching.

The main thing in CSS 370 with Chini was to ask for clarifications and flexibility, which he was happy to supply. A friend and I found ourselves overwhelmed by vague assignment descriptions and tight due dates but we were able to negotiate more understandable and fair assignments. Essentially, he's enjoyable to work with while not being a pushover.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Chini is the best! I wish I could take him for all of my CS classes. He's extremely knowledgeable and his lectures are engaging. Even with no experience in coding I found Java easy to understand with him. He's very generous with grading and is always willing to help you if you need it. After taking his class, I know I want to major in CS.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Feel free to talk to Chini about questions/clarifications/concerns; you will need them. He can be flexible with due dates, which was essential because some assignments were very difficult to complete in the 24 hours we were given. At least grading was pretty lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's so nice and it's obvious he cares about his students. Make sure to do the readings or you'll regret it, I didn't and was a little lost during lectures. Pick a good group since you stick with them. The quizzes and tests are worth a LOT so really study for those. He lets you bring a notecard though, front and back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great person, funny lecturer, always gets to know his students! Hard grader, go to office hrs/meet him to understand feedback, hard to setup meetings. Offers extra credit and always open to discussing grades/giving back points. Quizzes r difficult but u can improve. Group projects not too heavy. Took him for CSS 360 & CSS 301. Would take him again!

Great person, funny/interactive lecturer, always gets to know his students! Hard grader, need to go to office hrs/meet w/ him to understand feedback but hard to setup meetings. Offers extra credit and always open to discussing grades/giving back points. Lots of easy reading assignments. Took him for CSS 301 and CSS 360, & would take him again!

OK professor, lectures are long (45 minutes). Workload is lowkey annoying, midterm practice doesnt help at all because midterms has stuff we have didnt go over. His TA graders are tough and take off points for such small things :( If you take this class be prepared to READ THE TEXBOOK EVERY WEEK! and stay on top of your work!! This class is hard

The homework is not too bad, only because you can use online resources. They can be very lengthy and tough. The MIDTERMS ARE THE WORST. The prep sheet was 75% useless, as it didn't even cover on the actual midterm. No curves and the average for midterm2 was was like 50% and professor thinks it's "expected",. JUST RUN HONESTLY! CHOOSE DHARMA DAILEY.

I would definitely take professor Chini again! His lectures are engaging and he makes it easy to understand the difficult material. When I read the book I'm lost, but he explains it so well that it clicks. The work itself is hard if you're new to coding like me, but he really cares about our success and tries to help us as much as he can.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Chini is good, but this class is by far the worst of the engineering curriculum. Chinis grading is very very harsh especially from what I've seen of some other professors. Chini is caring as a professor and willing to help
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class - be ready to put in work if you dont have any prior coding experience. Pay attention, do the work and you will be fine on the midterms as long as you make sure ur understanding things. Prof Chini is very nice happy to answer questions and seems to have a passion for what he is teaching, lectures can be long bec of that.

Professor Chini is very knowledgable, happy to answer questions, and has clear lectures and presentations. The coursework is not too difficult but challenging enough if you have been paying attention to the lectures and other homework assignments like readings and discussions.

Lots of reading that don't really relate to the lecture, good sense of humor, willing to help out, but the class description can be a bit misleading because you need to have a little prior coding experience or you will most likely struggle in this class unless you're da goat.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: do NOT take this class if you have little to zero knowledge on coding. all he does is lecture for 2 hours straight without actually walking you through what to write for code with examples. you can find the textbook online, but it's a hefty read every time. if you plan on taking this class, get to learning java beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be aware of the midterm. It's really hard and the practice ones didn't even look alike or cover some of the concepts in the actual midterm. Homework is not too bad but it can be quite lengthy. If you suck at logic based reasoning or coding in general, you'll struggle for sure unless your truly put in the effort.

Everything else that he does for the classes does not matter because at the end of the day, he does not allow open notes/note book for the tests. This is a CS class btw. It's important to mention it because every tech company doesn't care, in fact they encourage, you google the api, docs and stuff. Chini considers it cheating.
He is the best teacher I've had so far at UWB. Everything in the class was clear—what to do, how grading worked, and what to focus on. He also gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good lectures, nice, with a sense humor, though sometimes lectures didn't add much to the reading. If you do the practice problems you will do well on the exam, where he gives generous amounts of partial credit. Coding assignments are easy, though one time asked you to check for a tie for 2nd then check for a tie for 3rd in a 3 person race.

Lectures are clear and knowledgeable. He understands the material and teaches what he believes is necessary for students to understand. The group project is worth a lot of the grade but unfortunately, so are the tests. Tests and quizzes are just memory dumps of the material so just make sure to memorize what you go over in class.

Professor Chini is amazing and knowledgeable! Probably best in the department. This class overall isn't hard, but is reading/assignment heavy. The professor is super helpful and easy to reach even outside of class and will make sure to support in every way possible. He is a bit of a picky grader but gives clear feedback for future improvements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Chini is awesome! This course was easy. One thing was the other section of this class didn't have a final but this class did. All quiz/exam are open notes/book but no internet. Course consisted of a few at home quizzes, 2 group projects, one of them is a presentation. Find a good group!! As majority of your grade is based on group projects.

He is a great and caring professor, the only problem I had was his grading, you could complete a full weekly assignment with no bugs but forget 1 method level comment and get 2 points taken off, or if you forget to delete 1 line of code it's 1 point off. I understand he wants us to get better at these habits but not done well

Professor Chini is a phenomenal professor. Exams are open note, open book. His lectures are engaging and legitimately fun to listen to. He takes ALL student feedback VERY seriously, and is willing to fundamentally change the course structure to accommodate those recommendations. There are lots of readings, but they're easy as long as you keep up.

My first time rating a professor, and I must share about Professor Morteza. Take his course if you can! He prioritizes understanding over grades; don't get me wrong, his grading was good. The workload is heavy, but his clarity and care make it manageable. With three exams, group work, one final project, and presentation.

Class as a whole was fine, but the 1.5 hour lecture with a five minute break make you really bored. The in class assignments also do not open up until a certain time so you can't work on those until he finishes the lecture. Professor is amazing though. I would agree with others about study guides being meh. Take if you have some prior experience.
Tough grader, has an accent, too many reading assignments.

Embarking on the computer science journey with this class was like entering a maze without a map. Exams threw curveballs with untaught content, and the study guide was a mere decorative piece. This course was a rollercoaster of frustration and isolation, leaving me with a bad taste. Future adventurers, beware!

The computer science class I took left much to be desired. Exams were challenging due to unexpected material, and the study guide failed to provide meaningful guidance. The lack of support made the course a disappointing experience. Would caution others against taking it.

This computer science course was a disappointment. Exams included untaught material, and the study guide offered no real help. Seeking clarification during office hours proved fruitless, leaving students frustrated and unsupported. Overall, a subpar learning experience. Not recommended.

Outside of the test, the class is okay, it's lots of readings and lots of boring lectures. He has no idea how to make lectures interesting. But the test is what ruins it, the material he covers on the test is stuff he barley covered in class. He made a completely useless study guide and half the stuff on the test was not on the study guide.

easy going for most of the quarter but during the last 2 weeks he assigns a final group project that's like a 20-page research paper 2 days before a final exam which makes it extremely stressful. Additionally, he has the audacity to throw in a group presentation and some mini-sub assignments in there as well as if we already weren't busy enough.
RUN! Don't take this class if you don't have prior coding experience.

Professor Chini can be very intimidating at first but he does care for his students and their success. I really like how he encouraged us to join small group study sessions with a peer facilitator by offering extra credit which really boosted my grade. Although the class is very hard, as long as you stay on top of deadlines you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Chini is a kind and caring teacher. He is very invested in the success of his students. Because of his investment, he also grades very strictly. These strict standards are laid out in his 10-14 page requirements documents and the book chapters. Very reasonable, will negotiate due dates if you show him you are on top of your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I know many students will beg to differ but in my view, Professor Chini is an excellent professor. Make sure you read the textbook and come up with any questions you have. The exams are based on the textbook so make sure you really understand what you are reading. I wish I could take him for 143.

I like him as professor, he's a very nice guy. His class relied heavily on group assignment, choose good teammates or you will have horrible time. Quizzes honestly is not that hard, all on his slides, final is combined of the quizzes's question, you can easily get 75% for final, other 25% is diagram questions. His class has a lot of works though.

He is very knowledgeable and really nice when you ask him questions. However, he is very micromanaging: refuses to post slides before lectures, locks assignments until half-way through class. And what he says he wants is not what the assignments says, but you'll still get marked down 4 it. Didn't even show up for the final, despite requiring us too

Professor Chini makes learning how to code fun! He is very friendly and his lectures are very interesting. He loves to teach and genuinely cares about his students. He knows everyone in my class by name and wants to help you succeed! It is very easy to ask him for clarifications or questions when you are confused or need extra help! Great teacher!

Really friendly professor and is great if this is your first programming class. His lectures really go into the material and provides examples. Homework really isn't that hard, just put in effort and. There are coding assignments weekly so do them early the grade relies on how lenient the TA is. Midterms are also a reason for lower grades so study.

Chini's class was honestly fun. His grading is not confusing and he actually tries to help wherever you are struggling. only thing that sucked was his class was early in the morning. The group projects were fun to do, and do not procrastinate in this class. Overall, definitely take him if you can, fun class and fun person to talk to about things!

He's super nice, he remember everyone's name. Willing to answer and check the quality of work before turning in. The course is not hard, but it is critical that you find a good people in your team, because his grading criteria depend a lot on group activities and project, he also splits it into phases so not much pressure on deadline.

CS is hard, he'll be available, running around to answer all your questions to the best of his ability. Just take him, he has lots of knowledge in CS cause he used to be a developer himself, so anything you wanna ask him about the industry, he probably knows. Go onto YouTube and watch a few programming videos first if you're new.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Chini is great! You can take his class for 301. 301 is not easy; you need to figure out many details by yourself or ask some questions, but he is so patient and nice. He talks to every student with respect. I think he also has an amazing ppt set which can help you understand the textbook quickly.

Cares about the success of his students. Easy to approach and is accessible outside of class. Had no computer science knowledge before taking this class. Won't have a problem on exams if you fully understand the concepts taught in class. Just be prepared to do a good amount of studying and practicing in order to master the concepts. Optional final.
He cares a lot about his students, also he is very supportive, respectful, and intelligent. TAKE HIS CLASS.

Professor Chini is fast to respond to emails and he is really nice and caring, really wants you to succeed. I would say that his lectures in class are not really good at preparing you for in class assignments or the coding assignments, you will need to use outside resources. For exams they are all closed-book, so make sure you are prepared.

Chini for 350 is very easy, with almost the entire class being group work. The assignments are so easy, but get ready for a lot of reading. Skimming readings is an option, but he has 1-2 weekly reading assignments where you answer questions about the text. If you need an easy class to take with your heavy course load, take 350 with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Chini is an extremely kind professor. He always took student feedback seriously and would incorporate it into the course. The class was basically quizzes, reading HW, and 2 projects. All of these are pretty straightforward and he gives good guidance if you ask. Would take again 10/10
Professor Chini is a very kind professor. If you need CSS 350 or CSS 301, definitely take him!
Lost of homework, a lot of work, but he is such a great professor. So accessible and easy to talk to. The class is completely boring but he makes it a little interesting. TAKE HIM!!! DONT DOUBT IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you get a chance, just take him without any thinking. Source: Trust me bro!

Professor Chini is awesome! He's extremely extremely respectful which is very admirable, and he's sensitive to students needs and their work outside of his course. The class itself is straightforward, assignments every week, 3 quizzes, and a final project. Just work hard and he'll see it, even if you're online :)
Cares for his students a great deal. The class is VERY time consuming, but Chini is very willing to help. I hated the material, but Chini made the class tolerable.

Professor Chini is a really great guy. Although the grading process was really slow at times, he gave solid feedback and was very responsive to messages. Sometimes, it's hard to get to know someone when it's an online class with no lectures, but the class overall was super straightforward and the Professor was almost always available for feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While CSS 301 is a tough class, Professor Chini makes it a lot more bearable by giving great feedback on major writing assignments and having good humor during the lectures. His grading is pretty tough on assignments, but not at all unfair given his explanations in his feedback. Cares a lot about the student's growth both as a person and a writer.

Solid professor. Ditto on the previous two, his class is not like the other professors and is overall much more accessible and supportive. He doesn't assign a lot of work but can be a tough grader sometimes, but he listens to student feedback about the course and its content. Overall pretty good :)

At first, I took this class just because he had the best rating among all the other instructors. I think I made the right choice even though it's before I take the final. He is really accessible outside of class either through office hours or email. He gave us a lot of work, but this course is designed to be that way. So, not his fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this class for my minor (I'm an IAS double major minoring in IT). We mostly wrote about the concept of technical writing while also doing essays and projects based on our own interests/things in our major(s). Professor Chini was really supportive and helpful and seemed to know the class was hard for many people.

Professor Chini cares a lot about his students. I came into this class without any prior knowledge of programming and was pleasantly surprised. He asked the class what programming experience we had and tailored his explanations based the responses. Tests can be difficult if you don't do the review, don't read the text, and don't attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chini was an amazing teacher who cares deeply for his students. Personally, I believe the past reviews are very unfair. Chini may be very frank with his responses and feedback which you must follow word by word. If you actually go to class and take notes of what he says, you will definitely pass the class and do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He doesn't write clearly himself, so he grades on whims. What was okay when he gave feedback is bad when you submit it. He subtracts literally 2.5 % of a paper's grade for every "will" you have in your paper (even if it is used correctly). If you want to learn anything other than his whims, don't take the class with him. You will hate it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sorry to say but he is not a good professor. I do agree that he is accessible outside class and prompt on emails but his teaching methods are not good. He expects people in his class to already know programming. His exams are too hard and review sheet for exam is useless because nothing ever comes from those sheet. I will never take his class again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is the hardest grader ever. He subtracts points as for the most trivial reasons. You will follow the rubric and think that you did well only to realize that you get 2.0. 4.0 is 98% and every 0.1 gpa is 2%. But he will subtract points for the most trivial of reasons. It is impossible to do well in this class. This isn't tech writ, it is paranoia.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pros: He's a nice person and incredibly fast to respond to questions. He genuinely seems to care about his students. He grades quickly too, so you always know how you are doing. Cons: Lectures disorganized with tons of unrelated topics. He does not address open cheating. Gives favorite students the answers on tests. Lots of memorizing.

Professor Chini is one of the best professors in UW, especially in CSS. Initially, I wasn't happy with my grade, but at the end of the semester, I had a lot of respect for him. He appreciates when his students actually try to understand the material and work hard to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: In general technical writing is a joke of a class. It's way too much work for something that we will never use. However, Chini is a great professor and really cares about his students. He does grade very hard, but if you talk with him about your draft grade, he will tell you exactly what to do to get a higher grade on the final paper. Chini >Laurie
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Chini is a funny professor, but his grading criteria is very unclear. He never answers your questions directly. He gives you different answers at different times. Make sure to go to his office hours to ask him what he wants before turning in anything. There's a lot of deadlines before the midterm, after that it gets easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Morteza Chini is excellent. Very knowledgeable, give great explanations and goes out of his way to ensure you understand the concepts presented. Also has a great sense of humor and engaged with the class using several fun exercises which helped increase my understanding of the topics being covered.

Css484 taken. Be ready for completely unorganized lectures: instead of going through all sub-topics in one topic, she teaches pieces of them over several weeks. Lots of repetitions during lectures. The material covered is only very basic. Quizzes open only for a couple of minutes. You'll spend more time on GUI rather than actual algorithms.

Min Chen is a literal gem at UWB. She had a way of explaining things that just made sense compared to my previous 342 professor. It's not because her class is "easy" per say, the problems are pretty difficult. Her explanations are just so clear thorough, that its hard not to get a good grade if you watch her online lectures and come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I heard that this class is significantly easier when compared to how other instructors teach it. The class teaches you basic SQLite sql. Most of the class is focused on drawing ER diagrams and normalization, which might too useful. If you want an easy class while learning relatively useful information, it is not a bad choice.

Professor Min Chen taught CSS475 as if it were a 100-level class. Half of every lecture was review from the previous session. Barely any material was covered, the only SQL we learned was the bare basics. She asked the class if we liked the pace and many students said "yes", since it made the class an easy A. Avoid if you want to learn anything.
Super good prof.

She really is a gem of a professor! Gives lots of examples for students to learn topics. Listens to feedback and speeds up or slows down accordingly. Spent the first half learning about ER diagrams and relational mapping while the second half covers SQLite and normalization. 4 HWs, midterm and final. Highly recommend her for the database class.

Very solid choice to learn databases. Explains concepts very well and is open to adapting her lecture speed and style to accommodate struggling students. Course structure is well organized with a fair amount of work that is clearly relevant to the course material. Covers SQLite throughout the class and for the final project (not any coding).
I learned a lot from her Multimedia database class. Very good professor. She records each lecture, and describes each topic very clearly. She is very patient for answering questions.

Professor Chen is not available via email, so unless you have the spare time to go to office hours on her schedule, you will probably not get a response. Her lectures are good, but her class was graded on a total of 4 coding assignments, and 2 exams, thats all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Min Chen is a wonderful professor and person. Her 343 class was amazing. She works really hard to make sure everyone understands the material and posts video recordings of her lectures online so that you can go back and review. Altogether, an amazing and fun class.

All teachers should teach CSS like Min teaches it. She records her lectures, and makes sure that the class understands every topic before moving on to the next topic. She emphasizes, and draws diagrams and makes you practice the concepts in class to really understand this! I would say she is the best teacher I've had at UW bothell CSS program.

Very helpful when you come to office hours or email with questions, will give partial credit for showing all the correct steps on homework and exams. Goes out of the way to help students succeed. Very clear and strait to the point lectures.

Good lecturer. Lots of examples in class. Utilizes the class time extremely well. No textbook reading required, which is not necessarily a good thing. By the end of the class, u know "how" but wouldn't know "why" since she doesn't really cover the "why". It's better to spend the time to read the optional textbook. Btw, class difficulty is medium

Min Chen is an excellent professor. She has a great attitude and is always happy to answer questions or help. She is great at explaining concepts and simplifies them where possible. Her tests are easy because they are open-note (anything non-electronic) and she is a fair grader. Class was not an easy A, but it was interesting and reasonably hard.

Multimedia Data Processing (CSS490). No textbook. No homework other than the 4 assignments. Easy assignments. 3rd assignment is a group assignment. Average on everything was about around a B+. Two tests (both open notes).

While the content is conveyed clearly, the way this professor grades is very unhelpful when it comes to promoting learning. Her grading techniques aim to punish for slight error instead of giving partial credit. My experience in another class with this professor revealed this same problem. Grading criteria are not always clear.

Clear assignment requirements and grading criteria. Well-structured lectures. Plenty of examples and in-class practice exercises.  This is the most straight forward class I have taken by far. Min will not try to trick you or make the class unnecessarily hard. She's well organized. She's will teach you everything you need to know to succeed.
This is by far the best professor at UW Bothell. Her lectures are clear and she tells you exactly what will be on the test. If you try hard enough, you will get an easy A.
Best prof ever! She prepares her lecture with excellent and interesting example. She knows exactly where students may be confused. Must have!!

Lecture are good, she tried to make everything simple. She really care for students, which is good and bad - the downside is she could take 15 minutes to explain a concept if one or two persons keep asking that concept over and over again (where everyone is clear about it), which drag the whole class down instead of moving on to the next concept.
Amazing professor! She makes the class easy, and really shows that she cares about her students. I highly recommend her class!
Good professor. There are four assignments, and two test. Tests are easily.

Dr. Chen is an amazing teacher who actually cares if her students are understanding the material. One class she came up with half a dozen examples in a row when our class was having trouble understanding a concept and she didn't quit until she was convinced we understood. Lectures are very organized and her handouts are extremely helpful.
Great Teacher,  helpful. Very Organized. Good Lectures. Would recommend for 342, 343.
Excellent instructor.  Well organized and clear presentations of the materials.  Middle of the road in terms of grading toughness.  I would highly recommend this professor.

She is a pretty decent professor. She always wants student feedback, whether that's through mid-course evaluations or nodding your head occasionally throughout the lecture to show you actually get what's going on. Her tests and assignments can be tricky, but if you read through her powerpoints and do practice problems you should be good.
CSS 370 was a breeze with her! She is one of the best at UWB! Would take any CSS class with her again. Highly recommend. Easy A, if you try.

Very helpful and knowledgeable professor. She relies heavily on feedback to direct the lecture in a way that will most benefit the students so it is important to give feedback (something my class is not very good at).  I dropped into her office not even during her regular office hours and she still spent a couple of minutes giving much needed help.

I'm surprised no one made a page for Professor Chen, as this is her secondthird quarter teaching.   Prof. Chen is very knowledgeable and is probably the nicest CSS professor. She's always willing to help and take time to explain concepts in depth. In class, make sure you explicitly tell her if you get something or not. She relies on feedback.

With the horrible experience I had with professor Katherine Cook, Hillyard was a breath of fresh air. She genuinely cares about the students and wants to see you succeed. Literally just show up to class and you'll be on track for an A. She gives a lot of chapter quizzes, participation matters,  kahn academy requirements were simple enough.
Didn't teach much at all. Tough grader on projects. Requirements are often vague. Takes forever to give feedback. Nice lady but not a good teacher
I took her for IAS inquiry, and while it was really easy, it was clear her heart wasn't into it. Lots of class discussion where only one or two people end up talking. Lots of busy work.

The only people getting bad grades are the ones who do not show up to class or do not complete the homework problems (moderate - semi-difficult). On the flip side, these problems over prepare you for the midterm and final which are seem easier than the homework/challenge problems. She is not a fan of using calculators so know the material

Had her a couple times, and both times felt like I had to rely on myself to learn the material. She always makes people work in groups, and online homework is awful.  I really did not enjoy the class at all, but I guess that can be expected when it's calculus. :)

She is a good teacher for the IAS program.  I feel that we got a lot of leway on our work and that there was not much busy work which made it easier.  The portfolio is practiclly spoon fed to you and it is kind of hard not to get a good grade if you do your work and show up for most of the classes

I learned a lot in this class, unlike several of my classmates who spent most of their time whining and complaining. The subject matter was dry but examples made it better. A lot of in-class work and only 2 quizzes. She was very helpful in answering students' questions and any question was a good question. I feel more prepared for stats now!
Doesn't answer email. Uses lots of small group work to have your peers teach you the material. Disconnect between online homework and offline tests.

very nice lady but don't take her if u need a good grade for grad school! doesn't teach you how to use programs on your calculator...its all by hand! tests are very hard and worded confusingly, she clearly loves stats but doesn't seem to notice not everybody does. I've worked my ass off and am just passing with a 2.0
If you had a prior knowledge of higher level math (calculus or above) then the class time and lectures were a waste of time. Fairly easy grader if you did the homework.
No Comments
The class was rediculous-which might been see as a good thing, but in this case it wasn't. Pure torture!

Easy class! She grades hard on the mid-term and final, but it's opened book with notes, make sure you are very specific and use what is talked about in class and not JUST what's in the text. Sweet lady!
Very nice teacher. Easy class. She cares about her students. You read all the books she gives and it's definitely helpful to read the books.
I liked this class a lot but many students seemed to come unprepared. The material was really interesting and I'll never look at a fairy tale the same way! Easy grader.
