Not very organized. Late in getting grades back. Follows textbooks very closely. Struggles to get the class involved.
Dr. Cooper was a cool professor. There was a lot of group work and projects but it made the class fun. It is pretty lecture heavy so make sure you pay attention in class and ask questions.

Dr. Cooper is all over the place. Teaching style was a mess and his slides were disorganized. Often times we would ask questions for clarification and he wouldn't know how to answer or doesn't understand what we were asking. I ended up studying on my own and used YouTube to learn core concepts. Exams are fair though, nothing too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his class and his character. His slides are a little too wordy but he is good at clearing up the concepts. His exams do have some tough application based questions but are doable. He does expect previous knowledge but he does go over review. His exams were 75% similar to practice exams + study guides. He is very helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for research, and it was really bad. He expected the students to create their own procedures for concepts we've never been taught, and he gave very little guidance. He did not treat us like students who are there to learn, but as people who were already supposed to know how to do the methods within our research. Do not recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His slides are disorganized, making it hard to follow or connect topics. I would just write down his definitions and study them later. His last exam was nearly impossible to understand since he designed it to be like Anti-ChatGPT, so good luck.

Wording on test questions was confusing, study guides don't come with answer sheets, voice is monotone during lectures. Assumed previous knowledge from students - difficult to understand him when he used terminology we did not know. Difficult class that requires effort outside of lectures because the pace of lecture. Possible to get good grade.

He is contradictory and told me something different every time regarding what he wants. Im a straight A student, I am not lazy and am liked by my profs, but he got me to a point where one day i cried after class to a classmate because he made me feel so dumb in my ideas and gave me the lowest grade. i think it became something personal at the end.

Took him for research and he expected so much from undergrad students. People said he used to work with grad students before moving to the US. He treated Bio495 and independent research. He would be so vague yet harsh. It is so weird that he has a specific want in mind, but will not tell students steps to achieve it- just keeps bashing student work

Worst professor I have ever had. Did not explain concepts well at all, and exams covered very niche topics that he barely explained in lecture. Questions on his exams are also worded to trick you. He does curve at the end, but regardless I regret taking his class and wish I took it the next semester. Nobody knew what was going on in this class!

A okay professor not the worst but could be better. Tests were super application based. This is not a memorization game and spiting it out on the test. You need to put the concepts into application. Some of the questions are worded weirdly. He does give a really good curve. The curve only is good if you are a bit below the avg.

Generous grading, nice personality, cares deeply about her students, and is forgiving with assignments and due dates. I had her for BWRIT 134, and there are very good differences between her class and the standard UW classes. As long as you don't take advantage of her leniency and actually participate in class discussion, you'll probably be happy.

Lots of extra credit offered. I don't think I did well on my paper but got full points. If you put in the effort then you should be fine in the course. Also lots of extensions given as needed with no reasoning needed. Professor is just looking for students to do their best and improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a nice person. Clear and reasonable expectations. Her class was enjoyable and manageable when taking three other classes. It expands your writing skills, but doesn't make you question getting a degree.

Such a sweet prof, attend her office hours for extra credit! Super lax grader, just don't be lazy in your writing and it's an easy A. Provides free textbook snippets when we need to read something, more extra credit opportunities regarding assignments attached to those. Second half of quarter is focused on just writing your paper.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Prof: nice, engaged with students, knowledgeable

Class: some lectures, interesting class activities

HW: readings (intuitive, boring). GROUP PROJECT THE WHOLE QUARTER.
It was very doable, pretty repetitive, mostly research and writing on a community intervention and then a final poster presentation.

HE BROUGHT DONUTS FOR THE POSTER PRESENTATION!

There's weekly readings that he provides, and lots of discussions (in person and online), there's a few in person graded participation, and Professor Collin's is an overall is a nice professor. Though the class work felt like a lot at times, at least there weren't any presentations, just a lot of writing and thinking about the theoretical.
This course is very easy, consists of reading 1-2 articles assigned and doing a short quiz. Definitely would recommend for an add-on class if you have a difficult quarter coming up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Collins' class was a great experience. Expectations were always made very clear. Helpful resources, such as video lectures, were great to have. I learned a lot, but this class was also easy to balance with other aspects of my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Collins is an excellent professor. Low pressure and relatively low stress, but a much better learning experience in return, which is great for anyone who is stress sensitive but wants to learn. Great lectures and activities in class that accompanied the reading materials each week. Organized, easy to reach, and knowledgeable. Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very kind, accomodating, and knowledgable professor, but not much that forces you to actually learn. painfully easy open-internet assignments. if you have a surface level knowledge of the subject and know how to use ctrl+f, you could pass with a 100% without attending a single lecture or doing any of the readings.
The most caring professor I have EVER had. He is there for all his students and offers great support for school and non-school-related issues. Would 100% take again.

Loved this class! Expectations and grading criteria were extremely clear (and repeated in both the syllabus and each assignment itself), including expected word counts. Good grades were as easy as following instructions and participating. Both the Prof and his TA were amazingly supportive and worked to help students improve throughout the quarter.

This teacher and his pet rat of a TA are some of most pathetic educators that Ive ever had. Arguably has the most irrelevant grading rubric. Strict on word count? Give it a rest! The class itself is asynchronous, and these two have the presence of mind to be rude to students and not acknowledge their work. Both are completely worthless!

Really chill dude. The class was online during the pandemic and was very easy to follow. Mostly busywork but not difficult to do. Easy concepts to understand. Literally, just follow and watch his lectures and you're all good.

He is a great professor, he works with you, and wants you to succeed. You will get a good grade if you go to class and participate. He'll give you a couple freebies on the major tests. He also uploaded his course material for community psychology on youtube making studying a breeze. This course needs 2 hours/ week volunteer time.

Lectures are interesting. He is young so he seems more understanding to our generation. He is very passionate about his work and his classes. Lots of reading and engagement activities in class for points that you have to be there to get credit.   Reasonable amount of work.

I enjoyed taking his statistics class! He made it fun and understandable by using easy examples that students can relate to. Breaking up into small groups was very helpful as well to make sure everyone understood the statistics words. His test wasn't that bad as long as you do the reading! I would take another class with him! Excel is a big factor!

Hes an awesome prof. He only gave 6 online quizzes, bumped it down to 5.  Very easy grader, in class assignments that your peers grade. Only a paper at the end of quarter with your group, just beware of the people in your group because I had one drop the class because she couldnt handle it... very easy class,  awesome guy who jokes a lot
You're either willing to learn or just be a duck on the water, but do keep in mind of the consequences

His lecture is very theory basesd. Also, his lecture is very conservative as it is lecture based. One thing good about his class is that he has open book tests to make grades up. However, he has favors in students.

He made the class very interesting at times through various activities, some that will make you step out of your comfort zone. The required book is extremely boring. The bad thing about his course was that his assignments were often very confusing, not according to just me but other students as well. Required a Community Based Learning (volunteer).

Great teacher! I was nervous to take this course, but it came out to being an easy class. Because he taught us all very well and was very understanding! Btw if I may mention, he is a cutie!! :) You will love him and his personality (:

Professor Collins at first seemed tough and unapproachable, but as the quarter progressed, I began to really like him and he was a lot more approachable than what I first thought. He's an easy grader. I would be able to get a hold of him easily if I needed to. He seemed to care if students learn.

I do not understand the positive feedback for this prof. I took a class with him last quarter and it was a mistake.  No feedback on work over the entire course of the quarter. Then he missed the end of quarter grade deadline by over a week. I got blindsided with the lowest grade of my school career! 2 full grades lower than chem and bio.  Avoid!!

Pretty good class. Some components seemed like busy work but in general it was an interesting to see how he approached the this particular subject. However, I did get bored of the material because it felt very repetitive by week 5 or 6.

I took Prof Collins' CP and Stats class this summer. He's nice, approachable, funny and pretty chill. Statistics was good but I felt I didn't learn as much as his CP class. His CP class was great, but the book is too dense. He's still fairly new so he's making adjustments for future classes. Both the classes had a research project at the end.

Professor Collins is definitely one of my favorite professors at  UWB and very passionate about his subjects. Very knowledgeable and able to assist you in anyway possible. He's approachable and and kind, and willing to make sure everyone is comprehending the material. In addition a very handsome guy to look at ;)

I am going to have to disagree with the person below. If you are looking for a real professor, if you wanna learn in a flexible way, and if you want an A while learning, take his classes. He has a very unique way of teaching. If you want interesting class sessions that are unique, TAKE HIM!!!!

I absolutely LOVE Dr. Collins! His online lectures are amazing and really get you through the class if you take notes! He's the EASIEST grader on earth and is really giving with points! I'm currently in his stats class...SO easy!!
Great professor

Thermo, Heat Transfer,Ethics, HVAC, Electro Power Machine Design. 10/10 on all things. His notes are amazing prepares you for the exams. Doesn't think students should fail, but is not scared to give a bad grade. While he does freeze from time to time, because he's trying to optimize his speech so everyone can understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Treats students with respect and kindness.

I loved him. He has a solid voice that you can hear anywhere in the room and he is very excited about the material he teaches. The thermo series is  difficult, so prepare to read a lot & do TONS of practice problems. But, quizzes are straight from the HW so that's good. And 40% of the final was take home! Very approachable & willing to help u.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is a very self-less professor, always giving to his students. The dude brings in coffee and croissants to my 8:45 to help wake students. Summarizes tough material in packets and is very clear cut with grading and expectations. He struggles a bit with material, but fluid dynamics was never easy and he hasn't ever taught it. Good stuff.
Definitely prone to confusion at times, however I expect the next time around he'll have a much easier time of it.  I expect future themal fluids courses he teaches may be smooth as butter

His exam prep materials are great, but lectures aren't the greatest. He confuses himself a lot and  freezes mid-lecture to stare at his notes. It's not his fault though. He never taught fluid mechanics before, and I think he was forced to. Exams are easy, and he always posts solutions for practice problems ,so studying is pretty painless for me.

One of my favorite professors so far. Chem is not my forte, but he made it engaging and interesting. Very enthusiastic and animated. Homework and exams were fair and he was a generous grader. Also a very nice man.

The course is fairly simple with some online homework.  In class he has trouble teaching and confuses himself often, and that makes me not trust what he says.  I did, however, end up understanding everything and doing well in the class without having to put in more than the average amount of effort.
I had to take this class only because it was a prerequisite for my major, but he help made chemistry easy and fun to learn for me.

Definitely knows his stuff about chemistry (he is a chemical engineer), but not the best at teaching it. Fairly easy, mostly because he is unfamiliar with how to teach a general chemistry class (mine was his first one ever). Props for trying!
Excellent Professor. He has a genuine interest in the subject, and is passionate about teaching.

Collins is a very knowledgeable and passionate professor. He assigned one major paper which wasn't too hard and his final exam was very similar to his practice exam. You do have to attend classes because he'll throw a pop quiz every once in a while. HW is also mandatory but easy and not too time consuming.

He is very intelligent and a genuinely nice guy. He can go off on tangents, but his notes are outstanding. You don't even need the textbooks. One paper, two midterms and a take home final. He has some busy work excersises, if you do them you get credit. The paper is really flexible  also. All in all, he is a solid prof.

Very well-informed about the subject. Another great Professor that does not throw curve balls in the quarter-gives ample time for students to prep for papers and tests. Fair graders with helpful suggestions for improving papers. Loved the class.
I thought this was a pretty smart and useful course. Collins was very organized and clear in  presenting the material.
I expected more tech, less society, but I enjoyed this class and this teacher

The most worthless class I have ever taken at UWB.  This class was a waste of time and only added stress to my schedule.  The professor is willing to give extra help, but his explainations are not well thought out.  There are numerous times in class where he confuses himself with the problems he assigns.  If you don't need BIS 250, don't take it.

He made the history of science and technology pretty fun even though the class can be a little boring at times, which it is.  We watched a lot of videos and had good class discussions.  He is very fair at grading so you should do well if you put a little work in.

I've had Steve for two classes now.  As a warning, he's become more critical of laptop use lately, but allows if you make a request.  He loves to talk with his students, and really enjoys doing so after class, to the point of catching a meal together or the like - he has a genuine interest in the topics he teaches, and your own input.

If you need Motion and Mechanics BIS 250, take Steve. A great intro to basic physics, and he's one of the most laid back, knowledgeable, and good-humored profs I've had. It's not all nuts and bolts, and Steve makes the course interesting by including the scientists and their place in history. Fascinating, fun course. Flexible final exam, to boot.

This professor is one of my personal favorites because he taught in a way that was complex  enough to challenge everyone where they were at in their own education. I felt much more knowledgable after taking his class and he was helpful as well.

Collins has an in-depth understanding of the material and explains it well.  The research project was structured very clearly, showed us where to go for the information, but had high expectations.  Great class.
Steve is one of the best teachers on campus. If you like to learn about other cultures, his class is the place to be. With his presentation the material seems very interesting.
Pretty interesting class, he is well educated in Japan, and the tests weren't too difficult. i'd definitely take his class again
Good formal lectures, tho infrequent. Excellent dialogue with class - highly values and respects others opinions regardless of basis. Engages students makes us want to learn.
Collins is one of the best profs in the program.
Unbelievably helpful and accessible to all his students.  A genuine, caring, honorable man.

Do not take. The homework was manageable, but his grading is insanely unfair. He will write comments at the bottom that doesn't make sense, even if you clearly answer his questions. getting a 0 or below half credit after actually being right about something because you didn't perfectly mimic his description of it is the worst part.

Avoid

The class I took with him, is a hybrid class. We learn on our own and see him in person once a week. I almost failed my first exam because my definition wasn't exactly word to word in the textbook. He's a very harsh grader and nitpicking over the smallest thing. The exams are hard if you don't teach yourself but the homework is really easy.

He is very helpful in office hours- i'd recommend going to them before every exam. He grades extremely unfairly in my opinion, and rubrics are often unclear. I found him to be rude to a couple other students for talking during class when they were confused/lost.

I was able to go from a 65 on the midterm to an 88 on the final by going to office hours. The classes are almost entirely group work, if you do the group work and fill out the worksheets in class, you will do well!! Go to office hours, he will draw graphs for you for 30 minutes until it makes sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's an insanely strict grader. Every other writing class or writing related class I've gotten good grades, he picks on random things and completely fails you. He does not care if you have family emergencies or anything. I highly recommend not taking any of his classes unless you want to put all your effort in and get a terrible grade.

BBUS220/BIS200 It's surprising how many bad reviews Danby has. He's really nice and seems super passionate. He give us one homework a week and our midterm was literally identical to the practice he gave us. Danby does his best to make it as easy as possible. If you just show up to class and follow along you don't actually need to study at all.

Danby is an extremely hard grader, and his feedback is rude and unhelpful. It seems like if you don't write exactly what he would write then you're wrong. Absolutely the worst class I have ever taken and if you have another option of professors to take go with that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor was so rude. I suffered the whole quarter, was not understanding at all. DO NOT TAKE. rude feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: he's a very knowledgeable professor especially about academic writing, but a tough grader. he gives feedback (he's passive aggressive with the feedback, can come off as insulting with the language he uses), even when you make changes according to his feedback, he'll find something else to pick on. i would avoid if u can, dont expect to get a 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is my first quarter at UWB, from the first day I came to this class I felt very uncomfortable because he was very disrespectful to the students, In the whole semester, I don't think you taught me anything. Higher does not recommend taking this class is a waste of money and time.
He's ok. Grades hard for essays but seems like a nice guy. Lectures are great. Not a fan of the online format of this class.
Avoid. Worst teacher in IAS by a mile. Completely arbitrary grading and doesn't explain his logic. Don't make the mistake of disagreeing with his opinions (shown in class) on essays.
His 394 class last spring was like a Dhar Mann video: "OLD ECONOMICS TEACHER TAKES STUDENT'S PHONES, LIVES TO REGRET IT."

He's a nice guy and cares about students' learning, as long as you are willing to put in effort. My only problems with him are that he grades on attendance and that he grades rather strictly, as others say.

He is not a historian which makes sense once you take his class. 303 (History of Globalization) is less about history or globalization and more about Danby showing off his Economics PhD. The class is largely based on essays. Boring class. Not a lot of learning. I blame UWB for the failure that came with keeping him as a prof and tenuring him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prolly the weirdest prof ive ever had. he be kicking people out of his class just for looking at their phone. He just makes you read a bunch of pages, and when u go to class you just watch movies and do a lil worksheet. His essays are like the only thing he grades, and he wants u to repeat what he says in class in the essay. But the content is wack

I am astounded that many people felt the need to rate this professor with a 1 in terms of quality. He gives very straightforward assignments and is really helpful in office hours. I have taken him for two classes (300 and 303) which were both great experiences. There's a lot of work, like other reviews say, but he's not out to get you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've seen many negative reviews on professor Danby, but overall he has been an enthusiastic professor who knows his stuff and engages in plenty of in-class discussion. Moderate amounts of reading, overall very manageable. Large portion of the grade is solely based on submitting the work, so just try and you'll get an A. Would, and will, take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: If you've taken other economics classes then take this class (Global Economies) by all means, otherwise don't waste you time. He treats it like a 400-level seminar when there's students without an econ background in it, and doesn't offer lots of help. Exams are much more complicated than the practice exams. HARD grader.

Tough professor. He knows his stuff, but he isn't the most clear in describing it, resulting in confusion. When students are confused, he rehashes exactly what he already said instead of giving alternate explanations. Although he verbally expresses his interest in helping students and has good intentions, his office hours aren't entirely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the worst professor I've had here. His grading is completely subjective. Even if you change you paper to what he recommends it should be, he still won't like it. I've gotten 4.0s in every other college writing class I've taken, but this guy makes it impossible. Super passive aggressive and rude on feedback. Just prepare to fail. Avoid!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I haven't encountered an experience like this with any professor at UWB, as a 4.0 student. Only gives negative feedback. Is very confusing, vague with expectations & makes it hard to succeed in class. Writes passive aggressive comments on assignments. Interrupts students while they are talking during discussion frequently. Wasn't enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's the best! He always goes into depth about our readings and makes it so we have good discussions. He also gives really good feedback and a chance to resubmit your bigger essays. Even if it's a rough draft, turn it in because he does take points off for late work, however. Overall would highly recommend his class!

Don't take Danby for this class or any class. Extremely confusing way of learning, makes you hate economics and anything to do with it by the time the quarter ends. Rarely answers questions well. Doesn't grade anything on time. The "cranky old tenured professor" myth is true if you meet him.

He should teach BIS 300, they are perfect for each other as both won't teach you anything useful under a large amount of busy work. No way to ask questions in lecture, terrible grading scale, and too many writing assignments. Also so, so hard to correct your paper based on his feedback. He desperately needs to put his Econ PhD to use.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ask him what percentage a 4.0, 3.8 etc is on the VERY FIRST DAY. He is very discrete and tough on that. I had a 97% and that was a 3.7!!! he refused to explain to me what class percentage a 4.0 was. usually anything above a 96 or 97% is a 4.0 I guess not with him. I am about to graduate and I have never had a class where a 97% was a 3.7.

There are 3 papers and they are worth 75%. He is the toughest grader of all time and he will make sound wrong no matter what you say. Do not take this class! it is not worth it because not only the professor is a tough grader but the material is horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class. He gives good feedback and the option to turn in your paper after revision for full points if you follow his suggestions after the first paper. He is also willing to look at rough drafts, which were really helpful.

The class has plenty of reading and a few papers. It also has small assignments due every week. Class isn't mandatory but beneficial because he goes over any questions you might have with the readings, and the class activities also help you grasp the main themes of the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is a little rough on feedback but if you correct what he asks for you will most likely get an A, just listen to his feedback. At least for this term that it was online, he was willing to look at every draft before you submitted which really helped so take advantage of that! It does not go deep into econ but it's helpful to have some background.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Danby is a wonderful professor, extremely intelligent person, wise, & passionate about what he teaches & student learning! Id take any & all classes he offers at the Uni! His lecturing skills rival all others, and the content of the class is very interesting! Hes top notch! He helps you become a better essay writer and critical thinker!

Favorite professor I've had so far. While he's certainly not the easiest, he gives great feedback and wants to make sure you actually succeed. Fair grader, and not really as frustrating as some people say. Very, very accessible out of class - can meet with you literally whenever.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class is very interesting, especially its topic (comparative studies of death). His tests are vocabulary-oriented, but the majority of the class is heavy on group work and group discussion, which fosters a great community. He's a very nice guy that is really passionate about his school, research, and teaching.

He doesn't sugarcoat it if people are wrong, so he can seem a little harsh, but he's actually very nice beyond that. More importantly, he is extremely knowledgeable and a good lecturer! I enjoyed his class.

Very fair, knowledgeable, and accessible. His lectures are intersting and the reading are light. I highly reccomend and would gladly take again. The test are designed to show comprehension and analysis. Thinking is required in this class, other than that very easy going.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I've ever had. He ridicules his students in front of the class when they make some comment. His exams are all take home and its usually two prompts with 500 words expected from each in an essay format. He likes taking off points even when your work is perfect. There is so much reading and weekly writing on canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are not on tests but tests are also unique in format.
Can be tough but fair and - you will learn about how to write effectively and staying on point.

Starts lecturing on the first day of class.  He assigns more reading than any other instructor I had over the last two years at UW.  I would say he needs to limit the reading and make his teaching more clear.  Tests should not be as hard.  He should be nicer on the grading.
One word: Terrible

PROS: He is a fascinating lecturer and goes out of his way to make sure he doesn't breaks up the lecture times. He didn't use textbooks but rather articles/e-readings. He is approachable. CONS: He was a financial professor teaching a liberal arts/lit class. He didn't have a clear rhyme or reason for the flow of the class/readings.

While he had a lot of negative feedback for my work, along with everyone else in the class, I managed to pull an A. I did the work, used his feedback and attended office hours. HOWEVER: He's not very nice,it's difficult to understand what he wants from you, the work is not really relevant (other than brushing up writing skills) and so boring.

Ridiculed me, ignored my appeal, and lacked communication skills. Good lecturer, but far outweighed by his pretentious attitude, and gift in demeaning students; like writing, “information dump” as feedback! Upon returning from a traumatic event, he was a nightmare come true! Do you value your GPA and sanity? Avoid his class like the plague!

I don't recommend him for BIS 300! It's not a particularly hard class, however, you wont learn ANYTHING! He'll tell you, you aren't doing something right but is unable to tell you why, or how to fix it. He doesn't teach you how to do anything. You just write papers and he gives you empty evaluations.

What a terrible class. This is something I NEVER say, in fact this is my first time on this website. Treats students childish, does not give students a chance when talking, scorns you if you are late or eating...PUBLICALLY! VERY harsh grader, and A LOT of very dense reading. I regret taking the course, I am not even interested anymore.

Gives you every resource possible, even extra on top of not used in class. Ready to read drafts- honestly just wants you to get the best grade. Very open to extra help outside. Tremendously knowledgeable.

The worst professor I have EVER had. Does not know how to communicate, teaches class as if we are all PhD students. Does not explain ANYTHING. Assignments are hard. Tests are just extremely difficult and he is not willing to help anyone. He should not be teaching undergrad students. Everyone always complains about him. DONT TAKE HIM!
Danby dance. Completely knowledgeable and is surprisingly funny (in that corny professor way).

If you're looking for an easy grade, this is not for you. Remember to focus on an argument and desist from mere summarization. Your arguments must be tight and evidence-based not generalizations. You need focused, critical-thinking skills to navigate the course.It's definitely worth taking if you're prepared to learn and not just regurgitate.

Colin is very intelligent and has the best of intentions...he's just not that good of a teacher.  He doesn't communicate very well at all.  But he is always willing to meet outside of class, which is nice.  Still, he is not all that helpful and is a DIFFICULT grader.  I've never worked so hard in a class only to get a below-average (for me) grade.
Worked hard to teach a good class. Fair / Lots of material to cover, lots of reading. Saved us signficant money by providing articles instead of a textbook.

Colin is not the best at explaining things in class, but he is more than willing to help you outside of class or via email.  He can be a tough grader, but he really wants you to understand the content.  He will grasp onto every word you say and write, making you really think what you're doing!

I can't say he's a bad teacher. He makes his expectations pretty clear. He grades hard, and there is a ton of reading (which are all e-reserves readings). He over-simplifies econ to the point that it is inaccurate - so that IS majors can understand it. He's also really high strung; kind of exhausting... BUT he's extremely helpful.

Terrible class. Terrible teacher. Sneaky, manipulative and arrogant. He changes due dates on the syllabus and doesn't tell you. He can't explain or back up his grading at all. You cannot use your laptop or any devices during the class, at all, period. You cannot talk during class or eat food. Worst class ever. Don't take it if you can avoid it.

Danby is an excellent teacher; he really pushes you to make the best possible work.  He does get after people for crinkling food wrappers, its a minor annoyance that can be dealt with (Don't eat in class!).  It's worth it to take his class.
He was nice at times.. He yelled at students for eating in class and picked students out when they were asking questions. He was a fair grader but i will NEVER be in one of his classes again

Terribly boring class. The reading material is weird and completely dull. Tons of reading and one or two papers due each week. He gives a rewrite option though, so if you put in the work you can get a passing grade in the class. Treats students like babies. Reprimands students for eating too loudly in class, and for being late.
The content may have been hard, but I felt his teaching made it more difficult to understand.

He is here to get you, forget one quote mark and you are guilty of plagiarism, sent to the commity for sanctions. DO NOT take his class. I am a good student and never had to deal with such a nightmare, save your time and money.

Prof. Danby is a good instructor. He's enthusiastic about his subjects, especially political economy. Although, I don't agree with how he simplified some of the material, he tries his best to help students without an economics background understand the material.
He is a bright guy, but he lacks communication skills.  He appears nervous at times which manifests a terrible stutter.  Not sure if it is him or the class, but it was not a good experience.
He made this class way to hard for a general introduction for the IAS program.  He wasn't very clear about any of the assignments either.

Great class. Very interesting books. Friendly, enthusiastic prof, but her organization isn't the greatest - schedule is unclear, particularly due dates, and the Canvas page is a mess. I did appreciate how much she cared about us.

Easy class (hybrid - only one day in person), decent professor. Her lectures were ok but the books assigned and her feedback on written work were great. Talks very fast. I like her outfits. I would take her again.

We missed a few days of class because of holidays but she made up for it. Stevi was nice, but like others said she talks very fast. Gives good feedback and is easy to talk to. 4 books, all of them interesting in unique ways (including Gone Girl!). Reading quizzes are online and pretty easy as long as you read.

Stevi is great and passionate about literature. BIS387 is basically a book club and it's super fun if you like reading. I genuinely enjoyed the novels. We read 4 and there was only 1 that I disliked. The reading quizzes are easy if you keep up with the novel. She only grades on reading quizzes and the final. Discussions are complete/not complete.

Stevi is a kind, encouraging English teacher who really cares about students' learning. The books we read were awesome, I liked the class discussions, and I thought her feedback on writing was very good. She talks FAST and it's sometimes hard to keep up - take good notes because they may be helpful on essays.

We missed a lot of days of class. I think she's nice and a good prof to take in person but she doesn't seem to understand that there's a difference between online and on campus. It's not uncommon for a single week to have 100 pages of reading along with a quiz and a mandatory "discussion." She grades easily and responds quickly to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Heard she's teaching here again. Her literature class was easy when I took it: no tests, a few essays and one big project. It covers a lot of content but it's not difficult. The teacher is...interesting, to say the least. Very typically "liberal," but still supportive and accommodating if you ask. Feedback on written work is great.
UWB needs to get her back, she was based.
She cares a lot about your opinions and success in class. She is always every nice and helpful. She is willing to make extra office hours if you need them. Solid class, pretty easy.

Stevi is the ideal first-year writing instructor. She knows what she's talking about and always made our class enjoyable. She's really kind, approachable, and empathetic too, which makes talking to her very easy. We've talked several times about some of our shared interests. I had her a year ago but it's nice to see she's still got it.

Not the best teacher I have had at UWB but she still is a very kind-hearted and enthusiastic person which is something to admire. She's got some quirks for sure but they help drive her teaching. She weighs quality and effort equally on essays which is nice and knows and values the fact that everyone learns differently.

Dr. Costa is a nice teacher. Her Zoom class was very interactive, and she tried to integrate student participation as much as she could. She is very clear about assignments, even if she's on the easy-grader side in terms of grading techniques, and gives excellent feedback. She likes to get to know her students which is cool too.

Stevi is awesome. The books and the supplemental literary criticism were easy reads, but relevant and beautifully selected. She is also very kind, encouraging, and understanding, and recognizes effort and honesty. The only small problem I have is her grading - my work wasn't the best yet I got 100% on all 3 essays and my final project.
I have never met somebody this optimistic and passionate about teaching in my life like literally wth how can someone be this positive and supportive yet also love their job

Professor Costa is great! Super caring, always helpful if you ask, gives great feedback. I had her during quarantine, and she was always super optimistic and upbeat. Lectures were kinda long, but there's was lots of in class-discussion. She clearly cares about her students and their learning. Take her class if you get a chance!

FANTASTIC class. Please please please take anything you can with her - she is so kind, caring, and understanding. I go to office hours all the time just cause I feel comfortable talking with her about the class and our shared interests. Don't listen to the person below. If you ever read this, love you Stevi! (from JL - also why do I have 115%)

I cannot say enough good things about her. I am in the same class as the person below and I agree - she's definitely eccentric, but is so engaging and caring that it's not an issue. She's very open about her personal life, and wants students to get to know her outside of the lecture setting - something not enough people take advantage of. Love her.

In her Zoom class right now. Love her. She may seem eccentric and is a little disorganized, but she is so dedicated to keeping a positive environment in class and it shows. You'll have to write a lot but the books are great. She also encourages students to talk with her outside class about their interests - which I did because we share interests.

Stevi was an awesome professor. She was really caring and understanding, and the class content was really interesting (circuses and freak shows). She is super funny, and she lets you input your opinion in class discussions, and does not discredit you. There are papers to write, but overall she's super awesome!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Stevi is a superbly engaging teacher. I really enjoy the subject matter of this class (it's about circuses), especially the book we read - Geek Love, and think she's very kind, supportive, and accessible outside class. I also like her fashion sense and her jokes :P

She's awesome! Gives great feedback and really wants students to succeed. She can tell when students put in a lot of effort and is very enthusiastic about her job. I got an A (3.9) in Composition Stretch 1 with her last quarter and now I have her for Stretch 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Solid professor, amazing human being. By no means outstanding in terms of teaching but she's extremely kind, caring, and supportive. Assignments are straightforward and grading criteria is extremely clear, especially on the final paper.
Solid professor, very good feedback and really kind/supportive.
Research writing is difficult but Dr. Costa made the class really accessible and interesting. She's really approachable and friendly.

Never a dull lecture with professor Cram! She is very passionate about technological ethics and extremely approachable both in and out of class. 

The class itself has a very manageable workload and no finals or midterms, points mostly come from participation and weekly responses then a final group project. 10/10 would recommend to anyone!

Attendance is graded like it's high school or something, students really should have the freedom to come to class for more support and information, or read and complete work outside of class on one's own time if they wish. On the bright side, Cram is at least seemingly lenient with grading so far...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Cram is very knowledgeable in her area of study and you can definitely see her passion for the subject that she is teaching. This class was very well-structured and provided a great opportunity for leaning interesting ways of thinking about science and tech.

Dr. Cram's online class was terrible, even if she's a pretty nice person. If this class was in person, it would've easily been a 4 or 5, but she did not adapt well to an online format. The discussion boards were universally hated and the final was graded pretty vaguely. I would take her in person just to see if all these 5s are REALLY accurate.
Bless this professor. Reached out and worked with me to get late work in despite my insane schedule. Reviews below have pretty much covered it all. A must-take.
Everything said in the other reviews is true. Best professor here. She cares about you and you're practically guaranteed a 4.0.

Cram is one the best professors I've ever come across. She's passionate, hilarious, enthusiastic, and extremely approachable. She cares about what she's doing and how well you do in her class. Easy grader too which is a nice bonus. I've taken 3 of her classes (BIS 252, 307, and presently 115) and wish I could take more.

Cram is a must-take at UWB. She is a sweetheart and she really cares about her students, very understanding with them. The material was interesting, and the prompts and essays really helped my learning. I received 100% on every assignment and put anywhere from 5 to 10 hours into the class each week. Responds to emails very quickly.
Dr. Cram is one of the nicest professors I have had in college. She is very understanding and caring. The class was pretty easy. If you do the work, she will give you full credit. Easy A.

Professor Cram deserves all of her excellent ratings on here! By far the most nice and caring professor there is. She just knows how to do her job, and she does it well. Lots of writing in this class, but if you enjoy it definitely give it a shot. There’s a large paper at the end that is very fun to write!

If you dont absolutely love Shannon, youre doing something wrong. She didnt require attendance, but her lectures were sooo engaging. Shes kind&understanding. Put in effort youll easily get your 4.0 (98% is 4.0). She gives great feedback giving you full points even if you didnt necessarily grasp the material well. 10/10. Unbeatable at UWB.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Cram! Super interesting course content. Always presented material in a variety of ways, not just dry textbook readings. Scales grades weirdly (90% and above is 4.0) but she really values your work and is very kind and accessible if you need her. I'd love to take a class of her again.

There is no one quite like Prof. Cram, shes kind, understanding, gives insightful readings and assignments. Grades fair, and wants you to succeed. Ive never felt so understood by any other prof., she is truly the greatest. One of THE BEST if not the best at UWB. ABSOLUTELY TAKE A CLASS WITH HER! Wish I could take another course with her shes A++

Professor Cram was very enthusiastic about each topic we went over and was very encouraging and clear on what she wanted from us. She's understanding and left fun feedback on my essays! Each topic was interesting to research and the workload was super easy to manage. Def would take again. :)

For 300, which all IAS students must take, she's a pretty solid choice. Lectures with passion and loves the class material. Very kind and supportive. Really accessible outside of class whether it's email or office hours, and gives us time in class (over Zoom) to get started on homework and ask any clarifying questions. Definitely a great class.

I can not say enough good things about Professor Cram! I took her online (due to the pandemic) and she was fantastic. We were assigned 800 words per week to write about Artificial Intelligence and other controversial topics in technology. She is a very lenient grader and grades based on effort. The class average for the discussions was a 3.9!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Cram was a fantastic professor that gave incredible freedom for all projects, which made them fun. I enjoyed it because she let us pick and choose what we were interested in. Most helpful professor I've had at UW, even for a rather niche major choice of mine (science, technology & society).

Literally a saint of a professor. Great class organization and setup with extremely interesting topics. You can tell she is someone who cares about her students well being and education. Cannot recommend Dr. Cram enough.
Phenomenal teacher. Knows her subjects really well and always ready to support students when they need it. Definitely one of the best classes I've taken at UWB.

Amazing professor. Extremely friendly and supportive, wants to get the best out of each and every one of her students and accommodates the class to every person's unique needs. She goes above and beyond to make sure the class is a positive intellectual and social environment. I made the right choice to do STS as my major because of her.

Prof. Cram is the BEST professor at UWB. I've taken a number of her classes and have enjoyed every single one of them. She's extremely nice, easy-going, and puts a lot of effort and enthusiasm in her lectures. As long as you put effort into the assignments and participate in class, you'll get an easy A. Take as many classes as you can with her!!!

The best prof I've ever had! No joke. It's my 2nd time taking her and I love her even more! She's knowledgable, funny, kind, and all around an amazing prof. Attendance is graded but it won't matter because you'll enjoy going to class. If you can, take her! You'll learn to love the topic she teaches and her! Also, it's an easy A :-)
Best professor I have ever met. Nice kind and patient. Encourage students to participate in the class. Gentle and humor

She is the best professor I have ever had at UWB. She is extremely understanding and approachable. Her lectures are actually interesting to listen to and make me look forward to her class. If you have a chance, definitely take her.

If you ever have a chance to take a class with Shannon Cram, do it. She is a phenomenal teacher, caring and passionate person that wants everyone to learn and have fun doing it. The class structure flowed so well that it left you wanting more! Her energy carries when she lectures keep you engaged and intrigued. She makes classes you want to go to

Take her class! She is by far my favorite professor Ive ever had. You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and is enthusiastic about her subject. Her class is orderly and shell give you full points as long as you did the assignment. Prof. Cram is full of wisdom and is easy to talk to outside of class & gives exensive feedback.

Other than being a morning class the professor made the course very enjoyable with her friendly and caring attitude and passion for the subject she was teaching. Be sure to do the readings and participate in class. No phones or laptops allowed which didn't end up being a big problem like I thought it would be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Favorite college professor I've had to date. Wonderful person.

Professor Cram is easily in my top 3 favorite professors of all time. She is caring, understanding, hilarious, encouraging and incredibly kind. They don't make many like her anymore. I really hope I can take another class from her before I graduate. She is also very passionate. I loved her class! And I truly enjoyed the the assigned reading.

Easy Grader and excellent teacher. She cares about the quality of discussion and how much you participate, makes the class feel comfortable and assigns interesting material. We made movie trailers, very fun. Workload is very doable if you bunker down and read for a week or two in order to finish the novel early.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: taking her class gave me a reminiscing feel of high school again.  Guaranteed to make the class laugh at least once because of her friendly personality.  Most classes are discussions with some lectures.  Online homework twice or once a week.  Always gives nice feedback and encourages every opinion.

Great professor! She is new here but she is an exceptional teacher. She is extremely helpful and makes the class assignments fun. She is also very inspirational and has a really cool story, she is a cancer survivor and works cleanup at Hanford Nuclear site. Everyone in the class definitely really liked and respected her. She definitely listens too.

This is one of the funnest classes I've ever taken. Shannon is very friendly and helpful. She even went out of her way to give me extra feedback upon request. Her curriculum is not boring and provides a great opportunity for critical thinking. She adapted to students with learning and social disabilities, which I've seen other profs struggle with.

Very disorganized, long-winded directions. The coursework wasn't that bad, but every little assignment had pages of time-wasting contradicting directions and dates for no reason. Did weird things like "study guides are optional unless you want an A." They were points worth 10% of your grade. Everything is optional if you don't want the points....

Second week of classes and she's already having us have a midterm on one lecture which is just plain terminology. This wouldn't be bad if it wasn't at least 50 slides (at most 75) with at least 2 terms on each slide. We also never went over this in lecture and never talked about it again. Definitely would not take if not required.
Powerpoint slides don't add up with study guide. And questions on quizzes are much different than what you might of studied for.

Long unorganized lectures . Canvas site is also unorganized. Opens drop boxes hours before assignments are due. Takes months to grade work. Not very responsive by email. But... she is very passionate about ecology. My recommendation: only take this class if it's in your major, you really enjoy ecology, and aforementioned points won't bother you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Yes, as a GST student, it was really hard to understand environmental science , graphs and data analysis but after Professor Crandell's teachings, office hours, help,  I was able to gain confidence and learn. She just grades your work late so expect to see your grade next quarter haha.

Caren is very passionate about what she is teaching, and is willing to work with students so that they get the most out of her class. I found her to be a great professor, she really pushes me to create the best work that I can. She expects a lot out of her students, but if you are a person who has high academic standards, you will succeed.

She has long lectures  is unorganized with the class information and often times wont post due dates til the day of. She claims participation is worth 5% of your overall grade but will randomly make class participation for an individual day worth 10 points. She then counts those 10 points towards your assignment grades and not participation grades
Except for how late she was in posting the grades she was a decent professor. She is always available to help and actually stays for hours after class to help.  It is hard to get a 4.0.

Expect your grades to not be published until the next quarter has already begun. Don't hold your students to higher expectations than you hold yourself to. Also, why wasn't the first quiz in January graded until after grades were due? In additon, she held us 30 minutes after class for a quiz she started late. Some of us have jobs we care about.

She is a tough grader, to the point that getting an A in her class is rare! She has to nit pick ever answer and will mark you of 1/4 of a point. Lectures are so long and boring! She is a total square and a stickler for the rules. No electronics in class,  or she takes them away. Haha, yes! In my opinion I think she should be teaching middle school.

This was her first time teaching BIS301 so I tried to be forgiving, but ... She often didn't post assignment materials until 3am  the morning it was due, waited until finals week to give feedback on research paper drafts, had everyone research GRASS! Because of in class work, you need to go to do well, but it's a waste of time. Nice lady, but jeez.

Not only was she an insanely hard and bias grader but she assigned so many useless assignments to distract you from studying from the exams. She requires alot of outside work with no reward. If you want to learn about this topic CHOOSE ANYONE ELSE. Literally everyone in the class agrees that she is not worth the bad grade. esp if no experience

I really enjoyed the class as a whole because the content was right up my alley. Yes, Caren seems to be disliked by most but that is because this class is challenging; it is content-rich, fast paced, and without any sort of background in ecologybiology etc. I can see how it would be frustrating. She expects a lot on exams but offers make-up points

Wetland Ecology. Took it as an elective because how hard can it be? HARD!!! My physics class was easier than this! I used to like Wetlands and now the word gives me shivers. Shes a great lady, very personable but what a terrible class. Also a lot of mandatory field trips and OMG the exams; they are pretty much impossible to get an A on.

Studied all of the power points, did all of the readings, attended each class, put in hours of volunteer work, begged for help on multiple occasions. I am a 4.0 student and I barely passed her class. Avoid her at all costs... if you got an A in her class, I am guessing you were chosen at random so she could maintain a bell curve.

I have never gotten less than a 3.5 in a class and I am pretty sure i am about to fail hers. I have done all of the readings, studied each power point, and have stayed up late preparing for each quiz. I feel like I have learned a lot of information but if you look at my quiz scores, you would never know this. Her tests do not reflect your effort.

I'm not even through this class and I can tell you Prof. Crandell is a fair grader. Do your homework, pay attention, take notes and you'll be fine. If I don't get a decent grade I am quite confident it's my own fault. She answers all questions and cares deeply about the course and her students. Again, just do the prescribed work and take notes.

I'm not even done with this class and I can tell you you get out of it what you put into it. Prof. Crandell is fair and accommodating. She does, in fact, answer questions. While she does rely heavily on PowerPoint, they're well-done, insightful and informative. Do the reading, pay attention, keep good notes and you have nothing to worry about.
It was the worst experience and now my best friend has to take class. He is going to record all her classes. I wish I would have thought of it. She is truly awful and does not know a lot.
Dry, Boring, Long-winded, should I go on? She constantly read the slides, wasn't engaging to the students, and is a ridiculously tough grader. I thought I loved science. guess not.

My GPA is a 3.88 and I have no idea if I will pass this class. The teacher is confusing, doesn't know the material and makes excuses. Average grade on midterm was just passing at 68%, and not because of the students. Before this I loved the topic, but I have lost a lot of that love after dealing with this teacher.

Lower level course - expects 400 level knowledge. She reads off the Power point and if you asks questions, she often says IDK. She takes forever to grade assignments and there is only 3 things you are graded on. She lectures on a level 200 course but exams you're expected to know more like a 300 or 400 level course information. TERRIBLE!! DONT TAKE

She is extremely nice but when she explains things she constantly says "um" making things difficult to understand & is a bit annoying. Her class sounded simple but after starting the first assignment, she expects a lot and expects students to be experts on materials researched.

For being a lower division class the coursework is crazy. She expects you to go out on field trips outside of class time 8 miles away from campus and do an all day field trip on the weekend. She has trouble public speaking and bounces around answers in an attempt to answer any questions in the classroom.  The class reminds me of high school.

She just reads off the PowerPoints and won't answer questions in class, saying you have to email. She doesn't manage class time well and often says "come to my office hours to learn the rest". There's mandatory Sat/Sun field trip, so she doesn't respect your time. She also threatens to take phones away and require them to be turned in before class.
Just really tough.  I am a 3.8 student and this course kicked my butt.  Nothing against her, interesting class, just really tough.

I really enjoyed this professor.  It was a tough class, but she was clear in what she wanted and she set up the class so that we had to do a little at at time towards a big project.  If I had more time at school, I would have tried to take more classes with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Readings are interesting & important for class discussions. Every class we have a discussion & group project on that reading. We get to only do 6 250 worded reading responses out of 11.  Some days class consists of videos which was cool. She's easy-going, a chill prof. No tolerance on phones& laptop use (unless for readings).

She's a good teacher with a very strong passion for teaching. She's clear, informative, and nice. Assigns quite a bit of reading and the class, unfortunately, was rather boring. Lots of essays, but as long as you follow her prompts and read the readings, you'll be fine. Does require a group project and presentation.

First quarter at UW Bothell. Really enjoyed her class and I thought overall she was a great teacher. BIS300 was pretty damn easy too! Would definitely recommend her. Just make sure you are willing to participate in groupclass discussions. Attendence was said to be mandatory at the beginning but after the first few weeks she stopped taking it.
She says write a paper is not clear, but then the next day goes more in depth on what she wanted!

Draws class material from many different publications, most of which she scans into a pdf so you can print them off for free. Not the best at explaining her expectations for assignments and projects, but not horrible. Assigns a lot of groupwork. Probably won't take her again if I can help it.

She is personable, but is a new teacher and seems to be overwhelmed easily.  Be cautious when asking for help because she might not really have the time but is afraid to say so. Teaches pretty well, but could use some computer skills classes...

Professor Crane is very knowledge in her area of study. You can definitely see her passion for the subject that she is teaching. This class was very structured and provided a lot of opportunity for leaning interesting ways of thinking about STS. She expects a lot from her students but grades fairly. There is a lot of reading involved.

1. We do very little actual writing during class, she treats class like a lecture 2. She sometimes goes into the TMI area. I don’t want to know my teacher has ADD, that’s personal information I don’t want to know about 3. Its a very disengaging class: she talks through most of it. Not structured. 4. Posts grades leisurely Take at your own risk
Boring and lazy. Doesn't post grades on time and also its hard to get a good grade in her class. I don't recommend her class.

She grades extremely hard. Very hard to get a good grade in her class. She does not posts grades on time. She is a very boring instructor although she "tries" to make it fun but its not. You should avoid just plainly for the sake of your grades.
She is a nice teacher. In her class, she does a lot of fun stuff. However, it is difficult to get a good grade in her class. She is strict when grading your work.

One of my favorite teachers I have ever had. Extremely helpful, extremely fun, and keeps things interesting. She is really kind and cares a lot about her students. I've taken 3 classes with her and all have been fairly difficult but I really enjoyed them thanks to her.

Sharon is very nice. We had a lot of readings to do for homework and we wrote a lot of short papers, but at the end for your final grade she will give you a grade based on how much your short papers improved upon the course of the quarter.

This project management course focuses on real experience you can actually use, not just theory. We worked through real scenarios, learned professional communication, and got helpful feedback. I left with skills I've already used in interviews and team projects. Truly prepares you for the workplace!

Just finished my last class of the quarter with this guy. He went out of his way to spend time with each team to review processes that are applicable in the real world. He gave extra credit when needed and even spent his own money to buy the class food to celebrate our project. Never had a class like this before, awesome.

They explain things in a way that actually makes sense, and throw in examples that make class less boring. Workload can be a bit much sometimes but it's not busywork, it actually helps you get the material. They're easy to talk to and pretty helpful if you're stuck. Overall a solid prof if you don't mind group work.
Refreshing change of pace from the grind of glass. Grading is set up so those who don't show up can't get a free ride. Professor seems reasonable to handle class issues when they come up.

Do not work with stuck-up petty and difficult people from day 1! Please switch to a group that has less people and work with them or you will suffer with revenge grading on peer evals that is worth most of your grade second half of the quarter. RUN, this destroyed my GPA.

Chill guy. No complaints from the professor. The classwork itself is pretty dry and most of it comes from the outside work. Also, a lot of group work in this class so if you don't like big groups (up to 15 people) then don't take it. Lastly, the work in this class would look great on a resume, so think about that.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Just got a 4.0 in one of the most rewarding classes I have ever taken! If you want to practice putting everything you have learned in school to practice, take this class. What I have learned here will stick with me forever.

You get out what you put into the course. Be prepared for a project with a real problem and a local business. If you've done this already, you may not learn many new things. If you want experience working with executives and leaders, this is great exposure for people who want to start their careers.

If you plan on taking this class, be ready for a real-life group project. You actually do outside research for a real business partner outside of school and it takes up a lot of your time. Grades really tough and even the slightest thing wrong will mark you down. If you don't like your group, strongly suggest to switch with someone. Be ready.

Professor Nick is a bad teacher. His grading is extremely unclear and expects that the class is all group projects. If you get a bad group then your grade will be bad. At most he will say "Tough Luck" and expect you to do the workload of the missing people.

I just finishing taking a course from him during winter quarter-- I agree with the last write-up. He starts off as a really tough grader but he becomes really easy by the end of the quarter. I enjoyed working with my business partner and had a good team so that was awesome.

.

He comes across as a really tough grader and nitpicks things early in the course--these things get easier as the course goes on and he comes an easier grader. My group ended up getting 100% on our final project. 


You get out of this course what you put into it--since you work on a real issue, if you put in a lot you will learn a lot.
Hope you get a good group--you work with real businesses so if you get people that don't care you can look bad.
Too many things to keep track of for project, expects over delivery on the smallest things, grades insanely hard, midterm is brutal to say the least
Class provides an opportunity for students to gain professional experience. Had a great experience working on a real project for Buck!

Took his class this last quarter and had a great experience. As others noted, this is a project oriented class (duh--it's a project management class)--so, if your group is solid then you have it good. If your group sucks then you're going to struggle. Peer evals are like 30% so group members can't leech to pass the class.

Gives real-world project experience in a class setting. The project partners can be a crap shoot--so, try to get a good one. This requires lots of group work so be prepared to carry the load if you have a poor group. Guest lectures were amazing.

Assignments were clear, she's nice, she made the midterm for my class jeopardy, there was really no study guide or layout of what will be on the final, she doesn't really teach just briefy goes over what you read for the week but didn't really learn anything. Easy class though

She is not tech savvy, which leads to complications when using Canva. The assignments do not feel connected to the final project, making the course seem disorganized. The class feels sporadic and lacks cohesion. Class time is not used effectively, and she struggles to engage the entire class. Much of the time in this course feels unproductive.

This is for 437 only. Her class is an absolute nightmare. She does not teach in class and expects a lot out of her challenge assignments. We are only given a textbook and told to refer to it to learn. HOW do you expect us to learn how to calculate budgets, FTE's, and be specific in our variables when you don't teach what that looks like????????????

criteria is extremely unclear in assignments. sends loads of feedback in that don't help. challenge assignments are not explained in class. we are expected to understand terminology and financial calculations all on our own. marks us down for not knowing, but also doesnt teach us how to do it right.

manage large class bad. kind professor. organization unclear. leaving the rest of class with no guidance

objectives each week not explained. assigned readings not reviewed. expected to apply concepts in assignments. connection for in-class activities and course is not clear

examples overly simple not aligned with course level

She can be really unorganized and she gets very frazzled easily which made me lose confidence in her. She made us take a quiz on a concept she gave the wrong formula for, saw the class failed, and had us retake it. Day of the retake she struggled to teach us the correct steps for an hour and then let us struggle on our own. She's very nice though.

Worksheets for weeks 1-7 (5 pts), discussion posts + response for weeks 1-10 (5 pts) + lowest score dropped, in-class work (10 pts) + lowest score dropped, midterm + final exams (15 pts each), Health issue brief final (25 pts), assignments submitted over 1 week late lose 25% for each week, due dates and assignment instructions unclear frequently

Cynthia Chang was amazing!! I took her and Jennifer Atkinson's combined bcore 110 class fall 2024 and it was a good decision. Be ready to participate and meet new people bc the whole class is based on groupwork. If you're looking for a fun bcore with reasonable workload, then it's perfect :) 
(Also the textbook is free if I remember correctly)

SO easy to understand, she gives the best lectures i have ever received. If you take notes and review her material she gives to study YOU WILL PASS and even get a good grade. Really easy to fall behind but she really cares about her students.

This is an easy A class if you understand the material you don't need to go to in depth into the material as she lets you use pervious tests that she uploads to canvas on the exam as notes (laptop notes are fine) but you can't look up answers. She is very nice. Lectures are boring tho. 3 tests and 1 final the lowest test gets dropped finals don't.

She's very sweet and passionate about the topic, making it more engaging. However, as others have said, she writes on her lecture slides as she goes along and they do not save, so if you want to keep track of that, you may want to ensure you show up. Exams are open-note and if you study previous exams and the answer keys, you'll likely do well!

I actually took her for BCORE 104 
-class takes place both ON and OFF campus 
-need a car to access if not you need a carpool
-Lots of pointless readings
-very passionate about subject but not great at grading
-Easy to pass
-Docs points from group projects without good reasons
-No tests or quizzes
-Mostly busy work/ readings
-nice professor
only the best professor ever. Lecture is straight forward and have a lot of extra credit opportunity. It's an easy A, if u just try to understand her material.

She's really sweet and passionate about what she teaches which I liked. She digitally writes on lecture slides but doesn't save them so when you go to Canvas to look at them, it's hard to understand so attendance is very important. If you participate and study, you'll pass with a good grade even without the textbook. Content is easy and 8/10 prof.

Polite prof; had 4 open note exams & extra credit opportunities. Usually accessible outside class. But graded finals 2 business days before grades being finalized (including extra credit) & made a few mistakes regarding grading to quite a few students. Never responded to messages about the issue despite having those 2 days to look over. Ok choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a really nice professor! The workload is manageable and I had a lot of fun in her class!

Dr. Sunkel provides a fantastic learning space that helps students learn how to be a great teacher. She is communicative and willing to work with you in any way you need. She goes above and beyond with her lesson planning and makes the course fun. If you are struggling, she will help. If you're doing well, she'll make sure to recognize it.

It is clear that she cares a lot about the class by the amount of prep work that she does before class.  She is an easy grader, and if you are struggling she will support you and most likely give you an extension if you ask. The most important thing is to go to all of the classes because ATTENDANCE IS MANDATORY! Ask her for help if you need it.

She seems nice but extremely unorganized online and in the classroom. Nothing on canvas makes sense, assignments are unclear, and refuses to respond to anything via email. I would not take any class with her unless it's required simply out of how frustrating trying to navigate anything is with her.

LAB: VERY VERY strict. Yells a lot. If you do anything to annoy him in any way he will yell at you. Make sure you know the procedure very well. But he does grade easier than the rest of the organic chemistry professors. He will let some things slide from the rubric so as long as you have everything on the rubric your fine for the lab reports.

SAVE YOURSELF AND TAKE W/ ANOTHER PROF! By far the WORST prof. I have ever had. NOT helpful in any way and encourages students to drop out by exam 2. Will not help when asked, and gives vague answers. Does not allow you to digest information before demanding answers. Will yell at class if quiet. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

Amazing lectures. No slides, he teaches by going through worksheets so you can't miss a single class. His exams are fair, he doesn't put in anything that he doesn't teach. If you study the worksheets he provides, you'll be good for the exam. He enjoys teaching and cares for his students, he is a really fair professor and he makes funny jokes.

Khushroo was really the ochem goat. He really cares about the subject and makes sure his students understand. He does extended office hours every time before an exam and even stays 3-4 hours! He responds to emails fast and does not mind helping or answering questions. The only reason i give him a 4/5 is because sometimes bro is moody and can berude

Dr. Khushroo is rigorous and kind. It reminds me of the feeling of taking classes in Asian countries. The class sheets given by him are very important. If you want to have a good grade, you need to keep practicing it. In addition, you need to think quickly because you will have a lot of questions in a limited time during the exam.

If anyone has studied in India, he is exactly like the teachers there. Very rude to the students but I can tell he still wants us to succeed. Although, he does not seem to set us up for success. I will say, only take him if you HAVE to otherwise avoid at all costs....GPA killer

Horrific experience. Exam averages have been in the low 50s and after getting exam 3 back, he said "if you are doing below average in this course and you need to withdraw, never take any of my classes again". Lacks compassion and is borderline unkind. Attendance is mandatory. No powerpoints, just worksheets, and he doesn't post all answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His curve is forgiving, if your scores are not so far below average then you will be fine. Exam is challenging, test you how much and how deep you understand the 40 pages handout per chapter. Content is kinda abstractive, people often stuck on molecular symmetry. This probably why average is low. Make sure to study in group and ask questions.

If you want to feel bad about not knowing the subject. Take him. Lots of packets that will be filled out in class. Recommended to be in class everyday if you want to learn. Office hours are not useful and ineffective.

First is the lecture, now is the lab.His intention is never to help students become successful. No matter how hard you try, he will find a way to oppress your grades. But then, he doesn't like asking about grades. The class is too much work and stressful, keep you busy with a bunch of work load. Really annoying micromanagement and questioning
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: A big no no. Nothing is effective in here, just trying to stick through and finish. If you don't need the lab, don't take it. If you want to be discouraged from liking Chemistry, be his guest

He is really caring, but it won't be very obvious. I'm impressed by how concealed his lecture is. OChem is bad because it's too long and we have to cover too much in fast pace.
