This is where quality outwin quantity, not his fault. He's very humble and knowledgeable. You just need to work hard, be respectful. Ask him good questions and practice well

He treats his students like children. Scolds students for being on their phone (even threatens to confiscate it), going to the bathroom when its not break time (there's only one 5 min break in a 2 hour class), or phrasing questions in ways he dislikes (don't use the word confused he wont like that and don't ask about the exam bc it's 'fair').
Just no.

First of all... Ochem is not as hard as people made it out to be imo. Make sure to listen to his lectures and try to participate because his exams are very reflective of his lecture. He also creates packets for each chapter and goes over it during lectures. Honestly, by taking this class, it helps you set yourself apart in the other Ochem classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I went to his office hours, he was very disrespectful and rude. Told me to get a tutor and was very condescending, actually made me quite upset. Basically humiliated me over 1 HW problem I was unsure about.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He does have some issues with respecting students. Will call you out if you dont participate. His notes are much more important than the book. 3 credit class that took the work of a 6 credit class. Review his notes long before exams, they are very hard, no one ever gets 90-100% but he curves. He loves students who put in a lot of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He knows what he's talking about and can give different explanations for a topic you're struggling with. His class is difficult but his packets are really good at breaking down the material and, more importantly, what he focuses on the exam. Exams are long (content-dense) but short in time so use time efficiently.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very disrespectful and unprofessional.
Very hard to follow during lecture. Moves very fast.
disrespectul and not an effective teacher.
He is a wonderful teacher. You will know and understand ochem after his class!!! His HW is time consuming but is very helpful. If you want to understand ochem he is the teacher for you!
Should do a better job of respecting his students

Great professor, tough class. 93% of your grade is Tests. They are hard, but fair. He so far has only graded what he lectures on. Studying that worked for me; study lecture notes, find online ochem tests, do review problems he gives along with the problems at the end of lecture notes. If you have a 4.0, just come to terms you will loose it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Khushroo is a phenomenal lecturer. He puts a lot into his classes, he also expects a lot out of students. He can be a little intimidating but he truly cares about his students. My advice: go to his office hours, he will tutor you for 90 minutes straight if you need help, he loves to teach and likes to see them take an active role in their education

Great teacher. I have been fearful of organic chemistry, and he explains things so thoroughly and so well, and has the best lecture packets and daily review sheets. He is always available over email and gets back to you quickly, grades things quickly, and goes above and beyond for his students. Wish he taught more classes at UW Bothell!!

Khushroo is UNDENIABLY the best organic chemistry teacher out there. Absolutley my favorite teacher at this school. His chapter packets are AMAZING. He is funny, helpful, motivating and extremely hard-working and you can tell he really cares about his students and how well they do. Go to his office hours and put in the work, you will not regret it!

He is a tough grader and his tests are tough as well, but he outlines his expectations very clearly, and problems from his handouts are nearly identical to the type of problems on exams. He can be kind of intimidating at times, but overall, he's knowledgeable, fair, and explains very clearly. Don't expect to get through without a ton of studying.
Would highly recommend buying the solutions manual to the book because sometimes he gives homework problems and gives you problems from the book to practice for each chapter.

Honestly the best professor I've ever had. Explains thoroughly, is funny, tough but very fair grader. He gives the best packets for lectures, with practice problems at the end (and lengthy explanations), and lists relevant practice problems in the book, which definitely should be done before exams. Made me go from hating OCHEM to loving it.

Amazing professor. He provided you with amazing notes that you needed to know on the exams. Doesn't even have to read through the chapter to understand it since everything was cover in his lectures and notes. Doing practice problems in the book is recommended! Really helpdul during his office hours don't be scared to go to his office hours for help

Great professor, provides us with notes and examples that he personally made. The course as a whole is definitely fast and rigorous, but with effort it is manageable. Khushroo is a great lecturer and if you pay attention in class and use his notes wisely there is absolutely no need to even touch the book. Definitely recommend!

He's a very difficult teacher. He asks you to print a tree's worth of paper for class lecture to follow along as he goes too fast. Although he knows his stuff, his explanations are often hard to understand. He can be a little tense at times and lectures tend to drag on. Wouldn't recommend for those who can't learn from the text themselves.

He doesn't respect his students and often loses his temper. After midterms he would rant and yell at us for over five minutes for not doing better. Very unprofessional. His explanations are often wrong, doing the end of chapter problems doesn't help, and his lecture slides are from 2006 and full of outdated subjects. Do not recommend.

Organic Chemistry is hard--deal with it. That being said, he knows his stuff and his teaching style and handouts allow students to actually actively learn in class instead of just mindlessly listening to him lecture. Go to his office hours. He will help you. I couldn't imagine having a different professor

The class is hard but Ochem itself is a hard subject so if you are looking to breeze through and NOT learn anything this is not the professor for you.  He is an excellent teacher and he expects you to work for your grade. In this case, the grade you get is a reflection of your effort and preparation not the professor's ability to teach.

Smart guy but terrible teacher. Goes too fast and thinks you know the material so he doesn't go in depth of what he is teaching. Do not take him unless you are good at ochem and can learn on your own.
Yep, welcome to ochem, different playing field.
welcome to ochem

He's nice but his grading makes no sense. he'll dock points for things not mentioned in the lab manual in a vague sentence. Pretty much every link posted doesn't work. Asking him for help/a question usually leads to a semi-related answer then to an unrelated topic and trying to get the answer you want feels re-prompting an ai over and over
Joe is a super chill dude I've heard he yaps but he has a lot of knowledge and cares about the students

I've taken multiple EE labs with Joe and appreciate his wisdom and experience. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. As long as you show up, participate, are respectful, and put the effort in, then you will pass. Don't arrive late and don't talk while he is explaining the labs as it's rude and you'll get on his bad side.

Be prepared to cover the same 3 same presentations slides over 3 months. Talks about himself constantly. Examples are given from the perspective of his own experience and it is always the same story! Interrupts Professor Hannachi constantly. Not sure if they are supposed to be a team or if Joe is trying to establish dominance.

I took CSS315 with her, and it was frustrating. She and her TA nitpicked minor details, leading to unfair point deductions. Attendance was strict—even if you were sick and couldn't join online, you'd still lose 10 points. Feedback was vague, and her rigid “my way or the highway” approach made learning difficult. I wouldn't recommend her class.

Not the best class I've taken at UWB. This isn't the professors fault but the cybersecurity curriculum is a hot mess and pretty disorganized. Lectures for about an hour each class, and you are given a very long worksheet afterwards. Class is sort of interesting but mostly boring. A good grade is doable in this class but a 4.0 is impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took the CSS 301 with her and enjoyed it. Prof. Deschene is knowledgable and helpful. I appreciate her.

Worst professor ever. Office hour is limited and if you do not follow what she wants you will fail this class. Horrible professor and the worst professor ever. Refuse to admit that she is wrong. Such a GPA killer.

Don't let the other reviews freak you out! Her class isn't nearly as hard or bad as most people suggest. Just attend class, do the homework, and try hard on the drafts so you get useful feedback. easy peezy lemon squeezey.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Marie is a nice person but not a good professor. The layout of this class is awful and doesn't make sense (e.g. we learned grammar at the end of the quarter). Terrible feedback and very subjective grading. If a quiz answer is not word for word then expect a 0 on that question. It's impossible to receive a 4.0 if you don't get 100% on everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 301 has serious academic problems. there is no thinking allowed and you will be graded down based on the metadata in your word document. Marie is not helpful and admits to grading based on opinion. office hours are a joke. she makes incorrect quiz questions multiple times and wont admit it, grades harshly and isn't flexible. take Sinclair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This teacher gives very little feedback if at all, and grading is based on "improvement" rather than actual measurable metrics. You need a 100% or above to get a 4.0, but extra credit is not given and if you miss points on even one assignment that drops you down to at most a 3.9. Office hours are both useless and the only way you will pass.

The problem with CSS 301 is not the professors. It is Laurie Anderson, the creator of this horrible curriculum. The professors are under her rule, are her puppets, and she is the supreme ruler. You will drown in homework, you will suffer, you will most likely not make it out alive. Marie Deschene is a great professor she is funny and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 301 is a demanding class so be ready to read 15 pages of reading before every class. Quizzes are easy if you read and prepare. LOTS of homework. Your life will become technical writing but overall the class is quite fun. The time goes by fast and class time is useful. Highly recommend taking prof Deschene over ANY other prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Perkins teaching style is amazing. Even through the class can feel tough at times, I always felt like I could ask him for help or a better explanation.

I'm not going to lie. This class was hard. But professor Detroit took it to the next level and really worked hard to allow each one of us to get work done and pass the class. Of the 3 1/2 years, Patrick is one of my favorites. There are so many opportunities to grow in this class. 100% recommend you take him.

I've been in college 6 years; majored in engineering, culinary arts, and accounting between 4 different colleges , and Patrick Detroit was the best teacher I've ever had. I don't care who else is teaching this class. Go out of your way to take this professor. You'll learn, you'll have a tremendous amount of fun, and you won't even work that hard.

Super chill dude. Interesting lectures. Gives no (or bare minimum) instruction on projects and assignments which is kinda frustrating. Come to class, do the Pearson hw and should do fine on tests. Doesn't ever respond to email so you gotta talk to him before or after class if you have a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Patrick was an amazing lecturer! Although I don't understand anything in manufacturing, his operations class was manageable with the help of littlefield simulation, stratapult experiments and boeing tour. A lot of team work is required for classes and he doesn't give any instructions for projects, but he is very laid back. Cares about his students!
Great lecturer, often had short class sessions depending on topic. Extremely supportive of students. Office hours were by appointment but he was very helpful and often available after class.

Patrick is probably one of my favorite professors at UWB. He is so incredibly awesome, and takes time to get to know his students. He is lecture heavy, but he posts all of his notes online and they really help! I would totally recommend taking him at least once if you have the chance.
He posts the lecture notes online in case you can't make it to class and shows you how to do everything. Very reasonable grader!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: she was great, great energy, great topics and I loved coming to class. she was also very helpful on assignments or if you needed accommodations. the only thing I didn't like was how assignments were posted with very short notice and not at the start of the week.

I wouldnt say Professor DeSmet was horrible, but she wasnt great either. I took this class because of the great ratings and I regret my decision. Throughout the entire quarter there were maybe 6-7 assignments and she doesnt grade them until the very end of the quarter. You literally have no idea how your doing. Please take anyone else
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like that professor desmet doesnt lecture the entire class and gives us breaks. She is decent, she definitely isnt a 5/5 easy 4.0 professor. It has been 6 ish weeks in the quarter and she hasnt graded anything. Dont take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a great people person and is willing to work around and reformat assignments to give you the most creative outcome.

Raissa is one of the most amazing professors I have had. I took her course last winter and she was so helpful, so clear with her instructions, and she gave a lot of feedback on the final. She allows you to express who you are in class as well!
She's very friendly. One of the best teachers I've had for sure.

His teaching style focuses on fundamentals, avoiding fashion in case studies or readings. This approach helped me understand management concepts better. I enjoyed the lively class discussions prompted by the professor's questions. While some readings were dense, most were engaging and relevant.

Very traditional, either 100% on quiz or get a 0 you have 10 minutes with 10 questions. Exam is in person, on paper, no electronics allowed, and puts on A LOT of reading. Is really nice and does care about teaching, but is a tough grader. Elective class with an avg 3.4/4.0 gpa, harder than capstones and other classes for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Denis is good, a solid mid average especially because he is very traditional. On todays competitive & dynamic business world, being very traditional at the core doesn't really makes sense. I could relate my everyday professional life with the lectures but he is heavily dependent on ancient techniques to solving concurrent business problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Denis is great at giving useful lectures replying to emails. He cares about the material and if you attend the lectures then you'll pass. There is a bit of reading and the quizzes pertain heavily to the material. Lots of group work, but the workload is simple and makes a lot of sense. Denis will be your friend if you make him yours.

Denis' class was mandatory for the MBA program. This class was beneficial but even with a one page for the exam, it was harder than I thought. I would focus on learning the concepts in his lectures and really hone in one some readings you like for the essay questions on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Denis is great at giving feedback and replying to emails. He cares about the material and if you attend the lectures then you'll pass. There is a lot of reading and quizzes almost every week, but you get 2 chances for the quiz. Most important is the group work because you are with them for the entire quarter. If your group sucks then good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Denis is extremely knowledgeable and values his students. He wants you to participate in discussions based on readings and enjoys hearing your ideas. He cares a lot about your learning and wants his students to become effective communicators. If any class in college so far has best prepared me for a career one day, it might be this one.
Professor Trapido is kind, however he is a tough grader and your grade is made up almost entirely of group projects. If your group is lazy youre going to struggle in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun professor who cares about students. Pop-quizzes can be about trivial things. Start group project early as you have to compare two different companies. The simulations are fun, especially the group culture/dynamics one. Test is ok, just be sure to get the main points. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Trapido's class was a lot of reading and pop quizzes sometimes had trivial facts you need to know. The group project plays a big part of your grade-- do not start last minute. Most of the lectures are intuitive but the simulations are fun. Personality wise, Trapido has an almost awkward sense of humor but genuinely cares about his students success.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Trapido is one of the impactful professors I have ever had. His class simulations are fun and are very applicable to the real world. He really cares whether the students are getting something from the lessons he makes. His lessons have helped me mature from a personal sense and a professional sense. 10/10 would take this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: A really awesome prof who cares a lot about the learning of his students. We played a lot of games and simulations that relate to the coursework that were both fun and a great learning experience. Read BEFORE class to be prepared for discussions + pop quizzes (which are mostly easy comprehension). Stay on track + do reading and it won't be hard
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Trapido is an excellent, hilarious teacher who uses really creative methods to teach the class and does an excellent job of it. He gives really good feedback and makes sure that everyone is not only learning, but is enjoying the class as well. 10/10 would take as much as possible.

Professor Trapido is a highly educated and experienced professor. There is always a case to read before class, they can be long sometimes but the concept, stories are familiar and helpful for the class and your knowledge in general. Reading before class helps with pop quizzes, participation and exams. He gives amazing lectures and inspirational.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: A very caring professor that actively strives to encourage his students to contribute. Attendance is mandatory due to pop quizzes, but as long as you do the assigned reading, you should be in good shape.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: pop quizzes can make or break your grade, don't miss class or you won't pass and don't miss any assignments because there are only a few, miss one and you'll likely fail. Boring lectures, read the Harvard articles and the slides he presents and you should be set for the pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: 4 pop quiz group paper dont skip class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Loved the class. Participation was very important but Denis made it a comfortable class to get involved in. Those who came to class got a good grade. Lots of readings to do outside of class but are not essential to passing the class. A very supportive kind and flexible teacher. He cares about his students and makes everyone feel appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: I really like Denis. He is an overall nice professor and he goes out of his way to help his students. The only downfall is his lectures and reading. They can be a bit dry a boring. Take good notes and have a good understanding on readings. They will help you on the pop quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's OK. I skipped class and he gave me a 2.0 for missing important class sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Denis was an amazing professor. Very very clear instructions and his manner in teaching is wonderful. What he teaches will definitely come in to use for anybody that will be working in any type of company. He knows what he is teaching and he gives you more than enough to prepare for any assignment or quizzes he gives. Denis is one of my favorite!!
Amazing professor. He is very helpful. Beaware of the pop quizzes.
What I really liked about this professor, was that he was truly caring and was a great help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I had the privilege of being a student of Professor Trapido's "Management of Organizations" course in my first quarter at UW Bothell.  Professor Trapido is one of my favorite professors at the UW Bothell School of Business.  Not only was his course fun and enlightening, but he is very personable and caring.  I absolutely recommend his course(s).
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Denis is very quirky. He is enthusiastic and wants students to learn. He has 4 pop quizzes on the reading material throughout the quarter. The biggest part of the grade are group projects, so if you get stuck with a bad group, good luck. The work isn't too difficult. He values participation very much.

The book that he uses is a good source. However, his grading method is kind of weird. Pop quizzes is 30% of your grade, so come to class and make sure you can take all the quizzes. There are just 4 pop quizzes but drop one. The questions are just about have you read the reading, not necessary apply to what you learn from reading.

Dennis is there to help you pass and succeed. This is pretty much an easy class and as long as you try then you will be fine. There is a lot of group work involved, group papers and assignments so be prepared to collaborate.

He starts very fast and expects you to already know C++, which can be rough. Tests are really hard, and doing poorly on one can affect the whole quarter. He's funny, explains well, and is lenient. Assignments aren't worth much. Final grade = weight×Test 1 + weight×Test 2 + w×Test 3 + w×assignmnt grade. A lot of outside effort is needed to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM! Unless you already know C++. His tests & EXAM ARE HARD and CLOSED NOTES. He gives no extra credit. Exams are worth 65% of the grade, projects are worth 35%

Professor Dimpsey is passionate about what he does and challenges his students. His assignments are difficult at times but he is always available to help out and guide you through struggles. Get ready for some difficult exams.
his teaching is great but his grades are HARSH. if you miss a bug it could mess up his tests and you would loss so many points because of it.

If you are reading this, DO NOT TAKE HIM! He assumes that you already know linux for this course. His tests are closed note and most of the code he writes are wrong. He gives no extra credit. You can have 100 on all your homeworks but if you struggle with the tests, you will fail this class. He don't care about you as a student. 


Just Dont...
Dimpsey is very caring, and he knows his stuff. The exams are a bit hard, but if you do the readings and attend his lectures, you should be fine.

Professor Dimpsey truly cares about his students - Whether it's responding to emails quickly or giving additional examples in class. This class was particularly challenging as the class itself was extremely difficult, and the professor did not make the class any easier. 2 midterms and 1 final with no notes but heavy curve which helped a lot.

Prof. Dimpsey cares whether we understand the material. He responds to emails very quickly and explains concepts from class.

The scale and magnitude of the assignments was overwhelming. I spent too much time on relatively meaningless homework assignments. He has good ideas for projects, but the instructions are unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: 2 exams and 5 projects (1 is optional). No extra credit. Exams r difficult and worth 55% of grade. Projects are worth 45%. Projects are not too hard but he uses alot of test cases so if your project isn't flawless you will lose points. He is good about letting you fix it if you ask. Coding guidelines were annoying and makes u lose credit. C++ class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hard not only because the tests are weighted heavily, but the content can be challenging for those who haven't worked with C++. He provides plenty of resources like recorded lectures, but expect to do at least some learning on your own when taking this course (as with any other 342 prof). Overall, a great class taught by a great prof.

By far the most lenient C++ professor I've seen so far. I've gotten a lot of extensions but ended up failing (severe depression). Be sure you ask him immediately if you have questions. This is C++, can't slack or falling behind will be easy. Compared to others, he doesn't force us to use Visual Studio Code- a lot more flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a very caring inspirational professor. He may respond late to email during weekends. Not easy grader but his class was very fun, I learnt a lot from him.

Try to attend this class in person as much as possible. Always ask questions ab HW edge cases, bc u can lose easy points if not covered. Study hard for tests because they are tough. Overall excellent professor bc he was kind, understanding, and made class fun. However, work HARD bc the class is not easy. DONT PROCRASTINATE or u will be humbled.
A must take class. The mid term and final exams are pretty tough, but we get to learn a lot through this class.

Great professor, Every assignment is very clear and descriptive. 342 is a demanding class by itself but Dimpsey does a great job teaching it without making it too difficult. The tests were difficult but they were a good opportunity to learn, and Dimpsey was always very forgiving with answers.

I enjoy that he seems like an understanding professor. He does not cross boundaries. Still expects students to put in the effort. He does his job- you do yours and it'll all be good. Some professors really do be praying for students' downfalls. I find it so unnecessary when professors go out of their ways to scare students. He has my respect.

The programs are kinda tricky; it is easy to lose a few points because you didn't cover an edge case. The tests are pretty hard, and some questions are designed to be tricky. Not an extremely hard class, but it can get frustrating. If you miss a few points here and there, it is fine. He will boost your grade by a little bit at the end.

Professor Dimpsey is a nice professor who gives solid lectures and is flexible with deadlines for student. But outside of that, he can be tough sometimes. His exams are tough and sometimes we don't have time to cover the difficult materials in class. Office hours are also limited. Overall, Dimpsey is a good choice, but don't expect it to be easy.
good lectures great assignments stupid exams
He makes a challenging subject really easy to understand. He welcomes questions and challenges. He is a very skillful teacher.

This professor was really amazing and considerate of students. He made sure not to test on anything we did not cover and made sure everything covered was clear. While homework specs werent always totally clear, he would clear them up in class, so ALWAYS show up to class. He has a lenient curving system and his tests are very fair but challenge you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I like him.

Well-experienced in cloud computing and teaches valuable lessons on modern tech topics (microservices, NoSQL, Cloud Architecture, etc.). Takes student feedback seriously and is flexible on deadlines to accommodate the speed of students picking up topics. Tests are tough but fair and projects are also tough but very applicable and realistic.

Professor Dimpsey is a great professor. If you get the chance to take a class with him teaching jump on it! You may not always have the chance to work with professors that really know their stuff and taking a class with prof Dimspsey allows you to reap what you put into the class.

Professor Dimpsey is a great professor, he takes his time in class and goes slow to make sure that you understand the algorithms that he teaches and makes sure that everyone understands before moving on. The professor is a little hard to access out of class. If you email him a question it will take a day and his office hours are only 1 hr long.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You may be asking why I only gave him a 3 if I tagged him as caring, but thats what he is. He really cares about his students understanding, but his tests and assignments can be so vague that even asking questions cant clear it up. It really sucks because hes such a nice guy, but he doesnt explain things enough on tests and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rob is very knowledgeable in his field and it shows in his lectures. He cares about his students understanding the material most of the time. His biggest flaw is his assignments. He's a VERY implicit grader. no official rubric provided prior to due date on assignments. At least he curves plenty so you pass. study groups are key for passing 342.

UWB is very lucky to have Dimpsey. He grades harder than other professors, but this pushes you to learn more. Very important if you want to get an internship or job, especially at FAANG. A 3.0 in Dimpsey's CSS 342 will take you miles farther than a 4.0 in a different CSS 342 section if you take everything he has to teach seriously.

Professor Dimpsey is a great person. You can really tell he likes to teach and wants you to learn. Now, the class is difficult. Programming assignments are extensive and grading is vague (50% of grade). The exams are a challenge (3 - 50% of grade). His grading is based on point accumulations rather than percentages set to a specific grade range.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pros: Is a nice person. 1 10min break for 2 hr lectures. Email-responsive. Cons: HW specs sometimes not clear. Gets caught up on his errors while showing class examples. Doing the summation steps for Big O polynomial but got himself confused by his own calculation and just tried to move on w/o clarifying.

Homework assignments were vague at best. You have no idea what you're being graded on. Constantly let students interrupt class with their off-topic I-know-everything questions. If you ask homework questions, his answer most likely contradicted what the spec said, so you really don't know what's going on. Lectures were boring. Not really a fan.

He is a nice teacher for sure but he grades so harshly. there isnt a good rubric and cuts points on random things. Expects us to know things he hasnt even covered in the class and those things may even show up in the exam. If students asks questions related to hw or anything then only he answer else get ready to participate enormously in office hrs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No rubric for programs. He only tells students who ask specific questions about certain things that will be deducted from the program. He isn't specific about what he wants in the program, so most people lose a lot of points. He expects us to know things despite him not teaching the subject. He is a nice teacher, but his test and grading system suc
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, passionate about his field and teaching. Explains complex topics well.

Professor Dimpsey is the best professor I had. Great teaching style and great lectures. The course is interesting and practical. Grading is vague but fair. He tests comprehension of the material, not memorization. Program assignments are not that tough but expect a lot of self-learning.

Dimpsy is a fun lecturer, but the difficulty of assignments and tests really makes the class feel painful. He's one of those professors where no matter how much you study, you can't help but feel unprepared for the tests. Complex assignments require too much time outside of class to complete, smaller topic focused projects would have been nice.

Dimpsey was a fantastic teacher. His lectures are clean and understandable. He does lots of practice problems (+ basically gives you the answer to the HW) during his lectures. Has lots of resources for preparation for tests and the questions are very similar. Overall, this was an easy A class. (Make sure you start HWs early)

He's a good professor but doesn't really understand the fact that other students have commitments too. Although he isn't very accomodating in that sense, I would say his classes are very structured and it's hard to fail this class. Mark it as S/NS if you're in interviewing season--his exams are hard and I doubt everything can be balanced
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher. Seems like a great guy in general. He really made me enjoy computer science again after going through so many professors that little by little have dragged my passion for it down. Professor Dimpsey really changed things for me with his lectures and inspirational teaching style.

One of the best professors in the Computer Science department. He makes lectures more fascinating and he doesn't give the answer to a question right away but gives hints and helps you make the connections yourself. He cracks some jokes which helps break up the lecture's heavy material at times. Programs and homework assignments are manageable.
Good class. Prof is very smart, nice guy, fair grader, good lectures.

Overall great professor. Taught Operating Systems in a way that everyone understood. Obviously experienced in teaching. Average on all assignments was an around an A but the hard part were the tests - a midterm and final. The grade is set in a way where it's easy to pass the class.

Nice guy, but I would not take him again as an instructor. His assignment requirements change in class during lectures but not on the assignment sheets. No rubric available whatsoever. His TA grades based on his opinions and not by requirements. His exams are long and tedious. Can be helpful but not available beyond office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best lecturers I've had so far. His style of teaching keeps you interested and he makes sure to teach you the key points of a subject. Somehow he manages to find realistic examples for almost everything taught...  Like other reviewers have said; his classes are tough but you will learn a TON if you put the effort in.

CSS342 is hard in general, but Dimplsey himself is pretty tough compared to other instructor. You will learn a lot, but getting A is hard (not impossible though). His only drawback is he didn't prep you very well for test, so you don't really know what to expect. Lecture are very good and he is helpful though.

Although some teaching techniques can be a little frustrating Dimpsey is a great professor, and youll learn a ton in this class. He really cares about his students and his office hours are well worth the effort. Labs are challenging and interesting. Tests are hard, and the final is comprehensive.

If you want an easy A, do not take him.  If you want to really become a better programmer, take him.  Dimpsey is a fabulous professor who writes all his own assignments for 342 and they are significantly more relevant to the real world, object oriented programming you will do in industry.

Said the first day people learn more when they struggle. Lectures are designed for 2 hrs, but 501 is only 1:40 so it was often cut short. Lots of practice problems  provided, but few solutions, so they are of limited help. Office hours are 4:45  5:45, nearly impossible if you have a 9-5 job. However, he's super nice and lectures were never boring.

Professor is the most awesome professor I have had so far. What makes him awesome is his ability to be challenging, yet caring for the success of students. He provides time to help students succeed as long as that student takes advantage of it wants to succeed by also caring about their own success. I am looking forward to another class with him.
Reasonable. Material is challenging for sure. Median class on quiz was 76%, and median on mid term was 78%. Office hour help a lot for me.
great teacher ad explain well.

The tests are the hardest I've ever encountered. Dimpsey teaches the class by giving you a sweep of the material, but its up to you to master it. It was very difficult determining what he wanted us to know, and if you don't prepare properly for the exams your grade will come as a shock. However he's very nice and accommodating of students' needs.

This was my first real class in the CSS program and it was a big challenge. I was really nervous starting out and had zero C++ experience before this class. All that being said, I ended up doing well and it was largely due to the professor. He provides thorough answers to student questions and presents material in a good order.

Explicitly says that his tests are very hard but are extremely curved. Class average was 60%, but he curves that average into a 3.5 gpa. Assignments were not made by him, but he is always willing to explain. Barely any office hours. Very friendly and knowledgeable guy. I see a lot of negative 342 reviews, but 342 is SUPPOSE to be a hard class.
If you want to have a good GPA, don't take his class.

Start early on the projects, STUDY HARD for the tests, because they are worth a lot. I struggled with them; they were very very difficult and he grades hard, but I learned plenty, and its a course about being precise. Be sure to practice your C++ because its a fast paced class. I would take a class with him again.

Worked very hard to present the information in a logical and understandable way.  He was very open to student questions and always took the time to answer them thoroughly.   Didn't give a lot of feedback on coding assignments, but otherwise a great class.
He's very smart, and holds students to a high standard. His tests are difficult but not impossible. You will learn a lot from him if you pay attention. CSS 332 along with 343 helps a lot.
No feedback on homework. Hard to meet professor. Exams were tough. You better know C++ before you take his class.

Never received anything less than an 'A' in a programming until this class. Dimpsey is a very nice guy, but very unfair in grading. Everyone of his assignments had changed requirements and instead of updating the document, he expected you to remember from lecture. If you missed class then you had no idea the requirements changed.

If you read his assignments carefully, the information you need is there. He spent a lot of time during class and breaks talking with students and answering questions. I thought his teaching style was clear and fair. He is the best professor I've had at this school so far and seems to really care about his students' learning.

He didn't give us a lot of office hours, which was very disappointing. It was also so hard to get feedback on assignments, meaning it is hard for me to improve. He is a very tough grader and I didn't trust the TA's with the grades they gave. Midterm was very hard but final was okay. Not everything he explained was clear.

Because he is not the grader of the assignment, he gives absolutely no feedback on them and neither does the TAs. For me, the assignments are hard and it is very difficult to get help on them because theres usually a line during his office hours. Unfortunately, he was the only professor teaching it so everyone had no choice.

His lectures were just fine and he clearly liked certain topics over others and emphasized them more such as creating an interface and recursion.  He seemed like a nice guy, but his grading was trash.  The average of the class seemed to be set around a 2.8, so if you did just average then thats what you got.

I took the add on class 332 as well. That class was actually really helpful and was also taught by him; however, his 342 class he had absolutely no time to help. When I came to him and asked how I could get additional help he told me I should just keep practicing coding. He does not give feedback on homework. Class is extremely difficult.

Yes, CSS is hard so it's not fair to complain about hard tests. Dimpsey does a good job of explaining concepts and never belittled anyone or anything that anyone brought up. Go to class, take good notes, and do the HW by yourself. You'll pass easily.

Graded on 5 projects, one quiz, a mid term, and a final. The projects are fairly easy but the tests are the hardest I've ever taken.... ever. Otherwise, Dimpsey is nice and funny and will help you in depth if you go his office hours. Take the 332 companion class, he goes over assignments and gives tips. Didn't open the text book once.

No feedback on programming projects. If you ask a question about the lab, he refers you to the grader, which in turn just tells you to run the test code.  Expects you to know above and beyond. Codes to the projector so fast that no one can catch up, so it's just better to sit back and look, trying to understand (or take photos of the projector).

I was not expecting to enjoy this class given that I just took it to fill in one of my higher-level elective requirements but Raissa made the class so enjoyable and engaging. Would love to take her again!

Raissa is a very nice person, not such a great professor, so unorganized, didn't let us know that a class was going to be on zoom, so people still showed up, wasted gas and time, very inconsiderate. Doesn't know how to use canvas ,idk?  But always issues with assignments, grading, posting announcements, and answering emails. Do not take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Raissa is super caring and the most engaging lecturer I have had at UW Bothell. If you need or want to take a Global studies/Ethnic studies you wont regret taking her class. She approaches her topics with a perfect blend of seriousness, considering the issues she presents, paired with her comical and uplifting personality when appropriate.

Absolutely loved having Raissa as my prof for this quarter. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches, and it shows. Attendance was mandatory which made me groan at first, but I ended up looking forward to coming to class every week. She makes sure everyone chats with each other so that we can create a sense of community. LOVE HER.

I just got a 5/15 for an assignment in which I put a lot of efforts... I don't understand. I work really hard for the class and now I am at the borderline of failing??? I won't really recommend her class.

Nice lectures, bad person. She will give you some "hints" instead of telling you what you should do. Sometimes I feel she is chill but sometimes it is frustrating and confusing to fulfill her requirements. She is always polite and we respect her. But she will keep distances from students and seldom respond email until days later. Not recommend

The system constantly removed my comment so i have to post it again. 

The professor never gave responses on time, and even after I asked for it, she would give ambiguous comments. Not to mention being a strict grader and never give me another chance to improve. 
DONT TAKE HER CLASS

Professor DeSmet is engaging and cares about her students. While the writing assignments can be challenging, following instructions and utilizing resources like Unstuck ai for study prep can help you succeed in her fair but thorough class.

Class was fine, quite boring and could have been condensed into one class rather than two. She's a tad un-amusing but fairly supportive when you are falling behind. Only thing that really bugged me is she never submitted my final grades and then went on sabbatical and is entirely unreachable. All of my grades are hidden and I don't know how I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's mother. Cares so much about students' growth and engagement, and creates avenues for success in the ways that they may learn best. I had such a great time across 3 classes with her. Deserved that Distinguished Teaching Award for being a queen.

She is very understanding and compassionate. The class itself was kind of boring but it was an easy class for Arts and Humanities credit. 4.0 not guaranteed because of how little assignments are graded. If you miss just a few points a 4.0 is impossible. Extra credit so little it barely affects your grade. Mostly watching movies, reading articles.

This class was extremely boring and pointless. I struggle to remember anything I learned as the content was so art-focused and shallow that it was impossible to stay engaged in class. Honestly, this class could probably be condensed into 2-3 weeks if you cut off all the fat of the course (which there is a lot of, movies, etc.). 4.0 not guaranteed.

Raissa is a very nice person. BIS 372 was not a tough upper elective class, but she can be a bit harsh with her grading on the 2 essays. She also unfortunately takes weeks to post grades, and since you are only graded by 5-6 things, your grade on Canvas might look scary. Lots of readings assigned, but you can just skim them. Overall, easy 4.0.

Raissa is the definition of a professor who cares about her subject and her students. Her energy, humor, and her enthusiasm for teaching this class were infectious. She is thorough but fair in his grading, and if you ever need help on your papers, she's more than willing to do so. By far the best prof I've had at UWB.

She is a VERY nice person but could have been a better teacher. The concepts are interesting but she could have been better at communicating them. I like that she doesn't lecture for the full 2 hours and has us take breaks.
Prof. DeSmet was very kind and understanding, and heavily encouraged self-care. She was a fair grader, and left thoughtful feedback on our written work. Would absolutely take another class with her!

I find Professor DeSmet to be great in terms of teaching what she is supposed to teach. However, she often oversimplifies things, and having some prior knowledge about what she teaches, she waters it down a bit too much. She is a very, VERY nice and engaging person, which I have nothing to complain about, but a little more depth would be nice.

I've done 3 classes with her (372, 490, and now 499). She's a very sweet teacher and person, who really has the best interests of students in mind. Her lectures are great and make the material much more accessible! She assigns lots of group work. The low reviews from recent quarters don't make sense in my eyes AT. ALL.

She is a very kind person and I appreciate how she's willing to support students with anything. This class is not hard but there is a lot of reading. Assignments are interesting especially the student authored exam at the end. I would take her again.
She is nice but not the best instructor when it comes to actually teaching. I paid tuition for CLASS, not a painful attempt at seeming relatable to students with humor.

The writing assignments were too complex and unclear for the level of writing most students were comfortable with. It's not fair that she was never satisfied with our writing and always nitpicked on little things.
She's nice & clearly sets her expectations. Her lectures are great. If you follow directions on assignments, you're in a good shape to get an A in this class.

I'm going to be the odd one out here. I was also in her class this quarter and I liked her. Y'all didn't read instructions or get help. Raissa is a fantastic instructor, incredibly knowledgeable and kind, but you need to actually do the work to succeed in her classes. This was my second class with her and I can tell she appreciates engagement.

She was ok. I like her personality but don't think I actually learned anything in the class. I got a 4.0 which is attainable despite what other students from this quarter claimed, just put in effort and follow directions. Core class for my major in CLA but feels disconnected from my other CLA classes (literature).

Passionate and can get stuck in lecture mode, but out of all the teachers I've had at UWB, she has been the most engaged, caring, and easygoing. She has a very generous late work policy. Everyone else is just bitter because they didn't put effort into the class.
She's just awful at her job and all of us had to suffer for it. I literally had no idea whether I was passing or failing the class the entire time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very slow to grade papers, disorganized, confusing grading and incredibly verbose lectures on subjects only tangentially related to the course.

She did not grade any of the assignments until the last day of quarter. She did not give much feedback on any of the papers. This was an incredibly frustrating class and almost everyone I talked to in it also hated it. Avoid this teacher if you want to know how you're actually doing in class.

Y'all need to chill. She had family issues! I'm doing the SEAPF independent study with her and was in two of her classes last year and had NO problems. You just need to put in effort and show her that you care about what you're doing. She's very kind and approachable.

Really sweet and caring. This class was interesting and challenges students to really delve into what readings are about. Graded on one group project, in class participation, and two big essays which she explains clearly and gives plenty of time to do and also offers extensions. I recommend!
She is a nice teacher and has a good sense of humor. She wants students to do well. I'd take her again.

Raissa is a REALLY good teacher. She really loves what she's doing and is here to support you if you need it. Her lectures are very lively, and she's quite funny even if you learn a lot too. Writing assignments will stretch your thinking. Office hours are helpful. Highly recommend!

She is a nice person but her portfolio capstone class is NOT what I signed up for. Too many useless assignments and then building the portfolio in the end, plus she's super slow with grading so this class was agonizing. Easy, but a waste of time and energy.

I think she's a very nice person but the way this specific class is organized could be improved significantly. You get group work late in the quarter and if your group sucks, you're screwed unless you talk to her. This happened to me and she let me work on my own to get a 4.0. Lectures are great, there's almost no confusion in what you're learning.

What a waste of time and tuition for Capstone class. Although she is nice, her class is terrible. The way the work is assigned and organized will drive you crazy. Should have been async, this class was only productive for about 15 minutes.

If u read and show up to class, ur guaranteed a 4.0. Lectures were interesting, but a tad long. You have no exams but u do have weekly discussions and 2 papers. Gives good feedback on ur writing. She makes it very clear she wants everyone to get a 4.0 but also learn. If u put some effort in u'll get a really good grade.

Easy class, great teacher. She's funny, a people person and makes all students feel welcome in class. She is open to discussion and alternative methods on assignments. She cares about students and wants to know what they think, and is super knowledgeable about many things. A+ professor.
Best available for the worst class in IAS. BIS499 is required but she is one of the best choices you can have in an instructor for it. FOR FUTURE STUDENTS: she teaches it only in winter and spring.

All the problems with this class are blamed on the structure and standardization of BIS 499, probably the most useless class in IAS, rather than on her. She is a great teacher, as evidenced by her other classes (I also took 372), but she kinda has no control over the way 499 is taught. If you want a good teacher for this required class, take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: You will learn a lot from her! She makes time in class for student questions and community-building. She is very approachable and kind.

Class is super interesting. Raissa is really funny and great at making the classroom a comfortable space for everyone. She can go on tangents but they somehow always relate back to our learning. If you pay attention and submit the work on time, it's pretty easy to do really well (> 3.5 as a grade) in this specific class.

She's a pretty nice teacher, very enthusiastic about the class, and her expectations are pretty clear. Most lectures have PowerPoints and they are usually posted after class. Essays aren't that hard. Some readings are LONG AF but if you skim for main arguments and themes, you'll be fine. She's really helpful in office hours if you need anything.

She is a little quirky but she really wants you to learn and have fun with it. She never gets mad, is excited about teaching, and loves student discussions. She is generally a pretty laid-back and kind teacher and a fair grader because of how she values effort. The class is really straightforward.

Even if you're not interested in literature or writing in the slightest, the class is awesome. Raissa is engaging, funny, and truly passionate about what she's teaching. There are really only 3 assignments: 2 essays that analyze readings, and a final group project. Most of the class is reading books/articles, watching films, and discussing.

Raissa is a good teacher. She's kind, really laid back, writes a lot on her lecture slides and whiteboard, and gives good feedback on assignments, especially essays. One thing I would say is that she isn't always the fastest at grading or responding to emails, but she was awesome nonetheless.

This class has a writing credit, so you have to write, but it's honestly too much writing for your own good. The reading material (books, articles, etc.) is very interesting, and not too hard to comprehend, but it's a pain to write essays about them every 2 weeks. Why can't it just be like high school where you write one essay at the end?

Raissa is awesome. I had her for two classes now. She gives great lectures and really understands her students. The material presented in his lectures really changed my perspective about race and diversity. She's very caring and honestly hilarious. Really doesn't go hardball on students, compared to other professors. I'd take a third with her.

Awful at grading on time. Final grades are due today, still no clue what I'm getting in the class. Doesn't respond to emails. I feel betrayed. Should be a relatively easy class but if you need an A, prepare to be stressed and clueless about your progress in the class. You won't know your grade all quarter and won't be able to talk to her about it.

I greatly enjoyed the Postcolonial Literature class. 2 essays that aren't graded harshly, and she leaves comments on the document regarding strengths and potential improvement aside from Canvas feedback. She really knows the material and teaches the class well, but is really funny and also accommodating. Also very helpful during office hours.

Interesting class. Raissa really did a great job at generating active class discussions and provided very useful examples to clarify some of the concepts. I'd take another class with her (and I'm signed up for one next winter).

Raissa is such a caring professor and puts her students first, so grades aren't the most important thing in this class. As long as you show up, participate, and do the work, you'll get an A. Although Raissa is a little unorganized, we all have things going on that she forgives and understands, so I don't mind her messing up here and there. Love her

Raissa is such a passionate professor and has a different teaching style than traditional instructors I've had in the past. Raissa encourages us to explore our creativity and do a lot of self reflection. SEAPF was a great way for me to connect with my culture in a way that I've never been able to do before and I recommend everyone take this course!

Prof. Desmet is a great instructor. She knows her stuff and is a very sincere and caring instructor. Her constant smiling and willingness to be goofy with us makes participation easier. Her course has a reasonable amount of reading for a upper division humanities class and she handles difficult topics in a very engaging and interesting way.

Patty is by far one of the best professors I've had thus far. This was a completely new subject to me and a class outside of my major, but she made things easy to follow and helped me to understand what was going on. Lectures were lots of fun and she cares so much.

Nice teacher. Very laid-back yet enthusiastic about the material. Has lots of internet issues which made remote learning kind of a pain but she was still accommodating, and after quarters of just exams, the projects are much better ways to measure students' knowledge. Perfect for STEM majors trying to get a VLPA credit like me.

Dr. Desmet is so great!! She is extremely caring and compassionate. Very easy to talk to so if you get behind just make an appointment to meet with her and talk about it. She also sets excellent examples for accountability when receiving constructive criticism from students. There are a lot of readings but most of them are very interesting.

Professor DeSmet definitely has a quirkier, and sometimes distracted, style of teaching but she also cares so much about students and how they are doing in her class. Lectures are easy to pay attention to and I always learn a lot (when her internet is working properly). Grading scale is odd but it's easy to work around it and still get an A.

Super passionate about this class. Reaches out to all her students and encourages many ideas even from the quieter people. She sets the classroom up to be a fun, understanding, and respectful space and makes everyone feel comfortable.

I think she is a great teacher. She is very funny, which makes her classes enjoyable. Also, she mixes class time well with discussions, interactive activities, group work, etc. Not very clear about grading but this can be to your advantage because it allows you to complete assignments without having to stress out much because it's easy to get an A.

Raissa is nice but maddeningly unclear. She talks a lot and doesn't seem to care too much about making sense, as she overcomplicates everything. But she means it when she says "the only way you can fail is if you don't try." Definitely an easy A, but the class has horribly frustrating instruction.

She was alright as a teacher. Decent activities on Zoom, but the asynchronous component got lost often. You could really not show up to class and follow the instructions to the essays given and still pass with a B. Also she is a very easy grader and very nice person. Class is interesting. Meh experience though.

Her enthusiasm during lectures is great. Were it not for her ardent, and sometimes ribald, love for literature, art, history, and anything else talked about, I don't think I could've made it through this 8:30 AM class. Also hilarious and a very easy grader. I can tell she cares a lot about students too.

Can't recommend. Class structure is too disorganized. Assignment descriptions and assignment due dates constantly changed. Knows the material and teaches the class well when she does teach, but lectures and assignments are TOO LONG. She is super nice though and will basically give you an A for just showing up. Unprofessional humor though.

This has been one of my least favorite professors at UWB. Unclear expectations and useless busy work. Skips important things in Zoom lectures, videos are extremely vague too. I really struggled with her lack of clarity. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! The only good thing about it was it being a hybrid.

Few classes can be touted as life-changing, but this was definitely one of them. This woman has more knowledge and understanding in her left pinky than most other professors do in their entire bodies. Hope I can take another class with her but over Zoom this time!

PROS: Interesting class material, funny/entertaining but genuine and not in an r/fellowkids way, gives good feedback, good at explaining things, cares a lot about students. CONS: Very scatterbrained, very slow at responding to emails, can be kind of a pushover, conversations get off topic fast. I'm sure she's only like this because Zoom.

Amazing person but not well-suited for remote teaching. Late to every lecture. Class was disorganized i.e. constantly changed assignments & course structure - sometimes after students had already submitted work. Slow grader/emailer. Pros: Super flexible deadlines, interesting curriculum, fun discussions. I've heard she's much better in person!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Raissa is quite the character, to be honest. She gets REALLY enthusiastic about what she's teaching and is extremely interested and enthusiastic when making sure the students understand that. She makes lots of jokes during class and acts like a friend if you ever need it. Takes a LONG time to grade papers, but she's a fair grader.

Terrible instructor. She overcomplicates simple things and is ineffective at communicating them as a result. Unprofessional too, can be insensitive and is way nicer to students than she ever should be. This class should have been fully asynchronous, it was only productive for about 15 minutes. Waste of tuition money.

Love Raissa. Yes she's super chaotic, and yes she seems "dumb" at first because of that, but she really knows a lot and expresses it in her own weird way. She has a lot of energy and joy. She loves teaching on Zoom now, especially because she never tried to learn stuff beforehand so she's experimenting in the moment and having the time of her life.

I took classes with her a year ago, but I have to say that Raissa is a very interesting and knowledgeable professor. And yes, she is definitely an entertainer. But it's not just her sense of humor you can appreciate - it is also her attitude and how it works in the class. She's a very kind, positive, and encouraging person, and def loves her job.

Raissa is not a very good professor in my opinion. She's overly friendly towards students and tries too hard to be "cool" which is a little awkward. The layout of this class is awful and doesn't make sense (readings aren't in any particular order, lecture topics are all over the place). Decent with feedback but very subjective grading. Easy A tho.

Raissa DeSmet is a goddess among mere mortals. She can heal your GPA with her blessing of 4.0s. She can vanquish evil with her spreading of positivity in class. She has really chaotic energy but it's also like super positive energy and it helps tbh - she's really outgoing and makes lectures fun and engaging, she's a big entertainer.

Awesome class. Raissa is very laid-back, very funny and extroverted, and tries to do various activities in class to make it more interesting. She says she sees potential in all students and really cares about them, so if you do too then the results are rewarding. I'm taking her again this fall because of the good time I'm having this summer.

I tried to like her, but she just comes off as unprofessional. She always comes late to class. She tries way too hard to befriend students. She grades everything on completion, with no feedback. She's way too open about her personal life and has made some "questionable" decisions in it. If she was a bit more competent her class would've been great.

Raissa puts in a lot of effort and really cares about her students. I really admire the fact that she engages the class through entertaining lectures that still manage to teach a lot. She's always happy to see students and she's really kind and encouraging. I'm a class of '20 student moving on to grad school, and she really made UWB a good time.

It's awesome when you find a professor who not only knows what she is talking about but is passionate about that. Like Raissa. She is such an enthusiastic, friendly, and hardworking person, there's never a dull moment with her. She truly cares about students, even if she's rather eccentric/quirky and scatterbrained. Also a very easy grader.

Great class and great professor! She is how all professors should be: enthusiastic, entertaining, and with a real zest for life! She lectures with passion, and genuinely treats students like her friends. Very reasonable with grading although I still question some of her morals. Besides that, she's hands down one of my favorite teachers ever.

Look, if she confuses/annoys you, look up the Myers-Briggs Typology Indicator (MBTI). Raissa is DEFINITELY an ESFP - very engaging, entertaining, and extroverted, which makes some students love her and others not love her so much. I personally enjoyed her class because she keeps lectures interesting and her class materials are always fascinating.
She called me a nerd when I told her I use Linux on my laptop, 10/10 would take again. Took 3 classes with her, she's amazing, please take.

Raissa may come on WAY too strong at first, but it's out of passion. She cares so much about her subject and her students, and she always finds ways to make the class relevant and entertaining. There's a fairly easy workload but you still learn so much. If you turn in all the work on time, you'll get an A easily. Definitely recommend.

She is SUPER passionate about teaching and students gaining insight into whats going on in the world around them, and she's also really caring, energetic, and humorous. Take advantage of her office hours too!

These reviews are all highly inaccurate. She's obnoxious and doesn't give good feedback or reward hard work at all. She tries WAY too hard to be all buddy-buddy with her students but a lot of them laugh at her and insult her behind her back. If she were even a bit more competent and professional, I'd like her more.

CAN. WE. TALK. ABOUT. THIS. QUEEN and how AMAZING she is!? She has a lot of energy and makes you want to go to class. She also supports her lectures a lot of videos and culturally relevant things to keep material engaging. She's really kindhearted too.

Honestly, she's awesome. Be aware that your grade will be greatly, greatly affected by attendance and participation. It seems she really values your effort, and you will be getting back what you put in. If you're used to more "traditional" grading criteria and technique that you can easily follow on canvas, probably steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor! Very kind, supportive, and helpful, and encourages students to try their best. Genuinely treats students like her friends and makes them accepted and comfortable

I loved this class and everything about it. I'm so sad that it's almost over because not only did I learn a lot but I met a professor who genuinely cares for students and has a lot of enthusiasm. Raissa is amazing and I 100% DO NOT regret this class.
Get ready to laugh during lectures, participate A LOT, and have way too many high fives. That is all.

One of my favorite classes that I've taken. Lectures and discussions are extremely engaging thanks to her energy and you can tell she's really dedicated to making students do the best they can. I wish she taught more classes for my major (GWSS).

AMAZING professor! Very kind, supportive, and helpful, and encourages students to try their best. Genuinely treats students like her friends and makes them accepted and comfortable. I've taken two of her classes (339 and 372) and love everything about her.

Love her. I've taken 2 of her classes (BIS 339 and BISCLA 372) at UWB. She really knows her stuff, for sure, and is very excited to teach it. She has lots of energy and is kind of all-over-the-place, which may not be the best teaching style for some people but she's aware of that and works to create a great environment in class.

By far one of the best professors I've ever had at UWB, and would definitely take again. She is so humorous, supportive, caring and helpful. She only wishes the best for all of her students. Prepare to laugh a lot (especially the way she talks about Latin names) but also to learn a lot.

She is compassionate and understanding. She will ask you to work hard but isn't unrealistic. Fair grader, but not a super easy one. She gives you great feedback. Attendance is highly encouraged and participation is extremely important in her class. She's a very funny lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I cant say enough good things about Raissa, she is such an amazing person and professor. More than anything she CARES, if youre transparent with her she will always help you. Her lectures were always thought provoking and Ive learned so much about myself and others through this course, couldnt be happier and more fulfilled.

Raissa has become one of my favorite profs. She is great at engaging people in class to get into discussions, and she gave me valuable feedback on my work. She cares about students success and is also very funny. I found the assignments and workload reasonable, and she is receptive to feedback.
it's a capstone guys... and IAS capstones especially are just compiling work and summarizing yourself. You'll do fine in most of these capstones no matter what.

Raissa is such a fun person to be around. She is knowledgeable about course content and cares about student learning. Makes assignments simple and straightforward. This was a CBLR course in the summer with students gaining practical experience with LETI, a nonprofit organization. Her lectures aim to apply class learning to the working world.

Caring professor that takes great concern for your learning. She is willing to help with any difficult you may be facing whether that is related to class or not. Cares for her students and is well respected. Makes learning fun and challenges critical thinking!

She is super kind, caring, and a wonderful person. The class I had with her was really disorganized, but that was because we were figuring things out as a class. There weren't many assignments and not a lot of work in general, mostly the final project. I might not take her "diaspora" class again, but I wouldn't hesitate to take her other classes!

She is one of the better professors that I have had, she is extremely passionate and kind. If you are trying your best and doing all of the assignments you will get a great grade. I would take her again, she takes her time to explain the readings which can be complex. Learned a lot from her and she was very inspirational!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She was an excellent professor, she really cared about people in the class and tried to get everyone participating in class dialog. She is extremely passionate and will help you with essays if need be. This course had a lot of readings but if you attempted to get an understanding from it then you'll do great! The focus of the class is learn a lot.

Definitely one of the nicest professors I've experienced, in terms of patience, understanding and friendliness. She wants students to "create their own knowledge" and share it with the class, which means that there are presentations involved. But they're not too stressful, since they're short, graded easily, and given really encouraging feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: She has helped me understand how Culture and identity lies within performance of Diaspora. She's a great professor meeting student needs when addressed in class and she gives extra credit for sharing a piece of music based on Diaspora.  I'd recommend her as a professor who is flexible and cares for students needs to make it fun and educational.

Pretty easy teacher. I skipped a bunch of class(which is strange cause in her syllabus she's serious about attendence) and never prepared and put minimal effort into this class and still managed to receive a 3.6. I don't understand the people whining, you have to be the biggest slacker in the world to do poorly in her class.

Don't like her. One of the worst professor I have ever had, she would give you poor grade without telling you why, and the way she grade is inconceivable. I don't usually say bad things about my professors, and this is the first review i' ve written, she deserves it though.

If every teacher was like Raissa, there'd never be a complaint about college, ever. She is a genuine and understanding professor. Her feedback is incredible and timely. The readings can get difficult, but she ALWAYS breaks them down and reviews them in class to ensure understanding for the students. I plan on taking two more courses with her.
Raissa is a great teacher and her lectures are interesting and she keeps the class engaged. There's a lot of reading but not a ton of homework. I would definitely recommend her.

She is NICE, kind, amazing professor. She is easy grader, and explains clearly the reading content. She is super helpful when you are asking question. She responds email quickly.  There is no test, only 4 short writing assignments, which are a piece of cake. I recommend to take the class with her. You will enjoy. I am 100% sure!

LOVE HER. Take her, very spiritual, helping teacher who wants you to succeed and will do whatever she can to help you with that. No hard work, readings you don't need to do in order to pass the class, and a fair grader. I love her enthusiasm for the class. If you want a good grade, TAKE HER.

Amazing professor. She is sos sweet & always there for each and every student. Gives a ton of reading, but are very interesting reads. If you are a shy student and don't like to talk much, she won't force you to speak up in from of everyone. Just make sure you connect with her outside of class time (like office hours) to show her you enjoy her.
She is a great lecturer and uses a variety of resources, (articles, movies, photos, books)  There is a ton of reading!  She is helpful though.  I would take her class again.

Raissa is awesome, very sweet. She understands this may be the last quarter and is very helpful. Her feedback was great. It's a standard capstone class, but I'm glad I took it with her. Not sure if attendance is mandatory, I was there for most classes. No textbook required. Be prepared to think about all the papers and projects you've ever done.

One of my favorite professors that I have had at University of Washington Bothell. She's really engaging with the students and has a great sense of humor that I think a lot of people are able to connect with. She's clear, and very interested in the topics that she professes.  I would take another one of her classes in a heartbeat.
Raissa is sweet and fair. I don't know what yall are complaining about. She assigns long reading, but just read the intro and conclusion and you're good to go.

Professor DeSmet is extremely passionate about her work. She creates a comfortable, engaging class environment. She gives clear expectations prior to exams & papers.  Her lectures are always interesting & compelling. And she includes a variety of activities, field trips, film viewings, etc. throughout the term. I highly recommend her classes!

She's a nice professor but was rather unorganized. She messed up on a few of the readings on the syllabus which was rather frustrating because she'd sometimes post the changes in readings rather last minute. She also doesn't give you an actual grade till the end of the quarter so you don't really know what you're going to get.

As a person she's very kind and all round respectable. As for her teaching, she lacks the ability to give clear instructions, very unorganized. She was even behind with the material we were suppose to do on the day of class. Worst of all you don't know what your grade it until the end of the quarter.
