reviews.comment: Like his course

This course has been an eye opening experience. Professor Doogar might be one of the smartest individuals I have encountered in my life. If you want to learn and expand your thinking beyond the norm, take his course. This course has helped tremendously in my confidence as a professional accountant, and I will always be grateful for our Professor.
Professor Doogar kept the class pace manageable and provided feedback to ensure we learned the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is an excellent professor and works to make the learning experience fresh and exciting. The class environment was positive and design to help student reach their full potential.

Rajib is one of the best professors. He helps students to develop oneself professionally. He also connects students with different professionals. It helps in networking and improves oneself professionally. His unique way of teaching and connecting with students help in learning in a friendly environment. He is a great mentor.
Rajib is a excellent professor. He goes out of the way to make student understand. He always inspires amd cares a lot about the success of his student. I recommend taking his class.

Rajib is a great professor at UW Bothell, he is enthusiastic about financial statement analysis. As long as you understand the fundamental concepts of the financial statement, then you'll perform very well in his class. The group exercises were a good opportunity to practice and apply your accounting skills to real-world F/S. Overall, He's great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I have never seen a professor who will work with student side by side at 2 a.m. in the morning, he is one of the most diligent, intelligent, and passion-driven person in this university. Ive worked with professor Doogar though every single quarter while I was in the program, and I've never seen any professor work as hard as professor Doogar.

Very nice and wise guy. I took his four classes. One of the best professors I have ever had at UWB. You have to work hard and learn independently to pass his classes. Don't worry about the GPA, he's a fair grader. Just ask him any questions you have, you will get some great feedback. He always willing to help and want his students to be succeeded!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: His class is only for people who are ready to grow professionally. Don't take his class if you were kids and had almost no responsibility.

Doesn't know how to use Canvas to save his life.. He literally codes hyperlinks into the pages instead of using the built in systems. Pages are non-accessible except through his hyperlinks, and he stores an arbitrary amount of the course files behind similarly hidden, but also broken links. He later bragged about doing this.

He is a master charlatan. I don't even know why the dean keeps him in the business school. He is condescending and literally hates students. I know because he told that he hates students in class. It is beyond me why he works at a job he hates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the worst teachers in UW. His lectures are not very clear or very organized. The wording on his homework/exams/instructions can be confusing. Plus, he is not timely in answering emails or in grading. This leaves students very confused.

Smart guy with tons of knowledge. Unfortunately he doesn't have the ability to teach in a clear and concise way. Talks too much gets off the topic constantly and gets offended by criticism. Very disorganized and cannot give students a clear idea of what students are expected to see throughout the quarter. Students stay confused and frustrated.

For those taking Cost Accounting, TAKE IT ONLINE AT CENTRAL WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY! He has this horrible philosophical approach to accounting. Definitely need to avoid him. The entire course was a work in progress, as he did not know how to proceed with his own b.s. He publicizes student emails, and cannot be trusted.

Arrogant and incompetent.  Worst possible combination.  I didn't learn anything about cost accounting.  Of course he also blamed us for complaining about his lack of teaching skill/effort.  Any other professor would try to make corrections. He clearly doesn't care about students.   Please UWB, don't hire any more faculty members like him.

Worst teacher I've ever had. Said there was no book required, then proceeded to refer to the book throughout class. Only learned anything because I did actually buy the book and read it. Posted grades for the final 65% of our grade almost 1 month after grades were due. DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES FROM THIS TEACHER. YOU WILL REGRET IT I PROMISE YOU.

Some people in life want everything handed to them or at least directions to how to do what is asked of them. If you want a real world wake up call of what it is like to work for a company for the first time &  experience what it is like to not have all those privileges then take any class with Rajib. Insanely smart, knowledgeable & ambitious.

From Day 1 the class was very UNORGANIZED.  His Exams were not fair to any of the students.  He was very helpful and very passionate about the Subject, but just did not know how to channel that knowledge to students.  Very lenient in his grading, but the frustration of taking his class was very overwhelming.  Please don't take him.

Undoubtedly the worst instructor of my academic career.It is not even close. Doogar is a terrible communicator who belittles his students with regularity. The reputation of the accounting department and the school as a whole are in jeopardy with Doogar involved. At this point, I would deter anyone considering UWB business school from applying.

This teacher is by far one of the worse I have ever taken. He doesn't really teach the material but uses vague abstract thought to explain it. Examples like a giraffe and a elephant mating... Really weird stuff that doesn't help you at all. Beware of what you say, he might call you dumb in the middle of class.

He teaches little & destroys your GPA. He has never worked as an accountant & doesn’t have an ACCT degree, & it shows. His projects are overwhelmingly long, complex & incomprehensible. Students are putting so much time into this class that their grades are suffering in other classes. He publicly posts private student emails which violates FERPA.

It sounds like I am taking this class online but with more confusion based on his lectures. I have not learned anything in this class and now spending my time on two gigantic capstone projects for his class at the end of the quarter and my most concern is how I am going to pass the CPA exam since I have not learned anything in this class.

Honestly she isn't that bad. She gets a lot of hate but I had her for 350 and 370 and they were both very easy classes. I would argue that the classes themselves are boring and poorly structured, and she is doing her best with teaching the material. The assignments and quizzes are relatively easy and tests are a reflection of the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Dutta curates 350 around Amazon; heavy emphasis on rapid fire group activities/presentations. Encourages students to really think and understand how organizations work. She is a bit disorganized; unclear/late grading and unclear deadlines. My group would often find ourselves needing to crunch complex analyses with under a week's notice.

She grades everything late. Week 8/10 and only week 1-2 stuff is graded. Heavy with group work so choose them wisely. Quizzes require you to make up things as you go. One textbook is an ok read while the other is tiny words with large paragraphs for pages. Not the most intellectually stimulating class. After class help is rare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Every day this professor would come late TO HER OWN CLASS. Then, when she FINALLY decided to show up, she would read off a power point FOR AN HOUR AND THIRTY MINUTES about content we had to read before class. The assignments and tests only really test your ability to make up BS. Very detailed BS. If you don't want to waste your TIME and MONEY, RUN!

Quizzes are heavy writing & inadequate time. Arbitrary grading. PowerPoint reader. PowerPoint are summaries of the reading. Groups are meant to simulate workplace groups. She will not let you switch teams. Does not answer emails quickly. A creative writing class, project is an imaginary engineering project.

She is a very kind and caring teacher, I took her for BUS 330.
While the grading and expectations are very confusing she is polite with her grades and cares that you do the work.
Videos in class and a group project to end it all.
Overall a easy but at times confusing professor.
If you show up, even half the time, you'll do well.

Be careful who you choose your group project with. I would have obtained a higher grade if I had chosen better classmates. Class is straightforward, weekly open-ended questions, one big group project.
Prof Keskinbicak is one of the best teachers who I met at University of Washington. Her lectures are up-to-date and very relevant to today's work. He cares her students' success so much.

Prof Duygu is extremely sweet and caring. She respects students a lot, whatever we suggested, she does take it into consideration. Tests are easy, we worked in groups but it was easy assignments. She invited a guest speaker into our class once and it was very cool. Definitely would take her class again.

She has been the worst I have taken in my last 4 years at this University. She is rude, and gets irritated with students very easily when asked questions. She is extremely unclear about her instructions and expectations on assignments and the group project. She doesn't know how to use Canvas so grades are not calculated until the end of the quarter
Sri was incredibly rude and was mean at times during class. She never knew how to answer questions and her assignments were super unclear. If you can avoid taking her I would recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's nice and not strict about grading. Her quizzes and tests are also not hard to handle as long as you pay attention in class and take notes from her slides. Decent professor!

I which I could pass this class, but it's seems like impossible. She only talks SPSS, which is useless for us. I hope UW Bothell gives us more teachers to choose. I won't take her class again for sure.

Duvurri is a nice person, but the lectures have been almost entirely about how to use SPSS or basic Marketing Terminology. The exams and hw, however, are much more difficult and are not covered in the lectures. Class scores: Quiz 1: Avg 6.2/10 max 8 HW1: Avg 42.3/60 max 59.5 Exam1: Avgf 77.5%, max 91 (HW2 and Exam2 TBD)

Absolutely leaves you in the dark as far as expectations. Really no assistance in class and cryptic beyond belief. Grading is horrible with no aim and no feedback. This was a core class for the MBA and it was horrible. Should never teach a class again, graduate or undergraduate.

She is such a good prof. Third quarter with her so far. Gives great feedback, and very accesible outside of class. Makes sure she gives you the tools to suceed. As long as you try you should get an A. You can tell that she cares about the material she teaches.

This professor made writing very easy. She broke down the process and walked us through it with weekly lectures. She responds quickly to emails and is willing to accommodate students who have trouble. She gives great feedback! Would def take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I adore Shari. I took her 201 and am in her 300 class right now. Lots of writing in both, but if you stay on top of it you'll do great. Lenient on deadlines and lots of amazing feedback while still being a kind grader. She's very knowledgeable and I can't wait to take another class of hers.

Absolutely love Shari. She is super flexible with deadlines and provides amazing feedback. Lots of homework but it's totally doable. She is also very quick to respond if you need any help and she truly cares about what she teaches.
way too many assignments
Nice professor but lectures don't seem to apply to an intro class. Too many assignments but they are manageable, and kinda boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but class was kinda boring. A lot more writing than I expected from a intro to pubhealth class. She grades very easy and is very lenient on deadlines--often pushing them back to give us more time. Wants to contour the class exactly how students want (hybrid, etc). I'm sure she could be more interesting if the topic was less broad.

I don't recommend; boring class, nothing much to learn, and too much writing for a social science elective. I chose this class because I'm hoping to contribute to biological research and wanted to know some aspects of public health along with the ethics behind research. I ended up doing other assignments during class time to make use of my time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not a difficult class but I didnt learn anything valuable in this class. Considering the other reviews I was hopeful that I would gain knowledge that pertained to my field. So if you wish to gain an easy credit, this is the class to take. If you want to feel like you are gaining something from your education, this is not the class for you
Not clear, lectures were set up poorly, not accessible to different learning styles

I've had Dr. E-T for a few classes now, and each one was as amazing as the other. In every class, she's shown that she cares about the material and cares about her students' success. If you show her you're trying and are putting in the work, you'll get the grade you want. She believes in a lot of little assignments vs a few big assignments.
Super easy but also extremely informative. Do your work and you will receive credit.
Prof. Eagen-Torkko was such a great teacher! I loved her and her class. Has quizzes, readings, and homework every week but manageable. 10/10, would recommend.
I learned a lot. Easy going, but provides information in an easy to understand manner. Always available to help outside of class too. Clearly cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super easy class. He was really nice and you could tell he was passionate about the material. Very little work needed to pass. No exams, 1 group presentation (video), and a bunch of discussion boards. You have to meet with him once every three weeks for 5 minutes and that's it!

[BCORE107]
Things to Expect:
-Small weekly in-class activities
-Small weekly journal entry analysis pieces on readings
-Heavy readings, but are mainly to keep busy
-Final group project lasts most of the quarter
-In-class lectures
-An open-ended Individual presentation assignment 

(Chill and funny professor. Unnecessary busy work. Rating: 3.85)

Professor Marc is a really kind and understanding person. His lectures are also engaging and full of interesting information. The reason he's not 5 stars is because the class work is the epitome of mind-numbing "busy work" but if you just grind out the work then you should get a good grade.

if you are a new student looking for a bcore class this class and this teacher is the one trust me ! he is the sweetest and is very understanding on how you may have other classes and other stress so hes super easy on you. take this class !!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really good teacher for BCORE last year. Hopefully he teaches it again so freshmen can have him! He answers emails frequently and really knows what he is talking about in lectures, and is really helpful with all student questions. I'm taking him again for cybersecurity this spring.

He was a good teacher committed to make sure that everyone understands the material. Open to questions at any point, and always answered clearly. The slideshows were a HUGE help, and as long as you can take good notes on what he talked about in class, you're set up for the homework and exams.

The materials were very interesting. You'd watch videos and practice hacking for some assignments. That was more fun compared to reading books. His exams were a nightmare. They included multiple choices, matching, open questions. You cannot find most of them on gg and you won't have enough time to search all. the average was around 80.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was a hybrid class and might as well be an asynchronous online class. Out of the 2 hours that we meet every week, one hour goes to presentations while the other hour is spent on cybersecurity topics. Midterm and final are difficult. The weekly quizzes and 3 assignments are fairly straightforward. You will need to rely a lot on the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dupuis does a great job of connecting the work of the syllabus to the real world. He is understanding of circumstance and will work with you as long as you communicate clearly.
Nice teacher with good feedback on assignments. he is accessible outside of class for asking any question.

Lectures are always fun and informative, but sometimes goes very off topic for most of the lecture. Content is very applicable to keeping yourself safe online and I learned a lot about useful tools I could use either for free or cheap. All readings/videos are posted on Canvas, and are a bit long but cover all relevant material needed.

This past winter was really bad though with the snow. School was closed several times. Two Monday classes were cancelled, which was a lot since we only met on Mondays with 2 holidays already. Unlike other profs, he did live lectures that he recorded for the class. Great lectures and assignments were fun. Just wish we had more class. Funny too.

Wanted to take a cybersecurity course and add some to my CS coursework. Wasn't sure how it would go. I liked the variety of assignments Prof. Marc gave us. It made it so it didn't get tedious. Stretched my thinking in different ways. Easy to talk with, both inside and outside of class. I had a lot of questions, but he never minded.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Dupuis knows what he's doing and is there for his students. His exams are a little lengthy, but the class itself is enjoyable and I felt like I learned a lot. Each week has a fairly simple lab that can honestly be done in a few hours, but don't really help for the midterm/final. Would recommend, but be wary of studying for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Didn't know much about cyber security before. Learned how to keep myself safer as a result of the class. Backing up my files and using a password manager still. There is hope for me!

Took 310 with Dr. Marc based on what I had heard from my friends. Lots of work, but also learned a lot about cybersecurity in the process. Didn't realize there was so much to know and didn't seem to even scratch the surface. Marc is easygoing and always made time for me outside of class. Taught as a hybrid too, which was nice.
Fun class and learned a lot. Difficult at times, but feel like I can keep my self safer online now and have already helped my mom some. Did better than I expected too.

He made class fun with lots of in-class activities. His use of real world examples was helpful. He really cares about everyone succeeding and tried his best to keep our stress levels low. He always told us what to study for quizzes and the final. The project was tedious (as it is for 370 with any prof) and he doesn't let you pick your groups.

took other intro programming classes before, but had a hard time with them. profs would make mistakes writing code and this easily confused me. shouldn't have, but did. yes, dr. dupuis used slides, but he made sure the code was correct before class. he stepped through it with the slides to show the progression. passed and finally get it.

Worst class I took during my entire degree. Uses online learning labs that don't involve any learning; they just waste time. He doesn't teach during class, just runs through the slides and cracks jokes. Do yourself a favor and get a good book on cyber security and work through it -- you'll learn more in just a few hours a self study a week.

This was a tough weed out class and by the end I was happy to have gotten a passing grade. He literally took the curriculum from other professors and modified to  his needs. Probably doesn't help that this was a 8pm to 10pm class section. Lots of reading and lots of quizzes. Tests (2-3) will make or break your grade. Literally presented off slides.
Lots of work, but very interesting topics covered in Secure Systems. Easy to talk to outside of class. Pretty easy going as well. Even helped me with my resume.

161 is an intro programming class. It was clear Dupuis put a lot of effort into teaching it. It was difficult for students that didn't work hard and didn't do the exercises he provided or use the practice exams he gave. For those of us that took advantage of them we did well. The exams were difficult, but fair.
She amazes me every class. I hope I can be half the teacher she is. She constantly puts the students first and practices what she teaches. Her enthusiasm is infectious!
She is a deeply passionate and caring professor. She inspired me personally. I would take another class from her in  a heartbeat!

I really enjoyed learning from this professor.  She was kind, caring and very informative.  Her many years in the field of education and being a parent herself really made her an expert in this class.  If I see her name again as a professor, I will gladly take another class from her.

Jean is so sweet! There is a bit of reading that goes with the class I took, but you could get away with not reading. You just won't get as much out of the class. Participation was part of the grade, so it wouldn't be good to skip a ton of classes, but she was enjoyable to be around and easy to learn from.

The biggest problem I had with this class was that his lectures were quite boring most of the time because nothing important was being taught in each class. I would recommend taking this teacher if you want an easy class, but not if you want to improve your writing ability. He has one main essay near the end of class that is quite time-consuming.

He cancels class so often and never follows the syllabus. This is a writing class but he never provides any feedback whatsoever or provides assignments that will strengthen our writting. The in class lectures feel so pointless and unrelated and the assignments feel pointless as well. Waste of credits. take a different teacher.

I really enjoyed my time in professor Reynoso's class! He is relatively lenient when it comes to late assignments although it is highly recommended to turn everything you possibly can in on time. He expects you to participate in class, but the workload I had was very manageable. He understands his classes often times aren't a priority but required.

Reynoso gave out little homework assignments. Weird grading system but assignments were easy. Takes forever to grade assignments but gives full credit as long as you do the work. I recommend taking this professor for a laid-back class and doing little to nothing. However, if you want to learn, I advise taking a different professor.

Also known as Ricky Reynoso. Rs are rolled. The pacing and the organization leave a bit to be desired. You may spend most of the quarter doing next to nothing. Then, you'll write a 2,968-word paper during finals week. However, I found taking notes while performing research helpful, and the overall workload is light.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best writing teacher I've ever taken. Charismatic and kind. Lectures are straight to the point and often finish early. Zero problems with workload and ended with an A+!
Lectures are a bit confusing, however, the book is completely useless.

When I found out she was the dean I thought she would be really strict, but she's actually really nice. Tests are pretty fair; fewer hw problems later in the quarter; the only annoying thing was the ethics paper, but even that was only 1000 words.

She's really nice, and if you ask her a question she'll help you out a lot. But her initial lectures are useless. Thermo can't really be taught using powerpoints. I ended up teaching myself since the book is crap. We ended up doing hw problem in class, which is nice, because she helped with solving them. Tests are easy.

PLEASE go to office hours. Labs are lowkey hard but go to office hours and she'll take you through the lab step by step. Helps and makes sure that you know what's exactly required to get full points on labs. No zoom meetings, just a vid each week. Always communicate if you need an extension or something- she's super kind and willing to help.

Great lab professor. Really helped me out during office hours by giving me feedback on my lab reports. Just ask her what you want to improve on and she will help. The chem lab sections are very difficult but she makes them much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Tyson for BCHEM 364 and 365 and she is amazing, she really cares to make sure that you are learning the content. If you study the lecture notes and her homework problems then you are golden for the exam. She refers to the textbook but you don't need it at all to study she does a really good job in covering the content in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Tyson for Biochem 1, and I am typically a pretty good student but I barely passed her class. Her lectures are clear and concise but the test questioins are HARD and specific. She curves the average of her class to a 2.7, so I wound up taking biochem 1 again the next quarter with a different proffessor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Tyson is a nice person, but her exams are really hard. Especially after classes got moved online during the Coronavirus pandemic. The final was completely different from what were used to. If theres another professor teaching dont take Tyson, but if shes your only choice go for it.

Prof Tyson is THE BEST at teaching Ochem. She will meet you outside of class and answer any questions because she wants you to understand and progress. Her quizzes and tests are easy if you know the material. I definitely recommend taking her and would definitely love to have her teach all the Ochem courses if given the option.

Dr. Tyson is one of THE BEST chemistry teachers I've had. She makes OCHEM so easy to understand. Her lectures are amazing and HW problems are very useful. She is a very kind and caring person. She agreed to stay after 4-hour lab (outside of her normal office hours)to explain some problems to me that I didn't get. I highly recommend her classes
The best professor i've had so far. She's so helpful and her lectures are so interesting. She grades fairly and is willing to do whatever it takes to help. Will take any class she teaches.
A great class by a professor who really knows her stuff and cares about her students.
What an amazing professor!  Very approachable, demands you call her by her first name!  Always willing to talk to students outside of class, great lectures, one of the best professors at UW-Bothell!

Dr. Thomas is a very high caliber Professor.  She knows what she is talking about, and isn't pompous at all.  She is very accessible, and had an observable interest in what she teaches.  I would recommend showing up and making yourself known to her.  Engage in her classes and you will not only learn a lot but be rewarded with a fair grade.

This profesaor is one of the best at UWB.  She covers a lot of ground but makes sure that everyone is with her and has a nujmber of assignments that help  you to know where you stand.  I would highly recommend taking a course with her if you are interested in psych issues.
I found that she often was not able to talk about material for class. She was always in a rush.

Elizabeth is a great professor!  She's absolutely clear in explaining the concepts you need to know, and she's very caring about her students learning.  Psychology students are very lucky to have her!

What a great prof!  Great energy, passion, terrific organization and she is teaching a very important topic.  This is a "core" course for the degree so its great to have a mandatory course be so effective.
The course was eye opening to a new way of looking at policies and programs. Dr. Thomas has such a wealth of knowledge. I learned a lot in this class.

This was a great course to take whether you are fulfilling the community Psychology prerequiste or in business. I would highly recommend this professor to any other student. The class was very interactive with one another and I learned alot from Dr. Thomas!

Elizabeth is a very helpful and interesting professor.  I appreciated her clarity and enthusiasm.  She was able to communicate some fairly complex material to the class.  I don't know anyone who was unhappy with her teaching or the course.

One of my very favorite professors here.  She goes the extra mile, is extremely helpful, and very clear about expectations on assignments.  Some of the material is challenging as are some assignments, but she works with you to understand what you need to do and end up learning a lot.

Elizabeth is an outstanding professor! She is enthusiastic and uses a variety of teaching methods to present course material (lecture, videos, pp presentations, small groups, etc.). She welcomes and responds to student feedback.
Elizabeth is a strong teacher who often seems willing to help students to better understand concepts. lectures can sometimes get a little boring, but I would definetly reccomend her.
A lot of work that can be confusing on what he actually wants. Grades hard. Provides feedback. Will never take this professor.

Stan is a great teacher. Very lecture heavy but his lectures are very interesting and informative. Has great credibility. He gave lots of extra credit assignments and it was group project heavy but if you do the work you will get an A.
Expect to have many group projects but he is a fair grader if you work for it. He is very knowledgeable in the business field. I've learned a lot from him.

Has you work in your group very frequently, assigns a lot of reading and isn't afraid to call people out from the roster if there isn't enough participation going on. Did provide my class with an extra credit opportunity! Really responsive via email and open to clarifying questions that you may have. Make sure you go to his class and DO THE READING
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's the most savage professor I've had and he does not sugar coat things for you. He's very straight up and his expectations are clear.   To succeed in his class, you are going to need to participate and to receive a good grade, you will need to study outside of class. Previewing the chapter is always so helpful and never been so true until this!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's definitely one of the kindest, most knowledgeable professors I've met. He answers all your questions and really cares about whether you understood or not. And what he does tell you isn't fluff, he really knows his stuff about the real business world, and business law as a whole. You'll learn a lot from him.

The book is amazing, really learned a lot. Mr Emert is very smart and has lots of experience in the business world, no doubt about that. I think his biggest problem is that he doesn't really care about his students' success. He expects a LOT from us and he is vague and a really tough grader. Lots of presentations and research.

Overall a good professor, a bit vague but not too bad. He's a really understanding guy if you reach out to him. I was really sick for a while and was able to retake some quizzes because I asked. If you take him for bbus 230 you need to show up to class to get participation points, and the book is your best friend since quizzes are open book/note
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Stan is a very good professor. He had a lot of people from his business network come speak during of class to do Q&As. He really makes you think to explore all areas of business. Would recommend him over any professor in the business department at UWB.

If you want an easy class this is your guy. He was very vague but, the book was interesting. The group presentations are not much because you can work on them in class, he does not care about laptops. I would recommend, because his exams can be answered by reading the book and looking at presentations.  Very easy mid term (95 avrg).

He knows his subject well, but he is vague when it comes to grading and feedback. The only think you learn in the class is researching a company, i dont like the presentation because the analysis is subject. It will be an analysis in our part, but be not for him because of his experience. Also, presentations are all you do in the class which is 80%
Nice person, not a good teacher. Knows his topic but pretty boring. Shows a lot of video and the video do a lot of the work for him. Vague lectures and project expectation and vague grading.
He has a lot of real world experience, which is a plus, and clearly knows and understands what he is talking about, however, he has extreamly vauge lectures, leaving much room for interpretation.
He is so passionate about this topic. He's more enthusiastic about assignments than the students are, but the class is an interesting topic and extremely easy.

Lectures are dry and quickly on in the quarter, you'll learn that there's really no point in going to class. His class was a complete joke and waste of time. He's a nice guy, but don't bother with his classes. They're easy, but you don't learn anything and they add no value to you whatsoever.

Stan is the only prof that I have had that has brought in relevant guest speakers. He has a powerful network. This class was the corner stone of my academic career. To do well: listen, read, and write well. Thanks Stan for being such an effective leader at UWB and in the business world!

Professor Esposito is amazing! He is the best professor in CS at UWB. The class is structured so well, every week you have one assignment that is part of the final group project. Then all you have is a midterm and a final. He is very knowledgeable and credible in his field, and his lectures really show this. Loved his class! take him!

Professor Esposito is such a sweet heart! I loved his class and would totally take him again. All of the homework is group work and it's incredibly easy. He's a really chill grader and just wants you to understand and pass.
I don't know if he's super boring or if the materials boring. Either way he was a nice guy. Easy class.

One of the most caring and knowledgeable professors in CSSE. As someone else mentioned he does have a speech impediment, but it doesn't interfere as much as you'd think. Incredibly sweet and thoughtful, you can really tell he wants his students to be successful. Definitely knows a thing or two about making a software diagrams.
Hes very lecture heavy and has boring lectures. Very knowledgeable and will post everything online for studying on your own. He does have a speech impediment, but hes is very kind and respectful.

Class seems almost useless. About half of the reading seems relevant, and the other half seems entirely outdated or not relevant. I don't think I learned how to manage anything, but maybe I learned how to be a better CEO of a billion dollar company? Maybe?
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took OB right as i got to UW, i was thankful the quarter was over. I was not happy to walk in to Bus300 and see Esther Hayman was my professor again. She is a very nice elder lady, but her teaching style is not the best. Most of the students in class including myself are lost more than half the time. She is also very aggressive, has strict rules.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I disliked Esther initially and was not looking forward to my 2nd class with her. But Esther has gracefully accepted feedback & designed her classes to be engaging, collaborative, and fun. She's always chosen amazing reads. She incorporates games, lectures, videos, discussion, and team building! I love class and was sad when the course was over.

She is really tough, but she is a really nice professor with great feedback and good lecture. There's a final team presentation and four exams. She cares about teamwork a lot, so you must show her how well your team participate. Overall, I think she is a helpful professor. Not an easy A, but I enjoy taking her class and work with our class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Good: If you contribute to her participation and do well in her assignments, she will be more lenient towards you. Bad: If you are not a native English speaking student, be wary. Tip: Pick a good teammate. You will be required to work with them a lot and final project requires entire team to participate well. --> Right person on the right bus.

The most work I have ever encountered for a 5 credit core class. Completely ridiculous expectations- she seems to forget we all have other classes and a major to concentrate on! Get ready to have zero time for anything else if you are taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Awful. Irrelevant content and poorly presented

Very knowledgeable; holds a PhD. Unfortunately, this class is a bore because of the topics. Most of the lectures are very boring and explain organizational theories dating back to the Ford days of Scientific Management. Really boring stuff means even more boring lectures which she tends to carry on stories forever.

Distracting and unclear lecture style. She tries to cram too many thoughts into her sentences and as a result makes them completely unclear. Her teaching is primarily based on her experience as an executive assistant at Boeing. If you want to learn all of the management buzzwords and cliches in existence as of 10 years ago take her class.

She gives participation points for who answers her questions in class every week. Quizzes are online and are multiple choice questions. No midterm and final. There is a presentation at the end of the course and it worth a lot of points. Good group members are important.

I would not take another class with Professor Hayman. She was always in a terrible mood, and was the worst lecturer I've had since high school. She gives points for speaking up once a week in class, and the quizzes are straight off the Power Point slides. Most boring class I've taken in a long time.

Very strict on participation grade, complains that we don't share our ideas enough even though her lecture is like a 2 hour run on sentence about mostly her life. She posts lecture PowerPoint's to help us study, but blanks out words because we should already have take notes. Problem is she flies through slides, but we still should "write faster".

She straight up didnt give us a rubric for our final assignment, an executive summary. It is worth 1/5 of the total grade. On other assignments she would give power points with blanked out words for study content then tell us that we should have taken quicker notes when in class she flew through lectures. WORST TEACHER YET.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Don't take her class. Lots of quizzes. She did't give enough time for us to write down what is on the power-point, and she put the power-point on Canvas with blanks. She is not organize. And never explain grading system clearly.

Everything is wrong with this class.  She tests and quizzes on content that is subjective.  e.g There was call for two "against the grain" textbooks (which are amazing). Each one held two different "Most applicable" answers for 4 questions on a test. Her response was "I was generous with everyone's participation points."   EqualityEquity? Horrible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His assignments actually challenge you to think and use the knowledge you learned which is refreshing and nice to see.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
At times he could be tough and a bit intimidating, but you can tell he was coming from a place of genuinely wanting to challenge and expand your knowledge. He was real and he owned it. He never sugar-coated anything with the class and encouraged us to find the good in things. 

My condolences to his family, def. won't forget his class.
Sucks that it wasn't until he was gone til I realized how valuable his class was, and how great of a teacher he really was. My condolences go to his family.

His class might of been a bit boring to other students, but I still found his class educational. He tried his best, and he cares for his students. 

My condolences to professor Stewart family and friends.

This professor was just not it. Lectures are LONG and BORING! He talks at you the entire time and there's little to no student engagement. His lectures basically go over the textbook readings that were assigned so there's really no need to go to class besides being there to get into a group for the project. I don't really know why I bothered going.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Stewart was really funny at first but then his true colors were revealed. He is incredibly rude and unhelpful. It feels like he doesn't care about being a teacher. He made it very clear that he didn't want to hear from us about anything other than the clas from the get go.

Lectures felt like going to Sunday sermon but his occasional quick quips made the lectures somewhat more enjoyable. He constantly acts upset for lack of engagement from students yet belittles students who do ask questions during lectures. (Would often ask rhetorical questions but expects answers). Tough grader, your work is NEVER at his standards.

His lectures take up the entire class time but he usually let's you go 20 mins early, you'll have 9 reading response and 9 quizzes BUT he will drop the 4 lowest reading responses and the 2 lowest quizzes so just skip them. He's got an attitude yeah, but if you're looking for an easy psychology class then take Dr. Stewart (he has no filter too FYI)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such boring lectures. The whole class time Prof Stewart just lectures, and half the time it doesn't make any sense. A lot of run off sentence and thoughts. Although you have to write a lot and go in-depth with your discussion post to get a good/high grade, he drops 4 discussion posts at the end of the quarter. The readings are thick and dense.

Very rude professor that would make generalized comments. Would leave harsh, passive-aggresive, and very unprofessional comments when grading assignments. Belittled students when they asked/answered questions. Made it clear he wouldn't put effort into knowing his students. Had no rubrics for the final, had spelling errors in canvas announcements.

Rude, mean and passive aggressive. Students were mocked for asking questions. Boring and redundant lectures, same content as the textbook. Lazily designed quizzes, questions were just sentences from textbook. A group research paper was 40% of the total grade and was graded extremely harshly, with a class average of 2.4/C+. I learned very little.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are very monotone and uninspiring. They are for the most part regurgitation of the essays he makes you read before class. Is a pretty graceful grader though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: tells you what you need to know and seems to enjoy the class, lots of relying on the reading tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I can absolutely see how Dr. Stewart was a clinical psychologist. Amazing lectures. Grading criteria isn't super clear, but my tips for reading responses are: Find an overarching theme to discuss, then add evidence from textbook. Don't talk about yourself too much, and write a lot (I averaged 600 words and did really well in all of them).

I really enjoyed his class this quarter. All he does is lecture during class (despite promising in-class activities), but you see he knows what he's talking about. 9 reading responses (very open ended), 4 get dropped. 9 quizzes, 2 get dropped. Is very approachable and encourages questions. If you are passionate about psychology, take this class!

Talks in a very preachy/soapbox manner and is generally hard to follow during lectures with his long and runoff answers that don't leave you feeling any more clear on whatever is being discussed Max 2 reading responses a week that he has no clear rubric for and will drop your worst 4 grades at end of quarter Easy grader but feels like waste if time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was a bit unsure about registering for his class after seeing the low rating here but turns out he is really a great professor. He might not give super clear instructions for assignments, but they're mostly about writing down your opinions on what you've learn. He's also pretty lenient with grading as long as you share your thoughts.

Professor Stewart can be very blunt at times. I found him to be hilarious, and very engaging. As long as you do the reading, you will appreciate the lectures, even if they go a bit off track. He knows psychology very well. He does curse, and can tease students occasionally, but the intent is not mean spirited. I loved having him as a professor.

He was awful to take. Assigns a group project that he hates grading, uses obscene language frequently to try be edgy. Does not give clear directions.  He also told the class on the last day of class that "If it was up to him, none of us would get psych degrees. I'm never taking him again if that means switching majors.

I didn't learn anything from attending his lecture because he was repeating the slides over and over again. Everything I learned was from either reading the textbook/assigned articles or our class Discord server (which that boomer surely isn't on). There are small mistakes on slides that make it harder to understand the material.

He looks tough, but he has a good heart. He's very expressive and straight-forwarded. I think people think he's aggressive but really it's because he judges and show his opinion (which you will desperate to see from other profs in the future). Only 1 paper for final and weekly response (which is not hard). He's very real

No helpful comment. Not helping students with their needed. Told us there is extra credit for us to earn by our participation from all the class meeting and or work, but finally not giving me any extra credits.

BEFORE YOU TAKE HIM READ THIS! Stewart is misunderstood because he often goes hard on his students. In reality, he wants you to use all of your resources as a student to GROW instead of trying the bare minimum. This was my second quarter with him and it was a far better experience. He is blunt but still SO caring and wants you to succeed, just try.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really inconsiderate & disrespectful. I really dont understand how he was a clinical psychologist. He is blunt and doesnt care about what he says wether its disrespectful. Weekly work & one research paper on cultural psychology. Trust your instincts and dont take him. As you see his rates arent great. Goodluck
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Stewart is an incredible professor. Yes, he can be intimidating and he has been known to call people out in class, but I learned more in two of his classes than the rest of my program. His lectures totally changed the way I look at psychology as a field, society and mental illness. Do the readings and participate & buckle in for a fun class.

Quite possible the worst professor in my undergrad career. Unclear on expectations and assignments, and when approached for clarification, he'll either say, "should've attended class." or "you got what you deserved." Even if you attended each class. You learn what you teach yourself, not what he teaches. If you thrive in negativity, go for it.

Dr. Stewart doesn't get a fair shake. Students aren't used to a teacher that won't unconditionally bend over backwards for them. He will not coddle you, but if you do the work he will be your biggest advocate and the payoff is huge. What he teaches can change your entire worldview. Go to office hours once even if it's just to chat, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an okay professor at best. Not very engaged in his lectures cause they're so boring and he goes off topic 85% of the time. Feedback for some of the assignments, especially the final group paper, were very dull and he wasn't clear on what he wanted. Super passive-aggressive if things don't go his way. Quizzes were a little difficult too.

While his lectures are information and to the point, his assignments are extremely poorly written. He offers little clarification to assignments, but then has a very tough grading standard. There is a huge disconnect between the textbook readings and his lectures, and the actual assignments given. He could stand to be more clear with expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Stewart was awesome! Super helpful in and outside of class- just stay on top of reading and you'll be solid in class discussions & with papers assigned. Make sure to give yourself plenty of time to brainstorm, write, and edit papers and you will be just fine! :) Prof Stewart is always accessible if you have questions about the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken. The class was so boring. Hard to stay awake. super disorganized, he does not match readings to class lectures you sit through 2 hours of him blabbing "Um, um, Um". You are only graded on 3 papers, but he doesn't provide clear criteria. He gives you the grade he wants. All I learned was from the book, stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting teacher, but if you are not a psych major, you will be judged accordingly. Grading is capricious, and feedback is mostly just yelp reviews at best. Not the worst teacher, not the best, he is plain average. But stay tuned in the lectures, never a dull moment, he averages about 3-5 people crying during class and mocks them for it!

Dr. Eric Stewart: Talented lecturer. Very knowledgeable about the subject he teaches. Articulates seemingly difficult concepts in a very eloquent way. Extraordinary and awe-inspiring. Class is well organized, readings are fascinating, uses Canvas advantageously for students.

Dr. Eric Stewart is an excellent teacher. The lecture is amazing. He is knowledgeable. Very helpful outside of class during office hour. He gives good feedback. I will love to take another class with him again. Fascinating, amazing lecture.

He seems to be a caring teacher but grades harshly. Participation and attendance are a high portion of the class. I do like that he lets you exercise a lot of creative freedom on the final. Feedback is rather helpful on essays, as far as improving your writing skills goes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He definitely knows his stuff and while he is scatterbrained his lectures are really interesting. His grading on papers is kinda tough but it's not the end of the world if you get a low grade. I got B's on all the essays yet still got an A- in the class because of participation.
This professor is a hard grader. He may seem weird at first but he does know the material well! Go to class, or else you'll get docked points.
Very tough grader, unclear assignments, and when you think you are doing well, you're really not.

I think Dr. Christiansen is a nice guy but a really hard grader, mostly because of the grade scale and expectations on papers. This was hard for an intro philosophy class. He encourages participation, cares about students, and is easy to have conversations with. Ask him about his poetry and his film narration side gig.
5 people dropped the class before mid-term. This should tell you enough. Avoid if you can. I'm only staying because I did well on the assignments so far.

Hermann Hesse pondered if a man could exist who had no redeeming qualities. He obviously didn't take BIS 193 at UW Bothell. Boring class that killed my interest in philosophy, taught by a highly opinionated, black sweater-wearing leftist who is best left "teaching" in a liberal arts college.

This prof is terrible...lots of reading, and a super hard grader but gives NO feedback about grades.....i would never recommend him to anyone except if i hated them. Take any prof expect him cause u will never learn anything in his class.

Im gonna be real with yall, this was one of the toughest professors I had in college. If you actually care about your GPA, dont take his class. Spent hours on homework and many late nights doing essays to only receive mediocre grades. Got a 3.2 but 4.0s in my other 2 classes. Simply unreasonable.

Participation (10% of grade) is required and he will call on you to answer. 2-3 readings every week (20- 50 pages avg). Grade is based on 3 Papers (30% each), he's extremely strict on those. Overall, this class structure is rigorous and draining. He's a really chill and caring professor though. Don't take this, if you're expecting a easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He speaks pretty softly so sit at the front of the class. Other than that he's a nice guy, extremely knowledgable, good at explaining complex concepts in a way that's accessible. Due dates are VERY soft, practically nonexistent. No penalty for late assignments. You can pretty much do the whole course a couple days before the quarter ends.

These ratings are NOT accurate to the class I took with him (climate impacts). I found him to be one of the friendliest, most engaging teachers I've had here. Really values students' learning and gives them many ways to input their strengths and opinions in class work and discussions. Extremely interesting topic and readings. Easy to get a 4.0.

Eric's BST200 class was one of the most confusing classes I have ever taken. He talks extremely quiet, and even though I am an IAS major, I could tell he had a ridiculous amount of mistakes in his lectures. You MIGHT be able to hear an estimated 25% of what hes saying. He does curve his grades, but I would avoid any of his classes at ALL costs.

He's nice and passonate to teach and help, but honestly I was lost throughout the whole quarter. He doesn't talk about concepts or terms in his lecture, he only talks about how to solve problems. If you're taking his class, be ready to self study

This guy makes math errors like nobodies business. If your good at teaching yourself, take his class. He makes too many errors during lecture to be much use. He curved our exams so that the class average was an 85%, I ended up with over 100% in exams. Easiest 4.0 ever.

Classic case of a smart professor who doesn't teach well. Prepare to struggle and friend the smartest person in the class at MATLAB b/c you'll need it. He tends to ramble and its hard to listen to him. Not to mention the lack of any sort of textbook was frustrating. Online stacks will save your life. Pluses: no exams, this class is HW &project base

Class was boring.  I hardly went or I would leave early. All he did was lecture and the slides were online. He doesn't respond to emails. The final was online and it was tough! He curves so he's not a super tough grader. Still hard though. There's a group project but it's easy and you can work alone if you're like me and you don't like group work.
Prepare to study on your own.
Salathe knows his stuff but lectures are incredibly repetitive and boring.
The exam is same as hw problem... Going to class once a month and got 100%on hw and exam. Must take!

Both of his classes were as easy as possible. I wish he taught other math classes. I didn't have to do much homework and I am not a savant by any means. I love the Climate Science class as well just too easy . I asked him to make it harder for me on both of the courses. i wanted my retention to be higher.

Never take this class if your major is not climate science. His lectures and tests are just confusing. He promised us that the final covers only last few chapters but it actually covered all chapters. Also he never see his emails.

This is a very hard class, you should never take this class.  He is somehow helpful, but however very hard to understand his lecture.  He himself is very passionate about lecturing.  But the class will not understand what he is talking about.  So you really need to rely with the textbook and the HW. I do not recommend to take his class.
Super easy class. Although he isn't great at teaching, he is nice and genuine. His exams and quizzes can't get any easier. Make sure you do the homework, and you'll get an easy 4.0

He was an okay teacher but he hard to understand and was confusing hence the class was very quiet. He did his best to help though even though half the class did not know what was going on. Pretty much he taught from the textbook. i loved his text and quizzes though plus he tried hard so that you understood the material so it was okay.
Eunyoung ssn is an amazing professor and is great at teaching intro level Korean. I really enjoyed attending her quiz section and look forward to studying under her more in the future!

Won ssn truly cares about you learning Korean and not just there to do her job. She asks if you are understanding if you are getting behind, and really wants everyone to succeed. Attendance is central since you need to practice a new language when learning, and memorizing the vocab is just as important. Heavily recommended class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I had her for Korean 101-103 and she's so sweet and caring. Workload isn't too much and TAs grade very easily. She tends to rush through lectures but you learn mainly from workbook and other assignments anyways. The exams do get harder from 101-103 but they're not totally unreasonable. Great class and professor.

Won ssn was wonderful for first quarter Korean. She is super nice and understanding. Her class is a lot of work, though. Daily homework and vocab mastery is needed to get a 4.0. A 4.0 last quarter was a 99%, which is difficult, but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Since language classes require more practice attendance is mandatory. Lots of homework but mostly for practice as well. She's really helpful and cares about her students. Make sure to do all homeworks and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She is extremely sweet and easy to talk to. Always willing to take questions and very fun! Always asking students how the pace of the class is to adjust how things are taught. Amazing to start Korean with her. Highly recommended. The class has vocab quizzes, oral tests, biweekly tests and a final. All used to help solidify language.

She is a great teacher! Very helpful and always willing to help students understand the material. Her lectures are fun and engaging. Does call on people to speak in class but helps out if you don't know the correct statement. Highly recommend taking her if you are going to take Korean.
Very helpful and caring of her students. Her classes are very fun and in her lectures she includes modern usage of the Korean language.
Sweet, caring, and genuine.  Has expectations, but is reasonable and understanding.  Includes pop culture references in her presentations.
Good instructor, very helpful if you go to her office hours.Class is not difficult. Remember to do everything as the rubric tells you and you should get a good grade.

Make sure to do the work EXACTLY like the rubric tells you to in order to get feedback (i.e. don't skimp on the # of pages or edit margins). Start the portfolio ahead of time, go to class and participate, and you'll do fine. She's a nice teacher and is very respectful in her feedback.
She was a pretty good teacher, although she was not one of those professors you always remember for their passion. Her grading was also a little strange to me.

Lost my graduation honors because of this one class. Missed one class from being sick with COVID, missed a single in-class participation activity, and it brought my grade from a 4.0 to a 3.8. So long as you don't miss anything, you get a 100, pretty much. If you miss a few things you probably won't even pass. She is incredibly unfair, try to avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mabel seemed disorganized for this class. She often created last-minute assignments for us, and her expectations were never clear. She would change her expectations for homework when we would only have a week to complete them. It was stressful, and she did not understand at all. It's difficult to reach her outside of class too.
I really enjoyed Dr. Ezeonwu's class! She provided good feedback and made the course very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall the course was fairly easy and really only involved showing up to class, biweekly reflections and coordinating an interview with your group. In-class time is not worth it but mandatory, Mabel does not even instruct but instead has other speakers come to teach for her. When she does teach it is often redundant time wasting information. F-

Mabel is an understanding and good professor, i really recommend her! She makes you work for your grade but it's reasonable and fairly easy. Assignments consisted of 2-3 videos and writing a short paper, 2-3 group projects and of course short readings. If you came to rate my prof to see if you she's a good teacher she is! Enroll in her class!

She doesn't go by the School of nursing & health grading system, she makes up her own. In her class a 97% is a 3.7, a 90% is a 3.0 and an 80% is a 2.0! She is pretty picky as well but there are not a ton of assignments or homework either. If you are concerned about your GPA, probably not your best choice if you can help it. Thick accent also.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher. She is very polite and respectful towards everyone. she is very flexible. she doesn't stress students in class but at the same time she will make you understand what the course is about and also she is a an easy grader. Thank you Prof. it was an honer to take your class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: knowledgeable and accessible.  She expects students to work in her class to earn a good grade.  A "C" is truly average, and a "B" is something to be proud.  Group discussions are informative and participation is required.  Professor allows students to explore sensitive topics, but intervenes where appropriate.  I would take a class from her again.
Excellent lecturer.  In charge of class discussion and steers them in a meaningful way.  No empty headed contributions in Mabel's class.
Culture and ethics in Nursing. pretty good teachers but lots of reading and writing. very interesting class. A little bit lenient with grading.

The organization of the course is not amazing. Due dates will be changed every class and grades take weeks to update, so you can't study off of your homework. Not too accommodating to students, but she does care for your success in her own way. You must speak with her TAs first before you speak directly to her therefore difficult to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I put her as a 3 because tbh the course wasnt THAT bad, however the class was hard, she gets distracted super easily and gets off topic a lot, which makes lectures hard, but she knows it and so grading rubric a lot easier than other CSSE courses (.6+ is a pass). Despite it being easy, she grades very slow and can be unclear in her own criteria.

I had a lot of fun writing parallel CPU and GPU (CUDA) programs with performance considerations like locality and occupancy. I liked analyzing computer/CPU/GPU architecture to write programs. The professor has bad reviews but really she is great. She likes sharing what she knows and hopes her students like to learn. I liked taking her again.

Data Mining for ML is awesome. It studies how statistics, linear algebra, and PCA are used behind the scenes to build ML models. Lectures felt conversational. The textbooks Pattern Classification by Duda et al and section 7.3 from Introduction to Linear Algebra 5th ed by Strang are great resources. I only wish we could have covered more material.

I will first off admit Processor Parson's teaching style is controversial, however her brilliance in HPC can't be denied. 

I learned a lot in this class both on HPC and on neurodivergnece, which was a bonus.

One feedback I'd like to suggest is to review the assignments in class after they are due to reinforce what they were trying to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: After paying the fee foe in-person classes, the professor according to her convenience took half of the lectures online. She is very unprofessional regarding clearing out doubts/ criteria for assignments and project work. She never responds to emails regarding concerns addressed in the course. Her mood swings also affected my grades.
Very unclear grading criteria.A large number of reports, even if written in full accordance with the requirements, can be accidentally deducted points.

Professor Parsons, who openly shares she is neurodivergent, excels in teaching but expects proactive effort. She adjusts deadlines when students struggle and emphasizes breaking and analyzing code. Respect her, and she'll reciprocate. I've never had trouble talking to her; I think many who claim otherwise lack social skills and expect an easy A.
Avoid her. Take this warning with a grain of salt.

Dr. Parsons is a unique professor. She is controversial, but she cares about what will make students successful in the workplace. The skills she aims to teach you in this role are to help teach you the technical and soft skills to help you be independent and successful as an engineer in any role. She teaches knowledge and a working style.

Avoid this professor at all costs. She graded all assignments basically 2 months after submission. The TA's do not answer questions or provide real help. The professor always pushes due dates and always can't find a time to meet. She always tells you to just ask the TA's.
The professor is not approachable outside class. I find her disrespectful to students

Prof Parsons is not a good teacher. She is hyper specific in assignment grading and grades extremely harsh based on a hidden rubric, and gives no instructions on how to do the assignment. The final project is a full stack project and she gives 0 help on the front-end or back-end, only the SQL. avg grade on quizzes/final is around 60%

I got a good grade in this class, but she relies heavily on a poorly organized textbook. She was always late in grading assignments (4+ weeks to know a grade on an assignment) which hindered my learning and increased anxiety if would pass or not. I resorted to alternative online learning resources. I recommend taking another professor if possible.
