reviews.comment: WARNING: Don't take any class with her, I repeat, don't take any class with her, you will make your life extremely painful.

She's a good professor, maybe more suitable for grad students than for undergrads because her course requires you to study and learn a lot sometimes by yourselves.
I almost didn't take her class due to so many bad reviews, but, if someone is thinking the same, take it, you are going to learn a lot, but expect to invest a reasonable amount of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Grades come late and Canvas is not set up intuitively. Only a few assignments that actually end up getting graded. You would likely learn more from watching YouTube than from taking this class. Final project does not have a specific enough rubric, and professor doesn't stay on topic all lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Parsons has gotten a bad wrap over the years, and you can 100% see why after taking her class. Previous feedback aside, she still isn't that great of a professor. She is kind of all over the place with how she teaches. Exams were okay, and so were the assignments aside from the final project, but the path to get there was painful.

forget asking her a question, she will answer weeks later. After taking a exam, she will release scores as late as possible. For someone with no tolerance for late assignments, she sure takes her damn time putting in grades. her tests are not that bad, questions are technically pretty easy-mid but requires you to read her mind. Overall shitty prof.
Professor,Parsons is really encouraging and a nice person.I don't see why so many negative comments about her

Hard but passable homework. Tests are not too hard. She teaches very closely with the book, so if you read it and study the slides, you can do well on the exams. I dislike how she sometimes acts unprofessional towards students and goes on tangents, but I learned a decent amount (mostly from the book and slides) and got graded fairly enough.

Thank you YouTube and GitHub for getting me through this class. This professor is a really nice person, but just not a good teacher and has a really distracted lecture style that includes rants often. The textbook is not helpful and she doesn't teach from it. Exams are average difficulty, not as hard as other CSS classes I took.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a good person. She could be a good professor also if she isn't such busy in other businesses. Her lecture and slide are good enough to cover her exam and assignments, but if you want to achieve the final project, you have to take time on the textbook. The exams are tough, but she will give you partial credits if you don't select the rights.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Parsons is a great person, but not the best prof I've ever had. I got through this class with YT, lectures were messy. She was really nice at the start, but after exam 2 (everyone did bad on the same Q), she feels more hostile. When going over exam 2, she spent half the lecture telling us we didn't have critical thinking skills. I didn't like that.

Professor Parsons definitely has a quirkier, and sometimes distracted, style of teaching but she also very much cares about her students and how they are doing in the class. Lectures are easy to pay attention to and I always learn a lot (when her internet is working properly). Some of the negativity in the reviews here is unwarranted in my opinion

Professor Parsons is a teacher who cares greatly about your learning outcomes as a student. I do not see why there is so much negativity surrounding her, as she is a professor that will give back as much as you put in. She can occasionally become distracted from topics, but I felt students were responsible for that. and bunnies

Her assignment description was not clear and she might not (half of the time) available to answer all of your questions. Her answers were not very helpful sometime, so you still had to do some research to find the right answers. I learned mostly from reading the book. Don't expect to just show up in class and study the slides to get good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don't take this professor for this class or any class. Gets distracted too often in lectures. Provides no examples or answers to any discussions, worksheets, or exams so you don't know what is right and what is wrong. Does not have proper office hours and rarely answers questions on Discord. Doesn't grade exams on time. Rude and unprofessional.

Awful or mediocre in all aspects of teaching this course. Often lectures go off-track for 30 minutes or longer and detract from learning the material. Exams had bad wording and/or missing information on multiple questions. Stranded students on the final project by not going over it until last minute and not answering questions on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pattern Recognition: Very nice professor but if you have the chance to avoid having her as a professor, do so. She tends to lash out at you if you don't understand something. She will be blatantly rude for no reason. Her class is very unorganized, due dates and requirements will change right before the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Parsons is a good person but a horrible Professor. We were one week behind on the project and she decided to skip introducing the project and instead expected us to read the slides and decipher what we need to do for it. Her exams are by far the HARDEST exams I've ever taken (and I'm a straight 4.0 student).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Please don't. Just don't do it to yourself. Don't take 430 or any other class with Parsons. She's a nice person, but as a professor, she is far from average. Tests are confusing. She doesn't answer questions in class and the Discord is pointless. She says to ask the graders for help but they never reply either. Good luck if you take her...

she's a nice enough lady, but she is just such a bad teacher. The class is disorganized. She changes the instructions and due dates of homework without telling anyone. She misunderstands questions but won't listen when you try to clarify. She is never available during her office hours and when she finally shows up wont help beyond "read the slide"

Can't recommend. Class structure is too disorganized. Assignment descriptions and assignment due dates constantly changed. Dr. Parsons seemed to care, but overall, had a tendency to dismiss or even lash out at students for expressing their difficulties with the course. Just too frustrating and unprofessional.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Look. She's a human, and she'll work with you. But over and over there are frustrations. She makes you install new things every assignment and they're not easy installations. She calls people out in the middle of lecture for having facial expressions because she wants to do gotchas that you're paying attention. I just can't.

She is super nice and understanding, but her lectures are incredibly boring. The assignments really arent difficult but they seem like busy work to me, I didnt feel like I learned anything from them. The worst part is that she NEVER responds to emails and takes forever to grade things.

I'm not sure why she has such bad ratings. She is very understanding, charismatic, and detailed. She's willing to change the pace of the class depending on the entire class' feeling on the current assignment or topic. In one of the other classes I took of hers she boosted me and a group mate's grades because one of our members dropped last minute.

She really knows the material and teaches the class well. Be sure to ask questions even if you don't quite understand what was just presented. She is very accommodating during class and office hours. She has strict rules but there are not unreasonable and i have never seen someone kicked out during my time in her class.

Boring lectures. Loves students who participate in lectures. She's a bunny furry if you didn't know. Never responds to emails, period. Lazy on grading (Slow and still gives bad grade) . She also loves bunnies if you didn't know. She loves everything Microsoft if you didn't know. . Did I mention she likes bunnies? She does, if you didn't know.

She is very nice and cares about her students success, but her teaching skills are crap. On top of that, the class has way too many assignments to manage it with the research project and another class. The lectures were also very repetitive which became quite boring.

Probably the worst professor I've had in all 4 years at this school. Tests are nearly 50% of the total grade, and she doesn't curve them even if the average is absurdly low. Exams are heavily based on her "discussion" questions, which she does not allow sharing and discussion of your answers. So no one knows if they are doing the question correctly

Clear your schedule and get your last naps in before taking this course; it's about a semester of material packed into a quarter. Prof. Parsons does her best, but the course material is locked down by the UW and out of date, so expect a lot of (deprecated) curve balls coming your way. Get a study fellowship together, else YOU SHALL NOT PASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Parsons has unusually communication requirements via email that detracts from being able to communicate with her. I learned that when I was in my 20s
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: GCSDD course. The course was interesting, but extremely challenging. There was just too much stuff and too little time. I liked her and she seemed to care, but there were too many problems to rate her highly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: unorganized and unclear explanations and presentations, inpatient to students, no desire to help students on discussion questions during office hour. Use many "this" and "that" to present computer terms and who god know what "this" and "that" mean. provide much confusing knowledge so have to use youtube to clarify. unwilling to adopt other opinions

Dr. Parson does not know the concepts very well, she is unable to explain things. You won't get feedback on discussions at all, which are included in tests. The only way to find out the correctness of your answers is if they appear on test, if not, you won't know the correct answers. When asking a question, she'll go with the flow. Avoid her!!

Terrible attitude and very unprofessional. She has reading quizzes, but otherwise doesn't use the book much. Her exams require you to know C++ even though it's not taught prior to or much in this course. I sent her several emails throughout the quarter and she didn't respond to any of them. Doesn't answer questions after class. List goes on and on.

reviews.comment: Parsons is usually very unclear with instructions on the homework and exams. If you ask her questions over confusion with what she wants, she gives you the "if you don't understand it, that's your fault"type attitude. That sounds very unprofessional and I thought it's a professor's job to make sure students are understanding the stuff correctly.
She teaches well; however you have lots of things to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This professor often has a negative attitude towards students who ask questions over homework, exams, and grades. If you go into her office hours over a disagreement with your grade, she will tell you that youre being very rude. As a CSSE major, Ive never had a professor unprofessional and frustrating as this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Erika Parsons is very unapproachable and only makes herself available for students for about one hour out of the week. In that hour, she will only help one or two students and tell them to help the rest while she chats with her colleagues. She is also very unclear of her expectations from her students. Her exams are hard, and she doesn't curve.

She's as bad as it gets, she has some sort of anger issue. Threatens to give pop-quiz in class if one study 'peeks' at their phones. She forces you to turn in printed homework (for a computer science course?) When she losses them she claims you never turned it in and fails you. Steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was really nice, and really enthusiastic about the topic. I think the class should either require linear algebra and go deeper into the material, or avoid linear algebra and cover many different classifiers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She doesn't qualify to be a professor. She makes mistakes on even the most basic concepts, she has no idea of what the assignment is about since none of the assignment is from her. She's rude most of the time. Don't expect to learn much from her. She doesn't update the slides or syllabus. I wonder why the school would hire her.
She seems has no passion for teaching and no patience with students.  Her response to emails are very slow, sometimes no response at all.

Her participation requirement induces painful questions that waste time in every lecture. You grow to hate anyone who speaks, especially yourself, because you know they're only doing it for participation points.

Solid lectures. She does cover 1 or 2 topics not typically covered in this class (K-maps) which I see as a bonus. Introduced to the material in class and must continue learning outside of class. Very understanding grader so long as you put assumptions in program reports. Put in the time, participate, follow assignment details and you'll do great.

Terrible class. First of all, she has a serious attitude problem. She seems to be angry all the time, about what, I have no idea. Keeps talking about pet bunnies, which seems cute at first, and then it just seems... wrong. She'll never give a straight answer to a tough question - expect lots of extracurricular work. Not hot at all, either.

She lectured too much on details, whereas it would have been better to get the overview of things and let us read the text for details. Her participation requirement means students ask redundant questions and/or add irrelevant comments to the "discussion". She told us we could use notes on the final and then revoked this 2 days before the test.
She waster too much time answer all student questions. Also, she spend much time in her computer.
Professor Parsons is an excellent instructor. She takes the time to make sure that students understand the material. I would take a class from her again.
Don't waste your money to take her class. If you take you will regret!

She was nice, generous with participation points and I think with that extra credit it motivates you to ask questions and discuss things to gain a better understanding of the material. Lectures might not be perfect but operating systems is one of those very tough courses so if you put effort/work into it you can get a decent grade.

Lectures are confusing, encourages students to answer each other's questions even though they may be wildly incorrect and ensures more confusion. Very difficult to succeed without putting a disproportionate amount of effort in.

Awful lectures. Not organized. Hard to follow because lack of visual aids. Discussion based classes not useful because Dr. Parsons will ask that we discuss in small groups topics we have only just been lectured on five minutes ago to "come up with answers on our own".  Not allowed to draw any pictures or diagrams on cheat sheet  for exams.

Man.. she's a really nice person, but her teaching is intolerable. Her lectures are completely scattered and unfocused which makes it really hard to learn from class. Additionally, it seems that when she is unsure about an answer to a question, she defaults to asking the class.. and somehow the right answer is never established. Tough class to in..

She reads word-for-word from her slides. The class is wildly boring and she answers questions in an extremely condescending manner. Her TA's are great though especially when it comes to grading. She does bring in interesting guest speakers which were the only way I got through this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I can see how the class would turn people away from social work. If you do the homework, are really careful about APA, and come to class, you should do well. But it was so boring, I really didn't feel like I was gaining anything from the class, and she treats us like kids. It felt like a waste of time. Textbook was interesting but not needed.

The TA for this class was really harsh about using APA correctly! I am from a discipline that uses Chicago so this was irritating. Just do the work and you will get a good grade. Dr. Farwell is very open to suggestions, she needs to learn how to use the classroom technology

I thought this was a pretty good class, you might need to be a good writer to obtain a good grade though.  The class is weighed heavily on papers alone.  The TA is a bit of a stickler.  I really enjoyed the movies and guest speakers.  Lectures were alright, professor knows her stuff... but, the material is boring.  Book is good though!

This class felt very disappointing. The professor talks in circles and the lectures didn't feel well planned. Also, a lot of class time was waisted on things that should have been discussed during office hours. This was not a good intro class, it may have been more enjoyable for someone already in the major

Meh, Nancy was okay, but this class felt like high school! (And not in a good way) The guest lectures and movies were the best part of class; her teaching style is not good, although it's understandable because she usually teaches grad students, not intro classes. Oh well.

She's a nice person and all, but really not the best lecturer out there. I often felt like she was a bit condescending toward her students, which is not what you would expect out of a social work prof. She also assigns pop quizzes, which I think are very ineffective, and her TA is a very harsh grader. That said, the material is very interesting.

Thankfully I only had her as a lab instructor. I would never recommend taking a lecture course with her. She would lecture for an hour during the lab and I had to try to tune her out so I could actually get some coding done. Half of the points for the lab assignments come from attending the lab, which is super annoying. She acts like a babysitter.

I studied C# in the past before taking this class (Java).  Many of the concepts were similar, but she rushed through most of the basics.  If I hadn't studied programming before, this class would have been impossible.  IMPOSSIBLE.

The CSSSKL lab was very straight-forward.  All of the material and expectations were clear.  Her voice isn't the clearest, she has an accent, but she definitely knows what she is doing.  She checks in with students and helps them when necessary.

she is really pretty and cute.  Explanations would pretty bad, but although she grades extremely rough--she actually bumps it up later.  BIG extra credit... do more than 30 questions on homework a week and guaranteed A.  I was expecting a B overall but got a 4.0.  Allows computers in class, but no graphing calculators on tests

Exams were hard, lectures were long and boring. But let's face it, this is the nature of programming. I highly recommend outside studying or some familiarly with Python before taking this class since it will focus on Java. Professor is kindhearted and works hard to help students. Although she might not be the very best, she is a decent professor.

Some people just shouldn't be teaching. Fabiana is nice but, often, she confused herself in front of the class, and that made the mathematics incredibly difficult to follow. She wasn't much better one-on-one, either. I mean, I'm sure she's smart but being smart doesn't make you a good teacher.
If you have another choice take it!

She would always confuse herself and would always get off topic quickly. Her quizzes were ok and her tests were hard. Its easier to ignore her after she gets to the point because after that you will scratch your head.

Her explanations in class would be more theoretical and she would give easy examples to go over. However the quizzes and exams were extremely harder than any of stuff we had gone over. A lot of students failed the first midterm completely. Also she seemed very inconsistent with what she wanted us to do.

Yes she is a hard prof. Her Midterms are medium/hard. She explains concepts mostly through the hard/confusing ways. Expect a good amount of challenging online homework. Shes sometimes seems to be unorganized. However she is quite reasonable, nice, and funny. Keep your eye on lecture and get plenty of help from the QSC center and you might be OK.

She was not hard for me, I did not struggle in her class although one bad thing that I don't like is how much homework she assigns, its way too much, sometimes you can have homework problems with 60 questions. Overall, I liked the class and had great experience.

I wanted to like this class. I tried everything to like this class. I attended almost every office hour, and yet this class still destroyed me. It is unfair, and unclear. She may be extremely intelligent, but she is a horrible teacher. Also her English can be hard to understand.

She's horrible! The kind of teacher that doesn't know the simplified way to teach people. I've learned most of this stuff already and was able to easily understand and coming to her class I'm now confused about all of it. She always makes mistakes when she is talking and doesn't seem prepared. I feel when I come to this class it's totally pointless

She is sweet but she can be irritating sometimes because she can get confused then fix her mistakes right away therefore leading me to erase some notes. dont think her pre exams were all too helpful. just know shes not that type of professor that lets you know you are wasting your time on practicing problems she not going to test on. shes bearable

Useless. The whole class either failed or barely passed our midterm and she refuses to help students, adjust grades or take any responsibility. Basically, it's our own faults. She often makes mistakes in lecture and is constantly correcting herself, making it very confusing to follow the lesson. HW does NOT help prepare students for exams.
Assigns a book and assignments that are almost worthless for help on the tests. When the class failed first midterm basically just says "its your fault"
Fabiana often confused herself with her lectures, which made her very hard to follow. This class was a waste of time and money.

His R Markdown file has everything you need. 3 R Assignments, one Midterm based on concepts, and one final project in which you find/create your own network dataset and make plots in R. Lectures are really helpful and the prof is easily accessible. Very, caring, considerate, chill, and supportive. Really engaging class.

Absolutely amazing professor! 11/10 would recommend! Caring, considerate, engaging, and intellectual. Very helpful, helps you a lot in office hours and gives you thorough feedback on your assignments. Easygoing and really wants you to get something out from the class. I took two classes with him and wish I could take more! One of the best I've had!

Dr. Ferrare is hands down the best professor I've had at UWB. So much so that I took another class that he taught purely because he was the one teaching it. His feedback is thoughtful and critical in the best possible way. He really understands constructive criticism and takes the time to thoroughly examine your work himself - seriously, 11/10.

Professor Ferrare was fantastic. This class was a hybrid so we only met once a week, though I found myself wishing we met more often. The lectures were interesting, and the way he explained new topics was very easy to understand. Homework was minimal and you had plenty of time to get everything done. 10/10 would take again.

This was a very fun class especially with how helpful Prof Ferrare is. Fair grader and is always willing to take the time to help and explain things. Class time was engaging and Joe creates an environment where its easy to ask questions and participate. Best prof I've had a UWB-- highly recommend especially for CS students to take him
Professor Ferrare was really good and very funny. His classes were always fun to attend and he explained the concepts well. He is a very fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredible Professor! 100% If you are looking for a professor that really takes the time to walk you through the process of learning, Ferrare is the man! He is super positive, talks clearly, gives constructive feedback, and makes sure that you submit your assignments on time. I would gladly take him again!

I really enjoyed Joes class. Its a hybrid course so there isnt a lot of class time but he was always willing to meet outside of class and help. Hes really kind and truly cares about his students. He gives good feedback and there wasnt a ton of homework.

The way he organizes the content and his classes is confusing and stressful. He grades the projects mostly by his opinion. It is really hard to keep up. You dont have to come to class but you will probably fail if you dont. Dont take this class if data visualization isnt part of your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Caring professor who takes great concern for your learning. Willing to help with any difficulties you may be facing whether that is related to class or not. Cares so much about students.

Joe's class was great. Certainly not hard but I felt like I learned a lot from him. I never thought I would do math or programming for my IAS degree (MCS major), but his data visualization class was fantastic. He was good at teaching it despite coming from a political science/policy research background, and is very approachable/helpful. Love him.

I'm in his statistics class right now. I really enjoy it because he introduces the concepts gently and always listens to students' feedback on whether he's going too fast or too slow. He's also willing to help on exams if you email him (they're all online) which is rare for a professor.
Great lectures, really cares about his students, yet the workload is tough. He also does a great job explaining different topics to student at different speeds and habits.

I think Dr. Ferrare did a very good job in teaching this class, especially because this was his first quarter at UWB. He has extremely engaging lectures and very good examples, especially the videos. He is not a tough grader and is extremely supportive towards students. He wants everyone to try their best.
He's an awesome guy, but his class is one of the hardest I've done this quarter. There's a lot of busy work but he is there to support you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The course was tedious but Professor Ferrare is still an excellent professor. I don't think there's ever been a day where I didn't look forward to his class. Statistics is hard in general but he made it slightly easier than I expected.

Curved grades downward. Grades by rank, even if 2 students had similar grades (983.9, 97.33.8, 97.23.7). Just reads powerpoints in monotone. Lets students talk loudly during lecture. Reveals private info. Couldn't answer basic lab questions. Says "I'm confused" a lot. Major typos. Left out details on homework. Grades inconsistently w/freq errs.

It will be self study in his class but it is worth it towards the end. His exams are not super difficult as long as you do the homework yourself. Go over his review before his exams and you will receive a good grade.

Expects students to know the material before coming to class. This is basically self-study class. He hardly gives answers to students questions. This is one of the must-avoid professor. Expect no help from professor for the lab. Textbook reading and lecture materials are way out of balance and doesnt correspond each other.
Not helpful in regards to CSS classes. He is an EE teacher who is teaching a CSS course. It was a train wreck.

She has extremely high and unrealistic expectations for an introductory class. So much of what she demands is really unnecessary and poorly planned. Class time is wasted doing tasks with the expectation that projects be completed outside of class with minimal time due to poor time schedules for the media lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very tough grader. Stay away.

She is an amazing professor. I know nothing about technology but the way she teaches the course is clear and relatable. She is also very understanding and cares about her students. Homework amount is reasonable and if you come to class, participate and do the homework you will pass. She's An overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Even though she is clear about how the assignments will be graded, she is way too tough on an introductory class. We meet once a week and it can be confusing at times, but overall, I enjoy the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: boy is he enthusiastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Encourages classroom debate among students and with himself, very respectful and intelligent. Fascinating lectures and examines multiple perspectives. Would definitely recommend.

Fantastic prof. Really cares about his students and promotes true freedom of speech and opinion, as well as encouraging open debate, in class. Lots of reading assignments and long lectures but his enthusiasm and energetic teaching style make up for them.

The teacher's lecture was basically him rambling off for an hour and a half. What he says make sense if you have basic knowledge of economics and you do the reading. I didn't do any of the readings, however, if you actually pay attention to his lectures you will be able to find the answers. But you must find the answers in his long ass lecture.
What a great prof!  Have learned more about politics in this one class than I ever have in any other course. Hope he stays.

if you are a person who doesn't like talking about gloom and doom and it legitimately stresses you out, take this class with a different professor, or take Macro instead. This class should also be something you are in with Farkasch. The more into the topic you are, the higher the grade you'll get because he wants your opinion.
I learned more in this one course than I did in all my other courses and he's always willing to help if you put in the effort. Lots of reading!

Lectures are the main course of the course, and while you do learn a considerable amount and the prof is clearly very well-learnt in the subject, he can come off as smug and patronizing, and tends to go on tangents to explain concepts that should only take a couple of sentences to get down. Basically, good knowledge, but mediocre personality.

I loved this class! The lectures were engaging and when he went off on a tangent, it still related to the overall theme of the class. There are two major writing assignments in the class, but he makes sure that you know the material and he helps you truly succeed. All in all, I would take this class again :)
He's a great professor, very chill. Cares about your future.
Another great class with this professor. Go to class, do the work, get an A.

This teacher is awesome! he DID take time to get to know students, he was very helpful you just have to ask! He is actually really funny, and he gives a week notice when something is due or if there is a test coming up. Great teacher!
Loves to hear himself talk. Impossible to take notes.  Lots of tangents.  Didn't learn a thing about US policy or processes.

If you want a class that is easy to pass, where the proff thinks he's a comedian and never makes an effort to get to know his students; this is the class for you. However, if you want to actually learn about international relations and how they are applied to current tissues... skip it.I was so disappointed. Least valuable course I have ever taken.

Rob is an awesome teacher! His teaching style gets you learn a lot, but in a easy way~ All you need to do throughout the quarter is just to read carefully of the reading assignment and do good on two big papers. He is super helpful so I'd absolutely recommend you guys taking it!

I've never met a professor who shared the same ideas as myself. Absolutely loved him, knows his stuff, very ineligible. The readings are important but not always necessary. Attended class everyday so did well in the class and did the study guides.

Fantastic lecturer and a great class.  Class is weighed on exams and 3 papers so there isn't any regular homework and he posts the exam questions (essay based) online before the exam.  You WILL need to do the readings for the exams and papers which is fairly heavy, but you can get by skipping a few here and there.  Definitely take this class.

Not a bad teacher. Lectures a lot but fairly lenient in terms of the assignments and essays he gives. Fairly knowledgeable if not judgmental. If you can deal with it, then it's the perfect class for you.

I took 3 class with Professor Farkasch and if he offered more I would take all of them. He lectures and it is fun to listen to him, you can tell he loves the topics he is teaching. Attendence isn't mandatory but you should since it is helpful for the exams. Exams are straight forward.
SUPER AWESOME PROFESSOR!! Very easy, helpful and fun! He is interesting and explains everything very well. Hands down the best professor i've had at UWB!

He's good at lecturing & gives a ton of examples, but he calls people out when they're having side conversations. The only homework is the reading he assigns & an 8-12 p paper that's a critical book review due at the end of the quarter. The midterm is pretty easy, since he tells you everything you need to know & gives the possible questions for it.

I absolutely LOVED this class! Went in terrified to learn about Internationl Relations but came out very well informed. Great professor always willing to help! No quizzes only 2 in class writing midterms super esay if you come to class everyday, take notes and pay attention. Ended the class with a 3.9 not what I expected!

GREAT Teacher!! Really entertaining. If you are not very good at self-learning I wouldn't recommend his course he lectures and there is a lot of discussion. If you can't study independently you may not do well. He expects you to understand concepts and be able to portray your understanding in the written tests. 3 assignments; Two tests, one paper.
Great Teacher!! learned a lot in his class, & is really enjoyable to be around. However, he does give out a lot of readings, that are around 9-14 pages long.

he gives insightful and really easy to understand lectures. if you already know about some global/domestic issues than this class is a piece of cake!! not much hw is given. just keep up with the readings, show up to class, take notes and everything else falls into place.
Great professor, my favorite ever. Not much homework and his lectures are very easy to listen to and follow. AND he is hilarious
This man is incredible - Literally the greatest human being of all time

Farkasch is a boss! He is an amazing speaker and even better, he didn't give us homework in Global Econ. We only had a couple tests and a paper at the end of the quarter. He is funny, lighthearted, and just a really cool guy overall. Sit at the front because then you will get a chance to talk to him and see how laid back he is.

I had him for both American Government and Global Economics one quarter, and that has been my favorite quarter by far! He's fascinating to listen to, and is very straightforward on what he wants from you as a student. Put in a little effort, and you'll be rewarded.  Just a lot of reading, and a large paper due at the end of the quarter.

Very well-spoken and super interesting. Plays devil's advocate during lectures. If you show up to class and give it a good go he will reward your effort. Very willing to discuss concerns with students, is respectful and brings the subject back around even when class participants say  some really dumbass things.

Ok everyone elses review was wrong, He is a good teacher i will give everyone that but his class arguably was one of the most boring things i have ever been to. and there is a fat 12 page essay at the end of the quarter that was ridiculous. Have fun this quarter if he is your teacher.
Great teacher, really wants you to understand what he's teaching-passionate about his class.
Easy to tune out and sit in class and do nothing, long essays, incorporate readings into tests and will be fine.
Hella intelligent and well spoken

Awesome stories, can seem doom and gloom, but really puts certain topics into reality. Touched on Rwanda, impacts of the UN, overall fantastic. I got an A in his class, the key lesson = read lecture notes he posts and attend class most who did bad was because of not knowing lectures, remember a few authors, answer exam questions before test day.

He is tough but I think it is for the best. He pushes his students to do better and I appreciate that, although my brain often hurt after lectures ;) I think we need more prof's like him to avoid the brain drian.
Tells stories relevant to the lecture to make difficult ideas more comprehensible and interesting. A good man and a good teacher. Exams are straightforward.

Excellent instructor. Everyones' comment clearly explain what an awesome professor he is. He does lecture a lot, but he is one of the few instructors that can pull that off without boring you. Definitely take one of his classes.
He makes class very interesting with his love for the subject.  I can sit in his class all day and not want to leave.  Great class discussions and he grades pretty well if yo interact. TAKE HIM!
Great professor, the best I've taken so far at UWB.
This guy is not only a great teacher, but also he is funny and very attractive!

He is the man people! if you want to learn about current stuff this guy know his subject. Extremely knowledgeable, very caring, charismatic individual. By far the best Professor the program can offer.
Extremely great professor.The best I've taken so far. Very Interesting and engaging lectures. Don't graduate without taken  one of Dr.Farkasch's classes you won't regret it!
The best instructor at UWB hands down. A must take class any of them!

My favorite Prof! This guy is straight up, and only wants to know that you are reading the material and making connections.  He is fair, caring, and gives the benefit of doubt for the first exams.  His teachings are current, and apply to what is actually going on in the world today, in many different aspects.  I have learned a great deal from him!

If you want to learn about IR this is this is the way to go. This guy is by far, the best teacher around. His other courses are great too,Political Ideas and a Terrorism class. Funny, smart and extremely helpful!

Lectures are more of a discussion format, tends to really wonder off course of the lecture outline.  Sometimes "know-it-all" students in class will not shut up and next thing you know class is over and you didn't cover anything.  As long as you read all the articles and lecture notes, a 3.5-4.0 in this class should be a piece of cake.
Loved the lectures and learned a lot. I would have liked more quizzes but the exams were straight forward.
Very straightforward course.  Basic stuff that's useful to know, and the prof is good at delivering it.  Don't expect too much intellectual challenge, but do expect to learn what you need to learn.

Very insightful and engaging. His lectures are almost always interesting, and is at times humorous. He does demand a lot of reading, but has relatively few actual assignments. His grading is very fair and can be easy if you've done any of the reading. Highly recommend.
He's an awesome prof. Class is interesting if you actually do the homework. Very helpful, friendly, smart and actually gets to know the students.

Lectures very boring and lack passion on subject matter. Lectures also do not help make reading material more interesting. As a business student forced to take BIS electives you will find class debates concering captialism vs marxism/feminism annoying.
Great prof. very helpful, down to earth, supportive, enthusiastic, understanding. Very knowledgeable in International Relations.
Not very understanding when uncontrolable events occur

Dr. Farkasch has a great deal of enthusiasm, and while his lectures can meander at times, you always come away feeling like you've learned something.  Fantastic instructor, very knowledgable, very Canadian.  :)
I had no interet in international relations before taking Prof. Farkasch's class but now I'm hooked. Take his classes and open up to the world of global studies.
Informative lectures. He's taking the year off which sucks since the other course offerings are a bit weak for Fall and Winter.
Great Prof! Brought a wealth of knowledge to the class even though he's Canadian. LOL
While the readings were difficult at times, Prof. Farkasch was able to explain them in light of recent events in the news.
Very bright and approachable prof. Knows his stuff!

Didn't grade a project that was turned in 6 weeks before finals until the last day before grades posted. Rudely rejected student's requests and questions if he didn't like them. In a class about management of people, Walt showed he can't manage time, complaints, or classes well in general. A big disappointment and frustration.

Tough grader. Feedback is given at the end of the quarter when you can't make any improvements. Lectures are long and PPT based. Reading the textbook is vital. Weighs participation high but not many chances to participate in class discussions. This is the 2nd class I've taken w/ him. I would try to avoid him unless mgmt is your major you can't.

Very dull lecturer. He will lecture off of boring powerpoints that seem to go on forever. The homework is extremely redundant and pointless. He put us into groups of 7 for a 8 pg. case study saying everyone has to participate. Why would any professor make a group of 7 for something so miniscule? The tests are vague. Would not recommend.

This whole class is based on the reading. Make sure you do the reading from day 1 and don't leave it until last minute like me. If you do the reading in depth you will do fine on the test. There is a group project which is not to hard if you have good teammates. There is an essay which is do able. Lectures are semi interesting. Good teacher though.

Solid professor that really knows his stuff. Grades fairly and with a curve. He cares that students not only get a decent grade but understand the material. He even graciously navigated an obnoxious student that proved to the class once and for all that there really are dumb questions. Attendance is required.

Dr. Freytag's lectures are extremely dry and dull. I learned more from the textbook than him. However, he is extremely like and helpful. You have two exams, and he is a fair grader. He'll throw out questions if the majority of the class gets it wrong, and also adds a giant curve.

An okay professor, super boring though, spends 5x longer than should explaining a concept and pauses in between loosing his train of thought. Expects students to know textbook inside out and laughs when someone doesn't know something as if wow how did you not learn that. Seems paranoid and doesn't grade fairly.
I really enjoyed his class. He taught very useful information that can be applied in the real world.
Knows his stuff. Very dry lectures at times. Very hard grader. Not sure if I would recommend or not, but definitely not the worst professor I had that quarter.

mgmt of ppl. Freytag is a nice guy, but incredibly boring. Spends 3X as long to explain concepts as needed. My coffee intake doubled over quarter. Book is 2-color, no pix, very boring. In addition, he graded very strictly--I received much less than I expected. Next time will switch to Rock Star.

Good Teacher. He is very enthusiastic about his subject. Tests are about 50 multiple choice and 2 essay questions. Not very timeconsuming and the group project was able to be completed in class. I would take this teacher again, definitely!!
Pretty good teacher, we did a lot of group work during class so lectures weren't too boring or dry

Boring lectures. Just plain boring. The MC ?'s, just memorization, but he is so critical on your essays. My advice, don't take him. People in my group messed up, of course everyone gets the same group grade. The book sucks too. And now I have to take him again for Managing Employees. Oh Joy!

Very intelligent professor who enjoys flushing out concepts presented in class. Frequently calls upon students who volunteer and expects them to be able to hold their ground when answering a question. Participation is key. Lectures can be dry at times. Tests are primarily from the reading and lectures. Focuses on memorization, no room for ambiguity
He knows the topic but is a bit dry.  He also has tons of industry experience.
Excellant professor who has wealth of knowledge that applies to current career field. Very fair and ethical professor!! Very devoted to his field and to the students at UWB.

Excellent working experiences - draws on them frequently. A bit academic and theoretical on some topics. Way too concerned about definitions and committing terms to rote memory vs. learning and applying concepts. Follows the text too closely.
If you care about learning Walt is the way to go.  Nothing flashy but very clear and you leave the course really understanding the material and able to apply it elsewhere.
A little dry but has a wealth of knowledge.

I've taken four of his courses so far. A little dry sometimes, yes, but garunteed you will learn more in his classes than anywhere. They aren't overly difficult, and there aren't many assignments at all. I always recommend this professor. Don't slack on your group projects, they're a big part of your grade and he expects good work. Great professor.

Has a lot of real-world experience. He can get boring especially when he "preaches" about something he seems to like. Assignments and tests not too difficult if you follow the readings. His average grades are about 2.8 for almost all his classes, and he likes to brag about that. Overall, not bad.
He makes the Sahara seem like a moist place.  The dryest presentations that are not clear.  Little help and really believes that he is a good and fair teacher.
Adds papers within Assignments without notice to class or transparency. Lacks quality of feedback to be helpful. If you can take the class by another professor, I would recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Have taken a couple classes. Would avoid this one if other options are available. Warning: Number of changes syllabus after quarter starts. Changes test and homework scores weeks after grading. Lazy instruction, not a great, and not good teaching style. Learned more through tutoring.
Poor understanding of disabilities with accommodation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gayle is one of the greater teachers I've had. She obviously cares about her students and their success. Gayle is a TOUGH grader but do the work and ask questions and you will do well. Never thought I'd get a 4.0 in her class but put in the time and work and you're golden.

Lots of homework but she helps you out and you are allowed to work on it with others. You definitely won't pass if you don't attend class or pay attention to the material. She knows what she is talking about though, very well educated in the topic of epidemiology

Honestly one of my least favorite profs I've had, mainly because I took this class during a pandemic and she didn't really seem to care that her students were struggling with other issues. One thing she said to us will always stick with me: "I took this class too and didn't have any issues." She was nice but lots of hw and not very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I learned a lot with professor Wei Gao, the class is pretty interesting and she's very nice! She's willing to help the students and provide good feedback for essay ! Work hard and get good grade!:)

The class was very interesting. She definitely lectures a lot and most of the class  time will be the lecture. They can be boring at times but if you really are able to pay attention she provides interesting information. Uses atalyst rather than canvas. Her assignments and files were very confusing to follow. And due dates were very unorganized.

Yeah, she's nice and friendly but she's extremely boring. And, make sure you know her grading criteria - especially if your essay is worth 40% of your grade for instance. In that case, it doesn't matter if you do well on the final or anything, you could still end up with a relatively bad grade if you do bad on essay. Probably won't take again.

Professor Gao was very sweet and kind. If you need help she'll be there. She definitely has an accent so during lectures. And be warned she talks for two hours straight. But if you do every assignment and complete all of the essays with good cited work with a good argument, then you should be safe taking her class.

She definitely has an accent but not enough to distract anyone completely from the learning process. She has a lot of knowledge but don't trust her pronunciations of certain characters (it personally bothers me). Be on her good side, show up everyday and get an A. She really cares about her students but flaky due dates and disorganized sometimes.

Make sure to bring a laptop to class... Most of the times you need it to kill some time; I liked to download and play games.  She'll randomly put up group quizzes during class only.  In total you might get 3 group assignments and 2 major assignments.  The major ones are clumped into the last week (10-15 page report + 10-15 min group presentation).
Easiest 135 writing class, nearly impossible to failget a bad grade unless you do not turn in your work.

This teacher is a mixed bag. On one had, it's very easy to fly by in her class, it's intended for international students, but if you're a native english speaker, a lot of the class becomes easy. On the other hand, she's very unclear about her expectations, and she's ALWAYS talking, it's impossible to get work done cause of her broken english.
Take her, she has a slight accent. But she tries to engage the class, easy 4.0 if she sees you are working for it.
ezpz 4.0 just do your work well and your good. She's also very nice and will help you with whatever you need.
She has a slight accent, but is funny and sweet. She is passionate about her teaching and is willing to help the students. The workload is fair.

I took her Chinese history class just because I couldn't get into another class. This class blew my mind. We actually learned a lot. It's not as hard as is sounds and its interesting unlike other history classes.

I took her Chinese language class from 100 to 103 and I have learned a lot! I learned not only the language, but also the culture as well. She genuinely cares for her students and makes sure that each and every student is doing well and she offers a lot of opportunities for those who are falling behind. I am looking forward to studying abroad with her when she offers a course! Definitely will take her for any other class.
the class is pretty interesting and she is so nice

I really enjoyed this class with Dr Galindo, she seemed really invested in students' learning and success.   There were 3 exams (1 cumulative), 5 homework assignments, and in-class worksheets almost every lecture. The workload was definitely manageable as long as you read the textbook or showed up to class. I recommend her to anyone taking BIO466!

HOLY MOLY SHE MADE ME WANT TO RIP MY HAIR OUT. the biggest possible yapper. talks and acts like a robot aka has no empathy. She made writing a paper the most difficult, tedious tasks possible. not to mention she treated us like high schoolers: "If you miss more than 2 classes we need to have a talk about why" EXCUSE ME DONT TELL ME WHAT DO BABE
Lecture heavy but very passtionate about the subject. She is very approachable and answers any questions you have, would reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's super sweet, approachable, & understanding. On exam days, she would always give us 5-10 extra minutes after the time limit was over. Homework assignments are a big part of grades but she gives you a week to do them. Lectures are important, in-class worksheets help & you write lots of notes. Course concepts can be heavy so make sure you study!

She's sweet and organized. You write your paper throughout the quarter so your final is just revising. She gives good feedback and opportunity for revisions which boost your score at the end of the quarter. The only thing I would say is her email times are very limited. If students are given a deadline, they should be on email around that deadline!

Dr. Galindo is fantastic. I'd take any of her classes again. She will work with you, just communicate. Missing class will definitely impact your grade on exams. She has in class assignments and does a lot of lecturing. Just looking at her slides will not help. If you take notes and attend class, you will succeed. She is knowledgable and passionate.
Very good professor, she has a passion for what she teaches and is very understanding. I highly recommend taking any of her classes!
Very nice and understanding professor, fair with homework

To be fair, I didn't really put a lot of effort into the class because it's note a core class for my program. I didn't like the class itself, but she is a great professor. She's super kind and understanding - always willing to help. She's a good grader too! I just didn't like the course content because I'm not a science person, lol

She is a very sweet woman, she is sort of an easy grader, but the content was hard. She definitely made the class as easy as it could be, but I hate scientific writing. If you had to pick, definitely pick her. Im not an advanced writer but I got more than 90% in all my writings. Super easy to pass, but attendance MATTERS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very clear with everything that is needed and expected in class. I just love the way she teaches and to make sure she keeps the class entertaining but we also still learn something. She is very considerate and cares so much about her students. Loveeee her!

Professor was really nice and clearly is passionate about class content. Two exams, two very simple group projects, and 4 homework assignments. Come to class and take notes and you should be fine. My only issue was the exams often had questions that were not on review and that I was not expecting. I still got a great grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Galindo has a great sense of humor, & is no stranger to cracking jokes during lectures. Also, she uses lots of visuals on her slides which are extremely helpful. She is one of the most engaging profs I've taken, & her lectures fly by because they're honestly so fun. Only downside of this class was the about 30 page readings before each class.

One of the best Prof's I've had at UWB. Great lecturer, very engaging and thoroughly explains concepts. Homework and reading are reasonable. Take her if you're on the fence about it. Do the reading and read/ do all the other stuff she tells you to (videos, etc.) and you will get a good grade.

Dr. G is amazing!! First professor I've connected with & she is so supportive! Her intro to oceanography has 4 HW assignments, 2 exams, 2 presentations, & in-class assignments. You don't NEED the textbook BUT it will help give background information before lecture. She is super helpful in class & in office hours; also is EXTREMELY smart/passionate!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, easy access to powerpoints & gives many chances to learn and make mistakes, solid professor if you are interested in the environment or oceans!

I really loved prof Galindo. She is so nice and so unbelievably smart. This class was super interesting and fun to learn about. For a 100 level class it is definitely a lot to learn. There are 4 hw assignments every other week, midterm, & exam. They are fairly difficult but fine if you pay attention & take notes. Highly recommend her & this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Galindo is a really nice person. Her lectures do not have a lot of notes, and she is kind of confusing in regards to course work. There was a lot of group work, pop quizzes, and the exams were also extremely difficult. You will need to show up every day if you intend to pass her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. G is very passionate in teaching and she wants her students to success. Writing assignments and peer review due every week. But she'll let you revise before receiving final grades. She gives helpful feedbacks and also helps students outside of class with their papers.

An interesting class that goes very in-depth about climate change. Professor Galindo was very nice and caring. She makes sure her students are respected and passes if you put in the effort of course. 2 tests (you get a notecard front and back), a couple of pop quizzes about textbook reading and 2 group presentations. Not difficult at all. Good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Galindo is very passionate about the topics she teaches. She's very knowledgeable and approachable making it easy for students to talk to her.
Excellent teacher, cares about students and puts in effort to make sure the material is understood.
She is a great teacher, but really heavy work load for a 100 level class. 6 quizzes, 2 exams, and 2 presentations. If you go to class everyday, you pretty much would pass in this class.
Dr. Galindo was great for scientific writing. Very straightforward on her expectations, and on the feedback she gives. Her lectures are a little repetative, but the class was pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class. Just do the work and show up for peer review days and will get an easy A. Super amazing professor though. Very caring and helpful. Also helps that shes gorgeous too.

She's great but the work for this course is ALOT. I missed class often & it's starting to really affect my grade so be cautious. Procrastination will kill your grade in this class so if you're a big procrastinator STEER CLEAR. The HW can't be done in one day. But she's organized & a great teacher. If I wasn't such a bad student I'd take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I must clarify, there are ONLY 5 extra credit points! She is great and tells you everything that is expected. Of course, she does not 'baby' you, but even in this 300 level class, she reminds you of dates and gives you LOTS of tips on how to ace her quizzes (95% of the class gets 10/10 points each time). Exams are straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at UWB. Great and informative lectures. She's variable knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches. Clear grading criteria and actually useful in class activies.

I'd say she's fair grader, her lectures are helpful. Readings are lengthy, but she allows you to use notes for pop reading quizzes, a note card is allowed during the 2 exams. Many group work, and that is where you get your attendance aka participation points :) the 2nd exam is easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Great professor you can tell she is passionate and knowledgeable. Make sure you show up to class and do the readings and you will be golden! She is a fair grader and gives informative feedback, her lecture slides could be bit more specific since we do in-class stuff that is not on there listed on there. I would take her again... plus shes hot!

Heather is an amazing professor. She makes sure that you understand the concepts as well as what's going on through out the course. Make sure to do the readings due to pop quizzes and participation. She is extremely organized and inspiring since she is passionate about what she teaches! I'd love to take another class from her!!

Long lectures and if you aren't science-inclined (like me) it could be difficult. She's a fair grader and does everything she can to help you best as you can. Lots of reading but she is very clear of what she wants. Awesome professor

She's a new prof as of Fall 2015. Very understanding of the college life. We have 6 pop quizzes where she does give us hints when she'll give them out. Readings are essential because of group discussion during class. Her tests are a bit hard but the topic was interesting & she makes it interesting. She's very open minded & very easy to talk to.
don't take her courses. waste of time.

She doesn't record her lectures, but at least she's able to clear up anything confusing. She does work with you and if you need any accommidation she's give it to you within reason. Her exams are based on her lectures, and she is very lecture heavy. Overall, I would take her again.
Very unprepared and would often get confused mid-lecture. The class itself is good and covers important topics, but her delivery of the material was very poor.
Memorize a lot for the tests. Participation in class discussion is required.
changed the syllabus during week 8 in favor of pop quizzes that are 50 points each. midterm was due during thanksgiving break. literally trash.

No textbook needed as he said "these books for international marketing aren't even helpful", fun lectures and he tells great stores. He's enthusiastic and very experienced. Simple lectures with slides to go along

Toxic! Although his lecture is fun and informative, his quizes are totally away from 'LOGIC'. You cannot learn from the lecture or the textbook to answer some of his questions. He always quote, 'I'm old. You should figure this out. I am the customer. You need to .....'
Great prof! Interesting lectures, great sense of humor, and good information! Would definitely take again!

To educate means to develop the powers and facilities of someone by teaching.  Dr. Barnett does an exemplary job of doing just that. If you have an opportunity to take his class, do so.  At the end of the last class of the semester, my class have him a round of applause.
I wish I could take more classes from Gerald, he is one of the best instructors I've ever had.

P. Barnett likes to talk a lot. Some of the topics he talks about are relative, some aren't. Coming to class is part of your participation grade.  He allows revisions of papers up until the last day of the quarter. Offers a lot of help. 1 major paper w 4 1-pg essays and small participation assignments. Overall a well-rounded class in terms of work

Smart guy. Tries to remove contrived constraints as a lesson in ethics, but also to open up learning-options. All I can say is it worked for me. Very vivid memories of valuable information. Verbify those sentences! He works through a lot of information so his sense of humor is appreciated.

He is a nice guy but confusing with what he expects from you on papers. Willing to talk with students. However, he is a tough grader and marks you done points for the smallest things. Allows revisions. Aka be his friend and make revisions. Classes are confusing- he talks about random things. Easy class until you start papers and he grades them.

He was ok overall, but often confusing and unclear on assignments and projects. He tries to get students to do something unique and original, which is great, but doesn't really help out at all, so most people just end up confused and not doing well on any of the assignments. And just when you thought you understood, he'll change everything around.
Very very unclear about assignments and tasks. Demands a lot from the students but does not give clear instructions as to what to do. Do not recommend this teacher.

He's the king of rabbit trails! He spends almost all the class time just jabbering on about random things, but he's entertaining to listen to. Didn't really learn much, but he's very helpful on assignments that initially seem confusing if you don't ask for help. He usually just wants you to do something creative and will grade according to effort.
Gerald is a fantastic instructor.

He is very passionate about teaching and matters outside of what we may generally learn in another writing class. He focuses on the fundamentals of sentence structure. Some students refuse to understand this, thinking they know what a writing course "should" be like. He is very dry but if you pay attention you do pick up on some interesting things.

Very hard to understand and isn't clear about what is desired on papers. Very passionate about his subject, although spends more time ranting (off subject) than teaching. Try to avoid taking his class, but if you have to - be sure to stay on his good side and keep in contact with him so you know EXACTLY what he wants on projects!

He is a nice teacher. Very patient and give lots to chances to revise and improve writing and score. Class itself is dry and boring and it is not structured but he provides lot of help if you ask for it. Good experience overall.
Dr. Barnett is an amazing teacher. At our final class of the quarter, my section applauded him. Highly recommend for people who are interested in expanding their minds and learning how to think.

Horrible. Completely unclear about what he wants from his students and will go on tangents for 2 hours yelling at the students because we aren't doing what he wants BUT HE WONT TELL US. I went from being an A writer to a C- writer in this class. Because of him.
Very unclear. Wasting time and money.
