LOVED THIS CLASS!!!  I'm not a science major so this was perfect!!  I loved how easy he put the terms and how friendly he was.  He was always wanting to make sure all students understood!!!  The field trips were so much fun!

You don't need the book. His lectures may put you to sleep but its exactly what's on the test. The SECOND PART of his class is HARD. Don't procrastinate lit review, BELIEVE ME! He tries to scare you in the begining but don't worry, its easy. Best part: nice guy. Worst part: no extra credit and the lit review. Just attend class w/an energy drink.

Excellent teacher but his teasts and grading style are harsh. Even though you may know the material, you risk  loering your GPA according to how he's feeling when he grades your work. Learn a lot,  but may get a c or lower for A work. won't take him again.
Excellent professor and very knowledgeble

Alan is a very kind professor who clearly cares about your success and isn't afraid to ask questions that will push students. Hardworking in how he brings in new industry professionals every week, honest in his feedback, and knows what he's talking about. If you show up to class, do your interviews, and contribute to your team, you get an EASY 4.0

Alan is the kind of professor who treats students like early-stage founders. He pushes you to think clearly, execute fast, and learn from the market instead of theory. He gives honest feedback, expects real effort, and genuinely cares about whether you grow. If you want a class where you can build something real, take Alan! 🔥

This is a good class. The professor is knowledgeable, and it's enjoyable that there are investors and you can learn various tools for programming and building businesses. Grading is challenging because of all the activities in every class, so it takes a lot of time, but overall the course is good.
The professor is very approachable, offers support outside class, and shares lots of real world examples of running a business. I learned from many experienced guest speakers. Very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class isn't difficult conceptually, but it requires a lot of time and effort. You basically build a startup from an idea, form teams, and submit daily assignments. It's very hands-on, with constant pitch deck work, ending in a real investor presentation. Interesting but demanding

Unclear grading. Very impressive outside investors from different backgrounds.
Clear Agile framework implemented in class.

Lots of exposure to industry grade tools (Retool, Figma, Azure DevOps, etc.) .
Very disorganized, but very available and hard working prof.

If you want a situation where 30% of your grade is determined by an unfair schema, where 'by design' each member gets around 65%, pick Alan! Likewise the guy's idea of fairness is to allow group members to select out-group sacrifices to take a massive grade hit. 

Would super not recommend, whatever you think you'll get form this class; you won't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're not genuinely interested in startups or building your own business, this class might not be for you. The professor is passionate and experienced, brings in industry experts and investors, and gives a real taste of launching a business. I realized entrepreneurship is something I want to pursue.

It's takes a lot of team effort to do good, but you actually get to learn on how to developed a product and pitch it to “investors”. It is lecture heavy and team evaluation will tank your grade if you aren't contributing to the team. However, the prof does give out a lot of opportunities for extra credit and you can pass easily with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class required a lot of teamwork, which was challenging at times, especially when working with people from different majors and work styles. Since much of the grade depended on group effort, it could be frustrating. Still, the professor's concepts were strong and showed real expertise. Overall, the content made the effort worthwhile. Overall.

This was genuinely the best class experience I have ever had. Professor is very genuine, and really wants to see all his students succeed. He pushes you to make something real and tangible. He spends so much extra time outside of class giving help and feedback, and treats each team like a real business. Brings in industry experts to give insight.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had an A- the entire quarter until the last day where one single assignment plummeted it down to a failing grade. The class is basically set up in a way that does not allow you to succeed. Professor refused to listen to student feedback as others have had this same problem. Do not take if you want to graduate on time.

This class was honestly one of the most frustrating experiences I've had at UW. The entire grade depends on a couple assignments that are structured in a way where getting full credit is basically impossible. There's no clear rubric no consistency and when students asked for clarification the answers were either vague or came way too late to matter

Entire grade is dependent on one assignment, and that one assignment is set up in a way where you can't get full credit. Makes no sense, impossible to have a good grade in this class no matter how hard you try. Threw off my entire graduation plan and left me no room to improve the grade so I could graduate on time.

The teacher had only one assignment, which was a customer interview, and the rest were daily activities, plus a few group presentation assignments. There was no structure to the class; I genuinely despised having to wake up and waste two hours of my life in this horrendous class.

If my graduation relied on this professor I'd rather skip a whole quarter and not take him. No system and his grading makes no sense. No way you can get an A in this class. Delusional professor can't believe he still has a job.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very cool professor, The class topic was interesting and you even get to develop a product throughout the class and present to real investors at the end of the quarter. I would recommend this class if you could make it to lectures.

class is about developing your product with a group. you need to come to class to do the daily activity, and hes lectures alot. its pretty cool how he brings people that do startsups and such. Those people will judge ur presentation out of 10 evry other week, & those score will average out in the end. need to pay attention or he will cold call you.

This class missed the mark. It's “Business Development,” but feels taught by someone who's never built a successful business. Endless lectures, zero real-world work. If you're late, prepare to be roasted. You'll learn more about awkward silences than entrepreneurship. YouTube > this class.

This professor is a terrible teacher. He has no structure, constantly goes off-topic to talk about his own businesses, and barely teaches the material. He singles out students, creating a tense atmosphere, and it's clear he cares more about himself than actually helping anyone learn.

The teacher lacks structure and often goes off-topic, mostly talking about business without connecting it to what we're learning. Class time is focused too much on lectures, and we rarely get to do hands-on work. I wish there was more organization and more chances to actually apply what we learn in class.

I've never seen a teacher less focused on teacher. His only goal throughout the whole class is to catch someone who isn't paying attention and try to humiliate them. The assignment are super vague and the over class structure looks like it was made by a toddler. Honestly if you don't have to, don't take this class at all.

Outside investors from different backgrounds rate your presentations (great), lots of exposure to industry grade tools (Retool, Figma, Azure DevOps, etc.) (great), hands on group work and work flow (great), full class discussion and inclusion (great). Very disorganized, unreasonable quizzes and time constraints. First time teaching, understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great person but incredibly difficult. You need to understand these topics to the point where you could teach them to students like a professor if you want a 4.0. Also, your first midterm is 30% of your grade and the second 35%. Good luck on the midterms because they're pretty difficult. Try attending office hours and actually spend time reading.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good luck

Do not take his class, he puts questions on the exam that he does not cover in class and that you have to understand in depth to get them right. You can find them in the book... if you read completely everything and understood completely everything. I did not understand the word he said, because he is hard to understand when he speaks.

Oh god, run as far as humanly possible from this class. Prepare for slow, insufficient  lectures that fail to prepare you for impossibly hard quizzes.  Pair that with an incredibly unintuitive online quiz configuration, and this is THE WORST professor I've ever had. Props for being a nice guy, but that doesn't quite cut it.

Shankar is great. Knows finance very well. The bad posts here are due to student's unwillingness to properly prepare themselves. Finance is difficult conceptually and you should expect to spend a considerable amount of time on this class. Most student's come to class unprepared, which is folly.
Tbh, you could learn more by not showing up to class. Exams are hard to study for, because his practice exams contain irrelevant questions. 0/10 would not recommend

He is one of the worst teachers I have had. He seems easy in the beginning but once the midterm comes around you are screwed. He jumps around in his lectures and doesn't teach the concepts mostly just the equations. He expects us to teach ourselves the concepts. The exam is ridiculous and nothing like what you go over in class. do not take him!

He is not teaching at all. His exams are out of context. He is not helpful if you have any questions. He does not even listen to you as if he is always in a hurry. If you want good grades. Don not take his class. He is a horrible teacher. I got the lowest grade in my business prerequisite courses
Shankar is one of the best professors that I have come across at UWB.  Funny, clear, helpful, and very intelligent.  Take his class for finance if you ever have a chance!

Gowri is a good teacher dont get me wrong, but 70% of your grade is off two tests. Most instructors are in the 50-60%. If you struggle at exams you might want to take the class with another finance teacher. Most of his grades are 3.5 and above or 2.3 and below. You either get the material or you dont

He is a good professor. His test are not that hard but you have to do your homework and study. He is funny and in class very helpful. If you put your part you should be fine. I will like to take more classes with him. Very fair.

He does a good job of going through how to solve problems, his quizzes are extremely easy if you keep up with the homework.  His exams are a little intimidating, but really aren't that hard.  Once he throws in the curve it should be pretty easy to get a 3.5-3.8 if you just read and do the homework.
Great teacher, my best one yet here at the UW

Finance isn't an easy class, but Shankar makes it a subject that's easy to understand.  He has an accent, but not something too extreme.  Teaches fast, but there's tons of material to cover.  Quizes and exams are much like HW problems; but he spicens some up because it's a test, DUH.  Very good teacher.  Recommended.
The course is tought, the teacher teaches it really fast. He's not helpful even if you ask for extra help, as he does not have time. My recommendation is, do not take him.

Read the assignments, do the homework, pay attention in class, and ask when you don't understand something.  You'll do well.  Exams are mostly easy problems from the homework, with a couple of thoughtful kickers at the end.  Uses the highest exam score instead of max points in the exam to calculat % scores.

Horrible teacher, doesn't speak clearly, participation doesn't necessarily matter. His tests are very difficult and he doesn't make an attempt to help if you express that you are having trouble. I would rate him one of the worst at UWB, please take Tilden instead. Ron is awesome!!
makes exams really hard to push students
Tests are basically repeats of homework problems. Do the optional homework and you will succeed with ease. Good guy - willing to be flexible to accommodate schedules of students. Decent curve too!

WOW. this guy doesn't use powerpoint at all. all his lectures are by hand, has a very hard to understand accent. some people liked it, some didn't. his tests are NOTHING like his papers. not fair at all. hard class overall.

The only downside is you will be provided with a sheet that has generic formulas rather than having your own note card of formulas & own notes. This is a great professor though. He's very quick at replying to questions you email him with. Also, he does a great job clarifying concepts when you ask him questions.  Course moves fast, no room for slack
Great teacher! Very fast-paced class. If accounting isn't your strength you should avoid this class. Each class we studied a long chapter and we never had time for exam reviews.

Take this class with understanding the cost accounting. The class is very tense and require a lot of self studing. The teacher explains the material very fast, and his exams are much harder than lectures.

Excellent professor! Was extremely helpful, supportive, and took the time to make sure everyone understood the concepts before moving on. Easy to approach for help. Shows a passion for educating. Sympathetic to students who are responsible and show interest. Has very helpful group quizzes that can boost a low grade. Highly recommended!
Not very helpful. Lecture is boring.
loved him!
Good anough

Unless you are interested+comfortable in working with math, you may be disappointed with your grade.  He is pretty clear, and gives practical examples to some models.  The pace was a bit faster than I was comfortable with.  The exams are on the longer side. The highlight of my experience was the info on practical usage for models.

Model prof. I had to travel for work, missed a lot of class and finished at the top of the class because he took the extra time to help me. If you initiate the contact, his time is your time. Very smart but knows how to transfer knowledge to his students. One of the best!
great professor but tough class

The material was difficult, but Shankar took the time to teach it effectively. Always friendly in class, came to the quarterly reception to meet students and always had a friendly greeting when passing students in the halls. Profs like this are one of the reasons UW Bothell is a great environment to learn in.
GREAT PROFESSOR! Smartest person ever!
He is very fatherly and takes the class slow.
No Comments

Probably one of my favorite teachers at UWB.  He is really nice and helpful.  I always see him helping students out of class, in the lobbies with their work.  He has a good way of teaching material that would be otherwise hard to understand.

Gowri is just a real nice guy. I have never done well in econ classes, so this course was a bit tough for me, but my classmates did well. There were quizzes here and there and tests were not too difficult.
super easy A and easy class. Homework is just reading LONG articles and answering questions. lectures were a little boring as it was just her rambling for hours.
Great professor. This class was very manageable as long as you kept up with the assignments. If you followed the instructions and completed the work on time, it was very possible to earn full points.
I learned absolutely nothing but she was nice so it was worth it.
Easy class, nice professor, love it.
So nice!!! Take her if you can.
Easy class, take it if you need the credits, not if you want to learn something. There is one group project at the end of the quarter.

Professor Griffin's Israel/Palestine Conflict class was super interesting but also very easy. Not easy because of the material but because it was super straightforward. I found her to be a great wealth of knowledge on the subject, and very kind.
Professor Griffin was ok. The class was easy but still interesting, and she was very nice. The material is important.
Braindead class. Material was part propaganda and part regurgitation of the news. Everything was so easy.
Teach us like we're in college, not preschool, please.
Easy useless class. She doesn't lecture and doesn't really teach us anything useful.
If you want a 4.0, take her. You'll probably learn nothing, waste your tuition money, etc. but you'll have a 4.0! She seems nice but cannot teach in an organized way.

This is the easiest class at UWB. Probably the easiest TEACHER given the other reviews. She is terrible at her job and the whole class had to suffer. I took this for my major and I don't think I learned anything. Those earlier reviews are either herself or a bot.
Easy class, just not a good class AT ALL.
Easy class. There's no way to not get a 4.0 in this class unless you're braindead. Prof is not a good lecturer.

This class is a joke. Really self-involved lectures, she doesn't make material accessible and chooses topics that suit her interests over what best fits the course. There is an overwhelming amount of readings, some of which seem unrelated to the class. She didn't really put any effort into grading (all pass/fail until final). Don't take her.
Don't bother with Prof. Griffin. Her class is way too easy that it's not even an intellectual challenge. I think most of the class got over 100% since she has so many extra credit assignments.

Nice teacher, but for a fully asynchronous online class, this class was not the best fit. I think a lot of the readings and materials would be better when discussed in-person. Canvas page is a mess. I'd take her in-person or synchronously.
Interesting class even if it was really easy. Instructor did a good job generating discussions about the materials and provided very useful examples to clarify concepts.

I appreciate her class and the way she grades. Based more on critical thinking and understanding than just memorization. You can easily pass her class and get a good grade on assignments by just doing the readings, participating, and listening to your classmates. There's 2 extra credits, one due by mid-term and one due by the end of the quarter.

The Zoom format ruined this class. Professor Griffin is nice but NOT suited well for online teaching. Lectures were awesome, and she was helpful when you needed it, but the Canvas page organization was the worst way a teacher has ever done it -- everything's due in a different place and it's hard to keep track.

Professor Griffin is ineffective and incompetent. She seems like a nice lady, but should not be teaching a law class. Her lectures are basically pointless because she can't stay on topic for more than 3 seconds, the homework doesn't relate to the readings, and her Canvas page is a mess. That said, this is the easiest class I've ever taken.

Prof. Griffin is nice and probably the easiest teacher at UWB in terms of grading. There's not only quite a bit of extra credit, but almost everything is graded on completion. It does center around group participation in class, but she makes it slightly tolerable.

If you like group work and active participation, this class is the right fit for you. Griffin is organized, kind, and a very engaging lecturer, and she posts lecture slides before class which is really nice. The only work aside from weekly group activities is weekly written responses that are 1-2 paragraphs and two longer writing assignments.

Easy but straightforward class/professor. A lot of reading, but not boring and she goes over them in a way that makes them memorable by applying them to contemporary human rights/political issues. Weekly group activities graded on attendance/completion. She is very understanding and it's easy to do well in her class.
She is really kind and understanding but sometimes her lectures are hard to follow through. Her grading is very clear and there are no quizzes nor exams.

Prof. Griffin is extremely approachable, interesting to listen to, and really cares about students' learning and how she can support them. This specific class is easy because the content is very straightforward - no hard readings, no unnecessarily busy work - and she's really organized on Canvas. Hidden gem of UWB right here.
She was really caring and understanding, and the class content was really interesting. Lets you input your opinion in class discussions, and does not discredit you.

She has been a very friendly and engaging teacher who really loves, and wants, to see students succeed. Moderate amounts of reading, overall very manageable. A large portion of your grade is solely based on submitting the work, so just try and you will get an A.

If you put even the smallest amount of effort and care even a little about the class, you will get an A. She is very nice. Participation is very important for the student-made Google Slides, they take up a lot of points.

One of the best teachers I have had yet. She is extremely kind, informational, organized, patient, and engaging all at once. I loved the class's focus and I felt very motivated all throughout the quarter. She's a really great teacher!

Dr. Griffin is extremely kind and inspirational, and she works hard to make sure all her students feel welcome in class. She opens your eyes to a lot of important issues, and the class makes you think and reflect on your own life and experiences. Would recommend taking any class she teaches.

Prof. Grifin is amazing and has a desire to share information with students regarding human rights and law. She is kind and heartfelt. Readings are hard but still doable because of the interesting assignments and engaging discussions. Take her if you have any interests in law, human rights, history, etc.
The readings are very challenging and hard to understand. The homework is a good level, it just takes forever because you are answering questions from the readings. The professor is really nice

Prof. Griffin is very knowledgeable and does a great job at lecturing and leading class discussions. She comes off as opinionated sometimes, but she backs up her arguments really well and can be engaging and fun occasionally. Grading criteria are outlined and very clear. She really values effort and participation! I took BIS 353 and 414 with her.

I loved Professor Griffin's Media & Law class. She is EXTREMELY nice and approachable, she cares about effort over quality, and her lectures always make the class interesting and helped me understand the readings and assignments better. The low ratings are just salty for one reason or another, don't listen to the haters because she is awesome.

She is the most amazing teacher. Her lectures were amazing, her readings were interesting, and she was just straight up a nice person. There's a lot of reading and work but it's not very hard work, however, she wants to see you work hard if that makes sense. This teacher is all about showing the most effort and critical thinking.

She had good quality lectures. I didn't like that part of your grade is based on participation; she has favorites and she tends to pick on them making it harder to participate. She was rude to me often for no reason. Going to her class gave me anxiety based on how she interacted with me. She was nice to the students she likes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor.
She is wonderful. As with seemingly every other class at UW Bothell there will be group projects though.
She was a great professor, would highly recommend.

As a woman, I found it offensive when she claimed that she cares about the plight of minorities. She has no life experience to back up that claim. Simply put, she is a phony. She told me that she barely passed law school. SOC is all she had to save face. She has my sympathy.

Shes not a lawyer which makes sense once you take her class. I initially thought she was in the wrong room. BIS 283 (Intro to Law) with Maryam is less about law and more about her showing off her PHD in Sociology. The class is largely graded based on a final group project. Boring class. Not a lot of learning. I blame UWB for the failure.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor went to law school and knows her stuff but doesn't make you feel like you're talking to a lawyer and as if shes smarter than you & knows EVERYTHING (like some professors do). Very easy to talk to and likes to have fun in class while getting things done. Recommend her for all levels (100-400 classes)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Shes a great teacher, she is really interested in you learning. Only some difficult reading but the rest are at average level.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Griffin is an amazing teacher. She assigns some hard readings just to help develop your reading skills, and then goes over them in class about the main argument and continues to be very precise on word choice and information she gives you. The class is also especially funny and gives tons of leisure room to goof off and enjoy the class.
She's honesty amazing. She did give us a lot of long readings, but they were really fun and she went over them in class so we could actually understand them

Professor Griffin is very nice, caring and is really passionate about human rights. This class definitely was overwhelming with the amount of readings, but we go over them in class which helps. I took this class for an elective credit, so it doesn't have much to do with my major. She is super awesome and sweet but this class is somewhat tough.

Dr. Groom is great. 
Her BES 312 Ecology course at the EERC is simple, fun, and informative. 
Attend labs and submit work on time and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy class, very light work, and the most time I spent on an assignment was twenty minutes. She's very passionate about what she's teaching, but her B-Core is very rudimentary and if you have basic knowledge on climate change it will feel non-challenging and boring. Professor Groom is EXTREMELY nice though.

I learned so much from her class about climate change. She is a very easy grader although the assignments can be hefty. I think the content and enrichment from her lessons offset the work load. I wouldn't call her B CORE class an easy A. If you're a freshman, its easy to make friends because of lot of group work opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I love Professor Groom! There is a lot of reading and mini assignments but it is manageable and very relevant. I learned so much this quarter and even though you might not be interested in the topic, she makes it very interesting and fun! She gives amazing feedback to every assignment and really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Groom's BIS 300 class Fall Quarter of 2019. She is a really caring professor, and she brings a LOT of chocolate to class! There is quite a bit of writing, and some of the course material is a little dense, but she is really supportive and fast with answering questions. I definitely recommend her BIS 300 class!

I took her BIS300 course prior to taking BIS459, and loved both of the courses. She is not the easiest grader, but she is fair and will provide you with detailed feedback and will guide you towards success. For the first half of the quarter, it was lecture heavy, but the latter half was a group project. She will work with you and help you do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Gives good feedback--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She answers her emails frequently and will respond fast! She's not exactly the toughest grader I've seen but she will give you an appropriate amount of feedback on your assignments. It's a little challenging to understand the criteria for some of her assignments but overall, great teacher!

Probably the most caring professor ive had! She also knows what shes doing. And gave us lots of dark choco! I never write about professors but she was really great! Also, the class is very laid back. But you really have to show up to class.

I took BIS300 and BES485. I think she is a great person that means well. Expect a lot of smaller assignments. She gets flooded by the end of the quarter with grading. Overall I'd definitely recommend her and her content is fairly interesting. Preferred the BIS300 curriculum to the 485.

Martha really cares about her students and it shows. She is accommodating and knows that students have outside lives. There are clear expectations and assignments. This class was amazing and I feel like I got a lot out of it because I put a lot in to it. Excellent professor, excellent class!

For anyone looking at potential electives before graduation, Conservation Biology BES 485 is a fantastic course. Martha Groom is a great professor with a wonderful personality. This class goes beyond conservation ideas - it ties in stakeholders, funding, and a unique devil's advocate approach to conservation solutions. Thanks for the great quarter!

This class was very atypical in structure. No formal tests what-so-ever (not complaining), and attendance didn't matter (still not complaining). She was very willing to help and clarify anything, and was easy to reach with questions. The final was a community project or a case study (I did a study).
Awesome professor. Very understanding and laid back. She knows her course very well. Two thumbs up!

Fantastic course! Martha is an awesome professor who is excited about the material and wants everyone to succeed. +1 for choosing a LOW COST textbook. Lots of reading, but I learned a ton in this introspective class. Stellar prof!

Dr. Groom is a great instructor and cares more than almost any instructor about the subject matter that she teaches.  The class that I took focused on oil and its role in the US and the world.  I learned a lot and enjoyed the whole quarter.
I had little interest in this class but Prof. Groom made it incredibly profound and filled with depth.
Lots of reading, lots of work, super teacher.  Really wants you to succeed, and tells you what you need to do to get there.
Martha is THE coolest & cutest prof. chick on campus.  LOTSA material to read, but she makes the class fascinating.  Would DEF. take her class again.  Magic Martha :)
Martha is a lovely professor that tried her best to make sure every individual coule succeed. She was very encouraging to our class.

Is science not your thing, but they say ya gotta?  Than ya gotta gota Martha!  Science made fun, if not exactly easy.  But what do you want, the moon?  Martha will go eco-crazy on ya, so go crazy on Martha!
my favorite professor so far here.  she is incredibly helpful and very clear when she lectures.  and she's cute.
MANDATORY science course which could be a drag, but fortunately Martha was funny, encouraging, and very clear.
No Comments
We love Martha!

I'm conflicted. She is a nice teacher. But, it is a "read the textbook class". First day of class, no warning, she made it virtual, meeting 6 times whole quarter to do group activities (waste of time but graded). Most of her prerecorded lectures were useless/ from dif class as the exams are on the textbook. But, Ez A+, only spent 2-3 hours per week
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Lasker is outstanding. I just graduated and out of all the prof. Ive had she is one of my top 3. She is enthusiastic, knowledgeable, easy to talk to and an all around great person. She has inspired me to be a better student and Ill never forget her. If you have the chance to take a class with her DO IT, you will not regret it!

Honestly my favorite professor so far. Nutritional science was fun bc of her, and she clearly stated that she doesn't want us to "memorize" anything but just have basic understanding. Overall easy class but there's a lot to read from textbook/powerpoints. Also labs+program needed are 110 dollars (price doesn't include textbook,I found mine online)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Grace Lasker is an amazing teacher who really cares about your education. She loves what she teaches and makes sure all students understand the material before moving on. Although attendance is not mandatory she grades participation and you cannot make it up. I highly recommend this teacher !

Professor Lasker is a sweetheart and cares about all of her students success. Very passionate about what she teaches, and has hands on experience which makes it 100x better. Few quizzes and discussion posts on interesting topics, usual midterm and final, and final group project which isnt too hard. Took this class as an elective and recommended!

The sweetest professor at UWB! Wish I could take more classes with her as her teaching style was very unique and engaging. The class was overall really easy but required students to actively participate. We had a few quizzes, about 4 discussions, and a group project! If you're interested in Public Health, this class will be a breeze.

She is the best professor at UWB. She is understanding and wants you to do your best. She will give you a great score if you follow her discussion requirements, like using APA citations and as long as she sees that you are putting in your BEST work. I learned a lot in her class and would take her again in a heart beat. She answers all your question
Easily the best bcore teacher you could take. Loved her got a 4.0 in the class fairly easy just show up to class since she doesn't allow make up work.

She is the absolute best, super nice, cares both about students and the subject and whether you got it, really knows what she's doing, and makes sure you learn. I was never bored in her lectures, they're lit. I somehow learned all the course content and also learned life lessons while at it. She's invigorating to talk to, and is easy to reach.

She's out-going, passionate about public health, and she wants her students to succeed. Class time was spent on lectures and group activities. The course was a hybrid: 4 big canvas posts, online quizzes, group project and presentation, online midterm/final, and occasional extra credit. Wish it were more lecture-based instead of class activities.
Super easy class, no grades just cr/nc this was for the pathways to health studies requirements. Shes VERY optimistic and Id like to take her for a 5 credit course. Dont stress this course AT ALL!

Dr. Lasker is amazing. She really wants and helps every student succeed. She is available for help when needed and her lectures are anything but dull!! That being said, I believe it is quite easy to get an A if you're actually interested in the material and genuinely put the effort in. 50% hybrid class so many (interesting) discussions online.

Loved Trevor Griffey's class and would have taken more classes with him if I could have. His breadth of knowledge is expansive and the lectures were very interesting. I particularly liked learning about Conservative Thought and Movement because that's just me, but if you aren't into that subject, it can get confusing. He's very kind and helpful too
His class and the material was interesting. He's very nice and will help clear up any confusion. He is a tough grader when concerning essays though. Besides that, everything else was good.

Great guy and personality! He will help as long as you show up and show you get the work! Make sure to do all the readings and understand all the papers that are given!  Great teacher! Would take him again :)

Excellent professor. Relaxed discussion-based lecture. No exams, instead 3 unit papers and a final paper. political history, philosophical analyzation, and deep thought- professor's bias was apparent but not problematic. I hope to take him again, great prof!

Trevor is a pretty chill guy and he can talk on and on which can get dry since it was an early morning class. The class was based on Conservatism so the first part of learning old-english texts wasn't that great. As we progressed towards modern day conservatism, it became interesting! No tests or quizzes. Just 4 essays and a group presentation!

I dont understand why this professor has a decent grade on rate my professor. He should have a very low grade for the way he teaches. Essentially, you can learn everything he "teaches" online. Ask about him on campus, I doubt you will get any good responses. One of the worst classes I have ever taken.

WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD - seriouslyhe doesn't teach. If you have questions he asks other students for the answers half of the time and can not explain how to do things. I learned more from my peers than him. Class in primarily online and in-class group work, lots of busy work. Not worth taking!

If you want to learn something then you basically don't have to show up to class. The course is mainly online with HW embedded in to the book. you have to buy the program too but its cheap. if you go to class its just group work. the tests are nothing like the HW. I wouldnt take him again. I was lucky i got a decent grade.

Little to no lectures, the book is online & terrible. Entire course is group work, which is unhelpful and frustrating. The book doesn't help because the examples don't work for everyone. WORST CLASS EVER! Tell anyone on campus you have stats w Gray, they say "I'm soooo sorry!" Don't take this class!

The class was a great class but it definitely requires a lot of outside dedication.  Most of the class learning is online with class time used for explanationclarification of the material.  If you have a busy outside of school schedule I would be careful of what courses you taking it with as far as work load.
Good instructor

James was a great math teacher. He only had two exams and that is 60% of the grade and the other 40% is easy to get. In the beginning, I was worried about taking this class with him as the comments here are really bad but when i met him, he eased my worries. You do have to go to class though as he expects students to be very hands-on.

For me, I feel like I needed to be in class in order to learn anything because the classwork is what made the material familiar. Half the class is online and that is great and all, makes it easier, but it doesn't teach as well. He's great lecturing in class but when it comes to help online, almost useless. I rely on classmates to help vs. him.

He tends to put people in groups and have them work through the problems on hand outs while he walks around and answers questions. If you want to do the HW, you can't not get full credit. Online hw assignments only which can be answered until you get it right. Flexibility on when you turn in work (late passes) and super friendly. Hard yes, helpful!

I've had lots of math classes, but never Stats.  I loved this classprof.  I'll take more stats classes in grad school because it's interesting and useful.  Mr. Grade does not lecture much.  Class time is spending doing activities.  They are mostly good unless you're stuck with bad group.    There were many winers in my class which sucked!

James Gray admitted to the class that he knows that a majority of students hate the way he teaches, but he is going to continue to teach this way because the mean exam scores are apparently higher. I find it difficult to learn from him and wouldn't take him unless needed. That being said, he is extremely generous and willing to help.

James Gray is one of the worst professors I've taken. He is not clear with explaining stats, he reads packets aloud to the class and relies on this method to teach us versus him teaching us. The workload will consume your entire quarter, he makes a lot of mistakes when explaining, online, sending emails etc. Not adequate to teach.

Probably one of the worst class and professor I have ever taken at UW Bothell. I'm very disappointed with his style of teaching.  He gives so much homework and so many exams. The in class exam is so hard and there's also a long ass online portion of the exam that is super duper hard.  He's the type who expects you to learn on your own.

I like to think James is a nice guy, and he definitely tries to be helpful! However first all hw, quiz's etc. textbook and due on two opposite days of the class all online (you still have to meet every time) SO MUCH WORK! you're basically taking an online and in person class so unless you want to live and breathe stats don't take stats with him!

James makes the class pretty interesting and puts the material in context to the real world. Very nice guy and willing to help with homework or questions during office hours. No use of the text book at all everything is online. He makes you work hard but is a great prof!

I thought I'd had bad professors before, then I took James' class. He definitely takes the cake as the worst professor I have ever had. He does not teach; he relies on the online textbook to do that for him. You basically teach yourself. He doesn't answer questions and his lectures are painfully embarrassing. He should only be an online teacher.
Very engaging and caring professor. He still makes a point to come talk to me and catch up four years later. Loved the DC1 I took wish him and wish I could have taken more.

Had Gray for an intro course, pretty simple stuff. Regardless, Gray is an amazing prof. If you are looking for someone who will challenge your way of thinking (not to his way but in general) then take a class with Gray. He is the kind of Prof that will have you leaving the class smiling and glad you came to class, btw you'll learn as well !
Great Prof and nice guy! Very approachable. I had him my first class as a freshman.  and i would definetly take a class from him again.
I thought he grades pretty hard for essays, but he was a pretty cool guy. Not too much work to do in the class. I would consider taking another class with him
His writing assignments are hard and challenging but people still sign up for his classes.  Wonderful classroom experience.  He is very funny.

Unclear grading rubrics and assignment details. Class isn't hard but you might get points taken off for something she claims was on the assignment that is nowhere to be seen. Overall I would take the class again but it was a little rough at times. She's really nice and provides pretty good feedback.
This class drags my grades down so I'm a little mixed feeling here...

An amazing professor all around a great human being that just wants to pass down their knowledge to the next generation. She's an amazing person to have a discussion with and has a wealth of knowledge not only from what she knows but she continues to keep learning new information and I find this to be quite inspiring. I highly recommend her classes
Really easy class with a really nice teacher. What's not to love?
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: A genuinely great person that I got to know through class. Easy workload with an emphasis on participation in class and just be present in the discussions.

A nice and knowledgeable professor with an interesting background: real-world experience in game design, museums, and other interactive media work. The best part of the class is the group projects, but the reading responses are not that hard either. She cares a lot about your learning. Overall, I had a really, really good experience in the class.

Honestly her class was really great, It was her Black Mirror class but shes honestly such a cool teacher. Her grading can be a bit wonky and is hard to reach outside of class, but if you ask her in person, shell be cool about it. Not a lot of homework, the final project and paper is kinda a lot at the end, but overall very fun and interesting.

I would take a class with her because she is nice, but I wouldn't take this specific course again. It was a prerequisite course for my initial choice of the IMD major before switching. This class was overall easy, just be in class and do the work. Projects (ex: group projects) are most of the grade. Friendly course for credit, not rigorous.

She started out the class seeming to be a very nice and helpful professor, but as the class goes on you realize shes more interested in being your friend than teaching you. Almost all of the grade is based on group projects and she gives no rubric or specific instructions for them. Most disappointing is she communicates very poorly outside class.

Wanda is really good person, her intentions are always to help her students and make sure they are ready for whatever career the students chose. while her classes do lack structure, the design problems we got were nothing more than fun and eye-opening! Overall I learned a lot!

At first, she seems like really laidback professor, but then you realize that she's not laidback, she's lazy. She doesn't really have any rubrics, any instruction or feedback she gives is super vague. Overall, I'm never satisfied with any of the classes I take with her. I'm sure there are other professors teaching dope subjects.

I have learned more about her and her backstory than any of the content I wanted to learn about. Has no rubrics for any papers (marked me down for non-existent errors) and gives awful, vague feedback. Lectures are long and poorly prepped/designed (ironic).

She gives no instructions or feedback. Grading criteria seems random and based on what she likes. She looks for anything to take off points from and marks off for things she never told you to do. You learn nothing in this class and get a bad grade. I was a straight 4.0 student before taking her. Workload is light, but she's power-tripping.

Wanda has been an inspiration and big help on not only pointing out how can I apply my communication, social skills, and writing skills but also encouraging people to be free to pursue their passion and helping them out. She's been a lot of great help and I would gladly take a class with her again if I could.

Some of the same things other have said: not organized; no lesson plan; makes you watch irrelevant videos; pretends to be tech savvy but doesn't uploads your grades onto canvas; not approachable; use buzzwords; vague instructions on assignments; illegible, unhelpful feedbacks; Obsessed with your final presentation being exactly 5 minutes.

I had no idea this class was going to be about video gaming. She is a very nice woman, but I felt like the class was very repetitive. It was hard to go to class every day because it was pretty boring. The papers are pretty easy if you follow the rubric she puts out. Participation is part of your grade but I didn't make it to every class.

I like the professor overall, however I often believe she's forgotten it's an intro course. Also, she reminds you often that you need to understand xyz to do xyz but we've yet to learn the ways we go about understanding anything! I feel that is a big fail on the course. We talk about the fact that people are fans but never analyze why!
Pretty easy and good teacher. Definitely recommend.

She has a background in lit, worked for a gaming co. and brings a different perspective to topics such as: technology and privacy. She enthusiastically will guide you to find topics that spark your interest for papers and presentations. In regards specifically to my class she structures her class organically to take you where your interest sparks.

She has a unique teaching style than most professors do and for the senior seminar class it is discussion based. She doesn't require you do to all the readings but expects a well written paper. Overall, she has an interesting perspective on technology/ social media /hackers / privacy etc. She is friendly and easy to talk to.
Poor use of class time. Vague on assignment guidelines. Learned a fair amount, but nothing incredibly useful.  Easy class overall.

An amazing class for those interested in the universes of video games, marketing, and social media. No textbooks were required. Readings were available online but it was clearly stated in her syllabus (and word of mouth) that these readings would not be required but would serve as another resource to students wanting to learn more. Great professor!

Wanda is the most passionate and knowledgeable teacher I have experienced in my two years at UW:B. She is the only critical game studies teacher with many many contacts in the gaming world. She worked at Wizards of the Coast before they were bought, and uses her knowledge to put you in contact with books and articles relevant to your interests.

Terrible professor! She was unorganized & had no lesson plan. Assigned readings were never once discusses in class--instead class time was spend talking about WOW, watching irrelevant videos,and watching her present the same powerpoint multiple times. I trust that she has knowledge of the subject manner however she has no teaching abilities. AVOID
Really funky. Friendly and nice. Not a difficult teacher at all. Missed tons of lectures and still got a 3.8

Wanda's background is in gaming and literature. Wanda makes class fun and interactive.  The readings & assignments are interesting. She expects papers to be well crafted, but her grades seem fair. This wasn't the class I expected, but I am glad I stuck with it. Students into gaming or Sci-fi like her classes.

BIS 179 was asynch, Gustafson had bad communication skills. It was obvious that she reused canvas assignments but did not update the instructions, so you had to guess what you were answering. Most things were graded by student graders who did not explain why you got the grade you got unless you pushed back. 

Workload was not bad, material was easy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was a whole lot of busy work. For an online elective class, I don't understand why there needs to be such harsh grading. Prof was nice but there's too much useless work and too much to read.

Taken this professor twice now, trying to meet requirements.... I should've looked for alt routes. She's awful. Her and Amy Elridge, her TA, are so harsh of graders that if I got full credit, I felt like it was a miracle. They would rip my submissions to shreds, nothing is perfect. It's so frustrating how heavy-handed the workload is as well.SMH
Strict deadlines, heavy reading, and expects cameras, all just for a college preparedness class. She really tries to force this as a weed-out class.

I hate how she requires you to turn on your camera. She nags at you until you turn it on and if not you will need a reason why it's off. Also lots of reading which we barely cover during class time. She thinks she is helpful but is not..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take this class, that is all lmao.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: literally all i have to say is dont do it. she says to do the best you are able and is one of the harshest graders ive had. literally nothing is good enough for her and she has a ta named amy who just docks points for no reason. i want to drop the class. the feedback is pretty okay but the ta and professor are mad nit picky. id stay away lmao.

Graded everything way too harshly. Took off 50% of points for work handed in even just a couple hours late, which is insane considering the workload. I'm a stem major so I guess I wouldn't know, but it also felt like way too much emphasis was being placed on formatting for an intro writing-based class. The prof also seems clueless regarding tech.

If you want a class that will be a challenge due to trick questions on tests, harsh grading, and an extreme workload, you should sign up! You will be expected to coordinate meetings outside of class for an asynchronous course. This professor did not respect my DRS accommodations, which made learning much more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had joined her class a week late into the quarter and she had made no accommodations to help me make-up for what I missed from not being registered yet. Also, she has group assignments for every class sessions and if you miss a class (even if you are sick and let her know that) she will make no accommodations for you to make anything up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Gustafin is actually so annoying. She is extremely nit picky about EVERYTHING. Its really annoying that no matter how much you try you will never be good enough for her. Please do not make the same mistake I did by taking this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I mean she's not terrible whatsoever. Yes, she is very nit-picky when it comes to grading, but not aggressively harsh. One thing to keep in mind is if you have taken a college readiness course, or something relevant, then this course will feel like a repeat for you/ Just keep that in mind.

i hate that this class is required, it is very useless to me i would rather just take an english class. Every assignment you do will always have some sort of comment that you didn't meet to her expectations. It sucks that this class is required for first year. Only upside is that this class is online show up for the first 6 weeks though.
I don't think anyone actually likes this professor unless they're delusional.

I think she's genuinely one of the worst. as many here have mentioned, she is SO nitpicky with grading... and she has docked points for things that she has asked us to include. also when she docks points she doesn't give a valid reason for why. no clear instructions. i think some higher-level profs really dont know how to teach - she's one of em.

Dr. Gustafson is very uncaring and vague when she grades assignments. I have had it happen to me multiple times where she messed up on grading something of mine properly! Make sure you double check the work shes graded. Also, she doesnt provide helpful feedbackit seems like everything she assigns she just expects you to complete w/ no guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Aside from the class being very boring, she comes off as very passive-aggressive in grading comments. The class is easy enough, just put in some effort and make sure to turn it in on time. She is very picky about things being turned in on time, doesn't matter if you message her in advance.

She takes a 3 credit class made for students to learn and reflect from there college experience and turns it into a philosophy class. She a hard grader and gives out homework with no direction plus she hard grader and marks you down for unreasonable things . Basically she is rigorous for no reason which takes away from your learning .
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Out of all the professors I have had at UWB, Professor Gustafson is the most challenging and hard to follow professor. Many instructions are extremely unclear and she will nitpick any of your assignments. She assigns heavy work and reading load as if you don't have other classes or work. If you asked me, I would say take any class without her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: trust me you will never want to take her class again, it is a 3 credits class make people feel it is 10 credits. she is not clear at all and a lot of work to do. You cannot learn anything through this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: assignments were never clear and micromanages students. lots of assignments

She is a very enthusiastic teacher who has real experience in her field. I trust that she either knows the answers to my questions or is happy to explain everything she can. She wants us to learn real experience in relation to journalism, although I wish we had more practice writing articles. She is so friendly.

Workload is HEAVY. Don't know how other teach this class, but the it can be up to 120 pages a week.  No way to make up full points if you miss class, even with advance notice. Can be tedious with way she wants things done. That said, she's interesting and invested in her students' success. Meet with her during office hours. Not a harsh grader.

Every single week there is an essay and an 40-90 pages of reading. Then in class there is a "contribution to knowledge" which is a stupid way of saying a quiz on wether you did the readings. So if you miss class, you miss points, and it brings your grade down fast. I missed two classes and had my grade go down about 5%! The work load igsoverwhelmin

If you don't show up, you lose your points for the day so if you don't go to class you will not pass. HEAVY reading load, 2-3 articles per day plus a worksheet to fill out on the readings. Followed by a quiz every class on those readings. Relates everything to journalism which is annoying since its supposed to be a core class.

Such an awesome professor. Ive taken her 3 times now and she gets better every time. She isn't easy by any means, but if you want to really learn a lot this is the place to be. She cares about how well you do in class and is there for you when you need her. One of the very best professors I've ever had.

EXTREMELY HEAVY WORK LOAD. Don't take this class unless you have a lot of free time. Assigned 200+ pg readings from textbook. This will also be during group projects, & she may overlap two projects and give you VERY LITTLE TIME. I signed up for this class under title ISSUES IN MEDIA STUDY, class is actually HISTORY OF JOURNALISM IN U.S.

Extremely helpful! She's definitely interested in making sure that students understand the assignments and in making sure that students are successful. She can be intimidating at first but once you get to know her in class, you'll see that she's probably one of the coolest teachers at UWB. Definitely recommended.

Taught directly from ppt slides. Unclear and unspecific. Exams are literally word for word questions abou textbook, which is completely ueless and poorly organized/written. "Doesn't require attendance" but takes roll and gives participation points. Boring. Easy enough but definitely not a fun class.
Great personality and sense of humor. I really enjoyed this class. It reinforced what I'd already learned and corrected that which needed to be corrected. The class was informative.

The busy work gets in the way of any actual education you might receive. The professor isn't very good at explaining something if you get confused and just assumes you understand the first time. Not open to re-distributing work if any particular day is over-loaded. Over all don't take this class with her. She is not helpful and you will hate it.
I could have learned more if she cut down the amount of busy work. She was very helpful and cared about student's leaning.
Ton's of textbook reading.  Lots of projects.  BUSY WORK
Gives waaaay too many projects.  The amount of reading required for the course is outrageous.  Definitely difficult for those who work outside of going to school.
She may seem a little intimidating at first, but really is not. She is willing to listen to your argument about Exam scores/questions. She is interested in student success.
Really nice and clear on her expectations. Go to class, do the reading and you will do great!

She is a very knowledgeable person and expects a lot of effort from her students. She really wants the students to succeed and cares about them. I would definitely recommend her to someone who really wants to learn. She dose assign a lot of work and grades pretty fairly.
Class can be a little boring but very good professor/person all around

You can't B.S. the whole class, which is why I think some don't like her.  Do the readings, engage in conversation (especially if you aren't clear on something), and you'll do fine.  At least for my class, homework was barely sufficient to prove you did the reading, nothing more.

One of the worst classes I've taken. She is s stickler when she grades. She will never give a straight answer and will ask around the class until she is satisfied with what she has heard without clarifying what she wanted. If you misinterpret one of the readings, she will just slap a failing grade on it even though she never says what she wants

Terribly unclear! Changes in the syllabus throughout the quarter.  Her expectations are higher than any person I have ever met. When asking a question she goes around the answer before asking if what she said helped.

Homework for this class was absurd - I counted 47 assignments. It's normal to have a paper due, and a long dense reading and write up, all on the same day. She also changes the instructions for the assignments all the time so you pretty much have to wait until the night before to do the work. I regretted taking this class.

She is out of control with her assignments.  The amount of reading and expectations on the home works itself are extremely time consuming.  She assigned home work due on the Friday after Thanksgiving with a paper due Monday!  She is extremely critical on work.  It's hard to get full credit on anything.  I would never recommend her to anyone.

Though the information is interesting, she (like other people have said) is very dry.  She assigns far too much reading and assignments- for instance, a high stake paper will be due Monday and she assigns 2-3 20 page readings with homework for Monday as well.
Awful professor.  Incredibly hard grader.  And absolutely no real passion to teach.  Avoid Ottinger at all costs.  And check her facts, more often than not she's teaching  things that are wrong.

Professor Ottinger assigns cutting edge and relevant material to cover, has well-thought out lectures, and grades homework primarily on effort, with article presentations & tests on understanding. Her focus around Bruno Latour's Science in Action opened my eyes to how science, technology, and society are made. It's a lot crazier underneath it all!

A lot of people coplain because she is a bit dry and boring I guess, but she is SUPER CLEAR on her expectations and gives really specific grading rubric's.  Bottom line is if you can follow directions and participate in class you'll do really well.  I got an A and I still don't think I gave it my 100% efort.

Terrible professor. If you want a really dry course and an extremely hard grader then take this course. I don't recommend taking her to anyone. She assigns a lot of readings and if you don't have the same perspective on every issue as her she will grade you accordingly. Seriously the worst professor I have ever had in my 3 years of school.
Really dry.  This course offers a lot of busy work, but she paces it pretty well.  It is possible to get a good grade, but it is a very long class.

Not the easiest class I've ever taken... but professor knows her stuff and is willing to help outside of class if you put in the effort. If you do all the readings, come to class, and take good notes you should do fine.
Not helpful and very strict.  I wouldn't recommend her to any of my friends.

I took her my first quarter at UWB and she is very rigid, but does know her stuff. I can't say that I recommend her because she is VERY difficult but well thought out and when you can get her to relax for a second she is quite interesting. Very intense which sucked any fun out of an already boring subject.

Professor Haldipur is an awesome professor and honestly the main reason his class was so great. His teaching style really helped us focus on the key concepts and big takeaways from each lecture, which made everything way easier to understand. The material was organized really well and each lecture built on the last one.

Professor Haldipur is honestly one of the best professors I've had so far. He taught us brain development which can get kind of dense but he explains it in this really engaging way that makes it easy to follow. He also genuinely cares about how you are doing and is willing to accommodate your learning style. I really enjoyed his class.

if you get the chance to, definitely take him!! he's a neuroscience researcher and you can see his passion come through in the lectures. he loves participation but nothing is mandatory and he's also open to any suggestions for example changing exam dates, etc. he also breaks difficult topics into smaller concepts which make it easier to process.

Dr. Haldipur's knowledge of neuroscience, combined with his ability to communicate complex concepts clearly and effectively, makes him an outstanding professor. He was approachable by nature & showed genuine interest in the class's success which created a supportive learning environment. I would strongly recommend taking his classes.
Professor Haldipur was the greatest professor of all time

Fast and monotone. Very passionate, but unclear on expectations. Expected hefty background in microbio and neurobio even though not listed in prerequisites. No rubric for any assignments, assignments graded on which paper is the best. Exams are ridiculously heavy so do not miss ANY details from class.

She is a nice person and has passion for what she does but... She will not email you back and cant use the internet to save her life. Her feedback is not helpful and has a weird way of grading. To me it seemed like if she like you, you got a good grade if not she will not give you high marks. not the professor for me but for other maybe.

Honestly, this teacher kind of sucks. The biggest issue is that we are in the middle of a pandemic, so you think accesability would be a top priority for this professor right? Nope, they edited the syllabus to remove that they'll record classes for those that can't make it. Why? To make it easier on herself when they already do so little.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She cares about her students's success but marks you down on the smallest things that are not mentioned in the guidelines for assignments. She doesn't know how to carry the lectures, leaving the class either sleepy or distracted. If you don't have a good grasp of English Literature you won't get a good grade. See her office hours if you are stuck
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A very knowledgeable professor who listens to her students well and tries to help them in whatever possible way.

plenty of extra credit allowed.  Not an easy grader, but was worth it considering the credit range of the class (10cr in my major!!!).  got a 3.3 or 3.2 because I was good with the 3 very short papers, and long final essay, but did okay with participation and failed the mid term essay.  You can sleep, play games, skip.   very old though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: While I felt that this class had potential it fell short in terms of structure. Lectures were slow and you never knew how well you were doing. I did receive a high grade but never understood why. I say take this class if you have no other choice but realize that you may be confused throughout most of the quarter. Be sure to read reviews below.

The class has a lot of potential but the teacher is VERY boring. The syllabus is unclear and had tons of changes. Due dates always changed, but when we turned in papers she was a strict grader so it made no sense. Doesn't e-mail and hardly has availability for office hours, but says she prefers face-to-face. Take a different teacher.
Interesting class, quite a few assignments but nothing too hard or challenging. Sometimes she doesn't seem to like other interpretations of the prose in class discussions.

I took her creative writing class and it really ended up being more about literary analysis. Also, she was not open to diverse writing styles or topics and wanted students to only write about their personal lives. Getting a good grade was still a fairly easy task, though. Save yourself a huge load of frustration and avoid her at all cost.

Heuving is well organized, but she will overload you with busy work at the end of a quarter. It was a ridiculous amount. She speaks very slowly and can be irratating to listen to. Pass on her classes.
Very interesting class! I learned alot.
The teacher has alot of insight to the readings, and a wonderful sense of humor. I really enjoyed taking this class with this professor!

Possibly the most feeble minded prof I've ever seen.  Constant mix ups on sylabus, no one clear on assignments, she's completely lost.  Take this course if you want to experience frustration.  Her opinion is what matters, do no make the mistake of thinking that yours matters.  If your opinion does not mirror hers, you will not get full credit......
take the time for office hours
I enjoy this class. Work load is light and assignments are easy. Recommended.

heuving is the worst prof i have ever had, i took a language of poetry class with her and got a 3.8 BUT!!, acording to her there is only one right interprion which is hers...no room for free thinking she will shoot you down and tell you that you are "wrong". She teaches like a politition speaks.
No Comments

Sam is a great instructor, he knows his stuff, and also his midterm is extremely  similar to the homework, so do the homework and you will pass. His examples are hilarious and kept falling as sleep in his class. His lecture is really boring so bring some coffee. Great teacher i would take his macro his he teaches it next quarter.
He is a very laid back person. Just do the homework every week, you will pass with flying colors.

This guy is subtlety extremely funny and uses funny examples. He goes slow and gives you all the info you need to pass the class. tests are EXACTLY like homework. DO THE PROBLEM SETS, make sure you know them well, and you will ace the tests. Micro econ is somewhat of a boring subject and he makes it more interesting with his funny examples

Sam's lectures are boring, but in order to succeed, you have to pay attention. He will give you all the information you need to be successful in his lectures. The homework problems are almost exactly the same as the tests. If you keep up on the homework and can explain each problem to yourself then you will ace the exams!

Sam Henley is easily the funniest person on UW Bothell's campus - PERHAPS THE PLANET. Besides showing up to class every day looking DEVILISHLY HANDSOME in his HIGH FASHION, Sam will tell you what's what about micro economics, as long as you're there and engaged. 11/10 would take again. All the peppers!

He is nice and a genius but he is horrible at teaching students AND boring. A lot of people in my class are not doing well, and when I tell my friends that micro is hard, they laugh b/c micro is suppose to be easy but Henly makes it very difficult. Do NOT take his class if you want to keep your gpa up. Qsc tutor was stuck when asked I for help too.

Do not take this unless you're an microecon fanatic. He's boring, disorganized, REFUSES to ever review. No study guides, concepts are vague/ confusing. You mostly have to learn it all yourself. He's a very nice person, but cannot teach at all. Especially a beggining course.

He is pretty quiet and his lectures are super boring. He's super chill though so you can sit on your phone or laptop the whole time You don't need the textbook but it can be easier to learn from the book than the lectures. The homework isn't graded so you don't have to do it. Just study the hw answers and the tests will be easy.
Econ is a tough subject, but Henly made it so much easier. Honestly the tests are common sense more than anything he teaches, so if you don't get an A its your own fault. Awesome class.

Very difficult subject matter for me, but he made it really relevant.  As long as you study, and definitely do the homework, there is no reason you shouldn't do well in this class.  I found it essential to attend class, because the lectures are very important to supplement critical comprehension of subject matter.
One of the greatest professors I've ever had. Highly recommend!

Wesley is honestly the best professor I have ever had while in college. He's so funny, really understanding, and cares about what he's teaching. He makes sure to make things interesting and wants everyone to do really well. There's only 3 big assignments all of which are easy to do. Definitely take his classes!

Wonderful professor, a lot of activities and group discussions. Speaks very well, makes people  of all opinions feel welcome. It was a 4 hr 1x/week class. To make that an enjoyable experience is a huge challenge but he did it! It was my favorite class of the quarter. weekly canvas discussion based on readings, one 2pg paper, project, final paper.

Wesley is such a fabulous professor. He has a relaxed and easygoing attitude yet professional and knowledgeable at the same time. The classes are organized into online discussions (once per class), presentations, and group discussions. He is funny, which makes the classroom atmosphere cool. He seems to have the answer for every question!
Good professor.

reviews.comment: Overall great professor. Learned a lot of things. Enjoyed working working with him along the way. Will definitely take his class again.
