reviews.comment: Professor Miyamoto is a great professor. The course is heavy, but it's worth it because you learn a ton. He's very understanding, allows you to do quiz makeups and sometimes lets you turn in homework for full credit depending on the circumstance. He's funny as well and super chill. If you want to learn Japanese, this is a perfect opportunity to.

He sucks as a professor. Barely teaches you stuff on his own or lectures but relies on the textbook and workbook for everything. Calls you out in front of the class to do excercises. Would emberass students in front of the class.

He doesn't care for his students as if you're sick, you're still expected to do work. No extensions are given out even if you're crippled or in a hospital bed. He gives tons of homework to students each day and there's a quiz at the beginning of each class. He is rude in his emails by responding with only one worded answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Quizzes every class, expect to learn Japanese! Miyamoto Sensei is extremely understanding and an amazing teacher. As a commuting student, he was always forgiving of my absence and lets students retake missed quizzes the following class if you give notice. His teaching style is excellent, I can't believe I learned hiragana/katakana so fast. 10/10

Miyamoto Sensei was a wonderful professor, he was genuinely excited to teach his culture and his language to us students. Miyamoto was understanding as to how difficult the language is to learn. It was my pleasure to take his course he genuinely made me feel like he was looking forward to teach us everyday. I would definitely take his course again.

Miyamoto-sensei is a cool guy. He knows Japanese is hard and will do everything he can do prepare you for it. His anecdotes are funny and relate a lot to Japanese culture. If it matters, yes he actually lived in Japan.
A down to earth, wonderfully nice man who is excellent at teaching his native language.
Dont take his class

Sensei is encouraging in every class. He brings a wonderful sense of humor but also emphasizes good work ethic and professionalism. Sensei makes Nihongo easier to learn with his unique lectures and assignments. His class is fun; participate, study, practice and you can succeed. I love Sensei like a father, arigatou gozaimashista Sensei!

He's a good guy at heart. Really respectful to students that sometimes it feels like I'm the one grading him. He's really clear on what's expected of you on quizzes/exams and posts all the materials that you need to study on Canvas. The only downside is that there's a lot of quizzes every day, but that's just how language classes are.

He is really good teacher, very care for students, he feels like if you do not get a good grad, that is his fault. Although there are a lot of small quiz, but very easy, only take about 10 mins to prepare. If there is any problem, just talk to him. This is a language class, so you need to prepare for the exam, but it will be really easy to get A.
Easy to pass the class if you participate and attend the class. He's really down to earth person who really cares for the students. I highly recommend to take his class.
Awesome Japanese professor! Super friendly and will go to great lengths to help you succeed! Always a joy to be in his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment:
Dr. Hillesland is a great project mentor. 
She is very helpful and gives good feedback for your investigative biology research project. 
Attend labs/lectures and communicate frequently (especially when you have questions) and you will do well in her IB course.

BBIO 470 - She is a really nice person and knows what she is talking about. The content isn't well organized however. Lectures are not structured so you won't know what you're going in to learn that day. Easy grader and gives amazing feedback on your grant proposal writing though. Definitely allows you to learn to write a scientific paper.

I like her. She is a very generous person. I ask for extensions because of other exams, they are reasonable and she really accommodates. She is super passionate about her field and is very inspiring. I feel like things I learn in Bio 2 didn't make much sense until this course, very holistic review of everything. I wish I could take more classes

she was an ok professor. Her lectures were kinda confusing to me. She records her lectures which is helpful if the audio is working. She takes forever to grade stuff. Worksheets before every class, three exams open book and you'll have several days to complete it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures can be unorganized. Come to class!! Effort you put in=grade you get. Study guides completed for extra credit. Worksheets done before class to prepare. 3 take home exams,open internet. Polleverywhere in class. She is very caring/good humor.She wants her students to succeed, makes herself accessible if you need help. Overall great professor!

I don't understand the negative reviews. She was pretty funny during lectures, seems like a genuinely good person. The labs were really fun. You really can live vicariously through her excitement for microbiology. Our exams were long, but they were open resources and you had several days to do them - Exam 2 we had like five days to finish the test!

pretty good imo. the other past reviews say she's unorganized, but canvas etc seemed tidy to me. typical week is worksheet before class & then go over it together in class. u can ask questions anonymously via class poll. the worksheet is useful cuz they can help u on exam. also u can have partial credit on exams. genuinely cares for students

She is extremely unorganized and she doesn't care if the students learned something or not. She will deduct points even if you answered the questions correctly. She doesn't know the material and keeps complaining how long ago she studied it and how she can't remember anything. The questions on the exam are very general. NOT RECOMMENDED
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was a horrible mistake to take her class. Not only extremely unorganized and doesn't know the material, but also docks you points when you put in the effort and didn't even answer it wrong. I have had so many problems with her this quarter and want to warn people that she cannot teach and doesn't even care about her students. Ruined micro!!

She was a great teacher, especially in lab! You have to give her a chance and ask questions. The second exam is the hardest when you have to learn all the microbes she gives you. I would definitely take her again, but she was challenging!!! BUT I LEARNED SOOO MUCH!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good Class. She is a bit unorganized and can be hard to approach. But I thought she was effective and fun to learn microbiology from. I think that if you love 1 project, 4 exams, some readings when needed to better understand the material, then this is the class for you.
Terrible teacher. Extremely unorganized and not ANY help when you ask her questions. She has ruined microbiology for me.

Also took her for Investigative biology and Love her. Her lectures can be unorganized and confusing but she is happy to clarify and is fantastic in lab. The tests can be tough but study activities and ask her about anything confusing. The lab and final project is actually fun and inspired me to explore microbiology further.  Favorite class here.

Kristina really cares about her students and is actively interested in making sure her students understand the material. The class moves fast and the material is challenging, but she's always happy to focus on things kids are confused about. Overall, she has given us a solid foundation on microbiology.

She is adorable and really cares about making sure her students understand the material. Doesn't prepare us well for the exams, theyre pretty difficult. Use the studyguides and activities from class, understand the chapters and you'll be okkk. The final project is actually fun. Her class birthed my new love for microbio honestly(:

Shes passionate about microbio, but simply not a good teacher. In lab she was great and helpful, but lecture was scattered, boring and you basically have to self teach yourself the entire quarter. Exams are not easy. She picks the most random facts from the book to test you on when you memorized whole concepts. Do-able, but a lot of busy work.
Great in lab.
Only good at lab, bad in Lecture. Will go behind student's back...

DO NOT TAKE HER! The name of this class is misleading, its not an intro class AT ALL. she locks everything  until the day when it is due. reviews.comment: She was a good professor. Most of the content was relatively easy if you just read the readings that were assigned and if you were organized. I can see why other students did not really like her but genuinely if you just pay attention to the readings, go to the lectures, and follow the syllabus, you will be fine and she was somewhat an easy grader.

The teacher's class is hit or miss. Weak organization and gives vague instructions. Communication's a challenge with passive-aggressive vibes. Deadlines are strict and random (ranging from 2 pm to 9 am), allowing little flexibility. If you don't care and just prioritize passing the class, just meet deadlines, go to class, and you'll manage.
really organized. really bad.

Although not a mean-spirited person whatsoever, I have noticed that she's very easily irritable. Feels as though it's her first year of teaching -- she seems very overwhelmed and disorganized. Make sure to do all of the readings because all of her quizzes are based on them. Lecture is very heavy on discussion and group work.

She does not know what she's doing. Not organized whatsoever. Her canvas is so hard to manage, doesn't open modules until a day before. Plans too much for the day, and doesn't get through her lesson plan. Doesn't respond on time. Feels like it's her first year teaching.

There are in-class assignments, but they are easy to do and learn from. Homework is usually once every two weeks, quite fun. Midterms are two parts, one multiple choice with 25 questions and one online IDE with three programming questions. Final is one homework and 50 multiple choice question. Laid back and great at teaching! Highly recommend!!
Nice group work. Pretty laid back tests. Textbook prepares you very well for next class 143 if you read it and do the challenge questions.

No coding experience before and was happy I did it with her. Super understanding and caring in explaining and making sure you understand the basics of Java. Class is spent listening to slides then group work on practicing what you learned. Homework is just an online textbook Zybooks. Only professor I know who allows IDE for tests rather than paper!

Professor Gunnerson is a considerate and kind professor. The course is focused on coding and involves several projects which makes the workload heavy. The online platform used as the textbook, ZyBooks, is not great. However, the professor explains the concepts very well, making the class a little easier to comprehend.

One of the best CS professors here at UWB! You are allowed to use ur IDE for the programming on the exams, the multiple choice portion is on canvas, and gives a lot of extra credit on the exams as well. Really good at explaining things and makes class enjoyable. Participation does matter for in class work so be prepared to come to class.

Professor Gunnerson is awesome and one of the best professors you could get for CS. She always helps students and will do her best to make you succeed. Study with a good schedule and try and do work a little bit in advance you will be fine. Go for her office hours as you can learn so much and get one on one time to improve. She is awesome!!!!!!!!!!
I had her for CSS142, her class is great. Highly recommend her regardless of coding experience. Everything makes sense, work load is regular, professor is pleasant and grading is fair.

This professor doesn't really know much about the java but she is a very very generous grader when it comes to tests. When I was taking her course her grader was tough for some of the assignments and didn't really give full credit but she was the one grading the tests and almost always gave a very good grade.

Dr. Kim is the best! She will always help you and also even assist you with anything. Even though there are three exams, you can do the coding portion on BlueJ and multiple choice on Canvas. Super helpful during office hours. Highly recommend you take her for any CSS class.

Prof. Gunnerson was so kind and always willing to answer questions! Go to office hours! All sections of CSS 142 are very test heavy (40 % 2 midterms and 25% final). Tests are composed of multiple choice questions and a couple coding questions. Partial credit is given for coding questions, but mainly graded on if the program is correct and runs.

reviews.comment: Her office hours are hella useful bruh she literally gives you the answers. My least favorite thing about her is that she is really slow at grading. Its an amazing class, really interesting and its basic java coding. Not much coding you do but you see the foundation of how it works, she is one amazing professor and will help if asked. Always go to office hours they really help, easy A if you attend class and ask for help when needed, a lot of workload tho but its easy.

She is very good, and very humorous. She we do whatever it takes for you to succeed

She's a good teacher but doesn't know how to help when you ask her questions. She'll assign you assignment or reading but doesn't know whats the questions are. So when you're struggling she doesn't know how to help you.

I'm not sure why there's a lot of negative comments on here. This teacher is the best and the nicest teacher I have had so far in UWB. I struggled and really needed her help. tough class

the slowest grader ever! she would update once which is after a month and that is it she doesn't update the grades at all. This class bring tons of stress to me.

SHE DOESN'T UPLOAD GRADES AT ALL!!! this class is tough, and you desperately need to know if you're doing good in class or not because nobody wants to get disappointed at the end of the quarter, but you won't know because she doesn't post anything at all, not one assignment even, many students ask her but she doesn't answer the question at all.

You won't be able to have time to study for any of your other classes, she gives loads of work, one after the other, to the point it gets too stressful and you'll fall behind even if you're trying your best, I tell ms Kim that I'm worried if I fail and need to know what my grade is, she doesn't respond. Leaving you not knowing anything at all.

I expected ms Kim to be different when I checked to rate my prof. So far, the worst class I have taken. A lot of students are struggling in her class.

Gunnerson is a great person, but man does she moves FAST and If you don't keep up you'll be left behind. reviews.comment: Great teacher do the stuff and you pass grades everything at the ends so I went from 47 to 93%

reviews.comment: There's like no homework but she's really nice and helpful in class.

Fun and funny professor. Actually TEACHES you the subject, not an Easy A but she have clear criteria of what you need to know. Exam questions are similar to the ones in lecture, discussion and aleks. Gives one notecard cheatsheet for exams, drops one exam. Lectures are easy to follow, posts notes online. 1-2 extra credit at the most. No curve.
She is a great teacher and has helped me look at college in a better way.

I have 143 with Kim and while it seems others like her lectures, I hate them. I feel like when its most important she jokes around and tells semi-irrelevant stories in class when she could be teaching what we need to know for the test and explaining it better. She skims whats important. I was a Chem major but now Im switching to business.

reviews.comment: Kim gunnersons chem series was the hardest sequence of classes I've had in my life, however it was been an awesome experience. She knows her stuff, is hilarious and caring. She gives great feedback on exams, and once you know how she runs things, it gets easier! One of the best classes I've taken.

Kim is funny, caring, passionate about her lectures and really knows what she's teaching. Miss a lecture before an exam and you will miss a lot of what will be on it. ALEKS hw is terrible, but she gives you full credit if you finish most of it! Chem is hard, Kim will be there for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance is optional, but missing one lecture is like missing 25% of whats going to be on the test. Her humor is amazing and she is really understanding if you go and talk to her in office hours.

Dr. Gunnerson is great. She's funny and she makes her lectures interesting with cool stories. While attendance is not mandatory, you'll want to show up to get POGIL points. ALEKS, the homework platform uses, is crappy, but do it for points. Take notes from the book to supplement her lectures. Again, you'll learn a lot if you work for it.

Kim knows her stuff very well seeing how passionate she is about chemistry. Exams shouldn't be too hard if you read over discussion session worksheets and POGIL questions (it's not completely useless). She doesn't curve and the highest you can really get is a 3.9 so don't expect a 4.0 in her class. Only downside? Online HW is a pain.

I took the entire general chemistry series with Kim, she's the best prof! She's really helpful during office hours-- definitely go to her office hours! Chemistry will make a lot more sense! You can tell she loves chemistry and she'll make you love it too. She's super funny and her lectures are amazing.

Kim uses advanced pedagogy and carefully structured metaphors to create lessons and learning that sticks. She is not easy, but chemistry is not easy. Not her fault. Not UW's fault. The universe's fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This was my first programming class and I struggled with it. We used the program Alice  and it was just hard to program and the rubrics for projects were out of this world to follow. Willing to help but doesn't know how to help when asking a question. 4 total projects with one presentation of project4. 8 weekly pop quizzes online.

Amazing Professor! If only she could teach all of the Chem classes. She's really enthuastic about the topic and will go above and beyond to help you understand. The online hw is a lot but it really prepares you for her exams. If you attend class, go to discussion, and do the hw you'll be fine.

Hardest class I've ever taken. lecture is minimal compared to what will be on the exam. Even if you read the entire chapter straight from the textbook, do all the study review, and all of the massive amounts of ALEKS she has assigned for the chapter, prepare to fail anyway. Average grade on her exams is almost always FAIL, or very close to it...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her lectures was not at all helpful. She would explain things too quickly & kind of expect us to know what to do. sometimes she would even get mad at us for not knowing. The Pogil thing was useless, & did not help with the exams at all. Neither did the discussion sessions, it was always a week ahead, & not what we were learning in class....

The exams are fair. If you don't show up to class and skip discussion, you better be doing very well on the exams because will fail. For homework, she uses an online system called Aleks, and it is annoying, but she gives you a 100% on each homework, if you get at least 80% of the topics in Aleks completed.

There was an exam about once every 7 days which was stressful but preferred as each covered less new material. She assigns online homework using one of the best platforms I've ever used. I really enjoyed her class and her energy and wish she was teaching more classes I needed. Don't fear early morning classes, she's energetic and excited to teach.

She is by far one of the best science professor's I've ever had. She explains concepts so well, and in ways that help you better understand them. She's straightforward, and she's absolutely hilarious, so lectures aren't boring.

Kim Gunnerson is the best teacher I have had overall. Her class isn't easy, she makes you work for it. As long as you go to class and pay attention you will do fine. She helps A LOT in her office hours so I would suggest those. Other than that she is hilarious and makes her lectures fun. Can't brag enough about this teacher. THE BEST!

You can tell she knows the material thoroughly and explains things in multiple ways so students understand. Her analogies are both hilarious and informative. Definitely need to go to class, participate, study, and do homework to be successful though. Very helpful when you ask questions.

Kim is literally your average college professor. Majority of your grade rides on your exams, which is 60% of your grade to be exact. She really makes your work hard for your grade. But, Kim is a great person and really wants you to know the material and will make strides to make sure you know it. The rigor of her course is worthwhile in the end!
DO YOUR HOMEWORK
Very clear in her expectations, show up and follow directions and you will get an A
This was a fun and easy animation course to help give students a basic understanding of programming. Highly recommended if you want to get into higher level programming courses in the future.

She keeps the class fun, funny, and engaging. She's very accessible during work time and has answers to any questions that may come up during lectures, tangents included. If you're not afraid of working for your keep, she will become your new favorite professor

She makes you practice problems in a POGIL book, but it doesn't have answers and she doesn't go over them. She lectures half the time, gives you participation points for clicker questions (even if you get them wrong), and there's quite a bit of quizes and exams that are kind of hard. Definitely need to read the book, do homework, and study a lot.

She is tough! She expects a lot and teaches a little differently than other chem instructors, so if you take her, do it from the beginning of the series if you can. Her class is a real challenge, and she is sometimes intimidating, but she is a nice person and good lecturer and keeps it mostly interesting.

I really hated taking class with her. She's very sarcastic and makes you feel intimidated by her. She gets off topic sometimes and she keeps class for longer than the allotted time. There are better choices than her. Take her at your own risk.

Kim is amazing. She always answers questions and put her notes up on the canvas site. She's always willing to help and makes it really fun and interesting. Taking all my chem classes with her made them so much more interesting thanks to her great attitude and constant jokes. Best chem professor ever!

She is the best chemistry professor out there! She really tries to help and answer your questions! Her lectures can be confusing at times, but as long as you pay attention and DO THE HOMEWORK, you will be fine. If you're having trouble, just ask her. She's the best!
Amazing teacher! Keeps you engaged and makes you interested in what you're learning. She makes a lot of jokes which is always fun. Just be sure to do the homework and study for tests and quizzes!
Trust me, take her class. She will be one of the best professors you have had. She isn't easy, but you will learn a lot and have a lot of fun doing it.

Kim is such a wonderful professor overall. She will crack a lot of jokes and it amuses the whole class. You will get a lot out of this professor, my schedule revolves around her class time, thats how much of a great prof. she is. You need to make sure you do your homework to understand the material and read your book and take notes by hand!
Class requires a lot of outside studying to succeed, material introduced in class is quite basic. Exams are exceptionally hard and are not graded on a curve but are easy to pass.
book work was stupid but pay attention to her lectures, overall this class was easy and she is very helpful

She's nice, great attitude, fair grader, but clear your schedule because there is alot of work to do in her simulation class: weekly quizzes, midterm, final, quarter long group project and individual project.  Weekly check-in reports on the projects which are aimed to help you making sure you don't get behind.
Very fun programming class to do, you get into it. It gets frustrating sometimes but Kim is not hard to reach with either email or asking her questions during class.

Although challenging, she makes it easy to get a good grade if you care enough. She was extremely helpful in class and during office hours and was willing to answer questions over e-mail if you werent able to make it in. In class she was always excited and in being so, engaged her students. She is an amazing teacher and i loved her class.
Not a easy teacher. Although she explain questions pretty good, it take effort to get a good grade.
Kim is simply amazing, she helped me get through some personal difficult times and kept encouraging me to succeed. With out her i would not be where i am today.
Absolutely loved this teacher. Extremely helpful! While this class was not for me, she made it as easy as possible. One of the nicest teachers I have had here at UWB. I highly recommend her!!!
Kim is a top professor. Highly recommended!

She is the nicest person, but I felt like lectures went by extremely quickly.  I had her for two classes in calculus, and after the first quarter she switched over from grading weekly homework to giving quizzes 1 or 2 times/week. I definitely preferred the first quarter since I received feedback on my homework without taking a hard hit on my grade.

Kim is so friendly and she is such a fun professor to have. She actually made Calculus kinda fun because of her examples used and the jokes she was always making. She is ALWAYS willing to spend extra time to help students understand and will really go the extra mile to make sure you do well in the class. Great Prof!!
Very helpful, nice and wants you to do well.
I love her! She is so helpful and just plain sweet! I would totally recommend taking a class with her!!!

Kim is a great teacher who is very passionate about the material she is teaching. She does a great job explaining the material in class but also expects you to read your book and do the problems. Her powerpoint slides are very helpful before exams and the math learning center and Kim are always willing to help you.

I loved Kim.  I already have an interest in Math and it is my major which may explain my reason for liking her, but I felt that those that did not put the effort into learning struggled.  She does expect you to try to learn things on your own, but in my experience, if you don't teach yourself math, you won't really grasp the concept.
Doesn't teach. Gives homework and expects you to figure it out yourself. No reviews for tests. Not helpful when you talk to her and is not willing to curve or take suggestions.
No Comments

The class itself is useless and a waste of time, which is disappointing considering how much education and experience she has. 3 hour long class with no takeaways. Assignments are easy and pointless. Be prepared to come to class and be bored out of your mind! Only giving Professor Hintz a 2 because she is very kind and cares about kids.

Alison is my favorite professor!! Her lectures are always inspirational, authentic to what is happening in the world, and I always learn so much from her. Plus, she really truly cares about what is going on in her students' lives! She is the absolute best :)
Alison is super enthusiastic about what she teaches. I did feel like the class was a little long and easy, but she is inspirational and truly cares about kids!

Weirdest and most boring class I've ever taken. She has no plan when she comes to class, instead rambles on and on and it's impossible to pay attention to, let alone for 3 hours. She is very rude when asking for helpAssignments were super unclear on what was expected. The assignments were really easy and she graded really easy. Learned nothing.

tbh she wasnt that bad. she seems intimidating and rude by face. i didnt learn much about ELL endorsement. she doesnt use a textbook or have slides. just rants on and walks around while she talks. this class was just boring and i couldve put my energy into a better class that wouldve taught me something. if you want to be bored then take her.

Did not learn anything for an introductory class for the ELL endorsement. No structure or rubrics for any assignment. She did not come prepared with ANY curriculum and instead ridiculed us, shared sensitive topics without trigger warnings, ranted about random opinions, gave us unhelpful solutions, and challenged our knowledge as future teachers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are one of those people who can not adapt, or change, or be open minded, or expand your perspectives: don't take the class. If you came to college to learn, and actually stretch your mind, take this class!

Terrible, terrible, terrible. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. She is absolutely the worst. Never came to class prepared, never gave us any assignments except group presentations that she never explained, and NEVER spoke respectfully to students. I learned absolutely nothing and you won't either. Avoid at ALL costs.

Absolute terrible teacher. She did not talk about the course material and other than reading and 15 hours of volunteer work, she assigned open ended group work. No grades are updated or even discussed until the final grade. She is disrespectful when students ask questions, and impatient when students do not discuss irrelevant material. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is very disorganized and is never clear about what she wants from the students. She doesn't post ANY grades until the day they are due so you aren't sure how you are doing in class. She makes you feel uneasy when you participate. I would take her class simply for the easy A, but I didn't get anything out of it.

This professor is amazing. He is so good at encouraging students to be creative and think out of the box. This class is no-stress and super fun. Almost all assignments are basically credit/no credit. You can try as little or as hard as you want, but if you are extra creative, you are able to earn extra credit.

Professor Ted is amazing! He was accepting of everyone's photography work, never shaming anyone and always giving very meaningful comments on our submissions. Creates a respectful environment, especially when reviewing student work. This course is team-taught by him and one other prof. After week 4 they switch and week 5 is a "break" week.

Fun and easy class. Grading came back fast and with good comments. He was quick to reply to any messages and was willing to change grades after due dates if you wanted to change/ add something. Created fun projects and had interesting topics to talk about in class. A lot of the class was group based, but never marked down because of group mates.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ted was very engaging and cared about his students. The in-class group "projects" were entertaining and made you open up your creative side. The assignments were also exciting and really brought out everyone else's creative side. This class was very enjoyable.
There's a participation group assignment every class and HW every other week. Ted is nice and accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took photography and it was really fun and easy. For assignments, he gives very clear guidelines and if you follow them, he gives 100%. You do have to come to class because in-class activities are a big part of your grade. He is very nice, I had to miss class once, and he was very helpful and excused me from an assignment. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love this professor he is an amazing teacher and is willing to go out of his way to help you. I say he is an easy A just because he will inspire you to push your self and make your work that much better. If you like art and have a passion for that type of thing take his class. made me fall in love with the art world again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Philosophy class with him was really fun. His knowledge of all these different schools of thought is really interesting, and his lectures are awesome - especially the existentialism one when he fell on the floor and screamed. He needs to teach more philosophy classes, his art isn't really that good to be honest...

Ted's an amazing professor! Gives reasonable homework and realistic deadlines. This class was a lot about participation and despite being a beginner in Photography, this class didn't seem intimidating. He actively listens to what a student says and helps develop individual strengths and does not expect students to fit in. Great class!

Doesn't seem to know much about photography. In case you forget, he'll remind you every class that he's Canadian. If he makes you look at his "art" (he subjects every class to this) make sure to give him lots of compliments and tie it to something existential--he desperately needs to put his PhD in Philosophy to good use.
This is my favorite professor at UW!!!! He gives great feedback and is always willing to help you out. Seriously take him!!!

Professor Hiebert went above and beyond to help me succeed. He allowed us to incorporate his feedback into our work, which not only helped us create a polished portfolio, it also helped improve our initial grade. From quickly replying to emails, to helping me when I was ready to give up, Professor Hiebert was instrumental in my success at UW.

This class was phenomenal. Ted is an extremely articulate as well as open minded professor -- he is good at creating a dialogic space that exists within the structure of his academic intentions (while allowing for student contribution). The material & workload was woven into the class sublimely. Great class. Great Professor.

The course load was well balanced and the content and class discussions were interesting.  As long as you do the work, put in genuine effort and participate in class you'll get a good grade.  However, I got almost perfect grades on the assignments and written feedback that my participation was excellent, so am left wondering how I got a lower grade

Nice guy so far, but a bit of bait and switch:  the first week he talks as though there is a low amount of writing req'd, but at the end of the second week when the first two assignments are given, there is actually alot of writing that will be due.  I've just noticed that he likes to be smooth and stay positive rather than just saying how it is.

Ted is great, although his lectures get pretty deep. If you are willing to go to him for help he'll do all he can to guide you. I learned a lot and was exposed to many new artists and ideas. If you want to learn about photography and modern art philosophy I recommend Ted's classes.

Really enjoyed Ted's class. Not difficult. If you just make sure you attend class, do the assignments, and participate, you're guaranteed a good grade. He does a good job of explaining the books during lectures, (but sometimes it gets boring), but it still helps for the two essays. The final art project is fun! Take his class!

Loved the subject of the class (photography) did very well on projects-however received a lower final grade, for no reason. Very unclear with his expectations and loves to hear himself talk. Just be certain that you know what he wants, or you will be left with a grade that does not at all reflect the work you put in.
he is just awesome.
Ted is a great teacher! Very helpful and wants his students to do well in the class! I would take his class again! Very much so recommended!

VERY AWESOME PROFESSOR!!  He is so open about ideas and thoughts you may have!  I brought up Anime links for the class and didn't think he would show them but he loved them and showed them!  Saying they were exactly what he was talking about!!  He never downs anyone and always helpful!!!  RECOMMENDED!!

Ted is a very good teacher when it comes to art. He is very passionate about the subject and on projects he will tell you his opinion so you can do better. Be ready to keep an open mind and read the required books!

One of the worst Professors I've had.

And the class was terribly unorganized, strenuous in its virtual interface. This class would have been fine with one textbook. This class was all over the place. 

Worst class I've had at UW Bothell and it was the only class I had to pay for, unfortunately. Still loved the subject matter, nevertheless.
Absolutely Abhorrent. Constantly rude, ultra strict, and does not respect her students. She wants you to fail. I got the top grade in the class last quarter and it was only a B+.

I am sorry, but the rating below is mostly inaccurate. Although it is true she is passionate about what she teaches, that does NOT make her a good teacher. A class where you pretty much have to go to office hours to get any sort of info, is not a good thing. Like yeah she will help you in office hours, but in class... nope. Too many assignemts.

One of my favorite professors ever! She is super passionate about what she teaches and cares the students understand the subject at hand. If you care about the classes she teaches spend some time in the office hours she gives you will be amazed how much she cares and explains. 

:)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Completely crazy class for an introductory course. This course feels like we are taking a class meant for fourth year students who are ready to graduate with a degree in the science field. As some of the reviews stated below, the professor assigns too much homework and too many projects. Do yourself a favor and stay away from this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this class is insane for a 101 course. it is SO MUCH information every single week i feel like im drowning, i spend way more time for this class instead of classes for my major i hate it. Prof. doesnt really sympathize for other students whatsoever so it feels hopeless to even bring it up. this course has made me sad with how much time it takes up
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As a student who always gets As in classes and has a 4.8 gpa I can honestly say this teacher was the worst one ive ever had. Most people took this cosmos class for the credit, during a pandemic, with the world falling apart and she gave no sympathy or cares to us! Horrible grader, Unclear on most directions, Not supportive, And wants us to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dumbest teacher I've ever taken. Doesn't know how to teach and makes the whole class about group work and won't give you your points if you don't work with other people. Don't ever take her. She should honestly get fired from teaching.

She is very clear about what you are expected to know, and she gives rubrics for homework that tell you exactly what she is looking for. She is so passionate about the subject and is also very funny and approachable. Best part, you actually LEARN in her class. The group work is extremely helpful in understanding the material.

As a physics major, she is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is deeply passionate about the subject and will do her best to help the class to succeed. She does have higher expectations for her class then most professors, which translates to more pre-class preparation in order to get the most out of her lectures.

Cons: Failed to adapt teaching styles with students feedback; Need to make effort to modify talking speed and ways of explaining to aim for better lecture quality; Homework and exams questions: not worded in a clear fashion; Grading comments confusing and not helpful; Pros: Make you think of the reason to use an equation; Nicereading assignments

The reason she has such a low score is the pandemic, which has been challenging. However, she is extremely caring and absolutely loves the subject. She really does care for the students and tries to listen to them as much as possible. This course is not easy, but if you do the work you should be alright. Overall she is a great person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She doesn't care about her students and gives tons of homework that we can't handle especially during this pandemic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No accommodations were made for the pandemic. Homework is released at inconvenient times, and even when we expressed wanting more time for valid reasons, she still said no. This class is a lot of outside work, and I mean a lot. You will spend most of your time reading and learning the material by yourself. Zoom classes are easy "zone out" classes
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She gives out too much homework and doesn't explain things thoroughly. She expects you to learn the material on your own. She doesn't care about her students and how they might have a hard time juggling their other work along with jobs. I would not recommend her AT ALL.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Taking this class during COVID-19 and she hasn't done anything to accommodate with what's going on with the pandemic. She gives a lot of homework and only releases them at the end of the second lecture of the week. We've told her to ease up on the homework and she only told us to manage our time better, DURING A PANDEMIC. It's not worth it trust me
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Paola is one of a kind. Her teaching style is based off of a flipped classroom. While in the class, students will find this incredibly challenging, however, I walked away learning more than I have ever learned in my undergraduate career. Do the homework, go to lecture and office hours, and you'll be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really liked professor Rodriguez. Though she had a different approach to teaching i can honestly say that it was successful in teaching the course content. I have never had a professor as passionate about the content. Along with this, ahe cares about her students. In a class of over 80 students i felt like an individual. She was very approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever had. Stay away from her!!! Learned nothing from the class even though her teaching style was supposed to "help students learn more". Was actually hoping to learn physics but this class taught me little. Wait for another professor to teach this class I didn't and regret it heavy.

Her class is heavily relies on you reading the material prior to coming to class. Her office hours are extremely helpful and she will always try to use different explanations to ensure your understanding. She's pretty stuck in her ways of doing things and isn't that open for change, but do everything she assigns and you will succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I would recommend taking another professor for mechanics if possible. The entire class is based on what you teach yourself at home and she is not open towards any of the students' feedback or criticism. The homework is reasonable however lectures consist of discussions and not actual lectures or teaching. Take another professor if you can!
Worst prof/class combo I've ever had. Def recommend taking a different professor for this class unless you thoroughly enjoy physics and are proficient with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hard class for sure, and she expects a lot of work out of students more than I have experienced in the past at UWB. However, she is super enthusiastic and truly cares for her students. Putting in the work before lectures is EXTREMELY essential. One of my favorites professors Ive had very upbeat and funny. Would recommend if you are willing to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Before the final grades were put in my reviews would have been like the others. However she did put a slight curve at the end with a mean of 2.5. Grading is incredible tough but she is accessible outside if class and really does want you to learn physics. She makes it clear from the get go however, NOT AN EASY A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and wait for a different lecturer. She cant explain a thing and has the worst grading scale at UW Bothell. 96 percent for a 4.0 with test highs around 90. Almost impossible to get a 4.0.

This was by far the worst class I have ever taken. She didn't teach us much, if at all. Also, it is a self taught class, which means that you have to learn almost everything by yourself. Class average on her exams are very poor, and the worst part is that they aren't curved. I recommend that you look for a different lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: -Class is mostly group work and practicing problems with almost immediate feedback (this is a fantastic thing!) -The textbook is clear and easy to read -Shes super funny and passionate, you can really tell that she wants everyone to do well -Every class is worth going to. Seriously. -Not a class for people who like plug and chug problems

She has to be up there for one of the worst teachers at UW Bothell. She explains even the simple physics concepts very poorly and her class consists of people doing problems in groups of 4 and her lectures dont provide any neccesary information. I highly recommend to not take this class with her as your lecturer, she will make u miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gets you engaged in class, and trying programming concepts hands on. Just the right amount of lecture and hands on practice. Also super helpful when asking for help, and accessible for anyone who's struggling. Probably the best professor I've had.

If you don't read the textbook very carefully, you're going to be confused in class. Also when she assigns a difficult problem for group work, usually one or two groups know the answer and the rest of the class leaves the room struggling. But in all fairness I respect her system. So ALWAYS ask questions and go to her office hours if you're stuck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Hill expects participation and prepared students--don't fall behind on the reading. She gives very clear expectations and if you do the work, a 4.0 is within easy reach. She's very accessible, understanding, and open to constructive criticism. Would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Hill uses an "active learning" style so, while attendance isn't mandatory, you should show up. Her tests are difficult but are weighted fairly, and are largely off-set by lab. She is incredibly accessible outside of class and offers partial credit back on one exam question per quarter. It's not an easy class, but the work is worthwhile.

Hill's exams are nearly impossible to do well in, as they are extremely difficult and are graded harshly. Also, the lectures are more-so group problem solving sessions rather than actual lecture. In addition to this, the in-class participation is worth a lot of the grade as well.

I wish she would lecture more. She lectures maybe 20-30mins a week. Her Exams are plain difficult. Rigorous grader. Impossible to receive full points on homework. Her exam averages are usually in the 50s-low 60s. This is a self taugh class, she expects you to work in groups and figure most things on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: u will easily find that no one in the class really follows her lecture. here is the situation, if u know it, u dont need her to explain it. if u dont know it, u cannot figure out her lecture. Now, she doesnt show any question which will be in the exam before the exam. And u only have 80 minutes to solve a 2hrs test. u will waste many time on clas

She's an awesome lecturer, the 10 minutes or so a class she'll talk. The rest is all group work and teaching each other what to do. If your group doesn't know how to do the problem, you're stuck. You just hope she doesn't randomly call on you to answer the question. If you don't know the answer of the question, she makes you feel stupid publicly.

Worst teacher I've had at uwb yet. This is essentially a self-study class because she doesn't teach you anything or walk you through anything. I took an intro class with her but i felt disadvantaged that I didn't already know physics. She's very condescending too and gives an aura of pretentiousness.

Quite possibly the worst teacher I've ever had period. Her in-class material that she 'teaches' if you can call it that is all so basic compared to the exams and homework she gives you. Almost every problem has super confusing or off-putting wording. Her lectures are the equivalent of teaching 1+12 then asking you to solve calc-level math.

Dr. Erin Hill has an interesting teaching methodology . She claims she never lectures but the rare case she does, she calls them 'mini lectures'. She is organized and wants the best for the class, but instead of teaching us stuff we need to know, she uses a guided leaning method where students figure things on their own. This is self study class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The lectures are very group-oriented and focuses a lot on examples that 95% of the class won't solve on the first try. Be prepared to undergo a lot of tight/close scheduling. By the time you take the second exam, homework (resource worksheets) for chapters not covered by the exam will be due. You'll need to self-learn a lot of things to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She doesn't lecture on the chapter, she lectures on couple questions that apparently "majority of the class asked for," but I didn't and overall throughout the quarter, you're going to be confused and not know what you're learning in the class and she expects you to know physics before you enter her class.
She doesn't give good lectures, she doesn't explain the problem well. She expects her students to not use online resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Hill is a great professor and is probably one of the best professors I've had at UWB. Her lecturing style involves randomized group work, but don't be dismayed by this; it makes lectures extremely interactive. Her exams are initially difficult, but decrease in difficulty over the quarter. I really recommend that you take her for mechanics!

She's really good and has students work in teams, which is nice but is not a very good lecturer as she doesn't really give time to take notes on the rare occasion that she lectures. She gives amazing feedback and knows what she's talking about, I highly recommend you take her class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is a great professor overall. She helps people engage into group work and conversations that will be useful in the future. She shows interests in her work and gives everyone a fair chance and help. I wish she taught more physics classes because I enjoy the way she teaches - more group work and practice problems, less lecturing.

Erin is awesome. She really cares about her students' learning. If you go to her office, she will spend as much time as needed until you understand the material. She will even approach you in the QSC and offer help. She can be a little snippy occasionally. She is really excited about her peer-education based teaching method, but I am not a fan.

Erin uses an awesome innovative teaching style that fosters student collaboration. The collaborative aspect made the class very enjoyable. The criteria for succeeding in the course was very clear in my opinion.

Unless it is essential to your major or you're super into physics already, do not take this class.  Her teaching style is more you read the book and then during lecture she answers your questions with other questions to "lead you along the right path".  Very much a self taught class so if you'd like someone to teach you, I would take another class.

She was very interested in physics, but even more interested in her teaching methodology. She has cut some stuff back like her problem solving guideline, but sometimes the method seems to come before the material. Lots of work outside of class, and no late work accepted. She is very passionate though, and willing to change a little if students wish

If you plan on taking physics 121 @ UWB, I recommend Professor Hill! She requires a lot of work out of classroom then most professors, but it is manageable. As long as you put in the effort and work, you will get a good grade! Her  grading it not heavily based on exam (35%). She will clarify anything that students are unsure about. She cares a lot!
Took her for physics 121 and all I have to say is WOW, she blow my mind away, who would have thought physics would be so interesting. Highly recommended, take her you won't regret it.

Class was awesome, she expects alot of out of class work but you will know the material very well.  In class lectures involve covering concepts in a group discussion type of way.  Good way to get the knowledge in class then practice/develop the skills through homework

Professor does not lecture, uses alternative learning approach of group-work. Assigns WebAssign HW that needs to be hand written. She isn't clear in what is expected of us in her opportunities (exams). Duration of class time is used to discuss a single basic problem that in most cases is way too broad compared to the material in exams.

This class felt extremely extremely time consuming outside of class. He is a tough grader, often not giving full points. He is a nice guy and gives good feedback, but that isn't enough to keep a class going smooth. He assigned a lot of readings and would always say he disagrees with what the author was saying.

Overall, I think Howard Hsu is a nice professor. However, his lectures often felt very unrefined, as though he was just telling rather than teaching. The assignments tended to be fairly easy. However, he does have an in-person midterm. Overall, take this class if you want a less test-heavy class, since there is no final exam, only a midterm.
Very boring class, lectures basically the whole 2 hours of the class time. The class is very project based, and the criteria is not very clear. Sometimes it feels like he makes up stuff for feedback.

Very easy class. Some of the assignments he gives can be tedious to follow the guidelines, but overall he's pretty lenient. Encourages participation on all assignments and discussions. Textbook used very little. Understanding and pretty lenient on most things, but be ready to follow hard guidelines on assignments occasionally.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was easy, minimal assignments, and one group project. Prof. Hsu doesn't judge your artistic talent, just be sure to have reasoning for the decisions you make. Submit assignments complete and on time and you'll get great grades. The only class I've had where I wish the lectures were more in-depth, he makes the subjects really entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Each reading assignment (20-60 pages per week) is followed by a quiz (20-minutes and 3-5 multiple choice questions). Be sure to take notes since you don't have time to comb through. Midterm is open book and open notes taken from the projects, lectures, and book. Very relaxed and understanding teacher. Overall easy course, highly recommend.

I really enjoyed this class because it was recreational and helped me discover something new about myself. Learning in this class was a meditative process for me, and I feel like I've healed because of it. I took Calculus 2 and a coding class along with this class, and without this class and Prof Hsu, I might have gone crazy.

The class was easy as it's simply a first-year requirement; however, Hsu was picky about aspects of projects that didn't fit a certain "vibe" that he never even specified. I was close to losing my 4.0 due to ambiguous instructions. Also, most of the time feedback looks exactly the same across multiple students. Overall, pretty chill class.

Fun guy, gives wonderful, thoughtful and useful feedback on photos. Some textbook reading but if you pay attention and take notes you'll be fine. Midterm was open note. Some lectures get boring. Overall great class, easy and creative. You'll love it if you're artistic.

He is really nice but his grading is kind of harsh. He wants assignments done his way and won't give you full points even though what you submitted fits the criteria of the assignment.He is really passionate about what he teaches.Weekly attendance is required he gives a class code to submit for points at the end of class (can't leave early)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had this professor a few times, and he's great honestly. Participation points, and give clear good constructive feedback. I highly recommend his classes, the only thing is they can feel like they drag on when we're just looking at student presentations but other than that it's fun.

Howard is a very caring professor and always made class feel welcoming. Sometimes it can get a little boring, but I liked how when we had class discussions, he was very open ended and encouraged people to speak. His assignments are fun to do and feel like a hobby, not hw. You will not regret taking this class. Great guy, doesn't grade hard either.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very interesting class and you can tell that he's passionate about photography. He provides great feedback and you will do fine as long as you pay attention. Lots of actual photography practice in class and he will answer any and every question you ask. You need 98% for a 4.0, but he's not a tough grader. Just make sure you study for the midterm.

Howard Hsu is an amazing professor and I am going to miss him next quarter. He is caring, funny, and just overall an awesome guy. His class was not difficult at all, as long as you pay at least a little bit of attention you'll be okay. Even if you do have questions or need help, he is always there to help you. I recommend Professor Hsu 100%.
He is a great teacher, very smart, and totally worth taking this class as well.. Just take his classes, he is awesome

Kind professor that wants to listen to his students, but has a heavy emphasis on lectures. There is little homework outside of the weekly quizzes that we get based on a 50 page reading from the textbook. I was bored to death, and although he isn't a tough grader and the workload is light, I was sick of textbook reading and quizzes based on them.

Howards a nice guy and fun prof. I took BIS132 BISIA350 and BIS331 with him (331 in person). Fairly easy grader and very understanding, and a quick emailer. My only gripe with him is that his classes are a bit heavy on presentations (though thats understandable since theyre mostly workshops). If you have social anxiety, look into DRS accommodations
Very good Professor of IAS, I like his classes!

Nice enough guy and interesting class, but often shared (what was probably the majority) of the classes political views but strongly neglected that other people might not share the same views if that makes sense.

Howard is far and away one of the best professors I've had during university. He's super down-to-earth, supportive of all his students, and assigns a really manageable amount of work -- I never felt stressed out about getting assignments done for his class. Would take the same class for credit if I could. A+ professor.

I took history of photography with him and I felt like I learned nothing, maybe he's better in actual photography classes like these reviews (which is why I took him) say. This class is not easy and is very writing intensive. He grades on your own opinion and assigns WAY too much at the end of the quarter. Lectures are very boring and rather dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Howard is a great professor and great person. I had tons of fun in his photography class, and he was always understanding in terms of workload and support. Some may find him boring, but he's invested in your learning and I find him hilarious and full of good ideas and lessons.

I'm still taking Howard's class and honestly, he's a great teacher. He gives great feedback on your work and the class is a lot of fun if you want to get into photography or if you have a good amount of experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took all 3 BCOREs with him (104, 117, 120) this year. He is a pretty fair grader who knows not everyone is artistically inclined and has a lot of compassion for students. He's very good at explaining content and helping you find additional resources, and has a great sense of humor. Also his cat is the best. He made my freshman year worth it.

This class was phenomenal. Howard is an extremely knowledgeable as well as kind and open-minded professor, which is really something to admire in a teacher. I've never really looked at photography the way he does. His own photography work is really interesting too. If you want to learn both photography AND modern art philosophy I recommend 350!

Howard Hsu is a great teacher. His lectures are fun and interesting, and he always manages to keep the class engaged. I came to really enjoy his dry humor and his impactful teaching style. He also has a decently impressive career background in the photography world. I'd take another class with him for sure.

I took this class expecting a lot of the usual boring photography stuff but the class turned out to be more fun than work. The material from the readings is interesting and the projects give you a lot of freedom. We had a great Zoom class and everyone in it had fun and bonded, which he helped initiate by playing online games on the first day.

Howard is awesome. He is very knowledgeable about photography, and he really cares about students and what they learn. Speak with him and let him know who you are, he often asks about students' interests and would love to talk with you about them after class. Great sense of humor too, even if he doesn't seem that way at first.

Howard is really knowledgeable and insightful, yet he makes the class accessible to all learning styles, levels, and speeds. He is also very organized and caring, and likes to talk about current events and wants to get to know his students on a more personal level, which is something to admire.

Howard is a superb professor. He's really friendly, positive, and organized, and very knowledgeable about his subject too. That's probably the perfect package in terms of a professor, tbh, especially a photography professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: In his photo class right now and I'm having such a great time. We just finished the class yesterday, and I had such a good time! Howard is really knowledgeable and passionate about photography, and he's really helpful in and outside of class. His feedback is really in depth which helps students invaluably.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In his class (photography & digital art) right now, I really enjoy it, it's a really fun class to take! He doesn't really make the class more difficult than it needs to be, he gives great feedback, and he's interesting to learn from and listen to. I like how he covers both actual photography practice and the history of photography in our class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hsu was amazing. You can tell he is passionate about photography and knows what he's teaching. He gives helpful feedback and actually gives suggestions for improvement. Attendance is important, but just talk to him and he'll understand if something's going on. Would take again.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Very enthusiastic, clear and fun to work with. Willing to answer/clarify and go over any topic. Teaches photography the right way by practically taking photos and using various camera settings. The class has 2 projects, 1 midterm and lots of in-class activities. Fun, easy A class for VLPA credits.

Definitely one of THE best professors I have had so far, for sure. I'm only in my second quarter at UWB (MCS major and Bellevue College transfer) and he's better than all the professors I've had before. Really enthusiastic about teaching, loves supporting students, and is very accessible outside class.

Howard made photography class so simple. Hes a funny guy and definitely knows what hes teaching. I bought the textbook but didnt use it once, so save yourself $20. Takes attendance everyday and always gave good feedback to everyones images. Open minded and overall easy A class
LOVED his class and his teaching style! Howard is awesome.
awesome professor & definitely goes to his office hour (help a lot especially for midterm and finals)
Great professor.
I would suggest as a professor, this guy is fair and organized, which can be hard to find in professors.

reviews.comment: Overall a solid pick if you need VLPA credit, a cool and laid-back guy with actual photography experience. Helpful if you go to him with questions, but isn't necessarily one to seek YOU out if you're struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Howard was a pretty cool guy, I had to miss a lecture due to an orthodontist appointment and emailed him a few days in advance and he didn't lower my participation!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Won't give you 100% on ANYTHING.  That's ok though, Howard was great at explaining both the technical side of photography, as well as being clear with the art history half of the class.  Made sure that everyone was on the same page before he moved on.  Really chill guy, if you like bikes, he'll like you a lot more.

Howard was a very good teacher. He explained things really well and helped students whenever needed. He gives a couple extra credit opportunities throughout the quarter which are definitely helpful! Super approachable and an overall chill guy.
He is pretty dry. You might want to fall asleep during his lectures. He also assigns a lot of stuff at once, you might have a break for about 2 weeks but then he will drop a lot on you.

Professor Hsu is very clear and has a lot of interest and experience in the subject (photography).  Lots of time is given for each project, and therefore a lot of creativity and thought is expected to go into each assignment.  On the midterm, the only test given, do not underestimate the material he expects you to know!
Really clear instruction. Not too hard and made class very enjoyable.

The class was well organized and creative. Howard was very clear, helpful, and supportive of everyone's work. He gave students just the right amount of time to prepare for big projectsshoots and he made the material VERY interesting. The structure of the class was very good. The class was very fun, explorative, and intellectual!
This class was so hard! Jim Hogg or "Jimmy Bob" was a very strict teacher when i was in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Jim is one of the best professors in the CSSE program. Midterm/Final are weighted very low so what matters most is your compiler assignments, which are all very doable. Gives extensions if you need and is very willing to work with you to succeed. Definitely would recommend this class and take Jim anytime you can!

Took CSS112 (didn't show up as an option). Super qualified, and clearly loves coding and teaching. Make sure to submit HWs on time -- he doesn't accept late work! But, office hours are helpful and the class is easy. Has very reasonable grading criteria and expectations. There were extra credit problems at the end of most HWs.

Best CS professor at UWB hands down. his tests are easier than other professors but that doesn't mean the class is hard. The class is VERY difficult and you have to really work for it with Hogg to get a good grade. The HW/Projects are challenging too
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a good teacher.

reviews.comment: Prof. Hogg is one of the best in UWB. He is very caring and easily accessible outside of the class. Responds to emails fast, and answers any questions that you have. The course itself is hard, and if you are taking someone else then you are gonna make your life more hard. Take him, hes the nicest teacher hands down.
You are doing yourself a disservice by not taking Professor Hogg. One of the nicest, fairest, and most engaging professors at UWB.

Brilliant instructor who has industry experience with everything he teaches. Extremely clear grading criteria - he gives you his tests. He cares so much about his students. He is very kind and will help you a lot to make things easier. I went through a tough time outside of school during one of his classes and he was very understanding.
Professor Hogg is one of my favorite professors at UWB, hes really understanding and will try his best to answer all your questions. Fast reply on questions via email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great at teaching operating systems, he did it for years at Microsoft. Caring dude.

Professor Jim is a new teacher and I was worried that he would be another hard grader and boring lecturer. He defiantly scored way above my expectations, his lectures are great and he does a very good job answering questions in class. He asked for feedback about his lectures and had office hours right after class, which were very convenient. 10/10
Takes too long to grade

Takes way too long to grade, doesnt give any feedback, barely answers your questions. He barely puts any effort into the class, you can clearly tell. I took his lab class and he was so great. He could go off tangent at times, but he was readily available to help, when you needed it. It was my first lab for physics, but it felt like a breeze with his help. I am taking for BPHYS 118, next quarter as well.
Tough class (but it's physics and in summer quarter too), super nice grader though, he gave people back points. Just work hard and you'll earn a good grade.
