I liked the assignments and readings. He was alright as a teacher. Seems like a cool person. Didn't like the hybrid format.

Nice guy but could be a better teacher. He told us this was his first time teaching this class. Assignments have confusing directions and are tough but doable even for non-art majors. Don't miss class, you'll miss out on a lot of important info and lose points.

He's an interesting guy and I liked the way he taught and the readings, but I found his assignments to be incredibly confusing. The instructions are very long, to the point where I had to read everything multiple times. He gives critical feedback but is a somewhat easy grader. I lost a ton of points for missing class which shouldn't be the case.
I liked the class material and the activities (especially as we moved onto video editing) but I really didn't like the way he treated students or gave feedback. At least I got a 4.0.

He took a potentially interesting topic (remix culture) and kinda butchered it. He was nice enough, and good at teaching the editing software, but somewhat critical of students. I feel like wanted us to get good grades in his class but he didn't really teach in an effective manner to accomplish this. The assignments take more time than they should.

This was an OK class experience. Prof. Milutis is a good teacher, in that he communicates in a clear and understandable way and makes learning accessible, but he's disorganized, pretentious, and can just be insufferable sometimes. At least he knows what he's talking about. The stuff we read in this class was really cool though.

He's rather narrow-minded (especially for an artist) and he doesn't understand that everyone learns differently, but he was still very responsive and accessible outside of class. Grading is unreasonably tough and feedback is very cryptic.

Interesting personality, doesn't assign a lot of work, but can be a tough grader. There are many small in class participation points that really add up if you skip class. He WILL shoot down your work for arbitrary, personal reasons.

While the content is conveyed clearly, the way this professor grades is very unhelpful when it comes to promoting learning. His grading techniques are very, very subjective and critical. My experience in another class with this professor (took BISIA 340 and 483) revealed this same problem. Has a real "I'm better than you" mindset.

Terrible prof. He caused me to drop my art minor, told me that I was going to fail the class early in the quarter (which I didn't, but still dropped my minor because he told me I'd fail), violated my FERPA rights by telling others about his comments on my work, was extremely rude, attacked my work constantly, and made me cry often.

Smart and knowledgeable but extremely full of himself. Class structure indicates he does not care if your grade reflects what you've learned in any way because he's extremely critical of everything. He is clearly making his job easier by making ours harder. I would recommend avoiding this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is brutal. I log off Zoom every day feeling dumber than I did the day before. He's extremely critical BUT puts in no effort when grading despite the insane amount of work this class has you put in.

Solid class. There's a lot to learn in a short time, but it's worth it. Lots of freedom in your projects, as long as you put in the workyou'll get from this class what you put in. Joe is crazy knowledgeable about a lot of subjects and can be super helpful. I think he really cares about helping people expand their tool set and make good work. 5s
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Genuinely fun to be in his class - can't remember the last time I both laughed til I couldn't breathe and learned something entirely new about writing. Like the tags say, exceptionally committed to solid, workable feedback. If you actually give a damn about improving your craft and learning new stuff, you will do well and enjoy it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I tried to like him, I really did but he was nothing but rude from the first day. I worked my ass off in this class, but nothing is ever "good" for him, he always has to complain about something. I went to multiple office hours, & every class, always did homework, & he still gave me an ok grade. Seems like teaching was his only career option....

I took this class expecting a lot of usual boring chore type assignments but the class turned out to be more fun than work. The material from the readings is interesting and hip and the projects give you the freedom to work on media that you chose if it will fit the parameters in the assignments. We had a great class and everyone had there had fun.
Professor Milutis is extremely knowledgeable and enthusiastic. He gives blunt, honest, and refreshingly useful feedback in a creative workshop setting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very snobby, very vague and very into Freud. Be prepared to be down graded if your ideas don't match his, and to be confused about assignments even after asking repeatedly for clarification. I do not recommend him at all.

It's easy to do well in his class if you want to. Honestly, all you need to do is be there, do the readings, and participate (duh). A lot of people have issues with his attendance policy, but C'MON. My experience with Milutis was very positive and he helped me create projects I wanted to in the course with good, honest critique and available help.

The class was engaging and the material was extensive. Having no background in the arts, I found the course challenging and complex.Overall the professor was knowledgeable in the material and techniques used within the course and programs used. Limited in class time for projects requires additional out of class commitments for the students.

His idea of what is considered to be "good work" is the complete opposite of our culture right now.  It is extremely hard to follow along with editing in the software unless you have had previous experience, there aren't textbooks or guidelines to follow.  Be prepared to spend a lot of time outside of class on the projects.  He talks A LOT.
Ok. Smart but distractingly full of himself.
He is a great professor, interesting, funny and very passionate about his classes. He is also a talented artist and well worth taking.
I really like this teacher. He's in general just a pretty cool guy and he really knows his stuff. Yes you have to work hard but it's worth it.
Milutis thinks most Americans are bourgeois. He's right, but to look down thy nose is bad form for an instructor.

He does bring a new perspective to UWB but is snobby. He picks favorites in the beginging and if he doesnt like you there is not way on getting on his good side. He make inappropriate comments and assumptions about students. You need to put in a lot more work than you think for the class

very fun class a must for any student who wants to succeed in the media driven world. Creativity is highly encouraged. If you find yourself confused, don't worry about it. That is the intent. Joe has a very real and effective teaching approach.

Milutis is a new instructor to UWB campus. He brings some much needed fresh air and new teaching style, but he has a snobby side to his personality. He made many offensive remarks to the students or their work. He gets frustrated easily. The instructions were vague. prepare to use alot of media.

Salmon man can be really disorganized at times but honestly if you just go to class and listen you'll probably be more than okay on the exams. People give him too much criticism but hes more understanding than many of the other professors

Doing all the codon assignments and having a high lab grade gets you a decent passing grade for this class. The lectures were sometimes helpful and not helpful, and he makes some jokes here and there but not worth going to every lecture. The exams required a lot of writing. He's an alright professor overall.

He is a nice person but lectures are long and exams are difficult, you can pass with all exams avg of 50-60% when asked about concepts will just repeat himself instead explaining it in a different way. you walk out of lectures knowing nothing and having to teach yourself everything, but still attend them cuz HW sheets will randomly be passed out.
He cared about his salmon more than his students. Being so serious when I say avoid this class. Nice dude but has no teaching skills

The professor is very nice, and is passionate and knowledgeable in what he's teaching. The class is a bit lecture-heavy, but if you go to every class, pay attention and grasp the material, the exams are fairly straightforward. The main downside for me was that the Canvas page felt a bit disorganized (helpful materials), and grades were posted late

Lectures are really boring because it's just him yapping, but be sure to take notes on the slides because many exam questions come from it, so read the slides religiously. You can pass this class with low exam scores (~50-60) but you have to do all the homework and lab work. Be prepared to love salmon by the end of the quarter :)
The class is disorganized, codon sucks, exam averages are 60-65%.

Harsh grader, marks answers incorrectly and doesn't explain why, answer key is vague, study guide is vague, does not grade or respond fast, always has issues with Codon. lectures are okay but they can be unproductive. Had to reteach myself some topics as it wasn't clearly provided in his lecture slides.

If I could again, I wouldn't ever take him, to be honest. The TA does a horrible job at grading, and I don't think they're even sure what they're grading or even how to grade, cause the Key is so vague. If you don't use a sentence, the key has your whole answer is wrong. Rather would of skipped this professor to be honest. DO NOT TAKE HIM
Don't take him isn't organized and doesn't seem to care if the students pass his class or not.
exams hard af, study guides make me feel like im cramming the whole textbook for one exam
bro is terrible, very unorganized no actual study exam prep.

Will send out a study guide for the exam on Sunday morning, and expect you to have enough time to study to take it on Tuesday morning (until people mass email him to change it to Thursday which still isn't a full week of study time.) No open note with tons of different material to memorize, and is too difficult for an intro 100 class.

Kind and comedic lecturer but doesn't communicate what will be covered on exams at all. That said, super protective of his students and their learning which I appreciate eg. Some communist group barged into our classroom for a protest, they were led by some oddball named Mantak Singh(?) who was shouting on a megaphone. Jeff booted the creep out!!

I loved Jensen as a professor and as a person. Although his other upper level classes may be considered difficult, his Bio180 class is really light and manageable. One of the best choice for bio prof at UWB

Took his class for research, there are both lab based and field based focuses, you will need to do a presentation at the end but it's very simple. The class is enjoyable and very engaging. Would recommend 100%!

Jensen's great if you want to do research! He's a fish enthusiast and I've learnt a lot from him. He can be a little scatterbrained and hard to reach online, but he's dedicated to research and is really amazing to talk to. BBIO495 and 499 are easy, enjoyable classes with heavy work involved. Showing up matters.

Class was a bit challenging with lots of information to learn, but professor provides useful lecture recordings + homework through Codon. (homework was very helpful to earn more points and understanding the concepts) Professor frequently keeps up with posting worksheets and study guides and that helped a lot. Overall, I'd take the professor again.

Great professor, wants you to learn. Lectures are amazing, but the recordings suck so make sure to attend. Course content is difficult, but he teaches it really well and gives plenty of assignments so one bad exam wont screw everything up. Never responds to emails, though. Take notes and do all handouts/homework and you'll be fine. Just gotta try.

amazing prof & great person. people way too harsh bc they don't do well in course. course material tough and high volume. not an easy A, but absolutely do-able w proper effort. funny lecturer & entertaining. super busy, never responds to emails. cares ab his students & wants them all to do well. highly reccomend. non-conventional teaching style

He's a great professor who is really knowledgeable in his subject. He uses a new software called that gives his students better readings and assignments that help you learn and prep for exams, but his lectures are most important. If you have any questions though, prepare to talk to him during class or office hours, He never responds to emails.

This professor doesn't communicate with the students all he does is give lectures and exams. Class averages for the exams was around a 58%. He doesn't hold office ours but rather leaves it up to the TA to answer questions that people may have. If you're planning on applying to med school or anything like it DO NOT take him, he will destroy your GPA

His exams are weighed heavily but are similar to his lectures so pay attention when he's teaching. He also gives other assignments and quizzes to help your grade so you can still pass even if you fail one of his exams. His lectures are straightforward forward and he gives amazing examples.

Dr. Jensen was an amazing professor and his class was a great introduction to the biology series! Before exams, he would give out study guides and so long as you do those and look over the key afterwards, you're practically set for his exams. Exams were never graded harshly and you could make up a bad exam score by doing what is asked in lab.

He gave a great overview and foundation for this subject. Has a lot of passion and lectures include tons of examples to build understanding. ~75% of these reviews are too harsh - while you do need to pay attention in lectures to succeed, taking good notes and reviewing his worksheets/lectures (all are recorded) is all you need to study for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As a lecturer, he is completely useless, but the diagrams he draws on the board are what you really need to pay attention to. Take pictures and try to get an intimate understanding of the concepts rather than trying to remember every word he says. He never replies to emails, so you're better off emailing the lab prof for help.

Avoid, I know its impossible because he is the only one who teaches the class but he does not care about students passing (weed out professor). I have taken bio 2 and 3 now and gotten A's in both, so I know its not me....Literally ended his class with a C- as most of my class did as well.

As I can only write 350 characters, here is a summary. Have spoken to him once and he told me to "hold on a minute," and the only time I ever wrote him an email, he never got back to me. With harsh grading, and hard to follow during lectures, I mostly go home and go through the slides on my own time. Does not communicate well regarding assignments.

I have no clue why Jensen has a bad rep -- he's genuinely a great lecturer and you can tell he spends a lot of effort curating the course. He values comprehension rather than memory -- so all of the concepts in his lecture tie into one-another very cohesively. He is a fish enthusiast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, one of the worst class experiences i have had in my entire college term and I am a CSS student. Avoid him at all costs, it does not matter how much you study it is impossible to say what will be on the exam and he grades like passing us is going to cost him both his kidneys. GPA killer, med school killer..not joking at all.

He lectures like he is letting his intrusive thoughts win every single time! It is so hard to follow what he says during lectures and unclear what to expect on the exam.There are always going to be those sweaty people in the class who get a good grade and say he is good, but he really isn't. Avoid at all costs, GPA KILLER! MED SCHOOL KILLER!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So unorganized, and the exams don't even relate to what you learn on or do worksheets on. He'll ask questions he barely goes over in class and doesn't grade things probably by till the quarter is over, so you don't know your grade. Don't take unless you wanna tank your gpa.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer and kind/helpful. He may grade hard but going to class and actually studying is integral to success. GO TO CLASS. Lectures are recorded but not as good as in person. Honestly, the organization was fine, not as bad as these reviews made it out to be. I don't doubt these reviews, but I think that Jensen definitely learned from them.

midterms are not too bad, just study days prior. The final shouldn't be so hard given already bad test averages. not accessible outside of class. grades 90% of things end of finals week. says the curve will help a lot but only helped my GPA of 0.1. lectures recorded but hard to see so go to the lecture. I think only 1 or 2 got a 4.0 out of hundreds

Knowledgeable person, lectures are easy to understand. EXTREMELY unorganized course, very hard grader, takes forever to grade. If you have the chance to avoid him, you should. Coming from a student who manages their own time well, studies frequently, and gets good grades in other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not the worst teacher, but bad in ways. First, gives us worksheets that are graded that are very beneficial for exams, but cant use them because they arent even graded until after taking the final exam. Study guides dont help, takes way too long to post final graded (literally does them the day they are due), therefore cant talk to him about em

Jensen does not teach to teach, he stated that he doesnt expect us to remember anything from this class. I wanted to do well but it was hard when the study guides are posted 1 week before each midterm and final and they are 20-30 pages long. We all studied our hardest but still had a class average of 61 on both midterms. Unorganized

I would avoid taking a class with Jensen. Specifically 335. He's very passionate about the fish but that DOESN"T mean he should teach students. Most unorganized professor i've had. People warned me about him but I didn't believe them until I experienced the horror. Quarter is over and still hasn't opened the modules. But will still test you on it.

People complain a lot about him because they are truly lazy. Jensen's lecture is easy to understand. It's his voice that makes people sleepy. Rewatch the lecture and you'll see. His tests are not tricky at all. Everything is based on the class lecture. Textbook is helpful, just look at yurs before complaining. He's a good person at heart, seriously

Attendance isnt mandatory but it should be. You have to buy the book but you won't use it. His lectures cover what will be on the exam. His exams are outrageously difficult. Not to mention, his lectures are an hour and a half of nonstop info. This class requires an insane amount of time and energy from the student and none from the prof. Avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible organization, minimal effort by Jensen to facilitate learning in an online learning environment. Class is almost entirely self-taught, and there are hours upon hours of recorded lecture material to get through. "Study guides" vaguely related to material covered in the exam. Be ready for a lot of independent study.

Jensen focuses lectures on the main points. As the student you have to come prepared or fill in the between as supplement with the textbook. This is a weed out class. Dont expect an easy A. Work hard. Communicate with the TAs and come to office hours.

The class was interesting in terms of content. It was HOURS AND HOURS OF RECORDED LECTURES. I took this class during covid, and the amount of material, assignments, quizzes, labs, exams, and work was just insane. The professor is not accessible outside of class. He doesn't reply to ANY emails and disregards any student questions/grade changes/etc!

The worst teacher at UW Bothell do not take him if you can avoid it!! Lectures rarely relate to actual tests and quizzes, study guides did not help with exams or final. Overall very unorganized, doesnt follow the same standards that most other professors tend to follow, not helpful and unclear when answering students questions... I could go on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lectures and readings barely related to the test and any problems done in class were not on the test. His Pfs do all the grading and they grade hard, but maybe it wouldnt be so hard if the tests related to what we did in class. Lectures are hard to follow. Does the least amount to prepare for tests, no study guides, no reviews at all.

Obviously online learning is a hard thing to adjust to. But we need effort from the student and teacher to be successful. It feels as thought Jensen did the bare minimum to transfer to online. He gave the lowest amount of study resources out of any teacher I have ever had in person or online. He gives long confusing explanantions. Overall. BAD.

This professor is extremely unorganized. The exams are weighted very heavily. The class material rarely relates to what is on the exams. He made us take a huge exam 1 week before our comprehensive final, and added new material the week of our final. I would strongly suggest that you do not take a class with this professor. It will save your gpa.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I hate leaving this review, but I feel I must. Personally I like Jensen.. but he's a terrible lecturer. Lectures are extremely convoluted and barely line up with the tests. Even though he says to "focus on concepts," the PFs do all of the grading and have a key with terms. So yeah, focus on vocabulary. I worked my butt off and still only got a 3.5
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He came across as really disorganized, only two of our many assignments had been graded by the end of the term. His exams are out of left field. study all you want 3/4 of the material will not be on the exam, and the questions on it won't really connect in a sensible way. It felt like he put a very low level of effort into teaching this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. He does not try to make things easier for students to understand. He does not care if the class average is a D. His letures are very hard to follow and the PF's grade harsh, you have little room to mess make mistakes. If you have an option to take a different professor, do it!

Hes such an awful teacher. This is considered an introductory level biology class. He should be teaching concepts in detail, not going over concepts like theyre review for students new to Bio. I dont learn from these lecturers. If I have another teacher like this at UWB im leaving this school and going elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He is a very approachable professor and really cares about his students learning but he is too smart to the point where he doesn't explain the material too well and expects people to understand what he is rambling about during class. Going to office hours is helpful but it takes a LOT of time to direct through all of the information given.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Jensen is a great teacher and really cares if you learn in his class. He is willing to put out alternate explaination for when you dont understand. I was taking his undergrad research class, and it was great. A little unorganized, but overall I would have made the sam echoice to take his class. Would recomment!

Attend lectures! Jensen is pretty straightforward about everything, he tells you what you need to know, and he even goes over concepts MULTIPLE times and does everything step by step. The only way to not do very well in the class is if you don't dedicate time & effort to looking over lecture notes and truly understanding the material for an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Jensen's BBIO 180 class was one of the most difficult classes I've ever taken. The content itself was not difficult, but his test grading was ridiculous unfair! This created a lot of unnecessary stress. He lets the peer facilitators (students who have taken this class) grade the tests and they are incredibly harsh graders.

His class is unbelievable no matter how hard you work he makes it impossible for you to do well on the test. The graders are very harsh and unfair. The lectures are very confusing. Don't take his biology classes unless you can handle an overwhelming amount of stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Jensen lets his peer facilitators grade the exams. The pfs grade Exams unfairly by taking off points when they dont see an answer that is exactly as it is in the answer key, but may still be entirely correct. Dr. Jensen has still not given my regrade back after 4 weeks since returning my exam. He takes ages to grade anything.

His lectures are very disorganized and sometimes confusing. You have to attend the class because some of the material is not in the book. Despite the fact that his questions are vaguely written on exams and you can't really tell what he is asking for he lets his assistants (students) grades the papers and they grade it very harshly and not fairly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jensen is an interesting lecturer and does not assign too much work. His tests are very heavy. They all consisting of purely 100% short answer questions. Good thing to be aware of. Attending lectures is helpful because he repeats many questions on the exam, but they are also in his incredibly detailed study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Extremely approachable and knowledgeable professor. You must attend lectures because he has material on the exam not discussed in the book. I found that by reading all the chapters in the book, attending lectures, and reviewing all of the in class activities, you should do decent on the exams. This class takes ALOT of your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His Salmon and society class was really fun and informative, I would take it again in a heartbeat. This class was heavily dependent on student participation, so if you are hoping to fly under the radar than DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. If you want real world explanations and applications than this is your class.

Evolution was a hard class but if you go to lecture and give each assignment some genuine critical thought you will make it through. His tests are difficult but if you go over the study guide he provides then you will be ok.

Jensen is an ok professor. His lectures are kind of scrambled and does not explain well. His writing tends to be disorganized and  you need to be in the front of the class to be able to read it. If you can't read it then you need to be able to listen and follow along for the full 2 hour lecture, which sucks coz it takes so much energy at 8:45 AM.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He says so from the beginning of the quarter that you won't do well if you're not in class because he mentions stuff that are not on the slides or textbook. I don't know why you would want to skip class because you're paying to be here. Dr. Jensen is a great professor. You can see him at office hours and he answers questions fully.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jensen is highly underrated.  Just pay attention in lecture and the exams will be a breeze. Plus he repeats himself enough that you know exactly what's going to be on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures go on tangents very often. Questions on worksheets are very confusingly written, and answers can often not be found by looking at slides he posts online or in the textbook. Relies heavily on remembering things he says in class. He also has not answered a single email I have sent him all quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I've had Jeff for 3 different classes. He's one of the most knowledgeable people I've ever met in my entire life. Lots of lecture happens on the whiteboard, slides are skimpy, attendance is important. Can be dry but is also witty and drops jokes often. Very personable and easy to approach, and can be easily reached outside of class. Great Prof!

I like Jeff. He's an interesting enough person, and he really knows his stuff and is genuinely interested it in. My issue is not about the course content or that way it's taught. It's the fact he is a tough grader, assignments/lecture notes are posted and expected to be done last minute, and the fact that grades aren't known until the last minute.

Though Jensen is very passionate about what he does, his lecture slides are very bland so it is very important to go to class or view panopto. The most aggravating part  was that he wrote so small and crammed all his drawings and terms together  on the white board making it very difficult to follow. Be prepared to put in work and lots ofstudy time!

Very confusing lecturer. I was clueless the first day and for the most part remained clueless for the rest of the quarter. I had to make a HUGE effort in order to do semi-decent. Tests are long, hard, unpredictable.. a good 10 people weren't able to finish the last exam. He goes in circles when answering questions, I never felt like I got an answer

He's a cool guy. Read his lectures, summary sheets, review sheets and you're off to a great start. His grader grades, it takes sometime for him to get back to regrades, but he will eventually if you have a good reason. Only bad thing its hard to predict what your final gpa is bc canvas messes up your percentage.
Take him if you really want to learn. Hes a really good biology teacher, and does everything he can to make sure everyone understands everything. He's the best lab teacher I ever had.
This guy real easy.. he curves.. I never went to class.. just did his study guides and 4.0 class...

Overall, I robust class when it comes to learning and integrating topics such as natural selection, evolutionary patterns and ecology. PAY ATTENTION in class and you should be fine. Didn't read the book at all. Test are heavily essay based. Material is covered quickly, so I would recommend not skipping class.

If you have horrible memorizing skills, then I would encourage you to develop the habit of memorizing something each day because all he's going to ask you in exams are the most random terms and gives you the weirdest scenarios. So goodluck, sleep a lot, and memorize memorize memorize!!
memorize, dont go to class, sleep.

MAKES EVOLUTION INTERESTING! MAKES CLEAR EXAMPLES, VERY FAIR ON EXAMS IF YOU STUDY AND HE CURVES SO ITS NOT HARD TO GET AN A- OR A. LABS ARE EASY. THE WHOLE CLASS IS EASY AND HES GREAT AT RESPONDING TO EMAILS. BEST PROFESSOR FOR EVOLUTION EVER! HE SAYS NO MEMORIZING BUT IF YOU MEMORIZE ITS LIKE A 20 MINUTE TEST IF YOU KNOW YOUR STUFF.

This professor is a ninja. He pulls curve balls and his tests are heavily weighted towards pure memorization of the weirdest terms. about 30%. Yes learn the bio concepts, but dont think for a second you wont be memorizing random useless terms. Very unclear on his learning goals. Very strict grader. Very chill in class. on his game with bio. 3.5-4.0

He is a pretty chill guy. He is pretty organized, but he is very knowledgeable about the tech industry which make it pretty cool to show up to class. Not a very good teacher but a very good leader/advisor I'd say.

His class is almost entirely group based but fairly boring if you arent super interested in the topic. However in general youll come out of the class with some nice and useful things learnt and a good grade.

Graded on a 100 point scale. 25 points were quizzes that happens every 2 weeks and they were easy. 70 points were group projects and the assignment expectations weren't that clear so it was pretty easy to lose points. 5 points peer review so make sure you contribute. Overall, class wasn't bad but to do well, you need a good group.

He knows his teaching style is unorthodox. Take his word for it when he says "you need to ask questions in order to succeed in this class". Lectures were very boring and not helpful for someone with minimal previous knowledge of the subject matter like me. He focuses on letting you do stuff with Pi's but its mostly copy-pasting commands into Linux.

This class is not what you expect. Multiple in-class group presentations (pretty low key but very boring when you're not presenting). Lectures are interesting but a lot goes over your head. Quizzes are not that hard if you study for like an hour or two total. Joshi is really cool though and extremely likable. More of an overview class.
Knowledgeable professor

He is the worst professor I have ever had. Prepare to not learning anything in this course. Not much homework, basically just do presentations each week. During the class presentation, I feel people are more nervous about their presentation than listen

He lied about assignment requirements, is extremely ambigious, did not honor is word when he asked for work when it was provided, and good luck figuring out what exactly he wants from his assignments.

He's not like a professor that just stand and talk, he's very into startups so a handful of advice towards getting jobs/internships. I get to know towards the end that his name is well known in the AI/ML space, he's an advisor for 2 bio AI startups, and is WELL connected. While hw instructions are confusing, but you can weight pros & cons
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easiest class I have ever taken. Professor is also very nice and caring. You can tell he actually cares about what he is teaching and has a lot of experience in the field he is teaching. He changes the class every quarter to stay up to date with relevant technology trends. Good class and actually useful information if you want to start a business.

This professor spends his entire lectures on tangents of business and talking about his resume and all the important people he knows. Comes off very entitled. Easy 4.0, but at the cost of a bad professor, long boring lectures, and a group presentation. Would not recommend course or the professor

The professor overall was great. His lectures are interesting. One downside is his instruction for his assignments are confusing. 1 point on each assignment will worth 1% of your grade. Grades can easily go down 1%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very solid choice! I enjoyed his class. He has a lot of experience/knowledge in the field. Comes from a cybersecurity background in the biomedical industry, so he can sometimes go on tangents with that type of stuff during lectures. His lectures are fun and you will learn a lot! He's one of those professors that don't like to stress students out

He's really hard to communicate with. If you ended up in certain assignments where your risk of not getting support is high, then I suggest you drop his course because there is little to not help at all.
He's very difficult to communicate with and doesn't reply  any emails about assignments. Id been in his class twice.

What i did not expect in this class is that there is just lack of enthusiasm when it comes to delivering the materials itself. I hope that whoever teaches this course will actually want to engage fully with high communication. Get additional support from other students to save your grades if you are taking this class.

The tests are challenging because they don't have study guides and are all based on lectures. Not being specific can bring down points aw well. I want to see improvement on the way exams are designed in the future.

It's hard to consume all the information he is lecturing on, because of his difficult teaching style. There are unnecessary things included in his presentation that were not on the exams which requires you to study 2x more if you don't catch all of it.

I agree with the others here. I just think his lectures are boring and sometimes it makes you wanna skip his class. Contents are not that interesting, i highly recommend taking another professor. I understand he is old but his instructional performance is affecting our grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Sisneros has been my favorite professor at UW so far! His lectures are really interesting I enjoy his use of outsourced clips. Tests are fair and give you the chance to showcase your knowledge in different ways which I appreciate as someone who struggles with tests. I will be taking his future classes and would highly recommend:))!

He is a great professor, his lectures and examples are very clear. Just try to read lectures intentionally and incentively so you can get a good grade. The exams consist of MCQ, Short answers and true/false questions! There are also quizzes based on the papers to read so watch lecture online!!

Lectures basically say monogamy, altruism, and free will don't exist. His lecture recordings are horrible because he walks towards and away from the mic. No study guides or consolidation of information. It's clear he is just here for research opportunities. Basically cram as much as you can from the slides, flush the info and repeat.

Lectures are basically one rambling run on sentence. He posts slides after class so you need to go back and try to add your notes later. His exams are full of trick questions and require you to memorize slides word for word. The sections and quizzes based on research papers are the only enjoyable part of the class. This is NOT an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is interesting but he is a boring lecturer. No need to use the textbook, he takes exam questions from lecture slides. If you utilize your notes and study well, easy A.

Dr. Sisneros became one of my favorite professors at UW after I took this class.  His lectures are so interesting and I learned a lot every day.  It's important to be really prepared for the tests but reading the book isn't necessary to get an A.  His slides are posted and really helpful for reviewing.

This class is definitely 4.0 possible. All of the slides are posted online and that's where the majority of his test questions come from, but I would still go to classpay attention because I didn't the last two weeks and bombed the final, which resulted in a 3.1 grade when I easily could've gotten a 3.5. So just work hard and you'll be fine!

Despite people saying it's a GPA killer class, I got a 4.0. There are 3 exams, 3 quizzes and a presentation. The quizzes are easy if you come to class the day he discusses the paper. The tests have MC, TF & short answer. He is VERY precise and specific so I suggest readingmemorizing his slides word for word. No textbook needed.

this class killed my gpa. I attended lecture everyday and attempted to take notes( tons of writing on each slide and moves quickly). definitely not a good test writer. all about memorizing the slides. and the textbook is not needed.

Easy class! You don't need to do the readings cause all of his tests were on his lecture slides and as long as you take good notes and study hard you will ace them! He's a nice guy, pretty chill and lectures well.

Very nice professor, very boring class. Tests are awful and I wish someone had told me to not even buy the textbook. It isn't helpful at all. You basically just memorize the slides. Worst part of all is there aren't any study guides. He tells you to just read his slides, which is bad when there are 200+. Huge disappointment.

LOVE THIS CLASS! The book he used complements lecture, but I rarely used it. Go to lecture (or record) and KNOW WHATS ON THE SLIDES! He gave group paper pres. followed by open paper quizzes Exams: Short answer, FIB, MC, T/F. awesome guy. Quiz lowered my grade, but thanks to exams, I got a 4.0. Just memorize & understand main topics!
Good class. Definitely recommend.

I loved this class, but he is a terrible test writer, great lecturer. The tests do not see if you understood concepts, just if you noticed and remember wording on slides. Writing good tests is hard, but when 135/200 pts are tests it matters. Either learn the info and take the GPA hit, or memorize the slides w/o processing and do well. Your choice.

Nice enough person, but boring class. Removes all of the cool examples and boils animal behavior down to a set of rules. I love animals and psychology, but I was VERY bored in this class. Sisneros also has an obsession with testing over the names of researchers instead of concepts, so be sure to study those.

Seems to be guessing about what to do in class and doesn't come across as very knowledgeable. Defensive any time students question her about something. Makes us switch seats every class and treats us like kids. Discouraged to know she is an adviser in the education program and that I will have to deal with her for 2 more years.

She is a nice person overall, but a mediocre professor. She does not explain classwork very well and is unclear with expectations. She says she is good with emails, she isn't. A lot of her readings are VERY long and she rambles on a lot of stuff that don't correlate with the course. Take a different education professor.

She seems like a nice person outside of class, however, she is not suited to be a college professor. She is EXTREMELY unprepared for class, and is very unclear about her expectations and discussion questions. She is a tough grader, is visibly uncomfortable with the course content and curriculum, and is very disorganized. Steer clear if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 'Professor' Anderson is a very, very, very, very, very bad teacher . Unclear expectations, awful lectures, doesn't respond to emails, mandatory attendance, rants that don't go anywhere, the list goes on and on... Get ready for discussions every class because she's too lazy to plan anything else. Certified rotten. 0.5/5
Don't misunderstand, she's actually looking out for you.  You just have to communicate with her.

She grades on attendance despite UW policy not to. Show up you get "participation points" that day. Don't and you get 02 points. This dropped me from an (A) to an (A-). The subject matter was adolescence in American culture. I felt we spent as much time on the topic of diversityrace as writing skills. The textbook was nice, though - cheapbrief.

I had a great experience in Kae's class even though writing is not my fav. She's not easy but if you put in the time and effort you can get a good grade. She is also very helpful in office hours. Some of my classmates were pretty disrespectful and she was quick to point it out. I think her directness can be off putting to some,  but that's on them.
She likes things done her way and her way only. Not very understanding. Her grading is very rough, and I am a good writer. I would not recommend her to anybody in my opinion.

Her class was okay she was rude, she expected too much especially for a 100 level class. Had her last year if you want a gpa booster this class is not for you. Worst class ever taken at uwb. She isn't even a real professor but a lecturer so snobby.

Contemporary Literature class was great. I am definitely not a reader, but she was able to pick our 3/4 amazing books that got me hooked and helped me become a better reader and deconstruct the readings. If you read and participate in class discussions, you will do great. I loved the final presentation and the test wasn't bad. She was amazing!

no homework but almost entirely self taught.  Her presentations usually do not include the equations--most of her teaching is done by telling you to do random things by looking at a problem.  80% of teaching is done on your own at home--so there's going to be several students who only show up for the exams.  everything is graded out of 80% curve
Grading scale is etrocious. You won't pass if your not great at fast test taking. Yes, extra credit is available but only makes up for no partial credit.
Professor Tronsen reads her powerpoint slides word for word. Her class is extremely boring but was a requirement.

AWESOME teacher. So helpful, goes out of her way to help students. There is work involved, she explains very well. Drops worst quiz and worst homework. Midterm and final are also doable. Highly Recommend!
there's group work every day, so don't miss class! read the chapters assigned before classes.

I learned a great deal in this course.  Professor Combs challenges you to learn the material, but is definitely there for support if you need it. If you are willing to put in the work you can learn a great deal and walk a way with a good grade. Quite a bit of reading and at home work required.

Prof was really clear on what material was going to be on exams. She provided study guides, which were really helpful in preparing for exams and showing what topics were important. Grading was fair and she offered opportunities for regrades. She always answered questions/emails. If you spend time studying, you can get a good grade in this class.

She doesn't curve. Her exams were super hard she seriously had 11 short answers for one exam like seriously ? We had to ask her to make a study guide if we didn't she would'nt had told us what would be on the test instead of the chapters. One of the worst professors I ever had at UWB never again!!!!!!!!! GPA KILLER.

Love this class! Prof used lots of different learning approaches e.g., clicker questions (which I like because it helped prepare for exams), in class group work, nice lecture slides with examples outside of what we read in the book etc. Challenging but learned a lot!

Nice professor, but very disorganized. Expects you to teach yourself from the book, then class is nothing but confusing power points with misinformation and graded clicker questions, making attendance pretty much mandatory. Always correcting herself as students point out contradictory information. Not hard to pass. Very hard to stay interested.
She expects you to do your work & is a great teacher!

Professor Shaw was a really understanding and kind teacher. Her lectures are about writing small prompts we then talk about in a seminar format. She cares for her students and tries to bring outside opportunities whenever possible.

Easy A, the prof is nice and respectable. The class is chill and you do a lot of prompting in journals. Its good to attend since certain deadlines could be unclear however you never have homework! Start early on your manuscript so you can reach the 10 page minimum requirement.

super easy class with katie shaw, lwk did nothing whole quarter lol, just prompts she would write on board and we answer, we grade ourselves at the end but make sure you participate in class to back yourself up. only paper due was a 10 page manuscript that has no prompt, super chill super easy class take it for the 307 credit trust me :)

Prof. Stephie is an amazing prof. She has a genuine passion to teach and can be clearly seen through her PowerPoints. I always appreciated her feedback and her "What's going on around campus" slides at the beginning of each class. She is so kind hearted and easy to follow.
Flexible to work with, nice professor, if you do the minimal grade you get an A-/A+
Really Chilll
Classes are very simple, structured in a simple manner and she accommodates all students regardless of writing ability. If you show up to class and do homework you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
An amazing professor. I highly recommend taking her class! 

She has a genuine passion for teaching and is incredibly kind and supportive. Her feedback on assignments is thoughtful and detailed.

Her grading is labor-based, so as long as you complete all the assignments, you should have no trouble earning a 4.0.

Professor Mlodnosky was very nice. The B Core class was not the most interesting. I would say that expectations for assignments outside of the group project were pretty clear, but the group project was not super fun due to it being overly complicated and confusing. You do need to actually do all the assignments to get a good grade in class.

lectures weren't that engaging but super chill class. got like 2-3 months behind on grading at one point but course load is 100% doable and she tries. no final/midterm, couple group projects, overall easy bcore credit

Very kind, knowledgeable, and caring. Class was very easy and expectations were clear. Slightly disorganized but had just started teaching at another university as well and trying to manage cross continental projects for our class (unplanned but easy) good class for a bcore to finish a last science credit before starting my major! 10/10 great prof.

Lots of assignments that are unclear and confusing, especially when it comes to the group project. The perusall is useless and takes forever to complete, I'd recommend just skimming it and adding a few comments here and there. This professor is otherwise really chill and flexible

BCHEM 164 Summer '25: The lab itself was hard but easier than 154 & 144 imo. The experiments were usually stressful, but she was super understanding and helpful, giving the class 30 min over time, every time, to finish the lab as much as we could. She was accessible and approachable to ask for help, and overall friendly & cared about her students!

Very test heavy, slides are messy and lots of irrelevant content, only reactions and a few concepts are useful. Prepare to use outside materials. No answer keys to any practice problems. No multiple choice questions. 
If you want a 4.0 only take if it's you're only hard class the quarter, or are very competent in learning ochem yourself.

I took B CHEM 154 with her, but RMP won't let me select that. Dr. Mlodnosky gives fantastic feedback on lab reports, and uses the rubric in a way that lets you understand exactly why you got the grade you did. She's also very willing to help during lab exercises, and will help you understand why a mistake you made may have changed your results.

Very tough grader, often deducting half-points/quarter-points or full-points on assignment worth 5 or less. Very unclear on grading criteria, which makes these deductions all the more frustrating. Easy to communicate with through canvas.

She such a thoughtful professor! I took her class for a discovery core class and you can tell when she's giving a lecture, she wants everyone to be engaged, is a student advocate for sure, and she's a gem :) Really puts the time into teaching topics. Recommend taking her if your also trying to go through the chem route (she gives really good tips)
Very easy class, was just a discovery core class. She's great tho. Karyn is a charming little gem. She devotes her time to teaching and you can tell she cares about us as students. Keep it up.
she is a good professor but she graded very harshly. she emails you back quickly compared to the other professors but her insight is not always the best. this is for her labs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Update: Course and professor were great! Class was canceled a few times and sometimes gave extra credit She's nice and understanding but for a 3-credit class, she could be a little picky on grading and gave a lot of work for only 1-3 points. If you have a good group that cares, then this class will be easy & you'll do great on assignments. 8/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment:
Currently still taking this class but so far so good as a course and professor. 

Will update/post another review when the quarter ends.

Her lectures r so boring but she'd force you to attend because there's graded classwork at the end. She doesn't care how bad or good your asm is cuz either way she gives you 0 feedback. NEVER put in any effort into your work. Discussions r also forced around boring and uninteresting topics. 99% of the time you just sit there in silence.

She is honestly the WORST professor I have ever had. I have taken multiple different art classes but she is the only professor who never gives you any feedback. Her lectures are boring, but you must sit through them to get the attendance. Always leave 30 minutes early because she obviously hates her job. Im not sure why the school is paying her

She is monotone and doesn't have much energy in her lectures. That being said, the class was fun and she clearly has a lot of experience in photography. She knows what she's talking about and what she's doing. I would recommend taking this class just to get your hands on a camera and the motivation to take pictures. This is for BISIA250 though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to take any of her classes, don't. Her monotone voice and her, what feels like, lack of interest in what she's saying will make coming to class impossible. Genuinely felt like torture to sit in her lectures. At least pretend to care about what you're teaching. Also stated to not come to class if sick, but are penalized for doing so.

Dr Shayne is truly an amazing professor & she singlehandedly is the reason I applied for a minor in GWSS. Yes her courses involve lots of reading and engagement but it's SO worth it. I've taken 2 of her classes and my only regret is that I didn't register for more before I graduated.

Hands down one of my favorite classes and professors I've had thus far. I can see on the surface how some of the negative reviews can feel true, but I assure once you attempt to pay attention and enjoy the class, your perception changes, mine from day one compared to end of quarter was certainly different for the better. Incredible class and prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: the greatest there ever was but also a tough grader. love this woman from Infinity to Infinity. she knows what she's talking about and is very passionate on the topic

I took this course as a cs major to branch out my knowledge. Dr. Shayne is the best professor I've ever had. You can tell she loves teaching and having meaningful conversations in class. The final exhibit assignment was so fun and I feel I grew a lot from learning the content. Assignments were pretty easy too if you do readings. Great class + prof!

Dr.Shayne is a passionate professor and very accomplished in her academia. People complaining about the grading of the papers just didn't spend enough time working on them, it's truly not that hard to score well if you put genuine effort into the assignments. It's a lot of reading, but I don't know what else you'd expect from a 300 level class.

Subject matter is irreplaceable and important in her courses. But the favoritism was through the roof. She'd have some biting remark every time some of the only cis guys in my class raised their hands. Things like "Alright, let's hear what the white guy has to say." 
Some laughed, but she was inappropriate given the equality we were discussing.

She will like you if you talk a lot in class, very rude to others. 5 papers through out the quarter and 600 word limit. If this class is important to your major, take it. If not find a better professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very passionate about GWSS, and cares a lot about teaching. Can come across as rude at times. Class participation is a major deal to her, to the point that it is extremely overbearing. The course content is amazing and super interesting. Course workload is overly heavy, which detracts from the learning experience more than it helps.

Dr.Shayne is VERY passionate in her work. However, she speaks rudely and highly sarcastic. There is clear favoritism and she only likes one that speaks/attend the most in class. If you ask any clarifying question for the essays, she says to just look into the rubric. Lots and lots of reading, 5 essays, and one quarter long project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly If you have this subject find another professor. The 500 word limit for this class was especially tough since you're going to be talking about complex topics. Unless you participate in this class she'll ignore you or seem like she doesn't want to talk to you.

Gives four essays throughout the quarter, 500 words min and max, yet grades every essay as "too vague." Essays are due before class. No time to work on assignments in class and has no regard for students' lives outside school, everything is homework. Along with every assignment, there is group work outside of class. Lecture prep every weekend :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Essays are 500 words min/max and you lose points for going over, super sarcastic in rude way, false confidence due to teaching anti misogyny class as a woman. Has obvious favorites and least favorites, would rather go to war in Europe than take her class again.  No regards for personal lives outside of class and doesn't talk about homework in class

Topic of the class was interesting, but nothing like the course description. Grade was based largely on contributions to group project. Material and lectures were good, but overall difficult to grasp. She's intelligent on the topic, but class was not structured well.

Dr. Shayne is a great teacher, very invested in students' learning. Some readings are hard but I like that she goes over them in lecture. She had really good lectures and I liked the quarter-long project.

She is VERY passionate about her work. But she still has a hard time communicating the concepts of the class in a way that doesn't dumb them down. We often asked her to repeat or rephrase. What I disliked most about her teaching style, though, is that it was very repetitive. She is approachable and nice though, and helpful if you need anything.

Dr. Shayne is one of the best teachers I've had at UWB. She cares a LOT about students' learning and is very approachable 1:1. Her class was difficult but very rewarding in terms of learning, particularly critical reading and writing skills. Lectures are insightful and I always get something valuable from them. Feedback on writing is good.

Dr. Shayne is very passionate and knowledgeable. Homework and grading are straightforward. She gives opportunities to make up for missed assignments. She explores many ways of learning which keep the class interesting (movies, art, poetry). If you don't like to come to class or do homework or participate, she is not the teacher for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Annoying, she's very passionate and that's good but she's rude and should be a high school teacher instead with the way she teaches and the attitude she has. She likes some students responses but when it's not to her liking she just gives you an uninterested response. She's very desperate for people to participate which makes me like the class less

*Very* passionate about GWSS, however she'll vocally critique your analyses in class and when asked a direct question about a subject presented in the readings will redirect for another student to explain. She does not hate men (I'm a cis man), she valued the opinions of men/women equally in class. LOTS OF READING, papers have clear guidelines
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: (I am reviewing BISGWS 302) Dr. Shayne is a passionate about GWSS and her lectures demonstrate her profound knowledge. This course includes heavy reading, several mini essays, and one big group project but no "busy" work. She provides clear rubrics and valuable constructive feedback. Attendance is mandatory, especially for the group project!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's tough, but very passionate about her field and it shows.

I dont complain about the amount of work assigned, but rather the kind of work assigned. Although some papers and assignments are valuable to the students learning, some are not. I.e) shouldn't need to read her publications and write a 100pt essay on it. Waste of time. I believe some reviews are fake since the professor made rude remarksallquarter

I'm not complaining about the work. Got an a, but taking this professor made me doubt the reliability of rate my professor. Opinionated, occasionally makes rude remarks about students, and needs to care more about students time. She sent an email to her students "apologizing" for her behavior . I say "apologize" becauseshesaidtheremarkwassarcasm.

She is the worst teacher I have ever had especially since It was my first feminism class. I thought it would be a great environment to learn more about this topic that I am passionate about, but I was wrong. She will belittle you and your opinions, and she kicked out a guy that just wanted to voice his opinion and she yelled at him. She hates men.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was a challenge for me, but I liked it a lot. Prof. Shayne is an amazing teacher; her teaching style makes you want to soak up every bit of information. Her humor, sarcasm and sometimes attitude made the class so engaging for me. She recently won a teaching award and well deserves it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Shayne is very knowledgeable and does a great job of facilitating dialogue in the classroom. She comes off opinionated but she backs up her arguments well and really engages the students. Sometimes she is very funny too. The grading criteria are outlined and very clear. Put in the work and participate, and you'll do good in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It's clear that the professor cares about her subject passionately, and if you're a favorite she'll learn all about you. But if you're anything but that she's incredibly cold, and will scoff or bark at your answers in front of the class. Clipped and stand-offish, proudly harsh on grading. Don't go to learn, only go if you can impress immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was scared to take her class because it sounded very intense but honestly I have never met a more motivated yet caring individual. She comes off intense but she knows her stuff and wants nothing more than to share it with her students. I would totally take another class with her again.
Solid lectures, very knowledgeable, and her passion for the course material is inspiring! I personally didn't think she graded too harshly at all, although you do have to put in a serious effort!

Prof Shayne is an incredible professor. Her expectations are clear, her lectures are well organized, and she is very passionate about what she teaches. She always keeps her students' best interests in mind and will advocate for those being marginalized/exploited by the university. I encourage everyone to take a class with her.

Anyone on here complaining about the amount of work doesn't take their job as a student seriously. You will never find a professor who advocates more for her students. Her classes make you leave feeling inspired and informed.  Yes. You read. And write. Welcome to college. I'll take every class possible with Professor Shayne.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Shayne really cares about her students and their learning. She is very passionate about her area of study. Class had 3 Section write ups( 2pgs long) , group project - early thoughts paper, presentation and final paper)  Material is def interesting, lots to learn. I kind of prefer having a few larger assignments than many little ones.

Shayne is one of the best professors at UWB. I took her for my DC1. She sets high expectations and pushes you to your limits. It's intimidating at the beginning but you'll begin to understand her humor and unique personality. In the long run Shayne helps you improve both critical thinking and your writing skills.

Dr. Shayne is alright . She's passionate about her work which is nice  but I would be lying if I said her class didn't give me tremendous amounts of grief, stress, and sleepless nights when taken with other courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This is one of my favorite professors. I took away a lot from her class. Also, I feel that I was able to become a better writer while taking one of her courses. She's opinionated, but don't always refer to her opinions, as she wants you to refer to the readings. She's is funny, direct , and I would definitely take one of her classes again.

She is okay. Very opinionated, and even though I agree with her on a lot of things it still felt like too much for me. Very particular about things that really shouldn't matter that much, like how you turn something in, cover pages, etc. The class content is important, so that made it a bit better.

The readings are long and you have to write a lot of papers. But as long as you do all the readings, it isn't too bad. She emphasizes participation but does give you the chance to self-evaluate yourself, which is nice. Aside from it being challenging, this class was a real eye-opener and I learned a lot of valuable things.
This class was the hardest class I've ever taken at UWB. She requires you to understand all the concepts on the readings enough to write papers on BEFORE you even go over them in the class.

Professor Shayne is my favorite teacher at UWB. The work is tough but the readings are interesting and the in class discussions are so helpful, so go to her class every day. She expects a lot of you because she expects a lot of herself as a teacher, her passion for teaching made me excited to learn. No text book but lots of readings.

I took my DCI Course and BIS 300 course with her. My favorite professor at UWB. She is someone who you will challenge you help you and care for you as her student. In addition if you open up to her on a personal level she will have your success at her best interest. Love her passion for social justice diversity and Latinoa studies. THE BEST

I took this class because it looked interesting and it ended up being the hardest class I've ever taken because of the level and amount of reading she assigns. However the discussions she has were very valuable and she is always accessible. She is a tough writing critic but encourages usage of the Writing Resource Center.
Shes very sweet and kind.

One of the best professors that I have ever had! She cares so much of her students and if you reach out to her for help then she will do anything possible to give you the help you need. There was a lot of reading to do and some you didn't even end up discussing but the overall content of the course was great!

Great introductory class for the program.  It really got me going in the right direction, although I was a little confused at first.   Do visit her in her office--she's actually very approachable one-on-one.  Really learned a lot.

I have taken three classes with Professor Shayne and I do because she is clear,organized and passionate about subjects she teaches as well as cares about the learning of students. She is a fair grader and she does challenges us but isn't that why we are in college? She has been my favorite professor thus far!

I have taken 3 courses with Julie Shayne. She is tough, she is strict, she does have high expectations. At first impression she seems unapproachable and rude. But on the contrary, she's super helpful and cares about her students. Do the work, discuss in class, and push yourself.

VERY hard teacher!!!  She is very smart but if you miss a class or if you do not like to talk in class or do all the reading 100%...good luck!!  I got an A, but I worked WAY too hard for it.  I would not take her classes again.

I loved Shayne! although she is strict! I love her interest in Latin American people and the culture. If you're a Latino/a you'll definitely like her, even if she seems "mean" And i love her advocacy for undocumented students/families rights :)!

This class was really horrible. The format was unorganized and nobody wanted to go to class. The structure didn't make sense and she graded papers as if it was a 500 level class. She was the only one passionate about her subject and assigned a ridiculous amount of reading in which she was alway frustrated that nobody could complete.

Like others before me have said this women will challenge you to be the best you can be. She is hard, BUT she is inspiring and very encouraging if you apply and challenge yourself. She taught me to write and to articulate myself in class. I am forever grateful. Shayne is perfect for those who want to learn and see themselves grow!

Only really learned one topic even though we were told we would learn many. She was very political during discussions. She seems nice but a little rude. If you want 4 hours of learning about Latin American immigrants and illegal immigrants rights this is the class for you. If you don't feel interested in that then she isn't the professor for you.

Fantastic teacher - she is passionate about the material She is a really tough grader, so if you want an easy grade, don't take the class. But if you are in college to learn, take any class she offers, they are amazing. I highly recommend her, despite the tough grading. I probably learned more in this class than my entire educational career.
I took her women, culture development class. she is very opinionated. and you better not disagree with her. thought she was rude and demanding. you have to work hard for a good grade

Good teacher, genuinely cares about subject and is extremely knowledgeable. easy grade as long as you do the readings. just a few short 2 page reading summaries and only one 8-10 page paper due at the end of the quarter and you choose the topic.
good teacher. i recommend!

As long as you do the readings, attend class, and participate there is no way you cannot succeed in this class. While she stresses the writting center, as long as your writting has been decent in the past you dont need to go.
She is really into what she does so it's an interesting class. She has a lot of instructions on the syllabus, which she requires you to read and she's fairly okay on grading...

hardest prof. not available and not easy to approach and talk to. at times mean and unfeeling. class should've been a 500 level instead of 300 really, for the level of work, specially the reading and writing assignments
Very fast paced and difficult to understand at first.

Kellejian is kind, respectful, and clearly cares about what she teaches. Bcore104 is very fun and engaging. Along with watching movies, there is some reading and response work, however, it is very doable. Be ready to talk about the movies with other classmates and share out. There are no formal presentations or group projects and the final is easy.
Very supportive professor. Interesting essay topics.

Genuinely the best professor I have taken. Workload is minimal, essays are clear and easy to write/follow through with. She gives good feedback on your work and makes an effort to get to know you even if its just your name. She is super nice and kind I love this professor so much! Participation is just going to class and doing in class assignment.

This is for the queer trans film course. I highly recommend taking this course. It was very fun and easy. And its a very easy A class. If u need to boost your GPA take this class. Professor is very kind and easy to approach. Participation matters during class but you don't have to talk a bunch.
Honestly a great teacher. it wasnt my ideal class to take but i went in with an open mind and learned a lot. the teacher is amazing and super understanding. participation is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Taken as a queer & trans film course. Professor Kellejian is easy to approach and talk about anything. Easy A; The class required minimal effort--- literally watching movies by yourself and writing 200 words. Plus lots of extra credit! "Mandatory" attendance due to participation activities, but the lecture is just a yapping session for students.

Great teacher. Felt burnt out in this class with no motivation, and I heard from others they felt the same way, but in the end, she graded easily, and the class did not stress me out. I would recommend taking her. She has a one-time late pass for 24 hours; everything else is heavily punished daily for it being late. Many extra credit opportunities

It's a movie analyzing class. You don't have to agree with professors since the contents are a bit sensitive for the class. It's quite fun and engaging. You wil explore a lot of different movies you may never seen before. She's caring and respectful. The class guideline is clear and the class material is quite accesible. She's a impressive prof.

First off; what a wonderful teacher! Curriculum and the way they teach is super easy to understand. Their grading criteria is wonderful, the assignments have clear due dates and directions, overall workload is super low. PARTICIPATION MATTERS THO... don't expect a great grade if you skip a lot, but class is only once a week.

Professor Kellejian was very helpful and gave very good feedback. I don't usually enjoy taking english classes and I'm not very good at writing papers but i really enjoyed all the material. Very clear grading criteria and not too much work. Very understanding person and easy to talk to! Would definitely take the class again

Great teacher for this specific class. They were clear when explaining things, very helpful with essays, and very accessible outside of class. The Canvas site is really helpful with the overall class structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing choice. The class is really nice. All you have to do is write and read sometimes. It's not super complicated and the teacher gives really good feedback. I don't have much to say but the class was nice and chill. The goal is to write one big essay over the quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A huge workload, but if you put in the work you will be rewarded. Dr. Kellejian is one of my favorite professors I've had, and she helped me develop confidence in my writing skills. If you get the option, please choose her! It is worth it 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I genuinely cannot think of anything to critique about Professor Kellejian. If you have the option to ever take her, do it. One of my favorite Professors I've had so far. Excited to have her again next quarter.

Dr. Kellejian is one of the best professors on campus! The course load was light and the grading criteria was very clear. There is plenty of time in between assignments and discussion boards so you won't be slammed. She was the first professor that made me fall in love with the GWSS degree! I've been lucky enough to take her for other courses!

Dr. Kellejian is one of the nicest professors at UWB. Although it is a core class, she made sure to make it entertaining and providing material which students would actually benefit from. She was very understanding to student's personal situations, and made sure that student's opinions and perspectives were heard. Would recommend!

Professor Kellejian was an amazing professor who always answered any questions or queries we had, and had clear instructions as to what was expected of the class. If you put effort in the answers, you will do well. For the final essay, she was willing to meet outside of class to look at our essays and give feedback. Very happy with class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Genuinely an amazing teacher that cares about students. Dr. Kellejian will spend the time to make sure youre on the right track and give great guidance as long as you ask for it. Dr. Kellejian made BWRIT135 an extremely enjoyable and interesting class. It was engaging even as a hybrid class!
Fair minded and creative. This professor has a professional patience and demeanor that makes it easy to discuss topics that are typically taboo. I suggest this professor.

Dr. Kellejian cares about her students learning and succeeding in class. She offers to help with future needs and understands when there are personal issues that come up. The readings were interesting and she doesn't require you to buy a textbook for this class! Would definitely take her again!
Shes a great professor. Clear cut expectations, never makes you feel like your answer is stupid, gives useful feedback and is truly a caring person. Take her if you have the chance!

Really nice and understanding professor, very easy to talk to. It feels like everyone in the class is comfortable in speaking, there honestly is no "wrong" answer. Only assignments we had were two discussion posts a week, one on Monday and one on Friday (since it's a hybrid course). The readings are very interesting and not super extensive
