Great professor, really cares about all students. I have taken two courses with her and enjoyed them both. Takes the time to give feedback which is appreciated. It is clear she puts a lot of time and energy into lesson plans. Great professor!

Kris Kellejian was so unprofessional and she demonstrated a lack of interest on her students. I understand that there are requirements and expectations to pass a class but she was disobliging. I wouldn't recommend her or wish to take another course taught by her.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Really a great prof! She picks awesome reads and makes class discussions enjoyable. I have taken a few classes from her and have loved them all. There is a bit of reading and responses involved but the topic is interesting enough to make it feel like less work. 10/10 would take again.

I wish I had found this professor prior to the end of my schooling.  I really enjoyed how she ran the class and the class discussions.  She seems to really care and I looked forward to going to class each week.  She did offer some extra credit in class as well.

Kris was clear cut on what she expects and her class was extremely easy as long as you show up. Easy to approach after class and extremely helpful if you ever need clarification. A bit awkward at times if the class isn't actively participating.

Dr. Kellejian is an amazing and inspirational professor at the University of Washington. She is hilarious, understanding, and timely of student's schedules and works. By taking her writing class, I was able to become a better writer by her amazing feedback. KELLEJIAN! WE LOVE YOU!
Took this class for my major and am so glad that I did! Kris was so helpful and always clear about what was expected of us.

I enjoyed her BIS300 class! I recommend her!! She's an amazing instructor and shows that she really cares about her students future. I ended this class with a 4.0. This class may seem easy but it requires a lot of work and dedication. She is very helpful and clear about her assignments as well.
Really helpful. Offers some extra credit opportunities and grades easy if you do what needs to be done. Follow instructions, do the readings, assignments, and research paper. You'll do well.

Boring class by an even more boring educator.  Treats us like we're in kindergarten and thinks UW Bothell is second rate to UW Seattle.  Don't take her, she will bore you death and treat you like a 5th grader.

Great teacher, she really cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. She is down to earth and can make the class laugh. Grading is very easy I almost felt as if you showed that you put in a lot of effort you would get the automatic A. There were some times she graded things a bit tougher, but she offers extra credit to make up for it.
Awesome teacher! Super nice and helpful.

She's a great teacher, and definitely my favorite at UWB so far. She's funny, nice, tries to keep things interesting, and encourages people to come to her office hours(even offered extra credit to those who went). The few essays and quizzes were a breeze, and HW doesn't take more than an hour. You won't regret taking this class with her.
All opinions all the time. Social justice warrior

Nora is engaging in teaching global health. This class is mostly self led and based on coming to class for discussion. Lots of reading/films but they are valuable and relevant to our current politics. She can be tough at grading when it comes to quiz questions if it's clear you didn't actually read tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Intro to Health Topics Through Film was light and fun. The class is mainly just watching documentaries and weekly readings, and class time is used for small group discussions. Super easy to pass as long as you just do the work and show up for class.

Professor Nora is an amazing professor who really cares about her students. She is very clear about her expectations and is very understanding. She made class fun by adding interactive activities and interesting video during lecture. There is a lot of reading but if you keep up with it the quizzes are super easy. Highly recommend!
Taking class with her is very a load work. Lots of course work, reading and assignment.

She is very insightful and passionate about what she teaches, but that means that she will be tough on grading at times. Quizzes are sometimes confusing but if you skim through the assigned chapters and listen in class, you'll pass easily. Also, participation is not manditory but gets you on her good side!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: UNFORTUNATELY, If you are a health studies major you probably won't be able to avoid taking one of Nora's classes. Not a friendly teacher, very unapproachable and unhelpful. Has high expectations even when she is not clear about an assignment, her grading is absurd.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If youre a health studies student be prepared for this professor to be rude and a tough grader. I had to take her 3 times unfortunately and I hated coming to her class because she always had movies or guest lectures come in rather than her teaching us the material herself. Try to avoid her. Not equipped to teach global health.

Probably the easiest class I've ever taken. You literally just complete whatever she tells you to complete and you get full points as long as you did everything as asked. Watch the movie every week, answer the questions (literally multiple choice) and then participate for the discussion. She is so nice and cares about creating safe environments

Not qualified to teach global health; spent more time soliciting personal life matters rather than staying on topic. Answers questions with questions. You'll do all of the teaching. Read the book; lectures are tangental and irrelevant. Got an "A," but learned nothing outside of my own self-teaching. Invites extremist guest speakers to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Despite the comments for other classes, the class I took had a fair work load for a hybrid class. She is super nice and is passionate about her work. Her film class is east work. Watch the class, answer questions, participate in discussions. She does not ask for much and grading is pretty standard if you really stick to what she's asking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You're forced to take a class with her eventually if you're a health studies student.. unfortunately. She wasn't offering much insight on solutions, rather just repeating obvious issues in health care. Says that attendance is important but I went a total of 3 times and still got a 3.5 in class. A LOT of readings and discussions. Good Luck!

If you're a health studies major, you can't avoid her but this is a warning for you. She  is not very friendly & doesn't like to explain herself when she dishes out poor grades for good work. She likes group projects and constantly changes her expectations & then becomes defensive when you ask for clarification. Try to avoid her as much as u can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof. Kenworthy is REALLY tough and makes you work but every minute is absolutely worth it.  Show up, pay attention, do the work and you'll learn more in her class than any other you'll take.
Be prepared to attend every class as participation matters.  She is tough when it comes to grading, even small mistakes will affect your grade.  Also, not a very approachable person.

She is a very tough grader.  Won't always respond to e-mails, and she is not very approachable.  She gives too much reading when compared to other courses that i've taken.  Also,  participation matters in her class.

Professor Kenworthy is a great, inspirational teacher. She is always open to office hours and willing to talk to students to make sure they succeed. However, her grading is pretty tough and she likes group projects.

Professor Kenworthy is a great professor, she is very organized and is always very open to her students for help. However, she is a tough grader. She gives quizzes that were intended to be 'easy' but were not and made a big impact on our grades.

I think she is very knowledgeable and passionate--no doubt. But she is unapproachable and seems to take questions as insults or confrontation. She will not explain her grading methods openly, and you must make an appointment to speak with her on your own time. Most teachers will leave this info for you in their grading feedback? Just dont ask Q's.
I had a great experience. Great information, challenges students to stretch their thinking. Group work was more beneficial than I had expected.

I have had Professor Kenworthy for two classes and really enjoyed them both. She is extremely knowledgeable and plans classes well so they are always interesting and informative. Her assignmentsreadings and tests are challenging but she is a very fair grader. She really wants to help her students succeed in her classes and in their future careers.

Professor Kenworthy is the best of the best in my opinion if you want to learn and do well. Her expectations and grading is very clear. She provides extra materialevents and really goes above and beyond for her students. I really enjoyed both classes with her. She is very knowledgable and fun. Definitely recommend her!

I took Global Health as an elective for Spring Quarter, and it was the best class I had all year. The course was always engaging and interesting, and she was always happy to help clarify or explain something. There's a lot of reading, but it's all relevant material for what will be discussed in class. A fair grader and never looked or sounded angry

You know the coaches who mock you and push you harder than you want? Who you want to hate, but looking back realize they were the ones who genuinely made you better? That's Dr. Sung.

After finishing his class I gave him a copy of "Whiplash," saying he's like the teacher but not mean. Spicy, yes. Also, one of my final project committee members.

Sung is unique in that while CSS 451 had a lot of work, expectations were fairly low. Besides the occasional weirdly specific requirement in assignments, you could get away with doing a lot of random stuff and possibly earn extra credit while doing so. It also doesn't hurt to know Unity somewhat, as he doesn't teach its usage much.

His 451 was class was really difficult and I would warn anyone looking to take this class. Unless you have a serious interest in computer graphics and don't mind sacrificing your social life (Lets be real, you probably don't have one if you like computer graphics) then take this class. I enjoyed the professors teaching style, but YMMV.

accused me of cheating, I was found innocent by investigator,
very rude (put two students emails up on the board and shamed them)
asking questions is met with ridicule and insult,
improvised lectures - weekly quizzes worth 30% of our grade had avgs of 50-60%
ridiculous workload (doesnt teach c++ yet assigns full projects on it)
hard to understand

Do yourself a favor and choose another elective unless you have no life and are a graphics nerd. The professor knows his stuff, but is super stern. The syllabus is ambiguous, and the assignments are weekly, massive, and silly. Even with past Unity experience + AI usage, this elective still takes more work and time than TWO core classes combined.

I took his 451 class having looked at the prior ratemyproff reviews, and I can honestly say he is nowhere near as bad as people make him out to be. That being said, the course uses Unity (Of which I had over a year of experience with) and the workload was far beyond anything I could have imagined - Made my 430&422 workloads seem like kindergarten.

Prof. Sung is an amazing instructor. If you really want to learn, you'll enjoy the lectures. The lectures will prepare you enough to dive into the assignments. Grading was very clear and got great feedback. Would highly recommend. The teaching style is not the same as any other average instructor but I thoroughly enjoyed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
he gives warnings about the difficulty of this class, and generally means the best. the issue w him is hes not lenient, so make sure you start early.

for the class itself, definitely take it if you're interested in this stuff and willing to put in a good amount of effort, you will learn a ton! i was skeptical from reviews but it was worth it.
Professor's teaching style is not good. He doesn't clarify assignments and goes way too fast for lectures.

Kelvin is the worst professor I've had at UW. Unavailability, a concerning lack of flexibility, respect, and consideration, paired with a goofy accent and a demeaning manner is the tip of the iceberg. If because of a car crash you're late and your assignment shows as 12:00 instead of 11:59 you get a zero. Makes you wish you got totaled with the car

This course curriculum is outdated and Sung refuses to update it. For one, Unity is obsolete in the industry, and two, you will learn nothing from this class. I was very excited to take this class but the course objective and its' content are unhelpful. Sung's lecture style consists of rambling, bad dad jokes, and complete disorganization.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Never take this prof's lessons, he always gives lots of tasks and homework... and unnecessary to take this course, it is not helpful for your future work literally...

Has no format or structure in his lectures and jumps from point A to point H instead of A to B. He uses a mic that is shoved deep inside his throat so the audio is always muffled and difficult to understand. He says he is always willing to help outside of class but dismissed all my questions about assignments as they were, "simple to understand".

I was excited to take computer graphics. Kelvin Sung ruined the class. He assigns more than twice as much work as other 400-level CSS electives (easily more than CSS 430), with weekly 20+ hour assignments that take up all of your time. He also does not accept any late work at all, and his lectures are very unhelpful and poorly organized.

This professor is very nice and funny. But be warned he likes to scare people with the future. For cssskl 342 only have 5 classes and for each class, we have 5 assignments. if you fall more than one you fail.

Probably the most direct but very understanding instructor I have ever met. Kelvin is clear about what he does and does not expect from his students. He makes sure that we get all the help we need even not during class time. As long as you submit your work, even with a couple of errors in the work, you will pass the class.

The difficulty and expectations of his class grows exponentially. First things seem doable with how the lectures cover the topics, but soon the lectures cover more and more complex topics with homework asking more and more from you within the same time frame. This class really should be split up into a Part 1 and Part 2 with how complicated it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a useful class. Kelvin spends time on irrelevant subjects and the content is not useful in the industry. Kelvin expects you to spend an excessive amount of time on his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: First day of class kelvin sung was scary and intimidating, but the more time you spend in his class the more you realize what an amazing teacher he is. He emphasizes and dives deep into concepts instead of just scratching the surface, his class is full of energy and his lectures are awesome!

This class is supposedly to learn C++ language for improved score in CSS 342. On the first day of class he told us he would not teach us any C++ and we had to learn it on our own. He admit he does not know C++. You are better off learning from a text on your own. The projects were so long it took away from time to study for credit classes.

His lectures are fast paced but unorganized. Definitely read the book/slides and do the projects early! Plenty of office hours but so little help for so much time spent listening to him :( the midterm was open laptop though! (But still hard)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Kelvin is awesome. His teaching style for most of his classes is very applied, which may throw people off but is a great preparation for  the real world. He encourages going above and beyond, loves anything cool that students do, and pushes students to push out an awesome final product, using whatever tools they can. He was a huge part of my degree

Kelvin Sung is an amazing instructor. At first, his brutal honesty and high expectations come across as very intimidating, but once you get to know him, you find out he is this way because he really cares about his students. His classes are very challenging, and he doesn't go easy on anyone, but you will definitely learn a lot from him.

More work than you can imagine, 100% worth it. Lectures were not much theory, more focus on how to think/design/solve problems for assignments. May seem unclear in class, but you learn a lot. Kelvin is helpful, great with e-mails. With Kelvin we had 8 huge assignments, and only 4 in the 2nd part of the same course, with different instructor.

Kelvin gives challenging and work intensive classes, so expect to put in your time. Exams are difficult, but with plenty of studying are manageable. He is VERY helpful in office hours, VERY active on class forums, and will review your code with you to help you find your bugs. I learned a ton in his class, despite his letting Q&A cut into lectures.

This prof is one of those who is more interested in showing off in front of the students than help them learn. He knows a finite set of things and anything other than that would just be a waste of time asking him. Doesn't teach a single thing in class but the assign&exams are so confusing and useless that everyone scores less and feel demotivated.

Kelvin is the rare professor who loves what he's doing.  This makes it a lot easier to get excited about class!  Also, I found it very easy to relate to him, compared to the average CS person.  As others have noted, there can be discrepancies between what he teaches and what's on the tests/assignments, but it's not really a big deal.

Kelvin knows the material and loves to teach.  He worries too much about being ESL and upsetting students. I don't feel either is a problem.  Assignments will keep you up late, so start early.  His mantra: "Don't worry about the implimentation, you must understand the concepts."  True! To this end you will find quizzes obscure and frustrating.

Very knowledgeable professor who makes time for one on one reviews. His lectures, quizzes and tests are based purely on logical problems (was very difficult for me).  One word of advice is to start on his weekly coding assignments as soon as it's posted. I did not use any of the text books but it's still good for reference.

Be prepared to put in a LOT of time on the homework but if you do you'll definitely learn it.  Entertaining Prof who loves the subject.  He's very open to hearing student view, good tests, fair grader.  Just a lot of time.  He says 2 hrs/1% worth.  I spent more.  Some assignments are worth 12%; you do the math.  You get 1 wk to do the homework.

A very funny and enthusiastic professor, who clearly loves teaching a lot. He is very fun to learn from. He will go way out of his way to help you. His test questions don't always exactly reflect the in-class material, so studying for exams is not easy, but he is a fair grader. He is very responsive to feedback and works to accommodate students.

Kelvin is an awesome professor.  He is enthusiastic about computer science and he gets the students in his classes just as excited.  He is very knowledgeable regarding his subjects and is a demanding instructor.  However, you will learn a lot and have a fun time doing it.

Had Camas for both 114&115. Not the greatest. He's a sweet & funny guy, but doesn't really teach. Both courses were logistically frustrating. Messed up grades, posting things wrong/late, never responds to emails. The good side was the class was somewhat straightforward and not too many assignments. Quizzes, HW, and one final. Didn't learn much.

I was in BPHYS 311, 312, and 324 with him, kept coming back when he was an option because he's so awesome. Cares a lot about students' learning, very funny and good at explaining complex physics concepts, and rather easy to get an A compared to other upper-div physics profs here. Only problem is that he never checks his email.

He's very nice, funny, and always willing to work with you. I learned a lot about this subject even though it was an online class. If you have a chance to choose this professor, do it! I also know people who have taken physics with him and they also really enjoy his class. Glad I took this astronomy course.

Professor Key is by far one of the funniest teachers ive had. His dry humor is hilarious. He’s very good at what he does & will help out if you can ever track him down. Never answers emails which is so frustrating. Nonetheless, amazing teacher. 96% is a 4.0 but it’s very doable. I would recommend him! 1 final + wkly onl. quizzes & assignments.

He is a good teacher, teaches well goes into detail you can tell he really likes his job and is very passionate about teaching physics. However the communication skills are poor, he offers his email the first week of classes but never answers them all quarter, he doesn't seem like he cares about answering students or is very forgetful.

The good: Is a pleasant person to interact with, explains the concepts in depth, only one exam, a take home final. 

The bad: takes forever to respond to email, isn't great at communicating in general, hasn't graded anything all quarter that wasn't graded automatically, homework is often hard. Seems to generally treat this class as a 2nd priority.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is good and nice. He really teaches and goes over lectures compared to the rest of UWB Phys faculties. But he doesn't really care if you understand it or not, or try to connect with you. This can be good&bad at the same time, especially if you take higher ed tests later. He is not responsive, never replies to email

Dr. Key is a unique and passionated professor. He isn't just there to teach you how to solve your homework but want to show you how beautiful physics is, he's also very nice to his students. Being able to take him is a blessing. Give him tenure position please.
Loved him! Take him if you can! He is very reasonable and very knowledgeable. I look forward to going to PHYSICS every week! And I used to hate physics.

Love him! He is practically the only teacher that  makes me like physics! He is fair and straightforward. His lectures are clear and very understanding. The quizzes and assignments are big help! I really hope he teaches physics 115 next quarter. I would take him every quarter if I could!
A real standout cool guy, there's a reason why his ratings are good. Not too tough on grading, and if you do well, you'll feel like you earned the grade. Very good introductory class to astronomy.

Dr. Keys is an amazing professor, really cares about his students. Pay attention in class, and do all the homework and you will be fine for exams. I wish I would've taken the entire physics series with him.

Dr. Key is truly one of the best teachers I've had. I have taken his physics class during the pandemic, and he his teaching style has made Physics really easy to understand. There is group work and quizzes every week, including homework online. For tests, he gives us 48 hours which is nice and accommodating. He is awesome 10/5.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Key is truly the most amazing professor I have had yet. Despite having 100 students in my class, he knows everyones names. Lectures are engaging and helpful, and his exams are fair and straightforward. He makes physics easy to understand and apply to life. Attendance is important for doing the in class assignments but the classes are great!
Physics is a tough subject, he makes it seem really simple and straight forward. Really good lectures, and group quizzes almost every class.

Everything I've ever wanted in a professor. He's just incredible. Physics is weird, because you have to see the world through a new lensthat's where my struggle was. If you want to actually learn "physics," I couldn't recommend another professor more highly than Dr. Key. He made class engaging and fun, good luck finding that from someone else. ��

One of the nicest/most personable profs Ive had at UW across both campuses! He really does his best to present the material in the most easy to understand way, so if youre struggling with something, let him know. Assigned textbook was also helpful. Very reasonable grading and tests are fair & reflective of things from lecture, worksheets, hw etc.

The best physics professor at UWB hands down! He cares about his students success. It takes a minute to get used to how he teaches, but eventually the class flows well. Tests are pretty easy. Would highly recommend.

Awesome teacher who actually cares about his students success. He is a very positive and upbeat guy, which makes the class fun. Half the class is lecturing, second half is working on worksheets in groups. His tests are not bad either as long as you pay attention in class. He allows for a page of notes front and back. Would recommend 10/10!
I took this teacher all though the physics series, I had a lot of fun and learned a lot. He conveys the concepts very well in class and isn't a harsh grader.

Dr. Key is a great professor. I like his way of lecturing - half group work, half lecture. He has a happy personality, and is eager to help. Seems like he actually wants to be there teaching you! His tests, so far, are easy - part t/f, part multiple choice, and some short answer. The homework really helps you understand the concepts. And he's cute!

Whether you go to class or not, it wont matter. Exams are not based around lectures or textbook hardly. You can write the entire lecture on your note card but none of it will be on the exam. Exams will also have content not lectured on at all. Homework is lengthy. Never inputs grades. In class work is nearly impossible without outside assistance.
Really nice and genuine guy - he is always eager to help. The in-class work can be a bit boring if he isn't lecturing, but it helps to understand that material.

Humorous professor. Expect exams very similar to problems in the book. The online homework, WebAssign, is terrible as usual, but it will help you succeed if you thoroughly understand how to do the problems.

DK was the best prof. I've ever had. He is a very funny guy, but can seem intimidating at first. He is very passionate and has lots of debates during his lectures. Attendance does matter. Very easy grader and cares more about effort than anything else. No midterm, optional final, one quarter-long group project.

I had DK this fall quarter and he was great! Super funny (I often couldn't stop laughing in class), understanding, and has very clear instructions. 

By far one of the best professors at UWB. The material is connected to real world issues that matter and he does a great job expressing higher level concepts in a simple manner. 

Highly recommend

I felt this professor made several inappropriate comments that felt sexist or hurtful to students. This discouraged students from engaging in the class. He verbatim said, "I hate my wife" which was incredibly inappropriate. The class structure was disorganized and instructions were not clear. If the professor likes you, you will get a good grade.

Openly speaks about hating woman like his wife, made fun of a woman in my class because she had tattoo's. he started every single class saying he was a " dictator " just like Donald Trump and Elon musk....I have never felt compelled to write such a review.

He was rude to students during class. At time we made discriminatory comments (I don't think he was ill-intended, but still). Huge ego and picked on students; he made us purchase the McGraw hill online book ($150+) and very heavy on group projects. He was not a really tough grader tho, if he liked you, you didn't have any issues
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: DK has been one of my favorite professors so far. Really caring, genuine guy that is so passionate about the subjects he teaches. Classroom involvement and participation is really important, but he does a great job of facilitating it. Definitely recommend.

Avoid is possible. Tough grader for an easy subject so it comes across really petty in his grading. His lectures are actually terrible and you will learn nothing from them but are completely mandatory. Get ready to hear him yap for 2 hours and not give you a single break.
Goat-ed professor. Chill, laid back, easy work. You won't have to worry about taking this guy.

DK is the best professor I have had at UWT. He is personable, understanding, and aware. He offers several opportunities to enhance our skills through participation. He is fair and well respected. Communication is definitely key in his class. As long as you communicate what you need, you should have no problems passing his class with an A.

DK is great! He definitely has a lot of information to share, and he is a great lecturer. I would note his exams are based off of the book not his lectures though, they do merge a little. I definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had taken two classes of his. DK is a change leader and truly wants to inspire students to become great leaders. He has a great optimistic attitude and creates a physiologically safe environment for his students. He values participation in students and is fair in his decisions. If you do the work there is no reason why you should fail.
Solid professor. Was lenient and had great real-life experiences to share. Would definitely take it again.

This class consists of 1 final paper that you do as a group, 3 easy quizzes, and weekly discussions based on one chapter. All professor Khaleghi asks is that you participate in the in-class discussions and that is not much to ask. In-class discussions are fun, and he also gives time in class for the final paper. He's such a great professor

This class is really about what you put in is what you take out. I enjoyed this class as I learned a lot and changed my perspective on how to become a better leader. Just talk in this course and communicate effectively with team members.  Pop quizzes were not hard if you read the book and showed up to class. A great course for sure! Great work DK.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The instructor is very passionate about the course material and allows for optimal flexibility and creativity. There are no tests but the grading can be challenging. When considering taking this course, ensure you can diligently complete assignments and the readings. The group portion is tough but welcome to managing people. Extra credit for attend

Best Professor so far here at UWT. Wish he taught more classes so I could take him again. He wants his students to succeed. Gives everyone a fair chance. Very understanding and realistic. Lectures are always interesting and engaging unlike other classes I have took. Highly recommend.

Homework and quiz are easy but test is really hard. Barely any homework, but the professor isn't the greatest at teaching, so you gotta self teach. The material isn't too tough, the sample problems are walked through in the slides so you just follow the solving process. Review barely helped at all for the test, I hope he curves
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: It's clear he has passion for the subject and the field as a whole, however, he has a thick accent that's hard to decipher at times. Moreover, he ready directly off the slides, which are direct copies of the textbook. 2 Weeks in and he made attendance mandatory because noone was showing up unless there was a quiz. All other reviews seem consistent.

A complete joke, be ready to self-teach everything. This guy can't explain half of the topics covered, and just tells you "It's obvious". Gets confused when you ask him questions, refuses to listen about poorly written questions (which were literally impossible to solve), says "no need to understand anything, just get the right answer". NEVER TAKE!

Constantly says "it's quite obvious" and skips over explanations. Doesn't know own slides, stumbles for a painfully long time through derivations (and does so incorrectly). Brushes away any questions with "don't think about it, it doesn't matter". Because he actually doesn't know the answer, but won't admit it. Always bragging of personal projects.

Grade was determined by midterm and final. Quizzes were on the same day homework was due but he would not go over homework before quizzes so you never have a chance to actually check your understanding. His lectures are convoluted and a lot of stuff he skips over and says "its so easy" and that "you should know how to do it".  Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were incoherent and example problems often contained mistakes that he had to go back and correct halfway through, making it very confusing to follow. I basically had to teach myself everything from YouTube videos.

hands down the worst teacher I have ever taken. his lecture notes are full of large equations with variables he doesn't explain. his homework's and exams are heavily focused on MATLAB. If you take him get ready to spend 20+ hours for a test on material you haven't seen. and if you ask questions his answers "its obvious" or "you should know this"

I would reconsider taking this class as an elective solely because of the professor. The professor is available for office hours but gives no useful help. Questions and criticism are not received well. Be prepared to self learn the topics. Probably the worst class I've ever taken

Be little's you when you ask him questions, the class is not helpful at all. When he makes mistakes he'll try to pin it on the students. I do not believe this person is suited for teaching. I think he's a very smart person no doubt, but he made me question my whole academic career. Not only is he not prepared a lot, he does not take criticism.

Ive always been an A student because I communicate professors for clarifications on lectures/work (if Im stuck.) He puts things on exams we didnt go over AT ALL , nor is he helpful when you reach out w/ questions . He isnt good at instructing, so youll do A LOT of self learning/reading. I recommend TheOrganicChemist on YT. Hes why I passed!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's enthusiastic about the subject and I trusted he knew his stuff. He also checks on us to see if we understand the information he's giving. LOTS OF READING at the beginning of the quarter, but he lets up near the end to let us work on our finals. The reading material was relevant though and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: What impressed me most about Prof  Kim was his desire for input.  He consistently gauged how we felt about the content, if we needed more time in our groups, etc.. You can tell he wants to ensure people want to be there and feel they are getting what they need out of it. He is also extremely knowledgable so you will learn plenty. Recommend for sure
Kevin is a great professor that provides clear information and feedback on work. The class was very lecture based so be ready to listen. Overall a very interesting and wonderful course.

Professor Kim gave good, informational lectures and assigned interesting reading material. Expectations on assignments were clear, and I appreciated the feedback he gave when grading papers and tests.

Professor Kim was an excellent teacher that tried to engage the students despite not having practiced this before. Since he came from an Ivy League university, he knew his stuff and he understood everything. I found his lectures enjoyable despite the lack of interaction, and he is working on that.

Professor Kim is an extremely engaging and thoughtful professor. He knows his material very well. Dr. Kim is very reasonable when it comes to grading. Very discussion oriented. He is not so much concerned with what you say, but how you substantiate your claim. Overall, I highly recommend him!

Dr. Kim approaches American Capitalism from multiple perspectives to encompass more than the traditional historical approach you learn in high school and contemporary news. He allows for you to understand trends and changes in different locations that helped create the form of Capitalism we experience today. Great objective Prof.

Professor Kim is very knowledgeable  and shows a great interest in helping students succeeded.  His lectures aren't always exciting, but with student feed back he does try to change it up. Fair grader. Just have to put some effort into the assignments.

The majority of what I took away from this class came from in-class discussions. These consisted of Prof. Kim inviting us to build our own individual views of the issues of the periods/concepts we were studying.  He absolutely wants you to succeed. He's open to having email/in-person conversations to make sure that everyone understands what to do.

Decent. Shes really sweet and kind. Curves tests. Can be pretty funny at times and tries to make class interesting. I thought this was going to be a hard class but it ended up not being bad at all. Pay attention in class and do the readings a little and you will pass with a good grade.
She is such a nice teacher, and is very approachable and really knows her stuff. I would advise anyone to take her if they can.

2 midterms, 1 final, and 1 paper. They were relatively easy, but she grades too hard on participation. I got a 4.0, 3.8, 3.5, and 3.5 for the midterms, final, and paper. But gave me a 1.0 in participation. Even though I went to every class and contributed in discussions and did the group exercises. Ended up with a 3.2, which was not what I expected

Karrin Klotz is AMAZING! Her introduction to law class was so enjoyable! She always defines terms in ways that make them easy to understand, such as using real world examples. She has a great sense of humor and her lectures are rarely dry, as she finds ways to keep them funny and interesting. I feel like I learned a lot and earned the A I received.
I thought Karrin was a great professor. She made all the different terms and concepts easy to understand and was very easy to talk to

She seems to think students already know about law but its an intro to law class. All she does is lecture and its very monotone and boring. Had a hard time focusing and her review sheet for the final has nothing to do with what is on the final.

Sweet woman. Gives in class work every couple classes. Plays movies. BEWARE its easy to lose pts! SO ANSWER ALL Q's THOROUGHLY 4 EVERYTHING! No notes on midterm but its just MC memorization, then open book 4 essay part. Final=take home. 1 paper 3pg-EASY & 1 PowerPt-EASY. Curves everything. Posts lectures but you WON'T know your grade til xscripts.

Never discussed textbook in class, yet book was needed only for tests. Very little discussed in class was found on tests. Spent lots of time watching left-wing movies bashing all companies. Made us buy a $40 course pack that contained nothing but printouts of articles freely available online from a store that does not allow refunds. Worst teacher!

This class was a core class for the MBA program. I enjoyed it and learned a lot. This class was primarily online and group is super helpful as you get to do assignments in groups and the final project is fun! The exams tend to be fairly simple if you pay attention and study. Usually they are open book.

Lectures super fast for no reason. The only important things in lectures are the example problems which are exactly what will be on tests. Textbook has same examples if lecture makes no sense. She grades pretty easy on projects and papers, but they are boring. I would just say try to take this class with a different professor if you can.

Not good. She does extra credit in class and has students teach students, except the students don't teach. No one teaches. It's just bloody guess and fill in the blank for the extra credit. Group projects are predominant in the class, and Pearson will teach you.
Extremely talented and outstanding lecturer. Assignments and simulations reflected real world situations. Would definitely take again. One of my favorite profs at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Interesting and entertaining class. Course layout was very organized and clear. A wide variety of sims and activities to bring topics into real-world applications. Got to exercise useful skills that I've already begun to implement at my firm. Professor Kennedy made 4 hour lectures as painless as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She gives you sample tests but her her actual examples are way more difficult than expected. She also assigns a lot of work which is unnecessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Deanna is a great instructor, she is always prepared for class and teaches any topic with enthusiasm. She may not be the best with arithmetic skills, but she is very knowledgeable with operations management topics. Expect to attend class and participate, expect to spend considerable amounts of time on homework, and expect to work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Horrible

The load for this class was more then I have ever had for any other 5 credit class. We were assigned tons of problems (from Pearson) which did little to nothing to improve what I really know about the subject on top of several group projects and 2 field trips (Who goes on field trips in college?).

Deanna is good at explaining the materials and she gives students a lot of opportunities and activities to get involved in the class. Exams are easy if you pay attention to her lecture and study guide. Homework is reasonable as there is a 300 level class.
A really tough grader. Getting us confused in lecture.

Told us on day one that she was only teaching the summer class because she got a new dog and needed to pay for it. Doesn't even grade projects herself; only takes grades you get from classmates and adds them up. Homework took too long and was useless, example tests she posts are not at all like the actual tests. Would not take her class again.

She seemed to know statistics but she was very unclear and not very organized.  Not helpful unless specifically asked.  tests were not clear.  too many homework assignments that were not relevant to statistics

She gives you example tests  but the real tests are Way more difficult. She doesn't always do or not do what she says.  Homework is extensive. Projects instructions not clear  and grading criteria changes midstream. She has great experience but isn't able to communicate her knowledge.

She uses Pearson Labs for her homework which automatically detracts from the class. I honestly didn't learn anything in this class. The homework was pointless and took FOREVER. She doesn't even include the homework on the tests. The tests are based on in-class lectures so you can't miss class.
She knows her stuff, and does a good job explaining. This is a challenging subject, but she is approachable when you need help. The projects are fun.

Wasn't a horrible teacher but wouldn't take again. She often would get confused when lecturing and look back at her notes or correct what she had said. Also didn't explain cases and projects in depth. Really nice lady though and although I struggled ended up w 3.4. Suggestion prof: split the projects between the quarter instead of both at the end!
Professor Kennedy was awesome. She had a strong grasp of the topic and provided various activities that enriched the learning experience.

Grad level stats.  Overall a TON of information she was required to cover and she did.  She tirelessly met with students and had extra classes whenever needed to help folks learn the material.  It was a challenge but excelent class!  Wish she would teach more of the classes

Simply incompetent. Didn't know the material, class corrected her math problems. Used random tests from online. Operations class became a Six Sigma class. Useless when you need help. Textbook reading expected, but seldom covered. Generally rude.
Professor Kennedy truly cares about the topic of operations management. There is a lot of writing assignments, but she only tests on what she teaches. She is a great professor!
Best teacher I have ever had! She was able to make the material 'click,' and made the class interesting. I took her last year, and still remember quite a bit from her class.
She is very nice and pretty!If you attend the class regularly, then you will be ok!
Katie was a fantastic teacher! She made the material clear, had great examples and really cared that you learned. No curve-balls. Highly recommend!

Katie is an amazing teacher. She is great at getting the class to participate, uses clear examples, and is genuinely enthusiastic about whether students learn. She is not pretentious and doesn't talk down to the students. She was awesome!

The class is inspirational, and it is great when everyone's discussing materials. We do have emotional moments also. He's a very caring person and he understands when you need extension on late deadlines. Materials are organized and his 'chill' attitude gives us comfort and respect to share our stories. Show up and be sure to join the talk

His class is fun, energetic. He is a very chill person. Everything sounds tough and overwhelming at first, but when you're in his class and be adaptive to things, it will be better. His book review assignment and group project weren't too hard though. He is not a tough grader, he really wants you to engage with the materials more. Nice lecture also
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Kohlsdorf cares about his students and encourages everyone to share their lived experiences during class. We had weekly blogs instead of discussion boards which was a nice break. There is a midterm essay and a 18-20 page final group essay with a 10 minute presentation. You MUST attend class if you want to pass this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Honestly a super cool guy and one of the better professors I've had. For a short period I thought I was dying and he was chill about me having to miss class. Gave really good feedback.

You won't learn anything, but compared to other CSS 370 classes, this is the option of least resistance. Try to get the best group possible, it will make or break the quarter. Kochanski likes to ramble a lot. Attendance taken through OneNote comments (and not even enforced). Lots of assignments and you might turn into the Joker by the end.

Terrible, disorganized, confusing teacher. Its like being taught by someone with Alzheimer's. He's so lazy that he doesn't even check his quizs OR exams for typos. There'll be missing words, misspelled words, and grammatically errors everywhere in every assignment, quiz, and test. I mean I know your not English teacher but come on dude. DISLIKE!

I don’t think Professor Kochanski deserves all the bad ratings on here. He was always willing to help his students, did lots of example problems in class, and gave feedback wherever he could. Having a group that can work well together, watching all videos, using his examples of worked problems, and paying attention in class will get you far.

If you can take anyone else for databases, pls do it! He is a nice person, but doesnt teach databases really well, and I had to use many external resources to teach myself SQL. Provides lots of resources on his google drive, but most of it is really unorganized. Overall tough grader and is sometimes unclear in feedback.

THIS CLASS DOESNT REALLY TEACH DATABASES ITSELF! It just goes over a lot of terminology of it. That's really it. He wont use canvas for grading-- he will put the grades in, but has disabled the "calculating" part to see your overall score. TONS of group work. Google drive is a mess. Not super clear on homework. TONS of fluff but tedious work.

The lectures were stimulating and interesting class discussions were very interactive. canvas quizzes which counted for a substantial amount of points required you to study quizzlets and notes provided by the teacher. Multiple quizzes featured content that was not on any of the study material and questions that were vague and ambiguous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I had Kochanski for various classes at UWB years ago. After you've been in the field for awhile, you'll realize that Kochanski is one of those professors who likely doesn't actually know how to create software systems, and that's why he teaches instead. He never responded to any of my group's emails regarding project questions. He's really bad.

Professor Kochanski hasn't taught me anything. Most, if not all, of what I've learned was from Google. You won't learn proper SQL syntax or anything else besides the basics UNLESS you look up external sources. For a database management professor, his google drive is a mess despite how important he claims it to be. Pick anyone else for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Decent professor that provided flexible deadlines and adequate guidance for students throughout the course. Module Quizzes often had ambiguous questions that required specific details from many long readings. Assignments were often vague and needed clarification and feedback was either heavily delayed or not given at all. Good energy during lecture

Prof Kochanski (pronounced KOE-HANSKI) does not teach traditionally. He teaches the way professional tech-speakers (who are hired and flown around the country to various companies to teach things to their employees) teach. You will come out of his classes with something to say during your interviews. Solid professor with a progressive style.

If you can take this class with any other professor-DO IT! This class is mainly teaching yourself the course material by searching google. Mark will not answer your questions, no matter how straightforward your question is. Mark will say there's many resources he offers, but navigating his google drive files is a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is nice, but a bad teacher. He doesn't prepare for lectures, will ask the class if they have questions and spend an hour or two answering only one of them. He spends way too long going over models, and you are pretty much left to learn SQL on your own. He loves group projects because he hates grading. Outside of tests, it's group work only.

Mark is just bad. He does not teach well, and is possibly the most disorganized professor. He says his avg score is 70 on exams and that is because no one knows how they are gonna do cuz he sucks at teaching. Dont take Mark Kochanski or your grade will suffer and you wont learn at all

he is a disaster. he is DBMS instructor, ironically his canvas and and other file systems are messed up. files are all over, no clear instruction for homeworks, projects. he dont teach difficult part of the material, ask him a yes/no question, he will give you a 10 min, non answer rambling.i recommend not to take the class with him at all
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Instructor knows his stuff, but does not give great feedback on any of the assignments. Though he does go over stuff in class, there is a lot of self learning and tedious work. A lot of unnecessary group projects and is a tough grader. Goes over the basic stuff but doesn't really get into the tough material
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: In-class work is meant to get you to practice applying your teamwork/team management skills he teaches you through his modules on various types of management. His quizzes are tough but definitely passable if you really study the concepts. He's easy to work with and you'll get a good grade if you just put in considerable amounts of effort to learn.

CSS350 is all about group work so you can't skip out on the class if you want to pass. I thought Mark did a great job teaching us management principles by forming teams in class together. Don't worry about not knowing anyone for your group, you will likely not be able to choose your full group anyways. Don't slack off on the quizzes & participate.

Lectures are extremely involved and beneficial to understanding concepts. Grading is a little bit unusual, but if you demonstrate learning, you will do well. Everything is done in groups, and the workplace simulation that takes place all quarter helps to enrich the experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. He intentionally makes assignment expectations unclear to increase your stress level. If you ask a question expect a 5 minute soliloquy that doesn't answer it.

Marks strongest points are his lectures.  He's loud, passionate, and incredibly knowledgeable. His weakest points lie in his lacking clarity surrounding assignment guidelines and his email response time (doesn't respond). He won't hold your hand through the (tons of) material, but he'll catch you if you fall and help you back on your feet.

Drags on explaining very simple concepts via lecture and doesn't accept an answer unless it is worded exactly as he words it. Scares a lot of people out of participating in class because of the badgering of a students answer. If I could I would take this with another prof but IMD is very limited in its faculty. He is knowledgeable but teaching nsm

One of the worst teachers I have had. He talks down to students and makes you feel stupid for asking him any questions. He wastes a lot of time in lectures explaining simple things and skips over explaining things that are harder to understand. Material is simple but he over complicates it.

Could be a great professor if he explained things more clearly and set clearer expectations. Still got a good grade in the end but hated having to wait until the end of the quarter to see what my grade would be. Doesn't grade on many assignments. Hope you love group projects. You barely use the book.

He is a knowledgeable professor but doesn't communicate it very well. His notes and videos are very confusing. The classes are interactive and interesting. But he gives marks only if the answers are exactly the same as he wants, does't accept alternate explanations at all. He is very harsh when it comes to grading assignments and exams.

His class was not extremely difficult, but a lot of busy work. Class was unorganized; assignments were added randomly, often last minute. Interesting concepts were covered, but the quizzes covered so much, it might as well have been an exam. It was definitely a do-able class, but a bit frustrating for me personally.

Not organized at all... graded homeworks the last week of the quarter, so there was no time to learn from the past homeworks. Really a harsh grader as well. Avoid if possible. Uwb css program is really messy

Very engaging lecture style. He brings a deep understanding/background related to the computing industry as a value add. Tests are not that difficult but sometimes group work (output) expectations are ambiguous.

There is no structure to this class and nothing is really taught. You're expected to create this project in a large organization but are never told what kind of work should be completed - you make it up, which doesn't really teach you how to follow good software engineering principles, just how bad you are at coming up with them on your own.
Not helpful at all, very confusing, never available, never answered emails, very disorganized in both content material and grading, always changing course syllabus
He is very inconsistent, and assigns work at the last minute all the time. I've spent much of my finals week doing last minute busy work

Kochanski's lectures are interesting and applicable. However that is dampened by his terrible class notes, laziness and lack of communication. The fact that his lecture notes are extremely vague and he expects all sorts of information in your answer on exams doesn't help either.
Inconsistent grading and ambiguous direction on assignments.
Mark is great teacher. His tests and assignments tend to be a bit difficult, but the knowledge he has and provides is outstanding. Thanks for a great class!!!

Great insight into the computer industry. If you can't wait to graduate and be a coder, this class will make you fall asleep. If you can't wait to graduate and MANAGE coders, sit up and pay  attention - this class will be very valuable. Mr. Kochanski is a solid lecturer, knows his content inside and out, and is a very reasonable grader. The key to getting a good grade is simple: read the book and take notes in class. Review all the lecture notes right before tests and quizzes you will be fine.

Great teacher for DB classes, his managment classes are not quite as good (but still good value).  Lectures are animated and info packed.  I don't love his short answer testing style, you won't either.  He is clearly passionate about teaching and I appreciate that.  Avoid needing special attention, he's still overbooked.

I have had him for several classes, including an independent study.  I learned a lot in each of the classes, and wouldn't hesitate to sign up for another.  He is over-committed, so if he doesn't respond to e-mail, catch him in his office.

Clearly very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the topic. Writes everything on the board (no slides) which makes it easy to take good notes. The textbook is mostly useless; be sure to take good notes and study them well for the quizzes. Not the easiest class in the world, but he was my favorite professor this quarter.

Gives very little preparation for what's on tests. Courteous and professional. Easy going. Not enough application of the knowledge. Comments and hilights solely what you've done bad on your projects. Doesn't give students hope of success. Intense book reading is a must if you want to pass with anything more than a 2.

I had him for a couple of classes and as an internship advisor for a project I worked on with another student. During the entire 11 week internship, he ignored every email I sent, he ignored every question I asked and took absolutely no interest in what I was working on. He obviously saw our GPAs since our grades matched our GPAs exactly. Avoid!

I'm not sure how his grading curve works, but, umm, be prepared to be uncertain on how you are going to do. Enjoy his quizes. This is coming from a student with consistently higher scores in different classes.

Is entirely redundant from his slides and does not adequately prepare you for assignments. If you haven't worked in industry, you will have a lot of trouble understanding his test questions and assignments. Reading the book (which he never used) would have been more useful than taking his class. He is the worst teacher I have ever had at UWB.

Lazy, only uses lecture materials from other instructors who have previously taught the class and rather than acknowledge a lack of knowledge, he tries to fake an answer when faced with a question he cannot truly answer.  A painfully incompetent fraud, but an easy grader.  Tenure was created by and for people like him.

Lectures are from pure powerpoint. Does not make the subject even remotely interesting. He is a classic DBA that has poor communication skills from the old IT world. You can probably get away with just printing out the PP slides and not going to class
Kochanski lives off of his slides.  Print them out and study them and you'll do just fine.  He sometimes argues with students in class.

AMAZING professor. As a person, he's very caring and supportive, and loves to talk with students. As a professor, his class is very conceptual - which makes it slightly difficult - and he's hard to understand due to his accent, but he's still a phenomenal lecturer and grades very, VERY fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His class promotes expansive thinking on philosophical and global issues. He is very wise and seems to have liberal opinions, and encourages participation. Classes are lecture-based and graded based on five short synthesis papers on topics of choice. He is a great guy but his old-school teaching style may not be for everyone.
Requires you to think outside of your comfort zone and involve critical thinking in readings. Make sure to be detailed and specific in reading response and seminar papers to do well!
Extremely caring professor. However, looks for specific details in reading responses and seminar papers.

First time taking Bruce, his class structure was a bit confusing in the beginning but he started to acknowledge students better through feedback on their reading responses and seminar papers. Focuses on Eastern European Human Rights connecting about culture and religion. He's an okay professor, hilarious, and strict but a TOUGH GRADER so watch out!

Professor Kochis is one of the best teachers I have had at UWB! I took his BIS466 class and BIS468 and enjoyed both. He assigns multiple short papers and gives you the freedom to write on topics that interest you relating to the readings. Class time is mostly lecture and it is easy to participate. Definitely Recommend!

Human Rights and Sustainable Development. You will learn everything about that. Had to read 5 books and most of them are pretty interesting. Very interesting class discussions. No tests or quizzes. You get graded based on the quality of your short papers (2 pages max) and attendance, professionalism, and participation.

Brilliant professor. He's wise, intelligent, and his teaching style is very old school.  Doesn't use technology-- no updates on canvas (so good luck getting a response when emailing) and he will make it clear he doesn't want it in classroom either. Come to class, be involved in group discussions, and follow his writing guidelines b/c he's picky.

Excellent professor and course. His lectures are interesting, and he not only lectures but really helps facilitate a good conversation between himself and all students in the classroom. There was a lot of reading, and the course was very challenging, but I felt myself grow as a writer and become better at structuring arguments because of Kochis.

The course was interesting at times. Some readings are very tough to get through because it's hard to pin point the author's argument, however the instructor will kind of clear that up in class. Has a randomizer list to call on students that was used during the first half of the quarter.
Very interesting class, good guy. Expect to do the assigned readings and actually come to class.

I took Kochis for BIS 353 and it was a very intellectually stimulating class. You could tell the guy was passionate and knowledgeable about the topic which was nice. He tried to come across as really tough in the beginning of the quarter but he actually is a really nice guy. Come to class, do the reading and reading responses, and you'll be good.
Great class and professor to take if you enjoy feeling inadequate 90% of the time

Great Great Guy! Fairly old but he has such a passion in teaching his classes! His classes will all overlap! He will love to always help out his students!  He has a different & weird way to have his papers written!  But good guy & easy going guy!

There are no tests, only weekly readings which can be pretty lengthy. This class wasn't really about Human Rights, more about Czechoslovakia and his heritage. Lectures are really boring, actually fell asleep once. He doesn't give prompts for the weekly papers, just says to write about whatever you want. Nice enough guy and easy class but boring.

Great Teacher! Mostly readings and lectured based. My only issue is that you don't know where you stand grade wise most of the quarter and he doesn't give much feedback. However, he's engaging, interesting and you learn so much. The class challenges what you've always known but in a good way. Loved this class. Recommend it to everyone!

Great professor. Lectures are definitely geared toward a more mature audience. He doesn't "dumb down" the material at all. It's an interesting course, and Dr. Kochis is a great lecturer. I would love to take another class offered by him,

His style honors mature students who can write well and do the reading. It was a refreshing class to take - no silly exams or quizzes, just prove you did the reading through papers. I am definitely taking another class from him because he really has let go of the banking theory of education and it really is much better this way.

Kochis is not open to ideas that question his opinions. Very unhelpful during office hours as he only looked up a few times from his computer screen to answer questions I had about the readings. He appears to be open but if you are critical he has no time for you. Will not take another course.
He is a fantastic teacher.  He can ramble a bit but it's always interesting and on topic. You can expect lots of reading and analysis writing. However, the readings are usually worth the effort.

The randomizer list is very intimidating because you never know when you are going to be called on, so obviously everyone does the readings. Creates great class discussions. Very interesting topics, great prof!
There is a lot of reading. A book every two weeks and a test after. Hes not hard, but He tends to get side tracked and rambles about one topic.

The first day of class, he tells you that he has his "Randomizer List" where he calls you on the spot what your answer is. It's intimidating, but Professor Kochis is really nice and adds humor to his lectures which can sometimes be dry. There are 3 essays on 3 diff books, final project is your choice. Take him though, you will learn so much!

Bruce Kochis is AMAZING! Never have I felt so empowered in my life. I think everyone should take one of his courses before they leave UW Bothell. He's tough, but he pushes students to their full potential. He makes you think real critically about life. He has made me a more aware and responsible global citizen!
He is one of my favorites. Actually the best I had ever. His teaching style is great. YOu will learn a lot of things from him, not just class subject. You can cultivate your humanity
Really enjoyed his class. He is a great teacher and mentor. Taking a different class with him this quarter!

This has been one of my favorite classes of all times.  The in class discussions were informative and interesting.  Dr. Kochis isn't an easy teacher, but he is very fair and always helpful.  You will learn a lot in his classes and might actually change the way you think.  He is a great lecturer and a wonderful teacher.
I think Bruce is brilliant. He made me think.  He brought ideas to me that blew my mind.  He is a constant inspiration, even 15 years later.

Had an issue with the assigned group; no help at all, and no desire to be of help.  A paper was marked wrong when it was not, tried to talk to the professor he turned his back on me - ending the conversation.  Grades are more about grammar than knowledge. One of the worst classes ever!
Prof Kochis is amazing! And he is absolutely adorable!!!! I highly recommend him to anyone who really wants to learn.

I have taken several classes from Professor Kochis. He is absolutely the most inspiring and able teacher I have ever had. His insight and kind nature are truly inspiring and redefined my chosen career path. Hard, but SO worth it!

The only person who didn't like this professor doesn't even know how to write! Shows how much he actually cares about school. Anyhow, Kochis is the best Prof. I've ever had. You will love his strong desire for students success and his immense community involvement and knowledge.

Bruce Kochis is the BEST professor I have ever had. His claases are challenging, but so enlightening and inspiring. His intelligence and skills as a teacher are admirable and I wish I could take his class every quarter!
Best teacher at UWB. His classes are very challenging, but he gives great lectures and the content is interesting. Cannot recommend his classes enough!

I cannot remember the exact course number. However I had about 4 classes with this professor. He is one of my favorites. This man is brilliant and speaks 8 languages fluently. He has strict expectations and will randomly select you to answer questions. Never use the word "interesting" it is a banned word. Lots of writing and research. Be prepared.

U have 2 read a 400 pg book every wk & write 2 pg analysis. He isNEVER clear about what ur supposed to write-only says "challenge urself" then dings pts for "too much description" U must attend once a wk for "Seminar" 2 hand in paper-You can BS the papers and skim book BUT expect a low B. He grades VERY subjectively but you pass 4 turning it all in

I loved this class!  It was one of my favorites and based on the strength of Kochis?s personality.  He is very intelligent, kind, funny and a good person overall.   There were 6 books to read of which 4 were very fast and easy to get through.  Fascinating content and class discussions.  I loved our group ? we met once a week to discuss the papers w

Class: Human Rights.  The format was lecture and group discussion.  Overall I found the professor to be very knowledgable in this feild and quite inspiring.  He presented very provacative information and encouraged students to delve deeper into understanding the issues surrounding human rights.  This class was easy and intellectually stimulating

I expected a lot from the class, but none of my expectations were met.  Too much reading, poor lectures, rarely answers emails.  This class was very poorly taught and I didn't learn anything.  I wouldn't take another class from Kochis.

I did not like the class at all.  I didn't learn a thing and I am one of the students who put in the most work.  I have no idea what I was supposed to get out of that class as Kochis gives little direction yet expects specifics.  Class was a waste of my time.
Hard but the best class ive ever taken
His classes are personality contests.

I thoroughly enjoyed his Human Rights class. Not only will you gain significant knowledge in the subject matter, you will also learn helpful study hints. Professor Kochis is a sincere man whose wisdom benefits every individual.

I took Kochis for human rights and he was great.  I would have to say that he is my favorite teacher at UWB.  When looking at the syllabus on the first day it can seem like a lot of reading but the thing is that the writing work required to comment on the reading can be read in either the conclusion or the intro. Great guy!
No Comments
My favorite teacher at UWB. Very smart and respectable professor. There is a lot of reading in this class but very managable! Mid-term but no final. There is a final paper but short (5 pages).
No Comments
Great professor who makes class interesting and goes beyond the usual textbook stuff.  Nice person too.
Top shelf,  This guy is the real deal and if you take his class, show him the respect he deserves by taking his classes seriously.
He starts off as a hard ass, then, turns very cool.  I believe he's trying to weed out some students.  He requires A LOT of reading about 200 pages a week.  One of my Favorites
One of the best professors I have encountered. She is very caring and understanding of every student's needs. Clear grading expectations. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Kovalesky was one of my first professors and I am so so  glad I took her class. It was so interesting. She is so honest, humble, and has a very warm personality. She is so easy to talk to.  Her class expectations are not demanding and she gives you the necessary tools to perform well. You learn a lot and you'll love it!

I've had Prof. Kovalesky for three quarters now and she's AMAZING! Not only does she pay attention to her class and remain attentive, but she is reluctant to have one-on-one meetings with every individual in her class. I love how she tries to be there for every student. That's what counts for me. But she also grades accordingly and is very lenient!

She is such a great teacher! She is very lenient on due dates. She give quiz guides that have the same questions the quiz has. Super easy and entertaining class! Lots of hands-on activities and videos. She is really easy to talk to and makes the class interesting. I would totally take her again!
She is sort of disorganized, but she is so nice and sweet. She is willing to get to know the students and very friendly. She is also an easy grader.
BEST PROFESSOR I EVER HAD! I WAS SO SAD ON THE LAST DAY OF CLASS! TAKE HER CLASS, I PROMISE YOU WON'T REGRET IT!!! :D
Loved her! Such a nice teacher! Awesome!

I took this class after hearing some good things about the teacher and it's been the easiest class I've taken so far. While there are a few essays you need to write, there's a lot of freedom in your topics so as long as you do something you enjoy, it shouldn't be bad.
she is best teacher ever. she is my favorite professor i love her :D she is always nice to people and she is wonderful person! :D
I took her art and healthcare class and i loved her! Very nice and understanding,, we had snow days and she told us to not even worry about coming! Learned a lot in this class too!

I love Professor Kovalesky. She is the nicest and most helpful professor. She is always looking out for her students and makes sure that they understand. She have great enthusiasm for her topics and is open to new ideas.

very disorganized! lost all my papers at the end of the semester...i was so frustrated at the level of work she gave us and the unessary projects and papers she made us do. we also have to read 4 novels over the semester and it was very difficult for her to tell clear directions. her expectations were too much!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is kind of crazy, but the class was interesting.  It is a lot of work and reading, however.  Assignments are nothing but busy work, but I got 100% on all.  Expect to do some interprative dances as she is a performance teacher and expects all of her classes to 'perform.'

If you want to learn aout thing through sund and movement take this techer.  She makes you dscribe how yo feel about important issues by using movement.  This teacher got a PHD in Theatre and should not be teaching any other non-related classes.  You'll have to read 5-6 books and write a paper 4 every class!!!

This teacher has no idea what your grade really is. She doesn't keep track so requires you return a portfolio with all yur papers at the end, and she loses the papers she needs to give you back.  I have taken 2 classes with her and I am sure she gives grades on how she feels about you. I got a 3.6 even though I got A's on everything; dead serious!!

If you like structure and clarity it is unlikely you will enjoy this professor. There is a tremendous amount of worthless assignments and you always have to be in class because there is always something due. She is a nice person but very hard to follow at times.

Kanta does not like students who don't agree with her views, boring class and is really out there. Be prepared to read every day and two books a week and write a response and papers on the reading. Lots of class assignments, but not helpful at all, unless you are into liberal stuff.

The most useless class I have ever taken. We had 6 required books and 3 online required readings (each book was at least 300 pgs). Papers were due EVERY class and we had SO much busy work. By the end of the coarse I wanted to go insane!!! We had so much reading that we kept moving forward in the readings but back tracking b/c too much info!!!!

Wow.  I never worked so hard.  Readings and responses due every class.  On the flip side...I loved that she worked very hard to help us to understand the material on a deeper level.  I have never stretched my mind like this before.  I thought it was a wonderful class.
I hated this class. SOO much pointless homework.  I have NEVER had so much busy work in any other course ever.  I didn't learn anything and she wasn't clear about assignments or expectations.
i loved this class, and it was the easiest grade i have gotten at the UWB so far. alot of class participation, but its worth it.
a total waste of time -- class title is appropriate
very unusual course.  took me awhile to get into it, but the instructor was very patient with  "shy" types like me.  pretty easy course, too.

I love her teaching style. Covers many different learning styles, less lecture, hands on in class activities. It really keeps you on top of the material because you have to use it in class to develope your understanding. Her expecations are reasonable.
Very frustrating class and getting in touch with her to get papers back after class was very difficult.  Still don't have all my stuff back
Very much a change of pace course for me.  Not as much heavy thinking but a lot of "doing."  Kanta is very engaging and caring, but leave your hangups at the door!  I enjoyed the course tremendously.
Very subjective grading. Does not communicate well.

Kanta is an amazing professor and person. She really cares about her students educations and would go the extra mile for anyone. Her classes are interactive which helps you retain the info better and makes the class time enjoyable. i highly recomend this prof.
