reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Other than Alice being a bum program (the program you use in class), this class with this professor is an easy A as long as you do the work. Lectures were okay but often times people just fazed out or skipped lecture entirely but were able to do the homework fine in the end and got As. P.S. this class is very time consuming & tedious of Alice

She is definitely a very safe option for a professor. Very clear expectations, well-organized course, lectures can get a bit boring as the class itself is on the theoretical side. This class has a major portion of the grade in group work, so choose your teammates well. The exams have 2 parts- on canvas and on paper. One page of notes is allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very chill class. If you have good teammates for group projects, the class gets a lot easier. The exams are easy if you studied and created your note sheet
I feel privileged to have such a great professor. She is extremely helpful and replies to emails very quickly.

Look, the class/material itself is hard, but the prof is pretty good at explaining the concepts. I came into this class knowing next to nothing and now I'm in the major. Go to her office hours and ask for help, it's that simple

She is such an amazing teacher, her lectures are quite slow to me, but the material she teaches is so useful and I'm glad I took this class with her. She is amazing and helps alot with the homework! She also gives extensions so she is super super understanding. Take her if you see her!

She is very understandable, knowledgeable, and caring to students. If you come up with any questions, the first crucial key is to ask questions and do not feel ashamed to do it. There are many students out there that will be beneficial for your questions.

Being in her 342 class, there are many mistakes in the lecture slides and wastes class just setting up code exercises in class. But, GO TO OFFICE HOURS. If the HW seems impossible, she will explain it until you understand and know what to do (almost too much so). If you are new to C++, take Kalmin! Lectures are boring but she's very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best comp sci class Ive ever had! Go to office hours she will help you
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Get ready for fast-paced lectures. Can manage if already read the textbook and attended reading quizzes. Prof helps a lot with weekly assignments -make use of it. would recommend taking her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are quite poor in material and does not provide any depth as to why or how something works. This class will expect you to learn outside of class. The slides will not be useful and her TAs are really strict with grading. If you are a beginner to java, you will suffer taking her class.

Pretty good prof! Dont know why shes so downrated here. Had her for 142, 143 (in-person) and 360 (online) and shes by far my favorite prof. Lenient, kind and gives help or second chances on assignments frequently to students who need it. She also referred me for a great job I got, and I worked as her TA for a quarter!

Her two hour lectures feel like days. Extremely bland, and she just reads off the slide notes. Sometimes when going over examples, she will get confused and skim over them. Also, some of her test questions seemed unfair, testing us on multiple things that were mentioned BRIEFLY in like 2 seconds. Waste of my time.

Prof. Kalmin is very kind, but had a hard time teaching virtually. Almost no one talked during class, so she went through the lecture slides very fast. She does a few coding problems during class, but sometimes she gets confused. The exams are MC and 4-5 coding problems, which are graded on concepts, not if the program runs. Gave partial credit!

Not sure why shes rated so low as shes one of the nicest CS professors Ive seen. She goes over materials needed for HW and exams thoroughly in class. HW and exams were also very reasonable and she gave leeway in grading coding questions on exams as long as she can tell you got the material. I honestly barely used outside resource to do anything.

I would not recommend taking her class unless you know the materials beforehand. Although she's caring to her students, she doesn't deliver her lectures well, so a beginner would have to rely much on outside sources. Homework weighs only 30% of the grade, the rest is weighed on tests (2 midterms and 1 final). There's only 1 extra credit assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this teacher. She does not even know Java (not even the basic syntax) She always talks an example and stop explanning because she does not know how to solve the problem. You don't learn anything from her. Don't take her class unless you already know how to code.

Let's be honest the class was a free GPA boost. The teacher is very flexible, I was able to get an extension for several assignments just by emailing her. If you just do the homework that is posted by her then you should be fine in the class.

Pretty easy A for a VLPA class. Just do the guided walkthroughs in each chapter and you will be set fo the class. The book has a few errors so beware. There are only 4 animation projects that need to be submitted. No midterm or final. The animation software, Alice 3 is pretty glitchy and annoying at times. But she will do her best to help.

Such an awesome teacher! Yes, her lectures are a bit dull, but it's honestly an easy class to achieve great marks if you pay attention AND are paired with a great group. Projects are heavily group-dependent so take that with what you will. I would HIGHLY recommend her; she's lenient, caring, and the workload is light.

Very boring professor. If you want to sit in a 2-hour lecture with a few activities at the end, then pick her. The class was half full by the end. Very disorganized and unclear with project specifications. The midterm and final were fairly straightforward. 4 group projects that are graded very leniently because I scored full marks in all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice and warm human being, but not the greatest teacher. I assume a lot of students who took her class would empathize. Her homework instruction can be vague. Multiple mistakes on every slide or quiz. I understand she's a human being that mistakes sometimes, But really? This many?

A good teacher who is competent in her grading. Her grader is unnecessarily specific and will mark you down for small mistakes, despite meeting expectations. Still, the professor herself is generous and will curve your grade at the end of the quarter depending on everyone else.

Very nice, accessible, and approachable professor who's always willing to help students on anything (lecture materials, homework, prep for tests/quizzes). Pushes back due dates when students are struggling with the homework and drops questions on tests/quizzes if it was too hard or worded incorrectly. cout << "Most lenient prof in a CS Course";

Currently in her first 342 class. Homework, quizzes, and midterm were all fair. She pushed back homework frequently if enough people ask which was kind of a kick in the face to the people who actually did it on time. Her homework instruction documents aren't always clear so ASK to be 100% sure on what to do. Learn some c++ before this class.

Lesley really does want her students to succeed, and is fair about grading. If a question was difficult to understand, she gives the point back. The lectures are long. There is one quiz, one hw assignment and one lab assignment due each week, and the assignments get difficult at the end. The labs & hw are the same for all sections of CSS 143.

Overall good professor. Class and lectures are pretty laidback and she answers questions well. Lectures arent't too boring and breaks are given. Her only downside is her tests... some of the questions she puts on it are ambiguous  but she usually gives everyone the question if enough people complain.

Really chill and approachable professor. Flipped model class works well. Online lectures are slow and long, but slides are easy to skim and videos help when reviewing. Exams are very easy with a moderate amount of work. Highest class test averages I've seen in any STEM course (94%).

Funny professor. Flipped classroom, videos are too in-depth and slow for me but skimming through the slides was enough. Lectures in-class added great understanding and exams are easier than the HW. Optional attendance every other day (but attendance EC) for R Labs and quizzes. Review the Pearson and review sheet and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom model; would highly recommend watching the lecture videos if you want to feel confident with the content. I found the exams fairly easy, especially after the first exam. She allows a notesheet (8.5 x 11, both sides,) and if you're familiar with the stats functions on your graphing calculator, you will at the very least pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took in Winter 2025, the class uses a flip class technique where you're meant to watch recorded videos by Dr. Dundon and in class we do practice problems. Depending on the day she even lets you out pretty early. There's R Labs and Pearson HW. Exams allow cheat sheet. Dr. Simonsen is very kind and funny however I wished she taught more in person

You watch pre-recorded lectures made by Prof. Dundon, who seems to know more about the material than Prof. Simonsen. For the R portion of the course, you just do an internet tutorial in class, but Prof. Simonsen hides in her office while you do it because she doesn't know how to use R. She pads her reviews on RMP. Just take Stats with Prof. Dundon.
One of the best professors at UWB!

This is the best class I've taken at UWB and the best prof I've ever had! I never enjoyed attending class or thought it was worthwhile until I took this class, as I usually teach myself everything. She is truly the only teacher who has ever taught me anything. Also, attendance was only mandatory once a week for anyone wanting to know.

She's very chill and understands what she is teaching. Her lectures are very applicable to reality. She is very caring to students and is ready to give help outside of class if needed. This class this quarter is SUPER! One of the best class I have ever had in UWB. I wish she taught Calc 2 & Calc 3. She really cares about what students learns
Great professor!

The only consistent thing in this class so far is how inconsistent it is. First there's a quiz every week, then she says no more quizzes, then she says ok we have quizzes but only on weeks when we don't have a lab due. She also mixes up material on the quizzes. This week our week Chapter 7 quiz was actually on Chapter 9 material.

This class was very fun and informative. The class does seem intimidating at first, because of the vast amount of content, but if we mainly use the calculator wisely, the class becomes much easier. There are assignments due at the end of each class, so paying attention during class is important. The tests are a good reflection of the exam reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She expected us to know how to calculate before she started her PPT. She's really nice but her teaching is a bit confusing. I managed to pass this class by self-studying.
This class was awesome, only thing was a bunch of group work. I've taken her before and would defintely take her again!

She is really good at lecturing. You will know what the material will be on for the week. It's only for once a week, but she makes it two hours of class instead of three. She's clear concise and makes the topic much more interesting then it is. If you do all your work, then you'll do fine.
Great teacher. Not boring at all. Good sense of humor. Learned a ton.
Great teacher! Very easy (even for those who don't like math!), but attendance is crucial. There's a lot of in class assignments that will boost your grade. Definitely recommended!
Average teacher, knows what she talks about, keeps you bored once in a while. If you do take it you'll find out that most of the work is easy
Pretty dope prof, very lenient on test/quizzes
Hella boring, but otherwise can teach pretty well

Alan's 476 class is ridiculously hard for no reason. He has an incredibly high opinion of himself. He claims he's the one and only who can teach this class, and there is no other class like this one in the country. One group project is almost 60% of your grade. It's impossible to get 4.0. He is quite rude at times as well. Avoid him at all costs.
This man has a high opinion of himself. He is an egotistical maniac and thinks he better than everyone else. It is literally impossible to get a 3.7-4.0. Avoid at all costs

Alan is a good professor. He is nice, kind and his lecture is well organized. But, the problem is one of TAs named Trixie. She grades arbitary, starts grading from 60%. Once you luckily get a high grade, it doesn't mean your overall grade would be also high. Avoid her, she is a type of person who ruins your grade, and makes her GPA look nice.

WARNING: This class is unlike every other classes you will take, but in a good way! Professor is absolutely amazing. Alan really pushes you and tries to get the best out of you! New-tech alumni are equipped with the tools to make a dent in this world. He draws out student's creativity to look at technology and innovation differently. 100% take him!

This class kicked my butt in the best way possible. The competitive environment of creating products to win the customer pushed me and my team not just to meet requirements on paper but to do our best. Amazing guest speakers come in to present and as advisors for our products. Harsh grading on assignments but best class I've ever taken at UWB

This is a prof who dedicates his life to his students. He is kind, genuine, and honest and will prepare anyone who's interested in entreprenuership how to navigate the ropes. His teaching style is not like most classes, but again it prepares you for the real world more than any other class. He will go out of his way to help you if you ask for it :)

Alan is an absolute hero. Huge network, very kind, gets to know everyone personally. He is always willing to go out of his way to help teams and has a quirky sense of humor. Very genuine and knowledgeable. Just make sure you're passionate and have a good group since you'll be with them for 6 months. I'd say avoid doing food, it can be forgettable.

Alan's kind of an odd cat among the professors at UW. He tends to judge things holistically and adapts his classes on the fly to suit his needs. Despite this, there's a definite method to his madness. If you're there to coast, you'll get roasted, but if you put in the effort, Alan's classes are arguably the best way in Foster to learn and network.

He is a cool, quirky professor that expects you to get out of your comfort zone. Take notes of everything, and it is a great environment to meet new friends while networking with Alan's speakers and other connections. His class inspired me to apply for the UW Entrepreneurship minor! OPEN TO ALL MAJORS.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Alan is a very unusual professor. You really don't learn a whole lot in class as this is mostly done on your own time and at his office hours. He brings in really cool guest speakers. He doesn't grade assignments until the very end and there are not many throughout the class. You HAVE to come to class and participate every time in order to do well.

This class: Amazing, you will not believe the quality of the "screening report" you'll be able to write after the class finishes. You'll get in touch with a lot of different businesses and learn about them! Exciting.  Alan: He won't lecture you much, but will always provide resource for you! Very caring man, he'll be the best thing for you at UW

The creating company class as a whole: Amazing experience, you learn so much about starting a business and you'll see significant personal growth from this! Don't be afraid of it being hard, you'll have unlimited resources to help you!   Alan: He's the most caring man, though the class structure is quite free, alan is always there to help you!
The man!
Alan is the most helpful professor ever!

He rarely lectured and the lectures that were given didn't form a coherent theme. I did well on the exams and worked my ass off on the final presentation and still got a terrible grade in the course. I think he could do a better job of communicating what's expected in the final presentation.
Great Professor! Very helpful! Very interactive class

Alan is dedicated to serving his students, he will give you 100% support. He doesn't do textbook lectures but likes to be a facilitator (as educators should be!). For those of you people who say he plays favorites: ITS TRUE! However he's super approachable and if you can't get him to like you have no one to blame but yourself.

Life changing. Its not about the grade you will get on a test or assignment, its about life people! He really nails it, its about what are you going to do with your life. The resources he gives you makes it easy to figure your life out. Its much more then a class.

Alan is an AWESOME professor!! He has a unique teaching style that keep the class interesting and fun. He believes that you should not take a class that you can learn from a book. I completely agree with him! He makes class fun by bring in guest speakers every class and having them tell the class about their business experiences. Super fun and EASY

Didn't know what to expect coming into the class, and was at first thrown off by his different teaching style. But it became one of my favorite classes, and he gave a wonderful introduction to the world of entrepreneurship. His projects were a lot of fun to do, and don't necessarily require a great amount of time outside of class.
He's an extremely nice guy. Slightly ambiguous but a really good person to have in your contacts for networking later on if you plan to go into entrepreneurship.

On the - side: his book is nowhere near adequate and poorly written. he's not very helpful, loves being fawned over. Definitely plays favorites and mind games, as one user noted. also, it's a big s@it pile of work (6-8 X average). on the + side: he does seem to care about what he's doing. he organized a great group of speakers worth checking out.

I have taken 3 classes from Alan. He is such a great prof who thinks outside the box to get students interested. His classes are always frontloaded so you do the big stuff upfront and then get a nice break at the end of the quarter when other classes have final projects.

Avoid if you like structure.  Take if like ambiguity. Mkts himself by ?great? prof'l contacts but aren?t that impressive. His lectures improvised. It's apparent no  effort put in lesson plans. Alan plays mind games w/ students & makes them doubt their choice in majors. Be guarded (he loves to gossip) and take what he says with a grain a salt.
Go in with an open mind. He's very untraditional to the way he teaches. Very stimulating.

This guy has an amazing ability to draw talant into his classroom. In one quarter I've met more successful business people than most of the people on campus in their lifetime. He's very engauging and passionate. A fair warning: if you always thought of running your own business, but never started, expect reality to slap the hell out of you though.

He is a very nice guy that is willing to help but he is unfocused in this class (I have heard different for other classes).  You may finish this class asking if you learned enough, but you will have definitely learned some things.
Was not information!
Worst teacher on campus
Expressive and engaging!

Awesome! He makes you talk, so dont expect to ride the class from the bench; wants class to be competitive, giving you a taste of reality. No multiple choice, you'll actually have to think (sorry). He does jump a lot between ideas making classes very rich in content, but at times hard to follow. Teaching aside, he's very powerful outside of school.

As a female student that that raised my hand, alot, I worked really hard for my 3.6.  I don't think he gave out easy grades to his "favorites".  That is very insulting to those of us that worked hard, and sounds like sour grapes.   He could be scattered, but he offered speical study sessions before tests, that covered everything on the test.
No Comments
Worst teacher on campus. Definitely would never take a class from him again. He is always trying to get close to his female students.

I have had Alan for Ops and Ent. He is a pretty good instructor. Plan on going to class because he tests on his lectures quite a bit. Also, try to be a "favorite", he plays them. He likes his favorites and treats them differently than the rest. He's fair with the rest of us, but different than the favorites by far.
Doesn't teach at all. Everything comes from your own self studing. Absolutly disorganized. Talks about "waste" a lot, but being in his class is really waste of time.
I am glad to have dropped his class. Flirts with the female students and gives them preferential treatment. Avoid this professor if possible.
No Comments
Has favorites and grades accordingly. Gender has a large part in how you will be graded.
No Comments

Leong knows what he is talking about. You can tell by the way he grades your assignments and quizes. He does not engage in favoritism in terms of grading. However, the grading is fair and his goal in the classes are not about helping students get the best grade, but rather actually absorbing the material. He is popular for a reason.

Horrible teacher!!  And I actually got a good grade in his class.  If you dont brown nose, he'll ignore you.  A lot of what he teaches is useless.  Most of the time it seemed like the students knew more than him.

If you take one of Professor Alan Leong's classes, then you are in for a long ride.  I suggest not to take any of his classes if you are not willing to put in a lot of work and effort.  His mentality is all about giving his students their money's worth when it comes to their education.  It's been over a year since I've taken a class from him, and I still do remember most of the things he teach us.  I've applied some of the knoledge from his class and applied it in the real world. Alan is the real deal!

Alan is an outstanding teacher.  He goes for quality over quantity meaning that if the class is going fast enough (class participates) you will likely go home early.  He brings a lot more to the classroom than the textbook.  He feels that his role as a teacher is to facilitate learning and add value beyond the textbook.  Most people like his teaching style but it may not be for you.  I recommend you try a class of his and you may end up taking many more.
He is an awesome teacher!!!
Alan is a great teacher, who goes above and beyond his way to help his students excel in his classes.  He does not favor one student over another.  He rocks!!!

BBUS 330, 340, 479, & 497. Alan is one of the Best Teachers out there! He's hard but you respect him! I'd definitely go back to take more of his classes even now after graduation. He's an inspiration to all students! Best of Wishes Alan; Cheers!

BBUS340 and I am taking BBUS479 with him. Alan's a great person. He isn't the best teacher (knowledge transferrer) but you might find yourself hanging out at a bar with him. Once a quarter he takes the class out but he can't buy your drinks.

Alan is not a good teacher.  He seemed to take a liking to certain students and ignored the rest.  I think he may make too many assumptions before he gets to know the students.  All this in turn makes it hard to be around him and to learn anything.

Alan is a great teacher. I enjoyed his class and learned a lot. My favorite thing about the class was the group assignment where we toured a manufacturing facility. I wish more teachers took Alan's stance in teaching and free speech.
Alan has a unique way of teaching. Lectures never go longer than necessary. Usually notes are allowed for tests. Often, my emails went unanswered, though.
He made me feel like a retard on the same day my Grandma died.  That's just plain old mean.
No Comments

Why would this class be offered to students and be REQUIRED to take alongside your internship. Imagine working a full-time job and working hard to even secure the internship in the first place just to be greeted by an evil professor who fully expects you to come to every class session. This class takes up the time needed to learn in an internship.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overwhelming amount of work, but prof is caring, fair with grading, and gives you a break now and again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a communist recruiter. Her into to sociology class is a way for her to vent about having people that make money through hard work. She gives 3 essays a week to brain wash you into believing her own agenda. Stay away from intro to sociology if you are not a leftist radical
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible structure of the class. Imagine working full-time as an intern and you are required for 3 mandatory 2-hour meetings throughout the quarter which covers absolutely nothing. Meanwhile being assigned a bunch of readings which is not informative at all. Do not take this class unless your really don't like other IPR requirements.

Shes a nice person but this class was NOT for me. Shes not ver clear in what she wants and there is so much material. I had to use my annual drop for another class just so I could get a hold on things. I am an excessive note-taker which doesnt help. And I have a disability. She rarely responds to messages. Its taken a toll on my mental health
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her assignments are very unclear. Written and verbal instructions are often contradictory. The assignments themselves are in no way challenging and honestly felt like a waste of time. You will not learn anything through the homework or the outdated films we have to watch.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this class was 50% hybrid which she doesn't say in her schedule. have to watch a lot of shows and films have to write weekly journals on the movies you watched and Social justice journal for current event related to racism. Come to class be a part of the discussion and you will pass the class. She is really understandable.

Loren is really sweet though she rambles quite a bit and often loses her train of thought. Lots of group projects and online assignments (too many imo and some felt pointless) but they aren't too hard and she's an easy grader. Just read the textbook and do the practice "quizzes" and you should be good for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Loren is a very humble professor cares about her students. She always gave good feedback and never shut down students answers. The class is graded among very small group work assignments and BCORE activities. We watched a lot of videos and was a super laid back class. Recommend if you have an interest learning about politics and DACA. Easy A class

Not sure why her ratings are so low! Loren is such a caring, sweet professor that really loves what she teaches. There are about 1-2 online assignments a week, lots of in-class activities based on participation, and two exams that were quite easy. There are also a couple of extra credit opportunities that really help to boost your grade as well!

she's very nice and sweet. but for this bcore It was 50% hybrid and I think it could have been 100% because what we did in class was just discussions. she makes you work in your groups most of the time, but its nothing hard. I can say you don't need to do the readings, assignments are time consuming but very easy.

She's a really nice and humble person although her talks in class are often boring. Cares a lot about political topics and social issues. Lots of group work and a fair amount of outside classwork. But be sure to turn your work in on time or no credit. I've taken two of her classes, recommended if you want an easy A.

I don't know what I learn in this class because she didn't teach anything in the class. She even didn't talk about the lecture and we just did a lot of group project and watch the movie. Most time we did is figuring out what she wants. Her grading rubric is also unclear so you will never know what grade you will get.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Her lecture is not so clear. The topics are interesting but she does not make it interesting to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She rambles a lot. VERY bias and political. She's not open to other people's opinions. There was no point in doing the readings that are due that day because she doesn't address them in class. She has you watch a lot of movies that degrade people who are not "truly marginalized."

I have her for a class on social change and the DREAM act, and it seems every time she talks my whole class gets more and more confused. She says "um" a lot and has to answer questions over and over again because no one knows what she's talking about. It's a month in and she hasn't put in any grades yet. She's a nice lady for sure though.
Loren Redwood is a great teacher and super nice. Homework is reasonable.  I will take another class with her for sure. Cool lady.

She seems to have a hard time spitting out what she's trying to say. Lots of 'ums' and 'I lost my train of thought' which is annoying since she basically lectures the entire class. There's an attendance sheet so you have to show up to each class AND participate. Sucks that it's not better taught because the subject seems interesting.

This class requires way too much work on top of the required internship hours. BEWARE!!! Professor is nice and willing to work with you but she is terrible at returning emails in a timely manner. I would not recommend taking this class with a heavy class-load. Five credits feels more like eight credits.

Because of medical excuses, much of the class was disoriented and even crucial days, like the day of presentations, were cancelled. The syllabus was rearranged several times and caused many students to be on different pages- confusing. The majority of the class is based on reading & there are no lectures- fairly UNNECESSARY to go to class.

Everything is clearly laid out. Do it and you'll get a good grade! Quizzes easy, exams open note. Make sure not to come to class lateuse cell phone or she'll call you out. Sometimes class will be canceled due to medical problems. Only thing I didn't like was her grading took a while. She also rambles a lot + hour long videos in class got boring.

She isn't necessarily a bad teacher per se, If she thinks you are a disrespectful person she will call you out on it and your relationship won't improve from there. If you need help, she'll help you, but her tone of voice towards you will reflect how she feels of you. Take her class but don't get on her bad side, you'll never leave it.
She has a lot of knowledge on the subject but didn't really share it. The class relied on the texts but you didn't really need to read for the assignments.
Easy A, let her know who you are and shine!

One of the most wonderful, caring, and understanding professors I've had. Gives us reasonable work within a reasonable amount of time and it is not hard at all. Her attempts  to get the class to critically think about their surroundings and use it to reflect on their lives. Class was great and mind-stretching. RECOMMEND!

Assigns a lot of reading in order to complete in-class reading responses (with specific length required). Her class was easy overall, but not very enjoyable, since our discussions were mostly recaps of what we read in our own words. Felt like we went around in circles with the same topic. She's very nice and friendly. Sometimes takes attendance.
This professor is super easy, just write something for the assignment and you'll get full credit. Easy A from this professor!
Honestly, I didn't do any of the readings and still received a 4.0, write something relevant down for the reading responses and you get full points, so easy.

Professor Redwood is a great person and easy to deal with. There is a lot of busy work (reading and writing)and the final paper was large at 12 pages. Her lectures were difficult to follow as she says umm and ahh a lot. It was very distracting. The books assigned overlapped each other so that it felt like you were reading the same book three times.
Race, Ethnicity & Immigration. Professor Redwood helped us to connect immigration issues that occurred in our area and the Japanese internment during World War II in an interesting way.

His lectures were interesting and sometimes the 2nd half of the class we worked on an in-class worksheet. There were 5 mapping projects to do. They did take some time, but he gave enough time for it. There were multiple short quizzes, but he drops the lowest score. The mid-term and final were both worth 10% each.

Professor Santiago is so kind. Attendance isn't required since slides and assignments are on Canvas. The midterm and final are online and open book. There are 10 small assignments, a couple of bigger but easy ones, and one group presentation. He's super responsive and helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely G. Love this guy, straight forward teacher no bs. Super info rich lectures with tons of accessible info on canvas. Easy to talk to and humble guy. Consider yourself lucky to land a spot in his class I enjoyed it.
Very nice teacher and passionate about helping students learn GIS. Lectures are good at helping you grasp concepts. Tests are open note. Easy to get help with him outside of class.

Professor Lopez is kind and very knowledgeable and passionate about GIS and geography. His exams can be very tricky, and his courses really require constant review of notes to fully grasp concepts. But you learn a lot of valuable skills in his courses.

Overall, I would say he is a good professor. Easy graders. Eager to help. Quizzes are relatively easy. Midterm and final are based on questions on the quiz and study guide. And don't waste your money buying books, you won't need them for this class. He has PowerPloint slides for lectures, that's all you need.

I think this professor has an excellent approach to teaching, and has a great attitude. His classes are well paced and has very reasonable expectations.  Definitely one of my favorite professors thus far at UWB and I would recommend him to anyone. He's easy to follow and goes out of his way to make sure you understand. Make sure to study for exams!

Santiago is a good professor who is very knowledgable about geography. There are 4 labs, 2 exercises, a midterm, a final, final reflection, and a group project and presentation. He is very flexible on his grading and gives good feedback. His class is mainly lecture based during the first half and activity for the second half.

He is willing to help out students and he cares about whether students understands the concept or not. Final is take home test. There are few assignments through out the quarter, but you have class time to finish most of it. He does not check attendance. He is great instructor.

Santiago is a great instructor and he is very helpful. Any problems/questions you have, you should feel comfortable talking to/asking him. Most of the material is from the lectures slides which he also posts on canvas. The class is not hard if you do the work, but there is a lot of work to do for this class. Going to class is necessary for points.

I was really intimidated by this class at first but it ended up being my favorite class of the quarter! The instructor is so dedicated to the course content and is very helpful to struggling students. Lots of assigned work but it only makes you understand the content more thoroughly! Plus he's nice to look at :)

He is great! I've never taken a Geography class and the first 2 weeks i was scared. But as soon as I met up with him in his office hours, it all was easier. He was very helpful even if you don't get it and show him you're trying. You should be good to go! He has a slight accent but it won't bug unless you let it!! LOL Overall, great teacher!

Although Professor Lopez is nice and helpful, the class was only interesting to how certain environmental issues affect the Earth. But I found the class generally to be a drag. He lectures the whole time from his power points and if not all, most of the class seems to lose interest. Allowed to use laptops. Midterm was not easy. Final was better.

The class had a heavy work load but was organized incredibly well. There are a lot of components that go into the class, and they do take a lot of time to complete. His lectures were so well planned and he was very nice. I had no interest in GIS prior to taking this class but the professor made the subject interesting! Don't miss class!
Professor Lopez is a very fair, considerate, helpful, engaging instructor. Loved his geography class. Highly recommended. And he's adorable. ;)

What a wonderful Professor! I loved his lectures and he made all the work easy and simple to do. Don't get me wrong, it took time to complete the labs and some of it was challenging but the instructions and preparation made it very straight forward. Make sure you give yourself at least two days to complete any of the assignments so you have time.
Great instruction very helpful when needed. Look forward to taking another one of his courses.
he is very helpful and great teacher ever!
He is the best professor I've ever seen. Easy Grader. Assignment (Lab) is not difficult at all but takes some time to finish them. Exams are easy with the practice he provides.

AVOID. I felt like she simply didn't have time to legitimately help students outside of class. Feedback on proof assignments weren't helpful whatsoever, the feedback is essentially "judging" your proofs. Hardly learned anything, despite spending so much time to study. Looking at the mean scores, probably at least 70% of the class did not get a 2.0

Did not feel prepared for a single exam or quiz, class average scores were very low. Everyone who sat around me had the same complaints that the review's before exams were not helpful. Just all in all way too hard for no reason.

I really enjoyed taking Calculus with Professor Loreto. Definitely one of the most fun classes and I know other students felt the same way. The main issue was the way the exams were written, however that is decided by the department. She is super committed to helping students pass and takes the time to get to know students. The best for Calc!

I will do a two-part review (maybe three) because I want to explain my experience thoroughly. I'd like to start positive, Prof Loreto is nice and will help you if needed. She seems slightly intimidating at first but don't be afraid to reach out. Despite other reviews, I enjoyed how she instructed, which worked for me. However...(part 1/2).

There is a clear problem with how exams are formatted in her class. They are worth an immense amount of your grade, however the resources provided in class will never be enough to prepare your for them (which she knows considering she makes remarks about this while lecturing). Her harsh grading and indifference to class-wide failure doesn't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Leaves 90% of the teaching up to the student, and the resource students are left with is MyMathLab, which is terrible when it comes to actually explaining concepts, and tells you that you got an answer wrong for writing it in a different way, even though it means the same thing
Professor Loreto is very flexible with deadlines and any special circumstances. The key here is you have to ask questions to understand the lectures and/or assignments clearly.

Professor Loreto is tough and that is what is expected out of a professor for Real analysis. Her lectures are clear and provide examples for proofs that are on the homework, but she does make it clear that you need to put the effort in to understand the theorems and definitions. She held tons of office hours and was a great prof. I recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's not shy about slashing points for the smallest thing and talks down to the class. We just finished a midterm and the class average was 56%. She seems unconcerned by this.

Your grade will be based mainly on test. She lectures and then allows for time homework. While she is going around the room helping she is constantly commenting on how easy all the problems are while the class struggles. When handing out practice exams for upcoming midterms she also exclaims how easy it all is and how much harder the test will be.

She's nice but her teaching is super confusing. She's strict on grading; I did my homework the way exactly the same from the book and I got half points off for no justification. When I looked at the solutions, the steps were even less than mine. The most stressful class I've ever had.

Professor Loreto is one of my favorite math professors on campus. She cares about the students and how they learn. She's super enthusiastic about math! When she talks about formulas or graphs or functions, she calls them all beautiful. You can just tell that she cares about the material and the students.

Dr. Loreto is an amazing person. She clearly shows that she is interested in her students' learning and is readily available for office hours. If you are a good self-learner, she is a great professor to take. If you need to put the onus on your teacher to teach you the material, she may not be the one for you.

Biochem is crazy hard, but she's a great lecturer. Engages students with questions, spends a lot of time on the fundamentals of each topic. She focuses more on theory than practicing problems, so it seems like a lot of test questions come out of nowhere. Really make sure you understand the concepts. She isn't very responsive to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was the absolute WORST!! Her lectures are too long and full of information which makes it difficult to follow and retain the material. She meets out of class, but makes you feel stupid for asking questions that, to her, are common knowledge. I would NEVER in a million years take her again.
She is wonderful. I wish she is more accessible outside of class but her lectures are amazing.

the exam for biochem was incredibly difficult .. even though she curves the grade, in the end, it is still not fair for students to have such difficult exams.. No homework, no exam prep (you'll find out her exam prep is not helpful for the exam, the material just seems unrelated.. ) she makes the class more unnecessarily difficult..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Robins is a student favorite. She is personable, bright, and always SO enthusiastic about biochem. Her excitement is contagious and no matter how hard the class is, you can't help but love it when she teaches it.

She will make you work for your grade, but if you do not understand something, she is always available to clear things for you. I love the fact that she cares for your success and for you to take the most out of the class.

Seems to be a smart person; however, lacks the ability to translate her knowledge to students. One of the worst professors I've ever had. BEWARE: her exams rarely relate to anything learned in class. BUT not to worry, when the whole class fails, she'll just inflate the grades. No one will learn anything from the class, but most will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is definitely very nice, so I feel bad writing anything negative at all. However, if I could avoid taking her class, I would. The subject matter is hard, so you have to expect to study a lot. She is very unorganized, and her quizzes and exams count for almost all of your grade, but are extremely difficult. Also her teaching style is bad.

This is the toughest professor that I have ever met in university. The grading policy for her class only count from ridiculously hard Quiz and the exams. She will read through the PPT the whole time in class and the problems on quiz and exams are completely different from the ones in HW. The HW that she gave does not help at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There was no book, but there were readings and a suggested book. We learned to read the financial reports. Every person chose a company.  I think the class was fine. It is a difficult topic, because every company report is different, but I felt confident to invest in stock for the first time.

Teaches her classes like she's teaching to people who already understand that field. She does not have any sympathy when you dont understand a topic... often just saying, "well you can google it" or... "we talked about this last week, weren't you listening?"... gets very frustrated when many students arent understanding material and blames class.

This professor is TERRIBLE. She's required in the MBA classes, but is a terrible teacher, doesn't provide a textbook because apparently, she's the only person that can teach accounting. And she quizes you on things she DOESN'T TEACH. Class time is a waste of time, but you have to go cause of the weekly quizes.

I was very fortunate to take cost accounting with  Dr. Hardin who normally teaches graduate courses at the UW.  She is simply outstanding.  Very knowledgeable, engaging, and so genuine.  She marshals her experience in both public and private accounting besides academia in her lectures and amazing perspective.  My team and I absolutely loved her!

Best teacher I ever had! Hard subject but she uses many alternative methods to make students understand.  Class is heavily graded on group case studies.  If I could, I would take all my classes with her!!!  Don't be fooled by the negative comments, they are because the subject is hard!  She is an excellent teacher!

Lorna is a good professor. She is very clear about what will be on her tests-- provides a study guide and practice test. The text book homework is optional, so minimal reading. She is always available for help, which comes in handy on all of the case studies-- lots of group work using Harvard case studies..!

She is the WORST accounting Prof. I have ever seen at UWB. Extremely annoying class w minimal help from her. All the assignments and case studies are disconnect from her lecture which is also extremely boring. When she hates you, everything you did will be harshly graded. Avoid her if possible.
She can sometimes be a bit unprofessional sometimes and impatient, which takes away from the students' learning. The lectures were decent, but I would avoid taking one of her classes if possible.

Rediculous  amount of homework. No time to actually study,  just piles of work. Boring lectures that are not helpful. HUGE case studies that are not connected to course material & she grades harshly.  She yells at students and shames them if they don't participate in the manner she deems correct. Worst prof at UWB.

Lorna was extremely helpful! I came into this class as my first business class with no understanding of accounting and I found her material clear and concise. I would take another accounting class from her in a heartbeat.

Lorna is a great professor, but her group projects are excessive.  During the final three weeks of the quarter, we had 3 group projects to complete in addition to regular classwork.  Each group project averages between 10-15 hours per person.  You'll learn a lot, but be ready to work for it.

Professor Hardin is one of the most caring professors out there. She teaches the material not just because it's her job. She genuinely wants to help her students understand the material. Highly recommend her for Financial Accounting.
Teach yourself through the book and online connect and you can get an A. Exam multiple choice will try to trick you.

Class is really boring, but the tests are easier when you attend all classes. I thought she taught the class very well. Doing all the homework assignments is super helpful. Her tests weren't as hard as I thought they would be. Ended up with a 3.6

She treats the class like it's an advance math class and your overall grade is based your midterm and your finals. She sounded calm when the class midterm of about 44 students averaged out to a D (66 percent) as if it is nothing and didn't make any deal on how to improve the way she tests students.  Best of luck if you take her class.
Very boring. Does not make any effort to make the class interesting. Most of your coarse grade is based on the midterm and final. Also a very annoying personality.
I had Prof. Hardin for cost and tax. She is great. The material is tough so paying attention/attending class is crucial to be successful.

She can be VERY strict, over the top occasionally. Her lectures are INCREDIBLY boring, but paying attention is vital. I would suggest taking w/ different teacher if available, but she isn't terrible if you can manage to pay attention.
Had her for cost accounting, I enjoyed the class and she taught it well.

I have no idea why my previous rating was deleted. well, this teacher has very annoying personality and knows little about cost accounting. Her class is totally boring and she is very lazy. if you take her class you are wasting your  money and time. you can do better by just reading the textbook, because her instruction might confuse you more.

Overall a good teacher, but painfully boring. If you can take cost accounting from another teacher I would highly recommend it. Her subject is not the most interesting but her voice and the way she teaches is so hard to pay attention to.

Had Dr. Hardin for Cost and Tax. She's better at tax but was not bad at Cost. The complaints that people have posted are mostly unfounded in my opinion. If you put on your big-boy/girl pants and study, you'll do fine which is a reasonable expectation for a third or fourth year college student. The choice is yours.

Dr Hardin is a nice professor with great style. She is a real person, not a teacher-bot, so occasionally she makes mistakes. I actually learn better that way, because I make mistakes too. She knows her stuff, and I would recommend her.

She seems nice, but her teaching is not good. She is not well-organized about what she is teaching. Thus, it is not easy to understand. Then, she has a bad attitude with students' questions. She does not solve the homework problems on her own, but basicially copies the answers from the answer key provided by the book publisher.
Everything seems ok, untill you take an exam. The exams are nothing like the homework or practice exam. Very unhelpful when you seek help.
Lorna was my professor for both 373 and 450. She taught very well for the way that I learn with many examples. She was also easy to approach when I needed extra help.

Her tests are irrelevant to her lectures. Do you know why? Because she does not know what she taught during her lectures since she comes in unprepared, stumbles through.  She is a kind, nice person but is an unprofessional professor. I just do not know how to succeed in this class. Sad reality is - she is the only one teaching this mandatory course

She seems to know cost accounting, but her teaching methods are absolutely ineffective. She only grades on tests and a little participation, so it's hard to get a good grade if you do poorly on an exam. Her exams are nothing like the homework or practice exams, so beware. She's also got a horrible attitude and not friendly when there's a problem.

She may not have the most fruitful lectures, but she teaches.  Exams are ok as long as you study and work through practice exams.  She'll offer help if you ask, but she def expects you to be an adult and ask, so don't sit there and wait for her to come forward.  While I don't think she's teacher of the year, she's def not as bad as what others say.

Prof. Hardin treats her students like adults and does not monitor attendance or if they do their homework, all that will come out during exams anyway. She's pleasant, talks about her subject from a real life perspective, and is always there to help if you ask for it. She states her expectations clearly and provides necessary materials to meet them.

The professor makes the course not exciting, during lectures she makes frequent mistakes and are pointed out from her own students. Sometimes not sure what she is doing and asks the class for help...tests are easy if you follow through her practice exams. Grading is hard based on point-based system, so every point is precious to you.

She is literally the worst teacher ever! She is never prepared for class and she is easily distracted. A typical class session is her reading the book power points for two hours straight. She will also tell you one thing about her grading and then surprise you with another. Her grading system is the worst out of any UWB class and you will learn not
Lorna is an excellent professor, always there to help.

This is the worst teacher I had had at UW Bothell. Avoid her at all cost. She did not prepare for lectures and made many mistakes when doing the problems. She does not seem to know what she is doing. UW is providing a poor service with this kind of teachers.

By far the worst professor I have taken at UW Bothell. She doesn't help, barely teaches, constantly complains about teaching, and has the worst attitude in the world. I can't believe I have to pay for the absolute pitiful service provided by this professor. If you're an accounting major at UW Bothell, avoid Lorna at all costs.

Hardin was very helpful and seemed to have an interest in all of her students.  Homework, quizes, tests, one paper, and one small project comprise of the curriculum.  She has a review before the tests and generally quizes and tests reflect the less complex problems found in the homework. I would recomend taking her for accounting classes.

I took Operating Systems from him. He was very easy to work with. He responded quickly to emails and texts, he encouraged experimentation on assignments, and he did his best to make sure students weren't falling behind. His lecture notes were also very helpful.
One of the best professors I've ever had as well, this comments are real, and the class was challenging, but he taught in such a good way it seemed easy.

He gave some very good lectures that helped me understand. I know there were students in other sections that would sit in our lectures as word got out who were the best profs. He was hired away to WSU which is too bad as I wanted to take some more courses from him. One of the better profs by far!
One of the best professors I have had.  Had a LOT of real world experience. Gave out their cell phone and was available to help.  Explained difficult concepts.  Cared.
Easy to contact when I had questions and usually got quick responses.

You can't even understand his English as he is a foreign person. Very condescending and gives zero regard to his student. DO NOT TAKE...  My opinion is honest as I still received an A. Never take a class with a foreign professor.

The professor is great. As others have said, he has a very unique and witty sense of humor which keeps the class together and cohesive. It's very math based and not as much economics based, but if you follow examples, you should be able to get an A+. 2 Exams, 4 group assignments, 1 paper. Easy.
Ruobo is an excellent teacher. If you make sure to understand what is  taught in class, you will do great! Just don't miss a class,or you will be screwed.

Great professor! Really diligent, no nonsense. Even did a make up class on the weekend to catch up. Difficult class though, but he really makes it easier. Really wants to teach you. Funny and friendly. 4 group projects, 1 individual, quizes, mid and final, participation. Definitely take him if you want to learn, but do not expect an easy class.

He's difficult to understand at first, but once you get used to it, it's fine. His content is great, he breaks down difficult concepts into bite sized chunks. Don't miss class though, because it's really, really hard to catch up.

Roubo runs a fast paced class and you better show up and pay attention.  IF you do, you'll do well.  If you miss a day, you'll feel it. His quizzes and exams are straighforward and difficult.  His group work element is light, and doesn't require a ton of time outside of class.  He's cute and funny.
Ruobo was a great teacher, FUNNY and cute.  Everything is hands on so it's pretty important you come to class or else you probably will fall behind.
Nice and funny teacher! This class is all hand's on.
He is very hard to understand.

Excellent Teacher. Need to keep up on the material because there is a pop quiz every week. Everything on these tests will appear on the exams so pay attention. Exams can be done in little more than an hour. Fair grade, not easy but fair. I would take him for every class if I could.

Lectures are a bit dry, but directly applicable to tests. He gives clear examples and his expectations for what will be on the test will be conveyed to you. Funny guy - would take another class from him if it was possible.
very helpful professor

Funny, smart as hell, and helpful.  I got 90% of the material from his lectures, read the book for the rest. If you need help, he always stays after class to explain every little detail. He's very concious of his accent and tries to prnounciate every word. 15 minutes per quiz, and they are tough. 2 tests, most people get done in the first hour.
You'll have to study for this class.  The teacher is very knowledgeable and can be quite funny. I had a good experience.
Ruobo does expect a lot, but he is a great teacher.  I would recommend taking him, but yes you do have to pay attention, and translate through his accent.
Roubo is Awesome he may be tough but he is a good teacher and he is hella funny
very hard tests, quizes also hard. not a clear speaker. must read book to learn any material.
I really enjoyed taking Professor Maxwell's class and I'd love to take another one! She was very communicative and I really enjoyed the participation and group activity aspect of her course.

Back loading course. I took it in summer. If you missed the final few assignments then you are looking at a D grade. Not very friendly setting for a person who still got a job to do. Boring class also. Not recommended but if you want it you canstill take it.

Honestly, for an elective class, there's WAY too much work. It's my last quarter at UWB and I was taking it with the intent of an elective class but like there's so much homework for no reason. Literally essays every week, if you are taking it with the intent of an elective class don't take it. If you are interested in the ocean then it's cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is very fun and you get to learn a lot about marine life and animals! You do have to do a decently sized 'paper' but it is split up into several smaller portions that are due throughout the quarter and at the end you just combine them all into one paper and record a video of you presenting it. Very fun class, chill professor, recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Maxwell was an incredible professor! Clearly passionate about GIS and I had a great time in her class. Attendance isn't required but labs are done in class on ArcGIS (paid program only on school computers) so not advised to skip class. Labs have very clear instructions and she's open to answering any questions. Great class!

I took this as an elective and it did not disappoint! Prof. Maxwell is very knowledgeable and her class is super well organized. We did a variety of assignments (mainly discussion boards and untimed, open-note, quizzes). The final project is multipart and done over the quarter. Nothing was too hard or boring. Fun and informative.  Recomend!

Professor Maxwell is one of my favorite professors at UWB. She is super kind, considerate and overall knowledgeable of what she is teaching! You can tell she really cares about the class and what she is teaching. Her class is frontloaded with a bunch of assignments but gets much easier later on. Always responds to emails and is an easy grader!

Dr. Maxwell is such a caring professor. Starts every module with a check in quiz and really cares about students well being. The class overall was pretty easy but still learned a lot! Not too many assignments in each weekly module, there's one final project that you work on through the quarter. She even had reduced workload week. Take her class!!!

One of my favorite professors, I've had her twice and can only hope I can take more of her courses. First off, there aren't too many assignments, and the assignments that we do have, she makes it super fun and interactive! GIS can be tedious but Professor Maxwell really makes sure that your understanding is the #1 priority.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor is amazing I can't recommend her more, if you have a chance, please take a course with this professor you won't regret it.

Prof Maxwell is such a sweet woman, she made sure that everyone was not stressed out. The first few weeks are the hardest weeks, but the assignments were still super easy. The last two weeks of the quarter we have no assignments because she "knows that other professors give you a lot at during finals" She's a very easy grader and it's hard to fail.

One of if not the best teacher I have had in my entire academic career. This is my second class with her and I want to take another class of her's because she is such an incredible professor. She genuinely cares deeply for every student and wants to see you succeed. Best teacher ever, thank you Professor Maxwell!

Professor Maxwell is definitely one of my favorite professors at UW. You can tell she's passionate about what she teaches, and cares a lot about students and their learning - she makes learning new material very easy and fun. She's kind of an easy grader, however.

Dr. Sara Maxwell was, to put it mildly, fantastic. You would expect a class teaching Geographic Information Systems to be a bit tedious, but she made it very interesting, and, dare I say it, fun! She inspires you to look at things outside of the classroom that are tied to the subject, and seems genuinely interested in what you have to say.

Dr. Maxwell cares a great deal about both her students and the subjects she teaches! Make sure to stay on top of homework/activity deadlines (especially for the final project pieces that are due throughout the quarter!) and you will do well in this class. Highly recommended class.
Her assignments' expectations are very clear and easy to follow. Her support is incredible and the workload is just right. Just do the assignments and you will be absolutely okay.

Dr. Lin reviews homework on the day it's due, discusses textbook questions in class, and requires students to write an OMP. Unfortunately, his written exam problems often lack the clarity needed to fully understand the material.

Might be an unpopular opinion, but the exams weren't too difficult, at least compared to the homework, if you take advantage of the in-class practice opportunities and consistently do the online assignments. I found the lectures engaging. The hardest part of this class is translating problems into steps, so focus on deep reading comprehension!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor. Tests were rather simple, but only if you pay attention in class. Highly recommend attending class since there are "in class activities" that are graded by participation. Not as much lecture so much as answering questions and letting you practice coding in class.

Not a bad professor, it's just the exams that make it or break it. Midterms are 40% of your grade. The wording on the exams could be better; that's a significant reason why the exams were hard. Homework grading is somewhat strict as well.

Overall, Professor Lin's lectures are engaging and all encompassing, not only following the textbook but his real life application of Python. However, the grading in this course is the most difficult aspect, with a 97% and above being a 4.0, yet tests out of 20 points, making the room for error close to 0.
Even good students struggled. He expects handwritten submissions, ignores student questions, and punishes for minor formatting issues. Not beginner-friendly at all.
This class crushed my interest in programming. Everything is hard for no reason. Instructions are unclear, grading is brutal, and exams are traps. Please take this class with anyone else.
Worst professor I've had. He does not care about his students. If you're not already a pro coder, you'll get zero help or sympathy. Run.

Grading makes no sense. He cares more about handwriting, formatting, and flowcharts than actual working code. If your comments are off, expect points off—even if your solution is correct. It's frustrating and petty.

This professor treats everyone like they're CS majors, even though it's a BA class. People with zero coding experience were completely left behind. The material was already hard, but the teaching style made it unbearable.

The exams were open book, yet most people are failing... that says everything. Questions were nothing like homework, and it's only CSS112, not grad school. No one is learning just surviving. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He does not care about his students.

He is not understanding at all, he treats his students like they are all in CS program, yet, Keep in mind there  were BA student in the class who have never touched coding and are failing the class. His teaching structure is really hard and confusing to understand. He just goes based off of his book and the exam are not even from the book at all.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!! SAVE YOUR GPA AND TIME he is so extremely rude, he does not care about his students. he wont care if you are dying, he still expects you to turn in homework. please save yourself the mental stress by taking literally ANY other professor

The average for most people on midterm 2, closed book. how is it that everyone got a 5 out of 20? when it was OPEN BOOK?!?!?!The questions on exams are not even remotely similar to the questions on the homeworks, even tho this is only CSS112 not CSS500.

He is also so unreasonable. I got docked points for something that wasn't even mentioned in the rubric. Instead of listening, he is just dismissive and does not acknowledge when something is wrong. He does not have an open mind and that creates an environment that is not welcoming for students to learn and improve in.
Take this class elsewhere, unless you have previous experience. Not intended for people with zero coding experience.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!
SAVE YOUR GPA AND TIME
he is so extremely rude, he does not care about his students. he wont care if you are dying, he still expects you to turn in homework. please save yourself the mental stress by taking literally ANY other professor

This dude knows what he is teaching that even absolute beginners can get a grasp of all the different concepts introduced. The pacing is not too fast (as expected for an entry course), which allows for more clear explanations of the material. He is great to talk to outside of class but be prepared to write a little bit and also get late responses.

The class concepts are easy but the grading is absurdly skewed towards formatting and commenting and flow charts rather then accuracy, validity, and effectiveness/conciseness of code. The class also contains useless filler work on "software ethics" which is really just common sense and busy work. Every assignment is also forced to be handwritten.

Professor Lin claims to have high expectations, but I find them about average. Most weeks have two major assignments and three minor assignments. The minor assignments take a negligible amount of time outside of class. The major assignments each take about two-four hours outside of class depending on your familiarity with the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: idk why there are so many negative reviews. He is an incredible teacher who explains anything perfectly, if you take the time to inquire & attempt to understand. Class material is HARD, but he enjoys & teaches it well. Intensive volumes of textbook reading, but it truly does help. Grading is difficult, but very fair. Very patient & pleasant person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not as bad as I initially thought. Professor Lin is incredibly lecture heavy, but they were all extremely valuable to me. However, there are no slides (he uses a whiteboard), so the only way to document the lectures is taking notes. Wouldn't recommend if you don't have good note taking skills, dislike long lectures, or expect to be absent sometimes

Dude accepts late work for absolutely no reason unless it's catastrophic. Makes you do every assignment handwritten in a CS class? I noticed no one talked about this but he randomly calls out students to answer questions. Good as it forces you to pay attention for two hours but terrible if you are someone who can doze off quickly and you get picked

His way of teaching is definitely not a fit for this generation of college students. He is VERY by-the-book and doesn't really create room for unique engagement. I had to ask for help from many different sources to understand a certain concept. He doesn't accept late work.
Run from him and don't look back. Do not take any class from Johnny. He will make your life, and your college career, so much harder.
He should really encourage more open dialogue during class and not have such a rigid structure for teaching.

Worst class I've taken in college. The in-class activities and lack of lecturing discouraged me from attending class. This prof should be less rigid with instructions and guidelines and encourage open discussion more. I got a 3.7 which is apparently "high" for his classes.
I think most first-year students may find this class hard, but you just have to communicate and get whatever help you need. I thought the class was ok, needed it for my Business MIS major.

An absolute butchery of curiosity. The course and prof are overly concerned with insignificant details that prevent you from seeing the big picture. The homework is so scoped down it leaves no room for creativity. This course barely has anything to do with real programming.
does not care about his students and you will be forced to learn course material on your own.

I took BIS 111 and was pretty much lost the whole quarter. Explanations were short and vague, and the homework assignments were extremely complicated for someone with no previous coding experience.. Professor Lin is a nice and respectful person, it's just the course and the grading that was difficult. Personally would not take again.
worst professor do not take him. I wanted to jump off a cliff. He picks on asian kids, so if you are asian do not take him.

Eh. He's a nice person and is very open to student feedback, but he strictly follows the textbook and does not curve anything. Good intro to actually learning programming style and a lot of behind-the-scenes coding concepts, but if you take his class, prepare to work a lot. Participation and attendance are a heavy portion of your grade.

Worst professor I have ever had. Grades hard, DOES NOT CURVE ANYTHING, and has the worst attitude towards students. Teaches too closely from the book and requires us to write assignments IN A COMPUTER PROGRAMMING CLASS! WTF!? Got a 3.5 which is a "great" grade w/him but it could have been higher if he curved.

Incredibly challenging class. Very difficult assignments and tests that you are minimally prepared for during lecture. Be prepared to do A LOT of work. He's a nice guy, and in office hours, he is quite helpful, but the tests are still really hard. Doesn't curve.

Difficult, confusing, stressful class. The final exam was one of the hardest things I've ever taken. Never knew what to expect and felt like he was trying to make us fail every step of the way. I lost sleep this past quarter.
He's a nice guy but grades really hard on assignments and doesn't curve exams. The CSSSKL labs are useless and I learned all the concepts in them from Codingbat
If you don't want to cry and hate CS, don't take him.

This class itself was fairly easy, if you read the material for that week you should be ok. Prof Lin was very helpful and explained things in multiple ways without just giving the answers. The end of the class was very difficult and not explained well, it just felt rushed. Lin was a good professor as long as you do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Johnny is organized, very friendly, and always willing to help, but not the best prof for teaching CS fundamentals. The way he lectures is really helpful for making programming concepts stick, but I didn't like the way he had us do handwritten assignments pre-class and in-class. Final is easier than midterms. Got a 3.5 with a B average on exams.

BEWARE! Only take this class if it's required for you. For those who do have to take it, buckle up. Main thing is the homework, it is incredibly difficult and is graded on correctness NOT effort. The midterms and final multiple choice is ok, but the hand written portion is quite tricky. If you do poorly on either your grade will suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor thoroughly goes over topics conceptually and does many code implementation exercises in class. He also encourages group problem solving during class. Following his coding guidelines for style is very important, there were times people were docked points on writing exams for using a dot instead of an asterisk for multiplication.

In pure honesty, he's not as bad as the other reviews say he is. Thoroughly touches topics the book covers. He encourages a lot of groupwork to solve difficult problems which helps concepts stick better compared to him just lecturing the whole time. However, he doesn't record lectures, all his classes are in-person, and does not offer extra credit.

This new class he teaches (data science programming) is fine. JUST STUDY. Homework is fairly straightforward. Lectures are alright if you pay attention. Class isn't too bad. I also took CSS 142 with him and that was worse.

If you want to hate CSS please take his class, he assumes that everyone in class already knows java. His exams are hard compared to what he teaches, he should just retire. He said he was going to be like ur dad, at first I didn't know if that was a good thing or a bad thing, it was bad..... just added to my daddy issues fr. Please save yourself!!!

This is definitely a harder class but the Professor is very clear about what he expects of you from the beginning. He knows what he’s talking about and I learned a lot from his teaching. He is more than willing to help students and offer strategies for better understanding the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
I don't know why he has hate on here, at all!

He is a very good professor. He knows what he's teaching. His lectures are helpful. Exams are 40% of your grade and there hard, but review is similar to the exams. HW's are 30% and graded hard. The class is just a hard class in general and requires a lot of self teaching.  Nice and Caring!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What's with the hate here? Ok sure, he's a hard grader as well as kind of an oldhead with teaching methods, but he REALLY values student input and feedback as well as participation, and the way he explains things in class and in office hours is very helpful. Don't hesitate to reach out to him for how he can best support your learning.

Lin is a good person but the course is tough as well as his grading. 40% of your grade is just midterms so if you bomb it then you can't make the points back. Like 25% is understandable but 40% of our grade is insane since other assignments won't even budge your grade. Tests are also handwritten for coding....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is quite a rigorous course as it is only 4 weeks long. With CSS 142 being the only prereq, it is quite hard to grasp the material if you have very little coding experience. This class is also in Python, so there is very little time to learn the language and concepts being taught in class. There are 4 HW assignments and a midterm and final.

This professor should not be teaching this course. The course encourages lots of open dialogue and discussion and the professor made it extremely boring and rigid. The course has a LOT of interesting topics and the professor just made it as boring as possible
He is a useless teacher in this class

Lectures are disorganized with no good explanations, and his handwritten notes are hard to follow. He assigns photographs of written assignments, which makes literally no sense in Zoom, and doesn't like to provide any real resources or help for students. His exams are notoriously difficult. He's really good, but if you dont do teh reading and dont care about coding style he'll be hard on you.

Really good professor if you are there to learn. To have a good understanding of his lecture, you have to do the textbook readings beforehand. reviews.comment: hardest class I've taken so far, boring lectures, moves at a fast pace
